body.text: śikṣā-samuccayaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> (Compendium of Training)

body.text: dāna-pāramitā nāma prathamaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The first chapter, called the Perfection of Giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>). //

body.text: namaḥ sarva-buddha-bodhi-satvebhyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! //

body.text: yasya + a-śraveṇa naraka-ādi mahā-prapāta-dāha-ādi-duṣkham anubhūtam abhūd bhavadbhiḥ | tīvraṃ punaḥ punar an-antam a-śānta-cittais tac * chrotum ādaram udārataraṃ bhajadhvam ||
body.translated_text: By not hearing which, the intense suffering of the great abyss of hells and so forth — burning and the like — has been experienced by you, again and again, endlessly, with unpeaceful minds; listen to that with reverence!

body.text: śrutvā ... pāpaṃ an-uddhata-ātmā pūrva-arjitaṃ ca vipulaṃ kṣapayaty a-śeṣam | a-prāpta-pūrvam api saukhyam avāpnuvanti hāniṃ sukhāc ca na kadā-cid api prayānti ||
body.translated_text: Having heard... one who is not puffed up with pride exhausts completely even the vast [store of] previously accumulated sin; and they obtain happiness never before attained, and never at any time do they suffer a loss of happiness.

body.text: sambodhi-satva-sukham uttamam a-kṣaya ... apy a-sama-saṃpadam āpnuvanti | tad dharma-ratnam ati-dur-labham apy a-labdhaṃ labdha-kṣaṇāḥ śṛṇvata sa-ādaram ucyamānam ||
body.translated_text: They obtain the supreme, inexhaustible happiness of the awakening-being (<s>saṃbodhisattva</s>), the incomparable prosperity; therefore, you who have obtained the [rare] opportunity, listen with reverence to that jewel of the <s>Dharma</s>, so extremely difficult to obtain, yet [now] obtained!

body.text: āyāntu ca tri-bhuvana-eka-hitasya vākyaṃ śrotuṃ prasanna-manasaḥ sura-nāga-satvāḥ | gandharva-yakṣa-garuḍa-asura-kinnara-indrāḥ preta-ādayaḥ śravaṇa-jāta-tṛṣaḥ sa-harṣāḥ ||
body.translated_text: May the beings — gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>Indras</s>, <s>pretas</s> and others — come with joyful minds, delighting in hearing, to listen to the words of the one who is the sole benefactor of the three worlds!

body.text: su-gatān sa-sutān sa-dharma-kāyān praṇipatya + ādarato * akhilāṃś ca vandyān | su-gata-ātma-ja-samvara-avatāraṃ kathayiṣyāmi samuccita-artha-vākyaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Having bowed respectfully to the <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones) together with their sons and their <s>Dharmakāya</s>, and to all who are worthy of reverence, I shall expound the entry into the discipline (<s>saṃvara</s>) of the sons of the <s>Sugata</s>, in sentences whose meaning is gathered [from the sūtras].

body.text: na ca kiñ-cid a-pūrvam atra vācyaṃ na ca saṃgranthana-kauśalaṃ mama + asti | ata eva na me para-artha-yatnaḥ sva-mano bhāvayituṃ mama + idam iṣṭam ||
body.translated_text: Nothing unprecedented is to be said here, nor do I possess skill in composition; therefore, my effort is not for the benefit of others — my wish is to cultivate my own mind.

body.text: mama tāvad anena yāti vṛddhiṃ kuśalaṃ bhāvayituṃ prasāda-vegaḥ | yadi mat-sama-dhātur eva paśyed a-paro * apy enam ato * api sa-arthako * ayam ||
body.translated_text: For me, at least, by this, the impetus of devotion grows for cultivating the wholesome; and if another of similar disposition should see this, then this [work] too would be purposeful.

body.text: kṣaṇa-sampad iyaṃ su-dur-labhā pratilabdhā puruṣa-artha-sādhanī | yadi na + atra vicintyate hitaṃ punar apy eṣa samāgamaḥ kutaḥ ||
body.translated_text: This endowment of the [favorable] moment, so extremely difficult to obtain, has been gained — it is the means of accomplishing the purpose of a person; if one does not reflect upon what is beneficial here, when will this conjunction occur again?

body.text: yathā + uktam ārya-gaṇḍa-vyūha-sūtre | ārya-jaya-uṣma-āyatana-vimokṣe ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Ārya-Gaṇḍavyūha Sūtra</s>, in the <s>Ārya-Jayoṣmāyatana-vimokṣa</s>:

body.text: dur-labhā + aṣṭā-kṣaṇa-nirvṛttir dur-labho manuṣya-pratilambho dur-labhā kṣaṇa-saṃpat-viśuddhir dur-labho buddha-utpādo | dur-labhā + a-vikala-indriyatā | dur-labho buddha-dharma-śravo | dur-labhaṃ sat-puruṣa-samavadhānaṃ | dur-labhāni bhūta-kalyāṇa-mitrāṇi | dur-labho bhūta-naya-anuśāsany upasaṃhāraḥ | dur-labhaṃ samyag-jīvitaṃ | dur-labhaḥ sad-dharme tad-anukūlaḥ prayatno manuṣyalokae iti ||
body.translated_text: Difficult to obtain is freedom from the eight unfavorable conditions; difficult to obtain is a human birth; difficult to obtain is the purity of the endowment of the [favorable] moment; difficult to obtain is the arising of a <s>Buddha</s>; difficult to obtain is the completeness of the faculties...

body.text: tad evaṃ-vidhaṃ samāgamam āsādya saṃvṛti-parama-arthataḥ su-vidita-saṃsāra-duṣkhasya + upaśamana-sukha-abhilāṣiṇo buddha-gotra-anubhāvāt tu yasya mahāsatvasya + evaṃ pratyavekṣā + utpadyate ||
body.translated_text: Thus, having reached such a conjunction, one who knows the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> both conventionally and ultimately, who desires the happiness of cessation, and in whom, through the power of the <s>Buddha</s>-lineage (<s>gotra</s>), a great...

body.text: yadā mama pareṣāṃ ca bhayaṃ duṣkhaṃ ca na priyaṃ | tadā + ātmanaḥ ko viśeṣo yat taṃ rakṣāmi na + itaram | iti tena + ātmanaḥ satva-dhātoś ca ||
body.translated_text: 'When both I and others do not desire fear and suffering, then what is special about my self that I protect it and not the other?' — Thus, [reflecting] on oneself and the realm of beings,

body.text: duṣkha-antaṃ karttu-kāmena sukha-antaṃ gantum icchatā | śraddhā-mūlaṃ dṛḍhī-kṛtya bodhau kāryā matir dṛḍhā ||
body.translated_text: 'One who wishes to make an end of suffering, one who wishes to reach the end of happiness — having made firm the root of faith, one should make one's resolve toward awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) firm.'

body.text: uktaṃ hi ratna-ulkā-dhāraṇyām ||
body.translated_text: For it is said in the <s>Ratnolkā-dhāraṇī</s>:

body.text: śraddhayamānu jinān jinadharmmān śraddhayate cari buddha-sutānām | bodhi anuttara śraddhayamāno jāyati cittaṃ mahā-puruṣāṇām ||
body.translated_text: One who has faith in the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones) and their <s>Dharma</s>, who has faith in the conduct of the sons of the <s>Buddha</s>, who has faith in the unsurpassed <s>bodhi</s> — in such a one the mind of great beings is born.

body.text: śraddha puro-gata-mātṛ-janetrī pālika-varddhika sarva-guṇānām | kāṃkṣa-vinodani ogha-pratāraṇi | śraddha-nidarśani kṣema-purasya ||
body.translated_text: Faith is the forerunner, like a mother and genetrix, the protector and increaser of all virtues, the remover of doubt, the one who carries across the flood, faith is the indicator of the city of well-being.

body.text: śraddha an-āvila-citta-prasādo māna-vivarjita-gaurava-mūlā | śraddha nidhāna-dhanaṃ caraṇa-agraṃ pāṇi yathā śubha-saṃgraha-mūlam ||
body.translated_text: Faith is the clarity of an undefiled mind, the root of respect free from pride, faith is the treasure-store, the wealth, the foremost practice, the hand that is the root of grasping the wholesome.

body.text: śraddha pramoda-karī parityāge | śraddha praharṣa-karī jina-dharmme | śraddha viśeṣa-karī guṇa-jñāne | daiśika prāpaṇi buddha-gatī ye ||
body.translated_text: Faith produces joy in generosity, faith produces delight in the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Jinas</s>, faith produces distinction in the knowledge of virtues, faith is the guide that leads to the state of <s>Buddhahood</s>.

body.text: indriya-tīkṣṇa-prabhāsvaratāyai | śraddha-balaṃ a-vimardanatāyai | niśraya-kleśa-adharṣikatāyai | aiṣikā śraddha svayaṃ-bhu-guṇānām ||
body.translated_text: For the sharpness and radiance of the faculties, the strength of faith is for indestructibility, for the unassailability of the afflictions as a support — faith is the foundation of the qualities of the Self-Arisen (<s>Svayaṃbhū</s>).

body.text: śraddha a-saṅgata-saṅga-sukheṣu a-kṣaṇa-varjita eka-kṣaṇa-agram | śraddha atikramu māra-pathasya | darśika uttama-mokṣa-pathasya ||
body.translated_text: Faith is detached from attachment to pleasures, it avoids the unfavorable moment and [leads to] the foremost single moment; faith is the transcendence of <s>Māra's</s> path, the indicator of the supreme path of liberation.

body.text: vījam a-pūtiku hetu-guṇānāṃ | śraddha virohaṇi bodhi-drumasya | varddhani jñāna-viśeṣa-sukhānāṃ | śraddha nidarśika sarva-jinānāṃ ||
body.translated_text: An uncorrupted seed, the cause of virtues — faith is the sprouting of the tree of awakening (<s>bodhi</s>); the increaser of the happiness of the distinction of knowledge — faith is the indicator of all the <s>Jinas</s>.

body.text: ye sada śraddha sa-gaurava-buddhe | te tu na śīla na śikṣa tyajanti | ye tu na śīla na śikṣa tyajantī | te guṇavāṃ stutaye

children.translated_text: and those who do not abandon moral conduct or the training are virtuous and worthy of praise. //

body.translated_text: Those who always have faith with reverence in the <s>Buddha</s> — they do not abandon moral conduct or the training;

body.text: ye sada śraddha sa-gaurava-dharmme | te jina-dharmma a-tṛpta-śṛṇontī
body.translated_text: Those who always have faith with reverence in the <s>Dharma</s> — they listen insatiably to the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Jinas</s>.

body.text: ye jina-dharmm a-tṛpta-śṛṇontī | teṣv adhimukti a-cintiya-dharmme ||
body.translated_text: Those who listen insatiably to the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Jinas</s> — in them there is faith in the inconceivable <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: ye sada śraddha sa-gaurava-saṃghe | te a-vivarttika saṃgha-prasannāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Those who always have faith with reverence in the <s>Saṅgha</s> — they are irreversible, devoted to the <s>Saṅgha</s>.

body.text: ye a-vivarttika saṃgha-prasannās te a-vivarttika śraddha-balātaḥ | ye a-vivarttika śraddha-balāto | indriya-tīkṣṇa-prabhāsvara teṣām ||
body.translated_text: Those who are irreversible, devoted to the <s>Saṅgha</s>, are irreversible through the strength of faith; those who are irreversible through the strength of faith — their faculties are sharp and radiant.

body.text: indriya-tīkṣṇa-prabhāsvara yeṣām tehi vivarjita pāpaka-mitrāḥ | yehi vivarjita pāpaka-mitrāḥ dhārmmika-mitra-parigraha teṣām ||
body.translated_text: Those whose faculties are sharp and radiant — by them evil friends are abandoned; those who have abandoned evil friends — they obtain the companionship of <s>Dharma</s>-friends.

body.text: dhārmika-mitra-parigraha yeṣām | te vipulaṃ kuśala + upacinvanti | ye vipulaṃ kuśala + upacinontī hetu-bala-upagatāya mahā-ātmā ||
body.translated_text: Those who have the companionship of <s>Dharma</s>-friends — they accumulate vast wholesome [merit]; those who accumulate vast wholesome [merit] — they are great beings endowed with the strength of causes.

body.text: hetu-bala-upagatāya mahā-ātmā | teṣa udāra-dhimukti-viśeṣāḥ | yeṣa udāra-dhimukti-viśeṣās te sadā + adhiṣṭhita sarva-jinebhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Those who are great beings endowed with the strength of causes — they have distinguished, noble aspirations; those who have distinguished, noble aspirations — they are always blessed by all the <s>Jinas</s>.

body.text: ye sadā + adhiṣṭhita sarva-jinebhis teṣu + upapadyati bodhayi cittam | yeṣu + upapadyati bodhayi cittaṃ te abhiyukta maha-rṣi-guṇeṣu ||
body.translated_text: Those who are always blessed by all the <s>Jinas</s> — in them the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) arises; those in whom the mind of awakening arises — they are devoted to the qualities of the Great Sages.

body.text: ye abhiyukta maha-rṣi-guṇeṣu jātaya-buddha-kule anujātāḥ | jātaya buddha-kule anujātās te samayoga a-yoga-vimuktāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Those who are devoted to the qualities of the Great Sages — they are born in the family of the <s>Buddhas</s>, rightly born; those born in the family of the <s>Buddhas</s>, rightly born — they are rightly yoked, freed from the unyoked.

body.text: ye samayoga a-yoga-vimuktāḥ | āśaya teṣa prasāda-viśuddhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Those who are rightly yoked, freed from the unyoked — their aspiration is purified with devotion.

body.text: āśayu yeṣa prasāda-viśuddhaḥ teṣa adhyāśayu uttama-śreṣṭhaḥ | yeṣa adhyāśayu uttama-śreṣṭhas te sada pāramitāsu caranti ||
body.translated_text: Those whose aspiration is purified with devotion — their higher aspiration (<s>adhyāśaya</s>) is supreme and excellent; those whose higher aspiration is supreme and excellent — they always practice the perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>).

body.text: ye sada pāramitāsu carantī te pratipanna iho maha-yāne | ye pratipanna iho maha-yāne te pratipattitu pūjayi buddhān ||
body.translated_text: Those who always practice the perfections — they have entered the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) here; those who have entered the <s>Mahāyāna</s> here — they worship the <s>Buddhas</s> through practice.

body.text: ye pratipattitu pūjayi buddhān teṣu anusmṛti buddha a-bhedyā | yeṣu anusmṛti buddha a-bhedyā | te sada paśyiya cintiya buddhān ||
body.translated_text: Those who worship the <s>Buddhas</s> through practice — in them the recollection of the <s>Buddha</s> is unbreakable; those in whom the recollection of the <s>Buddha</s> is unbreakable — they always see and contemplate the <s>Buddhas</s>.

body.text: ye sada paśyiya cintiya buddhān | teṣa na jātu na tiṣṭhati buddhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Those who always see and contemplate the <s>Buddhas</s> — for them the <s>Buddha</s> never at any time ceases to abide.

body.text: yeṣa na jātu na tiṣṭhati buddhaḥ teṣa na jātu rahāyati dharmmaḥ | yeṣa na jātu rahāyati dharmaḥ te sada dhiṣṭhita sarva-jinebhir | ity-ādi-śraddhā-mūlo guṇa-vistaro * an-antas tatra + uktaḥ | tat parisamāpya saṃkṣepataḥ punar āha | dur-llabha-satva-pṛthag-jana-kāyā | ye imi śraddadhi īdṛśi dharmmān | ye tu śubha-upacitāḥ kṛta-puṇyās te imi śraddadhi hetu-balena ||
body.translated_text: Those for whom the <s>Buddha</s> never at any time ceases to abide — for them the <s>Dharma</s> is never at any time concealed; those for whom the <s>Dharma</s> is never at any time concealed — they are always blessed by all the <s>Jinas</s>. And so forth — the root of faith...

body.text: yo daśa-kṣetra-raja-upama-satvān kalpam upasthihi sarva-sukhena | na + uta tu tādṛśu puṇya-viśeṣo yādṛśa śraddadhato imi dharmmān ||
body.translated_text: One who for a <s>kalpa</s> (aeon) serves with every comfort beings equal to the dust-particles of ten fields — even so, such merit is not equal to that of one who has faith in these <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: iti | tathā + ārya-daśa-dharma-sūtre * api deśitaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Thus. Likewise, it has been taught in the <s>Ārya-Daśadharma Sūtra</s>:

body.text: śraddhā hi paramaṃ yānaṃ yena niryānti nāyakāḥ | tasmād buddha-anuśāritvaṃ bhajeta matimān naraḥ ||
body.translated_text: Faith is the supreme vehicle by which the guides (<s>nāyaka</s>) proceed; therefore, an intelligent person should cultivate being instructed by the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: a-śrāddhasya manuṣyasya śuklo dharmo na rohati | vījānām agni-dagdhānām aṅkuro harito yathā ||
body.translated_text: For a faithless person, the white <s>dharma</s> does not grow — just as a green sprout [does not grow] from seeds burnt by fire.

body.text: iti | ata eva + ārya-lalita-vistara-sūtre prativeditaṃ | śraddhāyām ānanda yogaḥ karaṇīya idaṃ tathā-gato vijñapayati + iti ||
body.translated_text: Thus. Therefore, in the <s>Ārya-Lalitavistara Sūtra</s> it has been proclaimed: 'The yoga of faith should be practiced, O <s>Ānanda</s> — this the <s>Tathāgata</s> makes known.'

body.text: tathā siṃha-paripṛcchāyāṃ | śraddhayā | kṣaṇam a-kṣaṇaṃ varjayati ity uktam ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, in the <s>Siṃhaparipṛcchā</s>: 'Through faith, one avoids the unfavorable moment' — thus it is said.

body.text: tad evaṃ | śraddhā-mūlaṃ dṛḍhī-kṛtya bodhi-cittaṃ dṛḍhaṃ kartavyaṃ sarva-puṇya-saṃgrahatvāt tad yathā + ārya-siṃha-paripṛcchāyāṃ | siṃhena rāja-kumāreṇa bhagavān pṛṣtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therefore: having made firm the root of faith, the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) should be made firm, since it is the collection of all merit. As in the <s>Ārya-Siṃhaparipṛcchā</s>: '<s>Siṃha</s>, the prince...'

body.text: saṃgrahaḥ sarva-dharmāṇāṃ | karmaṇā kena jāyate | priyaś ca bhoti satvānāṃ yatra yatra + upapadyate ||
body.translated_text: 'The collection of all <s>dharmas</s> — by what action does it arise? And [how] does one become dear to beings wherever one is reborn?'

body.text: bhagavān āha | sarva-satva-pramokṣāya cittaṃ bodhāya nāmayet | eṣa saṃgraha dharmāṇāṃ bhavate tena ca priyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'One should incline the mind toward awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) for the liberation of all beings; this is the collection of <s>dharmas</s>, and by this one becomes dear [to beings].'

body.text: iti | tathā + ārya-gaṇḍa-vyūha-sūtre * api varṇitaṃ | bodhi-cittaṃ hi kula-putra vīja-bhūtaṃ sarva-buddha-dharmāṇāṃ | kṣetra-bhūtaṃ sarva-jagac-chukla-dharma-virohaṇatayā | dharaṇi-bhūtaṃ sarva-loka-pratiśaraṇatayā yāvat pitṛ-bhūtaṃ sarva-bodhi-satva-ārakṣaṇatayā ||
body.translated_text: Thus. Likewise, it has been described in the <s>Ārya-Gaṇḍavyūha Sūtra</s>: 'O son of good family, the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) is the seed of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>; it is the field of all beings' wholesome...'

body.text: peyālaṃ ||
body.translated_text: [Abbreviation marker: <s>peyyāla</s>]

body.text: vaiśravaṇa-bhūtaṃ sarva-dāridrya-saṃchedanatayā | cintā-maṇi-rāja-bhūtaṃ sarva-artha-saṃsādhanatayā | bhadra-ghaṭa-bhūtaṃ sarva-abhiprāya-paripūraṇatayā | śakti-bhūtaṃ kleśa-śatru-vijayāya | dharma-bhūtaṃ yoniśo manas-kāra-saṃchedanatayā | khaḍga-bhūtaṃ kleśa-śiraḥ-prapātanatayā | kuṭhāra-bhūtaṃ duṣkha-vṛkṣa-saṃchedanatayā | praharaṇa-bhūtaṃ sarva-upadrava-paritrāṇatayā | vaḍisa-bhūtaṃ saṃsāra-jala-cara-abhyuddharaṇatayā | vāta-maṇḍalī-bhūtaṃ sarva-āvaraṇa-nivaraṇa-tṛna-vikiraṇatayā | uddāna-bhūtaṃ sarva-bodhi-satva-caryā-praṇidhāna-saṃgrahaṇatayā | caitya-bhūtaṃ sa-deva-mānuṣa-asurasya lokasya | iti hi kula-putra bodhi-cittam ebhiś ca + anyaiś ca + a-pramāṇair guṇa-viśeṣaiḥ samanvāgatam iti ||
body.translated_text: '...the <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (god of wealth) in cutting off all poverty; the wish-fulfilling gem-king in accomplishing all purposes; the <s>bhadraghaṭa</s> (auspicious pot) in fulfilling all wishes...'

body.text: kathaṃ punar jñāyate | pṛthag-janasya + api bodhi-cittam utpadyate | na vāṅ-mātram etad iti | an-eka-sūtra-anta-darśanāt ||
body.translated_text: How then is it known that even for an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) arises — that this is not mere words? From seeing [evidence] in the conclusions of many <s>sūtras</s>.

body.text: yathā tāvad ārya-vimalakīrtti-nirdeśe nirdiṣṭaṃ | sumeru-samāṃ sat-kāya-dṛṣṭim utpādya bodhi-cittam utpadyate | tataś ca buddha-dharmā virohanti + iti ||
body.translated_text: As indeed it is taught in the <s>Ārya-Vimalakīrtinirdeśa</s>: 'Having generated a view of the personal self as great as Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, the mind of awakening arises; and from that, the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> grow.'

body.text: ratna-karaṇḍa-sūtrāc ca pṛthag-jano * api bodhi-satva iti jñāyate ||
body.translated_text: And from the <s>Ratnakaraṇḍa Sūtra</s>, even an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) is known as a <s>bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: yathā + uktaṃ | tad yathā + api nāma mañjuśrīḥ aṇḍa-koṣa-prakṣipto * api kalaviṅka-poto | a-saṃbhinna-aṇḍa a-niśkrāntaḥ koṣāt kalaviṅka-rutam eva muñcati ||
body.translated_text: As stated: 'Just as, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, even a <s>kalaviṅka</s> (sparrow) chick thrown into an egg-shell, with the egg unbroken and not emerged from the shell, still emits the sound of a <s>kalaviṅka</s>...'

body.text: evam eva mañjuśrīḥ a-vidyā-aṇḍa-koṣa-prakṣipto * api bodhi-satvo | a-saṃbhinna-ātma-dṛṣṭir a-niṣkrāntas traidhātukād buddha-rutam eva muñcati | yad idaṃ śūnyatā-nimitta-a-praṇihita-rutam eva ||
body.translated_text: 'Just so, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, even a <s>bodhisattva</s> thrown into the egg-shell of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), with the view of self unbroken and not emerged from the three realms, still emits the <s>Buddha</s>-sound — namely...'

body.text: sarva-dharma-pravṛtti-nirdeśe * api kathitaṃ | jayamateś ca bodhi-satvasya pṛthivī vidāram adāt | sa kāla-gato mahā-nirayaṃ prāpatad iti | sa hi śūnyatāṃ na + adhimuktavān śūnyatā-vādini ca pratighaṃ kṛtavān ||
body.translated_text: In the instruction on the engagement with all <s>dharmas</s>, it is also said: "<s>Jayamati</s> the <s>bodhisattva</s> split open the earth. He, upon dying, fell into the great hell." For he had not accepted <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) and had generated hostility toward one who taught <s>śūnyatā</s>.

body.text: niyata-a-niyata-avatāra-mudrā-sūtre * apy ākhyātaṃ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Niyatāniyatāvatāramudrā-sūtra</s> it is also declared:

body.text: katamaḥ paśu-ratha-gatiko bodhi-satvaḥ | tad yathā | kaś-cit puruṣaḥ pañca-buddha-kṣetra-parama-aṇu-rajaḥ-samān loka-dhātūn abhikramitu-kāmaḥ syāt | sa paśu-ratham abhiruhya mārgaṃ pratipadyate sa cireṇa dīrgheṇa + adhvanā yojana-śataṃ gacchet | sa tatra mahatyā vāta-maṇḍalyā paścāt khalu punar aśītiṃ yojana-sahasrāṇi pratyākṛṣya pratyudāvartya + iti | tat kiṃ śaknuyāt sa puruṣas tān loka-dhātūn paśu-rathena + atikramitum | yāvad an-abhilāpya-an-abhilāpyair api kalpair ekam api loka-dhātum atikramitum | āha | na + u hi + idaṃ bhagavan | bhagavān āha | evam eva mañjuśrīḥ yaḥ kaś-cid bodhi-cittam utpādya mahā-yānaṃ | na dhārayati | na paṭhati | śrāvaka-yānīyān sevate | taiś ca sārddhaṃ saṃstavaṃ karoti | śrāvaka-yānaṃ ca paṭhati sva-adhyāyati mīmāṃsate paribudhyate * arthāṃś ca pāṭhayati yāvad bodhayati | sa tena dhanva-prajño bhavati so * an-uttara-jñāna-mārgāt pratyākṛṣyate pratyudāvarttyate | yad api tasya bodhi-satvasya bodhi-bhāvanā + ataḥ prajñā-indriyaṃ prajñā-cakṣuḥ tad api tasya dhanvī-kriyate pratihanyate | śrayaṃ paśu-ratha-gatiko bodhi-satva iti ||
body.translated_text: What is a <s>bodhisattva</s> who travels by ox-cart? It is as follows: Suppose a certain man wished to traverse world-realms equal in number to the atoms of five <s>buddha-kṣetras</s> (buddha-fields). He mounts an ox-cart and sets out on the road. After a long, extended journey he would travel one hundred <s>yojanas</s> (leagues). Then a great whirlwind from behind would drag him back and turn him around eighty thousand <s>yojanas</s>. Could that man traverse those world-realms by ox-cart? Even in inexpressibly inexpressible <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) he could not traverse even a single world-realm. He said: "No indeed, <s>Bhagavan</s> (Lord)." The <s>Bhagavan</s> said: "Just so, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, whoever, having generated <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), does not uphold the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle), does not recite it, associates with those of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> (Hearers' Vehicle), keeps company with them, and recites, studies, investigates, and comprehends the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>, and even teaches its meanings and leads others to understand it — he thereby becomes one of barren wisdom, and is dragged back and turned away from the path of supreme knowledge. Whatever cultivation of awakening, faculty of wisdom, and eye of wisdom that <s>bodhisattva</s> had — all that is rendered barren and destroyed. He is a <s>bodhisattva</s> who travels by ox-cart."

body.text: tad evam eṣā śūnyatā-an-adhimuktir mahā-yāna-an-abhiratiś ca + a-saṃpūrṇa-adhimukti-citta-caryasya + api prāyo na saṃdṛśyate | prāg eva + adhimātra-adhimukti-caryasya bodhi-satvasya | sa hi ratna-meghe | sarva-bāla-carita-vipatti-samatikrāntaḥ paṭhyate a-saṃkhyeya-samādhi-dhāraṇī-vimokṣa-abhijñā-vidyā-vikrīdito | an-anta-dharma-ārāma-rati-nir-āmiṣa-a-para-anta-kalpa-koṭy-an-ābhoga-nir-vikalpa-prīti-vega-āloka-pratilabdhaś ca + a-prameya-kalpa-koṭī-niyuta-śata-sahasra-parama-mahā-yāna-prasthāna-vicitra-bhāvanā-saṃpūrṇa para-artha-pratipatti-niryāṇa puṇya-jñāna-saṃbhāra-abhinihāra-abhinirvṛttiḥ pūrva-yoga-śata-sahasra-samṛddhaś ca paṭhyate | atha + etan neya-arthaṃ | kasmād anye bodhi-citta-utpādakā asyāṃ bhūmau na + iṣyante | na ca + atra + icchayā kiñ-cid viśeṣa-cihnaṃ nīta-arthaṃ karttuṃ labhyate | adhimātra-adhimukti-caryā + a-dharmatā vacanāc ca gamyate | yathā madhya-mṛdu-prakārā + apy adhimukti-caryā + asty eva + iti ||
body.translated_text: Thus, this non-acceptance of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) and lack of delight in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is generally not seen even in one whose practice of the mind of aspiration is incomplete, let alone in a <s>bodhisattva</s> whose aspiration-practice is intense. For in the <s>Ratnamegha</s> (Cloud of Jewels), one [at the incomplete stage] is described as having transcended all the misfortunes of childish conduct, as one who sports in innumerable <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations), <s>dhāraṇīs</s> (retentions), <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations), <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), and <s>vidyās</s> (sciences); as one who has obtained the radiance of the rush of bliss that is unwavering, effortless, non-conceptual, without material bait, delighting in the garden of infinite <s>dharmas</s>, throughout boundless hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s>; and as one whose accomplishment of the accumulations of merit and knowledge for the benefit of others is perfected through the varied cultivation of the supreme <s>Mahāyāna</s> path over immeasurable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> (millions) of <s>kalpas</s>, and who is enriched by hundreds of thousands of former connections. Now, this is of provisional meaning. Why are other generators of <s>bodhicitta</s> not accepted at this stage? And here nothing with distinguishing marks can be made definitive by mere wish. That the intense aspiration-practice is non-dharmic is understood from its statement; just as there exist aspiration-practices of the middling and mild kinds as well.

body.text: asya punas tathā-gata-guhya-sūtrasya ko * abhiprāyo | yad uktaṃ | kasya bhagavan bodhi-citta-utpādaḥ | āha | yasya mahā-rāja + adhyāśayo * a-vikopitaḥ | āha | kasya bhagavann adhyāśayo * a-vikopitaḥ | āha | yasya mahā-rāja mahā-karuṇā-utpādaḥ | āha | kasya bhagavan mahā-karuṇā-utpādaḥ | āha | yasya mahā-rāja sarva-satva-a-parityāgaḥ | āha | kathaṃ bhagavan satvā a-parityaktā bhavanti | āha | yadā mahā-rāja + ātma-saukhyaṃ parityaktaṃ bhavati + iti | bodhi-citta-mātra-a-santuṣṭānāṃ karuṇā-abhilāṣa-saṃjana-artham idam uktaṃ | yathā na te tathā-gata-śāsane pravrajitā yeṣāṃ na + asti tyāga iti | evam iha + anya-bodhi-citta-nindā draṣṭavyā na tu bodhi-cittam anyathā na + utpadyatae eva ||
body.translated_text: And what is the intent of this <s>Tathāgataguhya-sūtra</s>? It is said: "Whose, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, is the generation of <s>bodhicitta</s>?" He said: "His, O great king, whose aspiration is unshaken." "Whose, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, is the unshaken aspiration?" He said: "His, O great king, who generates great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>)." "Whose, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, is the generation of great compassion?" He said: "His, O great king, who does not abandon any sentient being." "How, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, are sentient beings not abandoned?" He said: "When, O great king, one's own happiness is abandoned." This is said for the purpose of generating the desire for compassion in those not content with merely generating <s>bodhicitta</s>. Just as those who have not renounced are not considered renunciants in the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching — so here the disparagement of other [forms of] <s>bodhicitta</s> should be understood, but it is not that <s>bodhicitta</s> does not arise in other ways at all.

body.text: yathā daśa-dharmaka-sūtre deśitaṃ | iha kula-putra bodhi-satvo gotra-sthaḥ sann an-utpādita-bodhi-cittaḥ tathā-gatena vā tathā-gata-śrāvakeṇa vā saṃcodyamānaḥ saṃvedyamānaḥ samādāpyamāno * an-uttarāyāṃ samyak-sambodhau bodhi-cittam utpādayati + idaṃ prathamaṃ kāraṇaṃ bodhi-citta-utpādāya | saṃbodher vā bodhi-cittasya vā varṇaṃ bhāṣyamāṇaṃ śrutvā + an-uttarāyāṃ samyak-saṃbodhau cittam utpādayati + idaṃ dvitīyaṃ kāraṇaṃ | sa satvā ... n-a-śaraṇān a-dvīpān dṛṣṭvā kāruṇya-cittam upasthāpya yāvad an-uttarāyāṃ samyak-sambodhau cittam utpādayati + idaṃ tṛtīyaṃ kāraṇaṃ bodhi-citta-utpādāya | sa tathā-gatasya sarva-ākāra-paripūrṇatāṃ dṛṣṭvā prītim utpādya an-uttarāyāṃ samyak-saṃbodhau cittam utpādayati + idaṃ caturthaṃ kāraṇam iti | tac ca bodhi-cittaṃ dvi-vidhaṃ bodhi-praṇidhi-cittaṃ ca bodhi-prasthāna cittaṃ ca | yathā + ārya-gaṇḍa-vyūha-sūtre bhāṣitaṃ | dur-labhāḥ kula-putra te satvāḥ sarva-loke ye * an-uttarasyāṃ samyak-saṃbodhau cittaṃ praṇidadhati | tato * api dur-labhatamās te satvā ye * an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhim abhisaṃprasthitā iti | tatra bodhi-praṇidhi-cittaṃ | mayā buddhena bhavitavyam iti cittaṃ praṇidhānād utpannaṃ bhavati | śūraṅgama-sūtre * api | śāṭhya-utpāditasya + api bodhi-cittasya buddhatva-hetutva-abhidhānāt | kaḥ punar vādaḥ kiñ-cid eva kuśalaṃ kṛtvā | yathā + uktaṃ bhadra-kalpika-sūtre | ghoṣadatto nāma tathā-gato yatra nakṣatrarājena tathā-gatena prathamaṃ bodhi-cittam utpāditaṃ tāmbūla-patraṃ dattvā gopālaka-bhūtena | evaṃ vidyutpradīpo nāma tathāgato yatra yaśasā tathāgatena prathamaṃ bodhi-cittam utpāditaṃ daśikāṃ dattvā tantra-vāya-bhūtena | evam anantaprabho nāma tathā-gato yatra + arciṣmatā tathā-gatena prathamaṃ bodhi-cittam utpāditaṃ tṛṇa-pradīpaṃ dattvā nagara-avalambaka-bhūtena | evaṃ dṛḍhavikramo nāma tathā-gato yatra duṣpradharṣeṇa tathā-gatena prathamaṃ bodhicittam utpāditaṃ datta-kāṣṭhaṃ dattvā kāṣṭha-hāraka-bhūtena + ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: As taught in the <s>Daśadharmaka-sūtra</s>: Here, O son of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s> belonging to the <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage), who has not yet generated <s>bodhicitta</s>, being urged, encouraged, and induced by a <s>Tathāgata</s> or a disciple of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, generates <s>bodhicitta</s> for supreme perfect awakening — this is the first cause for generating <s>bodhicitta</s>. Or, having heard the qualities of awakening or of <s>bodhicitta</s> being praised, one generates the mind for supreme perfect awakening — this is the second cause. Having seen sentient beings without refuge, without shelter, and having aroused a mind of compassion, one generates the mind for supreme perfect awakening — this is the third cause for generating <s>bodhicitta</s>. Having seen the complete perfection of the <s>Tathāgata</s> in all aspects and having generated joy, one generates the mind for supreme perfect awakening — this is the fourth cause. And that <s>bodhicitta</s> is twofold: the mind of aspiration for awakening (<s>bodhipraṇidhicitta</s>) and the mind of setting forth toward awakening (<s>bodhiprasthānacitta</s>). As stated in the noble <s>Gaṇḍavyūha-sūtra</s>: "Rare, O son of good family, are those sentient beings in all the world who aspire to supreme perfect awakening. Even rarer still are those sentient beings who have set forth toward supreme perfect awakening." Therein, the mind of aspiration for awakening arises from the resolve: "I shall become a <s>Buddha</s>." In the <s>Śūraṅgama-sūtra</s> also, since it is declared that even a <s>bodhicitta</s> generated through deceit is a cause of <s>Buddhahood</s> — what need to speak of one who has performed even a little virtue? As stated in the <s>Bhadrakalpika-sūtra</s>: The <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ghoṣadatta</s> — in whose presence <s>Nakṣatrarāja Tathāgata</s> first generated <s>bodhicitta</s> by offering a betel leaf, being a cowherd. Likewise the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vidyutpradīpa</s> — in whose presence <s>Yaśas Tathāgata</s> first generated <s>bodhicitta</s> by offering a towel, being a weaver. Likewise the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Anantaprabha</s> — in whose presence <s>Arciṣmat Tathāgata</s> first generated <s>bodhicitta</s> by offering a grass lamp, being a city-dweller. Likewise the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dṛḍhavikrama</s> — in whose presence <s>Duṣpradharṣa Tathāgata</s> first generated <s>bodhicitta</s> by offering firewood, being a wood-gatherer — and so forth.

body.text: caryā-a-vikale * api ca bodhi-citte na + avamanyatā karttavyā | tasya + apy an-anta-saṃsāra-sukha-prasavanatvāt | yathā + ārya-maitreya-vimokṣe varṇitaṃ | tad yathā + api nāma kula-putra cittam api vajra-ratnaṃ sarva-prativiśiṣṭaṃ suvarṇa-alaṃ-kāram abhibhavati | vajra-ratna-nāma ca na vijahāti | sarva-dāridryaṃ vinivarttayati | evam eva kula-putra + āśaya-pratipatti-bhinnam api sarva-jñatā-citta-utpāda-vajra-ratnaṃ sarva-śrāvaka-praty-eka-buddha-guṇa-suvarṇa-alaṃ-kāram abhibhavati bodhi-sattva-nāma ca na vijahāti | sarva-saṃsāra-dāridryaṃ vinivarttayati + iti | itaś ca vinā + api caryayā bodhi-cittam upakārakam iti jñātavyaṃ | yena + a-para-rāja-avavādaka-sūtre kathitaṃ | yasmāc ca tvaṃ mahā-rāja bahu-kṛtyo bahu-karaṇīyaḥ | a-sahaḥ sarveṇa sarvaḥ sarvathā sarvaṃ sarvadā dāna-pāramitāyāṃ śikṣituṃ | evaṃ yāvat prajñā-pāramitāyāṃ śikṣituṃ | tasmāt tarhi tvaṃ mahā-rāja evam eva samyak-sambodhi-chandaṃ śraddhāṃ tra ... praṇidhiṃ ca gacchann api tiṣṭhann api niṣaṇṇo * api śayāno * api jāgrad api bhuñjāno * api | pivann api | satata-samitam anusmara | manasi-kuru bhāvaya | sarva-buddha-bodhi-satva-praty-eka-buddha-ārya-śrāvaka-pṛthag-j anānām ātmanaś ca + atīta-an-āgata-pratyutpannāni sarva-kuśala-mūlāny abhisaṃkṣipya tulayitvā piṇḍayitvā + anumodasva + agrayā anumodanayā yāvad ākāśa-samatayā nirvāṇa-samatayā + anumodasva + anumodya ca sarva-buddha-bodhi-satva-praty-eka-buddha-ārya-śrāvakāṇāṃ pūjā-karmaṇe niryātaya | niryātya ca sarva-satva-sādhāraṇāni kuru | tataḥ sarva-satvānāṃ yāvat sarva-jñāta-pratilambhāya sarva-buddha-dharma-paripūraṇāya dine dine traikālyam an-uttarāyāṃ samyak-saṃbodhau pariṇāmaya evaṃ khalu tvaṃ mahā-rāja pratipannaḥ san rājyaṃ kārayiṣyasi rājya-kṛtyāni ca na hāyayiṣyasi bodhi-saṃbhārāṃś ca pari-pūrayiṣyasi + iti ||
body.translated_text: Even when <s>bodhicitta</s> is incomplete in practice, it should not be disparaged, for it produces the happiness of endless <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence). As described in the noble <s>Maitreya-vimokṣa</s> (Liberation of <s>Maitreya</s>): "Just as, O son of good family, even a diamond gem, though it surpasses everything, outshines a golden ornament, and does not lose the name 'diamond gem,' and removes all poverty — just so, O son of good family, the diamond gem of generating the mind of omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā-cittotpāda</s>), even when differentiated by aspiration and practice, outshines the golden ornament of all the qualities of <s>Śrāvakas</s> (Hearers) and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (Solitary Buddhas), does not lose the name '<s>bodhisattva</s>,' and removes all the poverty of <s>saṃsāra</s>." From this it should be understood that <s>bodhicitta</s> is beneficial even without practice. For in the <s>Aparārājavādaka-sūtra</s> it is said: "Since, O great king, you have many duties and many tasks, and are unable to train in the <s>dāna-pāramitā</s> (perfection of giving) in every way, at all times, entirely, and always — and likewise up to the <s>prajñā-pāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom) — therefore, O great king, whether going, standing, sitting, lying down, awake, eating, or drinking, constantly and continuously remember, attend to, and cultivate the desire for, faith in, and resolve toward perfect awakening. Bring together, weigh, and consolidate all the roots of virtue — past, future, and present — of all <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, noble <s>Śrāvakas</s>, ordinary beings, and yourself; rejoice with the highest rejoicing, even with rejoicing equal to space, equal to <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Having rejoiced, dedicate them to the worship of all <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and noble <s>Śrāvakas</s>. Having dedicated, make them common to all sentient beings. Then, for the attainment of omniscience by all sentient beings, for the fulfillment of all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, three times daily transfer the merit toward supreme perfect awakening. Thus engaged, O great king, you will administer your kingdom, will not neglect the duties of kingship, and will fulfill the accumulations for awakening."

body.text: atra + eva ca + asya vipāka uktaḥ | sa khalu punas tvaṃ mahā-rāja tasya samyak-saṃbodhi-citta-kuśala-mūla-karmaṇo vipākena + an-eka-śata-kṛtvo deveṣu + upapanno * abhūḥ | an-eka-śata-kṛtvo manuṣyeṣu + upapanno * abhūḥ | sarvāsu ca deva-manuṣya-upapattiṣv ādhipatyam eva kārayasi | na ca tāvat tava mahā-rāja tasya samyak-saṃbodhi-cittasya kuśala-karmaṇa ūnatvaṃ vā + a-pūrṇatvaṃ vā prajñāyate | api ca mahā-rāja ekam api samyak-saṃbodhi-cittaṃ sarva-sattva-uttāraṇa-ārambaṇatvāt sarva-satva-āmocana-ārambaṇatvāt sarva-satva-samāśvāsana-ārambaṇatvāt sarva-satva-parinirvāṇa-ārambaṇatvād a-prameya-a-saṃkhyeya-kuśala-upacayam | kaḥ punar vādo ya evaṃ bahulī-karoti + iti ||
body.translated_text: And here the result of this is stated: "Moreover, O great king, by the ripening of that virtuous action of the mind of perfect awakening, you have been reborn among the gods many hundreds of times. You have been reborn among humans many hundreds of times. And in all rebirths among gods and humans, you exercise sovereignty alone. And yet, O great king, no diminution or incompleteness of that virtuous action of the mind of perfect awakening is perceived. Moreover, O great king, even a single mind of perfect awakening, because it undertakes the rescue of all sentient beings, because it undertakes the liberation of all sentient beings, because it undertakes the consolation of all sentient beings, because it undertakes the complete <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation) of all sentient beings, accumulates immeasurable and incalculable virtue. What need to speak of one who cultivates it abundantly?"

body.text: etac ca bodhi-cittaṃ rūpa-kāya-darśana-utpannaṃ | tatra pūrva-avadāne paṭhyate | evaṃ tāvat praṇidhi-bodhi-cittaṃ veditavyaṃ | idaṃ tu vaktavyaṃ kim a-bhūmi-praviṣṭhasya + api bodhi-satva-samvara-adhikāro * asti na vā + iti | asti + iti veditavyaṃ ākāśa-garbha-sūtre lābha-sat-kāra-arthaṃ mūla-āpatti-śravaṇāt | daśa-bhūmika-sūtre tu prathamāyāṃ bhūmau darśitaṃ | na ca kañ-cit sat-kārāṃ kasya-cit sakāśāt pratikāṃkṣaty anyatra mayā + eva + eṣāṃ sarva-satvānāṃ sarva-upakaraṇa-bāhulyam upanāmayitavyam iti | tathā ca + āha | pramuditāyāṃ bodhi-satva-bhūmau su-vyavasthito bhavaty a-calana-yoge ... ti | punaś ca + uktaṃ | tathā-gata-vaṃśa-niyato bhavati saṃbodhi-parāyaṇa iti | ākāśa-garbha-sūtre tv āha | śrāvaka-yānam eva + asya na bhavati prāg eva mahā-yānam iti | tathā + ārya-ugra-paripṛcchāyāṃ mātsarya-paryavanaddhasya + api śikṣā-padāni prajñaptāni | pramuditāyāṃ tu paṭhyate | ātma-saṃjñā-apagamāc ca + asya + ātma-sneho na bhavati | kutaḥ | punaḥ sarva-upakaraṇa-sneha iti | tathā mastaka-ādi-dānam apy atra + asya + uktaṃ ||
body.translated_text: And this <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening) arises from seeing the <s>rūpakāya</s> (form-body [of a Buddha]). There, in the former <s>avadāna</s> (narrative of noble deeds), it is read. Thus, first, the <s>praṇidhi-bodhicitta</s> (aspiration-mind of awakening) should be understood. But this must be stated: does one who has not yet entered the <s>bhūmis</s> (stages) also have the authority for the <s>bodhisattva-saṃvara</s> (bodhisattva vow), or not? It should be understood that [the authority] exists, since in the <s>Ākāśagarbha-sūtra</s> the hearing of root transgressions for the sake of gain and honor [is mentioned]. In the <s>Daśabhūmika-sūtra</s>, however, it is shown on the first <s>bhūmi</s> (stage): 'And he does not expect any honor from anyone, except [thinking]: "By me alone must the abundance of all provisions for all beings be offered."' And thus it says: 'On the <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful) <s>bodhisattva-bhūmi</s>, he becomes well-established in the yoga of non-wavering...' And again it is said: 'He becomes fixed in the lineage of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, devoted to full awakening.' In the <s>Ākāśagarbha-sūtra</s>, however, it says: 'Even the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle does not belong to this one, let alone the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.' Likewise, in the <s>Ārya-Ugra-paripṛcchā</s>, training rules are prescribed even for one who is bound by miserliness. On the <s>Pramuditā</s> [stage], however, it is read: 'Because the notion of self has departed, he has no attachment to self. How then could there be attachment to all provisions?' Likewise, even the giving of the head and so forth is stated here for this one.

body.text: evam ādi sūtreṣu bhūmi-praviṣṭasya + api śikṣā-prajñaptir dṛśyate | yatra vā + a-sāmānyena bodhi-satvam adhikṛtya + upadeśas tatra + abhyāsa-yogyatayā pratiṣedha-vākyena vā + ādi-karmika-bodhi-satvena na śikṣitavyaṃ bhaved etat | ubhaya-a-saṃbhave tu sarvatra śikṣitavyaṃ | tatra + apy ekasyāṃ śikṣāyāṃ śikṣaṇāyām a-śaktasya + itara-śikṣā-an-abhyāsādana-āpattiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus, in various <s>sūtras</s>, the prescription of training is seen even for one who has entered the <s>bhūmis</s>. Where the instruction is given with reference to a <s>bodhisattva</s> of a special [advanced] kind, there — either due to its being suitable only through practice, or through the prohibitive statement — this need not be trained in by the beginner <s>bodhisattva</s>. But when neither [restriction] applies, one should train in everything. Even there, for one unable to train in one particular training, the fault of not practicing the other trainings [still applies].

body.text: ārya-akṣayamati-sūtre * apy evam avocat | dāna-kāle śīla-upasaṃhārasya + apekṣā + iti vistaraḥ | na ca + atra śithilena bhavitavyaṃ na ca śeṣāsu na samudāgacchati | yathā-balaṃ yathā-bhajamānam iti daśa-bhūmika-sūtre vacanāt | ayaṃ ca saṃvaraḥ strīṇām api mṛdu-kleśānāṃ bodhy-abhilāṣa-cittānāṃ labhyate | uktaṃ hi bodhi-satva-prātimokṣe | caturbhiḥ śāriputra dharmaiḥ samanvāgatāḥ bodhi-satvāḥ satya-vādino bhavanti + ity ārabhya + āha | iha śāriputra kula-putro vā kula-duhitā vā + an-uttarāyāṃ samyak-saṃbodhau cittam utpādya + ārabdha-vīryo viharati kuśala-dharma-paryeṣaṇāya + ity ārabhya sarva upadeśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Akṣayamati-sūtra</s> too, it was thus spoken: 'At the time of giving, there is the requirement of observing moral conduct' — and so on in detail. And in this [matter], one should not become lax, nor should one fail to accomplish the remaining [trainings]. Because of the statement in the <s>Daśabhūmika-sūtra</s>: 'According to one's strength, according to one's capacity.' And this <s>saṃvara</s> (vow) is obtainable even by women of mild afflictions who have minds aspiring to awakening. For it is said in the <s>Bodhisattva-prātimokṣa</s>: '<s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s> endowed with these four <s>dharmas</s> become speakers of truth' — beginning thus, it says: 'Here, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a son of good family or a daughter of good family, having generated the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening, dwells with exertion aroused for the pursuit of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>' — beginning thus, the entire instruction [follows].

body.text: saṃvara-grahaṇaṃ ca bodhi-satva-śikṣā-pada-abhyāsa-paramasya sāṃvarikasya + antikāt kartavyaṃ | evaṃ hy asya śikṣā-atikrame tīvram apatrāpyaṃ guru-visaṃvādana-bhayaṃ ca + utpadyate | tatra ca + an-ābhogataḥ prema-gaurava-siddhir ity eṣa sāmānya-saṃvara-dharmaḥ | ata eva bodhi-satvāḥ tathā-gatānāṃ purataḥ śikṣāṇām anyatama-śikṣā-niṣpatti-kāmāḥ samādānaṃ kurvanti | tasya ca kalyāṇa-mitrasya + a-bhāve daśa-dig-avasthita-buddha-bodhi-satva-abhimukhī-bhāva-bhāvanayā saṃvaro grāhyaḥ saṃvaram ātma-balaṃ ca tulayitvā | anyathā tu sarva-buddha-bodhi-satvāḥ sa-devakaś ca loko visaṃvāditaḥ syāt | sad-dharma-smṛty-upasthāna-sūtre hi kiñ-cin mātraṃ cintayitvā + apy a-dadataḥ preta-gatir uktā pratijñātaṃ ca + a-dadato naraka-gatiḥ | kiṃ punar an-uttaram artham a-khilasya jagataḥ pratijñāya + a-saṃpādayataḥ | ata eva + uktaṃ dharma-saṃgīti-sūtre | satya-gurukeṇa kula-putra bodhi-satvena bhavitavyaṃ | satya-saṃgītiḥ kula-putra dharma-saṃgītiḥ | tatra kula-putra katamat satyaṃ yad bodhi-satvo * an-uttarāyāṃ samyak-saṃbodhau cittam utpādya tac cittaṃ jīvita-hetor api na parityajati na satveṣu vipratipadyate | idaṃ bodhi-satvasya satyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: And the taking of the <s>saṃvara</s> (vow) should be done in the presence of one who holds the vow — one who is devoted to the practice of the <s>bodhisattva</s> training rules. For thus, when he transgresses the training, there arises in him intense shame and the fear of disappointing the teacher. And therein, the accomplishment of affection and reverence [occurs] without [deliberate] effort — this is the general principle of the vow. For this very reason, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, wishing to accomplish one or another of the trainings, make the commitment in the presence of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. And in the absence of that spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), the vow should be taken through the cultivation of turning toward the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s> abiding in the ten directions — having weighed the vow and one's own strength. Otherwise, all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and the world including the <s>devas</s>, would be deceived. For in the <s>Saddharma-smṛtyupasthāna-sūtra</s>, the destination of <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) is declared for one who, having contemplated even a small [gift], does not give it; and the destination of <s>naraka</s> (hell) for one who does not give what was promised. How much more so for one who, having promised the supreme goal for the entire world, does not accomplish it? For this very reason, it is said in the <s>Dharma-saṃgīti-sūtra</s>: 'A son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> should be one for whom truth is paramount. The recitation of truth, O son of good family, is the recitation of <s>Dharma</s>. Therein, O son of good family, what is truth? That the <s>bodhisattva</s>, having generated the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening, does not abandon that mind even for the sake of [his] life, and does not act contrary [to his vow] toward beings. This is the truth of the <s>bodhisattva</s>.'

body.text: yat punar bodhi-satvo * an-uttarāyāṃ samyak-saṃbodhau cittam utpādya paścāt tac cittaṃ parityajati satveṣu vipratipadyate * ayaṃ bodhi-satvasya pratikṛṣṭo mṛṣā-vāda iti | ārya-sāgaramati-sūtre * api deśitaṃ | syād yathā + api nāma sāgaramate rājā vā rāja-mātro vā sarvaṃ nāgarakaṃ janaṃ śvo bhaktena + upanimantrya + upekṣako bhaven na + anna-pānaṃ samudānayet satyaṃ sarva-jana-kāyaṃ visaṃvādayet | tatra te * anna-pāna-bhojanam a-labhamānā uccagghantaḥ prakrāmeyuḥ | evam eva sāgaramate yo bodhi-satvaḥ sarva-satvān āśvāsya + a-tīrṇa-tāraṇāya + a-mukta-mocanāya + an-āśvasta-āśvāsanāya yāvan na bāhuśrutye * abhiyogaṃ karoti na + api tato * anyeṣu bodhi-pakṣya-kuśala-mūleṣu dharmeṣu | ayaṃ bodhi-satvo visaṃvādayati sa-devakaṃ lokaṃ | evaṃ ca taṃ pūrva-buddha-darśinyo devatā uccagghanti vivādayanti | dur-labhās te yajña-svāmino ye mahā-yajñaṃ pratijñāya + uttārayanti | tasmāt tarhi sāgaramate na sā bodhi-satvena vāg bhāṣitavyā yayā sa-deva-mānuṣa-asuraṃ lokaṃ visaṃvādayet ||
body.translated_text: 'But if a <s>bodhisattva</s>, having generated the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening, afterward abandons that mind and acts contrary [to his vow] toward beings — this is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s most degraded false speech.' In the <s>Ārya-Sāgaramati-sūtra</s> too, it is taught: 'Suppose, <s>Sāgaramati</s>, a king or one of royal rank, having invited all the townspeople to a meal on the morrow, were to become indifferent and not prepare food and drink, and were to truly deceive the entire assembly of people. Those people, not obtaining the food and drink, would depart laughing [in scorn]. Just so, <s>Sāgaramati</s>, whatever <s>bodhisattva</s>, having reassured all beings [saying] "I will ferry across those not yet ferried, liberate those not yet liberated, comfort those not yet comforted," does not exert himself in extensive learning, nor in the other wholesome roots of the <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya</s>) — this <s>bodhisattva</s> deceives the world including the <s>devas</s>. And the <s>devatās</s> who had seen him in former [lives as] Buddhas laugh at him and reproach him: "Rare are those sacrificial masters who, having pledged a great sacrifice, [actually] carry it through!" Therefore, <s>Sāgaramati</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> should not speak that word by which he would deceive the world with its <s>devas</s>, humans, and <s>asuras</s>.'

body.text: punar a-paraṃ sāgaramate bodhi-satvaḥ kena-cid eva + adhīṣṭo bhavati dharmeṣv artha-karaṇīyeṣu | tatra bodhi-satvena vāg bhāṣitā bhavati yāvad ātma-parityāgo * api bodhi-satvena kartavyo bhavet tatra na punaḥ sa satvo visaṃvādayitavya iti | tasmāt sva-bala-anurūpeṇa + ekam api kuśala-mūlaṃ samādāya rakṣitavyaṃ | yathā + uktam ārya-kṣitigarbha-sūtre | ebhir daśabhiḥ kuśalaiḥ karma-pathair buddhatvaṃ | na punar yo * antaśa ekam api yāvaj-jīvaṃ kuśalaṃ karma-pathaṃ na rakṣati atha ca punar evaṃ vadati | ahaṃ mahā-yāniko * ahaṃ ca + an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhiṃ paryeṣāmi + iti | sa pudgalaḥ parama-kuhako mahā-mṛṣā-vādikaḥ sarveṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ purato visaṃvādako lokasya + uccheda-vādī sa mūḍhaḥ kālaṃ kurute vinipāta-gāmī bhavati + iti | yāvat kālaṃ ca śaknoti tāvat kālaṃ kuśalaṃ samādāya vartitavyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, <s>Sāgaramati</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> is commissioned by someone [i.e., by his own vow] for deeds that serve the purpose of the <s>Dharma</s>. When the <s>bodhisattva</s> has spoken a word there, even self-sacrifice should be undertaken by the <s>bodhisattva</s>; but that being should never be deceived.' Therefore, in accordance with one's own strength, even a single wholesome root should be undertaken and protected. As it is said in the <s>Ārya-Kṣitigarbha-sūtra</s>: 'Through these ten wholesome courses of action, <s>Buddhahood</s> [is attained]. But one who does not protect even a single wholesome course of action for as long as he lives, yet says: "I am a follower of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; I seek unsurpassed perfect awakening" — that person is a supreme hypocrite, a great speaker of falsehood, a deceiver of all the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, before their very presence, an annihilationist regarding the world; that deluded one dies [and] becomes one destined for the downfall.' And for as long as one is able, for that long one should undertake and abide in wholesome [deeds].

body.text: etac ca bhaiṣajya-guru-vaiḍūrya-prabha-sūtre draṣṭavyaṃ | yas tu mahā-satva evaṃ śrutvā + api bodhi-satva-caryā-duṣ-karatām api prajñayā + avagāhya + utsahatae eva sakala-duṣkhita-jana-paritrāṇa-dhuram avavoḍhuṃ tena vandana-pūjana-pāpa-deśana-puṇya-anumodana-buddha-adhyeṣaṇa-yācana-bodhi-pariṇāmanaṃ kṛtvā kalyāṇa-mitram abhyetya tad-ukta-anuvādena svayaṃ vā vaktavyaṃ | samanvāhara + ācārya + aham evaṃ nāma + ity uktvā | yathā + ārya-mañjuśrī-buddha-kṣetra-guṇa-vyūha-alaṅ-kāra-sūtre bhagavatā mañjuśriyā pūrva-janma-avadāne caryā-upetaṃ bodhi-cittam utpāditaṃ tathā + utpādayitavyaṃ | evaṃ hi tena + uktaṃ ||
body.translated_text: And this should be examined in the <s>Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha-sūtra</s>. But the great being (<s>mahāsattva</s>) who, having heard even this — the difficulty of the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice — comprehends it with wisdom and is still eager to bear the burden of rescuing all suffering people: by that one, having performed veneration, worship, confession of sins, rejoicing in merit, entreating the <s>Buddhas</s>, supplication, and dedication to awakening — one should approach a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) and, by repeating what that [teacher] says, or by oneself, should declare: 'Be mindful, O teacher! I, named so-and-so...' — thus speaking. Just as in the <s>Ārya-Mañjuśrī-buddhakṣetra-guṇavyūhālaṅkāra-sūtra</s>, the <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening) accompanied by practice was generated by the Blessed <s>Mañjuśrī</s> in his former-life narrative — so should it be generated. For thus it was said by him:

body.text: yāvatī prathamā koṭiḥ saṃsārasya + anta-varjitā | tāvat satva-hita-arthāya cariṣyāmy a-mitāṃ carim ||
body.translated_text: For as many as the first incalculable [aeons] of <s>saṃsāra</s> without end,

body.text: utpādayāma saṃbodhau cittaṃ nāthasya saṃmukham | nimantraye jagat sarvaṃ dāridryān mocitā + asmi tat ||
body.translated_text: I generate the mind toward awakening in the presence of the Protector; I invite the entire world — may I be the one who liberates from poverty!

body.text: vyāpāda-khila-cittaṃ vā īrṣyā-mātsaryam eva vā | adya + agre na kariṣyāmi bodhiṃ prāpsyāmi yāvatā | brahma-caryaṃ cariṣyāmi kāmāṃs tyakṣyāmi pāpakān ||
body.translated_text: A mind of ill-will and rigidity, or envy and miserliness — from this day forth I shall not produce [them], until I attain awakening. I shall practice the holy life; I shall abandon evil desires.

body.text: buddhānām anuśikṣiṣye śīla-saṃvara-saṃyame | na + ahaṃ tvarita-rūpeṇa bodhiṃ prāptum iha + utsahe ||
body.translated_text: I shall train after the <s>Buddhas</s> in the discipline of moral restraint. I am not eager to attain awakening hastily, in this [very life].

body.text: para-anta-koṭiṃ sthāsyāmi satvasya + ekasya kāraṇāt | kṣetraṃ viśodhayiṣyāmi a-prameyam a-cintiyam ||
body.translated_text: I shall remain until the final limit [of <s>saṃsāra</s>], for the sake of even a single being. I shall purify my [Buddha-]field — immeasurable and inconceivable.

body.text: nāma-dheyaṃ kariṣyāmi daśa dikṣu ca viśrutaṃ | kāya-vāk-karmaṇī ca + ahaṃ śodhayiṣyāmi sarvaśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: I shall make my name renowned in the ten directions. And I shall purify my actions of body and speech in every way.

body.text: śodhayiṣye manas-karma karma karttā + asmi na + a-śubham | iti ||
body.translated_text: I shall purify the action of mind; I shall perform no unwholesome action. //

body.text: na ca + atra sārvakālikāt saṃvara-grahaṇāj janma-antara-āpatti-śaṅkā kartavyā + atra + eva sūtre * a-kṣobhya-praṇidhāna-anujñānād evaṃ hy uktaṃ | yathā tena + a-kṣobhyeṇa tathā-gatena pūrvaṃ bodhi-satva-bhūtena + evaṃ vāg bhāṣitā | visaṃvāditā me buddhā bhagavanto bhaveyur yadi sarvasyāṃ jātau na pravrajeyam iti | ekā jātiḥ prayatnena saṃśodhyā vibudha-ātmanā | anyās tu jātīr ā-bodheḥ sa + eva saṃśodhayiṣyati + ity ukteḥ ||
body.translated_text: And here, the apprehension that from taking a vow valid for all time there would be a transgression in another life should not be entertained, since in this very <s>sūtra</s> [there is] the approval of <s>Akṣobhya</s>'s vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>). For thus it is said: 'Just as by that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>, when formerly he was a <s>bodhisattva</s>, this word was spoken: "May the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, be deceived by me if I do not go forth [as a renunciant] in every birth."' [And] because it is said: 'One birth should be purified with effort by the wise-souled one; the other births until awakening — that very one [the Buddha-to-be] will purify.'

body.text: evaṃ śāriputra bodhi-satvena a-kṣobhyasya tathā-gatasya anuśikṣitavyaṃ | evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ śāriputra bodhi-satvo mahā-satvaḥ sarvasyāṃ jātau pravrajaty utpādād vā tathā-gatānām an-utpādād vā + a-vaśyaṃ gṛha-āvāsān niṣkrāmati | tat kasya hetoḥ | paramo hy ayaṃ śāriputra lābho yad uta gṛha-āvāsān niṣkramaṇam iti | yāvat | bhāryā-putra-duhitṛ-tṛṣṇā ca + asya na bhavati + iti | yathā janma-antareṣv ayaṃ doṣo na bhavati tathā + atra + eva vakṣyamāṇam ity āstāṃ tāvad etat ||
body.translated_text: 'Thus, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> should train after [the example of] the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>. <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who trains thus goes forth in every birth, whether there is an arising of <s>Tathāgatas</s> or no arising — he certainly leaves the household life. For what reason? Because this, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the supreme gain — namely, the going forth from the household life.' And so on, up to: 'And he has no craving for wife, son, or daughter.' How this fault does not occur in other births — that will be stated here later; so let this matter rest for now.

body.text: tad evaṃ samātta-saṃvarasya sāmānyam āpatti-lakṣaṇam ucyate | yena + āpatti-lakṣaṇena yuktaṃ vastu svayam apy utprekṣya pariharen na ca + āpatti-pratirūpakeṣv an-āpatti-pratirūpakeṣu ca saṃmuhyeta | bodhi-satvaḥ sarva-satvānāṃ varttamāna-an-āgata-sarva-duṣkha-daurmanasya + upaśamāya varttamāna-an-āgata-sukha-saumanasya + utpādāya ca niḥ-śāṭhyataḥ kāya-vāṅ-manaḥ-parākramaiḥ prayatnaṃ karoti | yadi tu tat-pratyaya-sāmagrīṃ na + anveṣate tad-an-antarāya pratikārāya na ghaṭate alpa-duṣkha-daurmanasyaṃ bahu-duṣkha-daurmanasya-pratikāra-bhūtaṃ na + utpādayati | mahā-artha-siddhy-arthaṃ ca + alpa-artha-hāniṃ na karoti kṣaṇam apy upekṣate | sa-āpattiko bhavati | saṃkṣepato * an-āpattiḥ sva-śakty-a-viśayeṣu kāryeṣu tatra niṣ-phalatayā śikṣyā-prajñapty-a-bhāvāt | prakṛti-sa-avadyatayā tv anyad gṛhyatae eva | yatra sva-śaktya-gocare * api tyāga-sāmarthyād āpattiḥ syāt tan na cintyaṃ | sāmānya-pāpa-deśanā na ... vāt tu tato muktiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus, the general characteristic of transgression for one who has taken up the <s>saṃvara</s> (vow) is stated — by which characteristic of transgression one may, having examined the matter oneself, avoid it, and not be confused regarding things that resemble transgressions or things that resemble non-transgressions. The <s>bodhisattva</s> strives, without deceit, through exertions of body, speech, and mind, for the alleviation of all present and future suffering and mental distress of all beings, and for the production of present and future happiness and mental well-being. But if he does not seek the aggregate of conditions for that, does not endeavor to counteract obstacles to that, does not produce a small suffering and mental distress that would serve as the remedy for a great suffering and mental distress, and does not incur a small loss for the sake of accomplishing a great purpose, [but rather] remains indifferent even for a moment — he incurs a transgression. In brief, non-transgression [obtains] in cases beyond one's own capacity, since there is no prescription of training due to the fruitlessness thereof. But what is naturally blameworthy is grasped [as transgression] in any case. Where, even in matters within the scope of one's capacity, a transgression would occur through the power of renunciation — that is not to be considered [a transgression]. Through the general confession of sins ... liberation therefrom [is obtained].

body.text: etat samāsato bodhi-satva-śikṣā-śarīraṃ | vistaratas tv a-pramāṇa-kalpa-a-paryavasāna-nirdeśaṃ | atha-vā saṃkṣepato dve bodhi-satvasya + āpattī | yathā śakti-yukta-a-yuktam a-samīkṣya + ārabhate | nivṛttaḥ samīkṣate sa-āpattiko bhavati | nirūpya yathā-arham atikrāmaty antaśaś caṇḍāla-dāsena + api coditaḥ sa-āpattiko bhavati | kutaḥ ||
body.translated_text: This is, in brief, the body of the <s>bodhisattva</s> training. In detail, however, it is an instruction that extends through immeasurable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) without end. Or alternatively, in brief, there are two transgressions for a <s>bodhisattva</s>: when, without examining whether [the matter] is or is not commensurate with [his] capacity, he undertakes [an action]; [and when,] having withdrawn, he examines [only afterward] — he incurs a transgression. [When] having properly investigated, he oversteps as appropriate — even when urged by a <s>caṇḍāla</s>-slave — he incurs a transgression. Why?

body.text: etad adhyāśaya-saṃcodana-sūtre vacanāt | api tu maitreya caturbhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ pratibhānaṃ sarva-buddha-bhāṣi ... bhiḥ | iha maitreya pratibhānaṃ satya-upasaṃhitaṃ bhavati | na + a-satya-upasaṃhitaṃ dharma-upasaṃhitaṃ bhavati na a-dharma-upasaṃhitaṃ | kleśa-hāyakaṃ bhavati na kleśa-vivarddhakaṃ | nirvāṇa-guṇa-anuśaṃsa-sandarśakaṃ bhavati na saṃsāra-guṇa-anuśaṃsa-sandarśakaṃ | ebhiś caturbhiḥ peyālaṃ | yasya kasya-cin maitreya ebhiś caturbhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ pratibhānaṃ pratibhāti pratibhāsyati vā | tatra śrāddhaiḥ kula-putraiḥ kula-duhitṛbhir vā buddha-saṃjñā + utpādayitavyā śāstṛ-saṃjñāṃ kṛtvā | sa dharmaḥ śrotavyaḥ | tat kasya hetoḥ | yat kiñ-cin maitreya su-bhāṣitaṃ sarvaṃ tad buddha-bhāṣitaṃ | tatra maitreya ya imāni pratibhānāni pratikṣipen na + etāni buddha-bhāṣitāni + iti | teṣu ca + a-gauravam utpādayet pudgala-vidveṣeṇa tena sarva-buddha-bhāṣitaṃ pratibhānaṃ pratikṣiptaṃ bhavati | dharmaṃ pratikṣipya dharma-vyasana-saṃvartanīyena karmaṇā + apāya-gāmī bhavati ||
body.translated_text: Because of the statement in the <s>Adhyāśayasaṃcodanasūtra</s>: 'Moreover, <s>Maitreya</s>, by four reasons is eloquence ... of all the Buddhas. Here, <s>Maitreya</s>, eloquence is conjoined with truth, not conjoined with untruth; it is conjoined with the <s>Dharma</s>, not conjoined with what is contrary to <s>Dharma</s>; it diminishes the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), it does not increase the <s>kleśas</s>; it shows the benefits and advantages of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, it does not show the benefits and advantages of <s>saṃsāra</s>. By these four — [and so on in] abbreviated [form]. O <s>Maitreya</s>, whosoever's eloquence shines forth or will shine forth by these four reasons — with respect to that, faithful sons of good family or daughters of good family should generate the perception of the <s>Buddha</s>, having adopted the perception of the Teacher. That <s>Dharma</s> should be listened to. For what reason? Whatever is well-spoken, <s>Maitreya</s>, all that is spoken by the <s>Buddha</s>. Now, <s>Maitreya</s>, whoever would reject these [forms of] eloquence, [saying] "These are not spoken by the <s>Buddha</s>," and would generate disrespect toward them out of personal hatred — by that person all eloquence spoken by the <s>Buddha</s> is rejected. Having rejected the <s>Dharma</s>, he goes to a lower realm through an action that conduces to the ruin of the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: yaḥ punar etad abhyāsa-arthaṃ vyutpāditam icchati | tena + atra śikṣā-samuccaye tāvac caryā-mukha-mātra-śikṣaṇa-artham abhiyogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ śikṣā-ārambhasya + eva mahā-phalatvāt | yathā + uktaṃ praśānta-viniścaya-pratihārya-sūtre | yaś ca mañjuśrīr bodhi-satvo gaṅgā-nadī-vālikā-samebhyo buddhebhyaḥ praty-ekaṃ sarvebhyo gaṃgā-nadī-vālikā-samāni buddha-kṣetrāṇi vaśi-rāja-mahā-maṇi-ratna-pratipūrṇāni kṛtvā dahyād evaṃ dadaṅ gaṅgā-nadī-vālikā-samān kalpān dānaṃ dadyād | yo vā + anyo mañjuśrīr bodhisatva imān evaṃ-rūpān dharmān śrutvā eka-antena gatvā cittena + abhinirūpayed imeṣv evaṃ-rūpeṣu dharmeṣu śikṣiṣyāmi + iti | so * a-śikṣito * api mañjuśrīr bodhisatvo * asyāṃ śikṣyāyāṃ chandiko vatataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati | na tv eva tad dānam ayaṃ puṇya-kriyā-vastv iti | tasmād evam anuśaṃsa-darśinā bodhi-satvena na kathaṃ-cin nivarttitavyaṃ | yathā + atra + eva + āha | tatra mañjuśrīr ye tri-sāhasra-mahā-sāhasra-loka-dhātu-parama-aṇu-rajaḥ-samāḥ satva-s teṣām eka-ekaḥ satvo rājā bhavej jambū-dvīpa-adhipatis te sarvae evaṃ ghoṣayeyuḥ | yo mahā-yānam udgrahiṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravarttayiṣyati tasya nakha-chedena māsaṃ pañca-palikena divasena + avatārayiṣyāmaḥ taṃ ca + etena + apakrameṇa jīvitād vyaparopayiṣyāma iti | sacen mañjuśrīr bodhi-satva evam ucyamāno na + u trasyati na saṃtrāsam āpsyate * antaśa eka-citta-utpādena + api na bibheti na viṣīdati na vicikitsate | uttari ca sad-dharmma-parigraha-artham abhiyujyate pāṭha-sva-adhyāya-abhimukto viharati | ayaṃ mañjuśrīr bodhi-satvaś citta-śūro dāna-śūraḥ śīla-śūraḥ kṣānti-śūraḥ vīrya-śūraḥ dhyāna-śūraḥ prajñā-śūraḥ samādhi-śūraḥ iti vaktavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Now, whoever wishes to be instructed for the purpose of practicing this — by him, in this <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>, effort should be made for the purpose of training in merely the entrance to the conduct, since the very commencement of the training is of great fruit. As stated in the <s>Praśāntaviniścayaprātihāryasūtra</s>: 'O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, suppose a <s>bodhisattva</s>, having individually filled <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal in number to the sands of the Ganges River for <s>Buddhas</s> equal in number to the sands of the Ganges River with <s>vaśirāja</s> great <s>maṇi</s>-jewels, were to give thus — giving gifts for <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the sands of the Ganges River. Or suppose another <s>bodhisattva</s>, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, having heard <s>dharmas</s> of such a kind, were to go to a solitary place and reflect in his mind: "I shall train in <s>dharmas</s> of such a kind." That <s>bodhisattva</s>, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, even though untrained, being desirous of this training, produces far more merit. But that gift is not [equal to] this basis of meritorious action.' Therefore, the <s>bodhisattva</s> who sees such benefits should not turn back in any way. As stated in the same [sūtra]: 'Therein, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, suppose beings equal in number to the atoms in the great trichiliocosm — each one of those beings were to become a king, a lord of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> — and they all were to proclaim: "Whoever will take up, hold, recite, master, and propagate the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — him we shall torment by cutting his nails monthly, [reducing him] by five <s>palikas</s> daily, and by this treatment we shall deprive him of life." If, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s>, being spoken to thus, is not terrified, will not be seized by terror, does not fear even by a single arising of thought, does not despair, does not doubt, and further exerts himself for the sake of upholding the true <s>Dharma</s> and dwells intent on recitation and study — this <s>bodhisattva</s>, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is to be called a hero in mind, a hero in giving, a hero in morality, a hero in patience, a hero in vigor, a hero in meditation, a hero in wisdom, a hero in <s>samādhi</s>.'

body.text: sacen mañjuśrīr bodhi-satvaḥ teṣāṃ vadhaka-puruṣāṇāṃ na kupyati na ruṣyati na khila doṣa-cittam utpādayati | sa mañjuśrīr bodhi-satvo brahma-sama indra-samo * a-kampya iti ||
body.translated_text: 'If, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not become angry at those murderous men, does not become wrathful, does not generate even a single thought of hostility or malice — that <s>bodhisattva</s>, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is equal to <s>Brahmā</s>, equal to <s>Indra</s>, unshakable.'

body.text: itaś ca + agrya-kāle śikṣā-ādaro mahā-phala-vipākaḥ | tathā hi candra-pradīpa-sūtre | buddhāna koṭīn a-yutān upasthihe | dattena pānena prasanna-cittaḥ | chatraiḥ patākābhi ca dīpa-mālaiḥ | kalpāna koṭyo yatha gaṅga-vālikāḥ ||
body.translated_text: And furthermore, in the final age, reverence for the training is of great fruit and ripening. For thus [it is stated] in the <s>Candrapradīpasūtra</s>: 'I served <s>koṭis</s> and <s>ayutas</s> (myriads) of <s>Buddhas</s>, with a joyful mind through the gift of drink, with parasols, banners, and garlands of lamps, for <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> like the sands of the Ganges.'

body.text: yaś ca + eva sad-dharme pralujyamāne | nirudhyamāne su-gatasya śāsane | rātriṃ divaṃ eka careya śikṣām | idan tataḥ puṇya-viśiṣṭa bhoti ||
body.translated_text: 'But whoever, when the true <s>Dharma</s> is being destroyed, when the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) is being extinguished, would practice the training alone, day and night — this is more distinguished in merit than that.'

body.text: tasmāt kartavyo * atra + ādaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, reverence should be shown herein.

body.text: uktāni ca sūtra-anteṣu bodhi-satva-śikṣā-padāni | yathā + uktam ārya-ratna-meghe | kathaṃ ca kula-putra bodhi-satvā bodhi-satva-śikṣā-saṃvara-saṃvṛtā bhavanti | iha bodhi-satvaḥ evaṃ vicārayati | na prātimokṣa-saṃvara-mātrakeṇa mayā śakyam an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhim abhisaṃboddhuṃ | kiṃ tarhi yāni + imāni tathā-gatena teṣu teṣu sūtra-anteṣu bodhi-satva-samudācārā | bodhi-satva-śikṣā-padāni prajñaptāni teṣu teṣu mayā śikṣitavyam iti vistaraḥ | tasmād asmad-vidhena manda-buddhinā dur-vijñeyo vistara-uktatvād bodhi-satvasya saṃvaraḥ | tataḥ kiṃ yuktaṃ ||
body.translated_text: And the <s>bodhisattva</s> training-rules have been stated in the <s>sūtrāntas</s>. As stated in the <s>Ārya-Ratnamegha</s> (Noble Cloud of Jewels): 'And how, O son of good family, are <s>bodhisattvas</s> endowed with the <s>bodhisattva</s> training-vow? Here the <s>bodhisattva</s> reflects thus: "By the <s>prātimokṣa</s> vow alone I cannot attain supreme, perfect <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). Rather, whatever <s>bodhisattva</s> conducts and <s>bodhisattva</s> training-rules have been prescribed by the <s>Tathāgata</s> in the various <s>sūtrāntas</s> — in those I must train" — and so forth in detail.' Therefore, for one of dull intellect such as myself, the <s>bodhisattva</s> vow is difficult to understand because it has been stated in detail. What then is appropriate?

body.text: marma-sthānāny ato vidyād yena + an-āpattiko bhavet ||
body.translated_text: One should therefore know the vital points (<s>marmasthānas</s>), by which one would become free from transgression.

body.text: katamāni ca tāni marma-sthānāni yāni hi sūtra-anteṣu mahā-yāna-abhiratānām arthāya + uktāni | yad uta | ātma-bhāvasya bhogānāṃ try-adhva-vṛtteḥ śubhasya ca | utsargaḥ sarva-satvebhyas tad-rakṣā śuddhi-vardhanam ||
body.translated_text: And what are those vital points that have been stated in the <s>sūtrāntas</s> for the benefit of those devoted to the <s>Mahāyāna</s>? Namely: 'The relinquishment of one's own body, enjoyments, and merit accumulated over the three times to all beings; the protection of that [which has been given]; purification; and increase.'

body.text: eṣa bodhi-satva-saṃvara-saṃgrahaḥ | yatra bodhi-satvānām abhyāsa-viśrāme * apy āpattayo vyavasthāpyante ||
body.translated_text: This is the summary of the <s>bodhisattva</s> vow, wherein transgressions are established for <s>bodhisattvas</s> even in [periods of] rest from practice.

body.text: yathā + uktaṃ bodhi-satva-prātimokṣe | yo bodhi-satvena mārgaḥ parigṛhītaḥ sarva-satvānāṃ kṛtena duṣkham upagāmī | saced bodhi-satvasya taṃ mārgaṃ parigṛhya + avasthitasya + api kalpa-koṭer atyayena + ekaṃ sukha-cittam utpadyeta + antaśo niṣadya cittam api | tatra bodhi-satvena + evaṃ cittam utpādayitavyaṃ sarva-satvānām ātyayikaṃ parigṛhya + etad api me varjayan niṣīdāmi + iti | parigṛhyet tam
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Bodhisattvaprātimokṣa</s>: 'Whatever path has been undertaken by the <s>bodhisattva</s> — by which, having acted for all beings, he undergoes suffering — if, for the <s>bodhisattva</s> who has undertaken and abides in that path, even after the passing of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, a single thought of ease were to arise, even the thought of sitting down — therein the <s>bodhisattva</s> should generate the thought: "Having undertaken the urgent [duty] for all beings, even this [rest] I abandon and sit down." He should undertake that [path]...'

body.text: pañca + imāni deva-putra + ānantaryāṇi yair ānantaryaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhi-satvāḥ kṣipram an-uttarā-samyak-saṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyate | katamāni pañca | yadā deva-putra bodhi-satvo * adhyāśayaty an-uttarāyāṃ samyak-saṃbodhau cittam utpādya na + antarā śravaka-praty-eka-buddha-bhūmau cittam utpādayati + idaṃ deva-putra prathamam ānantaryaṃ | sarvasva-parityāgitāyāṃ cittam utpādya na + antarā mātsarya-cittena sārddhaṃ sa nyasati + idaṃ deva-putra dvitīyam ānantaryam | sarva-satvā mayā trātavyā ity evaṃ cittam utpādya na + antarā sīdati + idaṃ deva-putra tṛtīyam ānantaryam | an-utpanna-a-niruddhān sarva-dharmān avabhotsyae ity evaṃ cittam utpādya na + antarā dṛṣṭi-gateṣu prapatati + idaṃ deva-putra caturtham ānantaryam | eka-kṣaṇa-samāyuktayā prajñayā sarva-dharmān avabhotsyae ity evaṃ cittam utpādya na + antarā tiṣṭhati na viṣṭhīvati a-prāptāyāṃ sarva-jñatāyām idaṃ deva-putra pañcamam ānantaryam iti ||
body.translated_text: 'There are these five <s>ānantaryas</s> (immediacies), O son of the gods (<s>devaputra</s>), possessing which <s>bodhisattvas</s> quickly attain supreme, perfect <s>bodhi</s>. What are the five? When, O son of the gods, a <s>bodhisattva</s>, having generated the aspiration toward supreme, perfect <s>bodhi</s>, does not in the interim generate the thought [of attaining] the <s>Śrāvaka</s> or <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> stage — this, O son of the gods, is the first immediacy. Having generated the thought of relinquishing all possessions, he does not in the interim associate with a thought of avarice — this, O son of the gods, is the second immediacy. Having generated the thought "All beings must be rescued by me," he does not in the interim become discouraged — this, O son of the gods, is the third immediacy. Having generated the thought "I shall comprehend all <s>dharmas</s> as unarisen and unceased," he does not in the interim fall into [wrong] views — this, O son of the gods, is the fourth immediacy. Having generated the thought "I shall comprehend all <s>dharmas</s> with wisdom united in a single moment," he does not in the interim stop or spit out [the effort] before attaining omniscience — this, O son of the gods, is the fifth immediacy.'

body.text: tasmād evam ātma-bhāva-bhoga-puṇyānām a-viratam utsarga-rakṣā-śuddhi-vṛddhayo yathā-yogaṃ bhāvanīyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, the relinquishment, protection, purification, and increase of one's own body, enjoyments, and merit should be cultivated unceasingly, each as appropriate.

body.text: tatra tāvad utsarga-arthaṃ parigraha-doṣa-bhāvanā-dvāreṇa vairāgyam utpādayet tyāga-anuśaṃsāṃś ca bhāvayet | yathā tāvac candra-pradīpa-sūtre | adhyavasitā ye bālāḥ kāye * asmin pūtike samyag | jīvite cañcale * a-vaśye māyā-svapna-nibhā-upame ||
body.translated_text: Therein, first, for the purpose of relinquishment, one should generate dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) through the door of contemplating the faults of possessiveness, and one should cultivate [awareness of] the benefits of giving. As stated in the <s>Candrapradīpasūtra</s>: 'Those foolish ones who are thoroughly attached to this putrid body, to this unsteady, uncontrollable life, which is like an illusion, like a dream —'

body.text: ati-raudrāṇi karmāṇi kṛtvā moha-vaśa-anugāḥ | te yānti narakān ghorān mṛtyu-yāna-gata-a-budhā | iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Having performed exceedingly terrible deeds, following the power of delusion, those unwise ones, riding the vehicle of death, go to terrible hells.'

body.text: tathā + an-anta-mukha-nirhāra-dhāraṇyām uktaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, it is stated in the <s>Anantamukhanihāradhāraṇī</s>:

body.text: ye ke-cit satvā na bhavanti vigrahāḥ parigrahas tatra nidāna-mūlam | tasmāt tyajed yatra bhavet tṛṣṇā | utsṛṣṭa-tṛṣṇasya hi dhāraṇī bhavet ||
body.translated_text: 'Whatever beings do not become embodied — possessiveness is the root-cause thereof. Therefore one should abandon [that] where craving would arise. For one who has relinquished craving, there will be <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention).'

body.text: bodhi-satva-prātimokṣe kathitaṃ | punar a-paraṃ śāriputra bodhi-satvaḥ sarva-dharmeṣu parakīya-saṃjñām utpādayati | na kañ-cid bhāvam upādatte | tat kasya hetoḥ | upādānaṃ hi bhayam iti ||
body.translated_text: It is stated in the <s>Bodhisattvaprātimokṣa</s>: 'Furthermore, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> generates the perception that all <s>dharmas</s> belong to another. He does not cling to any entity. For what reason? Because clinging is indeed fear.'

body.text: ārya-ugradatta-paripṛcchāyām apy āha | yad dattaṃ tan na bhūyo rakṣitavyaṃ | yad gṛhe tad rakṣitavyaṃ | yad dattaṃ tat tṛṣnā-kṣayāya | yad gṛhe tat tṛṣṇā-varddhanaṃ | yad dattaṃ tad a-parigrahaṃ yad gṛhe tat sa-parigrahaṃ | yad dattaṃ tad a-bhayaṃ yad gṛhe tat sa-bhayam | yad dattaṃ tad bodhi-mārga-upastambhāya | yad gṛhe tan māra-upastambhāya | yad dattaṃ tad a-kṣayam | yad gṛhe tat kṣayi | yad dattaṃ tataḥ sukham yad gṛhe tad-ārabhya duṣkhaṃ | yad dattaṃ tat kleśa-utsargāya | yad gṛhe tat kleśa-varddhanam | yad dattaṃ tan mahā-bhogatāyai | yad gṛhe na tan mahā-bhogatāyai | yad dattaṃ tat sat-puruṣa-karma | yad gṛhe tat kā-puruṣa-karma | yad dattaṃ tat sat-puruṣa-citta-grahaṇāya | yad gṛhe tat kā-puruṣa-citta-grahaṇāya | yad dattaṃ tat sarva-buddha-praśastaṃ | yad gṛhe tad bāla-jana-praśastam ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Ugradattaparipṛcchā</s> it is also said: What is given need not be guarded again; what remains in the house must be guarded. What is given leads to the exhaustion of craving; what remains in the house increases craving. What is given is without attachment; what remains in the house is with attachment. What is given is without fear; what remains in the house is with fear. What is given supports the path to awakening; what remains in the house supports <s>Māra</s>. What is given is imperishable; what remains in the house is perishable. What is given brings happiness; what remains in the house brings suffering. What is given is for the abandonment of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions); what remains in the house increases <s>kleśas</s>. What is given leads to great wealth; what remains in the house does not lead to great wealth. What is given is the deed of a good person; what remains in the house is the deed of a base person. What is given captures the minds of good people; what remains in the house captures the minds of base people. What is given is praised by all <s>Buddhas</s>; what remains in the house is praised by the foolish.

body.text: yāvat sacet punar asya putre * atiriktataraṃ prema + utpadyate tathā + anyeṣu satveṣu tena tisṛbhiḥ paribhāṣaṇābhiḥ sva-cittaṃ paribhāṣitavyaṃ | katamābhis tisṛbhiḥ | samyak-prayuktasya sama-cittasya bodhi-satvasya bodhir na viṣama-cittasya bodhir na mithyā-prayuktasya | a-nānātva-cāriṇo bodhi-satvasya bodhir na nānātva-cāriṇaḥ | ābhis tisṛbhiḥ paribhāṣaṇābhiḥ sva-cittaṃ paribhāṣya + anyatre * a-mitra-saṃjñā + utpādayitavyā + a-mitraṃ hy etan mama | na maitraṃ | yo * aham asya + arthāya buddha-prajñaptā-śikṣāyā uddhuratād gatvā + asmin putre * atiriktataraṃ prema + utpādayāmi | na tathā + anyeṣu satveṣu | tena tathā tathā cittam utpādayitavyaṃ yathā yathā + asya sarva-satveṣu putra-prema-anugatā maitry utpadyate | ātma-kṣema-anu ... maitry utpadyate | evaṃ ca + anena yoniśaḥ pratyavekṣitavyaṃ | anyata eṣa āgata | anyato * ahaṃ | sarva-satvā api mama putrā abhūvan | ahaṃ ca sarva-satvānāṃ putro * abhūvam | na + iha saṃvidyate kaś-cit kasya-cit ... paro vā | yāvad evaṃ hi gṛha-pate | gṛhiṇā bodhi-satvena na kasmiṃś-cid vastuni mamatvaṃ parigraho vā kartavyaḥ | na + adhyavasānaṃ | na niyatiḥ na tṛṣṇā-anuśayaḥ kartavyaḥ | sacet punar gṛha-pate gṛhiṇaṃ bodhi-satvaṃ yācanaka upasaṃkramya kiñ-cid eva vastu yāceta | saced asya vastv a-parityaktaṃ bhavet | na + evaṃ cittaṃ nidhyāpayitavyaṃ | yady aham etad vastu parityajeyaṃ yadi vā na parityajeyam a-vaśyaṃ mama + etena vastunā vinā-bhāvo bhaviṣyati | a-kāmakena maraṇam upagantavyaṃ bhaviṣyati | etac ca vastu māṃ tyakṣyati ahaṃ ca + enaṃ tyakṣyāmi | etac ca vastu parityajya + ahaṃ ātta-sāraḥ kālaṃ kariṣyāmi etac ca parityaktaṃ na me maraṇa-kāle cittaṃ paryādāya sthāsyati | etac ca me maraṇa-kāle prītiṃ prāmodyam a-vipratisāritāṃ ca janayiṣyati | sacet punar evam api samanvāharan śaknuyāt tad vastu parityaktum | tena sa yācanakaś catasṛbhiḥ saṃjñaptibhiḥ saṃjñapayitavyaḥ | katamābhiś catasṛbhiḥ | dur-balas tāvad asmy a-paripakva-kuśala-mūlaḥ | ādi-karmiko mahā-yāne | na cittasya vaśī parityāgāya
