| sa-upādāna-dṛṣṭiko * asmi | ahaṃ-kāra-mama-kāra-sthitaḥ | kṣamasva sat-puruṣa | mā paritāpsīs tathā + ahaṃ kariṣyāmi tathā pratipatsye | tathā vīryam ārapsye | yathā + enaṃ ca tava + abhiprāyaṃ paripūrayiṣyāmi sarva-satvānāṃ ca + iti | evaṃ khalu gṛha-pate | tena yācanakaḥ saṃjñapayitavyaḥ | etac ca saṃjñapanam upari doṣa-parihārāya + uktaṃ | mā bhūd bodhi-satvasya tatra a-prasādo bodhi-satve vā yācanakasya + iti | na tu mātsaryam evaṃ an-avadyaṃ bhavati kutsitaṃ ca + idaṃ bhagavatā bodhi-satvānāṃ ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, if excessive love arises in him toward his son but not equally toward other sentient beings, he should reproach his own mind with three reproaches. Which three? Awakening belongs to a <s>bodhisattva</s> who is rightly engaged and even-minded, not to one who is uneven-minded, not to one who is wrongly engaged. Awakening belongs to a <s>bodhisattva</s> who does not practice partiality, not to one who practices partiality. Having reproached his own mind with these three reproaches, he should generate the perception of enmity elsewhere: "This is indeed my enemy, not my friend, that I, departing from the training prescribed by the <s>Buddha</s>, generate excessive love for this son but not equally for other sentient beings." He should generate such a state of mind that loving-kindness arises in him toward all sentient beings, accompanied by love as for a son, accompanied by concern for their welfare. And he should wisely reflect thus: "He has come from elsewhere; I have come from elsewhere. All sentient beings have been my sons; I have been the son of all sentient beings. Here no one is anyone's... nor anyone else's." Furthermore: "Thus indeed, householder, a householder <s>bodhisattva</s> should not create possessiveness or attachment toward any thing — no clinging, no fixation, no latent tendency of craving." If, however, a petitioner approaches a householder <s>bodhisattva</s> and asks for some thing, and if that thing has not yet been relinquished by him, he should reflect thus: "Whether I relinquish this thing or not, separation from this thing will inevitably come for me. Death must be faced unwillingly. This thing will leave me and I will leave it. Having relinquished this thing, I will die having extracted its essence. This relinquished thing will not overwhelm my mind at the time of death. This will generate joy, gladness, and freedom from regret for me at the time of death." If, however, even reflecting thus he is unable to relinquish that thing, then he should placate the petitioner with four explanations. Which four? "I am still weak, with unripened roots of virtue. I am a beginner in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. I have not gained mastery over my mind for relinquishment. I am one with views of grasping, established in egotism and possessiveness. Forgive me, O good person. Do not be distressed. I will act in such a way, I will practice in such a way, I will exert effort in such a way, that I will fulfill both your wish and that of all sentient beings." Thus indeed, householder, the petitioner should be placated. And this placation is stated for the avoidance of fault in the future — lest the <s>bodhisattva</s> lose faith in a <s>bodhisattva</s>, or the petitioner [lose faith]. But miserliness is not thereby rendered blameless, for it is condemned by the <s>Bhagavan</s> (Lord) for <s>bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: yathā + āha bodhi-satva-prātimokṣe | catvāra ime śāriputra dharmā bodhi-satvānāṃ na saṃvidyante | katame catvāraḥ | śāṭhyaṃ bodhi-satvānāṃ na saṃvidyate | mātsaryaṃ bodhi-satvānāṃ na saṃvidyate | īrṣyā-paiśunyaṃ bodhi-satvānāṃ na saṃvidyate | na + ahaṃ śakto * an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhim abhisaṃboddhum iti | līnaṃ cittaṃ bodhi-satvānāṃ na saṃvidyate | yasya + ime śāriputra catvāro dharmāḥ saṃvidyante sa paṇḍita.ir jñātavyaḥ | kuhako vata + ayaṃ | lapako vata + ayaṃ | naṣṭa-dharmo vata + ayaṃ | saṃkleśa-dharmo vata + ayaṃ loka-āmiṣa-guruko vata + ayaṃ bhakta-coḍaka-paramo vata + ayam iti | tathā citta-śūrāḥ khalu punaḥ śāriputra bodhi-satvā bhavanti | yāvat sva-hasta-parityāgī bhavati pāda-parityāgī | nāsā-parityāgī | śīrṣa-parityāgī | aṅga-praty-aṅga-parityāgī | putra-parityāgī | duhitṛ-parityāgī | bhāryā-parityāgī | rati-parityāgī | parivāra-parityāgī | citta-parityāgī | sukha-parityāgī | gṛha-parityāgī | vastu-parityāgī | deśa-parityāgī ratna-parityāgī | sarvasva-parityāgī + iti ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Bodhisattvaprātimokṣa</s>: "These four <s>dharmas</s>, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, are not found in <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Which four? Deceit is not found in <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Miserliness is not found in <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Envy and slander are not found in <s>bodhisattvas</s>. The thought 'I am unable to attain supreme perfect awakening' — such a dejected mind is not found in <s>bodhisattvas</s>." "Whoever, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, possesses these four <s>dharmas</s> should be known by the wise as: 'This one is indeed a deceiver! This one is indeed a prattler! This one has indeed lost the <s>Dharma</s>! This one is indeed of a defiling nature! This one indeed values worldly gains! This one is indeed concerned only with food and clothing!'" "Furthermore, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, are indeed heroes of the mind — to the extent that one relinquishes one's own hands, relinquishes one's feet, relinquishes one's nose, relinquishes one's head, relinquishes one's limbs and secondary limbs, relinquishes one's sons, relinquishes one's daughters, relinquishes one's wife, relinquishes one's pleasures, relinquishes one's retinue, relinquishes one's mind, relinquishes one's happiness, relinquishes one's home, relinquishes one's possessions, relinquishes one's country, relinquishes one's jewels, relinquishes one's everything."

body.text: evaṃ nārāyaṇa-paripṛcchāyām apy uktaṃ | na tad vastu + upādātavyaṃ yasmin vastuni na + asya tyāga-cittam utpadyate | na tyāga-buddhiḥ krameta | na sa parigrahaḥ parigrahītavyo yasmin parigrahe na + utsarjana-cittam utpādayen na sa parivāra upādātavyo yasmin yācanakair yācyamānasya parigraha-buddhir utpadyate | na tad rājyam upādātavyaṃ na te bhogā na tad ratnam upādātavyaṃ yāvan na tat kiñ-cid vastu + upādātavyaṃ | yasmin vastuni bodhi-satvasya + a-parityāga-buddhir utpadyate ||
body.translated_text: Thus it is also said in the <s>Nārāyaṇaparipṛcchā</s>: "One should not take up that thing toward which the thought of relinquishment does not arise, toward which the intention of giving does not proceed. One should not take up that possession toward which one would not generate the thought of releasing. One should not take up that retinue toward which, when petitioners ask, the thought of possessiveness arises. One should not take up that kingdom, those enjoyments, those jewels — indeed, one should not take up any thing whatsoever toward which the thought of non-relinquishment arises in a <s>bodhisattva</s>."

body.text: api tu khalu punaḥ kula-putra bodhi-satvena mahā-satvena + evaṃ cittam utpādayitavyaṃ | ayaṃ mama + ātma-bhāvaḥ sarva-satvebhyaḥ parityaktaḥ utsṛṣṭaḥ | prāg eva bāhyāni vastūni yasya yasya satvasya yena yena yad yat kāryaṃ bhaviṣyati tasmai tasmai tad dāsyāmi sat-saṃvidyamānaṃ hastaṃ hasta-arthikebhyo dāsyāmi pādaṃ pāda-arthikebhyo netraṃ netra-arthikebhyo dāsyāmi | māṃsaṃ māṃsa-arthikebhyaḥ śoṇitaṃ śoṇita-arthikebhyo majjānaṃ majjā-arthikebhyo * aṅga-praty-aṅgāny aṅga-praty-aṅga-arthikebhyaḥ śiraḥ śiro-rthikebhyaḥ parityakṣyāmi | kaḥ punar vādo bāhyeṣu vastuṣu yad uta dhana-dhānya-jāta-rūpa-rajata-ratna-ābharaṇa-haya-gaja-ratha-vāhana-grāma-nagara-nigama-jana-pada-rāṣṭra-rāja-dhānī-pattana-dāsī-dāsa-karma-kara-pauruṣeya-putra-duhitṛ-parivāreṣu | api tu khalu punar yasya yasya yena yena yad yat kāryaṃ bhaviṣyati tasmai tasmai satvāya tat tad deyaṃ saṃvidyamānaṃ dāsyāmi | a-śocann a-vipratisārī a-vipāka-pratikāṅkṣī parityakṣyāmi | an-apekṣo dāsyāmi satva-anugrahāya satva-kāruṇyena satva-anukampayā teṣām eva satvānāṃ saṃgrahāya | yathā me * amī satvāḥ saṃgṛhītā bodhi-prāptasya dharma-jānakāḥ syur iti | peyālaṃ ||
body.translated_text: "Moreover, O son of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> (great being) should generate the following thought: 'This body of mine has been given up and abandoned for all sentient beings — how much more so external things! For whatever sentient being, for whatever purpose, whatever is needed — I will give it to each one, if it is available. I will give my hand to those who need a hand, my foot to those who need a foot, my eye to those who need an eye. I will give my flesh to those who need flesh, my blood to those who need blood, my marrow to those who need marrow, my limbs and secondary limbs to those who need limbs, my head to those who need a head.' What need to speak of external things, such as wealth, grain, gold, silver, jewels, ornaments, horses, elephants, chariots, vehicles, villages, cities, towns, provinces, kingdoms, capitals, ports, female and male servants, workers, attendants, sons, daughters, and retinue? Moreover, whatever any sentient being needs for any purpose — I will give it to that sentient being if available, without sorrow, without regret, without expectation of result. I will relinquish it without concern, for the benefit of sentient beings, out of compassion for sentient beings, out of sympathy for sentient beings, for their very gathering together, so that when I have attained awakening, these sentient beings may become knowers of the <s>Dharma</s>." And so forth.

body.text: tad yathā + api nāma kula-putra bhaiṣajya-vṛkṣasya mūlato vā hriyamāṇasya gaṇḍataḥ śākhātaḥ tvaktaḥ patrato vā hriyamāṇasya puṣpataḥ phalataḥ sārato vā hriyamāṇasya na + evaṃ bhavati vikalpo | mūlato me hriyate yāvat sārato me hriyatae iti ||
body.translated_text: "Just as, O son of good family, when a medicinal tree is taken from — whether from its root, from its trunk, from its branches, from its bark, from its leaves, from its flowers, from its fruit, or from its heartwood — it does not have the discriminating thought: 'It is being taken from my root' ... 'It is being taken from my heartwood.'"

body.text: api tu khalu punar a-vikalpa eva hīna-madhya-utkṛṣṭānāṃ satvānāṃ vyādhīn apanayati | evam eva kula-putra bodhi-satvena mahā-satvena + asmiṃś cāturmahābhautike ātma-bhāve bhaiṣajya-saṃjñā + utpādayitavyā yeṣāṃ yeṣāṃ satvānāṃ yena yena + arthaḥ tat tad eva me harantu hastaṃ hasta-arthinaḥ pādaṃ pāda-arthina iti pūrva-vat ||
body.translated_text: "Rather, without any discrimination, it removes the illnesses of sentient beings whether low, middling, or superior. Just so, O son of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> should generate in this body composed of the four great elements the perception of being a medicinal tree: 'For whatever sentient beings need whatever — let them take that very thing from me: a hand for those who need a hand, a foot for those who need a foot' — as before."

body.text: ārya-akṣayamati-sūtre * api deśitaṃ | ayam eva mayā kāyaḥ sarva-satvānāṃ kiṃ-karaṇīyeṣu kṣapayitavyaḥ | tad yathā + api nāma + imāni bāhyāni catvāri mahā-bhūtāni pṛthivī-dhātur ab-dhātus tejo-dhātur vāyu-dhātuś ca nānā-sukhair nānā-paryāyair nānā-ārambaṇair nānā-upakaraṇair nānā-paribhogaiḥ satvānāṃ nānā-upabhogaṃ gacchanti | evam eva + aham imaṃ kāyaṃ catur-mahā-bhūta-samucchrayaṃ nānā-sukhair nānā-paryāyair nānā-ārambaṇair nānā-upakaraṇair nānā-paribhogair vistareṇa sarva-satvānām upabhogyaṃ kariṣyāmi + iti | sa imam artha-vaśaṃ saṃpaśyan kāya-duṣkhatāṃ ca pratyavekṣate kāya-duṣkhatayā ca na parikhidyate satva-avekṣayā + iti ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Akṣayamati-sūtra</s> it is also taught: "This very body of mine is to be worn out in service to all sentient beings. Just as these external four great elements — the earth element, the water element, the fire element, and the wind element — are enjoyed by sentient beings in various ways of happiness, various modes, various undertakings, various instruments, and various uses — just so, I will make this body, which is an assemblage of the four great elements, available for the enjoyment of all sentient beings in various ways of happiness, various modes, various undertakings, various instruments, and various uses, extensively." Seeing this purpose, he contemplates the suffering nature of the body, and through contemplating the suffering nature of the body, he does not become weary, out of concern for sentient beings.

body.text: ārya-vajra-dhvaja-sūtre * apy āha ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Vajradhvaja-sūtra</s> it is also said:

body.text: iti hi bodhi-satva ātmānaṃ sarva-satveṣu niryātayan sarva-kuśala-mūla-upakāritvena sarva-satvānāṃ kuśala-mūlaiḥ samanvāharan pradīpa-samam ātmānaṃ sarva-satveṣu + upanayan sukha-samam ātmānaṃ sarva-satveṣv adhitiṣṭhan | dharma-kukṣi-samam ātmānaṃ sarva-jagati saṃdhārayan āloka-samam ātmānaṃ sarva-satveṣv anugacchan jagat-pratiṣṭhāpana-samam ātmānaṃ saṃpaśyan | kuśala-mūla-pratyaya-bhūtam ātmānaṃ sarva-jagaty anugacchan | mitra-samam ātmānaṃ sarva-satveṣu niyojayamāno * an-uttara-sukha-mārga-samam ātmānaṃ sarva-satveṣu saṃdarśayamānaḥ an-uttara-sukha-upadhāna-samam ātmānaṃ sarva-satveṣu pariśodhamānaḥ sūrya-samam ātmānaṃ sarva-jagati samī-kurvāṇaḥ | evaṃ-dharma-upetam ātmānaṃ sarva-satveṣu prayacchan | yathā-kāma-karaṇīya-vaśyam ātmānaṃ sarva-loke saṃpaśyann agra-caityā bhaviṣyāmaḥ ... sarva-jagat-sthity-ātmānaṃ saṃpaśyan | sama-cittatāṃ sarva-jagati niṣpādayan | sarva-upakaraṇa-tīrtham ātmānaṃ saṃpaśyan | sarva-loka-sukha-dātāram ātmānaṃ pratyavekṣamāṇaḥ | sarva-jagato dāna-patim ātmānam adhimucyamānaḥ sarva-loka-jñāna-samam ātmānaṃ kurvāṇaḥ bodhi-satva-caryā-prayuktam ātmānaṃ saṃjanayamānaḥ | yathā-vādi-tathā-kāritvena + ātmānaṃ niyojayamānaḥ | sarva-jñatā-sannāha-sannadham ātmānaṃ pratyavekṣamāṇaḥ | pūrva-nimantritaṃ cittam anupālayamānaḥ | pratipattau ca + ātmānaṃ sthāpayamāno bodhi-satva-tyāga-cittatāṃ manasi kurvāṇa udyāna-bhūtam ātmānaṃ sarva-satveṣu saṃpaśyan | dharma-rati-bhūtam ātmānaṃ sarva-lokeṣv ādarśayamānaḥ saumanasya-dātāram ātmānaṃ sarva-satvānām adhitiṣṭhan | an-anta-prīti-saṃjananam ātmānaṃ sarva-jagato niryātayamānaḥ sarva-śukla-dharmāya dvāra-bhūtam ātmānaṃ sarva-loke saṃdhārayamānaḥ | buddha-bodhi-dātāram ātmānaṃ sarva-satvānāṃ praṇidadhat | pitṛ-samam ātmānaṃ sarva-prajāyāṃ niyojayamānaḥ | sarva-upakaraṇa-a-vaikalya-adhikaraṇam ātmānaṃ sarva-satva-dhātau pratiṣṭhāpayamānaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus indeed the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, devoting himself to all beings, bringing benefit through all <s>kuśalamūla</s> (wholesome roots), furnishing all beings with <s>kuśalamūla</s> (wholesome roots), offering himself to all beings as equal to a lamp, establishing himself among all beings as equal to happiness, sustaining himself in all the world as equal to the womb of the <s>Dharma</s>, following all beings as one equal to light, seeing himself as equal to the establishment of the world, | following all beings in the world as the ground of the condition for <s>kuśalamūla</s> (wholesome roots), | employing himself among all beings as equal to a friend, showing himself to all beings as equal to the path of unsurpassed happiness, purifying himself among all beings as equal to the source of unsurpassed happiness, making himself equal to the sun in all the world, | giving himself, endowed with such qualities, to all beings, | seeing himself in all the world as one to be used freely as desired — "We shall become foremost shrines" ... seeing himself as the support of all the world, bringing about equal-mindedness toward all the world, seeing himself as a ford of all requisites, regarding himself as the giver of happiness to all the world, | resolving upon himself as the lord of <s>dāna</s> (giving) for all the world, making himself equal to the knowledge of all the world, generating himself as engaged in <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct, | employing himself to act as he speaks, | regarding himself as armored with the armor of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), | guarding the mind that was previously invited, | and establishing himself in practice, contemplating the mind of <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>tyāga</s> (renunciation), seeing himself as a garden for all beings, | showing himself as a ground of delight in the <s>Dharma</s> in all worlds, establishing himself as the giver of joy for all beings, | offering himself as the generator of infinite delight for all the world, sustaining himself in all the world as a gateway to all wholesome dharmas, | dedicating himself as the bestower of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>bodhi</s> (awakening) for all beings, | employing himself among all progeny as equal to a father, | establishing himself in the entire realm of beings as the basis for the completeness of all requisites. ||

body.text: iti hi bodhi-satva ātmānam upasthāyakatvāya dadānaḥ yācanakeṣu nīca-manasi-kāra-citto bhūmya-āstaraṇa-adhiṣṭhāna-cetā dharaṇi-sama-sarva-duṣkha-sahana-manasi-kāra-pravṛttaḥ sarva-satva-upasthāna-a-klānta-mānasa-prayukto bāla-jana-duṣ-kṛta-sthiraḥ sthāvara-adhivāsana-jātyaḥ asthitaḥ kuśala-mūla-abhiyuktaḥ a-prayukta-sarva-loka-dhātu-upasthānaḥ karṇo nāsā saṃparityajan yācanakebhya upasaṃkrāntebhyo bodhi-satva-caryā-upātta-tathā-gata-kula-kulīna-saṃbhūta-cittaḥ sarva-bodhi-satva-anusmaraṇa-vihāra-prasṛto * a-sārāt sarva-trailokyāt sa ... tyavekṣamāṇaḥ sva-śarīra-an-adhyavasita-santānaḥ a-niketa-sarva-buddha-dharma-anusmṛti-vihāry a-sārāc * charīrāt sāra-ādāna-abhiprāya iti hi bodhi-satvo jihvāṃ yācitaḥ samāno ma ... vātā premaṇīyayā maitryā-upacāra-vitatayā bhadre siṃha-āsane rāja-arhe niṣādya taṃ yācanakam abhibhāṣate dṛṣṭaḥ | a-riṣṭa-citto bhūtvā + a-kṣata-citto * an-upahata-citto mahā-ātman salā ... citto buddha-vaṃśa-saṃbhūta-citto * a-lulita-santāna-citto mahā-sthāma-bala-ādhāno * an-adhyavasita-śarīra-citto * an-abhiniviṣṭa-vacana-citto jānu-maṇḍala-praṣṭhita-kāyo bhūtvā svakān mukhāj jihvā ... yācanakasya sarva-śarīram a-dhīnaṃ kṛtvā vācaṃ pramuñcan snigdhāṃ mṛdvīṃ premaṇīyāṃ maitryā-upacārāṃ | gṛhāṇa tvaṃ mama jihvāṃ yathā kāma-karaṇīyāṃ kuru | tathā kuru yathā tvaṃ prīto bhavasi prīta-mānasa ātmanā pramudito hṛṣṭaḥ prīti-saumanasya-jāta iti sa śiraḥ parityajan sarva-dharma-agra-śiraḥ parama-jñānam avataran sarva-satva-paritrāṇa-śiro-bodhi ... gacchan sarva-jagad-agrya-śiraḥ an-upama-jñānam abhilaṣan sarva-dik-chiraḥ prāptuṃ jñāna-rājam adhimucyamāno * an-uttara-sarva-dharma-aiśvarya-śīrṣatāṃ paripūrayitu-kāmo * an-anta-yācanaka-prīti-parisphuṭa-cetā | iti hi bodhi-satvo hasta-pādān parityajan yācanakebhyaḥ śraddhā-hasta-prayuktena + anugraha-cāritreṇa bodhi-satva-siṃha-vikrama-tyāga-pratata-pāṇinā vyavasarga-abhiratena hasta-pāda-parityāgena mahā-pratiṣṭhāna-krama-tala-vyatihāreṇa bodhi-satva-caryā-adhyavasāyena vedanā-an-upahatatayā dāna-prasāda-śaktyā vi-mala-citta-utpāda-saṃvaro niṣ-paryavasthāna-jñāna-dharma-śarīra-a-chinna-a-bhinna-a-lupta-kāya-saṃjñaḥ a-nīca-cittaḥ sarva-māra-karma-a-kalyāṇa-mitra-upastabdha-vṛṃhita-cetāḥ sarva-bodhi-satva-saṃvarṇita-eka-tyāga-niryāṇa iti hi bodhi-satvaḥ sva-śarīram ākṣipya rudhiram anuprayacchan yācanakebhyaḥ praharṣita-bodhi-citto | bodhi-satva-caryā-abhilaṣita-citto * a-paryātta-vedita-cittaḥ sarva-yācanaka-abhilaṣita-cittaḥ sarva-pratigrāhaka-a-vidviṣṭa-cittaḥ sarva-bodhi-satva-tyāga-pratipat-pratipanno * a-nivarttyayā prīti-prasrabdhyā sva-śarīra-an-apekṣa-cittaḥ sva-śarīrād rudhiram anuprayacchan jñāna-āyatana-mahā-yāna-prasṛta-cetā mahā-yāna-a-vinaṣṭa-manā iṣṭa-manās tuṣṭa-manāḥ prīta-manāḥ mudita-manā maitry--manāḥ sukha-manāḥ prasanna-manāḥ pramudita-prīti-saumanasya-jāto majjā-māṃsaṃ sva-śarīrāt parityajan yācanakebhyaḥ kalyāṇa-tyāgayā | yācaka-abhilaṣitayā vācā tān yācakān abhilapan | gṛhṇantu bhavanto mama śarīrān majjā-māṃsaṃ yathā kāma-karuṇāyā tulya-prīti-vivarddhanena tyāga-cittena | bodhi-satva-vijña-gaṇa-niṣevitena mahā-kuśala-mūlena loka-mala-apakarṣitena pravareṇa + adhyāśayena | sarva-bodhi-satva-samatā-upāttair mahā-dāna-ārambhair manasā + ākāṅkṣitaiḥ sarva-yācakair an-anutāpya-cittair dāna-vastubhiḥ a-pratyavekṣitena karma-vipāka-pratyayena sarva-loka-dhātv-a-vimukhayā sarva-buddha-kṣetra-alaṃ-kāra-vyūha-pūjayā sarva-jagad-abhimukhayā karuṇā-paritrāṇatayā | sarva-buddha-bodhy-abhimukhayā | daśa-bala ... cāraṇayā + atīta-an-āgata-pratyutpanna-sarva-bodhi-satva-abhimukhayā eka-kuśala-mūla-paricaryayā sarva-vaiśāradya-abhimukhena + ārṣabha-siṃha-nāda-nadanena try-adhva-abhimukhena | sarva-adhva-samatā-jñānena ... loka-abhimukhena + a-para-anta-koṭī-gata-kalpa-vyavasāyena bodhi-satva-praṇidhānena + a-paritrasyana-abhimukhena + a-kheda-citta-utpādena bodhi-satvaḥ sva-hṛdayaṃ parityajan yācanakebhyo dāna-vaśa-śikṣita-cittaḥ pāramitā-niṣpādana-cittaḥ sarva-bodhi-satva-dāna-an-uddhata-su-pratiṣṭhita-cittaḥ | adhiṣṭhāna-sarva-yācanaka-pratimānana-cittaḥ | adhyāśayaṃ pariśodhayamānaḥ | sarva-jagat-paripācana-nidānaṃ mahā-praṇidhānaṃ pratipadyamāno bodhi-satva-caryāyāṃ saṃvasamānaḥ sarva-jñatā-saṃbhāraṃ saṃbharamāṇaḥ praṇidhim a-riñcan so * atra yakṛt-bukkā-phupphuṣaṃ yācakebhyaḥ parityajan yācanaka-abhiprasannayā dṛṣṭyā prasanna-prīty-ākārair netrair bodhi-satva-niryātena premṇā + a-vyutthita-manasi-kāreṇa tyāgena + a-sārāt kāyāt su-pratyavekṣitena sāra-ādāna-cittena śmaśāna-paryantena kāya-anusmṛti-manasi-kāreṇa vṛka-śṛgāla-śva-bhakṣyaṃ śarīraṃ pratyavekṣamāṇaḥ para-bhakti-manasi-kṛtayā | śarīra-a-nityatayā + apaviddha-śarīreṇa para-bhakta-cetanena evaṃ dharma-manasi-kāra-prayukto bodhi-satvas tān yācanakān a-nimiṣaṃ prekṣamāṇa evaṃ cittam utpādayati | yadi ca + aham etad-yācanakasya etac-charīrād antraṃ yakṛt-bukkā-phuṣphuṣaṃ dadyāṃ | yadi vā na dadyāṃ | āyuḥ-kṣaya-paryante na + eṣo nityaḥ śmaśāna-paryavasāna iti | sa evaṃ manasi-kāra-saṃtoṣitena santānena + evaṃ dharma-jñānena + āśayena kalyāṇa-mitra-saṃjñā-adhiṣṭhitena yācanaka-darśanena + a-sārāt kāyāt sāram ādātu-kāmo dharma-kāmatayā sva-māṃsān nakhaṃ parityajann eva tat-kuśala-mūlaṃ pariṇāmayati + ity ātma-bhāva-utsargaṃ kṛtvā ||
body.translated_text: Thus indeed the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, giving himself for the purpose of attending upon others, with a mind of humility toward supplicants, with the intention of being a ground-covering seat, engaged in the disposition of enduring all suffering like the earth, with an unwearied mind devoted to attending upon all beings, steadfast amid the misdeeds of childish people, born with the nature of patient endurance, not standing still but devoted to <s>kuśalamūla</s> (wholesome roots), not occupied with attending to all world-realms — relinquishing ears and nose to supplicants who approach, with a mind born of the lineage of the <s>Tathāgata</s> family undertaken through <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct, engaged in the practice of recollecting all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, perceiving the essencelessness of all the three worlds ... with a continuum unattached to his own body, dwelling in the recollection of all <s>Buddha</s>-dharmas without fixed abode, with the intention of extracting the essence from the essenceless body — thus indeed the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, when asked for his tongue, ... with an affectionate, loving, and expansive <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) conduct, sitting upon a lion-throne worthy of a king, addresses that supplicant — it is seen. | Having become one of uninjured mind, of unimpaired mind, of unharmed mind, with a mind ... of great soul, with a mind born of the lineage of the <s>Buddha</s>, with an undisturbed continuum of mind, endowed with great power and strength, with a mind unattached to the body, with a mind unclinging to words, having knelt down upon his knees, from his own mouth his tongue ... making his entire body subservient to the supplicant, uttering speech that is gentle, soft, affectionate, and imbued with <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness): "Take my tongue, do with it as you wish; do so that you may be pleased, of pleased mind, delighted in yourself, joyful, filled with delight and gladness." | He, relinquishing his head, attaining the supreme knowledge that is the foremost head of all dharmas, going toward the <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) that is the head of protection for all beings, ... desiring the incomparable knowledge that is the foremost head of the world, resolving to attain the king of knowledge that is the head in all directions, wishing to fulfill the supreme headship of sovereignty over all dharmas, with a mind suffused with the delight of countless supplicants. | Thus indeed the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, relinquishing hands and feet to supplicants — with a hand extended through faith, with a conduct of beneficence, with an open palm stretched forth through the lion-like vigor and <s>tyāga</s> (renunciation) of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, delighting in giving away, through the relinquishing of hands and feet, through the exchange of steps at the great foundation, through the determination of <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct, through the unimpairedness of feeling, through the power of the grace of <s>dāna</s> (giving), with a restraint born of a stainless arising of mind, with the perception of body as uncut, unbroken, and undiminished as the <s>Dharma</s>-body of knowledge free from mental affliction, not lowly in mind, with a mind upheld and strengthened against all the works of <s>Māra</s> and evil friends, praised by all <s>Bodhisattvas</s> as one whose single act of <s>tyāga</s> (renunciation) is a going forth — thus indeed the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, casting forth his own body, gives blood to supplicants, with a mind gladdened toward <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), | with a mind desirous of <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct, with a mind of immeasurable feeling, with a mind desirous of fulfilling the wishes of all supplicants, with a mind free from hatred toward all recipients, having entered upon the practice of <s>tyāga</s> (renunciation) of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, with irreversible joy and serenity, with a mind regardless of his own body, giving blood from his own body — with a mind proceeding toward the great vehicle that is the domain of knowledge, with a mind intent on the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, of satisfied mind, of contented mind, of pleased mind, of delighted mind, of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) mind, of happy mind, of serene mind, filled with delight and gladness — relinquishing marrow and flesh from his own body to supplicants, with excellent <s>tyāga</s> (renunciation), | addressing those supplicants with speech desired by supplicants: "Let the good sirs take marrow and flesh from my body as they wish, with a mind of <s>tyāga</s> (renunciation) that increases compassion and delight equally, cultivated by the assembly of the wise among <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, with great <s>kuśalamūla</s> (wholesome root), with a supreme intention that removes the stain of the world, | with great undertakings of <s>dāna</s> (giving) obtained through equality with all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, with objects of <s>dāna</s> (giving) desired by the mind and given to all supplicants without regret, with a cause of <s>karmavipāka</s> (fruition of action) that is not looked back upon, with worship that adorns all <s>Buddha</s>-fields and is not turned away from any world-realm, with compassionate protection directed toward all the world, | directed toward the <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) of all <s>Buddhas</s>, with the exercise of the ten powers, ... directed toward all <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of the past, future, and present, with service to each and every <s>kuśalamūla</s> (wholesome root), with the bull-like lion's roar directed toward all fearlessness, directed toward the three times, | with the knowledge of the equality of all times, ... directed toward the world, with the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vow that perseveres through kalpas extending to the end of the infinite future, with an arising of mind without fear and without weariness — the <s>Bodhisattva</s> relinquishes his own heart to supplicants, with a mind trained in the mastery of <s>dāna</s> (giving), with a mind set on accomplishing the <s>pāramitās</s>, with a mind well-established and unagitated in the <s>dāna</s> (giving) of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, | with a mind of resolute determination to honor all supplicants, | purifying his intention, | undertaking the great vow that is the cause of ripening all the world, dwelling in <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct, accumulating the equipment for <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), not abandoning his vow — there he relinquishes liver, lungs, and spleen to supplicants, with a gaze of serene faith toward supplicants, with eyes whose aspect is serene delight, with the affection that is the going forth of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with a <s>tyāga</s> (renunciation) of undisturbed mental application, with a mind of well-considered extraction of essence from the essenceless body, with a contemplation of the body that ends at the charnel ground, regarding the body as food for wolves, jackals, and dogs, | with the impermanence of the body considered as devotion to others, with an intention of serving others through a body that is cast away — thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, engaged in such contemplation of the <s>Dharma</s>, gazing unblinkingly at those supplicants, generates this thought: "Whether I give to this supplicant from this body the entrails, liver, lungs, and spleen, or whether I do not give — at the end of the lifespan, this is not eternal; the body ends at the charnel ground." | He, with a continuum gratified by such contemplation, with such an intention of <s>Dharma</s>-knowledge, with a view of supplicants established through the perception of a <s>kalyāṇamitra</s> (spiritual friend), wishing to extract the essence from the essenceless body, through desire for the <s>Dharma</s>, even while relinquishing his own flesh and nails, dedicates that <s>kuśalamūla</s> (wholesome root) — thus having made the offering of his own being. ||

body.text: bhoga-puṇya-utsargo * apy atra + eva + ukteḥ | iti hi bodhi-satvo nānā-dakṣiṇīya-pratigrāhakeṣv anya-anya-pudgala-dig-āgateṣv a-prameya-kṛpaṇa-vanīpakeṣu bodhi-satva-śrava-āgateṣu bodhi-satva-śabdaṃ śrutvā + āgateṣu bodhi-satva-pratyaya-avakāśa-gateṣu bodhi-satva-dāna-pūrvaṃ praṇidhāna-śruteṣu | bodhi-satva-praṇidhāna-citta-nimantriteṣu | sarva-tyāga-manasa-abhilaṣiteṣu tṛpta-yācanaka-pratimānanā-cetana āgata-yācanaka-kṣamā-paṇa-cetano | mayā + eva tatra diśaṃ gatvā yūyaṃ pratimānayitavyā abhaviṣyata yena yuṣmākam āgamana-klamo na syāt | evaṃ samṛddha-praṇipātena kṣamayati sarva-yācanakān kṣamayitvā snāpayitvā viśrāmita-śarīrān kṛtvā tebhyo yad-ṛcchayā + upakaraṇaṃ pratipādayati | yad idaṃ maṇi-rathān jambu-dvīpa-kalyāṇa-kanyā-ratna-paripūrṇān yad idaṃ suvarṇa-rathān jana-pada-viśuddha-kanyā-ratna-paripūrṇān | yad idaṃ vaiḍūrya-rathān vā + anukula-gīta-vādya-saṃpravādita-paripūrṇān | evaṃ sphaṭika-rathān su-mukha-su-veśa-dhāri-sv-alaṃ-kṛta-rūpān a-pratikūla-darśana-catura-kanyā-ratna-paripūrṇān iti | tathā + atra + eva deśitaṃ maṇi-rathān vā dadānaḥ sarva-ratna-jāla-saṃchannān ājāneya-hasty-upetān | sa-vāhanān | candana-rathān dadāno ratna-cakra-rathya-prayuktān ratna-siṃha-āsana-pratiṣṭhitān yāvan nānā-ratna-chatra-saṃchanna-vyūhān ratna-vitāna-vitata-saṃchannān dhvaja-patāka-alaṃ-kṛta-catur-dikkān nānā-gandha-vidhūpita ... sāra-gandha-anulepa-anuliptān | sarva-puṣpa-vyūha-avakīrṇān kanyā-śata-sahasra-ratna-sūtra-prakarṣitān a-bhrānta-gamanān abhra-anta-sama-vāhana-prayuktān | yāvad a-pratikūla-mano-jña-pravāta-gandhān su-duhitṛ-putra-vacana-upacāra-prayuktān | vividha-gandha-cūrṇa-sambhṛta-kṛta-upacārān iti ||
body.translated_text: The relinquishing of enjoyments and merit is also stated right here: 'For thus, the <s>bodhisattva</s>, among various worthy recipients — those who have come from various directions, being various individuals; among immeasurable wretched peddlers; among those who have come upon hearing of the <s>bodhisattva</s>; among those who, having heard the word "<s>bodhisattva</s>," have come; among those who have entered into the opportunity of the <s>bodhisattva</s>; among those who have heard of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s former vow of giving; among those invited by the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s aspiring mind; among those who desire [one who has] a mind of complete renunciation — with the intention of honoring satisfied supplicants, and with the intention of showing patience toward those supplicants who have come — [he says:] "I myself should have gone to that direction to welcome you, so that the fatigue of your journey would not have occurred." Thus, with abundant obeisance, he shows patience to all the supplicants; having shown patience, having bathed them and rested their bodies, he bestows upon them provisions according to their wishes: namely, jewel-chariots filled with the jewel-maidens of noble beauty from <s>Jambudvīpa</s>; gold chariots filled with jewel-maidens of pure country [beauty]; <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) chariots filled with harmonious songs and music; crystal chariots of beautiful-faced, well-dressed, well-adorned forms, filled with jewel-maidens of agreeable appearance and skill.' Likewise, it is taught right here: 'Giving jewel-chariots covered with nets of all kinds of gems, equipped with thoroughbred elephants, with vehicles; giving sandalwood chariots yoked with jewel-wheeled carriages, established on jewel lion-thrones,' and so on, up to 'adorned with arrays of various jewel-parasols, covered with spread canopies of jewels, adorned in the four directions with banners and flags, perfumed with various fragrances... anointed with the finest essential unguents; strewn with arrays of all flowers; drawn by jewel-threads of hundreds of thousands of maidens, of unwavering movement, yoked with vehicles [swift] as the edge of a cloud; and so on, up to possessing agreeable, pleasing, wafting fragrances; attended upon with the courteous speech of good daughters and sons; attended with preparations made of various fragrant powders.'

body.text: punar atra + eva + āha | ātmānaṃ ca sarva-satvānāṃ niryātayann upasthānaṃ vā sarva-buddhānām upādadāno rājyaṃ vā parityajan paṭa-bhedakaṃ vā nagara-rāja-dhānīṃ sarva-alaṃ-kāra-bhūṣitāṃ yathā-arhaṃ vā yācanakeṣu sarva-parivāraṃ parityajan putra-duhitṛ-bhāryāṃ vā dadāno yācanakebhyaḥ sarva-gṛhaṃ vā + apasṛjan | yāvat sarva-upabhoga-paribhogān vā dadānaḥ | evaṃ pāna-dānaṃ rasa-dānam api bodhi-satvo dadāno vividhān kalyāṇān udārān viśuddhān a-vikalāṃs tiktāṃl lavaṇān kaṭakān kaṣāyān nānā-rasa-agra-upetān su-snigdhān vividha-rasa-vidhinā + upetān dhātu-kṣobhaṇa-samatā-sthāpanān citta-śarīra-bala-upastambhanān prīti-prasāda-prāmodya-kalpatā-jananān | yāvat sarva-para-upakrama-pratiṣedhakān sarva-vyādhi-samana-ārogya-saṃjananān | evaṃ vastra-dānaṃ puṣpa-dānaṃ gandha-dānaṃ vilepana-dānaṃ mālya-dānaṃ | śayana-dānam āvāsa-dānam apāśraya-dānaṃ pradīpa-dānaṃ ca | glāna-pratyaya-bhaiṣajya-pariṣkārān bodhi-satvo * anuprayacchan yāvan nānā-bhājanāni vividha-saṃbhārāṇy an-eka-kāṃsya-pātrīr a-prameya-saṃbhāra-upacitā hiraṇya-suvarṇa-rūpya-cūrṇa-paripūrṇās tāni buddhebhyo bhagavadbhyo dadāno * a-cintya-dakṣiṇīya-adhimukta-cetā bodhi-satva-ratnebhyo vā dadānaḥ | kalyāṇa-mitra-su-dur-labha-citta-utpādena ārya-saṃghāya vā dadānaḥ | buddha-śāsana-upastambhāya pudgalāya vā dadānaḥ | śrāvaka-praty-eka-buddhebhyo vā + ārya-guṇa-su-prasanna-cittatayā mātā-pitṛbhyāṃ dadāno | guru-śuśrūṣa-upasthāna-cittatayā ācārya-guru-dakṣiṇīyebhyo vā dadānas tatra tatra guru-saṃbhāra-avavāda-śikṣaṇa-prayuktaḥ | aśana-vasanaṃ vā kṛpaṇa-vanīpaka-yācanakebhyo dadānaḥ | sarva-satva-a-pratihata-cakṣur maitrī-paribhāvita-cittatayā | peyālaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Again, right here it says: 'And surrendering himself to all beings, or undertaking the service of all <s>Buddhas</s>, or relinquishing his kingdom, or [giving away] a royal capital adorned with all ornaments as if it were a cloth to be torn, or relinquishing according to merit his entire retinue to supplicants, or giving wife, son, and daughter to supplicants, or vacating his entire house, and so on up to giving all objects of enjoyment and use.' 'Thus, the <s>bodhisattva</s> giving drink-gifts and flavor-gifts also gives various excellent, noble, pure, complete, bitter, salty, pungent, and astringent [provisions], endowed with the finest of various flavors, well-seasoned, prepared with manifold flavoring methods — [substances] that balance the disturbance of the bodily humors (<s>dhātu</s>), that support the strength of mind and body, that generate delight, serenity, joy, and well-being; and so on, up to those that ward off all hostile attacks and that cure all diseases and produce health.' 'Likewise, the giving of cloth, the giving of flowers, the giving of fragrance, the giving of ointments, the giving of garlands, the giving of beds, the giving of dwelling-places, the giving of shelter, and the giving of lamps.' 'The <s>bodhisattva</s>, offering medicines and provisions for the sick, and so on up to various vessels, manifold supplies, numerous copper bowls, filled with immeasurable provisions and with gold, silver, and gold-dust — giving these to the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, with a mind devoted to inconceivable worthy recipients; or giving to the jewels among <s>bodhisattvas</s>; or, with a mind that [recognizes] the extreme rarity of generating the thought [of awakening through] a spiritual friend, giving to the noble <s>Saṃgha</s>; or giving to those who support the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching; or giving to <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> with a mind of faith well-disposed to noble virtues; or giving to mother and father with a mind intent on respectful service; or giving to teachers, preceptors, and worthy ones, being engaged in the instruction and training of the teacher's assemblage; or giving food and clothing to wretched peddlers and supplicants, with an unobstructed eye toward all beings, with a mind pervaded by <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness).' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: iti hi bodhi-satvo hasty-ājāneyān dadānaḥ sapta-aṅga-su-pratiṣṭhitān | ṣaṣṭi-hāyanān ṣaḍ-gantra-upetān padma-varṇān mukha-viśuddhān suvarṇa-alaṃ-kārān hema-jāla-praticchanna-śarīrān nānā-ratna-vicitra-alaṃ-kāra-jāla-śuṇḍa-prakṣipta-vyūhān suvarṇa-kalyāṇān kalyāṇa-cāru-darśanān | a-klānta-yojana-sahasra-gamana-upacārān aśva-ājāneyān vā dadānaḥ | sukha-vāhana-sukha-śarīra-upetān anujava-saṃpannāṃś catur-dig-gamana-āhāra-java-upetān āroha-saṃpannān divya-kalyāṇa-cāru-sadṛśa-sarva-vibhūṣaṇa-upetān | sa tān dadānaḥ parityajan gauraveṇa guru-janebhyaḥ kalyāṇa-mitra-mātā-pitṛbhyaḥ kṛpaṇa-vanīpaka-yācanakebhyaḥ sarva-jagat-pratigrāhakabhyo mukta-cittayā dadāno | na + āgṛhīta-cittatayā + avasṛjan mahā-karuṇā-parisphuṭena santānena mahā-tyāga-parimāṇa-bodhi-satva-guneṣu pratipadyamāno * abhijāta-bodhi-satva-adhyāśayān pariśodhayamāno yāvad iti hi bodhi-satva āsana-dānaṃ dadānaḥ parityajan rāja-bhadra-āsanāni vaiḍūrya-pādakāni siṃha-pratiṣṭhitāni suvarṇa-sūtra-ratna-jāla-vitānāny an-eka-cīvara-sparśa-upeta-prajñaptāni sarva-sāra-gandha-vāsita-upacārāṇi vicitra-maṇi-rāja-samucchrita-dhvajāny an-eka-ratna-koṭī-niyuta-śata-sahasra-alaṃ-kāra-vyūhāni hema-jāla-vitāna-vitatāni suvarṇa-kiṅkiṇī-jāla-saṃghaṭita-mano-jña-nāda-nirghoṣa-śabdāni mahāntya-āsanāny abhyudgato dviddha-cakṣur-daśanāny eka-chatra-mahā-pṛthivy--anuśāsana-niṣadana-abhiṣiktāni | sarva-rājya-aiśvarya-adhipateya-niyata-niṣadya-a-pratihata-cakra-śāsana-anuśāsana-sarva-rāja-adhipateye pravarttate | evaṃ yāvad iti hi bodhi-satvaś chatrāṇi dadānaḥ parityajan mahā-ratna-vyūha-pratimaṇḍitāni ratna-daṇḍāni kiṅkiṇī-jāla-saṃchannāni | ratna-sūtra-karṇa-kaṇṭha-āvalī-vināmita-vaiḍūrya-maṇi-hāra-abhipralambitāni nandī-ghoṣa-mano-jña-śabda-upacārāṇi hema-jāla-abhyantara-viśuddha-chadanāni ratna-śalāka-alaṃ-kāra-śata-sahasra-vitatāni ratna-koṣa-sandhāritāny a-guru-candanāny eka-sāra-vara-gandha-koṭī-niyuta-śata-sahasra-vidhūpita-vāsita-upacārāṇi jāmbu-nada-prabhāsvara-śuddhāni | tādṛśānāṃ chatrāṇām an-eka-koṭī-niyuta-śata-sahasra-alaṃ-kārāṇāṃ tad-atiriktāni ca + a-saṃkhyeya-koṭī-niyuta-śata-sahasra-alaṃ-kārāṇy an-apekṣa-citto dadānaḥ parityajann avasṛjann anuprayacchan saṃmukhī-bhūtebhyo vā satva-sārebhyo nirvṛtānāṃ vā tathā-gatānāṃ caitya-alaṃ-kārāya | dharma-paryeṣṭaye bodhi-satva-kalyāṇa-mitrebhyo vā + abhijāta-bodhi-satva-dharma-bhāṇakebhyo vā mātā-pitṛbhyāṃ vā saṃgha-ratne vā sarva-buddha-śāsane vā yāvat sarva-pratigrāhakebhyaḥ sa evaṃ tat-kuśala-mūlaṃ pariṇāmayati ||
body.translated_text: Thus, the <s>bodhisattva</s> gives thoroughbred elephants well-established in the seven limbs, sixty years old, equipped with six goads, lotus-colored, pure of face, with golden ornaments, their bodies covered with golden nets, their trunks adorned with arrays of ornamental nets variegated with various gems, golden and beautiful, of lovely appearance; [elephants] trained for traveling a thousand <s>yojanas</s> without fatigue. Or he gives thoroughbred horses — of comfortable carriage and agreeable body, endowed with speed, equipped with swiftness of travel in the four directions, fully trained for mounting, furnished with all adornments like divine, beautiful, and lovely ones. Giving these, relinquishing [them] with reverence to elders, to spiritual friends, to mother and father, to wretched peddlers and supplicants, giving to all beings as recipients with an unfettered mind, releasing [them] without a grasping mind, with a mental continuum overflowing with great compassion, practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> virtues of the measure of great renunciation, purifying the noble <s>bodhisattva</s>'s superior intention — and so on up to: 'Thus the <s>bodhisattva</s> gives the gift of seats, relinquishing royal throne-seats with <s>vaiḍūrya</s> legs, established on lions, with canopies of gold threads and jewel-nets, furnished with cushions of multiple fabrics, perfumed with all the finest fragrances, with raised banners of variegated jewel-kings, adorned with arrays of innumerable billions of gems, covered with spread canopies of golden nets, with the pleasing sound of tinkling golden bell-nets joined together, great throne-seats, with upraised teeth-like projections for the eyes, consecrated for ruling the entire great earth under a single parasol; established in the lordship of all kingdoms and sovereignty, seated upon the unobstructed wheel of command over all kings, he reigns.' And so on up to: 'Thus the <s>bodhisattva</s> gives parasols, relinquishing [those] adorned with arrays of great jewels, with gem-handles, covered with nets of bells, with hanging <s>vaiḍūrya</s> gem-necklaces bent by jewel-thread ear- and neck-garlands, with pleasing sounds of joyful proclamations, with inner coverings purified within golden nets, spread with hundreds of thousands of ornamental gem-shafts, held by jewel-caskets, of <s>aguru</s> and sandalwood, perfumed and scented with innumerable billions of the finest essential fragrances, radiant and pure as <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold.' Giving innumerable billions of such parasol-ornaments, and even more — innumerable billions of ornaments beyond those — with an indifferent mind, giving, relinquishing, releasing, bestowing [them] upon beings of excellent essence who are present, or for the adornment of the <s>caityas</s> (reliquary shrines) of <s>Tathāgatas</s> who have attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>; or for the pursuit of the <s>Dharma</s>; or to <s>bodhisattva</s> spiritual friends; or to noble <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Dharma</s>-preachers; or to mother and father; or to the jewel of the <s>Saṃgha</s>; or in the entire teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>; and so on up to all recipients — he thus dedicates that wholesome root.

body.text: yathā tāvat prathamāyām eva pariṇāmanāyāṃ sarva-kuśala-mūla-prastāveṣu + upadiṣṭaṃ | evaṃ praṇidhānam utpādayati | katham etāni kuśala-mūlāni sarva-jagad-upajīvyāny upakāri-bhūtāni bhaveyur viśuddha-dharma-paryavasānāni yena sarva-satvānām etaiḥ kuśala-mūlair naraka-apāya-pratiprasrabdhir bhavati | tairyagyonika-yāmalaukikād duṣkha-skandhān nivarttayeyuḥ | sa tāni kuśala-mūlāni pariṇāmayann evaṃ tat-kuśala-mūlaṃ pariṇāmayati | anena + ahaṃ kuśala-mūlena sarva-satvānāṃ nayanaṃ bhaveyaṃ sarva-duṣkha-skandha-vinivarttanāya | sarva-satvānāṃ trāṇaṃ bhaveyaṃ sarva-kleśa-parimocanatayā | sarva-satvānāṃ śaraṇaṃ bhaveyaṃ sarva-bhaya-ārakṣaṇatayā | sarva-satvānāṃ gatir bhaveyaṃ sarva-bhūmy-anugamanatayā | sarva-satvānāṃ parāyaṇaṃ bhaveyam atyanta-yoga-kṣema-pratilambhatayā | sarva-satvānāṃ āloko bhaveyaṃ vitimira-jñāna-saṃdarśanatayā | sarva-satvānāṃ ulkā bhaveyam a-vidyā-tamo-andha-kāra-vinivarttanatayā | sarva-satvānāṃ pradyoto bhaveyam atyanta-viśuddhi-pratiṣṭhāpanatayā | sarva-satvānāṃ nāyako bhaveyam a-cintya-dharma-naya-avatāraṇatayā | sarva-satvānāṃ pariṇāyako bhaveyam an-āvaraṇa-jñāna-skandha-upanayanatayā | peyālaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Now, just as was taught in the very first dedication, in the contexts of all wholesome roots, so he generates the aspiration: 'How may these wholesome roots become that which sustains all the world, that which is beneficial, culminating in pure <s>Dharma</s>, so that through these wholesome roots there may be the subsiding of hell and the lower realms for all beings, and they may turn away from the mass of suffering of the animal realm and the mundane world?' Dedicating those wholesome roots, he thus dedicates that wholesome root: 'By this wholesome root of mine, may I become the guide of all beings for the turning away from the entire mass of suffering; may I become the protector of all beings through the complete liberation from all afflictions; may I become the refuge of all beings through the guarding against all fears; may I become the resort of all beings through the accompanying of all stages; may I become the final goal of all beings through the attainment of ultimate welfare and security; may I become the light of all beings through the revelation of knowledge free from darkness; may I become the torch of all beings through the dispelling of the blinding darkness of ignorance; may I become the lamp of all beings through the establishment in ultimate purity; may I become the leader of all beings through the entry into the inconceivable method of <s>Dharma</s>; may I become the chief guide of all beings through the bringing near of the aggregate of unobstructed knowledge.' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: tac ca + adhyāśayataḥ pariṇāmayati na vacana-mātreṇa | tac ca + udagra-cittaḥ pariṇāmayati | hṛṣṭa-cittaḥ pariṇāmayati | prasanna-cittaḥ pariṇāmayati | pramudita-cittaḥ snigdha-cittaḥ pariṇāmayati | maitra-cittaḥ prema-cittaḥ anugraha-citto hita-cittaḥ sukha-cittaḥ pariṇāmayati | tac ca + evaṃ pariṇāmayati | idaṃ mama kuśala-mūlaṃ sarva-satvānāṃ gati-viśuddhaye saṃvarteta | upapatti-viśuddhaye saṃvartteta | puṇya-māhātmya-viśuddhaye saṃvartteta | an-abhibhūtatāyāṃ saṃvartteta | a-paryādānatāyāṃ saṃvartteta | dur-āsada-cittatāyāṃ saṃvartteta | smṛty-a-pramoṣatāyāṃ saṃvartteta | gati-mati-viniścayatāyāṃ saṃvartteta | buddhy-a-pramāṇatāyāṃ saṃvartteta | kāya-karma-manas-karma-sarva-guṇa-alaṃ-kāra-paripūryāṃ saṃvartteta ||
body.translated_text: And he dedicates that [merit] from [genuine] superior intention, not by mere words. And he dedicates it with an exalted mind; he dedicates it with a joyful mind; he dedicates it with a serene mind; he dedicates it with a delighted mind; he dedicates it with an affectionate mind; he dedicates it with a mind of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness); he dedicates it with a mind of love; he dedicates it with a mind of beneficence; he dedicates it with a mind of helpfulness; he dedicates it with a mind of happiness. And he dedicates it thus: 'May this wholesome root of mine conduce to the purification of the destinies of all beings; may it conduce to the purification of rebirth; may it conduce to the purification of the greatness of merit; may it conduce to invincibility; may it conduce to inexhaustibility; may it conduce to indomitable-mindedness; may it conduce to unfailing mindfulness; may it conduce to the determination of course, understanding, and discernment; may it conduce to immeasurable wisdom; may it conduce to the complete fulfillment of all virtuous ornaments of bodily action and mental action.'

body.text: anena me kuśala-mūlena te sarva-satvāḥ sarva-buddhān ārāgayeyur ārāgayitvā ca mā virāgayeyuḥ | teṣu ca buddheṣu bhagavatsu prasādam a-bhedyaṃ pratilabheran | teṣāṃ ca tathā-gatānām arhatāṃ samyak-saṃbuddhānām antike dharma-deśanāṃ śṛṇuyuḥ | śrutvā ca sarvā vi-matīr vinivarttayeyuḥ | yathā-śrutaṃ ca saṃdhārayeyuḥ | sandhārayantaś ca pratipattyā saṃpādayeyuḥ | tāṃś ca tathāgatān ārādhayeyuḥ | citta-karmaṇyatāṃ ca pratilabheran | an-avadyāni karmāṇi samudānayeyuḥ | mahatsu ca kuśala-mūleṣv ātmānaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayeyur atyantaṃ ca dāridryaṃ vinivarttayeyuḥ sapta dhana-pratilambhāṃś ca paripūrayeyuḥ sarva-buddhānāṃ ca + anuśikṣayeyuḥ kalyāṇa-indriya-pratilambhaṃ ca + adhigaccheyuḥ | udāra-adhimukti-samatāṃ ca pariniṣpādayeyuḥ | sarva-jña-jñāne ca + avakāśaṃ pratilabheran | a-pratihata-cakṣuṣmattāṃ ca sarva-jagaty utpādayeyuḥ | lakṣaṇa-alaṃ-kṛtatāṃ ca kāya-pratipūriṃ pratilabheran | sarva-guṇa-alaṅ-kāraṃ ca vākya-viśuddhiṃ parigṛhṇīyuḥ | saṃvṛta-indriyatāṃ daśa-bala-prayuktāṃ citta-kalyatāṃ samudānayeyuḥ | a-niścita-vihāratāṃ ca paripūrayeyuḥ | yena ca sukha-upadhānena sarva-buddhāḥ samanvāgatās tat-sukha-upadhāna-pratilabdhāḥ sarva-satvā bhaveyur iti ||
body.translated_text: By this root of virtue of mine, may all those sentient beings please all the <s>Buddhas</s>, and having pleased them, may they not displease them. May they obtain unbreakable faith in those <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones. May they hear the <s>Dharma</s> teaching in the presence of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones. Having heard, may they dispel all doubts. May they retain what they have heard. Retaining it, may they accomplish it through practice. May they please those <s>Tathāgatas</s>. May they obtain pliancy of mind. May they accumulate blameless actions. May they establish themselves in great roots of virtue and completely remove utter poverty. May they fulfill the attainment of the seven treasures. May they train after all the <s>Buddhas</s>. May they attain the acquisition of excellent faculties. May they perfectly accomplish the equality of noble aspiration. May they obtain access to the knowledge of the omniscient. May they produce unobstructed vision throughout the entire world. May they obtain bodily fulfillment adorned with the [major] marks. May they take hold of the purity of speech adorned with all qualities. May they accumulate the wholesomeness of mind endowed with the ten powers and guarded faculties. May they fulfill the state of dwelling without fixed abode. And whatever basis of happiness all <s>Buddhas</s> possess — may all sentient beings obtain that very basis of happiness.

body.text: yathā ṣaṣṭhī pariṇāmanā + uktena vidhinā pariṇāmayati | sarva-satvā | jñāna-āhārād bhavantu a-saṅga-prayukta-cetasaḥ | āhāra-prajñā-ātāpino * an-adhyavasita-āhārāḥ prīti-bhakṣā-nir-āmiṣa-āhārā yāvat kāma-tṛṣṇā-vinivarttakāḥ | sarva-satvāḥ dharma-rasa-megha-pravarṣakā bhavantu | an-uttara-dharma-rati-prīṇita-santānāḥ | sarva-satvāḥ sarva-rasa-agra-jihvā bhavantu rasa-nimittā grahītāraḥ sarva-buddha-dharma-cittana-prayuktāḥ a-vipanna-yānā agra-yānā uttama-yānāḥ śīghra-yānā mahā-yānāḥ | sarva-satvā a-tṛpta-darśanā bhavantu buddha-prīti-pratilabdhāḥ | sarva-satvāḥ sarva-kalyāṇa-mitra-darśana-an-upahata-santānā bhavantu | sarva-satvā agada-bhaiṣajya-rāja-upadarśanā bhavantu | sarva-satvāḥ kleśa-viṣa-vinivarttakāḥ | sarva-satvā āditya-maṇḍala-udgata-darśanā bhavantu sarva-satva-tamas-timira-paṭala-vidhamanatvāt ||
body.translated_text: As the sixtieth dedication transfers merit by the method stated: May all sentient beings, through the nourishment of knowledge, become those with unattached and engaged minds. May they become striving with the wisdom of nourishment, non-attached to nourishment, feeding on joy, with nourishment free of material bait, even removing the craving for sense-pleasures. May all sentient beings become those who rain down clouds of <s>Dharma</s>-nectar, with their continua delighted by the supreme bliss of the <s>Dharma</s>. May all sentient beings possess the foremost tongue of all flavors, grasping the signs of flavor, engaged in the contemplation of all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, with unimpaired vehicles, supreme vehicles, highest vehicles, swift vehicles, great vehicles. May all sentient beings have insatiable vision, having obtained the joy of the <s>Buddha</s>. May all sentient beings have their continua unimpaired by seeing all spiritual friends. May all sentient beings behold the king of healing medicines. May all sentient beings remove the poison of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). May all sentient beings behold the risen disk of the sun, because they dispel the covering of darkness and gloom of all sentient beings.

body.text: evam ātmānam upanidhāya sva-bhāvana-anukūlyena paṭhitavyaṃ | sarva-satvānām abhirucira-darśanatāyāṃ pariṇāmayāmi | saumanasya-darśanatāyāṃ kalyāṇa-darśanatāyāṃ pariṇāmayāmi | abhilaṣita-darśanatāyāṃ praharṣita-darśanatāyāṃ daurmanasya-a-darśanatāyāṃ buddha-darśana-upetāyāṃ pariṇāmayāmi ||
body.translated_text: Thus, placing oneself [in empathy], one should recite in accordance with one's own cultivation: I dedicate [merit] toward all sentient beings having a delightful appearance; I dedicate toward having an appearance [that brings] cheerfulness, toward having a beautiful appearance; I dedicate toward having a desired appearance, a joyous appearance, an appearance free from sadness, an appearance endowed with seeing the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: sarva-satvāḥ śīla-gandha-upetā bhavantv an-ācchedya-śīlā bodhi-satva-pāramitā-śīlāḥ ||
body.translated_text: May all sentient beings be endowed with the fragrance of moral conduct, with unbroken moral conduct, with the moral conduct of the <s>bodhisattva pāramitās</s> (perfections).

body.text: sarva-satvā dāna-vāsitā bhavantu sarva-tyāga-parityāginaḥ | sarva-satvāḥ kśānti-vāsitā bhavantu a-kṣobhya-cetanā-pratilabdhāḥ | sarva-satvā vīrya-vāsitā bhavantu mahā-vīrya-yāna-sannaddhāḥ | sarva-satvā dhyāna-vāsitā bhavantu pratyutpanna-buddha-saṃmukhī-bhāva-sthitāḥ samādhi-pratilabdhāḥ | sarva-satvā bodhi-satva-pariṇāmanā-vāsitā bhavantu sarva-satvāḥ sarva-śukla-dharma-vāsitā bhavantu sarva-a-kuśala-dharma-prahīṇāḥ | sarva-satvā divya-śayana-pratilabdhā bhavantu mahā-jñāna-adhigamāya | sarva-satvā ārya-śayana-pratilabdhā bhavantu | niḥ-pṛthag-jana-bodhi-citta-āvāsanatvāt sarva-satvāḥ sukha-śayana-pratilabdhā bhavantu | sarva-saṃsāra-avacara-duḥkha-parivarjanatvāt sarva-satvāḥ kṣema-śayana-pratilabdhā bhavantu dharma-kāma-sparśa-upetāḥ | sarva-satvāḥ pariśuddha-buddha-kṣetra-avabhāsā bhavantu guṇa-vāsa-su-prayuktā ārya-āvāsa-niketa-uccalitāḥ | an-uttara-sarva-buddha-āvāsa-a-virahitāḥ | sarva-satvā buddha-upaniścaya-vihāriṇo bhavantu | sarva-satvā an-anta-ālokā bhavantu sarva-buddha-dharmeṣu sarva-satvā a-pratihata-avabhāsā bhavantu sarva-dharma-dhātv-eka-spharaṇāḥ | sarva-satvā ārogya-śarīrā bhavantu tathā-gata-kāya-pratilabdhāḥ | sarva-satvā bhaiṣajya-rāja-upamā bhavantu atyanta-ākalpana-dharmāṇaḥ | sarva-satvā a-pratihata-bhaiṣajya-stambha-upamā bhavantu jagac-cikitsā-pratipannāḥ | sarva-satvā roga-śalya-niruddhā bhavantu sarva-jña-ārogya-pratilabdhāḥ | sarva-satvāḥ sarav-jagad-bhaiṣajya-kuśalā bhavantu yathā-āśaya-bhaiṣajya-prayoga-saṃprayoktāraḥ ||
body.translated_text: May all sentient beings be perfumed by giving, relinquishing all in complete renunciation. May all sentient beings be perfumed by patience, having obtained unshakable resolve. May all sentient beings be perfumed by vigor, armored with the vehicle of great vigor. May all sentient beings be perfumed by <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), established in the direct presence of all <s>Buddhas</s>, having obtained <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). May all sentient beings be perfumed by the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s dedication. May all sentient beings be perfumed by all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, having abandoned all unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>. May all sentient beings obtain divine couches for the attainment of great knowledge. May all sentient beings obtain the noble couch, because they do not dwell in the <s>bodhicitta</s> of ordinary beings. May all sentient beings obtain the couch of happiness, because they avoid the suffering occurring in all <s>saṃsāra</s>. May all sentient beings obtain the couch of safety, endowed with the touch of <s>Dharma</s> and desire. May all sentient beings shine with the radiance of purified <s>buddha-kṣetras</s> (buddha-fields), well-engaged in the abode of qualities, having risen from the dwelling and abode of the noble ones, never separated from the supreme abode of all <s>Buddhas</s>. May all sentient beings dwell with the resolve of the <s>Buddha</s>. May all sentient beings have infinite radiance in all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. May all sentient beings have unobstructed luminosity, pervading the entire <s>dharma-dhātu</s> (realm of reality). May all sentient beings have healthy bodies, having obtained the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. May all sentient beings be like the king of medicines, having the nature of ultimate non-conceptualization. May all sentient beings be like unobstructed pillars of medicine, engaged in healing the world. May all sentient beings have their diseases and thorns removed, having obtained the health of the omniscient. May all sentient beings be skilled in medicine for the entire world, applying medicine according to each one's disposition.

body.text: sarva-sattveṣu sarva-roga-vinivarttanāya pariṇāmayāmi | sarva-sattveṣv a-paryanta-sthāma-bala-śarīratāyāṃ pariṇāmayāmi | sarva-satvānāṃ cakra-vāḍa-parvata-an-avamardya-kāya-bala-upapattaye pariṇāmayāmi | sarva-satvānāṃ sarva-bala-upastambhana-a-tṛptāyāṃ pariṇāmayāmi ||
body.translated_text: I dedicate [merit] toward the removal of all diseases in all sentient beings. I dedicate toward all sentient beings having bodies of boundless strength and power. I dedicate toward all sentient beings being reborn with bodily strength that cannot be crushed even by <s>Cakravāḍa</s> mountains. I dedicate toward insatiability in supporting the strength of all sentient beings.

body.text: sarva-satvā a-pramāṇa-bhājanā bhavantv ākāśa-dhātu-vipulāḥ smṛti-indriya-upetāḥ sarva-laukika-loka-uttara-bhāṣa-saṃgrahaṇād grahaṇa-smṛty-a-saṃpramūḍhāḥ | sarva-satvāḥ kalyāṇa-viśuddhi-bhāvanā bhavantu | atīta-an-āgata-pratyutpanna-sarva-buddha-bodhy-a-bheda-prasāda-grāhiṇaḥ | sarva-satvā kāmaṅ-gamā bhavantu sarvatra-gāminī-buddha-bhūmi-pratilabdhāḥ | sarva-satvāḥ sarva-sattveṣv a-pratihata-cittā bhavantu | sarva-satvā an-ābhoga-sarva-buddha-kṣetra-parisphuṭa-gamanā bhavantu | eka-citta-kṣaṇa-sarva-dharma-vikramāḥ | sarva-satvāḥ śrānta-āklānta-sarva-loka-dhātu-gamanā bhavantu | a-viśrāmyamāna-mano-maya-kāya-pratilabdhāḥ | sarva-satvāḥ sukha-gamana-muktā bhavantu sarva-bodhi-satva-caryā-anupraveśinaḥ | anena kuśala-mūlena sarva-satvāḥ kalyāṇa-mitra-a-tyāga-citta-an-utsṛṣṭā bhavantu kṛta-jñāḥ kṛta-anupālanatayā | sarva-satvāḥ kalyāṇa-mitraiḥ saha-eka-arthā bhavantu sa-bhāga-kuśala-mūla-saṃgrahaṇatayā | sarva-satvāḥ kalyāṇa-āśayā bhavantu kalyāṇa-mitra-saṃvasana-saṃpada-vihāra-anudhanvanatayā | sarva-satvāḥ kalyāṇa-mitra-kuśala-mūla-karma-vipāka-viśuddhā bhavantv eka-praṇidhānāḥ | sarva-satvā mahā-yāna-abhiraktāḥ saṃprasthitā bhavantv a-viṣkambhita-yāna-sarva-jñatā-paryavasānāḥ | sarva-satvāḥ pracchādita-kuśala-mūlā bhavantu sarva-buddha-avasthā-gopana-pratilabdhāḥ | sarva-satvā guṇa-jñāna-abhicchāditā bhavantu sarva-loka-upakleśa-vyapavṛttāḥ | sarva-satvā a-cchinna-a-vikṣipta-śukla-dharmāṇo bhavantv a-vipanna-buddha-dharma-pravāhāḥ | sarva-satvāś chatra-bhūtā bhavantu daśa-bala-vitāna-anvitāḥ | sarva-satvā atyanta-bodhy-āsana-pratilabdhā bhavantu | sarva-satvā buddha-vikrānti-siṃha-āsana-pratilabdhā bhavantu sarva-jagad-avalokanīyā iti ||
body.translated_text: May all sentient beings become vessels of immeasurable capacity, vast as the realm of space, endowed with the faculty of mindfulness, unconfused in the retention and memory of grasping all worldly and supramundane languages. May all sentient beings cultivate the purification of what is wholesome, grasping with unbroken faith the awakening of all <s>Buddhas</s> past, future, and present. May all sentient beings go wherever they wish, having obtained the <s>Buddha</s>-stage that goes everywhere. May all sentient beings have unobstructed minds toward all sentient beings. May all sentient beings travel effortlessly to all <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, pervading them fully, traversing all <s>dharmas</s> in a single mind-moment. May all sentient beings travel to all world-realms without fatigue or weariness, having obtained a mind-made body that does not rest. May all sentient beings be released in easy travel, entering all <s>bodhisattva</s> practices. By this root of virtue, may all sentient beings have minds that do not abandon or relinquish spiritual friends, being grateful through the preservation of what has been done. May all sentient beings share a common purpose with spiritual friends, through gathering together compatible roots of virtue. May all sentient beings have wholesome aspirations, through pursuing the prosperity and dwelling of association with spiritual friends. May all sentient beings be purified by the karmic ripening of the roots of virtue of spiritual friends, having a single aspiration. May all sentient beings be delighted in and set forth upon the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, with an unobstructed vehicle culminating in omniscience. May all sentient beings have concealed roots of virtue, having obtained the guarding of the state of all <s>Buddhas</s>. May all sentient beings be covered by the knowledge of qualities, freed from the defilements of the entire world. May all sentient beings have uninterrupted, undispersed wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, with an unimpaired stream of <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. May all sentient beings become like umbrellas, endowed with the canopy of the ten powers. May all sentient beings obtain the ultimate seat of awakening. May all sentient beings obtain the lion-throne of the <s>Buddha</s>'s power, worthy of being beheld by the entire world.

body.text: ārya-gagana-gañja-sūtre * apy āha | mā bhūt tan mama kuśala-mūlaṃ dharma-jñāna-kauśalyaṃ vā yan na sarva-sattva-upajīvyaṃ syād iti ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Gaganagañja-sūtra</s> it is also said: "May I never have a root of virtue or skill in <s>Dharma</s>-knowledge that is not for the sustenance of all sentient beings."

body.text: atīta-an-āgata-śubha-utsargas tv ārya-akṣayamati-sūtre * abhihitaḥ | kuśalānāṃ ca citta-caitasikānānām anusmṛtir anusmṛtya ca bodhi-pariṇāmanā | idam atīta-kauśalyaṃ | yo * an-āgatānāṃ kuśala-mūlānāṃ nidhyapti-bodher āmukhī-karma-samanvāhāraḥ | ye me utpatsyante kuśalāś citta-utpādās tān an-uttarāyāṃ samyak-saṃbodhau pariṇāmiṣyāmi + iti idam an-āgata-kauśalyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: The relinquishment of past and future merit is stated in the noble <s>Akṣayamati-sūtra</s>: The recollection of wholesome mental and concomitant [factors], and having recollected, the dedication toward awakening — this is the skill regarding the past. The mental cultivation of the foundation leading to awakening through the ripening of future roots of virtue: "Whatever wholesome mental arisings will occur for me — those I will dedicate toward supreme perfect awakening" — this is the skill regarding the future.

body.text: tad evaṃ caitasikena + ābhyāsena sarva-tyāga-adhimuktiṃ paripūrye tyāga-citta-vega-āpannena kāya-prayogeṇa + utsṛṣṭa-sarva-parigrahaḥ | sarva-parigraha-mūlād bhava-duṣkhād vimukto mukta ity ucyate | an-uttarāṃś ca + a-prameya-a-saṃkhyeyān kalpān nānā-ākāra-an-antān laukika-loka-uttarān sukha-saṃpat-pravarṣān anubhavati | tena ca + ātma-bhāva-ādinā

children.text: vaḍiṣa-āmiṣena + iva svayam an-abhigata-upabhogena + apy ākṛṣya parān api tārayati ||
children.translated_text: even when one has not personally enjoyed [the offering], like bait on a hook, one draws others in and ferries them across as well.

body.translated_text: Thus, having fulfilled the aspiration for complete relinquishment through mental habituation, with bodily effort impelled by the force of the thought of giving, having abandoned all possessions — being liberated from the suffering of existence rooted in all possessiveness, one is called 'liberated.' And one experiences unsurpassed, immeasurable, incalculable, manifold, endless, worldly and supramundane rains of happiness and prosperity for [many] <s>kalpas</s> (aeons). And through that body and so forth,

body.text: ata eva + uktaṃ ratna-meghe | dānaṃ hi bodhi-satvasya bodhir iti ||
body.translated_text: Therefore it is said in the <s>Ratnamegha</s> (Cloud of Jewels): "Giving, for a <s>bodhisattva</s>, is awakening itself."

body.text: śikṣā-samuccaye dāna-pāramitā prathamaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>, [this concludes] the first chapter on the <s>Dāna-pāramitā</s> (Perfection of Giving).

body.text: śīla-pāramitāyāṃ sad-dharma-parigraho nāma dvitīyaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Under the <s>Śīla-pāramitā</s> (Perfection of Moral Conduct), the second chapter is named <s>Saddharmaparigraha</s> (Embracing the True Dharma).

body.text: evam eṣām ātma-bhāva-ādīnām utsṛṣṭānām api rakṣā kāryā | kuto | yasmāt ||
body.translated_text: Thus, even when these — one's own body and so forth — have been given away, they must still be protected. Why? Because:

body.text: paribhogāya satvā nāma + ātma-bhāva-ādi dīyate | a-rakṣite kuto bhogaḥ | kiṃ dattaṃ yan na bhujyate ||
body.translated_text: One's own body and so forth are given for the enjoyment of sentient beings. If unprotected, how can there be enjoyment? What is the use of a gift that cannot be used?

body.text: tasmāt satva-upabhoga-artham ātma-bhāva-ādi pālayet ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, one should protect one's body and so forth for the purpose of benefiting sentient beings.

body.text: uktaṃ hi bodhi-satva-prātimokṣe | paraṃ śāriputra rakṣiṣyāmi + ity ātmā rakṣitavyaḥ | evaṃ-rūpayā śāriputra hita-aiṣikatayā samanvāgato bodhi-satvo jīvita-hetor api pāpaṃ karma na karoti + iti ||
body.translated_text: For it is said in the <s>Bodhisattvaprātimokṣa</s>: "'I shall protect others, <s>Śāriputra</s>' — [thinking thus,] one's own self should be protected. Endowed with such concern for the welfare of others, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> does not commit evil action even for the sake of [preserving his] life."

body.text: vīradatta-paripṛcchāyām apy āha | śakaṭam iva bhāra-udvahana-arthaṃ kevalaṃ dharma-buddhinā vāḍhavyam iti | tathā + akṣayamati-sūtre * api | kāya-duṣkhatayā ca na parikhidyate satva-avekṣatayā + iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Vīradattaparipṛcchā</s> it is also said: "Like a cart, it should be maintained solely for the purpose of carrying the burden, with the thought of <s>Dharma</s>." Likewise, in the <s>Akṣayamati-sūtra</s> also: "He does not become weary through contemplating the suffering nature of the body, out of concern for sentient beings."

body.text: tac ca + ātma-bhāva-ādikaṃ kathaṃ pālayet | kalyāṇa-mitra-an-utsarjanāt | yathā + uktam ārya-gaṇḍa-vyūhe ārya-śrī-saṃbhavena ||
body.translated_text: And how should one protect that body and so forth? By not abandoning spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitras</s>). As stated by the noble <s>Śrīsaṃbhava</s> in the <s>Ārya-Gaṇḍavyūha</s>:

body.text: kalyāṇa-mitra-sandhāritāḥ kula-putra bodhi-satvā na patanti dur-gatiṣu | kalyāṇa-mitra-samanvāhṛtā

children.text: na + atikrāmanti bodhi-satva-śikṣāṃ | kalyāṇa-mitra-praticchannā abhyudgatā bhavanti lokāt kalyāṇa-mitra-paryupāsitā bodhi-satvā a-saṃpramoṣa-cāriṇo bhavanti sarva-bodhi-satva-caryāsu | kalyāṇa-mitra-parigṛhītāḥ bodhi-satvā dur-ddharṣā bhavanti karma-kleśaiḥ | sambodhakāḥ kalyāṇa-mitrā a-karaṇīyānāṃ sannivārakāḥ pramāda-sthānāt | niṣ-kāsayitāraḥ saṃsāra-purāt | tasmāt tarhi kula-putra evaṃ manasi-kārāt pratipraśrabdhena kalyāṇa-mitrāṇy upasaṃkramitavyāni | pṛthivī-sama-cittena sarva-bhāra-vahana-a-pariṇamanatayā vajra-sama-cittena a-bhedya-āśayatayā | cakra-vāḍa-sama-cittena sarva-duṣkha-a-saṃpravedhanatayā | loka-dāsa-sama-cittena sarva-karma-samādāna-a-jugupsanatayā | rajo-haraṇa-sama-cittena māna-atimāna-vivarjanatayā | yāna-sama-cittena guru-bhāra-nirvahanatayā | śva-sama-cittena + a-krudhyanatayā | nau-sama-cittena gamana-āgamana-a-paritrasyanatayā | su-putra-sadṛśena kalyāṇa-mitra-mukha-vīkṣaṇatayā | ātmani ca te kula-putra + ātura-saṃjñā + utpādayitavyā | kalyāṇa-mitreṣu ca vaidya-saṃjñā | anuśāsanīṣu bhaiṣajya-saṃjñā | pratipattiṣu vyādhi-nirghātana-saṃjñā | ātmani ca te kula-putra bhīru-saṃjñā + utpādayitavyā | kalyāṇa-mitreṣu śūra-saṃjñā | anuśāsanīṣu praharaṇa-samjñā | pratipattiṣu śatru-nirghātana-saṃjñā ||
children.translated_text: they do not transgress the <s>bodhisattva</s> training. Those who are sheltered by spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitras</s>) become elevated above the world. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are attended upon by spiritual friends become unfailing in all <s>bodhisattva</s> practices. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are taken up by spiritual friends become invincible by <s>karmas</s> and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). Spiritual friends are awakeners, restrainers from what should not be done, from the ground of heedlessness; they are liberators from the fortress of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Therefore, O son of good family, with such mental attention and with relaxed composure, one should approach spiritual friends: with a mind like the earth, through not wavering under the bearing of all burdens; with a mind like a diamond (<s>vajra</s>), through the unbreakable nature of one's intention; with a mind like the encircling mountains (<s>Cakravāḍa</s>), through not trembling at all sufferings; with a mind like a world-servant, through not being disgusted at undertaking all tasks; with a mind like a dust-remover, through abandoning pride and arrogance; with a mind like a vehicle, through carrying heavy burdens; with a mind like a dog, through not becoming angry; with a mind like a boat, through not being frightened at going and coming; like a good son, through gazing at the face of the spiritual friend. And you should generate, O son of good family, the perception of yourself as sick; of spiritual friends as physicians; of their instructions as medicine; of practice as the destruction of disease. And you should generate, O son of good family, the perception of yourself as timid; of spiritual friends as heroes; of their instructions as weapons; of practice as the destruction of enemies.'

body.translated_text: "O son of good family, <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are sustained by spiritual friends do not fall into lower realms. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are guided by spiritual friends

body.text: atra + eva vācanā-upāsikā-vimokṣe varṇitaṃ | kalyāṇa-mitra-anuśāsanī-pratipannasya kula-putra bodhi-satvasya buddhā bhagavanto * abhirāddha-cittā bhavanti | kalyāṇa-mitra-vacana-a-viloma-sthāyino bodhi-satvasya sarva-jñatā + asannī-bhavati | kalyāṇa-mitra-vacana-a-vicikitsakasya + asannī-bhavanti kalyāṇa-mitrāṇi | kalyāṇa-mitra-manasi-kāra-a-virahitasya sarva-arthā abhimukhā bhavanti + iti | ata eva + ārya-sudhanaḥ sāradhvajasya bhikṣoḥ pādau śirasā + abhivandya + an-eka-śata-sahasra-kṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇī-krṭya sāradhvajaṃ bhikṣum avalokya praṇipatya punaḥ punar avalokayan niyataṃ praṇipatan namasyann avanaman manasi kurvan cintayan bhāvayan paribhāvayann udānam udānayan hāk-kāraṃ kurvan | guṇān abhimukhī-kurvan nigamayann atra sann anusmaran dṛḍhī-kurvann a-vijahan manasā + āgamayann upanibadhnan praṇidhiṃ samavasaran darśanam abhilaṣan svara-nimittam udgṛhṇan yāvat tasya + antikāt prakrāntaḥ | tathā kalyāṇa-mitra-āgataṃ sarva-jñatāṃ saṃpaśyann aśru-mukho rudan yāvan meghasya dramitasya + antikāt prakrāntaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the same <s>Vācanā-upāsikā-vimokṣa</s> (the liberation [chapter] of the laywoman Vācanā), it is described: 'For the <s>bodhisattva</s>, O son of good family, who has entered upon the instruction of spiritual friends, the blessed <s>Buddhas</s> become well-pleased in mind. For the <s>bodhisattva</s> who stands without opposing the words of spiritual friends, omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) comes near. For one who does not doubt the words of spiritual friends, spiritual friends [themselves] come near. For one who is not separated from the mindfulness of spiritual friends, all aims become favorable.' For this very reason, the noble <s>Sudhana</s>, having bowed his head at the feet of the monk <s>Sāradhvaja</s>, having circumambulated him many hundreds of thousands of times, gazing at the monk <s>Sāradhvaja</s>, prostrating, again and again gazing, constantly prostrating, saluting, bowing, reflecting in his mind, pondering, cultivating, thoroughly cultivating, uttering inspired exclamations, making sighs of admiration, turning toward [his] virtues, drawing them together, being present there, recollecting, making [his resolve] firm, not abandoning, mentally approaching, binding fast his aspiration, settling into [his] vision, longing for the sight [of him], grasping the sign of his voice — at last departed from his presence. Likewise, beholding omniscience as having come from spiritual friends, with tears on his face, weeping, at last he departed from the presence of <s>Megha Dramita</s>.

body.text: bodhi-satva-pratimokṣe * apy uktaṃ | iha śāriputra bodhi-satvo dharma-kāmatayā na + asti tal loke ratnaṃ yan na parityajati | na + asti tat kāya-upasthānaṃ yan na karoti | na + asti taj jaṅghā-preṣaṇaṃ yan na + utsahate | na + asti tad vāk-karma yan na + utsahate ācārya-upādhyāya-gauravatayā ||
body.translated_text: It is also stated in the <s>Bodhisattvaprātimokṣa</s>: 'Here, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s>, out of desire for the <s>Dharma</s> — there is no jewel in the world that he does not relinquish; there is no bodily service that he does not perform; there is no errand on foot that he does not endure; there is no verbal act that he does not endure, out of reverence for teachers and preceptors.'

body.text: peyālaṃ ||
body.translated_text: [Abbreviated passage.]

body.text: tat kasya hetoḥ | bandha-cchedāya + eṣa dharmaḥ saṃvartate | jāti-jarā-vyādhi-maraṇa-śoka-parideva-duṣkha-daurmanasya-cchedāya + eṣa dharmaḥ saṃvartatae iti ratna-cittam utpādya bhaiṣajya-cittam utpādya | sarva-satvānāṃ glānya-vyupaśamāya + eṣa dharmaḥ saṃvartatae iti | eṣṭavyaś ca + asmābhiḥ sarva-satvānāṃ glānya-vyupaśamāya + evaṃ-rūpo dharma iti ||
body.translated_text: 'For what reason? This <s>Dharma</s> conduces to the cutting of bonds. This <s>Dharma</s> conduces to the cutting of birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, and mental distress' — generating the thought of [the <s>Dharma</s> as] a jewel, generating the thought of [it as] medicine — 'This <s>Dharma</s> conduces to the alleviation of the ailments of all beings. And such a <s>Dharma</s> for the alleviation of the ailments of all beings should be sought by us.'

body.text: ugradatta-paripṛcchāyām apy uktaṃ | sacet punar gṛha-pate pāṭha-sva-adhyāya-arthiko bodhi-satvaḥ kasya-cid antikāc catuṣ-pādikāṃ gāthāṃ śṛṇuyād uddiśed vā udgṛhṇīyād dāna-śīla-kṣānti-vīrya-dhyāna-prajñā-saṃprayuktāṃ bodhi-satva-saṃbhāra-upacayaṃ vā tena tasminn ācārye dharma-gauravaṃ karaṇīyaṃ yāvadbhir nāma-pada-vyañjana ... gāthā + uddiṣṭā | yadi tāvata evaṃ kalpāṃs tasya + ācāryasya + upasthāna-paricaryāṃ kuryād a-śaṭhatayā sarva-lābha-sat-kāra-pūjayā | adya + api gṛha-pate na pratipūritam ācāryasya + ācārya-gauravaṃ bhavati | kaḥ punar vādo dharma-gauravaṃ ||
body.translated_text: It is also stated in the <s>Ugradattaparipṛcchā</s>: 'If, O householder, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who seeks recitation and study were to hear, or be taught, or learn from someone a single verse of four lines — [whether] connected with giving, morality, patience, vigor, meditation, or wisdom, or [tending toward] the accumulation of the <s>bodhisattva</s> equipment — he should show reverence for the <s>Dharma</s> toward that teacher [in proportion to] however many name-words, phrases, and syllables ... [make up] the verse taught. Even if he were to perform attendance and service to that teacher for that many <s>kalpas</s> without deceit, with all gain, honor, and worship — even then, O householder, the reverence due to the teacher as teacher would not be fulfilled. How much less the reverence due to the <s>Dharma</s>!'

body.text: prajñā-pāramitāyām aṣṭa-sahasrikāyām apy uktaṃ | kalyāṇa-mitreṣu ca tvayā kula-putra tīvraṃ gauravam utpādayitavyaṃ | prema ca karaṇīyaṃ | atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhi-satvo mahā-satva evaṃ-rūpair guṇair gaurava-manasi-kārair gacchann anupūrveṇa + anyatama-nagaram anuprāptas | tatra tasya + antarāyaṇa-madhya-gatasya + etad abhūt | yan nv aham imam ātma-bhāvaṃ vikrīya + anena mūlyena dharmodgatasya bodhi-satvasya mahā-satvasya sat-kāraṃ kuryāṃ | dīrgha-rātraṃ hi mama + ātma-bhāva-sahasrāṇi bhagnāni kṣīṇāni vikrītāni punar a-parimāṇe saṃsāre * a-parimāṇāni yāni mayā kāma-hetoḥ kāma-nidānam anubhūtāni na punar evaṃ-rūpāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ kṛtaśa evaṃ-rūpāṇāṃ vā satvānāṃ sat-kārāya ||
body.translated_text: It is also stated in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> in eight thousand [lines]: 'And you, O son of good family, should generate intense reverence toward spiritual friends, and you should show affection.' Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> (Ever-Weeping), endowed with such qualities of reverential mindfulness, traveling gradually, arrived at a certain city. There, while he was in the middle of a marketplace, this thought occurred to him: 'Suppose I were to sell this body of mine, and with that price make an offering to the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s> (Dharma-Arisen). For, throughout the long night [of <s>saṃsāra</s>], thousands of my bodies have been broken, perished, and sold — again and again in immeasurable <s>saṃsāra</s> — immeasurable [bodies] that I experienced for the sake of desires, on account of desires, but never for the sake of <s>dharmas</s> of such a kind, nor for the honoring of beings of such a kind.'

body.text: atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhi-satvo mahā-satvo * antarāyaṇa-madhya-gataḥ śabdam udīrayām āsa ghoṣam anuśrāvayām āsa | kaḥ puruṣeṇa + arthikaḥ kaḥ puruṣeṇa + arthika iti peyālaṃ | atha khalu māraḥ pāpīyān brāhmaṇa-gṛha-patikāṃs tathā samupasthāpayām āsa yathā taṃ ghoṣaṃ na + aśrauṣuḥ | yadā + ātmanaḥ krāyakaṃ na labhate tadā + eka-antaṃ gatvā prārodīd aśrūṇi ca prāvarttayad evaṃ ca + avadad | aho vata + asmākaṃ dur-labhā lābhā ye vayam ātma-bhāvasya + api kretāraṃ na labhāmahe | atha khalu śakro devānām indro māṇavaka-rūpeṇa yāvat sadāpraruditaṃ bodhi-satvaṃ mahā-satvam etad avocat | kiṃ tvaṃ kula-putra dīna-manā utkaṇṭhita-mānaso * aśrūṇi pravarttayamānaḥ sthitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, standing in the middle of the marketplace, raised his voice and made a proclamation: 'Who wants a man? Who wants a man?' [And so on in abbreviated form.] Then <s>Māra</s>, the Evil One, so influenced the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders that they did not hear that proclamation. When he could not find a buyer for himself, he went to a secluded place and began to weep and shed tears, and spoke thus: 'Alas, difficult indeed is our gain — that we cannot even find a buyer for our own body!' Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, in the form of a young man, approached the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> and said: 'Why, O son of good family, do you stand here dejected in mind, distressed, shedding tears?'

body.text: sadāprarudita evam āha | ahaṃ māṇavaka dharma-kāmatayā imam ātma-bhāvaṃ vikrīya dharma-pūjāṃ karttu-kāmaḥ so * aham asya krāyakaṃ na labhe | peyālaṃ ||
