body.translated_text: <s>Sadāprarudita</s> said thus: 'O young man, out of desire for the <s>Dharma</s>, I wish to sell this body of mine and make an offering to the <s>Dharma</s>. But I cannot find a buyer for it.' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: atha khalu sa māṇavakaḥ sadāpraruditaṃ bodhi-satvaṃ mahā-satvam etad avocat | na mama kula-putra puruṣeṇa kṛtyam api tu khalu punaḥ pitur me yajño yaṣṭavyaḥ | tatra me puruṣasya hṛdayena kṛtyaṃ lohitena ca asthi-majjayā ca | tad dāsyasi tvaṃ krayeṇa ||
body.translated_text: Then that young man said to the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>: 'I have no use for a man, O son of good family. However, my father has a sacrifice to be performed. For that I need a man's heart, blood, and bone-marrow. Will you give [those] for a price?'

body.text: atha khalu sadāpraruditasya + etad abhūt | lābhā me su-labdhāḥ pariniṣpannaṃ ca + ātmānaṃ jāne prajñā-pāramitā + upāya-kauśalyeṣu | yan mayā + ātmanaḥ krāyako labdho hṛdaysya rudhirasya ca + asthi-majjāyāś ca ||
body.translated_text: Then this thought occurred to <s>Sadāprarudita</s>: 'Well-gained indeed is my gain, and I know myself to be accomplished in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means) — since I have found a buyer for my heart, blood, and bone-marrow!'

body.text: sa hṛṣṭa-cittaḥ kalya-cittaḥ pramudita-cittas taṃ māṇavakam etad avocat | dāsyāmi māṇavaka yena te ita ātma-bhāvād arthaḥ | yāvat sadāprarudito bodhi-satvo mahā-satvas tīkṣṇaṃ śastraṃ gṛhītvā dakṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ viddhvā lohitaṃ nisrāvayati sma dakṣiṇaṃ ca + ūruṃ viddhvā nir-māṃsaṃ ca kṛtvā + asthi bhettuṃ kuḍya-mūlam upasaṃkrāmati ||
body.translated_text: He, with joyful mind, delighted mind, exultant mind, said to that young man: 'I shall give, O young man, whatever you need from this body of mine.' Thereupon the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, taking a sharp knife, pierced his right arm and let the blood flow, and piercing his right thigh and stripping it of flesh, approached the base of a wall to break the bone.

body.text: atha khalv anyatarā śreṣṭhi-dārikā + upari-prāsāda-tala-gatā + adrākṣīt sadāpraruditaṃ bodhi-satvaṃ yāvat sā śreṣṭhi-dārikā yena sadāprarudito bodhi-satvas tena + upasaṃkramya + etad avocat | kiṃ nu khalu tvaṃ kula-putra + evaṃ-rūpām ātmanaḥ kāraṇāṃ kārayāsi + iti | yāvat sā dārikā pūjā-prayojanaṃ śrutvā punar āha | kā punas te kula-putra tato guṇa-jātir niṣpatsyate | sa tām etad avocat | sa dārike kula-putro mama prajñā-pāramitām upāya-kauśalyaṃ ca + upadekṣayti | tatra vayaṃ śikṣiṣyāmas tatra vayaṃ śikṣamāṇāḥ sarva-satvānāṃ pratiśaraṇaṃ bhaviṣyāmaḥ | peyālaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Then a certain merchant's daughter, from atop an upper terrace, saw the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> — and that merchant's daughter approached the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> and said: 'Why, O son of good family, are you causing such harm to yourself?' When she heard the purpose of the worship, she said again: 'And what kind of virtuous qualities will result for you from that?' He said to her: 'That son of good family, O maiden, will teach me the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means). Therein we shall train, and training therein, we shall become the refuge of all beings.' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: atha khalu sā śreṣṭhi-dārikā sadāpraruditaṃ bodhi-satvam etad avocat | āścaryaṃ kula-putra | yāvad udārāḥ praṇītāś ca + amī tvayā dharmāḥ parikīrttitāḥ | eka-ekasya + api kula-putra + evaṃ-rūpasya dharmasya + arthāya gaṅgā-nadī-vālikā-upamān api kalpān evam ātma-bhāvāḥ parityaktavyā bhaveyuḥ | tathā + udārāḥ praṇītāś ca + amī tvayā dharmāḥ parikīrttitāḥ | api tu khalu kula-putra yena yena kṛtyaṃ tat te dāsyāmi suvarṇaṃ vā maṇiṃ vā muktāṃ vā vaiḍūryaṃ vā yāvad yena tvaṃ taṃ dharmodgataṃ bodhi-satvaṃ sat-kariṣyasi | yāvad vistareṇa tayā dārikayā pañca-śata-parivārayā sārddhaṃ tasya dharmodgatasya saṃkramaṇaṃ kartavyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Then that merchant's daughter said to the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>: 'It is wonderful, O son of good family! How lofty and excellent are the <s>dharmas</s> you have proclaimed! For the sake of even a single <s>dharma</s> of such a kind, O son of good family, one should relinquish bodies for <s>kalpas</s> as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River. So lofty and excellent are the <s>dharmas</s> you have proclaimed. Moreover, O son of good family, whatever you need — I shall give you gold, jewels, pearls, lapis lazuli, and so forth — by which you may honor that <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>.' [In detail:] together with that maiden and her retinue of five hundred maidens, the visit to <s>Dharmodgata</s> was to be made.

body.text: atha khalu dharmodgato bodhi-satvo mahā-satvaḥ utthāya + āsanāt svakaṃ gṛhaṃ prāvikṣat | yāvat sapta varṣāṇy eka-samādhi-samāpanna eva + abhūt | sadāprarudito bodhi-satvo mahā-satvaḥ sapta varṣāṇi na kāma-vitarkam utpādayām āsa | na vyāpāda-vitarkaṃ na vihiṃsā-vitarkam utpādayām āsa | na rasa-gṛddhim utpādayām āsa + anyatra | kadā nāma dharmodgato bodhi-satvo mahā-satvo vyutthāsyati | yad vayaṃ dharmodgatasya bodhi-satvasya mahā-satvasya dharma-āsanaṃ prajñāpayiṣyāmo yatra + asau kula-putro niṣadya dharmaṃ deśayiṣyati taṃ ca pṛthivī-pradeśaṃ siktaṃ saṃmṛṣṭaṃ ca kariṣyāmo nānā-puṣpa-abhikīrṇaṃ iti cintayām āsa ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>, rising from his seat, entered his own house. For seven years he remained absorbed in a single <s>samādhi</s>. The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, for seven years, did not produce a thought of sensual desire, did not produce a thought of ill-will, did not produce a thought of harmfulness, did not produce greed for flavors — [thinking of] nothing other than: 'When will the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s> emerge [from samādhi]? We shall prepare the <s>Dharma</s>-seat for the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>, where that son of good family, having sat down, will teach the <s>Dharma</s>; and we shall make that piece of ground sprinkled, swept, and strewn with various flowers' — thus he reflected.

body.text: tāny api śreṣṭhi-dārikā pramukhāṇi pañca-dārikā-śatāni sadāpraruditasya bodhi-satvasya + anuśikṣamāṇāni dvābhyām eva + īryā-pathābhyāṃ kālam atināmayām āsuḥ ||
body.translated_text: Those five hundred maidens, led by the merchant's daughter, following the example of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, passed their time in only two postures.

body.text: atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhi-satvo mahā-satvo divyaṃ nirghoṣam aśrauṣīd itaḥ saptame divase dharmodgato bodhi-satvo mahā-satvo * asmāt samādher vyutthāya madhye nagarasya niṣadya dharmaṃ deśayiṣyati + iti | atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhi-satvo mahā-satvas taṃ nirghoṣaṃ śrutvā ātta-manāḥ pramuditaḥ prīti-saumanasya-jātas taṃ pṛthivī-pradeśaṃ śodhayām āsa sārddhaṃ śreṣṭhi-dārikā-pramukhaiḥ pañcabhir dārikā-śatair dharma-āsanaṃ prajñapayām āsa sapta-ratna-mayaṃ | atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhi-satvo mahā-satvas taṃ pṛthivī-pradeśaṃ sektu-kāmaś ca | na ca + udakaṃ samantāt paryeṣamāṇo * api labhate yena taṃ pṛthivī-pradeśaṃ siñced | yathā + api nāma māreṇa pāpīyasā tat sarvam udakam antar-dhāpitaṃ apy eva nāma + asya + udakam a-labhamānasya cittaṃ duṣkhitaṃ syād daurmanasyaṃ ca bhavec cittasya vā + anyathātvaṃ bhaved yena + asya kuśala-mūla-antar-dhānaṃ bhaven na vā bhrājeran kuśala-mūlāni | atha khalu sadāpraruditasya bodhi-satvasya mahā-satvasya + etad abhūt | yan nv aham ātmanaḥ kāyaṃ viddhvā imaṃ pradeśaṃ rudhireṇa siñceyaṃ | tat kasya hetoḥ | ayaṃ hi pṛthivī-pradeśae uddhata-rajasko | mā rajo-dhātur ito dharmodgatasya bodhi-satvasya mahā-satvasya kāye nipatatu | kim aham anena + ātma-bhāvena + a-vaśyaṃ-bhedana-dharmiṇā kuryāṃ | varaṃ khalu punar mama + ayaṃ kāya evaṃ-rūpayā kriyayā vinaśyatu na ca niḥ-sāmarthya-kriyayā | kāma-hetoḥ kāma-nidānaṃ bahūni me ātma-bhāva-sahasrāṇi punaḥ punar a-parimāṇe saṃsāre saṃsarato bhinnāni | yadi punar bhidyante kāmam evaṃ-rūpeṣv iva dharma-sthāneṣu bhidyantāṃ ||
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sadāprarudita</s> (Ever-Weeping) <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> heard a divine voice: 'On the seventh day from now, <s>Dharmodgata</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> will arise from this <s>samādhi</s>, sit in the midst of the city, and teach the <s>Dharma</s>.' Then <s>Sadāprarudita</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, having heard that voice, delighted, joyful, filled with gladness and happiness, cleaned that area of ground together with five hundred maidens led by the merchant's daughter, and prepared a Dharma-seat made of the seven jewels. Then <s>Sadāprarudita</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, wishing to sprinkle that area, could not find water anywhere even after searching on all sides, with which to sprinkle that ground. It was as if <s>Māra</s>, the Evil One, had caused all the water to disappear, so that, not obtaining water, his mind might become distressed and despondency arise in his mind, or an alteration of mind might occur, whereby his wholesome roots might be destroyed or his wholesome roots might not shine. Then <s>Sadāprarudita</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> thought: 'Suppose I pierce my own body and sprinkle this ground with my blood. Why? For this ground is dusty with risen particles. Let not the dust-element from here fall upon the body of <s>Dharmodgata</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>. What use is this body to me, subject as it is to inevitable destruction? Better indeed that this body of mine perish through such an act than through a useless act. For the sake of desires, on account of desires, many thousands of my bodies have been broken again and again as I wandered through immeasurable <s>saṃsāra</s>. If they are to be broken, let them rather be broken in such Dharma-occasions as these!'

body.text: atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhi-satvo mahā-satva iti pratisaṃkhyāya tīkṣṇaṃ śastraṃ gṛhītvā sva-kāyaṃ samantato viddhvā taṃ pṛthivī-pradeśaṃ sva-rudhireṇa sarvam asiñcat | evaṃ tābhir api dārikābhiḥ kṛtaṃ | na ca sadāprarudito bodhi-satvasya mahā-satvasya tāsāṃ vā sarvāsāṃ dārikāṇāṃ cittasya + anyathātvam abhūt | yatra māraḥ pāpīyān avatāraṃ labheta + iti ||
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sadāprarudita</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, having reflected thus, took a sharp weapon, pierced his own body all over, and sprinkled that entire area of ground with his own blood. Likewise did all those maidens. And neither <s>Sadāprarudita</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>'s mind nor the minds of any of those maidens wavered — where <s>Māra</s>, the Evil One, might have found an opening.

body.text: ata evaṃ catur-dharmaka-sūtre * apy uktaṃ | kalyāṇa-mitraṃ bhikṣavo bodhi-satvena mahā-satvena yāvaj-jīvaṃ na parityaktavyam api jīvita-hetor iti ||
body.translated_text: Thus it is also said in the <s>Caturdharma Sūtra</s> (Sūtra of the Four Dharmas): 'O monks, a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) should never be abandoned by a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> as long as life lasts — not even for the sake of one's life.'

body.text: tad evaṃ kalyāṇa-mitra-an-utsargād ātma-bhāva-ādīnāṃ rakṣā-ādikaṃ kāryaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Thus, through non-abandonment of the spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), one should perform the protection and so forth of one's own body and the rest.

body.text: sūtrāṇāṃ ca sadā + īkṣaṇād bodhi-satva-śikṣā-padāni hi prāyaḥ sūtreṣv eva dṛśyante | teṣu teṣu sūtra-anteṣu bodhi-satva-samudācārā bodhi-satva-śikṣā-padāni prajñaptāni + iti vacanāt | tasmāt tad-an-īkṣaṇe mā bhūd āpattim āpannasya + apy a-jñānād a-viratir iti sadā sūtra-darśanāya + ādaraḥ kāryaḥ | tad anena kalyāṇa-mitra-an-utsargeṇa sūtra-anta-darśanena ca sarvaḥ sad-dharma-parigraha ukto bhavati ||
body.translated_text: And through constant examination of the <s>sūtras</s> — for the training rules of the <s>bodhisattva</s> are for the most part seen in the <s>sūtras</s> themselves; as stated in the conclusions of those various <s>sūtras</s>: 'The conduct of the <s>bodhisattva</s> and the training rules of the <s>bodhisattva</s> have been set forth.' Therefore, lest one who has fallen into a transgression should, through ignorance, fail to refrain [from it], one should always make an effort to examine the <s>sūtras</s>. By this non-abandonment of the spiritual friend and this examination of the <s>sūtra</s>-conclusions, the entire embrace of the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharma-parigraha</s>) is stated.

body.text: yathā + uktam ārya-sāgaramati-sūtre | yābhir akṣara-niruktibhiḥ so * an-abhilāpyo dharmaḥ sūcyate tāsām akṣara-niruktīnāṃ yadā dhāraṇaṃ deśanā yāvad | ayam ucyate sad-dharma-parigrahaḥ | punar a-paraṃ kula-putra ye te dharma-bhāṇakā eṣām evaṃ-rūpāṇāṃ sūtra-antānāṃ deśayitāraḥ pratipatti-sārāś ca teṣām api dharma-bhāṇakānāṃ yat sevanaṃ bhajanaṃ paryupāsanam utthānam upasthānaṃ gauravaṃ citrī-kāraḥ śuśrūṣā ārakṣā parigrahaś cīvara-piṇḍa-pātra-śayana-āsana-glāna-pratyaya-bhaiṣajya-pariṣkāra-dānaṃ sādhu-kāra-dānaṃ svāmy--ārakṣā kuśala-pakṣa-rakṣā varṇa-bhāṣaṇam a-varṇa-praticchādanatā | ayam api sad-dharma-parigrahaḥ | peyālaṃ ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Ārya-Sāgaramati Sūtra</s>: 'The syllables and etymologies by which that inexpressible <s>Dharma</s> is indicated — when there is the retention, teaching [and so on] of those syllables and etymologies — this is called the embrace of the true <s>Dharma</s>. Furthermore, O son of good family, those <s>Dharma</s>-preachers who are teachers of such <s>sūtra</s>-conclusions and whose essence is practice — attending upon, serving, honoring, rising for, waiting upon, respecting, esteeming, heeding, guarding, and supporting those <s>Dharma</s>-preachers; giving them robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines for the sick as requisites; giving them praise; protecting them as one's own; guarding the faction of wholesome [dharmas]; speaking well of them; concealing their faults — this too is the embrace of the true <s>Dharma</s>. [Abbreviation.]'

body.text: punar a-paraṃ kula-putra yā a-vivāda-paramatā | a-dharme dharma-vādināṃ ca pudgalānāṃ saha dharmeṇa nigrahaḥ | ayam api sad-dharma-parigrahaḥ | punar a-paraṃ kula-putra + a-pratihata-santānasya sarva-satva-pramokṣa-buddher nir-āmiṣa-cittasya parebhyo dharma-dānam ayam api sad-dharma-parigrahaḥ | punar a-paraṃ kula-putra yo dharma-śravaṇa-hetuko vā dharma-deśanā-hetuko vā + antaśa eka-krama-vyatihāro * antaśa eka-ucchvāsa-praśvāso vā | ayam api sad-dharma-parigrahaḥ | peyālaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O son of good family, the supreme state of non-contentiousness; and the defeat, in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, of persons who declare what is not <s>Dharma</s> to be <s>Dharma</s> — this too is the embrace of the true <s>Dharma</s>. Furthermore, O son of good family, the gift of <s>Dharma</s> to others by one of unbroken continuity, whose mind is set on liberating all beings, whose mind is without material gain — this too is the embrace of the true <s>Dharma</s>. Furthermore, O son of good family, even a single step taken for the sake of hearing the <s>Dharma</s> or for the sake of teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, or even a single breath — this too is the embrace of the true <s>Dharma</s>. [Abbreviation.]

body.text: prahrutaṃ vata + idaṃ kula-putra cittaṃ viṣayeṣu | tasya yā nivāraṇā parirakṣā eka-agrī-bhāvo damaḥ śama upaśamo vinayo * ayam ucyate sad-dharma-parigrahaḥ | peyālaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'This mind, O son of good family, has indeed been scattered among the sense-objects. Its restraint, its guarding, its one-pointedness, its taming, its calming, its pacification, its discipline — this is called the embrace of the true <s>Dharma</s>.' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: punar a-paraṃ kula-putra yena dharmeṇa yo * a-dharmaḥ pravartate tasya dharmasya + a-parigraho * an-upādānam ayam api sad-dharma-parigraha ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O son of good family, the non-grasping and non-appropriation of that <s>dharma</s> by which what is not <s>dharma</s> prevails — this too is the embrace of the true <s>Dharma</s>, and so forth.

body.text: tatr dharma-bhāṇaka-sevā-ādinā kalyāṇa-mitra-an-utsarga uktaḥ | kalyāṇa-mitra-lakṣaṇaṃ ca | tad etena sad-dharma-parigraheṇa vinā | na rakṣā | na śuddhir na vṛddhis

children.text: tataś ca so * api na bodhi-satva ity a-vaśya-kāryaḥ sad-dharma-parigrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, one who lacks this is not a <s>bodhisattva</s> — hence the embrace of the true <s>Dharma</s> is absolutely necessary.

body.translated_text: Among these, by the attending upon <s>Dharma</s>-preachers and the like, non-abandonment of the spiritual friend is stated; and the characteristics of a spiritual friend [are given]. Thus, without this embrace of the true <s>Dharma</s>, there is no protection, no purification, no growth.

body.text: uktaṃ hi śrī-mālā-siṃha-nāda-sūtre | yāny api + imāni bhagavan gaṅgā-nadī-vālikā-samāni bodhi-satva-praṇidhānāni tāny ekasmin mahā-praṇidhāne upanikṣiptāny antar-gatāny anupratiṣṭhāni yad uta sad-dharma-parigrahe | evaṃ mahā-viṣayo bhagavan sad-dharma-parigraha iti ||
body.translated_text: For it is said in the <s>Śrīmālā-siṃhanāda Sūtra</s>: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, even those <s>bodhisattva</s>-aspirations as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> are all included in, contained within, and established upon one great aspiration — namely, the embrace of the true <s>Dharma</s>. So vast, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the scope of the embrace of the true <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: punar atra + eva + āha | syād yathā + api nāma devi mahā-balavato * api puruṣasya + alpo * api marmaṇi prahāro | vedhanīyo bhavati vādhā-karaś ca | evam eva devi mārasya pāpīyasaḥ parītto * api sad-dharma-parigraho vedhanīyo bhavati śoka-āvahaḥ parideva-karaś ca bhavati | na + ahaṃ devi anyam ekam api dharmaṃ kuśalaṃ samanupaśyāmi mārasya pāpīyasa evaṃ vedhanīyaṃ śoka-āvahaṃ parideva-karaṃ ca | yathā + ayam alpo * api sad-dharma-parigraha iti ||
body.translated_text: And further in that same [sūtra] it says: 'O Queen, just as even a slight blow to a vital point is painful and harmful even to a very strong man — just so, O Queen, even a small embrace of the true <s>Dharma</s> is painful to <s>Māra</s>, the Evil One, and brings him grief and lamentation. I do not see, O Queen, any other single wholesome <s>dharma</s> that is so painful, grief-bringing, and lamentation-producing for <s>Māra</s>, the Evil One, as even this small embrace of the true <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: punar āha | syād yathā + api nāma devi sumeruḥ parvata-rājaḥ sarvān kula-parvatān abhibhavann abhirocate ca samabhirocate ca + uccatvena vipulatvena ca | evam eva devi mahā-yānikasya kāya-jīvita-nir-apekṣasya na ca gṛhīta-cittasya sad-dharma-parigraho nava-yāna-saṃprasthitānām api kāya-jīvita-sa-apekṣāṇāṃ mahā-yānikānāṃ sarvān kuśalān dharmān abhibhavati + ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: And further it says: 'O Queen, just as <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, surpasses all the surrounding mountain ranges and shines forth in height and breadth — just so, O Queen, the embrace of the true <s>Dharma</s> by a <s>Mahāyāna</s> practitioner who is without concern for body and life, whose mind is not attached, surpasses all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> even of those <s>Mahāyāna</s> practitioners who are newly set out on the vehicle and who still have concern for body and life,' and so forth.

body.text: tathā + ārya-sāgaramati-sūtre * apy āha | parigṛhīto bhavatī jinebhir devebhi nāgebhi ca kinnarebhiḥ | puṇyena jñānena parigṛhītaḥ sad-dharma-dhāritva tathā-gatānām ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, in the <s>Ārya-Sāgaramati Sūtra</s> it also says: 'He is embraced by the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones), by the gods, <s>nāgas</s>, and <s>kinnaras</s>; embraced by merit and knowledge — through upholding the true <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

body.text: peyālaṃ ||
body.translated_text: [Abbreviation.]

body.text: sa śūnya-kṣetreṣu na jātu jāyate sarvatra jātau ca jinaṃ sa paśyati | dṛṣṭvā ca tasmiṃl labhate prasādaṃ sad-dharma-dhāritva tathā-gatānām ||
body.translated_text: 'He is never born in empty fields; wherever he is born, he sees the <s>Jina</s> (Victor); and having seen him, he obtains faith — through upholding the true <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

body.text: jāti-smaro bhavati mahā-ātma-dharmā pravrajya-lābhī bhavate punaḥ punaḥ | pariśuddha-cārī pratipatti-sāraḥ sad-dharma-dhāritva tathā-gatānām ||
body.translated_text: 'He becomes one who remembers past births, great-souled, righteous; he obtains the going-forth again and again; of purified conduct, whose essence is practice — through upholding the true <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

body.text: peyālaṃ ||
body.translated_text: [Abbreviation.]

body.text: lābhī ca bhotī vidu-dhāraṇīye na naśyate kalpa-śatebhi yac-chubham | pratibhānavanto bhavate a-saktaḥ sad-dharma-dhāritva tathā-gatānāṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'He obtains the <s>dhāraṇīs</s> (retentions) of the wise; what is wholesome does not perish for hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>; he becomes eloquent and unattached — through upholding the true <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

body.text: śakro * atha brahmā tatha loka-pāl-o manuṣya-rājā bhuvi cakra-varttī | sukhena saukhyena sa bodhi budhyate sad-dharma-dhāritva tathā-gatānām ||
body.translated_text: '<s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, the world-protectors, a king of men, a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal sovereign) on earth — he attains <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) with ease and happiness — through upholding the true <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

body.text: dvātriṃśa kāye * asya bhavanti lakṣaṇāḥ a-nindita-aṅgo bhavate vi-cakṣaṇaḥ | na tasya tṛptiṃ labhi prekṣamāṇāḥ sad-dharma-dhāritva tathā-gatānām ||
body.translated_text: 'The thirty-two marks appear on his body; he becomes one of blameless limbs, discerning; those who behold him find no satiation — through upholding the true <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

body.text: na tasya saṃmuhyati bodhi cittaṃ na ca + uddhuraḥ pāramitā carīṣu | a-saṃgṛhītaḥ kuśalaḥ śatebhiḥ sad-dharma-dhāritva tathā-gatānām iti ||
body.translated_text: 'His mind of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) does not become confused, nor is he disheartened in the practice of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections); skilled and unhindered by hundreds [of obstacles] — through upholding the true <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

body.text: śīla-pāramitāyāṃ sad-dharma-parigraho nāma dvitīyaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The second chapter, called the Embrace of the True <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharma-parigraha</s>), in [the section on] the Perfection of Moral Conduct (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>). //

body.text: dharma-bhāṇaka-ādi-rakṣā tṛtīyaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The third chapter: Protection of <s>Dharma</s>-preachers and Others (<s>dharmabhāṇakādirakṣā</s>). //

body.text: uktas trayāṇām api sāmānyena rakṣā-ādy-upāyaḥ | rakṣā-ādayas tu vācyāḥ | tatra + ātma-bhāve kā rakṣā yad an-artha-vivarjanaṃ ||
body.translated_text: The means of protection and so forth for all three [— body, speech, and mind —] have been stated in general. But the protection and the rest are to be specified. Therein, what is the protection of one's own body? It is the avoidance of harm.

body.text: tatra + iti sad-dharma-parigrahe varttamānasya + ātma-bhāva-rakṣā cintyate yathā parān na nāśayet | idaṃ ca an-artha-vivarjanam ārya-gagana-gañja-sūtre sad-dharma-dhāraṇa-udyatair bodhi-satvair bhāṣitaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Therein — for one engaged in the embrace of the true <s>Dharma</s>, the protection of one's own body is considered so that one does not destroy others. And this avoidance of harm has been spoken by <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are devoted to upholding the true <s>Dharma</s> in the <s>Ārya-Gaganagañja Sūtra</s>:

body.text: vayam utsahāmo bhagavan nirvṛte dvi-pada-uttame | sad-dharmaṃ dhārayiṣyāmaḥ tyaktvā kāyaṃ sva-jīvitam ||
body.translated_text: 'We are resolved, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, when the Supreme Among Bipeds has passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>, to uphold the true <s>Dharma</s>, having abandoned body and life itself.'

body.text: lābha-sat-kāram utsṛṣṭvā sarvaṃ ca + utsṛjya saṃstavaṃ | an-utsṛṣṭvā imaṃ dharmaṃ buddha-jñāna-nidarśakam ||
body.translated_text: 'Having relinquished gain and honor, and having abandoned all association, without abandoning this <s>Dharma</s> that reveals the knowledge of the <s>Buddha</s>.'

body.text: ākrośa-paribhāṣāṃś ca dur-ukta-vacanāni ca | kṣāntyā tān marṣayiṣyāmaḥ sad-dharma-pratisaṃgrahāt ||
body.translated_text: 'And abuse, reproach, and harsh words — we shall endure them with patience, for the sake of embracing the true <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: uccagghanāṃ tarjanāṃ ca a-varṇam a-yaśāṃsi ca | sarvāṃs tān marṣayiṣyāmo dhārayanta imaṃ nayam || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'Loud threats, intimidation, ill-repute, and dishonor — we shall endure all these while upholding this way.' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: evaṃ-vidhe mahā-ghore bhikṣu-rājāna-kṣobhaṇe | vilopa-kāle satvānāṃ sad-dharmaṃ dhārayāmahe ||
body.translated_text: 'In such a greatly fearsome [time], when monks are disturbed and agitated by kings, when beings are plundered — we shall uphold the true <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: gambhīrā ye ca sūtra-antā vimukti-phala-saṃhitāḥ | pratīcchakā na bhesyanti | citrā mṛkṣyanti te kathās || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'Those profound <s>sūtra</s>-conclusions that are endowed with the fruit of liberation — their hearers will not be afraid; those marvelous discourses will be sought out.' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: maitrīṃ teṣu kariṣyāmo ye dharmeṣv a-pratiṣṭhitāḥ | kāruṇyaṃ ca kariṣyāmo dhārayanta imaṃ nayam ||
body.translated_text: 'We shall practice loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) toward those who are not established in the <s>dharmas</s>; and we shall practice compassion (<s>kāruṇya</s>) while upholding this way.'

body.text: dṛṣṭvā duḥ-śīla-satvāṃś ca icchā-lobha-pratiṣṭhitān | aśru-pātaṃ kariṣyāmo gatiḥ kāndhasya bhāvitā ||
body.translated_text: 'And seeing beings of corrupt morality, established in desire and greed, we shall shed tears, [reflecting:] "The destination of the pitiable one has been cultivated."'

body.text: sahasā + eva ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā sad-dharma-pratibādhakaṃ | dūrato maitram eṣyāmo mā no ruṣyeta eva hi ||
body.translated_text: 'And seeing him who obstructs the true <s>Dharma</s> even rashly, we shall approach from afar with friendliness — lest indeed he become angry with us.'

body.text: rakṣiṣyāmo yathā-śaktyā vācā-karmasu saṃvṛtāḥ | sahasā + enān na vakṣyāmaḥ sva-pāpe * asmin pratiṣṭhitān ||
body.translated_text: 'We shall protect [them] as far as we are able, restrained in speech and action; we shall not speak to them rashly — those established in their own sins.'

body.text: dānais tathā + api sat-kāraiḥ paripācya + iha tān narān | paścā + enāṃś codayiṣyāmo bhūtam āpāya-go-carān ||
body.translated_text: 'And by gifts and likewise by honors, having ripened those people here, afterwards we shall urge them — [those who are] truly destined for the lower realms.'

body.text: gṛhi-saṃbhava-saṃtyaktāḥ prānta-araṇya-su-go-carāḥ | mṛga-bhūtā bhaviṣyāmo * alpa-arthā alpa-kṛtyakāḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: Having abandoned that which arises from householder life, dwelling well in remote forests, we shall become like deer, with few possessions and few duties. And so forth.

body.text: dāntāḥ śāntāś ca muktāś ca grāme * asminn avatīrya ca | deśayiṣyāmahe dharmaṃ satvā ye dharmata-arthikā ||
body.translated_text: Tamed, tranquil, and liberated, having descended into this village, we shall teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings who seek the meaning of the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: su-dūram api yāsyāmo dharma-kāmān niśamya ca | dharma-ārāma-rati-prāptā arthaṃ karttā + asma dehinām ||
body.translated_text: We shall go even very far, having heard of those who desire the <s>Dharma</s>; having attained delight in the garden of the <s>Dharma</s>, we shall act for the benefit of embodied beings.

body.text: saṃmukhaṃ tatra saṃdṛśya satvānāṃ skhalitaṃ pṛthu | ātma-prekṣā bhaviṣyāmo dharma-sauratya-saṃsthitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Having directly seen there the manifold failings of beings, we shall become self-watchful, established in gentleness toward the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: a-sat-kṛtāḥ sat-kṛtā vā meru-kalpāḥ prabhūya ca | an-upaliptā lokena bhesyāmo loka-nāyakāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Whether dishonored or honored, steadfast like Mount <s>Meru</s>, and untainted by the world, we shall become leaders of the world.

body.text: bhikṣūṇāṃ bhinna-vṛttānāṃ parivādaṃ niśamya ca | karma-svakā bhavisyāmo mā + eṣāṃ karma vipacyatām ||
body.translated_text: Having heard the censure of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) who have broken their conduct, we shall regard them as owners of their own <s>karma</s> — may not their <s>karma</s> ripen upon us!

body.text: badhakān yojayiṣyanti dharmeṣv eṣu hi vartatāṃ | ete dharmā na ca + asmākaṃ saṃvidyante kathañ-cana ||
body.translated_text: Obstructors will engage them in these <s>dharmas</s> in which they abide, saying: 'These <s>dharmas</s> are in no way found in us.'

body.text: asmākaṃ śramaṇānāṃ hi na ca śrāmaṇakā guṇāḥ | bhūtāṃ codana saṃśrutya idaṃ sūtraṃ pratikṣipan ||
body.translated_text: 'For us who are ascetics, the qualities of the ascetic life are absent.' Having heard a true reproach, they reject this <s>sūtra</s>.

body.text: saṃchinna-karṇa-nāsānām ādarśā + eṣāṃ kutaḥ priyaḥ | codanāṃ bhūtataḥ śrutvā sad-dharmaṃ te kṣipanti tam ||
body.translated_text: For those whose ears and noses have been cut off, how could a mirror be pleasing? Having heard the reproach as it truly is, they reject the <s>Saddharma</s> (true Dharma).

body.text: ye bhikṣavo bhaviṣyanti sad-dharma-pratigrāhakāḥ | ceṣṭiṣyante tathā teṣāṃ kaś-cid dharmam imaṃ śṛṇot ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) there will be who uphold the <s>Saddharma</s> (true Dharma), they will act against them so that no one may hear this <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: rājāno grāhayiṣyanti bhesyanti ca mahā-janaḥ | buddha-adhiṣṭhānataḥ satvā dharmaṃ śroṣyanti + imaṃ
body.translated_text: Kings will cause them to be seized, and great multitudes will arise; yet by the blessing of the <s>Buddha</s>, beings will hear this <s>Dharma</s>

body.text: tasmin kāle vayaṃ kaṣṭe tyaktvā kāyaṃ sa-jīvitaṃ | sad-dharmaṃ dhārayiṣyāmaḥ satvānāṃ hita-kāraṇād | iti ||
body.translated_text: In that difficult time, having abandoned body and life, we shall uphold the <s>Saddharma</s> (true Dharma) for the sake of the welfare of beings. Thus.

body.text: ārya-sad-dharma-puṇḍarīke * apy uktaṃ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> (Noble Lotus of the True Dharma) also it is said:

body.text: ācāra-go-cara-rakṣī a-saṃsṛṣṭaḥ śucir bhavet | varjayet saṃstavaṃ nityaṃ rāja-putrebhi rājabhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: One who guards one's <s>ācāra</s> (conduct) and <s>gocara</s> (domain) should be unassociated and pure; one should always avoid familiarity with princes and kings.

body.text: ye ca + api rājñāṃ puruṣāḥ kuryāt te hi na saṃstavaṃ | caṇḍāla-muṣṭikaiḥ śauṇḍais tīrthikaiś ca + api sarvaśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: And also the servants of kings — one should not cultivate familiarity with them, nor with <s>caṇḍālas</s> (outcasts), boxers, drunkards, and <s>tīrthikas</s> (heretics) of every kind.

body.text: adhimānīn na seveta

children.text: vinayec ca + āgame sthitān | arhanta-saṃmatān bhikṣūn duḥ-śīlāṃś ca + eva varjayet ||
children.translated_text: but should discipline those established in the <s>Āgama</s> (scripture); one should avoid <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) regarded as <s>arhats</s> (worthy ones) and also those of bad moral conduct.

body.translated_text: One should not attend upon the conceited,

body.text: bhikṣuṇīṃ varjayen nityaṃ hāsya-saṃlāpa-go-carāṃ | upāsikāś ca varjeyā prakaṭam an-avasthitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: One should always avoid a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun) whose domain is laughter and idle talk; and one should avoid <s>upāsikās</s> (laywomen) who are openly unstable.

body.text: strī-paṇḍakāś ca ye satvāḥ saṃstavaṃ tair vivarjayet | kuleṣu ca + api vadhukāḥ kumāryaś ca vivarjayet ||
body.translated_text: And whatever beings are women or <s>paṇḍakas</s> (eunuchs), one should avoid familiarity with them; and also in families one should avoid young brides and maidens.

body.text: na tāḥ saṃmodayej jātu kauśalyaṃ sādhu pṛcchitṛṃ

children.translated_text: and one should avoid familiarity with pig-herders and sheep-butchers.

body.translated_text: One should never greet them nor inquire after their well-being with solicitude,

body.text: strī-poṣakāś ca ye satvā varjayet tehi saṃstavaṃ | naṭair jhallaka-mallebhir ye ca + anye tādṛśā janāḥ ||
body.translated_text: And whatever beings are those who support women, one should avoid familiarity with them; actors, acrobats, wrestlers, and whatever other such people there are —

body.text: vāra-mukhyān na seveta ye ca + anye bhoga-vṛttinaḥ | pratisaṃmodanaṃ tebhiḥ sarvaśaḥ parivarjayet ||
body.translated_text: one should not attend upon chief courtesans and others who live by sensual pleasures; one should entirely avoid reciprocal greetings with them.

body.text: yadā ca dharmaṃ deśeyā mātṛ-grāmasya paṇḍito | na ca + ekaḥ praviśet tatra na + api hāsya-sthito bhaved iti ||
body.translated_text: And when the wise one teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to women, one should not enter there alone, nor should one remain in a state of levity. Thus.

body.text: ayaṃ ca + a-paro * an-artho bhaved yad idaṃ māra-karma + uktaṃ prajñā-pāramitāyāṃ | māraḥ pāpīyāṃs tasya bodhi-satvasya + a-ciraṃ yāna-saṃprasthitasya + antike balavattaram udyogam āpatsyate | atra + eva + āha | punar a-param ānanda yasmin samaye bodhi-satvo mahā-satvaḥ prajñā-pāramitāyāṃ yogam āpadyate tasmin samaye mārāḥ pāpīyāṃso bodhi-satvasya viheṭhanam upasaṃharanti bhayaṃ saṃjanayanti | ulkā-pātān diśi dig-vahān utsṛjanti saṃdarśayanti | apy eva nāma + ayaṃ bodhi-satvo mahā-satvo * avanīyeta vā roma-harṣo vā + asya bhaved iti | yena + asya + eka-citta-utpādo * api kṣīyeta + an-uttarāyāḥ samyak-saṃbodher iti | punar a-param anya-vijñāna-saṃjñino likhiṣyanti yāvat paryavāpsyanti | na vayam atra + āsvādaṃ labhāmahe ity utthāya + āsanāt prakramiṣyanti | evaṃ vijṛmbhamāṇā uccagghanto yāvat paryavāpsyanti + iti māra-karma | evam utpatsyante jana-pada-grāma-ādi-vitarkāḥ | evam ācārya-upādhyāya-mātā-pitṛ-mitra-amātya-jñāti-sālohita-manasi-kārāḥ | evaṃ cora-manasi-kārāḥ | evaṃ cīvara-ādi-manasi-kārāḥ | punar a-paraṃ dharma-bhāṇakaś chandiko bhaviṣyati imāṃ gambhīrāṃ prajñā-pāramitāṃ lekhayituṃ yāvad vācayitu.ṃ dharma-śravaṇikaś ca kilāsī bhaviṣyati | evaṃ viparyayāt | dharma-bhāṇakaś ca deśa-antaraṃ gantu-kāmo bhaviṣyati dhārma-śravaṇikāś ca na + iti neyaṃ | evaṃ dharma-bhāṇako mahā-iccho bhaviṣyati dhārma-śravaṇiko * alpa-iccha iti neyaṃ | saṃkṣepād dharma-bhāṇaka-dhārma-śravaṇikayor yā kā-cid vidhuratā sarvaṃ tan māra-karma + ity uktaṃ ||
body.translated_text: And this is yet another danger, namely what is called <s>māra-karma</s> (the work of Māra). It is said in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom): '<s>Māra</s>, the Evil One, will exert the most powerful effort against the <s>bodhisattva</s> who has recently set out on the vehicle.' Therein it also says: 'Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, at the time when the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> (great being) engages in the practice of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, at that time the evil <s>Māras</s> bring forth harassment against the <s>bodhisattva</s>, generate fear, and release and display showers of meteors blazing in every direction — thinking: "Perhaps this <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> might be led astray, or his hair might stand on end," — so that even a single arising of his thought toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening) might be destroyed. Furthermore, those perceiving other consciousness will write and so forth will obtain it, saying: "We do not find any savor in this," and rising from their seats will depart. Thus yawning and laughing loudly, and so forth they will obtain it — this is <s>māra-karma</s>. Thus will arise thoughts about countries, villages, and so forth. Thus will arise preoccupations with teachers, preceptors, mothers, fathers, friends, counselors, relatives, and kinsmen. Thus will arise preoccupations with thieves. Thus will arise preoccupations with robes and so forth. Furthermore, the <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> (Dharma-preacher) will be eager to have this profound <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> written and so forth up to recited, while the <s>dharmaśravaṇika</s> (Dharma-listener) will be afflicted with a skin disease. And conversely: the <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> will desire to go to another region, while the <s>dharmaśravaṇikas</s> will not — this should be understood. Thus the <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> will be of great desires while the <s>dharmaśravaṇika</s> will be of few desires — this should be understood. In brief, whatever discord there is between the <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> and the <s>dharmaśravaṇika</s>, all that is called <s>māra-karma</s>.'

body.text: ārya-gagana-gañja-sūtre * apy uktaṃ | iti hi yāvad a-kuśala-dharma-anuvarttanatā | kuśala-dharma-utsargaś ca sarvaṃ tan māra-karma + iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Gaganagañja-sūtra</s> also it is said: 'Thus, as far as conforming to unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> and abandoning wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — all that is <s>māra-karma</s>.'

body.text: ārya-sāgaramati-sūtre * apy āha | punar a-paraṃ bhagavan bodhi-satva āraṇyako bhavati prānta-śayyā-āsana-abhirato * alpa-icchuḥ saṃtuṣṭaḥ pravivikto * a-saṃsṛṣṭo gṛha-stha-pravrajitaiḥ | so * alpa-arthatayā + alpa-kṛtyatayā ca sukhaṃ viharati na ca bāhaśrutya-paryeṣṭāv abhiyukto bhavati na satva-paripākāya na ca dharma-śravaṇe vā dharma-sāṃkathhye vā + artha-viniścaya-kathāyāṃ vā vartamānāyāṃ saṃkramitavyaṃ manyate | na paripṛcchana-jātīyo bhavati | na kiṃ-kuśala-abhiyukto bhavati | tasya + araṇya-vāsena ca + eka-ārāma-ratitayā ca kleśā na samudācaranti | sa paryutthāna-viṣkambhaṇa-mātreṇa tuṣṭiṃ vindati | na ca + anuśaya-samudyātāya mārgaṃ bhāvayati | sa tatra na + ātma-arthāya pratipanno bhavati na para-arthāya | ayaṃ bhagavan bodhi-satvasya + araṇya-vāsa-pratisaṃyuktaḥ saptamo māra-aṅkuśa iti || pe ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Sāgaramati-sūtra</s> also it says: 'Furthermore, O <s>Bhagavan</s> (Lord), the <s>bodhisattva</s> dwells in the forest, delighting in remote beds and seats, of few desires, contented, secluded, unassociated with householders and renunciants. Through having few possessions and few duties, he dwells at ease, but he is not devoted to the pursuit of great learning, nor to the maturing of beings, nor does he think one should go to where discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, discussion of the <s>Dharma</s>, or determination of meaning is taking place. He is not one who asks questions. He is not devoted to what is wholesome. Through his forest-dwelling and delight in solitary retreat, the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) do not actively arise. He finds satisfaction merely in suppressing the active afflictions, but does not cultivate the path for uprooting the latent tendencies. Thus he is not practicing for his own benefit nor for the benefit of others. This, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, is the seventh hook of <s>Māra</s> connected with the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s forest-dwelling.' And so forth.

body.text: punar a-paraṃ bhagavan bodhi-satvaḥ kalyāṇa-mitra-prati-rūpakāṇi pāpa-mitrāṇi sevate bhajate paryupāste | ye hy enaṃ saṃgraha-vastubhyo vicchandya puṇya-saṃbhārāt sad-dharma-parigrahād vicchandya praviveke niyojayanti | alpa-arthāya + alpa-kṛtyatāyāṃ niyojayanti | śrāvaka-praty-eka-buddha-pratisaṃyuktāś ca + asmai kathā abhīkṣṇaṃ deśayanti ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> attends upon, associates with, and serves evil friends who appear as good friends. For they dissuade him from the means of gathering beings, from the accumulation of merit, from upholding the <s>Saddharma</s> (true Dharma), and engage him in seclusion. They engage him in having few possessions and few duties. And they frequently teach him discourses connected with the <s>Śrāvaka</s> (Disciple) and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (Solitary Awakened One) vehicles.'

body.text: yasmiṃś ca samaye bodhi-satvo viveka-vāsena mahā-yāne * abhyudgacchet tasmin samaye taṃ bodhi-satvaṃ vaiyāvṛtya-palibodhe niyojayanti vaiyāvṛtyaṃ bodhi-satvena + a-vaśyaṃ karaṇīyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'And at the time when the <s>bodhisattva</s> through dwelling in seclusion would advance in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle), at that time they engage that <s>bodhisattva</s> in the hindrance of service obligations, saying: Service must necessarily be performed by a <s>bodhisattva</s>.'

body.text: yasmiṃś ca samaye bodhi-satvo vaiyāvṛtye saṃniyojayitavyas tasmin samaye viveke niyojayanti | evaṃ ca + enaṃ vadanti | ārabdha-vīryasya bodhi-satvasya bodhir na ku-sīdasya | sacet tvam aṣṭābhir navabhir vā kalpair an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhiṃ na + abhisaṃbhotsyase | na bhūyaḥ śakyasy an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhim abhisaṃboddhum | tatra bhagavan | bodhi-satvo * aty-ārabdhena vīryeṇa sthānaṃ khalu punar etad vidyate yan nirvāṇa-phalaṃ prāpnuyād | ayaṃ bhagavan | bodhi-satvasya kalyāṇa-mitra-prati-rūpakeṇa daśamo māra-aṅkuśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'And at the time when the <s>bodhisattva</s> should be engaged in service obligations, at that time they engage him in seclusion. And they say to him thus: Awakening is for the <s>bodhisattva</s> of exerted effort, not for the lazy one. If you will not attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening) in eight or nine <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), you will never again be able to attain unsurpassed perfect awakening. In that case, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, with excessively exerted effort there is indeed the possibility that the <s>bodhisattva</s> might attain the fruit of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. This, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, is the tenth hook of <s>Māra</s> through the semblance of a good friend for the <s>bodhisattva</s>.'

body.text: ye * api tato * anye bodhi-satva-yānīyāḥ pudgalā māra-aṅkuśa-āviddhāḥ pratyaveteṣu dharmeṣu caranti taiḥ sārddhaṃ ratiṃ vindati | tathā hi tad-anuvarttakā bhavanti sa hīna-sevī viśeṣam an-adhigato hīna-gatiṃ gacchati yad uta dhanva-gatiṃ jaḍa-eḍa-mūka-gatiṃ yāvad ekādaśo māra-aṅkuśa iti ||
body.translated_text: 'And whatever other persons belonging to the <s>Bodhisattvayāna</s> (Bodhisattva Vehicle), who are pierced by the hooks of <s>Māra</s>, practice inferior <s>dharmas</s> — he finds delight together with them. For they become his followers; he, associating with the inferior, not having attained distinction, goes to a lower destiny — namely, the destiny of a desert-wanderer, the destiny of one who is dull, stammering, and mute — and so forth, this is the eleventh hook of <s>Māra</s>.'

body.text: yena ca + evaṃ saṃtaty-ārabdha-vīryasya nir-vedāt sarvathā bodhi-satva-bhāva eva bhavaty ata eva ratna-meghe * abhihitaṃ | iha bodhi-satvaḥ sarva-īryā-patheṣu vīryam ārabhate | tathā ca + ārabhate yathā na kāya-khedaṃ saṃjanayati | na citta-khed.am | idam ucyate bodhi-satvasya sāṃtatya-vīryam iti | kīdṛśaṃ tad vīryaṃ | yena khedo bhavati | yad idam alpa-balasya guru-karma-ārambho * ati-velāyāṃ vā + a-paripakva-adhimukter vā duṣkara-karma-ārambhas tad yathā sva-māṃsa-dāna-ādiḥ | dattaś ca + anena + ātma-bhāvaḥ | kintv a-kāla-paribhogād vārayati | anyathā hi teṣām eva satvānāṃ bodhi-satva-khedena bodhi-citta-vīja-nāśān mahataḥ phala-rāśer nāśaḥ syāt ||
body.translated_text: And for one whose effort is thus continuously exerted, it is precisely through disenchantment that the state of a <s>bodhisattva</s> itself comes about. Therefore in the <s>Ratnamegha</s> (Jewel Cloud Sūtra) it is stated: 'Here the <s>bodhisattva</s> exerts effort in all postures. And he exerts himself in such a way that he does not produce bodily exhaustion nor mental exhaustion. This is called the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s continuous effort.' What kind of effort is that which produces exhaustion? It is the undertaking of a heavy task by one of little strength, or the undertaking of difficult practices at an untimely occasion or by one whose aspiration is not yet matured — such as the giving of one's own flesh and so forth. And one has given one's own body; but one restrains from untimely consumption. For otherwise, through the exhaustion of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, from the destruction of the seed of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the thought of awakening) in those very beings, there would be the destruction of a great heap of fruit.

body.text: ataś ca gagana-gañja-sūtre * abhihitaṃ | a-kāla-pratikāṅkṣaṇatā māra-karma + iti | na + apy a-kāla ity ātma-bhāva-tyāga-cittam eva na + utpādya + abhyāsa-an-ārambhād * dhi na kadā-cid dadyāt | tasmād evaṃ smṛtim upāsthāpya bodhi-citta-paripācana-virodhibhyo mohāt sva-artha-ghātibhyaḥ piśita-aśanebhyaḥ karma-kāribhyaś ca + ātma-bhāvo rakṣitavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: And therefore in the <s>Gaganagañja-sūtra</s> it is stated: 'Aspiring at an untimely moment is <s>māra-karma</s>.' Yet neither should one, thinking 'it is untimely,' fail to even generate the thought of abandoning one's own body, for through not undertaking the practice one would never give. Therefore, having established mindfulness thus, one's own body should be protected from those who, through delusion, would obstruct the maturation of <s>bodhicitta</s>, who would destroy one's own welfare, from flesh-eaters and from those who would act upon their <s>karma</s>.

body.text: bhaiṣajya-vṛkṣasya su-darśanasya mūla-ādi-bhogyasya yathā + eva vījaṃ | dattvā + api saṃrakṣyam a-kāla-bhogāt saṃbuddha-bhaiṣajya-taros tathā + eva ||
body.translated_text: Just as the seed of the medicinal tree <s>Sudarśana</s> (Beautiful to Behold), whose roots and other parts are useful, should be protected from untimely consumption even after it has been given, so too is it with the medicinal tree of the <s>Sambuddha</s> (Fully Awakened One).

body.text: ayaṃ samāsato māra-karma + an-arthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: This, in brief, is the danger of <s>māra-karma</s> (the work of Māra).

body.text: asya visarjanaṃ ratna-megha-sūtre kathitaṃ | kathaṃ ca kula-putra + atra bodhi-satvo māra-karma-parihāra-upāya-kuśalo bhavati | iha bodhi-satvo * a-kalyāṇa-mitraṃ sarveṇa sarvaṃ parivarjayati | a-prati-rūpa-deśa-vāsaṃ lokāyata-mantra-sevana-bhāvanāṃ lābha-sat-kāra-pūjā-upasthāna-bahu-mānaṃ sarveṇa sarvaṃ parivarjayati | ye ca + anye upakleśā bodhi-pakṣya-mārga-antarāyikās tān sarveṇa sarvaṃ parivarjayati | teṣāṃ ca prati-pakṣaṃ bhajate ||
body.translated_text: The relinquishment of this is described in the <s>Ratnamegha-sūtra</s> (Jewel Cloud Sūtra): 'And how, O son of good family, does the <s>bodhisattva</s> herein become skillful in the means of avoiding <s>māra-karma</s>? Here the <s>bodhisattva</s> entirely avoids bad friends; he entirely avoids dwelling in an unsuitable place, the practice and cultivation of <s>Lokāyata</s> (worldly) mantras, and the pursuit of gain, honor, worship, attendance, and esteem. And whatever other secondary afflictions obstruct the path of the factors of awakening, he entirely avoids all of them; and he cultivates their antidotes.'

body.text: atra + eva ca + a-kalyāṇa-mitra-lakṣaṇam uktaṃ | śīla-vipanna-pudgala-vivarjanatayā pāpa-mitra-parivarjanā veditavyā | evaṃ dṛṣṭi-vipanna-ācāra-vipanna-ājīva-vipanna-pudgala-vivarjanatayā | saṅgaṇikā-ārāma-pudgala-vivarjanatayā | kuśīda-pudgala-vivarjanatayā | saṃsāra-abhirata-pudgala-vivarjanatayā | bodhi-parāṅ-mukha-pudgala-parivarjanatayā | gṛhi-saṃsarga-vivarjanatayā pāpa-mitra-parivarjanā veditavyā | tena ca kula-putra + etāni sthānāni parivarjayatā na teṣāṃ pudgalānām antike duṣṭa-cittam utpādayitavyaṃ na pratigha-cittaṃ na + avamanyanā-cittam utpādayitavyam | evaṃ ca anena cittam upasthāpayitavyam | uktaṃ hi bhagavatā dhātuśaḥ satvāḥ kāma-ādi-dhātuṃ āsravanti jāyante saṃsyandante saṃsargāc ca vinaśyanti | tasmād ahaṃ saṃsargaṃ varjayiṣyāmi + iti ||
body.translated_text: And right here the characteristic of a bad spiritual friend (<s>akalyāṇamitra</s>) is stated: 'The avoidance of evil companions should be understood through the avoidance of persons who have fallen from moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>). Likewise, through the avoidance of persons who have fallen from [right] view, fallen from [right] conduct, and fallen from [right] livelihood; through the avoidance of persons who delight in socializing; through the avoidance of lazy persons; through the avoidance of persons who delight in <s>saṃsāra</s>; through the avoidance of persons who turn away from awakening; through the avoidance of association with householders — the avoidance of evil companions should be understood.' 'And, O son of good family, by one who avoids these situations, an ill-disposed mind should not be generated toward those persons, nor a mind of aversion, nor a mind of contempt. And the mind should be established by him thus: For it was said by the Blessed One that beings, according to their [mental] elements, flow into, are born into, and are carried along by the element of desire and the like, and through association they are destroyed. Therefore, I shall avoid [such] association.'

body.text: bodhi-citta-saṃpramoṣo * apy an-arthaḥ tasya ca hetur ukto ratna-kūṭe | caturbhiḥ kāśyapa dharmaiḥ samanvāgatasya bodhi-satvasya bodhi-cittaṃ muhyati | katamaiś caturbhiḥ | ācārya-guru-dakṣiṇīya-visaṃvādanatayā pareṣām a-kaukṛtye kaukṛtya-upasaṃharaṇatayā | mahā-yāna-saṃprasthitānāṃ ca satvānām a-varṇa-a-yaśo * a-kīrty-a-loka-niścāraṇatayā māyā-śāṭhyena ca param upacarati na + adhyāya-āśayena + iti asya vivarjanam atra + uktaṃ | caturbhiḥ kāśyapa dharmaiḥ samanvāgatasya bodhi-satvasya sarvāsu jātiṣu jāta-mātrasya bodhi-cittam āmukhī-bhavati | na ca + antarā muhyati yāvad bodhi-maṇḍa-niṣadanāt | katamaiś caturbhiḥ | yad uta jīvita-hetor api saṃprajānan mṛṣā-vādaṃ na prabhāṣate | antaśo hāsya-prekṣikayā + api | adhyāśayena ca sarva-satvānām antike tiṣṭhaty apagata-māyā-śāṭhyatayā sarva-bodhi-satveṣu ca śāstṛ-saṃjñām utpādayati | catur-diśaṃ ca teṣāṃ varṇaṃ niścārayati | yāṃś ca satvān paripācayati tān sarvān an-uttarāyāṃ samyak-saṃbodhau samādāpayati | prādeśika-yāna-a-spṛhaṇatayā | ebhiḥ kāśyapa caturbhir iti ||
body.translated_text: The loss of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) too is a calamity, and its cause is stated in the <s>Ratnakūṭa</s>: 'Through four <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>bodhicitta</s> of a <s>bodhisattva</s> becomes confused. Which four? Through deceiving teachers, preceptors, and worthy ones; through inducing remorse in others who have no remorse; through casting disrepute, dishonor, ill-fame, and discredit upon beings who have set out in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; and through approaching others with guile and deceit, not with genuine intention.' The avoidance of this is stated here: 'Through four <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>bodhicitta</s> becomes present for a <s>bodhisattva</s> from the very moment of birth in all his lives; and it is not confused in the interim, up until the sitting at the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>). Which four? Namely: he does not, even for the sake of his life, knowingly speak falsehood — not even as a joke. With genuine intention he stands in the presence of all beings, free from guile and deceit. In all <s>bodhisattvas</s> he generates the perception of [them as] the Teacher. He proclaims their praise in the four directions. And all the beings he matures, he establishes in unsurpassed perfect awakening — through non-attachment to a limited vehicle. Through these four, <s>Kāśyapa</s>.'

body.text: siṃha-paripṛcchāyām apy āha | na jātu dharma-dānasya antarāyaṃ karoti yaḥ | tena + asau labhate kṣipraṃ loka-nāthehi saṅgamam ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Siṃha-paripṛcchā</s> too it says: 'He who never creates an obstacle to the gift of <s>Dharma</s> — by that [merit] he quickly obtains an encounter with the Protectors of the World.'

body.text: tathā jāti-smarād dharma-dānāj jānīṣva + evaṃ kumāraka + iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Likewise, from the gift of <s>Dharma</s> [comes] the memory of past lives — know it thus, O youth!'

body.text: tathā + atra + eva | bodhi-cittaṃ na riñcati tena sarvāsu jātiṣu | svapna-antare * api tac-cittaṃ kiṃ punar yadi jāgrataḥ ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, right here: 'He does not relinquish the <s>bodhicitta</s>; therefore in all his births — even in the interval of a dream, that mind [is present]; how much more so when awake!'

body.text: āha | yeṣu virati-sthāneṣu grāmeṣu nagareṣu vā | samādāya + iti bodhāya tena cittaṃ na riñcati ||
body.translated_text: It says: 'In whatever places of restraint, in villages or in cities — having undertaken [the vow] "for awakening" — by that, the mind is not relinquished.'

body.text: ārya-mañjuśrī-buddha-kṣetra-guṇa-vyūha-alaṃ-kāra-sūtre * apy āha | caturbhir dharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhi-satvaḥ praṇidhānān na calati || pe ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Mañjuśrī-buddhakṣetra-guṇavyūhālaṅkāra-sūtra</s> too it says: 'A <s>bodhisattva</s> endowed with four <s>dharmas</s> does not waver from his vows.' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: nihatamānaś ca bhavati + īrṣya-mātsarya-parivarjakaś ca bhavati para-saṃpadaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā ātta-manā bhavati + iti | idam eva pātra-bodhi-cittasya sphuṭataram a-saṃpramoṣa-kāraṇaṃ yat tatra + eva ratna-kūṭe * abhihitam | sarva-īryā-patheṣu bodhi-citta-parikarmaṇatayā | bodhi-citta-pūrvaṅ-gamatayā ca + iti ||
body.translated_text: He becomes one whose pride is destroyed, and one who avoids envy and miserliness, and upon seeing the prosperity of others, he becomes glad-minded. This alone is the clearest cause for the non-loss of the <s>bodhicitta</s> in a worthy vessel, which is stated right there in the <s>Ratnakūṭa</s>: 'through the cultivation of the <s>bodhicitta</s> in all deportments; and through making the <s>bodhicitta</s> the forerunner [of all activities].'

body.text: tathā hi candra-pradīpa-sūtre pāṭhaḥ | ārocayāmi prativedayāmi vo yathā yathā bahulu vitarkayen naraḥ tathā tathā bhavati tan-nimna-cittaḥ tehī vitarkehi tan-niśritehi + iti ||
body.translated_text: For thus there is a reading in the <s>Candrapradīpa-sūtra</s>: 'I announce and declare to you: however much a person engages in thought, just so does his mind become inclined toward that — [he becomes] dependent on those very thoughts.'

body.text: avasādo * apy an-artha etad-varjanaṃ ca ratna-meghe dṛṣṭaṃ | iha bodhi-satvo na + evaṃ cittam utpādayati | duṣ-prāpā bodhir manuṣya-bhūtena satā | idaṃ ca me vīryaṃ parīttaṃ ca ku-sīdo * ahaṃ bodhiś ca + ādīpta-śiraś-caila-upamena bahūn kalpān | bahūni kalpa-śatāni bahūni kalpa-sahasrāṇi samudānetavyā | tan na + aham utsahae īdṛśaṃ bhāram udvoḍhuṃ ||
body.translated_text: Despondency too is a calamity, and the avoidance of it is seen in the <s>Ratnamegha</s>: 'Here, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not generate the thought: "Awakening is difficult to attain for one who is a human being. And my vigor is small, and I am lazy, and awakening [must be pursued] for many <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) — many hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>, many thousands of <s>kalpas</s> — with the urgency of one whose head-cloth is on fire. I cannot endure to bear such a burden."'

body.text: kiṃ tarhi bodhi-satvena + evaṃ cittam utpādayitavyaṃ | ye * api te * abhisaṃbuddhās tathā-gatā arhantaḥ samyak-saṃbuddhā ye ca + abhisaṃbuddhyante ye vā + abhisaṃbhotsyante * api + īdṛśena + eva nayena īdṛśyā pratipadā | īdṛśena + eva vīryeṇa + abhisaṃuddhā abhisaṃbudhyante * abhisaṃbhotsyante ca | yāvan na te tathā-gata-bhūtā eva + abhisaṃbuddhāḥ | aham api tathā tathā ghaṭiṣye tathā tathā vyāyaṃsye sarva-satva-sādhāraṇena vīryeṇa sarva-satva-ārambaṇena vīryeṇa yathā + aham an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyae iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Rather, the <s>bodhisattva</s> should generate the thought: "Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones who have been fully awakened, who are being fully awakened, and who will be fully awakened — they have been, are, and will be fully awakened by just this same method, by just this same practice, by just this same vigor. And they were not beings who were already <s>Tathāgatas</s> when they became awakened. I too shall strive thus and thus, shall exert myself thus and thus, with vigor shared with all beings, with vigor [sustained by] the support of all beings, so that I shall attain unsurpassed perfect awakening."'

body.text: punar a-paro * an-artho ratna-kūṭe dṛṣṭaḥ | a-paripāciteṣu satveṣu viśvāso bodhi-satvasya skhalitaṃ a-bhājanī-bhūteṣu satveṣu + udāra-buddha-dharma-saṃprakāśanāt bodhi-satvasya skhalitaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Yet another calamity is seen in the <s>Ratnakūṭa</s>: 'Trust in beings who have not been matured is a stumble of the <s>bodhisattva</s>. The illumination of sublime <s>Buddha-dharma</s> to beings who are not [yet suitable] vessels is a stumble of the <s>bodhisattva</s>.'

body.text: udāra-adhimuktikeṣu satveṣu hīna-yāna-saṃprakāśanād bodhi-satvasya skhalitam iti | samyak-smṛty-upasthiteṣu śīlavatsu kalyāṇa-dharmeṣu prati-vimānanā duḥ-śīla-pāpa-dharma-saṃgrahā bodhi-satvasya skhalitam iti ||
body.translated_text: 'The illumination of the lesser vehicle to beings of sublime aspiration is a stumble of the <s>bodhisattva</s>. Contempt for those who are established in right mindfulness, who are virtuous and of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, and the embracing of those who are immoral and of evil <s>dharmas</s> — is a stumble of the <s>bodhisattva</s>.'

body.text: an-adhimuktir apy an-arthaḥ | yathā + uktaṃ rāṣṭrapāla-sūtre | yasya adhimukti na vidyati buddha-dharma-gaṇe ca na tasya dhimuktiḥ | śikṣa-vrateṣu na tasya dhimuktiḥ pāpamates tira-pāya-mukhasya ||
body.translated_text: Lack of faith (<s>anadhimukti</s>) too is a calamity. As it is said in the <s>Rāṣṭrapāla-sūtra</s>: 'He who has no faith — in the host of <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> there is no faith for him; in the trainings and vows there is no faith for that evil-minded one at the threshold of the lower realms.'

body.text: sa itaś cyuto manu-jeṣu karma-vaśād a-budho hi vimūḍhaḥ | narakeṣv atha tirya-gatīṣu preta-gatīṣu ca vindati duṣkham ||
body.translated_text: 'Fallen from here, among humans, by the power of <s>karma</s>, ignorant and deluded — in hells and in the animal realms and in the realm of <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) he experiences suffering.'

body.text: iti asya visarjanaṃ ratna-kūṭe * abhihitaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ | yeṣu ca + asya gambhīreṣu buddhinā + avagāhate | tatra tathā-gata eva sākṣī + iti kṛtvā na pratikṣipati | tathā-gata eva janīte | na + ahaṃ jāne | an-antā buddha-bodhir nānā-adhimuktikatayā tathā-gatānāṃ satveṣu dharma-deśanā pravarttatae iti ||
body.translated_text: Thus the abandonment of this [lack of faith] is seen as stated in the <s>Ratnakūṭa</s>: 'And whatever profound [<s>dharmas</s>] he comprehends with his wisdom — there, thinking "the <s>Tathāgata</s> alone is witness," he does not reject [them]. "The <s>Tathāgata</s> alone knows; I do not know. Infinite is the awakening of the <s>Buddhas</s>; because of the diversity of [beings'] aspirations, the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> to beings proceeds [in various ways]."'

body.text: vaiyāvṛtya-vartamānena + an-artha-vivarjana-kuśalena bhavitavyaṃ | bodhi-satva-prātimokṣe hi saha-dhārmike dharma-śravaṇe | tathā-gata-pūjāyāṃ ca vaiyāvṛtyam upadiṣṭaṃ tatra yā vṛttiḥ sā ratna-rāśi-sūtrād āgatā | tatra vaiyāvṛtya-kareṇa bhikṣuṇā sarva-bhikṣu-saṃghasya cittam abhirādhayitavyaṃ | tatra ye bhikṣava āraṇyakāḥ prānta-śayyā-āsanikās teṣāṃ | vaiyāvṛtya-kareṇa bhikṣuṇā sarveṇa sarvaṃ na karma-samutthānaṃ dātavyaṃ | yadi punar āraṇyakasya bhikṣoḥ saṃgha-paryāpannaṃ śaikṣakaṃ karma prāpnuyāt | etena vaiyāvṛtya-kareṇa bhikṣuṇā + ātmanā + eva tat kartavyaṃ | anyataro vā bhikṣur adhyeṣyo na punaḥ sa āraṇyako bhikṣur utpīḍayitavyas tatra yo bhikṣuḥ piṇḍa-cāriko bhavati tasya tena vaiyāvṛtya-kareṇa bhikṣuṇā praṇīta-bhojaneṣu saṃvibhāgaḥ kartavyaḥ | tatra kāśyapa yo bhikṣur yoga-ācārī bhavati | tasya tena vaiyāvṛtya-kareṇa bhikṣuṇā + anulomikāny upakaraṇāny upasaṃhartavyāni glāna-pratyaya-bhaiṣajya-pariṣkārāś ca | yasmiṃś ca pradeśe sa yoga-ācārī bhikṣuḥ prativasati tasmin pradeśe na ucca-śabdaḥ kartavyaḥ | rakṣitavyo vaiyāvṛtya-kareṇa bhikṣuṇā yoga-ācārī bhikṣuḥ | śayyā-āsana-upastambhanā + asya kartavyā | praṇītāni ca saṃpriyāṇi yoga-ācāra-bhūmy-anukūlāni khādanīya-bhojanīyāny upanāmayitavyāni || pe ||
body.translated_text: One who is engaged in service (<s>vaiyāvṛtya</s>) should be skilled in the avoidance of calamities. For in the <s>Bodhisattva-prātimokṣa</s>, service is taught in [the context of] listening to the <s>Dharma</s> among co-practitioners and in the worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. The conduct therein comes from the <s>Ratnarāśi-sūtra</s>: 'There, the <s>bhikṣu</s> performing service should gratify the mind of the entire <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s>. Therein, those <s>bhikṣus</s> who are forest-dwellers and who dwell in solitary beds and seats — to them, the <s>bhikṣu</s> performing service should not assign any and all communal work. But if a communal training-work falls to a forest-dwelling <s>bhikṣu</s>, then this service-performing <s>bhikṣu</s> should himself do that work, or another <s>bhikṣu</s> should be requested [to do it]; but that forest-dwelling <s>bhikṣu</s> should not be pressured. Therein, a <s>bhikṣu</s> who goes for alms — with that one, the service-performing <s>bhikṣu</s> should share excellent food.' 'Therein, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, whatever <s>bhikṣu</s> is a practitioner of <s>yoga</s> — for him, the service-performing <s>bhikṣu</s> should provide suitable provisions and medicines for the sick. And in whatever place that <s>yoga</s>-practicing <s>bhikṣu</s> resides, no loud sounds should be made in that place. The <s>yoga</s>-practicing <s>bhikṣu</s> should be protected by the service-performing <s>bhikṣu</s>. His beds and seats should be maintained. And excellent, agreeable foods and eatables, suitable for the stages of <s>yoga</s>-practice, should be offered.' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: ye bhikṣavo bāhuśrutye * abhiyuktā bhavanti teṣām utsāho dātavyaḥ | yāvat te * api parirakṣitavyāḥ | ye dhārma-kathikā bhikṣavo bhaviṣyanti | teṣāṃ pratīhāra-dharmatā kartavyā | yāvad dhārma-śravaṇikāś ca + udyojayitavyāḥ parṣan-maṇḍalaṃ parisaṃsthāpayitavyaṃ | sāṃkathya-maṇḍalaṃ viśodhayitavyaṃ yāvat sādhu-kāra-bahulena ca + asya bhavitavyaṃ || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'Those <s>bhikṣus</s> who are devoted to extensive learning — encouragement should be given to them; and so on, they too should be protected. Those <s>bhikṣus</s> who will be <s>Dharma</s>-preachers — the duties of a doorkeeper should be performed for them; and so on, and those who listen to the <s>Dharma</s> should be encouraged, the assembly-circle should be arranged, the discussion-circle should be purified,' and so on, 'and one should be abundant in [giving] the call of "well said!"' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: na kva-cid vastuni aiścarya-saṃjñā + utpādayitavyā | kiyat parīttam api kāryaṃ saṃgha-matena kartavyaṃ | na sva-matena yāvan na sāṃghikaś cāturdiśa-sāṃghikena saṃsṛṣṭaḥ kartavyaḥ | evaṃ viparyayād evaṃ staupikena saha + anyo-nya-saṃsarga-pratiṣedhaḥ | yadi cāturdiśe saṃghe vaikalyaṃ bhavet sāṃghikaś ca lābha utsado bhavet tena vaiyāvṛtya-kareṇa bhikṣuṇā bhikṣu-saṃgham eka-mānasaṃ kṛtvā | sāṃghika-lābhāc cāturdiśa-sāṃghika-kāryaṃ kartavyaṃ | evaṃ stūpe * api pralugne * ayam eva vidhir dāyakān dāna-patīn vā samādāpya pratisaṃskartavya ity ājñā | yadi punaḥ kāśyapa kiyad bahur api staupiko lābho bhavet | sa vaiyākṛtya-kareṇa na saṃghena cāturdiśa-saṃghe upanāmayitavyaḥ | tat kasmād * dhetoḥ | yā staupikā antaśa ekadaśā + api śrāddhaiḥ prasāda-bahulair niryātitā bhavati | sā sa-devakasya lokasya caityaṃ | kaḥ punar vādo ratnaṃ vā ratna-saṃmataṃ vā yac ca stūpe cīvaraṃ niryātitaṃ bhavati | tat tatra + eva tathā-gata-caitye vāta-ātapa-vṛṣṭibhiḥ parikṣayaṃ gacchatu | na punaḥ staupikaṃ cīvaraṃ hiraṇya-mūlyena parivartayitavyaṃ | na hi staupikasya kaś-cid argho na + api stūpasya kena-cid vaikalyaṃ yo hi kaś-cit kāśyapa vaiyāvṛtya-karo bhikṣū ruṣṭa-cittaḥ śīlavatāṃ dakṣiṇīyānām

children.text: aiśvaryād ājñaptiṃ dadāti sa tena + a-kuśalena karmaṇā naraka-gāmī bhavati + iti | yadi manuṣya-lokam āgacchati dāso bhavati para-karma-karo lābhī ca bhavati khaṭa-capeṭa-pracaṇḍa-prahārāṇāṃ | pe | daṇḍa-karma-bhaya-tarjitaṃ bhikṣuṃ karoty a-kāla-preṣaṇam a-kāla-jñaptiṃ dadāti | sa tena + a-kuśalena karmaṇā bahuśaṅkur nāma praty-eka-narakas tatra + asya + upapattir bhavati | yāvat sahasra-viddhaḥ kāyo bhavati | ādīptaḥ | pradīptaḥ saṃprajvalitaḥ | pe | yojana-śata-vistāra-pramāṇā jihvā bhavati | tasya tatra jihvā-indriye bahūni śaṅku-śata-sahasrāṇi ādīptāni ayas-mayāni nikhātāni bhavanti | yo hi kaś-cit kāśyapa vaiyavṛtya-karo bhikṣur āgata-āgataṃ sāṃghikaṃ lābhaṃ sannidhiṃ karoti na kāla-anukālaṃ dadāti | udvaśyāpayitavyā viheṭhayitvā dadāti | keṣāñ-cin na dadāti | sa tena + a-kuśala-mūlena jaṅghā nāma gūtha-mṛtikā-preta-yonis tatra + asya + upapattir bhavati | tatra + asya + anye pretā bhojanaṃ gṛhītvā + apadarśayanti | sa udvaśyamānas tad-bhojanam a-nimiṣābhyāṃ netrābhyāṃ paśyamānaḥ kṣut-pipāsā-parigato duṣkhāṃ | vedanāṃ vetti na ca varṣa-sahasreṇa + api tasya bhojanasya lābhī bhavati | yad api kadā-cit karhi-cid bhojanaṃ labdhaṃ bhavati tad uccāraṃ bhavati pūya-śoṇitaṃ vā + iti ||
children.translated_text: By his authority he issues a command [to punish a monk], and by that unwholesome action he becomes one destined for hell. If he is reborn in the human world, he becomes a slave, a servant of others, and one who receives blows from fists, slaps, and fierce strikes. [Abbreviated.] He makes a monk punished with penalties, terrified by threats, and issues untimely summons, gives untimely commands. By that unwholesome action, there is a particular hell called <s>Bahuśaṅku</s> (Many Stakes) where he is reborn. His body is pierced by a thousand [stakes], blazing, burning, flaming. [Abbreviated.] His tongue becomes one hundred <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) in breadth, and in that tongue-faculty many hundreds of thousands of iron stakes, blazing, are driven in. Moreover, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, whatever monk who is the attendant takes the communal gains that have been received and hoards them, does not distribute them at the proper time, gives them under duress after harassment, does not give to some at all — by that unwholesome root, there is a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost) realm called <s>Jaṅghā</s> (Dung-Earth) where he is reborn. There, other <s>pretas</s>, having taken food, hide it from him. He, being forced to watch, seeing that food with unblinking eyes, consumed by hunger and thirst, experiences painful feelings, and even after a thousand years he does not obtain that food. And whatever food he occasionally obtains turns into excrement or pus and blood.

body.translated_text: 'The perception of ownership should not be generated toward any thing whatsoever. However small the task, it should be done according to the opinion of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, not according to one's own opinion. And so on: property belonging to the <s>Saṃgha</s> should not be mixed with that belonging to the <s>Saṃgha</s> of the four directions. Likewise, in the reverse [direction]; and the prohibition of mutual mixing with <s>stūpa</s>-property [applies similarly]. And if there should be a deficiency in [the property of] the <s>Saṃgha</s> of the four directions, and the local <s>Saṃgha</s>-property should be in surplus, then the service-performing <s>bhikṣu</s>, having made the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> of one mind, should use the local <s>Saṃgha</s>-property for the purposes of the <s>Saṃgha</s> of the four directions. Likewise, if a <s>stūpa</s> is in ruin, this same procedure [applies]; having encouraged the donors and benefactors, it should be repaired — this is the instruction. But if, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, however abundant the <s>stūpa</s>-property may be, it should not be diverted by the service-performer to the <s>Saṃgha</s> or the <s>Saṃgha</s> of the four directions. Why is that? Whatever <s>stūpa</s>-cloth, even a single thread, has been offered by the faithful with abundant devotion — that is a <s>caitya</s> (reliquary) for the world including the <s>devas</s>. What need be said of gems or things considered as gems? And whatever robe has been offered to a <s>stūpa</s>, let that perish right there at the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>caitya</s> by wind, sun, and rain; but <s>stūpa</s>-cloth should not be exchanged for a monetary equivalent. For <s>stūpa</s>-property has no price, nor does a <s>stūpa</s> have any deficiency.' 'And whoever, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, being a service-performing <s>bhikṣu</s>, with an angry mind, toward the virtuous and worthy ones —'

body.text: saṃgharakṣita-avadāne * apy an-artha uktaḥ | yāṃs tvaṃ saṃgharakṣita satvān adrākṣīḥ kuḍya-ākārāṃs te bhikṣava āsan | taiḥ sāṃghikaṃ kuḍyaṃ śleṣmaṇā nāśitaṃ | tasya karmaṇo vipākena kuḍya-ākārāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ | yāṃs tvaṃ saṃgharakṣita satvān adrākṣīḥ stambha-ākārāṃs te bhikṣava āsan | taiḥ sāṃghika-staṃbhaḥ siṃhāṇakena nāśitaḥ | tena stambha-ākārāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ | yāṃs tvaṃ satvān adrākṣīr vṛkṣa-ākārān patra-ākārān phala-ākārān te * api bhikṣava āsan | tair api sāṃghikāni vṛkṣa-patra-pus.pa-phalāni paudgalika-paribhogena paribhuktāni tena te vṛkṣa-patra-puṣpa-phala-ākārāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ | yāṃs tvaṃ satvān adrākṣī rajjv-ākārān saṃmārjany--ākārāṃs te bhikṣava āsan | taiḥ sāṃghikā rajju-sammārjanyaḥ paudgalika-paribhogena paribhuktās tena rajjv-ākārāḥ sammārjany--ākārāś ca saṃvṛttāḥ | yaṃ tvaṃ satvam adrākṣīs taṭṭa-ākāraṃ sa śrāmaṇeraka āsīt | sa taṭṭukaṃ nirmādayati | āgantukāś ca bhikṣavo * abhyāgatāḥ | tair asau dṛṣṭaś ca pṛṣṭaś ca śrāmaṇeraka kim ayaṃ saṃghasya pānakaṃ bhaviṣyati | sa mātsarya-upahata-cittaḥ kathayati | kiṃ na paśyatha taṭṭukaṃ nirmāditaṃ pītaṃ pānakam iti | te vṛttā velā + iti nairāśyam āpannā hīna-dīna-vadanāḥ prakrāntāḥ | sa tasya karmaṇo vipākena taṭṭuka-ākāraḥ saṃvṛttāḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Saṃgharakṣitāvadāna</s> (Narrative of <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>) also, the harmful consequences are stated: "Those beings you saw, O <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, in the form of walls — they were monks. By them, a communal wall was destroyed with mucus. As the result of that action, they became wall-shaped. Those beings you saw, O <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, in the form of pillars — they were monks. By them, a communal pillar was destroyed with nasal discharge. Therefore they became pillar-shaped. Those beings you saw in the form of trees, in the form of leaves, in the form of fruits — they too were monks. By them also, communal trees, leaves, flowers, and fruits were used for personal enjoyment. Therefore they became tree-shaped, leaf-shaped, flower-shaped, and fruit-shaped. Those beings you saw in the form of ropes, in the form of brooms — they were monks. By them, communal ropes and brooms were used for personal enjoyment. Therefore they became rope-shaped and broom-shaped. That being you saw in the shape of a pot — he was a novice monk. He was preparing a beverage. And visiting monks arrived as guests. They saw him and asked: 'Novice, will this be a drink for the <s>Saṃgha</s> (community)?' He, with a mind overcome by miserliness, said: 'Do you not see that the beverage has been prepared and drunk?' They, thinking 'the time has passed,' became dejected, their faces downcast, and departed. As the result of that action, he became pot-shaped."

body.text: yaṃ tvam satvam adrākṣīr udūkhala-ākāraṃ so * api bhikṣur āsīt | tasya pātra-karma pratyupasthitaṃ | tatra ca + ekaḥ śrāmaṇerako * arhan mudrā-vāre niyuktaḥ | sa tena + uktaḥ śrāmaṇeraka dadasva me khalistākaṃ kuṭṭayitvā + iti | sa kathayati | sthavira tiṣṭha tāvan muhūrtaṃ vyagro * asmi paścāt kuṭṭayitvā dāsyāmi + iti | sa saṃjāta-āmarṣaḥ kathayati | śrāmaṇeraka yadi mama kalpate udūkhalaṃ spraṣṭuṃ tvām eva + aham udūkhale prakṣipya kuṭṭayeyaṃ | prāg eva khalistokam iti | sa śrāmaṇeraḥ saṃlakṣayati | tīvra-paryavasthāna-paryavasthito * ayaṃ | yady aham asmai prativacanaṃ dāsyāmi bhūyasyā mātrayā prakopam āpatsyati + iti tūṣṇīm avasthitaḥ | yadā + asya paryavasthānaṃ vigataṃ tadā + upasaṃkramya kathayati | sthavira jānīṣe tvaṃ ko * aham iti | sa kathayati | jāne tvāṃ kāśyapasya samyak-saṃbuddhasya pravrajitaṃ śrāmaṇerakaṃ | aham api bhikṣuḥ sthaviraḥ | śrāmaṇerakaḥ kathayati | yady apy evaṃ tathā + api tu yan mayā pravrajitena karaṇīyaṃ tat kṛtaṃ | kiṃ kṛtaṃ kleśa-prahāṇaṃ chinna-sakala-bandhano * ahaṃ sarva-bandhana-vinirmuktaḥ | kharaṃ te vāk-karma niścāritaṃ | atyayam atyayato deśaya | apy eva nāma etat karma-parikṣayaṃ tanutvaṃ paryādānaṃ gacched iti | tena + atyayam atyayato na deśitaṃ tena karmaṇā + udūkhala-ākāraḥ saṃvṛttaḥ ||
body.translated_text: "That being you saw, O <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, in the shape of a mortar — he too was a monk. His turn for pot-duty had come. And there a certain novice, an <s>Arhat</s> (liberated one), was assigned to the sealing rotation. He said to him: 'Novice, give me husked rice after pounding it.' The novice said: 'Elder, wait a moment; I am busy. I will pound it and give it to you later.' He, having become angry, said: 'Novice, if it were up to me to touch the mortar, I would throw you yourself into the mortar and pound you — let alone the husked rice!' The novice reflected: 'This one is overcome by intense affliction. If I give him a reply, he will become even more enraged,' and remained silent. When his affliction had subsided, [the novice] approached and said: 'Elder, do you know who I am?' He said: 'I know you — a novice who has gone forth under <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the perfectly awakened one. And I too am an elder monk.' The novice said: 'That may be so, but nevertheless, what was to be done by me as a renunciant — that I have done. What have I done? The abandonment of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). I have cut all bonds; I am freed from all fetters. Your verbal action was harsh. Confess the transgression as a transgression, so that perhaps this <s>karma</s> may come to exhaustion, diminishment, and an end.' But he did not confess the transgression as a transgression. By that action he became mortar-shaped."

body.text: yāṃs tvaṃ satvān adrākṣīḥ sthālya-ākārān | te kalpi-kārakā āsan bhikṣūṇām upasthāyakāḥ | te bhaiṣajyāni kvāthayanto bhikṣubhir a-priyam uktāḥ taiś cittaṃ pradūṣya sthālyo bhinnāḥ tena sthālya-ākārāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ | yaṃ tvaṃ satvam adrākṣīr madhye chinnaṃ tantunā dhāryamāṇaṃ so * api bhikṣur āsīl lābhī grāhikaḥ tena mātsarya-abhibhūtena lābhaḥ saṃparivartitaḥ | yo vārṣikaḥ sa haimantikaḥ pariṇāmitaḥ | yas tu haimantikaḥ sa vārṣikaḥ pariṇāmitaḥ | tasya karmaṇo vipākena madhye chinnas tantunā dhāryamāṇo gacchati ||
body.translated_text: "Those beings you saw in the shape of cooking pots — they were <s>kalpikārakas</s> (preparers of permissible items), attendants of monks. While boiling medicines, they were spoken to harshly by the monks. Having become angry in mind, they broke the cooking pots. Therefore they became pot-shaped. That being you saw, cut in the middle, held together by a thread — he too was a monk, one who received [gifts] and grasped [at them]. Overcome by miserliness, he exchanged the gains: what was for the rainy season he converted to the winter, and what was for the winter he converted to the rainy season. As the result of that action, he goes about cut in the middle, held together by a thread."

body.text: śikṣā-samuccaye dharma-bhāṇaka-ādi-rakṣā-paricchedas tṛtīyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>, [this concludes] the third chapter on the Protection of <s>Dharma</s>-preachers and Others.

body.text: a-pare * api mahanto * an-arthāḥ sūtra-anteṣu + uktāḥ | yathā tāvad ākāśa-garbha-sūtre | pañca + imāḥ kula-putra kṣatriyasya mūrddha-abhiṣiktasya mūla-āpattayaḥ | yābhir mūla-āpattibhiḥ kṣatriyo mūrddha-abhiṣiktaḥ sarvāṇi pūrva-avaropitāni kuśala-mūlāni jhāṣayati | vastu-patitaḥ pārājikaḥ sarva-deva-manuṣya-mukhebhyo * apāya-gāmī bhavati | katamāḥ pañca | yaḥ kula-putra mūrddha-abhiṣiktaṃ staupikaṃ vastv apaharati sāṃghikaṃ vā cāturdiśa-sāṃghikaṃ vā niryātitaṃ vā | svayaṃ vā + apaharati hārayati vā | iyaṃ prathamā mūla-āpattiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Other great harmful consequences are also stated in the <s>sūtras</s>. First, as in the <s>Ākāśagarbha-sūtra</s>: "These, O son of good family, are five root transgressions (<s>mūla-āpattis</s>) of an anointed <s>kṣatriya</s> (warrior-king). By these root transgressions, an anointed <s>kṣatriya</s> destroys all previously planted roots of virtue. He becomes one who has fallen from his position, defeated, destined for the lower realms before all gods and humans. What are the five? Whoever, O son of good family, as an anointed [king], takes property belonging to a <s>stūpa</s>, or to the <s>Saṃgha</s>, or to the <s>Saṃgha</s> of the four directions, or what has been donated — whether he takes it himself or causes it to be taken — this is the first root transgression."

body.text: yaḥ punar dharmaṃ pratikṣipati śrāvaka-niryāṇa-bhāṣitaṃ vā praty-eka-buddha-niryāṇa-bhāṣitaṃ vā mahā-yāna-niryāṇa-bhāṣitaṃ vā pratikṣipati pratiṣedhayati + iyaṃ dvitīyā mūla-āpattiḥ ||
body.translated_text: "Whoever rejects the <s>Dharma</s> — whether spoken as the vehicle of the <s>Śrāvakas</s> (Hearers), or spoken as the vehicle of the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (Solitary Buddhas), or spoken as the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) — rejects and prohibits it — this is the second root transgression."

body.text: yaḥ punar mām uddiśya śiras-tuṇḍa-muṇḍa-kāṣāya-vastra-prāvṛtaḥ śikṣā-dhārī vā śikṣā-a-dhārī vā tasya duḥ-śīlasya vā śīlavato vā kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇy apaharati apaharāyati | gṛha-sthaṃ vā karoti kāye daṇḍaiḥ praharati cārake vā prakṣipati jīvitena vā viyojayati + iyaṃ tṛtīyā mūla-āpattiḥ ||
body.translated_text: "Whoever, toward one who, directed toward me [the Buddha], has shaved head and face, wears the saffron robe, and either observes or does not observe the training — whether immoral or virtuous — takes away his saffron robes, or causes them to be taken; or makes him a layperson; or strikes his body with rods; or throws him into prison; or deprives him of life — this is the third root transgression."

body.text: yaḥ punaḥ kṣatriyaḥ saṃcintya mātaraṃ jīvitād vyaparopayati pitaram arhantaṃ bhagavac-chrāvakaṃ vā jīvitād vyaparopayati samagraṃ vā saṃghaṃ bhinatti tathā-gatasya + arhataḥ samyak-saṃbuddhasya saṃcintya duṣṭa-citto rudhiram utpādayati ||
body.translated_text: "Whoever, a <s>kṣatriya</s>, deliberately kills his mother, kills his father, kills an <s>Arhat</s>, kills a disciple of the Blessed One, splits the harmonious <s>Saṃgha</s>, or with evil intent deliberately draws blood from the body of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a perfectly awakened one —"

body.text: ebhiḥ pañcabhir ānantaryair karmabhir anyatara-anyataraṃ karma + utpādayati + iyaṃ caturthī mūla-āpattiḥ ||
body.translated_text: "By these five <s>ānantarya</s> (immediately-retributive) actions, producing any one of them — this is the fourth root transgression."

body.text: yaḥ punaḥ kṣatriyo * a-hetu-vādī bhavati para-loka-upekṣakaḥ | daśa + a-kuśalān karma-pathān samādāya vartate * anyāṃś ca bahūn satvān daśasv a-kuśaleṣu karma-patheṣu samādāpayati vinayati niveśayati pratiṣṭhāpayati + iyaṃ pañcamī mūla-āpattiḥ || pe ||
