body.translated_text: "Whoever, a <s>kṣatriya</s>, holds the view of no causation, is indifferent about the other world, takes up and lives by the ten unwholesome courses of action, and causes many other sentient beings to take up, trains them in, establishes, and confirms them in the ten unwholesome courses of action — this is the fifth root transgression." [Abbreviated.]

body.text: yaḥ punar grāma-bhedaṃ jana-pada-bhedaṃ nagara-bhedaṃ rāṣṭra-bhedaṃ karoti + iyaṃ mūla-āpattiḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: "Whoever causes the splitting of a village, the splitting of a province, the splitting of a city, the splitting of a kingdom — this is a root transgression." [Abbreviated.]

body.text: ādi-karmiṇāṃ mahā-yāna-saṃprasthitānāṃ kula-putrāṇāṃ kula-duhitṝṇāṃ vā + aṣṭau mūla-āpattayo | yābhir mūla-āpattibhiḥ skhalitā ādi-karmikā mahā-yāna-saṃprasthitāḥ sarvāṇi pūrva-avaropitāni kuśala-mūlāni jhāṣayanti | vastu-patitāḥ parājitā deva-manuṣya-mahā-yāna-mukhād apāya-gāmino bhavanti ciraṃ ca saṃsāre sīdanti kalyāṇa-mitra-virahitāḥ | katamā aṣṭau | ye satvāḥ pūrva-duś-carita-hetunā + asmin kliṣṭe pañca-kaṣāye loke upapannās tae itvara-kuśala-mūlāḥ kalyāṇa-mitraṃ saṃniḥśritya + idaṃ paramaṃ gambhīraṃ mahā-yānaṃ śṛṇvanti | te ca parītta-buddhayo * api kula-putrā an-uttarāyāṃ samyak-saṃbodhau cittam utpādayanti | teṣāṃ ādi-karmikā ye ca bodhi-satvā idaṃ parama-gambhīraṃ śūnyatā-pratisaṃyuktaṃ sūtra-antaṃ śṛṇvanti uddiśanti paṭhanti | te yathā-śrutaṃ yathā-paryavāptaṃ pareṣāṃ pūrva-buddhi-sadṛśānāṃ sv-arthaṃ su-vyañjanaṃ vistareṇa + agrataḥ smārayanti prakāśayanti | te hy a-kṛta-śamā bālāḥ pṛthag-janāḥ śṛṇvanta uttrasyanti saṃtrasyanti saṃtrāsam āpadyante | te saṃtrāsena vivarttayanty an-uttarāyāḥ samyak-saṃbodheś cittaṃ śrāvaka-yāne cittaṃ praṇidadhati | eṣā ādi-karmika-bodhi-satvasya mūla-āpattiḥ prathamā ||
body.translated_text: "For beginner sons and daughters of good family who have set forth upon the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, there are eight root transgressions. By these root transgressions, stumbling beginners who have set forth upon the <s>Mahāyāna</s> destroy all previously planted roots of virtue. They become fallen from their position, defeated, destined for the lower realms before gods, humans, and the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, and they sink long in <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), bereft of spiritual friends. What are the eight? Those sentient beings who, due to previous misconduct, have been reborn in this afflicted world of the five corruptions, who have meager roots of virtue, relying on a spiritual friend, hear this supremely profound <s>Mahāyāna</s>. And those sons of good family, though of limited wisdom, generate the mind toward supreme perfect awakening. Among them, those who are beginners and those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who hear this supremely profound <s>sūtra</s> connected with <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), teach and recite it — and as they have heard and understood it, they remind and reveal it in detail to others of wisdom similar to their former [understanding], [explaining] its meaning and its clear expression. But those [listeners], being untamed fools, ordinary beings, upon hearing it are frightened, terrified, and become seized with terror. Through that terror, they turn away their minds from supreme perfect awakening and aspire to the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> (Hearers' Vehicle). This is the first root transgression of a beginner <s>bodhisattva</s>."

body.text: yayā mūla-āpattyā sa kula-putraḥ sarvaṃ pūrva-avaropitaṃ kuśala-mūlaṃ jhāṣayati | vastu-patitaḥ parājitaḥ svarga-apavarga-sukhāt | visaṃvāditaṃ ca + asya bodhi-cittam apāya-gāmi bhavati | tasmād bodhi-satvena mahā-satvena para-pudgalānām āśaya-anuśayaṃ prathamaṃ jñātvā yathā-āśayānāṃ satvānām anupūrveṇa dharma-deśanā kartavyā | tad yathā mahā-samudre * anupūrveṇa + avatārayati || pe ||
body.translated_text: "By which root transgression that son of good family destroys all previously planted roots of virtue. He becomes fallen from his position, defeated, excluded from the happiness of heaven and liberation, and his <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening) becomes broken and destined for the lower realms. Therefore, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> should first ascertain the dispositions and latent tendencies of other individuals, and then teach the <s>Dharma</s> gradually, in accordance with their dispositions. Just as the great ocean is entered gradually." [Abbreviated.]

body.text: punar a-param ādi-karmiko bodhi-satvaḥ kasya-cid eva vakṣyati ||
body.translated_text: "Furthermore, a beginner <s>bodhisattva</s> may say to someone:"

body.text: na tvaṃ śakyasi ṣaṭ-pāramitāsu caryāṃ cartuṃ | na tvaṃ śakyasy an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhim abhisaṃboddhuṃ | śīghraṃ tvaṃ śrāvaka-yāne praty-eka-buddha-yāne vā cittam utpādaya | tena tvaṃ saṃsārān niryāsyasi | yāvad yathā-pūrva-uktam iyam ādi-karmikasya bodhi-satvasya dvit-yā mūla-āpattiḥ ||
body.translated_text: "'You are not able to practice the conduct of the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections). You are not able to attain supreme perfect awakening. Quickly generate the mind toward the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> or the <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s>. By that you will escape from <s>saṃsāra</s>.' As stated before in full, this is the second root transgression of a beginner <s>bodhisattva</s>."

body.text: punar a-param ādi-karmiko bodhi-satvaḥ kasya-cid evaṃ vakṣyati | kiṃ bhoḥ prātimokṣa-vinayena | śīlena su-rakṣitena śīghraṃ tvam an-uttarāyāṃ samyak-saṃbodhau cittam utpādayasva | mahā-yānaṃ paṭha | yat te kiñ-cit kāya-vāṅ-manobhiḥ kleśa-pratyayād a-kuśalaṃ karma samudānītaṃ tena pāṭhena śuddhir bhavaty a-vipākaṃ | yāvad yathā-pūrva-uktam ayam ādi-karmikasya bodhi-satvasya tṛtīyā mūla-āpattiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, a beginner <s>bodhisattva</s> will say to someone thus: "What need is there for the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> disciplinary code? With morality well-guarded, quickly generate the thought of supreme, perfect <s>bodhi</s>! Study the <s>Mahāyāna</s>! Whatever unwholesome <s>karma</s> you have accumulated through body, speech, and mind, conditioned by the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) — by that study, purification occurs and it becomes non-ripening."' And so on, as stated before. This is the third root transgression of the beginner <s>bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: punar a-paraṃ kula-putra keṣāñ-cid ādi-karmiko bodhi-satva evaṃ vakṣyati | varjayata yūyaṃ kula-putrāḥ śrāvaka-yāna-kathāṃ | mā śṛṇuta mā paṭhata mā pareṣām upadiśata | gopayata śrāvaka-yāna-kathāṃ | na yūyaṃ tasmāt mahat phalaṃ prāpsyatha | na yūyaṃ tato nidānāc * chaktāḥ kleśa-antaṃ kartuṃ | śraddadhata mahā-yāna-kathāṃ | śṛṇuta mahā-yānaṃ paṭhata mahā-yānaṃ pareṣāṃ ca + upadiśata | tato yūyaṃ sarva-dur-gaty-apāya-pathān śamayiṣyatha | kṣipraṃ ca + an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyatha ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, O son of good family, a beginner <s>bodhisattva</s> will say to certain persons thus: "Abandon, O sons of good family, the discourse of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>! Do not listen to it! Do not study it! Do not teach it to others! Conceal the discourse of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>! You will not obtain great fruit from it. You are not able thereby to make an end of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). Have faith in the discourse of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>! Listen to the <s>Mahāyāna</s>! Study the <s>Mahāyāna</s>! And teach it to others! Thereby you will pacify all paths to lower realms and miserable states of existence, and you will quickly attain supreme, perfect <s>bodhi</s>."'

body.text: yadi te tasya vacana-kāriṇo bhavanti + īdṛśaṃ dṛṣṭi-gatam upagṛhṇīyuḥ | ubhayor api mūla-āpatir bhavati + iyam ādi-karmikasya bodhi-satvasya caturthī mūla-āpattiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'If those [listeners], obeying his words, were to adopt such a wrong view — both [the teacher and the listeners] incur a root transgression.' This is the fourth root transgression of the beginner <s>bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: punar a-param ādi-karmikā bodhi-satvā dvi-jihvikā bhavanti anyathā nidarśayanti | idaṃ ca mahā-yānaṃ kīrti-śabda-śloka-arthaṃ lābha-sat-kāra-hetoḥ paṭhanti sva-adhyāyanti dhārayanti vācayanti deśayanti pareṣāṃ ca śruta-mātram upadiśanti | evaṃ ca vakṣyanti | vayaṃ mahā-yānikā na + anye | te pareṣām īrṣyāyanti lābha-sat-kāra-hetor yatas te labhante upabhoga-paribhogān parebhyas tat-pratyayāt te prakupyanti teṣāṃ ca + a-varṇaṃ niścārayanti kutsanti paṃsayanti vijugupsanti | ātmānaṃ ca + utkarṣayanti na tān | atas te īrṣya-hetunā ca + uttari-manuṣya-dharmair ātmānaṃ vijñapayanti | tatas te tena vastunā patitāḥ parājitā mahā-yāna-sukhād etāṃ mahā-gurukām āpattim āpadyante yayā + apāya-gāmino bhavanti | yathā kaś-cit puruṣo ratna-dvīpaṃ gacched gantuṃ nāvā samudram avatarate sa mahā-samudre svayam eva tāṃ nāvaṃ bhindyāt tatra + eva maraṇaṃ nigacched | evam eva ye ādi-karmikā bodhi-satvā mahā-guṇa-sāgaram avatartu-kāmā īrṣyā-hetos tad vadanti | tat-pratyayāt te śraddhā-nāvaṃ bhittvā prajñā-jīvitena viyogaṃ prāpnuvanti | evaṃ te bālā ādi-karmikā bodhi-satvā īrṣyā-hetor an-ṛta-pratyayā mahā-gurukām āpattim āpadyante | iyaṃ pañcamī mūla-āpattir ādi-karmikasya bodhi-satvasya ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, beginner <s>bodhisattvas</s> of forked tongue display themselves otherwise [than they are]. And these <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtrāntas</s> they hold, study, recite, expound to others, and teach extensively — [all] for the sake of fame, reputation, glory, and for gain and honor — what they have merely heard. And they will say thus: "We are <s>Mahāyānists</s>, not others." They are envious of others for gain and honor; when those [others] receive requisites and provisions, they become angry on that account, and they disparage, censure, revile, and express contempt for them, while exalting themselves but not those [others]. Then, out of the motive of envy, they inform others of their own attainment of superhuman states. Therefore, by that very fact, they are fallen, defeated, and — having fallen from the happiness of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — they incur this exceedingly grave transgression, by which they go to lower realms. Just as a certain man, having set out for a jewel-island, embarks upon the ocean in a ship, and in the great ocean he himself breaks that very ship and meets his death right there — even so, those beginner <s>bodhisattvas</s>, wishing to enter the great ocean of qualities, speak thus out of envy. Because of that, having broken the ship of faith, they arrive at separation from the life of wisdom. Thus those foolish beginner <s>bodhisattvas</s>, motivated by envy and conditioned by falsehood, incur an exceedingly grave transgression.' This is the fifth root transgression of the beginner <s>bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: punar a-paraṃ kula-putra bhaviṣyanty an-āgate * adhvani gṛha-stha-pravrajitā ādi-karmikā bodhi-satvā ye te gambhīrāḥ śūnyatā-pratisaṃyuktāḥ sūtra-anta-ādhāraṇī-kṣānti-samādhi-bhūmi-sv-alaṃ-kṛta-mahā-vidvat-puruṣāṇāṃ kṛta-śramāṇāṃ bodhi-satvānāṃ go-carās tān mahā-yāna-sūtra-antān dhārayanti paṭhanti sva-adhyāyanti pareṣāṃ ca vistareṇa vācayitvā prakāśayanti | ahaṃ ca + imān dharmān sva-buddhyā buddhvā + evaṃ ca punar ahaṃ kāruṇya-hetos tava + upadiśāmi | tvayā vā punas tathā bhāvayitavyaṃ yathā tvam atra gambhīreṣu dharmeṣu pratyakṣo bhaviṣyasi | evaṃ te jñāna-darśanaṃ bhaviṣyati yathā mama | etarhi na punar eva dadāti paṭhita-mātreṇa + aham imān evaṃ-rūpān dharmān gambhīra-gambhīrān upadiśāmi na sākṣāt-kriyayā ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, O son of good family, in the future age there will be householder and renunciant beginner <s>bodhisattvas</s> who hold, study, recite, and expound in detail to others those profound <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtrāntas</s> — connected with <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), <s>dhāraṇī</s>, <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), <s>samādhi</s>, and the [bodhisattva] stages — which are the domain of great learned men, <s>bodhisattvas</s> of accomplished effort, well-adorned [with those attainments]. And [they will say]: "I have understood these <s>dharmas</s> by my own intelligence. And moreover, out of compassion I teach them to you. You too should cultivate them in such a way that you will become a direct witness to these profound <s>dharmas</s>. Your knowledge and vision will become like mine." But in truth they do not give [what they profess] — [saying]: "By mere recitation I teach these exceedingly profound <s>dharmas</s>, not through direct realization."'

body.text: la-bha-sat-kāra-hetor ātmānaṃ vikrīṇāti | tat-pratyayāt sarva-try-adhva-gatānām arhatāṃ samyak-saṃbuddhānāṃ bodhi-satvānām ārya-pudgalānāṃ ca purataḥ sa-aparādhiko bhavati | mahā-gurukam āpattim āpadyate | visaṃvādayati deva-manuṣyān mahā-yānena | śrāvaka-yānam eva + asya na bhavati | prāg eva mahā-yānasya + avatāra-viśeṣa-adhigamaḥ | prāg eva + an-uttarā samyak-saṃbodhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'For the sake of gain and honor he sells himself. Because of that, he becomes an offender before all <s>Arhats</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddhas</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and <s>Āryapudgalas</s> (noble persons) of all three times. He incurs an exceedingly grave transgression. He deceives gods and humans by means of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Even the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> does not become his — how much less the distinctive entry and attainment of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, how much less supreme, perfect <s>bodhi</s>!'

body.text: tad yathā kaś-cit puruṣo mahā-aṭavīṃ prasthitaḥ kṣut-tarṣa-prapīḍitaḥ sa tatra mahā-phala-vṛkṣe pratiṣṭhitaḥ | āhāra-arthaṃ sa udāra-phala-vṛkṣam apahāya gandha-saṃpannaṃ rasa-saṃpannam an-āsvādya viṣa-vṛkṣam abhiruhya viṣa-phalāni bhuñjīta bhuktvā ca kālaṃ kuryāt | tad-upamāṃs tān pudgalān vadāmi | ye dur-labhaṃ manuṣya-lābhaṃ labdhvā kalyāṇa-mitraṃ sanniśritya mahā-yānam avatartu-kāmā lābha-sat-kāra-yaśo-hetor ātmānam upadarśayanti parān paṃsayanti evaṃ-rūpāṃ mahā-gurukām āpattim āpadyante yayā gurukayā + āpattyā sarva-vijñānāṃ parama-jugupsitā bhavanti | apāya-gāminas tathā-rūpāś ca pudgalā na sevanīyāḥ sarva-kṣatriya-brāhmaṇa-viṭ-śūdrāṇāṃ | yaś ca tān sevate sa sa-atisāro bhavati sarva-vijñānāṃ | iyaṃ kula-putra bodhi-satvasya ṣaṣṭhī mūla-āpattiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as a certain man, having set out for a great wilderness, oppressed by hunger and thirst, comes to stand beneath a great fruit-tree — and for the sake of food, abandoning that excellent fruit-tree, endowed with fragrance and endowed with flavor, without tasting [its fruit], climbs a poison-tree and eats poison-fruits, and having eaten, meets his death — I say those persons are comparable to that: those who, having obtained the hard-to-obtain human birth and having relied upon a spiritual friend, wishing to enter the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, display themselves for the sake of gain, honor, and fame, revile others, and incur such an exceedingly grave transgression — by which grave transgression they become utterly despised by all the wise. They go to lower realms, and such persons should not be associated with by any <s>kṣatriyas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>vaiśyas</s>, or <s>śūdras</s>. And whoever associates with them — he too becomes infected, [in the eyes of] all the wise.' This, O son of good family, is the sixth root transgression of the <s>bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: punar a-paraṃ kula-putra bhaviṣyanty an-āgate * adhvani kṣatriyāṇāṃ purohita-caṇḍālā amātya-caṇḍālā bhaṭa-caṇḍālā mūrkhāḥ paṇḍita-mānino mahā-dhanā mahā-bhogāḥ | bahu-vidheṣu dāna-maya-puṇya-kriyā-vastuṣu saṃdṛśyante te tyāga-mada-mattā māna-mada-darpeṇa kṣatriyaṃ vibhedayanti | śramaṇān kṣatriyaiḥ | te kṣatriyān niśritya śramaṇān daṇḍāpayanti | arthaṃ daṇḍena muṣanti | tena + upadraveṇa te bhikṣavaḥ paudgalikaṃ vā sāṃghikaṃ vā cāturdiśa-sāṃghikaṃ vā staupikaṃ vā śramaṇair apahṛtya teṣāṃ prāhṛtaṃ pradāpyante | te punaś caṇḍālāḥ kṣatriyasya + upanāmayiṣyanti | te ubhayato * api mūla-āpattim āpadyante | ye kṣatriya-caṇḍālāḥ śramaṇaiḥ sārddhaṃ praduṣyanti tathā-rūpaṃ ca te dharmaṃ prajñapayiṣyanti | a-dharmaṃ vā dharmam apahāya | sūtra-vinaya-śikṣā an-apekṣya kāla-upadeśa-mahā-pradeśān apahāya | mahā-karuṇā-netrī-prajñā-pāramita-śikṣā-upāya-kauśalya-śikṣāḥ yāś ca + a-pareṣu sūtreṣu śikṣā upadiṣṭās tā apahāya | tathā-rūpāṃ dharma-yuktiṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ viheṭhana-artha-pūrvakaṃ kriyā-ākāraṃ prajñapayanti | yaiḥ kriyā-ākārair bhikṣūṇāṃ viheṭhanā bhavati | rañcati śamatha-vipaśyana-anuyoga-manas-kāraṃ | te * avadhyāyanto vyāpāda-bahulā bhavanti | tena ca hetunā bhikṣūṇām apy upaśāntāḥ kleśā na + upaśamyanti na tanū-bhavanti | tat-kāle punas te bhikṣava āśaya-vipannā bhavanti śīla-vipannāś ca bhavanti | ācāra-vipannā bhavanti dṛṣṭi-vipannā bhavanti tad-dhetoḥ śaithilikā bhavanti | bāhulikā bhavanti | a-śramaṇāḥ śramaṇa-pratijñāḥ | a-brahma-cāriṇo brahma-cāri-pratijñāḥ śaṅkha-svara-samācārāḥ praṣṭavya-dharma-deśakāḥ | te bhūyasyā mātrayā sa-paricārasya kṣatriyasya sat-kṛtā bhavanti mānitāḥ pūjitā bhavanti | te ca prahāṇa-abhiyuktānāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ gṛha-stheṣv a-varṇaṃ niścārayanti | sa ca kṣatriyaḥ sa-parivāraḥ prahāṇa-abhiyuktānāṃ bhikṣūṇām antike praduṣyati avadhyāyati | yas tatra prahāṇikānāṃ bhikṣūṇām upabhoga-paribhogas taṃ sva-adhyāya-abhiratānāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ niryātayanti | te ubhayato mūla-āpattim āpadyante | tat kasya hetoḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, O son of good family, in the future age there will be among the <s>kṣatriyas</s>: chaplain-outcasts, minister-outcasts, soldier-outcasts — foolish, considering themselves learned, of great wealth and great possessions. They will be seen [engaged] in various bases of meritorious action consisting of giving. Those [persons], intoxicated with the pride of generosity, through the arrogance of the pride of self-importance, will set <s>kṣatriyas</s> against <s>śramaṇas</s> (renunciants). Relying on the <s>kṣatriyas</s>, they punish the <s>śramaṇas</s> and rob them of their property by force. By that oppression, those monks — whether their individual possessions, or those of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, or those of the <s>Saṃgha</s> of the four directions, or those belonging to a <s>stūpa</s> — are made to hand over what has been seized by the <s>śramaṇas</s> to those [outcasts]. And those outcasts will offer [the seized goods] to the <s>kṣatriya</s>. Both parties incur a root transgression. For what reason? Those <s>kṣatriya</s>-outcasts who act corruptly together with the <s>śramaṇas</s> will prescribe such a [false] <s>dharma</s> — or will abandon the [true] <s>Dharma</s> in favor of what is contrary to <s>Dharma</s>. Disregarding the <s>sūtra</s>, <s>vinaya</s>, and training, abandoning the great principles of timely instruction, abandoning the training in <s>Mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion), the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means), and the trainings taught in other <s>sūtras</s> — they prescribe such a code of conduct having as its prior purpose the harassment of monks, [a code] by which monks are harassed. It agitates the mindfulness directed toward the practice of <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). Those [monks], becoming resentful, become abundant in ill-will. And for that reason, even the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) of monks that had been pacified do not become pacified, do not become attenuated. Then at that time those monks become corrupt in intention, corrupt in morality, corrupt in conduct, corrupt in views; because of that they become lax, given to luxury, non-renunciants professing renunciation, non-celibates professing celibacy, of conch-shell-like conduct [hollow inside], teachers of <s>Dharma</s> only when questioned. They become increasingly honored, esteemed, and worshipped by the <s>kṣatriya</s> together with his retinue. And they disparage before householders those monks who are devoted to spiritual exertion. And that <s>kṣatriya</s> together with his retinue becomes hostile toward the monks devoted to exertion and disparages them. Whatever requisites and provisions belong to the monks devoted to exertion — they transfer those to the monks who delight in study. Both parties incur a root transgression. For what reason?'

body.text: dhyāyī bhikṣuḥ su-kṣetraṃ | na + adhyayana-vaiyāvṛtya-āśritā na + adhyayana-abhiyuktāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'A meditating monk is a good field [of merit] — not those who depend on study and service, not those devoted to study.'

body.text: sam-dhi-dhāraṇī-kṣānti-bhūmiṣu bhājanī-bhūtā dakṣiṇīyāḥ pātra-bhūtāḥ | āloka-kara-ālokasya mārga-upadeśakāḥ | karma-kṣetra-kleśa-kṣetrān satvān uttārayanti | nirvāṇa-gamane ca mārge pratiṣṭhāpayanti | imāḥ kula-putra + aṣṭau mūla-āpattaya iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Those who have become vessels for <s>samādhi</s>, <s>dhāraṇī</s>, <s>kṣānti</s> (patient acceptance), and the [bodhisattva] stages are worthy of offerings, are proper vessels. They are light-makers, instructors of the light-giving path. They deliver beings from the fields of <s>karma</s> and the fields of <s>kleśas</s>, and establish them on the path leading to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. These, O son of good family, are the eight root transgressions.'

body.text: āsāṃ niḥsaraṇam iha + eva sūtre * abhihitaṃ | yadi te bodhi-satvā ākāśagarbhasya bodhi-satvasya nāma śrutvā darśanam asya + ākāṅkṣeran | apāya-prapatana-bhayāt mūla-āpattīr daśayitu-kāmā | yadi te ākāśagarbhaṃ bodhi-satvaṃ namas-kuryuḥ nāma ca + asya parikīrttayeyus teṣāṃ sa kula-putro yathā bhāgyatayā sva-rūpeṇa + agratas tiṣṭhati brāhmaṇa-rūpeṇa yāvad dārikā-rūpeṇa purataḥ sthāsyati | tasya + ādi-karmikasya bodhi-satvasya yathā samutthitās tā āpattīḥ pratideśayati | gambhīraṃ ca + asya + upāya-kauśalyaṃ mahā-yāne caryām upadarśayati | yāvad a-vaivarttika-bhūmau ca pratiṣṭhāpayati || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'The escape from these is stated in this very <s>sūtra</s>: If those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, having heard the name of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Ākāśagarbha</s>, desire to see him — wishing to confess their root transgressions out of fear of falling into lower realms — if they pay homage to the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Ākāśagarbha</s> and proclaim his name, that son of good family, according to their fortune, will stand before them in his own form, or in the form of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, and so on up to the form of a maiden. He causes that beginner <s>bodhisattva</s> to confess whatever transgressions have arisen. He shows him the profound <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means) and the conduct in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, and establishes him on the stage of non-retrogression.' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: yadi teṣāṃ saṃmukhaṃ darśanaṃ na dadāti | yas tam abhiyācati | tena + ādi-karmikeṇa bodhi-satvena sa-aparādhena paścime yāme utthāya + āsanāt prāṅ-mukhena sthitvā dhūpaṃ dhūpayitavyaṃ | aruṇo deva-putra āyācitavyaḥ | evaṃ ca vaktavyaṃ | aruṇa aruṇa mahā-kṛpa mahā-bhāga mahā-uditas tvaṃ jambu-dvīpe māṃ karuṇayā + āchādayasva | śīghram ākāśagarbhaṃ mahā-kāruṇikaṃ mama vacanena bodhaya | mama svapna-antare tam upāyam upadarśaya yena + aham upāyena + āpattiṃ pratideśayāmi | ārye mahā-yāne upāya-prajñāṃ pratilapsyāmi + iti ||
body.translated_text: 'If he does not grant [the bodhisattva] a direct meeting — then whoever entreats him: that beginner <s>bodhisattva</s>, being an offender, should rise from his seat in the last watch of the night, stand facing east, and burn incense. He should entreat the <s>devaputra</s> (god-prince) <s>Aruṇa</s>, and speak thus: "<s>Aruṇa</s>, <s>Aruṇa</s>, greatly compassionate one, greatly fortunate one, greatly risen one! You who are in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, cover me with your compassion! Quickly awaken the greatly compassionate <s>Ākāśagarbha</s> on my behalf! In my dream, show me that means by which I may confess my transgression and attain the wisdom of skillful means in the noble <s>Mahāyāna</s>!"'

body.text: tena tat-kālaṃ śayyāyāṃ nidrāpayitavyaṃ saha + udgate * aruṇe iha jambu-dvīpe ākāśagarbhasya bodhi-satvasya + iha samāgamo bhavati sva-rūpeṇa ca | tasya + ādi-karmikasya bodhi-satvasya svapna-antare purataḥ sthitvā tāṃ mūla-āpattiṃ deśayati mahā-yāna-upāyena | tathā-rūpaṃ ca tasya + upāya-jñānaṃ saṃdarśayati | yena + upāya-kauśalyena sa ādi-karmiko bodhi-satvas tatra + eva bodhi-citta-a-saṃpramoṣaṃ nāma samādhiṃ pratilabhate su-dṛḍha-vyavasthitaś ca bhavati mahā-yānae ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: At that time, one should put [oneself] to sleep on the bed; and when the dawn has risen, here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Ākāśagarbha</s> comes in his own form. Standing before that beginner <s>bodhisattva</s> in a dream, he confesses that root transgression through the <s>Mahāyāna</s> method. And he shows him such knowledge of skillful means, that by that skill in means the beginner <s>bodhisattva</s> attains right there the <s>samādhi</s> called 'non-forgetfulness of <s>bodhicitta</s>' and becomes firmly established in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, and so forth.

body.text: atha vā yo * atra sūtre * adhyeṣaṇa-mantraḥ pūrvam uktaḥ | tena + ayaṃ vidhiḥ kāryaḥ | evaṃ syāt | araṇye upavane * abhyavakāśe vāgaraṃ vā tagaraṃ vā kāla-anusāri vā dhūpayitavyaṃ | prāñjalinā ca bhūtvā samantato dig-vidikṣu ca pañca-maṇḍalakena vanditvā ime mantra-padāḥ pravartayitavyāḥ | tad yathā | su-mṛśa

children.text: | vicara | sañcara | kāruṇika | murara | murara vega-dhāri namucame bhujayata kāruṇika cintā-maṇi pūraya kāruṇika sarva-āśāṃ me sthāpaya | ājñā-dhārī sphugu | rati-viveka gu | dṛṣṭi-viveka gu | pūraya kāruṇika pūrayantu mama + āśāṃ | sarvathā ca + a-śoka-gati svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Roam! Wander! <s>Kāruṇika</s> (compassionate one)! <s>Murara</s>, <s>murara</s>, O bearer of swiftness! <s>Namucame</s>! Nourish, O compassionate one! O wish-fulfilling gem, fulfill, O compassionate one, all my wishes! Establish [them]! O bearer of commands, blaze forth! O one detached from pleasure! O one detached from views! Fulfill, O compassionate one! May they fulfill my wishes! And in every way, O one whose course is sorrowless — <s>svāhā</s>!

body.translated_text: Alternatively, the invocation-mantra that was previously stated in this <s>sūtra</s> — by that, this procedure should be performed. It would be thus: In a forest, a garden, or an open space, one should burn incense — <s>agaru</s> (aloe-wood), <s>tagara</s> (valerian), or <s>kālānusāri</s> (black sandalwood). And with palms joined, having bowed in all the cardinal and intermediate directions with the five-point prostration, these <s>mantra</s>-syllables should be recited. Namely: <s>sumṛśa</s>...

body.text: vidhiḥ pūrva-vat | sarva-vyādhi-duḥkha-sarva-bhaya-sarva-upakaraṇa-vighāta-pratighāte sarva-abhīṣṭa-siddhaye ca kāryaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The procedure is as before. It should be performed for the repelling of all diseases, sufferings, all fears, and all obstructions to requisites, and for the accomplishment of all that is desired.

body.text: yadi kṣatriya-ādayo * api bodhi-satvāḥ katham eṣām āpatti-niyamo * anyeṣāṃ ca + ādhikyaṃ | atha tena sāmvarikāḥ | katham eṣām āpatti-vyavasthā | kathaṃ vā tad-doṣāt sāmvarikā api gṛhyante | na + eṣa doṣaḥ | yeṣāṃ yatra bahulaṃ saṃbhavaḥ te tatra + ā-koṭitāḥ sva-nāma-grahaṇa-darśanād bhaya-utpādana-arthaṃ | paras-paratas tu sarvaiḥ sarvā āpattayaḥ parihartavyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: If <s>kṣatriyas</s> and others too are <s>bodhisattvas</s>, how is it that the determination of transgressions belongs to these [specific groups] and the superiority to others? Or if they are bound by the <s>saṃvara</s> (vow), how is the determination of transgressions for them [established]? And how, on account of that fault, are even those bound by the vow implicated? This is not a fault. Those for whom there is frequent occasion [for transgression] in a particular [area] are classified there; and the mention of their specific names is shown for the purpose of generating fear. But all transgressions should be avoided by all, from one another.

body.text: yena vā prakṛti-mahā-sa-āvadyatayā + a-samādāno * apy a-bhavyo bhavaty ucchinna-kuśala-mūlaś ca sutarāṃ tena sāmvarikā ity alam anayā cintayā ||
body.translated_text: Or, one who by the great blameworthiness of his nature — even without having undertaken [the vow] — becomes incapable and has his wholesome roots cut off, is all the more [called] one bound by the <s>saṃvara</s>. Let there be enough of this deliberation.

body.text: upāya-kauśalya-sūtre * api mūla-āpattir uktā | kiṃ vā + api kula-putra bodhi-satvaḥ prātimokṣa-śikṣāyāṃ śikṣamāṇāḥ kalpa-śata-sahasram api mūla-phala-bhakṣaḥ syāt | sarva-satvānāṃ ca su-ukta-dur-uktāni kṣamet | śrāvaka-praty-eka-buddha-bhūmi-pratisaṃyuktaiś ca manasi-kārair vihared iyaṃ bodhi-satvasya gurukā mūla-āpattiḥ | tad yathā kula-putra śrāvaka-yānīyo mūla-āpattim āpannaḥ so * a-bhavyas tair eva skandhaiḥ parinirvātum | evam eva kula-putro * a-pratideśya + etām āpattim a-niḥsṛjya tān śrāvaka-praty-eka-buddha-manasi-kārān a-bhavyo buddha-bhūmau parinirvātum iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Upāyakauśalya Sūtra</s> (Sūtra on Skill in Means) too, a root transgression is stated: 'Even if, O son of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s> training in the <s>prātimokṣa</s> discipline were to eat only roots and fruits for a hundred thousand <s>kalpas</s>, and endure both well-spoken and ill-spoken words of all beings, and dwell in mental activities connected with the stages of a <s>śrāvaka</s> (hearer) or <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one) — this is a grave root transgression for a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Just as, O son of good family, a <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle follower who has fallen into a root transgression is incapable of attaining <s>parinirvāṇa</s> with those very aggregates — just so, O son of good family, without confessing this transgression and without abandoning those mental activities of a <s>śrāvaka</s> or <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, one is incapable of attaining <s>parinirvāṇa</s> on the <s>Buddha</s>-stage.'

body.text: āsāṃ ca mūla-āpattīnāṃ sukha-grahaṇa-dhāraṇa-artham ekīya-matānāṃ ca saṃgraha-kārikā ucyante ||
body.translated_text: And for the purpose of easy apprehension and retention of these root transgressions, and for the compilation of the views of certain [teachers], summary verses are stated:

body.text: ratna-traya-sva-haraṇād āpat-pārājikā matā | sad-dharmasya pratikṣepād dūtīyā muninā + uditā ||
body.translated_text: From stealing the property of the Three Jewels, the first <s>pārājika</s> (defeat) transgression is held; from rejection of the true <s>Dharma</s>, the second has been declared by the Sage.

body.text: duḥ-śīlasya + api vā bhikṣoḥ kāṣāya-stainya-tāḍanāt | cārake vā vinikṣepād apapravrājanena ca ||
body.translated_text: From stealing the saffron robe of a monk of corrupt morality, or from beating [him]; or from casting [him] into prison, or from causing [him] to lose ordination —

body.text: pañca + ānantarya-karaṇān mithyā-dṛṣṭi-graheṇa vā | grāma-ādi-bhedanād vā + api mūla-āpattir jina-uditā ||
body.translated_text: from committing the five <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) acts, or from holding wrong views, or from destroying a village and the like — [these are] root transgressions declared by the <s>Jina</s> (Victor).

body.text: śūnyatāyāś ca kathanāt satveṣu kṛta-buddhiṣu | buddhatva-prasthitānāṃ vā saṃbodher vinivarttanāt ||
body.translated_text: From teaching emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) to beings who have formed [only ordinary] understanding; or from turning back from perfect awakening (<s>saṃbodhi</s>) those who have set out toward <s>Buddhahood</s>;

body.text: prātimokṣaṃ parityājya mahā-yāne niyojanāt | śiṣya-yānaṃ na rāga-ādi-prahāṇāya + iti vā grahāt ||
body.translated_text: from abandoning the <s>prātimokṣa</s> and engaging [oneself] in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> [alone]; or from grasping [the view] that the <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle does not [lead to] the abandonment of attachment and so forth;

body.text: pareṣāṃ grahaṇād vā + api punaḥ sva-guṇa-kāśanāt | para-paṃsanato lābha-sat-kāra-śloka-hetunā ||
body.translated_text: or from holding [this view] among others; and again, from displaying one's own virtues; from disparaging others for the sake of gain, honor, and fame;

body.text: gambhīra-kṣāntiko * asmi + iti mithyā + eva kathanāt punaḥ | daṇḍāpayed vā śramaṇān dadyād vā śaraṇa-trayāt ||
body.translated_text: from falsely declaring, 'I possess the patience for the profound [Dharma]'; or from causing <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) to be punished; or from giving away [property] from the Three Refuges;

body.text: gṛhṇīyād dīyamānaṃ vā śamathe tyājanāt punaḥ | pratisaṃlīna-bhogaṃ ca sva-adhyāyiṣu nivedanāt ||
body.translated_text: or from accepting what is being given [wrongly]; and again, from abandoning <s>śamatha</s> (calm meditation); and from bestowing upon self-reciters [alone] the requisites reserved for the secluded.

body.text: mūlā āpattayo hy etā mahā-naraka-hetavaḥ | āryasya + ākāśagarbhasya svapne deśyāḥ puraḥ-sthitaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: These indeed are root transgressions, the causes of the great hells; they are to be confessed before the noble <s>Ākāśagarbha</s> standing [before one] in a dream.

body.text: bodhi-citta-parityāgād yācakāya + a-pradānataḥ | tīvra-mātsarya-lobhābhyāṃ krodhād vā satva-tāḍanāt ||
body.translated_text: From abandoning <s>bodhicitta</s>; from not giving to a supplicant due to intense jealousy and greed; from striking beings out of anger;

body.text: prasādyamāno yatnena satveṣu na titikṣate | ślokāt para-anuvṛttyā vā sad-dharma-ābhāsa-varṇanād | iti ||
body.translated_text: though being earnestly appeased, not showing forbearance toward beings; from reciting [false doctrines] in conformity with others; from praising a semblance of the true <s>Dharma</s>. Thus [are the transgressions listed].

body.text: ārya-kṣitigarbha-sūtre * apy uktaṃ | yo mahā-brahman mama + uddiśya pravrajito duḥ-śīla-pāpa-samācāro bhikṣur anubhūtaḥ kaśambaka-jāto * a-śramaṇaḥ śramaṇa-pratijñaḥ a-brahma-cārī brahma-cāri-pratijñaḥ | dhvastaḥ patitaḥ parājito vividhaiḥ kleśaiḥ | atha ca punaḥ sa duḥ-śīla-pāpa-samācāro bhikṣur adya + api sarva-devānāṃ yāvat sarva-manuṣyāṇāṃ yāvat puṇya-nidhīnāṃ darśayitā bhavati kalyāṇa-mitraṃ | kiṃ ca + api sa a-pātrī-bhūtaḥ tena ca punaḥ śiras-tuṇḍa-muṇḍena kāṣāya-vastra-prāvaraṇa-īryā-pathena darśana-hetunā + api bahūnāṃ satvānāṃ vividha-kuśala-mūla-upastambhana-karaḥ su-gati-mārga-darśako bhavati | tasmād yo mama + uddiśya pravrajitaḥ śīlavān duḥ-śīlo vā tasya na + anujānāmi cakra-varttir ājñām api yan mama + uddiśya pravrajitasya saha-dharmeṇa + api kāye daṇḍa-prahāraṃ vā dātuṃ cārake vā prakṣeptuṃ | aṅgam aṅgaṃ vikarttanaṃ vā kartuṃ jīvitād vā vyaparopaṇaṃ kartuṃ | kiṃ punar a-dharmeṇa ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Kṣitigarbha Sūtra</s> it is also said: 'O <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, a monk who has gone forth in my name, even if he is of corrupt morality and evil conduct, a vile person, a non-ascetic who claims to be an ascetic, a non-celibate who claims to be celibate, fallen, defeated, vanquished by various afflictions — even so, that monk of corrupt morality and evil conduct is still, to this day, the indicator of merit-treasures for all gods and all humans, and is a spiritual friend. Even though he has become unworthy, yet by his appearance — with shaven head and wearing the saffron robe and moving in the proper deportment — even by being seen, he supports the various wholesome roots of many beings and shows the path to the happy destinies. Therefore, whether one who has gone forth in my name is virtuous or of corrupt morality, I do not authorize even a <s>cakravartin</s>'s command to strike that body of one gone forth in my name — not even in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> — nor to cast him into prison, nor to sever his limbs, nor to deprive him of life. How much less [do I authorize it] when it is not in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>!'

body.text: kiṃ ca + api mṛtaḥ kathyate * asmin dharma-vinaye | atha ca punaḥ sa pudgalo go-rocana-kastūrikā-sadṛśa iti | atra + eva + āha | ye mama + uddiśya pravrajitān yāna-bhūtān pātra-bhūtān vā viheṭhayiṣyanti te sarveṣāṃ try-adhva-gatānāṃ buddhānām atīva sa-aparādhā bhavanti | samucchinna-kuśala-mūlā dagdha-santānā avīci-parāyaṇā bhavanti + iti | atra + eva + āha | sarva-buddhair adhiṣṭhito * ayaṃ mokṣa-dhvajo yad uta rakta-kāṣāya-vastram iti | asminn eva ca + uktaṃ | tena khalu punaḥ samayena bahūni śrāvaka-niyuta-śata-sahasrāṇi bahūni ca bodhi-satva-niyuta-śata-sahasrāṇi bhagavato * antike evaṃ-rūpaṃ pūrva-kṛtaṃ karma-āvaraṇaṃ pratideśayanti | vayam api bhadanta bhagavan bahūnāṃ pūrvakāṇāṃ tathā-gatānāṃ pravacane pātra-bhūtān pātra-bhūtāṃś ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ śrāvaka-yānīyān pudgalāñ jugupsitavantaḥ paṃsitavanto roṣitavanto * a-varṇa-a-yaśaḥ-kathāś ca niścāritavantaḥ | tena vayaṃ karma-āvaraṇena triṣv apāyeṣu vividhāṃ tīvrāṃ pracaṇḍāṃ duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ pratyanubhūtavantaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, though he is called 'dead' in this <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s>, yet that person is like saffron and musk. In this same [sūtra] it says: 'Those who will harass those gone forth in my name, whether worthy vessels or not — they become exceedingly guilty before all <s>Buddhas</s> of the three times. Their wholesome roots completely severed, their continuum scorched, they are destined for <s>Avīci</s> [hell].' And in this same [sūtra] it says: 'Blessed by all <s>Buddhas</s> is this banner of liberation, namely the dyed saffron robe.' And in this same [sūtra] it is said: 'Then at that time, many hundreds of thousands of <s>niyutas</s> (tens of millions) of <s>śrāvakas</s> and many hundreds of thousands of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> confessed such a previously committed karmic obstruction in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "We too, O venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, have despised, scorned, reviled, and spoken ill of worthy and unworthy vessels — the <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle followers — of the <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s> in the dispensations of many former <s>Tathāgatas</s>. By that karmic obstruction, we have experienced various intense, fierce, and painful sensations in the three lower realms."

body.text: peyālaṃ ||
body.translated_text: [Abbreviation.]

body.text: vayaṃ tat-karma-āvaraṇa-śeṣam etarhi bhagavato * antike pratideśayiṣyāmaḥ | ke-cid vadanti | vayaṃ bhagavataḥ śrāvakān vacanais tarjitavantaḥ paribhāṣitavantaḥ | ke-cid vadanti | vayaṃ bhagavataḥ śrāvakān a-pātra-bhūtān patra-a-bhūtāṃś ca praharitavantaḥ | ke-cid vadanti | vayaṃ cīvarān hṛtavantaḥ | ke-cid vadanti | vayaṃ bhagavataḥ śrāvakāṇām upabhoga-paribhogān ācchinnavantaḥ | ke-cid vadanti | vayaṃ bhagavantam uddiśya pravrajitān gṛha-sthān kāritavantaḥ tata a-sthānaṃ sāditāḥ | ke-cid vadanti | asmābhir bhagavan buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ śrāvakā a-patra-bhūtāḥ pātra-bhūtāś ca sa-aparādhikāś cārake prakṣiptās tena vayaṃ karma-āvaraṇena bahūn kalpāṃs tṛṣv apāyeṣu vividhāṃ tīvrāṃ pracaṇḍāṃ duṣkhāṃ vedanāṃ pratyanubhūtavantaḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'We shall now confess the remainder of that karmic obstruction in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Some say: 'We have threatened and abused the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>śrāvakas</s> with words.' Some say: 'We have struck the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>śrāvakas</s>, both worthy and unworthy.' Some say: 'We have stolen their robes.' Some say: 'We have confiscated the belongings and requisites of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>śrāvakas</s>.' Some say: 'We have caused those gone forth in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s name to become householders again, and through that have been brought to ruin.' Some say: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, we have cast the <s>śrāvakas</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s>, both unworthy and worthy, as guilty ones into prison. By that karmic obstruction, for many <s>kalpas</s> we have experienced various intense, fierce, and painful sensations in the three lower realms.' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: tad vayam etarhi karma-āvaraṇa-śeṣāṃ bhagavato * antike pratideśayāmaḥ | āyatyāṃ saṃvaram āpadyema | pratigahṇātu bhagavān asmākam anukampām upādāya | uddharatu bhagavān asmān an-anta-pāpebhya iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'We now confess the remainder of our karmic obstruction in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. For the future, may we undertake restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>). May the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept [our confession] out of compassion for us. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> deliver us from endless sins.' Thus in detail.

body.text: pravrajyā-antarāya-sūtre * apy an-artha uktaḥ | caturbhir mahānāman dharmaiḥ samanvāgato gṛhī a-kṣaṇa-prāpto bhavati | jāty-andhaś ca jaḍaś ca + a-jihvakaś ca caṇḍālaś ca jātu sukhito bhavaty abhyākhyāna-bahulaś ca ṣaṇḍakaś ca paṇḍakaś ca nitya-dāsaś ca | strī ca bhavati śvā ca śūkaraś ca gardabhaś ca + uṣṭraś ca āśīviṣaś ca bhavati tatra tatra jātau ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Pravrajyāntarāya Sūtra</s> (Sūtra on Obstacles to Ordination) too, harm is described: 'O <s>Mahānāman</s>, a householder endowed with four <s>dharmas</s> becomes one who has reached an unfavorable condition (<s>akṣaṇa</s>): he becomes born blind, dull-witted, tongueless, and an outcaste (<s>caṇḍāla</s>); and he is never happy, given to false accusation; and he becomes a eunuch, an impotent person, a permanent slave; and he becomes a woman, a dog, a pig, a donkey, a camel, a venomous snake — in birth after birth.'

body.text: katamaiś caturbhiḥ | iha mahānāman gṛhī pūrva-jina-krṭa-adhikārāṇāṃ satvānāṃ naiṣkramya-cittasya pravrajyā-cittasya + ārya-mārga-cittasya + antarāyaṃ karoti | anena prathamena ||
body.translated_text: 'By which four? Here, O <s>Mahānāman</s>, a householder creates an obstacle to the thought of renunciation, the thought of going forth, and the thought of the noble path for beings who have previously accumulated merit under the <s>Jinas</s>. By this first [dharma].'

body.text: punar a-paraṃ gṛhī dhana-laulyena putra-laulyena karma-vipākam a-śraddadhat putrasya vā duhitur vā bhāryāyā vā jñāti-saṃghasya + aiśvarya-sthāne vartamāne pravrajyā-antarāyaṃ karoti | anena dvitīyena + iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, a householder, out of greed for wealth, out of greed for a son, not believing in the ripening of <s>karma</s>, creates an obstacle to the going-forth of his son, or his daughter, or his wife, or of a member of his family who holds a position of authority. By this second [dharma].'

body.text: anya-dvayaṃ | sad-dharma-pratikṣepaḥ śramaṇa-brāhmaṇeṣu ca pratighaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The other two: rejection of the true <s>Dharma</s>, and hostility toward <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.

body.text: daśa ca + a-kuśalāḥ karma-pathāḥ an-arthāḥ | sad-dharma-smṛty-upasthānād vipāka-kaṭukā draṣṭavyāḥ | tataḥ kiñ-cin-mātraṃ sūtraṃ sūcyate | prāṇa-atipāta-vipāka-lavas tāvad | yathā + āha | tad yathā + agni-śikhā-carā nāma pakṣiṇo ye * agni-śikṣā-madhya-gatā na dahyante saṃhṛṣṭatarāś ca nārakeyāṇāṃ kapālaṃ bhittvā rudhiraṃ pibanti | kapāla-antara-carā nāma pakṣiṇo ye mastakaṃ bhittvā jvalita-mastaka-luṅgān pibanti | jihvā-āmiṣa-bhujo nāma pakṣiṇo ye jihvāṃ vidārya + abhito * abhitaḥ prabhakṣayanti | sā + api jihvā bhuktā punar api saṃjāyate padma-dala-komalatarā | evam artha-anurūpa-saṃjñā danta-utpāṭakā nāma kaṇṭha-nāḍy-apakarṣakā nāma | kloma-kāśinaḥ | āmāśaya-adāḥ | plīha-saṃvartakā | antra-vivara-khādinaḥ | pṛṣṭha-vaṃśa-carā nāma | marma-guhyakā nāma pakṣiṇo ye sarvāṇi marma-vivarāṇi bhittvā marmāṇi kṛntayitvā vivarāṇi praviśya majjā-maṇḍaṃ pibanti krandamānānāṃ | sūcī-chidrā nāma pakṣiṇo ye sūcī-sadṛśa-tuṇḍā raktaṃ pibanti | evam asthi-vivara-aśinaḥ ṣaṭ-tvag-bhakṣiṇaḥ | nakha-nikṛntakā medo-dāḥ snāyu-viśeṣakāḥ | keśa-uṇḍukā nāma pakṣiṇo ye keśa-mūlāny utpāṭayanti ||
body.translated_text: And the ten unwholesome courses of action are calamities. They should be seen as bitter in their ripening, from the <s>Saddharma-smṛtyupasthāna</s>. From that, just a fragment of the <s>sūtra</s> is indicated. First, a portion of the ripening of taking life. As it says: 'There are birds called "fire-crest-dwellers" who, having entered the midst of the fire-crests, are not burnt, and being greatly excited, they split open the skulls of the hell-beings and drink their blood. There are birds called "skull-cavity-dwellers" who, splitting the head open, drink the blazing brain-marrow. There are birds called "tongue-flesh-eaters" who, tearing open the tongue, devour it on all sides. And that tongue, even when eaten, is regenerated, softer than a lotus petal.' Likewise, [birds] named according to their function: 'tooth-extractors,' 'throat-vein-pullers,' 'lung-gnawers,' 'stomach-eaters,' 'spleen-crushers,' 'intestine-cavity-devourers,' 'spine-dwellers,' and birds called 'vital-point-seekers' who, splitting open all the vital-point cavities, cutting through the vital points, entering the cavities, drink the marrow-essence of those who are screaming. There are birds called 'needle-piercers' whose beaks resemble needles, who drink the blood. Likewise, 'bone-cavity-eaters,' 'six-skin-devourers,' 'nail-cutters,' 'fat-eaters,' 'sinew-separators,' and birds called 'hair-pullers' who uproot the hair at its roots.

body.text: sa evam avīci-pradeśas trīṇi yojana-śata-sahasrāṇi pakṣi-bhairava-pakṣo nāma | tatra tair anyair nārakeyaiḥ saha + an-ekāni varṣa-śata-sahasrāṇi bhakṣyate saṃbhavati ca | sa kathañ-cid api tasmān muktaḥ sarvasmād duṣkha-jāla-parivṛtaḥ | śvabhra-prapāto nāma dvitīyaḥ pradeśas tatra gacchati | trāṇa-anveṣī śaraṇa-anveṣī paritrāṇa-anveṣī samantata ekādaśabhir arci-skandhair āvṛto niḥ-sahāyaḥ karma-pāśa-bandhana-baddhaḥ samantataḥ śatrubhir āvṛtaḥ kāntāram anuprapannaḥ sarvasmān naraka-puñjād adhikataraṃ vyasanam abhiprapannas taṃ śvabhra-prapātaṃ nāma pradeśam anudhāvati | patite * atīva pādaḥ pravilīyate | utkṣiptaḥ punar api saṃbhavati | su-kumārataraḥ ślakṣṇataraḥ kharābhis tīvrābhir vedanābhir abhibhūtaḥ | tasya + evaṃ bhaya-viklava-vadanasya kara-caraṇa-sarva-aṅga-praty-aṅga-pravilīyamānasya sa pradeśaḥ śvabhra-prapāto nāma prādur-bhavati | sa tasmin deśe nipatati patitaḥ śvabhre prapatati trīṇi yojana-sahasrāṇi | punar api karma-kṛtena vāyunā + utkṣipyate | sa prapatamānaḥ kaṃka-vāyasa-grdhra-ulūkair bhakṣyate | yāvat tasya + evam utkṣipyamānasya ca prapatataś ca + an-ekāni varṣa-śata-sahasrāṇi gacchanti | kathañ-cid api tasmān muktaḥ paribhrāmitaś cakra-aṅkaṃ vivaraṃ nāma pradeśam anudhāvati | tasmiṃś ca pradeśe sahasra-arāṇi cakrāṇi prādur-bhavanti vajra-nābhīni tīkṣṇa-jvālāni śīghra-bhramāṇi tasya saha-gamanād eva tāni cakrāṇi śarīraṃ prāpya bhramanti | pe ||
body.translated_text: That <s>Avīci</s> region extends for three hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> — it is called the 'Terrifying Birds' section. There, with those other hell-beings together, he is devoured for many hundreds of thousands of years, and is reborn [again and again]. Having somehow been freed from that, surrounded by the net of all suffering, he runs to a second region called 'Precipice-Fall,' seeking shelter, seeking refuge, seeking rescue — surrounded on all sides by eleven masses of flames, without companion, bound by the fetters of <s>karma</s>, surrounded on all sides by enemies, having entered a wilderness, having come upon a calamity greater than all the masses of hell. He runs toward that region called 'Precipice-Fall.' When he falls, his feet are utterly dissolved; when flung upward, he is regenerated — more delicate, more tender — overwhelmed by harsh, intense sensations. As he stands thus, with a face distressed by terror, with his hands, feet, and all limbs and subsidiary limbs dissolving, that region called 'Precipice-Fall' appears before him. He falls there; having fallen, he plunges into a chasm three thousand <s>yojanas</s> [deep]. Again, by a wind created by <s>karma</s>, he is flung upward. As he falls, he is devoured by herons, crows, vultures, and owls. And so, as he is flung up and falls down, many hundreds of thousands of years pass. Having somehow been freed from that, whirled about, he runs to a region called 'Wheel-Marked Cavity.' And in that region, wheels with a thousand spokes appear — with diamond hubs, sharp blazing [edges], swiftly spinning — and merely from his arrival, those wheels, reaching his body, spin [through it].' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: praty-ekaṃ sarva-aṅgāni pramathnanto dahanti pāda-tale ca + asya śaṅkubhir bhidyete | evaṃ makkoṭaka-parvate | mākkoṭakaiḥ prāṇi-jātibhiḥ sa-antar-vahiḥ-parama-aṇuśaḥ prabhakṣyate | bhukto bhuktaḥ punar api saṃjāyate su-kumārataraḥ | su-kumāratayā bhūyo * apy ādhikatarāṃ vedanām anubhavati | bhukta-bhuktasya prabhūtataram eva + asya tvaṅ-māṃsaṃ prādur-bhavati | tasya prāṇa-atipāta-kṛta-upacitasya tat-phalaṃ bhavati ||
body.translated_text: Crushing all his limbs one by one, they burn [them], and at the soles of his feet he is split by stakes. Likewise, on the <s>Makkoṭaka</s> Mountain: by <s>makkoṭaka</s> creatures, he is devoured inside, outside, [down to] the finest atom. Having been eaten, he is regenerated ever more delicate; and through that delicacy, he experiences an ever more intense sensation. Of the one who is eaten again and again, an ever more abundant skin and flesh appears. This is the fruit for one who has committed and accumulated the taking of life.

body.text: a-datta-ādāna-vipākam āha | sa eṣa duṣkṛta-karma-anta-cārī ālāta-cakra-nirmāṇa-gandharva-nagara-mṛga-tṛṣṇikā-sadṛśaṃ mahad artha-jātaṃ paśyati ratna-vastra-dhana-dhānya-nikara-bhūtaṃ | tasya + evaṃ lobha-abhibhūtasya karmaṇā mohitasya + evaṃ bhavati | mama + idam iti | sa evaṃ mohitaḥ pāpa-kārī prajvalita-aṅgāra-karṣūr laṅghayitvā tad-draviṇam anudhāvati | sa karma-kṛtair yama-puruṣair gṛhyate śastra-jāla-madhya-gataḥ sarva-aṅga-praty-aṅgaśaḥ pāṭyate viśasyate dahyate * asthy-avaśeṣaḥ kriyate | na ca + asya + an-ādi-kāla-pravṛttaḥ sa lobhas tām apy avasthāṃ gatasya parihīyatae iti ||
body.translated_text: He states the ripening of taking what is not given: 'This one, who has pursued the end of evil deeds, sees a great mass of wealth — resembling a firebrand-circle, a conjured city of <s>gandharvas</s>, a mirage — consisting of heaps of jewels, cloth, riches, and grain, which belongs to others. Being overcome by greed and deluded by <s>karma</s>, the thought arises in him: "May this be mine!" Then that hell-being, leaping over blazing pits of embers, runs after that wealth. He is seized by the <s>Yama</s>-servants created by <s>karma</s>; caught in the midst of a web of weapons, he is split, slashed, and burnt limb by limb, reduced to a mere skeleton. And yet his greed — which has been operative since beginningless time — even when he has reached that state, does not diminish.'

body.text: kāma-mithyā-ācāram adhikṛtya + āha | eṣa sa pāpa-kartā tasmāc * chastra-saṅkaṭān muktaḥ katham-apy aṅgāra-karṣūr laṅghayitvā karmaṇā bhrāmitaḥ pradeśam anyaṃ prapadyate | vitatha-darśanaṃ nāma tatra karma-kṛtāṃ striyaṃ paśyati yā tena pūrvaṃ naṣṭa-smṛtinā dṛṣṭā | dṛṣṭvā ca + an-ādi-kāla-abhyasto rāga-agnir utpadyate | sa tena dhāvati yena tā striyaḥ | tāś ca + ayo-mayyo nāryaḥ karma-kṛtāḥ | tābhir asau gṛhyate | gṛhītvā ca + oṣṭhāt prabhṛti tathā bhujyate yathā + asya sarṣapa-phala-mātra-pramāṇam api na + avaśiṣṭaṃ | tasmiñ śarīre bhavati | punar api saṃbhavati | punar api bhujyate | sa kaṭukāṃ kharāṃ vedanām anubhavaṃs tasmād rāga-agner na nivartate | yena tā striyas tena bhūyaḥ saḥ saṃdhāvati | na ca + asya tat-pīḍā tathā bādhate yathā rāga-agniḥ | atha tā striyo bhūyo vajra-maya-ayo-maya-prajvalita-gātrās taṃ manuṣyam ādāya jvālā-mālā-ākula-sarva-śarīrās taṃ nārakeyaṃ siktā-muṣṭi-vad bhindanti | punar api saṃbhavati + iti pūrva-vat || pe ||
body.translated_text: Regarding sexual misconduct, it says: 'This evil-doer, having somehow been freed from that weapon-strait, having leaped over pits of embers, whirled about by <s>karma</s>, reaches another region. There, in [a place] called "False Vision," he sees a woman created by <s>karma</s> — one who was seen by him previously when his memory was destroyed. And upon seeing her, the fire of passion — habituated since beginningless time — arises. He runs toward those women. But those women are made of iron, created by <s>karma</s>. He is seized by them; and having seized him, they devour him from the lips onward, until not even a mustard-seed's measure of his body remains. He is regenerated; he is devoured again. Experiencing bitter, harsh sensations, he does not turn away from that fire of passion; he rushes again toward those women. And that torment does not afflict him as much as the fire of passion does. Then those women — with bodies of diamond, of iron, blazing — seize that man; and with bodies enveloped in garlands of flames, they crush that hell-being like a fistful of wet [clay]. He is regenerated again,' as before. And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: striyo mūlam apāyasya dhana-nāśasya sarvathā | strī-vidheyā narā ye tu kutas teṣāṃ bhavet sukham || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'Women are the root of the lower realms and of the destruction of wealth in every way; those men who are subject to women — how could there be happiness for them?' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: yāvat | strī vināśo vināśānām iha loke paratra ca | tasmāt striyo vivarjyāḥ syur yadi + icchet sukham ātmana iti ||
body.translated_text: And so on up to: 'Woman is the destruction of destructions, in this world and the next. Therefore, women should be avoided if one desires happiness for oneself.'

body.text: mṛṣā-vādam adhikatya + āha | sa tair yama-puruṣair gṛhyate gṛhītvā ca tan-mukhaṃ vidārayanti tasmāj jihvām apakarṣayanti | sā ca jihvā karma-vaśāt pañca-yojana-śata-pramāṇā bhavati | tasya mṛṣā-vādasya balena tasyāś ca saha-nirgamana-kāle te yama-puruṣā bhūmāv ānāhayanti pradīpta-ayo-mayyāṃ | karma-kṛtaṃ ca hala-sahasraṃ prādur-bhavati pradīpta-agra-saṃyuktaṃ balavadbhir balīvardais tad asya + antar-gataṃ jihvāyāṃ vahati | tatra pūya-rudhira-kṛmi-śrāviṇyo nadyaḥ pravahanti || pe ||
body.translated_text: Regarding false speech, it says: 'He is seized by those <s>Yama</s>-servants; having seized him, they tear open his mouth and drag out his tongue. And that tongue, by the power of <s>karma</s>, extends to five hundred <s>yojanas</s>. By the force of his false speech, at the time of its emergence, those <s>Yama</s>-servants pound it on the ground — on a blazing iron [floor]. And a thousand plows appear, created by <s>karma</s>, with blazing tips, drawn by powerful oxen, which plow within his tongue. There, rivers of pus, blood, and worms flow.' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: sā ca jihvā tathā su-kumārā yathā devānām akṣi ||
body.translated_text: And that tongue is as delicate as the eyes of the <s>devas</s>.

body.text: yāvat sa vedanātas tanati krandati vikrośati na ca + asya tad-duḥkhaṃ kaś-cid apanayati + iti vistaraḥ | tasya + evaṃ pracaṇḍām vedanām anubhavato * an-ekāni varṣa-śata-sahasrāṇi sā ca jihvā kṛṣyate | sā kathañ-cit tasya nārakasya mukhe praviśati | sa bhaya-vihvala-vadano yena vā tena vā niḥpalāyate * aṅgāra-karṣūṣu dahyamāno nimajjan | tasya + evaṃ duḥkha-ārttasya + a-śaraṇasya + a-parāyaṇasya punar api yama-puruṣāḥ prādur-bhavanti mudgara-asi-pāṇayaḥ | te taṃ puruṣaṃ mastakāt prabhṛti yāvat pādau cūrṇayanti + ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: And so on: 'He stretches out in agony, screams, and cries out — but no one removes that suffering of his.' And so forth in detail. 'As he experiences that fierce sensation for many hundreds of thousands of years, that tongue is [continually] plowed. Somehow that tongue enters the mouth of that hell-being. He, with a face overcome by terror, flees in whatever direction [he can], being burnt and sinking in pits of embers. And for him, afflicted by suffering, without shelter, without refuge, the <s>Yama</s>-servants again appear, with clubs and swords in their hands. They crush that man from head to foot,' and so on.

body.text: paiśunya-vipākas tu yathā + eva mṛṣā-vādasya trīṇi yojana-śatāni jihvā + iti viśeṣas tu | tāṃ yama-puruṣā nistriṃśān ādāya pradīpta-dhārān jihvāṃ nikṛntanti | jambukaiś ca + anysamin pradeśe bhakṣyate | parama-kaṭukāṃ vedanāṃ prativedayate sa krandati vikrośaty a-vyakta-akṣaraṃ jihvā-virahita ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: The ripening of slander, however — just as with false speech, the tongue extends three hundred <s>yojanas</s>; the distinction is: the <s>Yama</s>-servants, taking blazing-edged swords, cut that tongue. And in another region, he is devoured by jackals. He experiences the most bitter sensation; he screams and cries out with inarticulate sounds, having been deprived of his tongue — and so on.

body.text: pāruṣya-vipākam āha | te tāṃ jihvām āsyaṃ vidārya gṛhṇanti | gṛhītvā niśita-dhāraiḥ śastraiś chittvā tasya bhūya eva khādanīya-arthena mukhe prakṣipanti | sa ca jighansā-arditaḥ kṣut-kṣāma-vadanaḥ sva-rudhira-lālā-parisrutāṃ tām eva sva-jihvāṃ bhakṣayati | sā ca jihvā chinnā punar api saṃjāyate karma-vaśāt | atha sa bhūmau vedanā-ārttaḥ parivartate viceṣṭate krandate | tasya + evaṃ vedanā-ārttasya parivṛtta-nayana-tārakasya duṣkha-ārttasya dīnasya + a-sahāyasya + ekākinaḥ sva-kṛtam upabhuñjānasya yama-puruṣā anuśāsanī-gāthāṃ bhāṣante ||
body.translated_text: He states the ripening of harsh speech: 'They tear open his mouth and seize his tongue. Having seized it, they cut it with sharp-edged weapons and put it back into his mouth for the purpose of eating. And he, afflicted by hunger, with a face emaciated by starvation, streaming with his own blood and saliva, eats that very tongue of his own. And that tongue, when cut, is regenerated by the power of <s>karma</s>. Then he rolls about on the ground, afflicted by sensation, writhes, and screams. For him — thus afflicted by sensation, with upturned eyeballs, afflicted by suffering, wretched, without companion, alone, experiencing what he himself has created — the <s>Yama</s>-servants recite an instructive verse:'

body.text: jihvā-dhanor vinirmuktas tīkṣṇo vāg viśikhas tvayā | pāruṣyam iti yad dṛṣṭaṃ tasya + etat phalam āgatam ||
body.translated_text: 'Discharged from the bow of the tongue, the sharp arrow of speech — this was seen as harsh speech; of that, this fruit has arrived.'

body.text: iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus, in detail.

body.text: saṃbhinna-pralāpa-vipākam āha ||
body.translated_text: He states the ripening of frivolous speech.

body.text: tasya tat prajvalitaṃ tāmra-drava-lohitaṃ jihvāṃ dahati | jihvāṃ dagdhvā kaṇṭhaṃ dahati | kaṇṭhaṃ dagdhvā hṛdayaṃ dahati hṛdayaṃ dagdhvā + antrāṇi dahati | tāny api dagdhvā pakva-āśayaṃ dahati | pakva-āśayam api dagdhvā + adho-bhāgena nirgacchati ||
body.translated_text: 'That blazing, molten copper-red [substance] burns his tongue. Having burnt the tongue, it burns the throat. Having burnt the throat, it burns the heart. Having burnt the heart, it burns the intestines. Having burnt those too, it burns the lower stomach. Having burnt the lower stomach too, it exits from the lower part [of the body].'

body.text: yama-puruṣā gāthām āhuḥ | pūrva-uttara-a-baddha-padaṃ nir-arthakam a-saṃgatam | a-baddhaṃ yat tvayā proktaṃ tasya + etat phalam āgataṃ ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Yama</s>-servants recite a verse: 'Words with disconnected first and last parts, meaningless, incoherent — that which was spoken by you unconnectedly — of that, this fruit has arrived.'

body.text: yā na

children.text: satyavatī nityaṃ na ca + adhyayana-tat-parā | na sā jihvā budhair dṛṣṭā kevalaṃ māṃsa-khaṇḍikā | iti vistaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'always truthful, and not devoted to study — that tongue was not considered by the wise [to be a tongue]; it is merely a piece of flesh.' Thus, in detail.

body.translated_text: That which is not —

body.text: abhidhyā-vipākam āha | atha paśyati riktaṃ tuccham a-sārakaṃ karma-kṛtaṃ bahu-draviṇaṃ para-parigṛhītaṃ tasya karma-codita-vyāmohitasya + evaṃ bhavati | mama + idaṃ syād iti | tataḥ sa nārakas tena + eva dhāvati yena tad dravyaṃ | tasya + abhidhyā-ākhya-mānasasya + a-kuśalasya + āsevita-bhāvita-bahulī-kṛtasya tat-phalaṃ yad asau narake viparītaṃ paśyati | tasya + evaṃ paśyato * abhidhyā-bahulasya haste śastraṃ prādur-bhavati sa tena dhāvati | teṣām apy anyeṣāṃ nārakāṇāṃ haste śastrāṇi prādur-bhavanti | sa taiḥ saha śastreṇa yudhyate yāvat tathā kartyate yathā sarṣapa-phala-mātram api na bhavati māṃsam asya śarīre tathā + asthi-kaṅkāla-avaśeṣaḥ kriyate || pe ||
body.translated_text: He states the ripening of covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>): 'Then he sees — empty, hollow, without essence, created by <s>karma</s> — a great quantity of wealth belonging to others. In that one, driven and deluded by <s>karma</s>, the thought arises: "May this be mine!" Then that hell-being runs toward that very wealth. Through that unwholesome [deed] called covetousness, which has been repeatedly practiced, cultivated, and made abundant, the fruit is that he sees things in reverse in hell. As he sees thus, full of covetousness, a weapon appears in his hand; he runs [toward the others] with it. In the hands of those other hell-beings too, weapons appear. He fights with them using weapons, until he is so cut up that not even a mustard-seed's measure of flesh remains on his body — he is reduced to a mere bone-skeleton.' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: pareṣāṃ sampa ... mama syād iti cintitaṃ | tasya + abhidhyā-samutthasya viṣasya phalam āgatam iti ||
body.translated_text: "The wealth of others ... 'may it be mine' — thus he thought. The fruit of that poison born of covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) has come."

body.text: vyāpāda-phalam āha | karma-mayāḥ siṃha-vyāghra-sarpāḥ krodha-abhibhūtāḥ puratas tiṣṭhante | etebhyo bhaya-bhīto yena vā tena vā niḥpalāyate | sa kathaṃ śaknoti palāyitum a-śubhasya karmaṇaḥ | sa tair gṛhyate | gṛhītvā ca pūrvaṃ tāvan mastakād bhujyate yāvat pārśvataḥ sarpair viṣa-daṃṣṭraiḥ saṃdaśya saṃdaśya bhakṣyate | vyāghrair api pṛṣṭhato bhakṣyate | pādāv api vahninā dāhyete sa yama-puruṣair dūrād iṣubhir vidhyatae iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: The fruit of ill-will (<s>vyāpāda</s>) is stated: "Lions, tigers, and serpents made of <s>karma</s>, overwhelmed by anger, stand before [him]. Terrified by fear of these, he flees in one direction or another. But how can he flee from the fruit of unwholesome <s>karma</s>? He is seized by them. Having seized him, first he is devoured from the head downward; from the sides he is bitten again and again and consumed by serpents with venomous fangs; he is also devoured from behind by tigers; and both his feet are burned by fire; and <s>Yama</s>'s servants shoot him with arrows from afar" — and so on in detail.

body.text: mithyā-dṛṣṭi-phalaṃ punar a-parimitaṃ | pāṭhas tu saṃkṣipyate | śastra-varṣa-tomara-vajra-varṣa-aśani-pāṣāṇa-varṣe hanyate | ekādaśabhir arcci-skandhaiḥ kṣut-pipāsa-agninā ca sukha-nirgatena nir-antaraṃ dahyatae iti ||
body.translated_text: The fruit of wrong views (<s>mithyā-dṛṣṭi</s>) is again immeasurable. The reading is abbreviated: "He is struck in a rain of weapons, javelins, thunderbolt-rain, lightning, and stones. He is burned unceasingly by eleven masses of flame, by the fire of hunger and thirst, and by the fire that has departed from [any] pleasure."

body.text: kāma-mūlāś ca sarva-an-arthā iti tebhya eva + udvejitavyaṃ | yathā + atra + eva + āha | asty agni-kuṇḍo nāma narakaḥ | tatra katareṇa karmaṇā satvā upapadyante | yena a-śramaṇena śramaṇa-pratijñena mātṛ-grāmasya nṛtta-gītasya + ābharaṇānāṃ vā śabdaṃ śrutvā + a-yoniśena manas-kāreṇa + ākṣipta-buddhinā tac * chrutvā hasita-laḍita-krīḍitāny a-śucim uktaṃ || pe ||
body.translated_text: And all calamities have sensual desire as their root; therefore one should feel revulsion toward them. As stated right here: "There is a hell called <s>Agnikuṇḍa</s> (Fire-Pit). By what <s>karma</s> are beings reborn there? By a non-renunciant who has made the profession of a renunciant — upon hearing the sounds of women, of dance and song, or of ornaments — with improper mental attention, with distracted mind, having heard that, [indulging in] laughter, playful gestures, and sport, the impure is spoken of." [Abbreviated.]

body.text: tatra te nārakā ayo-varṣeṇa sarva-aṅga-praty-aṅgaśaś cūrṇyante * aṅgāra-varṣeṇa ca pacyante dahyantae ity ādi | evaṃ paurāṇa-kāma-āsvādana-smaraṇāt padumo nāma narakaḥ paṭhyate svapna-anta-bhūta-smaraṇāc ca | tatra te nārakāḥ kumbhiṣu pacyante | te droṇiṣv ayo-mayair muṣalair hanyantae iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: "There those hell-beings are crushed in every limb and secondary limb by a rain of iron and are cooked and burned by a rain of glowing coals" — and so forth. Thus, from the mere memory of savoring former sensual pleasures, a hell called <s>Paduma</s> (Lotus) is described; and from memory that has become like the end of a dream [as well]. "There those hell-beings are cooked in cauldrons. They are struck with iron hammers in troughs" — and so on in detail.

body.text: evam apsarasaḥ prārthanayā brahma-carya-pariṇāmanān mahā-padumo nāma naraka uktaḥ | tatra kṣāra-nadī-taraṅginī nāma pravahati | tasyāṃ nadyāṃ yāny asthīni te pāṣāṇāḥ | yac * chevālaṃ te keśāḥ | yaḥ paṅkas tan māṃsaṃ | yā āpaḥ tat kathitaṃ tāmraṃ | ye matsyās te nārakā ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: Thus, from praying for celestial nymphs (<s>apsarases</s>) and from dedicating celibacy [for that end], a hell called <s>Mahāpaduma</s> (Great Lotus) is described. "There flows a river of alkaline water called <s>Taraṅgiṇī</s>. The bones in that river are the stones. The moss is the hair. The mud is the flesh. The water is said to be [molten] copper. The fish are the hell-beings" — and so forth.

body.text: evaṃ puruṣasya puruṣeṇa saha maithuna-vipratipatteḥ a-prameyā a-kāraṇā viśeṣāḥ paṭhyante | evaṃ śiśubhiḥ saha vipratipatteḥ kṣāra-nadyām uhyamānān dārakān paśyati | te taṃ vilapanti | sa tāṃ nadīm avagāhate | teṣu bālakeṣu tīvra-sneha-pratibandha-śoka-duṣkha-vegāt | evaṃ go-vaḍava-aja-eḍaka-ādiṣu prakṛti-sa-āvadyaḥ kāma-mithyā-ācāraḥ kharatara-vipākaḥ paṭhyate | tāsām eva go-vaḍava-ādīnāṃ tapta-ayo-mayīnāṃ a-kuśala-nirmitānāṃ yoni-mārgeṇa sa tiryak-kāma-sevī praviśati | sa tāsām udare pradīpta-aṅgāra-nikara-paripūrṇe svidyate pacyate bahūni varṣa-śata-sahasrāṇi + iti vistareṇa draṣṭavyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Thus, from sexual transgression of a man with a man, immeasurable and causeless [i.e., unimaginable] varieties [of torment] are described. Likewise, from transgression with children: "He sees boys being carried along in the alkaline river. They cry out to him. He plunges into that river, due to the force of grief and suffering from intense affectionate attachment to those children." Thus, regarding cattle, mares, goats, sheep, and so forth, sexual misconduct with animals, which is inherently blameworthy, is described as having an even harsher retribution. "He, the one who indulges in bestial desire, enters through the genital passage of those very cows, mares, and so forth — which are made of heated iron and created by his unwholesome [<s>karma</s>]. He is burned and cooked in their wombs filled with heaps of blazing coals, for many hundreds of thousands of years" — this should be seen in detail.

body.text: evam anya-nāśitāsv api bhikṣuṇīṣu vipratipannānāṃ mahā-naraka-pātanāḥ paṭhyante | evaṃ sva-strīṣv apy a-yoni-mārgeṇa gacchataḥ | evaṃ prasahya + ānītāsv api para-strīṣu labdhāsu ca kanyāsu | evam upavāsa-sthāsu evaṃ gurūṇāṃ patnīṣu jñāti-śabda-mānitāsu ca vipratipatteḥ tīvrāś ca + a-parimāṇāś ca mahā-naraka-pātanāḥ paṭhyante ||
body.translated_text: Thus, for those who have transgressed even with nuns who had been corrupted by others, falls into great hells are described. Likewise for one who approaches even his own wife by an improper passage. Likewise regarding other men's wives taken by force, and maidens obtained [illicitly]. Likewise regarding those observing fasting vows. Likewise regarding the wives of teachers and those honored with the title of 'kinswoman' — for transgression with them, intense and immeasurable falls into great hells are described.

body.text: sapta-maithuna-saṃyukta-sūtre * apy āha | iha brāhmaṇa ekatyo brahma-cāriṇam ātmānaṃ pratijāṇīte | sa na + iha + eva mātṛ-grāmeṇa sārddhaṃ dvayaṃ samāpadyate * api tu mātṛ-grāmaṃ cakṣuṣā rūpaṃ nidhyāyan paśyati | sa tadā svādayati adhyavasyati adhyavasāya tiṣṭhati | ayam ucyate brāhmaṇa brahma-cārī saṃyukto maithunena dharmeṇa na visaṃyuktaḥ | a-pariśuddhaṃ brahma-caryaṃ carati ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Saptamaithumasaṃyukta-sūtra</s> (Sūtra Connected with Seven [Forms of] Sexual Conduct) it is also said: "Here, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a certain one claims himself to be celibate. He does not engage in intercourse with women in this very life, but he gazes at a woman, looking upon her form with focused attention. He then savors it, clings to it, and remains clinging. This one, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, is called a celibate who is conjoined with the dharma of sexual conduct, not disjoined from it. He practices impure celibacy."

body.text: evaṃ mātṛ-grāmeṇa sārddhaṃ saṃkrīḍataḥ saṃkilikilāyamānasya āsvādayataḥ a-pariśuddhaṃ brahma-caryam uktaṃ | evaṃ mātṛ-grāma-apasthānam āsvādayataḥ | evaṃ tiraḥ-kuḍya-gatasya tiro-duṣya-gatasya vā mātṛ-grāmasya nṛtta-gīta-ādi-śabdam āsvādayato maithuna-saṃyogam ity uktam | evaṃ pañca-kāma-guṇa-samarpitaṃ param avalokya + āsvādayataḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus, for one who sports and plays and flirts with women and savors it, impure celibacy is declared. Likewise for one who savors the proximity of women. Likewise for one who, while behind a wall or behind a curtain, savors the sounds of women's dance, song, and so forth — this is called conjunction with sexual conduct. Likewise for one who, having looked upon another endowed with the five qualities of sensual pleasure, savors it.

body.text: evaṃ deva-ādi-sthāneṣu brahma-carya-pariṇāmanāt saṃyukto maithunena dharmeṇa na visaṃyukta iti ||
body.translated_text: Thus, from dedicating celibacy [to obtain rebirth in] divine and other stations, one is conjoined with the dharma of sexual conduct, not disjoined from it.

body.text: yataś ca + ete kāmā evaṃ smaraṇa-prārthanā-viṣayam api gatā evam an-artha-karās tena + eva kāma-apavādaka-sūtre * abhihitam | nivāraya bhikṣo cittaṃ kāmebhyaḥ | sa-bhayaś ca + eṣa mārgaḥ sa-pratibhayaḥ sa-kaṇṭakaḥ sa-gahanaḥ unmārgaḥ ku-mārgo vedanā-pathaḥ | a-sat-puruṣa-saṃsevitaḥ | na + eṣa mārgaḥ sat-puruṣa-saṃsevitaḥ | na tvam evaṃ cintayasi | kasmāt alpa-āsvādāḥ kāmā uktā bhagavatā | bahu-duṣkha-bahu-upadravā bahu-upāyāsā | ādīnavo * atra bhūyān | rogo bhikṣavaḥ kāmā gaṇḍaḥ śalya-madya-madya-mūlam āmiṣa-vaḍisaṃ mṛtyur a-nityāḥ kāmās tucchāḥ mṛṣā-moṣa-dharmiṇaḥ svapna-upamāḥ kāmāḥ | kim apy ete bāla-ullāpanāḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: Since these sensual desires, even when they have become merely objects of memory and longing, produce such harmful consequences — therefore it is said in the <s>Kāmāpavādaka-sūtra</s> (Sūtra Denouncing Sensual Desires): "Restrain your mind from sensual desires, O monk! This is a path of fear, a path of danger, full of thorns, full of thickets — a wrong path, a bad path, a path of suffering, frequented by bad people. This is not a path frequented by good people. Do you not reflect thus? For it was said by the <s>Bhagavan</s> (Lord): Sensual desires are of little savor, of much suffering, much tribulation, much distress. The danger therein is greater. Sensual desires, O monks, are a disease, a boil, a barb, intoxication, the root of intoxication, bait on a hook, death, impermanent, empty, of a deceitful nature, like a dream. Are these not mere deceptions of fools?" [Abbreviated.]

body.text: yathā mṛgāṇāṃ bandhanāya kūṭaṃ dvi-jānāṃ bandhanāya jālaṃ | matsyānāṃ bandhanāya kupinaṃ | markaṭānāṃ bandhanāya lepaḥ pataṅ-gānāṃ bandhanāya + agni-skandhaḥ | evaṃ kāmāḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: "Just as a trap [is used] for the binding of deer, a net for the binding of birds, a snare for the binding of fish, glue for the binding of monkeys, a mass of fire for the binding of moths — so are sensual desires." [Abbreviated.]

body.text: kāma-paryeṣaṇāṃ carato dīrgha-rātraṃ siṃhānāṃ mukhe parivartitasya + anto na prajñāyate | yāvad go-ghātakānāṃ gava-āsanānāṃ mukhe parivartitasya + anto na prajñāyate | yāvan maṇḍūkānāṃ satāṃ sarpāṇāṃ mukhe parivartitasya + anto na prajñāyate | dīrgha-rātraṃ kāmān pratisevamānānāṃ corā iti kṛtvā gṛhītānāṃ śiraś-chinnānām anto na prajñāyate | pāradārikāḥ pāripanthikā grāma-ghātakā jana-pada-ghātakā yāvad granthi-mocakā iti kṛtvā gṛhītānāṃ śiraś-chinnānām anto na prajñāyate | duṣkhaṃ tīvraṃ kharaṃ kaṭukam anubhūtaṃ rudhiraṃ prasyanditaṃ pragharitaṃ yac caturṣu mahā-samudreṣu + udakāt prabhūtataraṃ || pe ||
body.translated_text: "For one who pursues the search for sensual pleasures, there is no end to having been turned about in the mouths of lions throughout the long night [of <s>saṃsāra</s>]; up to having been turned about in the mouths of cattle-slaughterers and cow-butchers, there is no end; up to having been turned about, being frogs, in the mouths of serpents, there is no end. For those pursuing sensual pleasures throughout the long night who were seized on the charge of being thieves, having had their heads cut off — there is no end. For those seized on the charge of being adulterers, highway robbers, village destroyers, province destroyers, and even pickpockets, having had their heads cut off — there is no end. The suffering experienced — sharp, harsh, bitter — and the blood that has oozed and flowed is more abundant than the water in the four great oceans." [Abbreviated.]

body.text: kāyo hy ayaṃ bahv-ādīnavaḥ | asthi-saṃghātaḥ snāyu-saṃbaddho māṃsena + anuliptaḥ carmaṇā paryavanaddhaḥ chavyā praticchannaḥ chidra-vicchidraḥ kṛmi-saṃgha-niṣevitaḥ satvānām an-arthakaḥ kleśa-karmaṇāṃ vastu ||
body.translated_text: "For this body is full of danger: a collection of bones, bound by sinews, smeared with flesh, wrapped in skin, covered by the outer skin, full of holes and openings, inhabited by swarms of worms, unprofitable to sentient beings, the basis of afflictions and actions."

body.text: asmin kāye vividhā ābādhā utpadyante | tad yathā cakṣū-rogaḥ śrotra-rogo yāvad arśāṃsi piṭako bhagan-daraḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: "In this body various ailments arise, such as: eye disease, ear disease, and so on up to hemorrhoids, boils, and fistula." [Abbreviated.]

body.text: kāyikāḥ santāpāḥ kāyikaṃ duṣkhaṃ | kāyasya jīrṇatā bhagnatā kubjatā | khālityaṃ pālityaṃ vali-pracuratā | indriyāṇāṃ pāripākaḥ paribhedaḥ saṃskārāṇāṃ purāṇī-bhāvo jarjarī-bhāvaḥ | yāvan na + arhasy evam udgharantaṃ pragharantaṃ jugupsanīyaṃ kāyaṃ pratiṣevituṃ || pe ||
body.translated_text: "Bodily torments, bodily suffering; the aging, breaking, stooping of the body; baldness, graying of hair, abundance of wrinkles; the ripening and decay of the sense-faculties; the aging and crumbling of the <s>saṃskāras</s> (mental formations). So far [you should reflect]: you are not worthy to indulge this body that is oozing, dripping, and disgusting." [Abbreviated.]

body.text: kā tava bhikṣo kāma-a-śāntiḥ | kaś ca tvāṃ pralobhayati | kathaṃ ca tvaṃ prāhito mūrchito * adhyavasito * adhyavasānam āpannaḥ | yadā + ahaṃ parinirvṛto bhavāmi | sad-dharmaś ca + antar-hito bhavati | tvaṃ ca kāmān pratisevya vinipāta-gato bhaviṣyasi | kadā jarā-maraṇād ātmānaṃ parimocayiṣyasi ||
body.translated_text: "What is this unquenched desire of yours, O monk? And who seduces you? How have you become infatuated, deluded, absorbed, and given to attachment? When I have passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> and the true <s>Dharma</s> has disappeared, you, having indulged in sensual desires, will fall into perdition. When will you liberate yourself from old age and death?"

body.text: alaṃ bhikṣo nivāraya cittaṃ kāmebhyaḥ | a-kālaḥ kāma-paryeṣaṇāyāḥ | kālo * ayaṃ dharma-paryeṣaṇāyā iti ||
body.translated_text: "Enough, O monk! Restrain your mind from sensual desires! This is not the time for the pursuit of sensual pleasures. This is the time for the pursuit of the <s>Dharma</s>."

body.text: ugradatta-paripṛcchāyām apy āha | tena kāma-mithyā-ācārāt prativiratena bhavitavyaṃ sva-dāra-saṃtuṣṭena para-dāra-an-abhilāṣiṇā + ārakta-netra-prekṣiṇā nirviṇṇa-manasā | eka-anta-duṣkhāḥ kāmā | ity abhīkṣṇaṃ manasi-kāra-prayuktena | yadā + apy asya sva-dāreṣu kāma-vitarka utpadyeta | tadā + api tena sva-dāreṣv a-śubha-anudarśinā uttrasta-manasā | kleśa-vaśatayā kāmāḥ pratisevitavyāḥ | na tv adhyavasāna-vinibaddhena nityam a-nitya-an-ātma-a-śuci-saṃjñinā | evaṃ ca + anena smṛtir upasthāpyā | tathā + ahaṃ kariṣyāmi yathā saṃkalpair api kāmān na paribhokṣye | kaḥ punar vādo dvi-indriya-samāpattyā vā + anaṅga-vijñaptyā vā + iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ugradattaparipṛcchā</s> it is also said: "He should abstain from sexual misconduct (<s>kāma-mithyācāra</s>), being content with his own wife, not desiring another's wife, looking with eyes free of passion, with a mind of disenchantment. 'Sensual desires are exclusively suffering' — thus he should be constantly engaged in mental reflection. Even when a lustful thought arises toward his own wife, then too, seeing impurity in his own wife, with a mind of alarm, he should indulge in sensual pleasures only under the compulsion of afflictions, but not bound by attachment — always perceiving [all things as] impermanent, non-self, and impure. And he should establish mindfulness thus: 'I shall act in such a way that I will not enjoy sensual pleasures even in imagination, let alone through the union of two sense-organs or through a bodiless intimation.'"

body.text: punar atra + eva + āha | bodhi-satvena sva-bhāryāyā antike tisraḥ saṃjñā utpādayitavyāḥ | katamās tisraḥ | rati-krīḍā-sahāyikā + eṣā na + eṣā para-loka-sahāyikā | anna-pāna-sahāyikā + eṣā na + eṣā karma-vipāka-anubhavana-sahāyikā | sukha-sahāyikā + eṣā na + eṣā duṣkha-sahāyikā ||
body.translated_text: And further in the same [text] it says: "A <s>bodhisattva</s> should generate three perceptions toward his wife. Which three? 'She is a companion for enjoyment and play, not a companion for the next world. She is a companion for food and drink, not a companion for experiencing the results of <s>karma</s>. She is a companion for pleasure, not a companion for suffering.'"

body.text: yāvad a-parās tisraḥ | śīla-antarāya-saṃjñā dhyāna-antarāya-saṃjñā prajñā-antarāya-saṃjñā ||
body.translated_text: Up to three more [perceptions]: the perception of her as an obstacle to moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), the perception of her as an obstacle to meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and the perception of her as an obstacle to wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>).

body.text: a-parās tisraḥ | cora-saṃjñā badhaka-saṃjñā naraka-pāla-saṃjñā iti ||
body.translated_text: Three more: the perception of her as a thief, the perception of her as a killer, and the perception of her as a hell-guardian.

body.text: candrottarā-dārikā-paripṛcchāyām apy uktaṃ | atha candrottarā-dārikā samanantaraṃ pradhāvantaṃ taṃ mahāntaṃ jana-kāyaṃ dṛṣṭvā tasyāṃ velāyāṃ vihāyasa-antarīkṣe tāla-mātram abhyudgamya sthitvā ca taṃ mahāntaṃ jana-kāyaṃ gāthābhir adhyabhāṣata ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Candrottarādārikāparipṛcchā</s> (Questions of the Maiden <s>Candrottarā</s>) it is also said: Then the maiden <s>Candrottarā</s>, having seen that great crowd of people rushing forward, at that moment rose into the sky to a height of one palm-tree and, standing there, addressed that great crowd of people with verses:

body.text: kāyaṃ mama + īkṣadhvam imaṃ mano-jñaṃ suvarṇa-varṇaṃ jvalana-prakāśam | na rakta-cittasya hi mānuṣasya prajñāyate śobhanakaṃ śarīram ||
body.translated_text: "Behold this body of mine — beautiful, golden-hued, shining like flame. But for a man whose mind is full of passion, no beautiful body is discerned."

body.text: ye etv agni-karṣū-upama-saṃpradīptān tyajanti kāmān viṣayeṣv a-gṛddhāḥ | ṣaḍ-indriyaiḥ saṃvara-saṃvṛtāś ca ye brahma-caryaṃ ca caranti śubham ||
