body.translated_text: "Those who abandon sensual desires — blazing like a pit of fire — who are free from greed for sense-objects, who are restrained with the restraint of the six senses, and who practice the beautiful holy life —"

body.text: dṛṣṭvā ca dārān hi parasya ye vai kurvanti mātā-bhaginī + iti saṃjñāṃ | prāsādikās te hi su-darśanīyā bhavanti nityaṃ paramaṃ mano-jñāḥ ||
body.translated_text: "And those who, having seen the wives of others, generate the perception of them as 'mother' or 'sister' — they indeed are graceful, beautiful to behold, always supremely delightful."

body.text: sphuṭām imāṃ vettha purīṃ samantād yo roma-kūpān mama ca + ati-gandhaḥ | na rāga-cittena mayā + arjito * ayam phalaṃ tu dānasya damasya ca + idam ||
body.translated_text: "You know this body of mine to be radiant all around, and the supreme fragrance from my pores. This was not obtained by me through a mind of passion — rather, this is the fruit of giving and self-restraint."

body.text: na me samutpadyati rāga-cittaṃ mā vīta-rāgāsu janīṣva rāgaṃ | sākṣī mama + ayaṃ purato muni-indraḥ satyaṃ yathā vedmi na jātu mithyā ||
body.translated_text: "No thought of passion arises in me. Do not generate passion toward one who is free from passion. This lord of sages is my witness here before [us] — I speak truth, never falsehood."

body.text: yūyaṃ ca pūrvaṃ pitaro mama + āsa | ahaṃ ca yuṣmākam abhūj janitrī | bhrātā svasā ca + api pitā babhūva ko rāga-cittaṃ janayej jananyāṃ ||
body.translated_text: You were formerly my fathers, and I was your mother; you were my brother, sister, and also father — who would generate a mind of <s>rāga</s> (passion) toward one's own mother?

body.text: praghātitāḥ prāk ca mama + atha sarve | ahaṃ viśastā ca purā bhavadbhiḥ | sarve a-mitrā vadhakāḥ parasya | kathaṃ tu vā jāyati rāga-cittam ||
body.translated_text: All of you were previously slain by me, and I too was slaughtered by you in the past; all are enemies, killers of one another — how then can a mind of <s>rāga</s> (passion) arise?

body.text: na rūpavanto hi bhavanti rāgāt | na rakta-cittāḥ su-gatiṃ vrajanti | na nirvṛtiṃ yānti ca rakta-cittā rāgo hi tasmāt parivarjanīyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, beings do not become beautiful through <s>rāga</s> (passion), nor do those with passion-filled minds go to a good rebirth; those with passion-filled minds do not attain <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation) — therefore <s>rāga</s> (passion) should be completely abandoned.

body.text: kāmasya hetor nirayaṃ patanti | pretās tiraśco * atha bhavanti rāgāt | kumbha-aṇḍa-yakṣā asurāḥ piśācā bhavanti ye rāga-parītta-cittāḥ ||
body.translated_text: For the sake of <s>kāma</s> (sensual desire), they fall into hell; from <s>rāga</s> (passion) they become <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) and animals; <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>piśācas</s> — such become those whose minds are consumed by <s>rāga</s> (passion).

body.text: kāṇāś ca khañjāś ca vi-jihvakāś ca | vi-rūpakāś ca + eva bhavanti rāgāt | bhavanti nānā-vidha-doṣa-bhājāś caranti ye kāma-carīṃ jaghanyām ||
body.translated_text: One-eyed, lame, tongueless, and deformed — such they become through <s>rāga</s> (passion); they become partakers of manifold defects, those who pursue the lowest course of sensual desire.

body.text: yac cakra-vartitvam avāpnuvanti | bhavanti śakrās tri-daśa-īśvarāś ca | brahmāṇa īśā

children.text: vaśa-varttinaś ca tad brahma-caryaṃ vipulaṃ caritvā ||
children.translated_text: and those who have mastery — that is by having practiced <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) extensively.

body.translated_text: That they attain <s>cakravartin</s> (universal sovereign) status, that they become <s>Śakra</s> and lords of the thirty-three gods, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Īśa</s>,

body.text: jāty-andha-bhāvā vadhirā vi-saṃjñā | śva-śūkara-uṣṭrāḥ khara-vānarāś ca | hasty-aśva-go-vyāghra-pataṅ-ga-makṣāḥ bhavanti nityaṃ khalu kāma-lolāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Born blind, deaf, unconscious; dogs, pigs, camels, donkeys, and monkeys; elephants, horses, cattle, tigers, moths, and flies — such always become those who are greedy for <s>kāma</s> (sensual pleasure).

body.text: kṣiti-īśvarāś ca + eva bhavanty udagrāḥ su-śreṣṭhino vai gṛha-paty-amātyāḥ | sukha-saumanasyena ca yānti vṛddhiṃ ye brahma-caryaṃ vipulaṃ caranti ||
body.translated_text: They become exalted rulers of the earth, the most excellent householders and ministers; and they grow in happiness and joy — those who practice <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) extensively.

body.text: kabhalli-tāpān atha dhūma-gārān bandhāṃs tathā tāḍana-tarjjanāṃś ca | chedaṃ śiraḥ karṇa-kara-akṣi-nāsāḥ | pādasya ca + arcchanti hi kāma-dāsā | iti ||
body.translated_text: Swallowing of hot iron balls, smoke-houses, bondage, beatings, and threats; the cutting off of head, ears, hands, eyes, nose, and feet — these are suffered by the slaves of <s>kāma</s> (sensual desire). Thus.

body.text: udayana-vatsa-rāja-paripṛcchāyāṃ ca vivarṇitāḥ kāmāḥ ||
body.translated_text: And in the <s>Udayanavatsarājaparipṛcchā</s>, sensual desires are described:

body.text: dṛṣṭvā vraṇaṃ dhāvati makṣikā yathā | dṛṣṭvā + a-śuciṃ dhāvati gardabho yathā | śvānaś ca śūnā iva māṃsa-kāraṇāt | tathā + eva dhāvanty a-budhāḥ striye ratāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Just as a fly rushes toward a wound, just as a donkey rushes toward filth, and just as a dog toward a butcher's shop for the sake of meat — so too do fools rush, delighting in women.

body.text: a-vidyā-pidhitā bālās tamaḥ-skandhane āvṛtāḥ | strīṣu saktās tathā mūḍhā a-medhya iva vāyasāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Fools blinded by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), enveloped in the mass of darkness, attached to women, deluded — like crows on refuse.

body.text: mārasya go-caro hy eṣa prasthitā yena dur-gatiḥ | āsvāda-saṃjñino gṛddhā mīṭa-sthāne yathā krimiḥ ||
body.translated_text: This is indeed the domain of <s>Māra</s>, the path leading to an evil destiny; they are greedy, perceiving flavor, like worms in a place of excrement.

body.text: kīṭa-kumbho yathā citro yatra yatra + eva dṛśyate | pūrṇo mūtra-purīṣeṇa dṛtir vā vāta-pūritā ||
body.translated_text: Like a colorfully painted pot of insects, wherever it may be seen, filled with urine and excrement — or like a bellows inflated with wind.

body.text: siṅghāṇaka-kapha-alālāḥ

children.text: śleṣmaṇi klinna-mastakāḥ | daurgandhyaṃ sravate kāyād bālānāṃ tad yathā madhu ||
children.translated_text: with skulls moistened by phlegm; a foul stench flows from the body — yet to fools it is as if honey.

body.translated_text: Nasal mucus, phlegm, and saliva,

body.text: asthi-pūrṇaṃ mukha-dvāraṃ māṃsa-carma-ādibhiś citaṃ | gaṇḍa-bhūto hy ayaṃ kāyaḥ kutsito hy āma-gandhikaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The mouth-opening is filled with bones, covered with flesh, skin, and the like; this body is indeed like an abscess, repulsive and smelling of raw flesh.

body.text: nānā-prāṇibhiḥ saṃpūrṇo mukha-gaṇḍo yathā bhavet | evam eva hy ayaṃ kāyo viṣṭhā-ādy-a-śuci-bhājanam ||
body.translated_text: Just as a facial swelling might be filled with various creatures, so too this body is a receptacle of excrement and other impurities.

body.text: antya-antra-ākulaṃ hy udaraṃ sa-yakṛt-phupphuṣa-ākulam | vṛkkau vilohitaṃ pittaṃ masta-luṅga-asthi-majjakam ||
body.translated_text: The belly is entangled with intestines, filled with liver and lungs; the kidneys, bloody bile, brain, bones, and marrow.

body.text: aśītiṃ krimi-kula-sahasrāṇi yāni tiṣṭhanti antare | aha bālā na paśyanti moha-jālena āvṛtāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Eighty thousand families of worms dwell within; but fools, enveloped in a net of delusion, do not see them.

body.text: nava-vraṇa-mukhaiḥ prasravanty a-śuciṃ pūti-gandhikam | bālā nimittaṃ gṛhṇanti vacane darśane * api ca ||
body.translated_text: Through nine wound-openings flows impurity of putrid smell; yet fools grasp at signs — in speech and in appearance.

body.text: uktāḥ paścān na jānanti yo deśaḥ sarva-kutsitaḥ | uccāra-go-carā bālāḥ kheṭa-siṅghāṇa-bhojinaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Having been told, they still do not recognize that place which is entirely repulsive; fools whose domain is excrement, who consume spittle and nasal mucus.

body.text: jugupsanīye rajyante vraṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā + iva makṣikāḥ | kakṣāsv āgharate svedo gandho vāyati kutsitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: They become passionate toward what is disgusting, like flies upon seeing a wound; sweat collects in the armpits, and a repulsive odor wafts forth.

body.text: kurvanti duṣ-kṛtaṃ karma yena gacchanti dur-gatim | hīnān kāmān niṣevanto hīnān dharmān niṣevya ca ||
body.translated_text: They perform evil deeds by which they go to an evil destiny, pursuing inferior sensual pleasures and following inferior teachings.

body.text: gatvā avīciṃ duṣ-prajñāḥ duṣkhāṃ vindanti vedanāṃ | uccāra iva dur-gandhāḥ striyo buddhaiḥ prakīrtitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Having gone to <s>Avīci</s> (the lowest hell), the foolish experience painful sensations; women have been declared by the <s>Buddhas</s> to be foul-smelling like excrement.

body.text: tasmād * dhīnasya hīnābhiḥ strībhir bhavati saṅgatiḥ | uccāra-bhastrāṃ yo gṛhya-bāla-āvāsaṃ nigacchati ||
body.translated_text: Therefore the inferior one has association with inferior women; he who, grasping a bellows-bag of excrement, enters the abode of fools —

body.text: yādṛśaṃ kurute karma tādṛśaṃ labhate phalam ||
body.translated_text: whatever deed he performs, such fruit he obtains.

body.text: tathā + atra + eva + āha | tad evaṃ-rūpair duṣkha-paryeṣitair bhogaiḥ sva-jīvika-artham upasaṃhṛtair na prabhavanti śramaṇa-brāhmaṇebhyo dānaṃ dātuṃ kṛpaṇa-vanīpaka-yācakebhyo * a-vaśī-kṛtāḥ strībhiḥ strī-nirjitāḥ strī-nigṛhītāḥ strī-dāsāḥ | tena + eva strī-premṇā tasyā eva poṣaṇāya na śaknuvanti dānaṃ dātuṃ śīlaṃ ca samādātuṃ | sa tatra raktaḥ samānaḥ strī-paribhāṣitāni sahate tarjana-avalokana-nirbhartsanām api sahate | sa mātṛ-grāmeṇa tarjitaḥ puruṣaḥ saṃsīdati viṣīdati sukhaṃ ca + asyā avalokayati | kāma-hetoḥ kāma-nidānaṃ ca vaśa-gatā bhavati | ayaṃ mahā-rāja kāma-lolupasya puruṣasya + uccāra-sukha-paramasya + a-śucau ratasya + a-saṃprajanya-ācāriṇo doṣaḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: And here it says further: 'With enjoyments of such a nature, sought through suffering, gathered for one's own livelihood, they are unable to give gifts to <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (priests), to the wretched, traders, and beggars — overpowered by women, conquered by women, seized by women, slaves of women. Through that very love of women, for the sake of her maintenance alone, they cannot give gifts or undertake moral discipline. Being passionate there, he endures reproaches from women, endures threatening glances and scoldings. That man, threatened by the female sex, sinks down and despairs, yet he gazes upon her happiness. For the sake of <s>kāma</s> (desire), on account of <s>kāma</s>, he becomes subject to her will. This, O great king, is the fault of a man greedy for sensual pleasures, whose highest pleasure is that of excrement, who delights in impurity, who acts without <s>saṃprajanya</s> (clear comprehension).' And so forth.

body.text: śrutvā + īdṛśaṃ tu saṃvegaṃ na teṣāṃ bhavati nirvṛtiḥ | bhūyaḥ kurvanti saṃsargaṃ strībhiḥ sārddhaṃ pramoditāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Yet even having heard such an exhortation to renunciation, they find no peace; again they engage in intimacy with women, delighted.

body.text: duṣkha-kāmān niṣevante bhāṣante ca jugupsitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: They pursue desires that bring suffering, and speak contemptibly.

body.text: dharmaṃ śrutvā + artha-saṃmūḍhāḥ bhāṣante ca su-bhāṣitaṃ | strī-gataṃ ca + asya tac cittaṃ viḍālasya + iva mūṣike ||
body.translated_text: Having heard the <s>Dharma</s>, confused about its meaning, they speak well-spoken words; yet their mind is fixed on women, like a cat's mind on a mouse.

body.text: muhūrtaṃ bhavati saṃvegaḥ śrutvā + atha jina-bhāṣitaṃ | punaḥ kupyati rāgo * asya viṣa-hālāhalaṃ yathā ||
body.translated_text: For a moment there arises a sense of urgency upon hearing the words of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor); then passion flares up again in him, like the poison <s>hālāhala</s>.

body.text: sūkarasya + iva uttrāso muhūrtam anuvarttate | dṛṣṭvā vai atha uccāraṃ gṛddhatāṃ janayaty asau ||
body.translated_text: Like the fright of a pig, it lasts but a moment; then, upon seeing excrement, it generates greed.

body.text: evaṃ sukha-arthino bālāḥ prahāya jina-śāsanaṃ | hīnān kāmān niṣevante yena gacchanti dur-gatiṃ ||
body.translated_text: Thus, fools seeking pleasure, abandoning the teaching of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor), pursue inferior sensual desires, by which they go to an evil destiny.

body.text: raktāḥ pramattāḥ kāmeṣu kṛtvā karma su-pāpakam | śīlavattāṃ visaṃvādya paścād gacchanti dur-gatim ||
body.translated_text: Passionate and heedless in sensual pleasures, having performed extremely sinful deeds, having betrayed those endowed with moral virtue, they afterwards go to an evil destiny.

body.text: yasya + īdṛśaṃ dharma-nayaṃ viditvā | strīṣu prasādaḥ puruṣasya na + u bhavet | viśodhitaḥ svarga-patho * asya nityam | na dur-labhā tasya vara-agra-bodhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: One who, knowing such a course of <s>Dharma</s>, would not have faith in women — the path to heaven is ever purified for him; not difficult to attain for him is the supreme, foremost <s>bodhi</s> (awakening).

body.text: labdhvā kṣaṇaṃ hi sa prajño dharmaṃ śrutvā ca īdṛśam | sarvān kāmān vivarjya + iha pravrajyāṃ niṣkramed budha | iti ||
body.translated_text: For the wise one, having obtained the opportune moment and having heard such a <s>Dharma</s>, should abandon all sensual desires here and go forth into the homeless life. Thus.

body.text: praśānta-viniścaya-prātihārya-sūtre * apy a-paro * an-artha uktaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Praśāntaviniścayaprātihāryasūtra</s> also, another disadvantage is stated:

body.text: yaḥ kaś-cin mañjuśrīḥ kula-putro vā kula-duhitā vā jāmbū-dvīpakān sarva-satvāñ jīvitād vyaparopya sarvasvaṃ haret | yo vā + anyo mañjuśrīḥ kula-putro vā kula-duhitā bodhi-satvasya + eka-kuśala-cittasya + antarāyaṃ kuryād antaśas tiryag-yoni-gatasya + apy eka-ālopa-dāna-saha-gatasya kuśala-mūlasya + antarāyaṃ kuryād ayaṃ tato * a-saṃkhyeyataraṃ pāpaṃ prasavati | tat kasya hetoḥ | buddha-utpāda-saṃjanakānāṃ sa-kuśala-mūlānām antarāyaḥ sthito bhavati | yaḥ kaś-cin mañjuśrīḥ para-kuleṣu bodhi-satvasya + īrṣyā-mātsaryaṃ kuryāt tasya tasmin samaye tato nidānaṃ

children.text: trīṇi bhayāni pratikāṅkṣitavyāni | katamāni trīṇi | naraka-upapatti-bhayaṃ jāty-andha-bhayaṃ pratyanta-janma-upapatti-bhayaṃ ca + iti ||
children.translated_text: three dangers are to be expected. Which three? The danger of rebirth in hell, the danger of being born blind, and the danger of rebirth in a border region. Thus.

body.translated_text: If any son or daughter of good family, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, were to kill all beings of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> and steal all their possessions; and if another son or daughter of good family were to obstruct even a single wholesome thought of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> — even to obstruct the wholesome root associated with a single morsel of food given to a being born in the animal realm — this latter one generates immeasurably more sin. Why is that? Because it constitutes an obstruction to the wholesome roots that give rise to the arising of a <s>Buddha</s>. If anyone, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, should harbor jealousy and envy toward a <s>Bodhisattva</s> in the families of others, at that very moment, on that very account,

body.text: punar āha ||
body.translated_text: Further it says:

body.text: yas tasya kuryāt puruṣo * a-priyaṃ vā bhūtaṃ hy a-bhūtaṃ ca vaded a-varṇaṃ | paruṣaṃ vadet kruddha-manā + api yas taṃ kṣobhaṃ ca kuryāt punar asya yo * api ||
body.translated_text: Whoever would do something unpleasant to him, or speak ill of him whether true or false, or speak harshly to him with an angry mind, or whoever would cause him agitation —

body.text: ātma-bhāvena mahatā narakeṣu sa dur-matiḥ | utpadyate vipanna-ātmā duṣkhāṃ sa vetti vedanāṃ ||
body.translated_text: that evil-minded one, with a great body, is reborn in the hells, ruined in self, and experiences painful sensations.

body.text: yojanānāṃ śataṃ pañca jāyate * asya samucchrayaḥ | koṭī-parivṛtaḥ śaśvad bhakṣyate ca śunā bhṛśam ||
body.translated_text: His body arises to a height of five hundred <s>yojanas</s> (leagues), surrounded by ten million, and he is incessantly devoured by dogs.

body.text: pañca-mūrddha-sahasrāṇi bhavanty asya + apavādinaḥ | jihvānāṃ ca śatāḥ pañca bhavanty eka-eka-mūrddhani ||
body.translated_text: Five thousand heads has that slanderer, and five hundred tongues on each and every head.

body.text: eka-ekasyāṃ ca jihvāyāṃ śatāḥ pañca jvalan-mukhāḥ | lāṅgalānāṃ ca vahanty asya vācaṃ bhāṣitva pāpikām ||
body.translated_text: On each and every tongue, five hundred blazing ploughshares are dragged, for having spoken sinful speech.

body.text: pratāpane ca pacyante tīvra-duṣkha-anala-ākule | utpīḍāṃ bodhi-satvānāṃ ye kurvanti a-saṅgatāḥ ||
body.translated_text: And in <s>Pratāpana</s> (the Scorching Hell) they are cooked, overwhelmed by the fire of intense suffering — those who, without justification, cause harm to <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: tiryag-yoniḥ sa-narakā na teṣāṃ bhoti dur-labhā | kalpa-koṭi-sahasrāṇi śatāni niyutāni ca ||
body.translated_text: Animal births and hells are not difficult to obtain for them, for hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons).

body.text: tataḥ cyutā ghora-viṣā bhonti sarpāḥ su-dāruṇāḥ | kṣut-pipāsa-abhibhūtāś ca kurvate karma dāruṇam ||
body.translated_text: Having fallen from there, they become serpents of terrible venom, extremely fierce; overcome by hunger and thirst, they perform dreadful deeds.

body.text: labdhvā + api bhojana-pānaṃ tṛptiṃ na + eva + adhigacchati | tataś cyuto manuṣyeṣu sa ... yady upapadyate ||
body.translated_text: Even having obtained food and drink, they never attain satisfaction; having fallen from there, if one is reborn among humans...

body.text: jāty-andho bhoti dur-medhā duṣṭa-cetā a-saṃvṛtaḥ | āryānāra-adhikāṃ

children.translated_text: that person, having spoken ill words —

body.translated_text: One is born blind, dull-witted, evil-minded, and unrestrained; having spoken words more contemptuous than those of the noble ones,

body.text: manuṣyebhyaś cyutaś ca + api punar gacchati dur-gatim | kalpa-koṭi-sahasreṣu jāta-buddhaṃ na paśyati ||
body.translated_text: having fallen from the human realm, again goes to an evil destiny; for thousands of millions of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), one does not see a <s>Buddha</s> who has arisen.

body.text: punar atra + eva + āha | yāvanti mañjuśrīr bodhi-satvo bodhi-satvasya + antike pratigha-cittāny utpādayaty avamanyanā-cittāni vā | tāvataḥ kalpān sannāhaḥ sannaddhavyo vastavyaṃ mayā mahā-narakeṣv iti | na mañjuśrīr bodhi-satvo * anyena karmaṇā śakyo vinipātayitum anyatra bodhi-satva-apavādād eva | tad yathā mañjuśrīr vajra-maṇi-ratnaṃ na + anyena kāṣṭhena loṣṭhena vā śakyaṃ bhettum anyatra vajrād | evam eva mañjuśrīr bodhi-satvo * anyena karmaṇā na śakyo vinipātayitum anyatra bodhi-satva-apavādād eva + iti ||
body.translated_text: Here again it says: 'As many moments of hostile thoughts or contemptuous thoughts, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, as a <s>Bodhisattva</s> generates toward another <s>Bodhisattva</s> — for that many <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) must one put on armor, thinking: "I must dwell in the great hells." A <s>Bodhisattva</s>, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, cannot be brought to ruin by any other deed except by slandering a <s>Bodhisattva</s> alone. Just as, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>vajra</s> (diamond) gem-jewel cannot be broken by any wood or clod of earth, but only by another <s>vajra</s> — even so, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> cannot be brought to ruin by any other deed except by slandering a <s>Bodhisattva</s> alone.' Thus.

body.text: ārya-śraddhā-bala-ādhāna-avatāra-mudrā-sūtre * apy āha ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Āryaśraddhābalādhānāvatāramudrāsūtra</s> also, it says:

body.text: yaḥ kaś-cin mañjuśrīḥ kula-putro vā kula-duhitā vā daśasu dikṣu sarva-loka-dhātuṣu sarva-satva-andha-kāreṣu bandhane kruddhaḥ praveśayet | yaś ca + anyaḥ kula-putro vā kula-duhitā vā bodhi-satve kruddhaḥ parāṅ-mukhaṃ tiṣṭhet | na + enaṃ dur-ātmānaṃ paśyāmi + ity ayaṃ tato * a-saṃkhyeyataraṃ pāpaṃ pravasati ||
body.translated_text: If any son or daughter of good family, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, were to angrily cast all beings of all world-realms in the ten directions into the darkness of blindness and imprisonment; and if another son or daughter of good family were to angrily stand with face averted from a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, saying 'I do not see this wicked one' — this latter one generates immeasurably more sin.

body.text: atra + eva + uktaṃ | yaḥ kaś-cin mañjuśrīḥ sarva-jāmbū-dvīpakānāṃ satvānāṃ sarvasvaṃ hared yaś ca + anyo yādṛśaṃ tādṛśaṃ bodhi-satvaṃ garhed tato * a-saṃkhyeyataraṃ pāpaṃ prasavati ||
body.translated_text: Here also it is said: 'If anyone, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, were to steal all the possessions of all beings of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>; and if another were to revile a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of whatever kind — the latter generates immeasurably more sin.'

body.text: atra + eva + uktaṃ | yaḥ kaś-cin mañjuśrīḥ kula-putro vā kula-duhitā vā gaṅgā-nadī-vālikā-samān stūpān vinipātayed daheta vā | yaś ca + anyaḥ kula-putro vā kula-duhitā vā mahā-yāna-adhimuktasya bodhi-satvasya vyāpāda-khila-krodha-cittam utpādya krośayet paribhāṣayed ayaṃ tato * a-saṃkhyeyataraṃ pāpaṃ prasavati | tat kasmād * dhetoḥ | bodhi-satva-niryātā hi buddhā bhagavanto buddha-niryātāś ca stūpāḥ sarva-sukha-upadhānāni ca sarva-deva-nikāyāś ca | bodhi-satvam a-sat-kṛtya sarva-buddhā a-sat-kṛtā bhavanti | bodhi-satvaṃ sat-kṛtya sarva-buddhāḥ sat-kṛtā bhavanti | sarva-buddhān an-uttarayā pūjayā pūjayitu-kāmena bodhi-satvāḥ pūjayitavyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the same [sūtra] it is stated: 'Whoever, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s> — whether a son of good family or a daughter of good family — were to demolish or burn <s>stūpas</s> equal in number to the sands of the Ganges River; and whoever else — a son of good family or a daughter of good family — were to generate a thought of ill-will, hostility, and anger toward a <s>bodhisattva</s> devoted to the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, and were to abuse and revile him — this [latter person] produces immeasurably more sin than that [former one]. For what reason? Because the blessed <s>Buddhas</s> proceed from <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and <s>stūpas</s> proceed from <s>Buddhas</s>, and all sources of happiness, and all the hosts of gods [proceed from them]. By dishonoring a <s>bodhisattva</s>, all <s>Buddhas</s> are dishonored. By honoring a <s>bodhisattva</s>, all <s>Buddhas</s> are honored. Whoever wishes to worship all the <s>Buddhas</s> with the supreme worship should worship the <s>bodhisattvas</s>.'

body.text: etat pūjā-vipākaś ca praśānta-viniścaya-prātihārya-sūtre * abhihitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The ripening of this worship is also described in the <s>Praśāntaviniścayaprātihāryasūtra</s>:

body.text: yas tv eṣāṃ kurute rakṣāṃ dhārmikīṃ dharma-vādināṃ | hitvā su-dur-gatīḥ sarvāḥ śakro bhavati deva-rāṭ ||
body.translated_text: 'Whoever protects with the <s>Dharma</s> these speakers of the <s>Dharma</s>, having abandoned all miserable states of existence, becomes <s>Śakra</s>, king of the gods.'

body.text: brahmā + api yāmas tuṣito vaśa-varttī punaḥ punaḥ | manuṣyeṣu + upapannaś ca cakra-varttī sa jāyate ||
body.translated_text: 'He becomes <s>Brahmā</s>, [born in the heaven of] <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Vaśavartin</s> — again and again. And reborn among humans, he is born as a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch).'

body.text: śreṣṭhī gṛha-patiś ca + api bhavaty āḍhyo mahā-dhanaḥ | prajñā-smṛtibhyāṃ saṃyuktaḥ sukhito nir-upadrava | iti ||
body.translated_text: 'And he becomes a wealthy merchant, a householder of great riches, endowed with wisdom and mindfulness, happy and free from calamity.'

body.text: atha katamaṃ bodhi-satvam adhikṛtya + iyaṃ kāra-apakāra-cintā | pṛthag-janam eva ||
body.translated_text: Now, with reference to what kind of <s>bodhisattva</s> is this consideration of benefit and harm? With reference to an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) alone.

body.text: yathā + uktaṃ śraddhā-bala-ādhāna-avatāra-mudrā-sūtre | yaḥ kaś-cin mañjuśrīḥ kula-putro vā kula-duhitā vā sarva-loka-dhātu-rajo-upamānāṃ satvānāṃ divase divase divyaṃ śata-rasam āhāraṃ dadyād divyāni ca vastrāṇy evaṃ dadaṅ gaṅgā-nadī-vālikā-samān kalpa-samudrān dānaṃ dadyāt | yaś ca + anyaḥ kula-putro vā kula-duhitā vā ekasya + upāsakasya + an-anya-śāstur daśa-kuśala-karma-patha-samanvāgatasya + eka-divasam ekam āhāraṃ dadyād buddhasya + ayaṃ bhagavataḥ śikṣāyāṃ śikṣita iti samāropaṃ kṛtvā | ayaṃ tato * a-saṃkhyeyataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Śraddhābalādhāna-avatāra-mudrā-sūtra</s>: 'Whoever, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s> — a son of good family or a daughter of good family — were to give, day after day, divine food of a hundred flavors and divine garments to beings equal in number to the atoms in all world-realms — giving thus for ocean-like <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the sands of the Ganges River; and whoever else — a son of good family or a daughter of good family — were to give a single meal for one day to a single <s>upāsaka</s> (lay devotee) who has no other teacher and is endowed with the ten wholesome courses of action, having ascribed [to him the thought]: "This one has trained in the training of the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>" — this [latter person] produces immeasurably more merit than that [former one].'

body.text: yaḥ kaś-cin mañjuśrīḥ kula-putro vā kula-duhitā vā sarva-loka-dhātu-rajo-upamānāṃ daśa-kuśala-karma-patha-samanvāgatānāṃ upāsakānāṃ divase divase divyaṃ śata-rasam āhāraṃ dadyād divyāni ca vastrāṇy evaṃ dadaṅ gaṅgā-nadī-vālikā-samān kalpān dadyāt | yaś ca + anyaḥ kula-putro vā kula-duhitā vā ekasya bhikṣor eka-divasam āhāraṃ dadyād | ayaṃ tato * a-saṃkhyeyataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati + iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Whoever, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s> — a son of good family or a daughter of good family — were to give, day after day, divine food of a hundred flavors and divine garments to <s>upāsakas</s> endowed with the ten wholesome courses of action, equal in number to the atoms in all world-realms — giving thus for <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the sands of the Ganges River; and whoever else — a son of good family or a daughter of good family — were to give a single meal for one day to a single monk — this [latter person] produces immeasurably more merit than that [former one].'

body.text: niyata-a-niyata-avatāra-mudrā-sūtre * apy āha | sacen mañjuśrīr daśasu dikṣu sarva-loka-dhātuṣu sarva-satvā utpāṭita-akṣā bhaveyuḥ parikalpam upādāya | atha kaś-cid eva kula-putro vā kula-duhitā vā teṣāṃ sarva-satvānāṃ maitra-cittas tāny akṣīṇi janayet parikalpam upādāya | yo vā + anyo mañjuśrīḥ kula-putro vā kula-duhitā vā mahā-yāna-adhimuktaṃ bodhi-satvaṃ prasanna-cittaḥ paśyed | ayaṃ tato * a-saṃkhyeyataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Niyata-aniyata-avatāra-mudrā-sūtra</s> also it is said: 'If, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, all beings in all world-realms in the ten directions were to have their eyes plucked out, by supposition; and if a certain son of good family or daughter of good family, with a mind of loving-kindness toward all those beings, were to generate those eyes [for them], by supposition; or if another son of good family or daughter of good family, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, were to look with a joyful mind upon a <s>bodhisattva</s> devoted to the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — this [latter person] produces immeasurably more merit than that [former one].'

body.text: yaḥ kaś-cin mañjuśrīḥ kula-putro vā kula-duhitā vā daśasu dikṣu sarva-satvān bandhana-āgāra-praviviṣṭān bandhana-āgārān mocayitvā cakra-varti-sukhe sthāpayed brahmatva-sukhe vā | yo vā + anyo mañjuśrīḥ kula-putro vā kula-duhitā vā mahā-yāna-adhimuktasya prasanna-citto darśana-abhilāṣī bhaved varṇaṃ ca + asya + udāhared | ayaṃ tato * a-saṃkhyeyataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati + iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Whoever, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s> — a son of good family or a daughter of good family — were to free all beings in the ten directions who have entered prisons from their prisons and establish them in the happiness of a <s>Cakravartin</s> or in the happiness of <s>Brahmā</s>; or if another son of good family or daughter of good family, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, with a joyful mind, were to desire the sight of a <s>bodhisattva</s> devoted to the <s>Mahāyāna</s> and were to proclaim his virtues — this [latter person] produces immeasurably more merit than that [former one].'

body.text: tathā kṣitigarbha-sūtre * apy āha | yaḥ punar bhadanta bhagavan kṣatriya-kalyāṇo vā + amātya-kalyāṇo vā bhaṭṭa-kalyāṇo vā śramaṇa-kalyāṇo vā brāhmaṇa-kalyāṇo vā paraṃ rakṣaty ātmānaṃ rakṣati para-lokaṃ rakṣati | bhagavac-chāsane pātra-bhūtam a-pātra-bhūtaṃ vā yāvan muṇḍaṃ kāṣāya-khaṇḍa-prāvṛtaṃ parirakṣati śroṣyati pūjayiṣyati śrāvaka-kathāṃ evaṃ praty-eka-buddha-kathāṃ śroṣyati pūjayiṣyati | mahā-yāna-kathāṃ ca mahā-yāna-saṃprasthitān pudgalān śīlavato guṇa-āḍhyān yukta-mukta-pratibhānān taiḥ sārddhaṃ ramati krīḍati paripṛcchati paripraśnayati teṣāṃ śrotavyaṃ kartavyaṃ manyate || pe ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, in the <s>Kṣitigarbhasūtra</s> also it is said: 'Furthermore, O Venerable Blessed One, whoever is a worthy <s>kṣatriya</s>, or a worthy minister, or a worthy soldier, or a worthy <s>śramaṇa</s>, or a worthy <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — he who protects others protects himself, protects the next world. In the teaching of the Blessed One, he protects those who are worthy vessels and those who are unworthy vessels — even the shaven-headed ones clad in patches of ochre cloth — and he will listen to and honor the discourse of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, likewise the discourse of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and he will listen to and honor the <s>Mahāyāna</s> discourse. And with those persons who have set out on the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — those who are virtuous, rich in qualities, of ready and liberated eloquence — he delights, plays, inquires, and questions, and considers what they say as worthy of being heard and done.' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: kiyantaṃ bhagavan pāpaṃ kṣapayiṣyati ||
body.translated_text: 'How much sin will he destroy, O Blessed One?'

body.text: bhagavān āha ||
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said:

body.text: tad yathā + api nāma kula-putra kaś-cit puruṣa utpadyate | yaḥ sarvaṃ jambū-dvīpaṃ sapta-ratna-paripūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tiṣṭhatāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ dānaṃ dadyāt tathā + eva madhya-ahna-samaye tathā + eva sāya-ahna-samaye dānaṃ dadyād anena paryāyeṇa varṣa-śata-sahasram evaṃ-rūpaṃ dānaṃ dadyāt | tat kiṃ manyase kula-putra + api nu sa puruṣo bahu puṇyaṃ prasavet ||
body.translated_text: 'Suppose, O son of good family, a certain man were born who, having filled all of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> with the seven treasures, were to give them as a gift to the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, who are present; and likewise at midday, and likewise in the evening he were to give such gifts — by this method, for a hundred thousand years he were to give gifts of such a kind. What do you think, O son of good family — would that man produce much merit?'

body.text: āha ||
body.translated_text: He said:

body.text: bahu bhadanta bhagavan sa puruṣaḥ puṇya-skandhaṃ prasaved a-prameyam a-saṃkhyeyaṃ | na tasya puṇya-skandhasya kena-cic * chakyaṃ pramāṇam udgrahītuṃ anyatra tathā-gatena ||
body.translated_text: 'Much, O Venerable Blessed One — that man would produce an immeasurable, incalculable mass of merit. No one could grasp the measure of that mass of merit except the <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: bhagavān āha ||
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said:

body.text: yas tu kula-putra kṣatriya-kalyāṇo vā yāvad yathā pūrva + uktaṃ | pe | sa bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati | yāvad vipulataram a-pramāṇataram a-saṃkhyeyataraṃ puṇya-skandhaṃ prasavati | yo mama paścimāyāṃ pañca-śatyāṃ vartamānāyāṃ sad-dharma-netrī rakṣati sa rakṣaty ātmānaṃ | rakṣati parāṃś ca rakṣati para-lokaṃ rakṣati mama śāsanaṃ śrāvakān pātra-bhūtān a-pātra-bhūtān vā yāvan muṇḍān kāṣāya-vastra-prāvṛtān api rakṣati | na viheṭhayati | yāvat svakaṃ rāṣṭraṃ para-rāṣṭraṃ ca vardhayati | apāyān kṣapayati | sura-ālayaṃ ca prāpayati ciraṃ ca + āyuḥ pālayati | sva-kleśāṃś ca para-kleśāṃś ca jhāṣayati | saṃbodhi-mārgaṃ ṣaṭ-pāramitāś ca + upastambhayati | sarva-apāyāñ jahāti | na ciraṃ saṃsāre saṃsarati | nityaṃ kalyāṇa-mitrair buddhaiś ca bhagavadbhir bodhi-satvaiś ca mahā-satvaiś ca sārddhaṃ samavadhāna-gato bhavati | satataṃ kalyāṇa-mitra-a-virahito na cireṇa yathā-abhiprāyeṣu buddha-kṣetreṣv an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyate ||
body.translated_text: 'But, O son of good family, whoever is a worthy <s>kṣatriya</s> — and so on, as stated before — [abbreviated] — he produces far more merit, produces a mass of merit that is vaster, more immeasurable, more incalculable. He who, during my final five-hundred-year period, protects the guiding light of the true <s>Dharma</s> — he protects himself; he protects others; he protects the next world; he protects my teaching; he protects <s>Śrāvakas</s>, whether they are worthy vessels or unworthy vessels — even the shaven-headed ones clad in ochre robes — he protects them; he does not harass them. He increases his own kingdom and the kingdoms of others; he destroys the lower realms; he leads [beings] to the abode of the gods; he long preserves [their] lifespan; he extinguishes his own <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and those of others; he upholds the path to <s>saṃbodhi</s> (awakening) and the six <s>pāramitās</s>; he abandons all lower realms; he does not wander long in <s>saṃsāra</s>; he is constantly in the company of spiritual friends, blessed <s>Buddhas</s>, and <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s>; he is never separated from spiritual friends; and before long he will attain supreme, perfect <s>bodhi</s> in <s>Buddha</s>-fields according to his aspiration.'

body.text: atha tāvad eva sarva-deva-indrāḥ sa-parivārā | yāvat piśāca-indrāḥ sa-parivārā utthāya + āsanād yena bhagavān tena + añjaliṃ praṇamya + evam āhuḥ | ye te bhadanta bhagavan etarhy an-āgate * adhvani yāvat paścimāyāṃ pañca-śatyāṃ kṣatriya-kalyāṇā bhavanti yāvad gaha-pati-kalyāṇāḥ | pe | evaṃ sad-dharma-rakṣakā evaṃ tri-ratna-vaṃśa-jvālayitāraḥ | pe | vayam api sarve sa-parivārās taṃ kṣatriya-kalyāṇaṃ yāvad gaha-pati-kalyāṇaṃ daśabhir ākārai rakṣiṣyāmaḥ paripālayiṣyāmo vardhayiṣyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then at that very moment, all the lords of the gods together with their retinues — up to the lords of the <s>piśācas</s> (goblins) with their retinues — rising from their seats, joined their palms toward the Blessed One and spoke thus: 'O Venerable Blessed One, those who in the present time and in the future age — up to the final five-hundred-year period — are worthy <s>kṣatriyas</s>, up to worthy householders — [abbreviated] — who are such protectors of the true <s>Dharma</s>, such igniters of the lineage of the Three Jewels — [abbreviated] — we all together with our retinues shall protect, guard, and increase that worthy <s>kṣatriya</s>, up to that worthy householder, in ten ways.'

body.text: katamair daśabhiḥ | āyuś ca + asya vardhayiṣyāmaḥ āyur-antarāyaṃ ca dharmeṇa nivārayiṣyāmaḥ | ārogyaṃ ca parivāraṃ ca dhana-skandhaṃ ca upabhoga-paribhogaṃ ca + aiśvaryaṃ ca yaśaḥ kalyāṇa-mitrāṇi prajñā-sampadaṃ ca vardhāpayiṣyāmaḥ | ebhir daśabhir iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'By which ten? We shall increase his lifespan and lawfully ward off obstacles to his lifespan. We shall increase his health, his retinue, his store of wealth, his requisites and provisions, his sovereignty, his fame, his spiritual friends, and his attainment of wisdom. By these ten' — and so on in detail.

body.text: evam a-bhūmi-praviṣṭeṣv eva + ayaṃ vipāka-vistaro draṣṭavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus, even with respect to those who have not yet entered the [bodhisattva] stages, this extensive [description of] ripening should be seen.

body.text: avalokanā-sūtre * api | saṃbodhau cittam utpādya hita-arthaṃ sarva-prāṇināṃ | yaḥ stūpaṃ loka-nāthasya karoti + iha pradakṣiṇaṃ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Avalokanāsūtra</s> also: 'Having generated the thought of <s>bodhi</s> for the benefit of all living beings, whoever here circumambulates a <s>stūpa</s> of the Protector of the World —'

body.text: ity ādy anuśaṃsa-vistaram uktvā + āha | yas tv eṣāṃ buddha-putrāṇāṃ naraḥ kurvīta a-priyaṃ | devān manuṣyān varjitvā narakaṃ tasya go-caraṃ ||
body.translated_text: and so forth, after describing the benefits in detail, it says: 'But whoever would do harm to these sons of the <s>Buddha</s> — apart from gods and humans, hell is his domain.'

body.text: iti vistaraḥ pūrva-vat ||
body.translated_text: And so on in detail, as before.

body.text: na ca + atra viśeṣa-hetuḥ kaś-cid upadarśayituṃ śakyatae ity alaṃ vikalpena ||
body.translated_text: And here no special reason can be shown [to explain this]; therefore, enough with speculation.

body.text: karma-āvaraṇa-viśuddhi-sūtre * apy āvaraṇa-śabdena + an-artha uktaḥ | āvaraṇaṃ mañjuśrīr ucyate rāga āvaraṇaṃ dveṣa āvaraṇaṃ moha āvaraṇaṃ dānam āvaraṇaṃ śīla-kṣānti-vīrya-dhyāna-prajñā āvaraṇaṃ | pe | tat kasya hetoḥ bāla-pṛthag-janā mañjuśrīr dānaṃ dadānā matsariṇām antike * a-prasādaṃ kurvanti | te tena + a-prasādena pratigha-cittam utpādayanti | pratigha-khila-doṣeṇa mahā-narakeṣu + upapadyante | śīlaṃ rakṣanto duḥ-śīlān kutsayanti paribhāṣanti | te teṣām a-varṇaṃ ca bhāṣanti | te teṣāṃ doṣaṃ śrutvā bahu-janasya + a-prasādaṃ kurvanti | te tena + a-prasādena dur-gati-gāmino bhavanti | te kṣāntiṃ bhāvayantaḥ kṣānti-madena + ātmānam utkarṣayanti pramādyanti | vayaṃ kṣānti-vādinaḥ | ime punar anye vyāpanna-cittāḥ | teṣāṃ kṣānti-madana-mattānāṃ pramāda-mūlakāni duḥkhāny utpadyante | te vīryam ārabhamāṇā ātmānam utkarṣayanti parān paṃsayanti | kusīdā ime bhikṣavo viharanty an-abhiyuktāḥ śraddhā-deyaṃ paribhuñjānāḥ | na + ete * arhanti pānīya-sthālakam api | te tena vīrya-ārambheṇa + ātmānam utkarṣayanti paraṃ ca paṃsayanti | tān ahaṃ bālān iti vadāmi | te dhyānaṃ samāpadyamānās tatra dhyāna-samāpattau spṛhām utpādayanti | teṣām evaṃ bhavati | vayaṃ samādhi-vihāriṇa | ime * anye bhikṣavo vikṣipta-cittā viharanti | kutas te buddhā bhaviṣyanti + iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Karmāvaraṇaviśuddhisūtra</s> also, by the word 'obstruction' (<s>āvaraṇa</s>), harm is meant: '<s>Āvaraṇa</s> (obstruction), O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is said [to be]: attachment is an obstruction; hatred is an obstruction; delusion is an obstruction; giving is an obstruction; morality, patience, vigor, meditation, and wisdom are obstructions.' [And so on in abbreviated form.] 'For what reason? O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, foolish ordinary persons, while giving gifts, generate displeasure toward the miserly. Those [miserly ones], through that displeasure, generate thoughts of hostility. Through the fault of hostility and malice, they are reborn in the great hells. Those who guard morality censure and revile the immoral; and they speak ill of them. Those [others], having heard their faults, generate displeasure in many people. Through that displeasure they become destined for miserable rebirths. Those who cultivate patience exalt themselves through the pride of patience and become heedless: "We are advocates of patience, but these others have corrupt minds." For those intoxicated with the pride of patience, sufferings rooted in heedlessness arise. Those who undertake vigor exalt themselves and revile others: "These monks dwell in laziness, without exertion, consuming what is given in faith. They do not deserve even a water-bowl." Through that undertaking of vigor they exalt themselves and revile others — those I call fools. Those who attain <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) generate longing for that meditative attainment. This occurs to them: "We are dwellers in <s>samādhi</s>. These other monks dwell with distracted minds. How will they ever become <s>Buddhas</s>?"' And so on in detail.

body.text: sarva-dharma-a-pravṛtti-nirdeśe * apy āha | bodhi-satva āpattyā codayati | dūrī-bhavati bodhiḥ | karma-āvaraṇaṃ ca parigṛhṇāti | īryayā codayati | dūrī-bhavati bodhiḥ | īryā-pathena codayati dūrī-bhavati bodhiḥ | saced bodhi-satvasya + antike hīna-saṃjñām utpādayati ātmani ca + udāra-saṃjñāṃ kṣiṇoty ātmānaṃ karma-āvaraṇaṃ ca gṛhṇāti | iha bodhi-satvena bodhi-satvam avavadatā + anuśāsatā vā śāstṛ-saṃjñām upasthāpya + avavaditavyo * anuśāsitavyaḥ | bodhi-satvena bodhi-satvasya + antike na paribhava-cittam utpādayitavyaṃ | saced asya + a-parityaktā bodhiḥ | na deva-putra bodhi-satvaḥ kva-cid eva kuśala-mūlāni samucchinatti | yathā + a-dvitīya-bodhi-satvam āgamya + iti | an-utpādita-bodhi-citte * api tāvad bodhir bhavye satve * avamanyanā pratiṣiddhā | kiṃ punar udita-bodhi-citte ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Sarvadharmāpravṛttinirdeśa</s> (Instruction on the Non-arising of All Dharmas) it also says: 'A <s>bodhisattva</s> who censures [another] for a transgression becomes far from <s>bodhi</s> and takes on a karmic obstruction. One who censures [another's] deportment becomes far from <s>bodhi</s>. One who censures [another's] mode of walking becomes far from <s>bodhi</s>. If one generates the perception of inferiority toward a <s>bodhisattva</s> and the perception of superiority toward oneself, one diminishes oneself and takes on a karmic obstruction. Here, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who admonishes or instructs another <s>bodhisattva</s> should admonish and instruct having generated the perception of [the other as] the Teacher. A <s>bodhisattva</s> should not generate a thought of contempt toward another <s>bodhisattva</s>. If his <s>bodhi</s> has not been abandoned — [then know that,] O son of the gods, a <s>bodhisattva</s> never in any case has his wholesome roots cut off — as taught in the <s>Advitīyabodhisattva</s> [Sūtra].' If contempt is prohibited even toward a being capable [of awakening] in whom <s>bodhicitta</s> has not yet arisen, how much more so toward one in whom <s>bodhicitta</s> has arisen!

body.text: yathā + uktaṃ śūraṅgama-samādhi-sūtre | tatra dṛḍhamate katamad an-utpādita-bodhi-citta-vyākaraṇaṃ ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Śūraṅgama-samādhi Sūtra</s>: 'Now, O <s>Dṛḍhamati</s>, what is the prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) of one in whom <s>bodhicitta</s> has not yet arisen?'

body.text: iha dṛḍhamate sa pudgalaḥ pāñcagatike saṃsāre upapanno bhavati | yadi vā nirayeṣu yadi vā tiryag-yonau yadi vā yama-loke yadi vā deveṣu yadi vā manuṣyeṣu | sa ca pudgalas tīkṣṇa-indriyo bhavati | udāra-adhimuktikaḥ | tam enaṃ tathā-gataḥ prajānāti | ayaṃ puruṣa-pudgalo yāvad iyadbhiḥ kalpa-koṭī-niyuta-śata-sahasrair an-uttarāyāṃ samyak-saṃbodhau cittam utpādayiṣyati || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'Here, O <s>Dṛḍhamati</s>, that person is born in the five-fold course of <s>saṃsāra</s> — whether in the hells, or in the animal realm, or in the world of <s>Yama</s>, or among the gods, or among humans. And that person has sharp faculties and noble aspirations. The <s>Tathāgata</s> knows him: "This person will generate the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) after so many hundreds of thousands of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>."' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: iyadbhiś ca a-saṃkhyeya-kalpa-śata-sahasrair bodhim abhisaṃbhotsyate || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'And after so many hundreds of thousands of incalculable <s>kalpas</s>, he will fully awaken to <s>bodhi</s>.' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: idaṃ dṛḍhamate ucyate | bodhi-satvasya + an-utpādita-bodhi-citta-vyākaraṇaṃ | atha khalv āyuṣmān mahā-kāśyapo bhagavantam etad avocat | adya + agreṇa + asmābhir bhagavan sarva-satvānām antike śāstṛ-saṃjñā + utpādayitavyā | tat kasya hetoḥ | na hy asmākam etaj jñānaṃ pravarttate | katamasya bodhi-satvasya bodhi-paripācakāni + indriyāṇi saṃvidyante | katamasya na saṃvidyante | tato vayaṃ bhagavann a-jānānās tathā-rūpeṣu hīna-saṃjñām utpādayema | tena vayaṃ kṣaṇyema ||
body.translated_text: 'This, O <s>Dṛḍhamati</s>, is called the prediction of a <s>bodhisattva</s> in whom <s>bodhicitta</s> has not yet arisen.' Then the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'From today onward, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, we should generate the perception of [all beings as] the Teacher toward all beings. Why? For this knowledge does not operate in us — [to know] which <s>bodhisattva</s> possesses the faculties that ripen toward <s>bodhi</s> and which does not. Therefore, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, we, not knowing, might generate the perception of inferiority toward such persons, and by that we would be ruined.'

body.text: bhagavān āha | sādhu sādhu kāśyapa su-bhāṣitā te iyaṃ vāk | idaṃ ca mayā kāśyapa + artha-vaśaṃ sampaśyamānena yuṣmākam evaṃ dharmo deśito | mā bhikṣavaḥ pudgalena pudgalaṃ pravicetavyaṃ | yac * chīghraṃ kṣaṇyati hi bhikṣavaḥ pudgalaḥ pudgalaṃ pravicinvan | ahaṃ vā pudgalaṃ pramiṇuyāṃ yo vā syān mādṛśaḥ | etena kāśyapa nirdeśena bodhi-satvena vā śrāvakeṇa vā sarva-satvānām antike śāstṛ-saṃjñā + utpādayitavyā | mā + atra kaś-cid bodhi-satva-yānikaḥ pudgalo bhavet tena tatra + ātmā rakṣitavya iti | yasya tu niyatam eva bodhi-prāpti-cihnam asti tatra sutarām avamanyanā rakṣitavyā ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Well done, well done, <s>Kāśyapa</s>! Well-spoken is this word of yours. And it is with this purpose in view, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, that I have taught you this <s>Dharma</s>: "O monks, a person should not scrutinize another person." For a person who scrutinizes another person is quickly ruined, O monks. Only I could evaluate a person, or one who is like me. By this teaching, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, whether a <s>bodhisattva</s> or a <s>śrāvaka</s>, the perception of [all beings as] the Teacher should be generated toward all beings — lest there might be some person of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-vehicle there, by [contempt for] whom one would have to guard oneself.' And toward one who definitely bears the mark of attaining <s>bodhi</s>, contempt is all the more to be guarded against.

body.text: yathā + uktam ārya-sad-dharma-puṇḍarīka-sūtre | iṣṭā-mayān mṛttika-saṃcitān vā prītāś ca kurvanti jinasya stūpān | uddiśya vā pāṃśu-kara-āśayo * api aṭavīṣu dur-geṣu ca kārayanti ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Ārya-Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra</s>: 'Those who, delighted, make <s>stūpas</s> of the <s>Jina</s> from clay mounds of pleasant materials, or even with the mere intention of [making] a handful of dust, in wildernesses and difficult terrain —'

body.text: siktā-mayā vā puna kūṭa kṛtvā ye ke-cid uddiśya jināna stūpān | kumārakāḥ krīḍiṣu tatra tatra | te sarvi bodhāya abhūṣi lābhinaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Or those who, making peaks of wet sand, whoever they may be, dedicate <s>stūpas</s> to the <s>Jinas</s> — children here and there in their play — they all have become gainers of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening).'

body.text: yāvat ||
body.translated_text: And so on —

body.text: ye citra-bhittīṣu karonti vigrahaṃ | paripūrṇa-gātrāṃś * chata-puṇya-lakṣaṇān ||
body.translated_text: 'Those who make figures on painted walls, with complete limbs, bearing the marks of a hundred merits —'

body.text: likhet svayaṃ ca + api likhāpayed vā | te sarvi bodhāya abhūṣi lābhinaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Whether one paints them oneself or has them painted — they all have become gainers of <s>bodhi</s>.'

body.text: ye ca + api ke-cit tarhi śikṣamāṇāḥ | krīḍā-ratiṃ ca + api vinodayantaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'And those who are trainees [of the path], dispelling attachment to play and amusement —'

body.text: nakhena kāṣṭhena kṛtāsi vigrahān | bhittīṣu puruṣā + atha kumārakā vā ||
body.translated_text: 'Persons or children who with a fingernail or a stick have made figures on walls —'

body.text: sarve ca te bodhi abhūṣi lābhinaḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'They all have become gainers of <s>bodhi</s>.' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: vādāpitā jhallariyo * api ye hī | jala-maṇḍakā vā + apy atha maṇḍakā vā | su-gatānam uddiśyatha pūjanā-arthaṃ gītaṃ ca gītaṃ madhuraṃ mano-jñaṃ | sarve ca te buddha abhūṣi loke ||
body.translated_text: 'And those who have caused drums or cymbals to be played, or water-drums or [other] drums — in honor of the <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones) for the purpose of worship; and who have sung sweet and delightful songs — they all have become <s>Buddhas</s> in the world.'

body.text: kṛtvā ca yāṃ bahu-vidha-dhātu-pūjāṃ | kim alpa-kampī su-gatāna dhātuṣu | ekaṃ pi vādāyiya vādya-bhāṇḍam | puṣpeṇa ca + ekena hi pūjayitvā | anupūrva drakṣyanti hi buddha-koṭyaḥ | yaiś ca + añjalis tatra kṛtā + api stūpe | paripūrṇa ekā-tala-śaktikā vā | onāmitaṃ śīrṣa bhaven muhūrttaṃ | onāmitaṃ kāya tathā + eka-vāraṃ | namo * astu buddhāya kṛta-eka-vāraṃ | ye hī tadā dhātu-dhāreṣu teṣu | vikṣipta-cittair api yathā + eka-vāraṃ | te sarvi prāptā imam agra-bodhim | su-gatāna teṣāṃ tada tasmi kāle | parinirvṛtānām atha tiṣṭhatāṃ vā | ye dharma-nāma + api śṛṇūṣu satvās | te sarvi bodhāya abhūṣi lābhina | iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Having performed worship of relics in many forms — even a slight trembling [of devotion] toward the relics of the <s>Sugatas</s>; having played even a single musical instrument; having worshipped with even a single flower — they shall gradually behold <s>koṭis</s> (millions) of <s>Buddhas</s>. And those who have even joined their palms at a <s>stūpa</s> — either with one hand fully [extended] or the other; who have bowed their head for just a moment, or bent their body even once; who have said "Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>" even once — [those who have done this] at those relic-shrines, even with distracted minds, even once — they all have attained this supreme awakening. Of those <s>Sugatas</s>, at that time, whether they have passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> or are still abiding — beings who hear even just the name of the <s>Dharma</s> — they all have become gainers of <s>bodhi</s>.'

body.text: mahā-karuṇā-sūtre * apy uktaṃ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Mahākaruṇā Sūtra</s> it is also said:

body.text: tad yathā vāḍiśikena mahaty udaka-sarasi matsya-ākarṣaṇa-arthaṃ sa-āmiṣaṃ vaḍiśaṃ prakṣiptaṃ bhavet samanantara-prakṣiptaṃ ca matsyena nigīrṇaṃ bhavet | kiṃ ca + api sa matsya udaka-sarasi bhramaty atha ca punar vaddha eva sa vaktavyo dṛḍhena sūtreṇa sthala-gata-daṇḍa-su-nibaddhena | yat sa vāḍiśika āgatya tena sūtra-lāghavena jānāti | gṛhīto matsya iti | tam enaṃ sūtrād gṛhītvā sthala-gataṃ karoti yathā-kāma-karaṇāya paribhogāya | evam eva ye satvā buddheṣu bhagavatsu cittaṃ prasādya kuśala-mūlam avaropayanti | antaśa eka-citta-prasādam api | kiṃ ca + api te satvā duṣ-kṛtena karma-āvaraṇena + a-kṣaṇeṣu + upapannā bhavanty atha ca buddhā bhagavantas tān satvān bauddhena jñānena saṃgraha-vastu-sūtreṇa gṛhītvā saṃsāra-udaka-sarasa uddhṛtya nirvāṇa-sthale sthāpayanti + iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as a fisherman might cast a baited hook into a great lake for the purpose of catching fish, and no sooner is it cast than it is swallowed by a fish — although that fish still roams in the lake, it should be called caught, for it is bound by a strong line fastened to a pole on the shore; and the fisherman, coming and knowing by the lightness of the line that "the fish is caught," takes it from the line and brings it to shore, to do with as he pleases — just so, those beings who, having generated faith in the <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s>, plant wholesome roots — even with a single moment of faith — although those beings, through evil deeds and karmic obstructions, may be born in unfavorable conditions, yet the <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s>, having seized those beings with the <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge and the line of the means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>), draw them from the lake of <s>saṃsāra</s> and establish them on the shore of <s>nirvāṇa</s>.'

body.text: tasmād eṣu śāstṛ-saṃjñā kāryā | vandamānāś ca manasā vanditavyāḥ | bhavati hi navako * api bodhi-citta-balād vandyo | yathā meghena dramiḍena mahā-bodhi-satvena + api satā navaka ārya-sudhanaḥ sarva-śarīreṇa praṇipatya vanditaḥ | niyata-arthaṃ ca + idaṃ | yathā + adhyāśaya-saṃcodana-ādiṣu sarva-bodhi-satva-yānika-pudgala-namas-kāro * anujñātavyaḥ | sarva-śabdena + ātmano * api grahaṇāt | katham ekatra vandya vandakatvaṃ na virudhyate | paras-paraṃ vandyatvena + eva + ālambanāt | ata eva + an-āsvādanād a-puṇya-bhāvaḥ | kiṃ ca buddhānām apy evam iṣyate | mā bhūd an-avasthā | ekasya ca + a-nyūnatā + iti ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, toward these [beings] the perception of [them as] the Teacher should be generated. And when paying homage, one should bow mentally. For even a beginner, by the power of <s>bodhicitta</s>, is worthy of homage. Just as the noble <s>Sudhana</s>, though a beginner, was bowed to by the great <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Megha</s> (called <s>Dramiḍa</s>) with full prostration of his entire body. And this has a definitive meaning. As taught in the <s>Adhyāśayasaṃcodana</s> and other [sūtras], homage to all persons of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-vehicle is to be sanctioned — since the word 'all' includes even oneself. How is it that being worthy of homage and offering homage are not contradictory in one and the same [person]? Because each relies on the other's being worthy of homage. And therefore, from not savoring [the significance], there is the state of demerit. Moreover, this is accepted even for <s>Buddhas</s>: lest there be an infinite regress, and because there is no diminution of any one [Buddha].

body.text: ārya-sarva-dharma-vaipulya-saṃgraha-sūtre * apy an-artha uktaḥ | sūkṣmaṃ hi mañjuśrīḥ sad-dharma-pratikṣepa-karma-āvāraṇaṃ | yo hi kaś-cin mañjuśrīs tathā-gata-bhāṣita-dharme kasmiṃś-cic * chobhana-saṃjñāṃ karoti | kva-cid a-śobhana-saṃjñāṃ sa sad-dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | tena sad-dharmaṃ pratikṣipatā tathā-gato * abhyākhyāto bhavati | dharmaḥ pratikṣipto bhavati | saṃgho * apavādito bhavati | ya evaṃ vadati + idaṃ yuktam idam a-yuktam iti sa sad-dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | na mayā pṛthak kaś-cid dharmaḥ śrāvaka-yāna-saṃprayuktaḥ praty-eka-buddha-yāna-saṃprayukto mahā-yāna-saṃprayukto deśitaḥ | tat te moha-puruṣā imaṃ mama dharmaṃ nānā-kariṣyanti | idaṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ deśitam idaṃ praty-eka-buddhānām idaṃ bodhi-satvānām iti | sa nānātva-saṃjñayā sad-dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | iyaṃ bodhi-satvasya śikṣā | iyaṃ bodhi-satvasya + a-śikṣā + iti sad-dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | dharma-bhāṇakasya + asti pratibhānaṃ na + asti pratibhānam iti sad-dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | dharmaṃ dharmatayā kathayati sad-dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | apagate buddha-utpāde na + asti dhāraṇī-pratilambha iti dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | na + asti dharma-bhāṇakasya dhāraṇī-pratilambha iti dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | dharma-bhāṇakasya caryāṃ dūṣayati dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | dharma-bhāṇako na pratipatti-saṃpanna iti dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | pramādena + enaṃ codayati sad-dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | īryā-pathena codayati sad-dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | akṣara-caryayā śīla-vipattyā codayati dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | pratibhānena saṃpādayati + iti dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | āloko * asya dharmāṇāṃ na su-vidita iti dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | mantreṇa mantram a-budhyamānaḥ prativadati + iti dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | akṣara-saṃjñyā tathā-gata-śāsanaṃ na + avagāhata iti dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | sūtreṇa sūtraṃ virodhayati + iti dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | gāthayā gāthāṃ virodhayati + iti dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | akṣara-saṃjñayā kañ-cid adhimuktaṃ karoti kañ-cin na karoti + iti dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | dharma-bhaṇakasya + arthāny a-kathām abhināmayati + iti dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | vi-cakṣuḥ karma + asya karoti dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | saṃlāpayan vadati + iti dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | iha + asya + asti caryā iha + asya na + asti caryā + iti dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | idaṃ su-uktam idam a-su-uktam iti dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | anena na + asti caryā + iti dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | anena buddha-vacana-samaya ukto na + anena buddha-vacana-samaya ukta iti dharmaṃ pratikṣipati iti hi mañjuśrīr yāvat kiñ-cid vilopayati tāvad dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | dharma-bhāṇakasya + idaṃ rūpam iti cintayati vadati bhikṣur vā bhikṣuṇī vā upāsako vā upāsikā vā | sarvaḥ sa sad-dharmaṃ pratikṣipati + ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Sarvadharmavaipulyasaṃgraha Sūtra</s> too, the harm [of rejecting the Dharma] is described: 'Subtle indeed, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is the karmic obstruction of rejecting the true <s>Dharma</s>. If anyone, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, toward any <s>Dharma</s> spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, forms the perception of "good" toward some and the perception of "not good" toward others, he rejects the true <s>Dharma</s>. By rejecting the true <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is defamed, the <s>Dharma</s> is rejected, and the <s>Saṅgha</s> is disparaged. Whoever says "This is appropriate, this is not appropriate" rejects the true <s>Dharma</s>. I have not taught any <s>dharma</s> separately as connected with the <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle, the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle, or the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. But those deluded persons will make this <s>Dharma</s> of mine manifold: "This was taught for <s>śrāvakas</s>, this for <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, this for <s>bodhisattvas</s>." He who, through the perception of diversity, rejects the true <s>Dharma</s> — [likewise:] "This is the training of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, this is not the training of a <s>bodhisattva</s>" — rejects the true <s>Dharma</s>. "The <s>Dharma</s>-preacher has eloquence" or "has no eloquence" — rejects the true <s>Dharma</s>. He who teaches <s>Dharma</s> according to its true nature — [saying he] rejects the true <s>Dharma</s>. "When the <s>Buddha</s> has departed, there is no attainment of <s>dhāraṇī</s>" — rejects the <s>Dharma</s>. "The <s>Dharma</s>-preacher has no attainment of <s>dhāraṇī</s>" — rejects the <s>Dharma</s>. He who disparages the conduct of a <s>Dharma</s>-preacher rejects the <s>Dharma</s>. "The <s>Dharma</s>-preacher is not endowed with practice" — rejects the <s>Dharma</s>. He who censures him through negligence rejects the true <s>Dharma</s>. He who censures through deportment rejects the true <s>Dharma</s>. He who censures [the preacher] for literal conduct or for lapse in morality rejects the <s>Dharma</s>. He who produces [what is good] through eloquence — rejects the <s>Dharma</s>. "His understanding of the <s>dharmas</s> is not well-known" — rejects the <s>Dharma</s>. He who, not understanding a <s>mantra</s>, replies with a <s>mantra</s> — rejects the <s>Dharma</s>. "Through the perception of the letter he does not penetrate the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching" — rejects the <s>Dharma</s>. He who makes one <s>sūtra</s> contradict another rejects the <s>Dharma</s>. He who makes one verse contradict another rejects the <s>Dharma</s>. He who, through the perception of the letter, causes some to believe and others not — rejects the <s>Dharma</s>. He who bends the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher's meanings toward idle talk — rejects the <s>Dharma</s>. He who makes his action blind — rejects the <s>Dharma</s>. He who says [something false] while conversing — rejects the <s>Dharma</s>. "Here his conduct exists, here his conduct does not exist" — rejects the <s>Dharma</s>. "This is well-said, this is not well-said" — rejects the <s>Dharma</s>. "He has no practice" — rejects the <s>Dharma</s>. "By him the <s>Buddha</s>-word teaching has been spoken; by that one it has not" — rejects the <s>Dharma</s>. Indeed, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, as much as one impairs, that much one rejects the <s>Dharma</s>. He who thinks "the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher has this appearance" — any monk or nun, or male or female lay follower who says so — all of them reject the true <s>Dharma</s>,' and so forth.

body.text: atra + eva ca + uktaṃ | yasya kasya-cit kula-putra tathā-gatasya parinirvṛtasya dharmaḥ pratibhāti yathā + adhimuktānāṃ satvānāṃ deśayituṃ | tasyāṃ ca parṣadi yady eka-satvasya + api eka-roma-harṣo bhaved eka-aśru-pāto vā sarvaḥ sa tathā-gata-anubhāvena | tatra moha-puruṣā a-bodhi-satvā bodhi-satva-pratijñā bodhi-satva-dūṣakā dharma-stainya-kuhakā evaṃ vakṣyanti dharma-upadeśakebhyaḥ | kim ete | na budhyantae iti || pe ||
body.translated_text: And right here it is said: 'Whoever, O son of good family, [among the <s>Dharma</s>-teachers of] any <s>Tathāgata</s> who has attained final <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the <s>Dharma</s> becomes manifest [in such a way] as to teach it to beings with faith — and if in that assembly even a single being experiences even a single thrill of hair-raising or a single tear-drop, all of that is through the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therein, deluded persons — who are not <s>bodhisattvas</s> but profess to be <s>bodhisattvas</s>, who corrupt <s>bodhisattvas</s>, who are <s>Dharma</s>-thieves and hypocrites — will speak thus to the <s>Dharma</s>-instructors: "What are they? They do not understand!"' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: ye bodhi-satveṣv avamanyanāṃ kurvanti | na + ahaṃ teṣāṃ paryanta-kṛtaṃ nirayaṃ saṃvadāmi | tat kasya hetoḥ | yo bodhi-satvo dharma-bhāṇakam apavādati buddhaṃ sa vigarhati dharmaṃ sa pratikṣipati saṃghaṃ sa jugupsati | buddhe so * a-gauravo yo dharma-bhāṇake * a-gauravaḥ | buddhaṃ sa na draṣṭu-kāmo yo dharma-bhāṇakam a-draṣṭu-kāmaḥ | buddhasya so * a-varṇaṃ bhāṣate yo dharma-bhāṇakasya + a-varṇaṃ bhāṣate | buddhas tena parityakto bhavati yaḥ prathama-citta-utpādike * api bodhi-satve pratigha-cittaṃ karoti + iti || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'Those who treat <s>bodhisattvas</s> with contempt — I do not describe a definite end to their hell [destiny]. For what reason? He who reviles a <s>Dharma</s>-preacher who is a <s>bodhisattva</s> — he reviles the <s>Buddha</s>; he rejects the <s>Dharma</s>; he despises the <s>Saṃgha</s>. He who is disrespectful to the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher is disrespectful to the <s>Buddha</s>. He who does not wish to see the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher does not wish to see the <s>Buddha</s>. He who speaks ill of the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher speaks ill of the <s>Buddha</s>. The <s>Buddha</s> is abandoned by him who generates a mind of aversion even toward a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has [only] first generated the [awakening-]mind.' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: yo * apy ayaṃ maitreya ṣaṭ-pāramitā-samudāgamo bodhi-satvānāṃ saṃbodhāya taṃ te moha-puruṣā evaṃ vakṣyanti | prajñā-pāramitāyām eva bodhi-satvena śikṣitavyaṃ | kiṃ śeṣābhiḥ pāramitābhiḥ | te * anyāṃ pāramitāṃ dūṣayitavyāṃ manyante | tat kiṃ manyase * ajita duṣ-prajñaḥ sa kāśi-rājā + abhūd yena kapota-arthaṃ śyenāya sva-māṃsāni dattāni | maitreya āha | na + u hi + idaṃ bhagavan | bhagavān āha | yāni mayā maitreya bodhi-satva-caryāṃ caratā ṣaṭ-pāramitā-pratisaṃyuktāni kuśala-mūlāny upacitāni apakṛtaṃ nu taiḥ kuśala-mūlaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Whatever, <s>Maitreya</s>, is this accomplishment of the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) of <s>bodhisattvas</s> for awakening — those deluded persons will say: "The <s>bodhisattva</s> should train only in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom). What [need] of the remaining <s>pāramitās</s>?" They think the other <s>pāramitās</s> should be deprecated. What do you think, <s>Ajita</s> — was that King of <s>Kāśi</s> of poor wisdom, who gave his own flesh to the hawk for the sake of the pigeon?' <s>Maitreya</s> said: 'Certainly not, Blessed One!' The Blessed One said: 'The wholesome roots connected with the six <s>pāramitās</s> that were accumulated by me, <s>Maitreya</s>, while practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct — were those wholesome roots harmful?'

body.text: maitreya āha | na + u hi + idaṃ bhagavan ||
body.translated_text: <s>Maitreya</s> said: 'Certainly not, Blessed One!'

body.text: bhagavān āha | tvaṃ tāvad ajita ṣaṣṭiṃ kalpān dāna-pāramitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭiṃ kalpān śīla-pāramitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭiṃ kalpān kṣānti-pāramitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭiṃ kalpān vīrya-pāramitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭiṃ kalpān dhyāna-pāramitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭiṃ kalpān prajñā-pāramitāyāṃ samudāgataḥ | tat te moha-puruṣā evaṃ vakṣyanti | eka-nayena + eva bodhir yad uta śūnyatā-nayena + iti | te caryāsu pariśuddhā bhaviṣyanti + ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'You yourself, <s>Ajita</s>, spent sixty <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) accomplishing the <s>Dāna-pāramitā</s> (Perfection of Giving), sixty <s>kalpas</s> in the <s>Śīla-pāramitā</s> (Perfection of Morality), sixty <s>kalpas</s> in the <s>Kṣānti-pāramitā</s> (Perfection of Patience), sixty <s>kalpas</s> in the <s>Vīrya-pāramitā</s> (Perfection of Vigor), sixty <s>kalpas</s> in the <s>Dhyāna-pāramitā</s> (Perfection of Meditation), and sixty <s>kalpas</s> in the <s>Prajñā-pāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom). Those deluded persons will say: "Awakening is by a single method alone, namely, the method of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>)." But will they be purified in their practices?' And so on.

body.text: iti śikṣā-samuccaye caturthaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the fourth chapter of the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>.

body.text: śīla-pāramitāyām an-artha-varjanaṃ pañcamaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The avoidance of calamities regarding the <s>Śīla-pāramitā</s> (Perfection of Morality) — the fifth chapter.

body.text: uktaḥ saṃkṣepato * an-arthaḥ | tasya vivarjanaṃ yathā + adhyaśaya-saṃcodana-sūtre | evaṃ-vidha-an-artha-śravaṇa-bhaya-bhīrukaiḥ ādi-karmika-bodhi-satvaiḥ samādānāni yathā gṛhītāni tathā kāryaṃ | evaṃ hi tair uktaṃ | ete vayaṃ bhagavann adya + agreṇa tathā-gatasya purataḥ | evaṃ samādānaṃ kurmaḥ | saced vayaṃ bhagavann adya + agreṇa bodhi-satva-yānikaṃ pudgalaṃ gṛhiṇaṃ vā pravrajitaṃ vā + āpattyā codayiṣyāmo bhūtena vā + a-bhūtena vā visaṃvādito * asmābhis tathā-gato * arhan samyak-saṃbuddho bhavet | saced vayaṃ bhagavann adya + agreṇa bodhi-satva-yānikaṃ pudgalam avamanyema + a-varṇaṃ ca + asya bhāṣema visaṃvādito * asmābhis tathā-gato bhaved arhan samyak-saṃbuddhaḥ | saced vayaṃ bhagavann adya + agreṇa bodhi-satva-yānikaṃ pudgalaṃ gṛhiṇaṃ vā pravrajitaṃ vā pañcabhiḥ kāma-guṇaiḥ krīḍantaṃ paricārayantaṃ daṣṭvā + a-prasādaṃ kuryāma vilekhaṃ vā cittasya + utpādayema + a-gauravaṃ vā + utpādayema na ca tatra śāstṛ-saṃjñām utpādayema | visaṃvādito * asmābhis tathā-gato bhavet | saced vayaṃ bhagavann adya + agreṇa mitra-kula-bhikṣād a-kula-nidānaṃ bodhi-satva-yānikānāṃ pudgalānāṃ kāya-pīḍāṃ citta-pīḍāṃ vā kuryāma visaṃvādito * asmābhis tathā-gato bhavet | saced vayaṃ bhagavann adya + agreṇa bodhi-satva-yānikaṃ pudgalaṃ dṛṣṭvā ekena + apy a-mano-jña-vacanena + ābhāṣema visaṃvādito * asmābhis tathā-gato bhavet | saced vayaṃ bhagavann adya + agreṇa tris-kṛtvo rātreḥ tris-kṛtvo divasya bodhi-satva-yānikaṃ pudgalaṃ na namasyema visaṃvādito * asmābhis tathā-gato bhavet | saced vayaṃ bhagavann adya + agreṇa + asya vrata-samādānasya kṛtaśo rājya-pratilambhaṃ vā dhana-pratilambhaṃ vā kāya-jīvitaṃ vā na parityajema visaṃvādito * asmābhis tathā-gato bhavet | saced vayaṃ bhagavann adya + agreṇa śrāvaka-yānikaṃ vā praty-eka-buddha-yānikaṃ vā pudgalam avamanyema | vayaṃ viśiṣṭatarā na + ete iti visaṃvādito * asmābhis tathā-gato bhavet |saced vayaṃ bhagavan nīca-cittāś caṇḍāla-sadṛśa-cittā na viharema visaṃvādito * asmābhis tathā-gato bhavet | saced vayaṃ bhagavann adya + agreṇa + ātmānam utkarṣayema paraṃ vā paṃsayema visaṃvādito * asmābhis tathā-gato bhavet | saced vayaṃ bhagavann adya + agreṇa vyāpāda-vigraha-bhayād yojanaṃ vā yojana-śataṃ vā na palāyema īritāḥ samānā visaṃvādito * asmābhis tathā-gato bhavet | saced vayaṃ bhagavann adya + agreṇa śīlavantam ātmānaṃ pratijānīma bahu-śrutaṃ vā dhuta-guṇinaṃ vā + anyatara-anyatareṇa vā guṇena + ātmānam udbhāvayema visaṃvādito * asmābhis tathā-gato bhavet | saced vayaṃ bhagavann adya + agreṇa praticchanna-kalyāṇā vivṛta-pāpā na viharema visaṃvādito * asmābhis tathā-gato bhaved arhan samyak-saṃbuddhaḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: The calamity has been stated in summary. Its avoidance is as in the <s>Adhyāśaya-saṃcodana-sūtra</s>. By beginner <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are frightened and fearful upon hearing of such calamities, the commitments should be fulfilled just as they have been undertaken. For thus they said: 'We, O Blessed One, from this day forward, make this commitment in the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>: Should we, O Blessed One, from this day forward, reproach a person of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-vehicle — whether householder or renunciant — with a transgression, whether true or false, then the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, would be deceived by us. Should we, O Blessed One, from this day forward, treat with contempt a person of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-vehicle, or speak ill of him, then the <s>Tathāgata</s> would be deceived by us. Should we, O Blessed One, from this day forward, upon seeing a person of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-vehicle — householder or renunciant — playing and enjoying with the five strands of sensual pleasure, produce displeasure, or generate annoyance of mind, or generate disrespect, and not generate the perception of [him as] the Teacher — then the <s>Tathāgata</s> would be deceived by us. Should we, O Blessed One, from this day forward, through begging among friendly families, cause bodily or mental affliction to persons of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-vehicle for reasons related to families — then the <s>Tathāgata</s> would be deceived by us. Should we, O Blessed One, from this day forward, upon seeing a person of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-vehicle, address him with even a single disagreeable word — then the <s>Tathāgata</s> would be deceived by us. Should we, O Blessed One, from this day forward, not salute a person of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-vehicle three times each night and three times each day — then the <s>Tathāgata</s> would be deceived by us. Should we, O Blessed One, from this day forward, for the sake of this vow-commitment, not relinquish [even] the obtaining of a kingdom, the obtaining of wealth, or [our] bodily life — then the <s>Tathāgata</s> would be deceived by us. Should we, O Blessed One, from this day forward, treat with contempt a person of the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle or the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle, [thinking] "We are superior, not they" — then the <s>Tathāgata</s> would be deceived by us. Should we, O Blessed One, not dwell with lowly minds, with minds like <s>caṇḍālas</s> — then the <s>Tathāgata</s> would be deceived by us. Should we, O Blessed One, from this day forward, exalt ourselves or denigrate others — then the <s>Tathāgata</s> would be deceived by us. Should we, O Blessed One, from this day forward, when provoked, not flee a <s>yojana</s> or a hundred <s>yojanas</s> from fear of ill-will and conflict — then the <s>Tathāgata</s> would be deceived by us. Should we, O Blessed One, from this day forward, claim ourselves to be moral, or learned, or possessing ascetic qualities, or exalt ourselves with any virtue whatsoever — then the <s>Tathāgata</s> would be deceived by us. Should we, O Blessed One, from this day forward, not dwell concealing our virtues and revealing our faults — then the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, would be deceived by us.' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: tatra bhagavān maitreyaṃ bodhi-satvaṃ mahā-satvam āmantrayate sma | karma-āvaraṇaṃ maitreya kṣapayitu-kāmena kula-putreṇa vā kula-duhitrā vā evaṃ samādānaṃ kartavyaṃ yathā ebhiḥ kula-putraiḥ kṛtam iti ||
body.translated_text: There, the Blessed One addressed the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>: 'A son of good family or a daughter of good family who wishes to exhaust the obstruction of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmāvaraṇa</s>) should make such a commitment as was made by these sons of good family.'

body.text: sarva-dharma-a-pravṛtti-nirdeśe * apy āha ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Sarva-dharma-apravṛtti-nirdeśa</s> too it says:

body.text: tṛṣ-kṛtva rātriṃ divasaṃ tathā + eva | sa bodhi-satvān praṇameta mūrdhnā | teṣāṃ na kiñ-cit skhalitaṃ gaveṣet | careta caryāṃ hi sadā yathā-iṣṭam ||
body.translated_text: Three times each night, and likewise each day, he should bow with his head to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>. He should not seek any fault in them — those who see the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>). He should not generate aversion; he should always be of a mind of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness).

body.text: paśyed yadā kāma-guṇai ramantaṃ | na tasya kiñ-cit skhalitaṃ gaveṣet | guṇair an-antāṃ vara bodhi-caryāṃ | eṣo * api kālena hitāṃ spṛśeta ||
body.translated_text: If he should see them enjoying the strands of sensual pleasure, he should not seek any fault in them. 'With infinite virtues, this excellent conduct of awakening — even this one, in time, shall touch the beneficial.'

body.text: yuktyā + anupūrvyā kriyayā + anupūrvyā | bhavej jino na + eva hi eka-vācā | bahu-kalpa-koṭyo niyutāni ca + eṣa | sannāha-saṃprasthitanāny a-bhāvī ||
body.translated_text: By method, in due order, and by practice, in due order, one becomes a Conqueror — not indeed by a single utterance. Many billions of <s>kalpas</s> of setting forth with the armor [of resolve] will this one [undergo], without ceasing.

body.text: atra + eva + āha | ye kula-putra + evaṃ-rūpeṇa karma-āvaraṇena + an-arthikāḥ | tair na dvitīyasya bodhi-satvasya sarva-caryāsu vipratipattavyaṃ | sarvāḥ kriyās tasya vimoktavyāḥ | evaṃ cittam utpādayitavyaṃ | na + ahaṃ para-cittaṃ jāne dur-vijñeyā satva-caryā | idaṃ ca khalu kula-putra + artha-vaśaṃ saṃpaśyaṃs tathā-gata evaṃ dharmaṃ deśayati | na pudgalena pudgalaḥ pramātavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Right here it says: 'O son of good family, those who do not wish for [the calamity of] such an obstruction of <s>karma</s> — by them, there should be no acting contrary toward a second <s>bodhisattva</s> in any of his practices. All his actions should be approved. The thought should be generated thus: "I do not know the minds of others; the conduct of beings is difficult to discern." And indeed, O son of good family, seeing this matter, the <s>Tathāgata</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> thus: "A person should not be judged by a person."'

body.text: ahaṃ vā pudgalaṃ pramiṇuyāṃ yo vā syān mādṛśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'I [alone] might judge a person, or one who is like me.'

body.text: yaḥ kula-putra + ātmānaṃ rakṣitu-kāmas tena na kasya-cic caryā vivecayitavyā | na pareṣāṃ vikuṭṭanā kartavyā | ayam īdṛśo * ayam īdṛśa iti | buddha-dharma-abhiyuktena bhavitavyaṃ rātriṃ divaṃ dharma-paliguddha-mānasena + iti ||
body.translated_text: 'O son of good family, he who wishes to protect himself should not scrutinize anyone's conduct. He should not criticize others, [saying] "this one is such, this one is such." He should be devoted to the <s>Buddha-Dharma</s>, with a mind intent on the <s>Dharma</s> day and night.'

body.text: tathā kṣitigarbha-sūtre * api kathitaṃ | atha tāvad eva bahūni śata-sahasrāṇi vidvāṃsaḥ satvā utthāya + āsanād yena bhagavāṃs tena + añjaliṃ praṇamya + evam āhuḥ | vayaṃ bhadanta bhagavataḥ purata evaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kurmaḥ yāvac ciraṃ vayaṃ bhadanta bhagavan saṃsāre saṃsarema tāvan mātra pratilabdha-kṣānti-kāmā rāja-sthānaṃ pratilabhema | mā + amātya-sthānaṃ | mā nagara-jyeṣṭha-sthānaṃ | mā grāma-jyeṣṭha-sthānaṃ | mā nigama-jyeṣṭha-sthānaṃ | mā purohita-jyeṣṭha-sthānaṃ mā bhaṭṭa-jyeṣṭha-sthānaṃ | yāvan mā sa-artha-vāha-jyeṣṭha-sthānaṃ | mā + upādhyāya-jyeṣṭha-sthānaṃ | mā śramaṇa-jyeṣṭha-sthānaṃ | mā gṛha-pati-jyeṣṭha-sthānaṃ | mā kuṭumbi-jyeṣṭha-sthānaṃ yāvat sarvaśo vayaṃ mā satvānām adhipati-sthānaṃ pratilabhema yāvan na kṣānti-pratilabdhāḥ syāma | yato nidānaṃ vayam evaṃ-rūpam ati-gāḍhaṃ karma buddhānāṃ śāsanam ākṣipema | iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, in the <s>Kṣitigarbha-sūtra</s> too it is told: 'Then, at that very [moment], many hundreds of thousands of wise beings rose from their seats, and joining their palms toward the Blessed One, spoke thus: "We, O Venerable One, make this aspiration in the presence of the Blessed One: For as long as we, O Venerable One, wander in <s>saṃsāra</s>, may we not, having merely obtained patient acceptance, obtain the position of a king, nor the position of a minister, nor the position of a city-elder, nor the position of a village-elder, nor the position of a town-elder, nor the position of a chief priest, nor the position of a military commander," and so on up to "nor the position of a caravan-leader, nor the position of a preceptor, nor the position of a chief ascetic, nor the position of a householder, nor the position of a family-head — and so on, in every way, may we not obtain the position of lord over beings until we have obtained patient acceptance. Because of this, we might throw off onto the teachings of the <s>Buddhas</s> extremely heavy <s>karma</s> of this kind."' And so on in detail.

body.text: candra-pradīpa-sūtre * apy an-artha-vivarjanam uktam | na + asti pāpam a-kartavyaṃ kumārā teṣu bheṣyati | mā tehi saṃstavaṃ sārddhaṃ kuryāḥ tvaṃ kāli paścime ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Candrapradīpa-sūtra</s> too, the avoidance of calamity is stated: 'There is no evil that those youths will not do; you should be afraid of them. Do not keep company with them, O <s>Kāli</s>, in the future [time].'

body.text: ālape saṃlapeyyāsi kuryāsī teṣv a-gauravaṃ | ānālīnaḥ sat-kareyyāsy agra-bodhayi kāraṇāt ||
body.translated_text: 'You should speak and converse [with them only formally]; you should treat them without honor. Being unattached, you should respect [the <s>bodhisattvas</s>] — for the sake of the foremost awakening.'

body.text: varṣa-agraṃ paripṛcchitvā yas te vṛddhataro bhavet | kuryāsi gauravaṃ tatra śirasā pāda-vandanaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Having inquired about seniority by [ordination-]years, whoever is senior to you — you should show respect there, with prostrations of the head at [their] feet.'

body.text: na teṣāṃ skhalitaṃ paśyed bodhi-maṇḍaṃ vipaśyatāṃ | pratighātaṃ na janayet maitra-cittaḥ sadā bhavet ||
body.translated_text: 'One should not see any fault in them — those who behold the seat of awakening. One should not generate aversion; one should always be of a mind of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness).'

body.text: yady eṣāṃ skhalitaṃ paśyed doṣāṃs teṣāṃ na kīrtayet | yādṛśaṃ kāhiti karma tādṛśaṃ lapsyate phalaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'If one should see a fault in them, one should not proclaim their defects. Whatever <s>karma</s> one performs, such fruit one will obtain.'

body.text: smitena mukha-candreṇa vṛddheṣu navakeṣu ca | pūrva-ābhāṣī bhaven nityaṃ hata-mānaś ca sarvataḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'With a smiling moon-face, toward elders and novices alike, one should always be the first to speak, and should be free from pride in all respects.'

body.text: cīvaraiḥ piṇḍa-pātaiś ca kuryāt teṣām anugrahaṃ | evaṃ cittaṃ pradadhyās tvaṃ sarve bheṣyanti nāyakā | iti ||
body.translated_text: 'With robes and alms-food one should render assistance to them. Thus should you establish the thought: "All [of them] will become Leaders [i.e., <s>Buddhas</s>]."'

body.text: yasya ca bodhi-citta-utpādike gauravaṃ prasādaś ca na + utpadyete | tena sva-dur-gati-prapāta-bhaya-rakṣā-arthaṃ dṛṣṭa-a-dṛṣṭa-prāmodya-anubhavana-arthaṃ sva-citta-kaluṣa-prasādana-arthaṃ citta-kalyatā-citta-karmaṇyatā-pratilābha-arthaṃ ca yathā + ārya-gaṇḍa-vyūhe bodhi-citta-utpādika-guṇā bhagavad-ārya-maitreyeṇa + ācārya-sudhanam adhikṛtya + udbhāvitās tathā bhāvayitavyāḥ ||
