body.translated_text: And for one in whom reverence and faith do not arise toward one who has generated the <s>bodhicitta</s> — by that one, for the purpose of protecting himself from the fear of falling into lower destinies, for the purpose of experiencing joy both seen and unseen, for the purpose of clarifying the impurity of his own mind, and for the purpose of obtaining mental readiness and mental workability — the virtues of generating the <s>bodhicitta</s>, as declared by the venerable <s>Ārya Maitreya</s> with reference to the teacher <s>Sudhana</s> in the <s>Ārya-Gaṇḍavyūha</s>, should be contemplated accordingly.

body.text: eṣa dṛṣṭva jara-vyādhi-pīḍitān prāṇino duṣkha-śatair upadrutān | janma-mṛtyu-bhaya-śoka-tāpitān teṣa arthi carate krpā-āśayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Having seen beings tormented by old age and disease, afflicted by hundreds of sufferings, scorched by the fear, grief, and anguish of birth and death — he moves about with a compassionate intention, seeking their welfare.

body.text: duṣkha-yantra-paripīḍitaṃ jagat dṛṣṭva pañca-gati-cakra-maṇḍale | jñāna-vajra-mayam eṣa te dṛḍhaṃ duṣkha-yantra-gati-cakra-bhedanaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Having seen the world oppressed by the machine of suffering in the circle of the five destinies, this firm [weapon] of yours, made of the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt) of knowledge, will break the wheel of the machine of suffering and [its] destinies.

body.text: rāga-doṣa-tṛṇa-khāṇu-kaṇṭakaṃ dṛṣṭi-saṃga-bahu-kakṣa-saṃkulam | satva-kṣetra-pariśodhana-arthikaḥ prajña-lāṅgala-dṛḍhaṃ gaveṣate ||
body.translated_text: Desiring to purify the field of sentient beings — overgrown with the grass, stumps, and thorns of passion and hatred, tangled with the dense thickets of clinging to views — he seeks the firm plough of wisdom.

body.text: moha-vidya-gahana-āśayaṃ jagat prajña-cakṣu-hata-naṣṭa-daiśikaṃ | tasya kṣema diśa-daiśikaḥ prabhuḥ sa-artha-vāha jagato bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: The world, whose disposition is the thicket of delusion and ignorance, whose guide has been struck down and lost by the eye of wisdom — he will become the lord who shows the way to safety, the caravan-leader of the world.

body.text: kṣānti-dharma-tri-vimokṣa-vāhano jñāna-khaḍga-ripu-kleśa-dharṣakaḥ | śūra-sūta a-bhayasya dāyako daiśako hi jagato bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: Riding the vehicle of patience, <s>Dharma</s>, and the three <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations), subduing the enemy afflictions with the sword of knowledge, a hero, a charioteer, a giver of fearlessness — he will indeed become the guide of the world.

body.text: dharma-nāva samudānayaty ayaṃ jñāna-sāgara-pathe su-śikṣitaḥ | śānti-ratna-vara-dvīpa-nāyakaḥ karṇa-dhāra tri-bhava-arṇave ayam ||
body.translated_text: He assembles the ship of <s>Dharma</s>, well-trained on the path of the ocean of knowledge. A leader to the excellent island of the jewel of peace — he is the helmsman on the ocean of the three realms of existence.

body.text: jñāna-raśmi-praṇidhāna-maṇḍalaḥ sarva-satva-bhavana-avabhāsakaḥ | dharma-dhātu-gagane samudgato buddha-sūrya samudeśyate ayam ||
body.translated_text: A circle of the rays of knowledge and aspiration, illuminating the abodes of all sentient beings, risen in the sky of the <s>dharma-dhātu</s> (realm of reality) — he is designated as the <s>Buddha</s>-sun.

body.text: maitri-candana-samādhi-śītalaḥ sarva-satva-sama-citta-su-prabhaḥ | śukla-dharma-paripūrṇa-maṇḍalo buddha-candra samudeśyate ayam ||
body.translated_text: Cool with the sandalwood of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), shining beautifully with an equal mind toward all sentient beings, with a full orb of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — he is designated as the <s>Buddha</s>-moon.

body.text: āśaye dṛḍha-tale pratiṣṭhito bodhi-carya anupūrva udgataḥ | sarva-dharma-ratana-ākaro hy ayaṃ jñāna-sāra-varo bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: Established on the firm ground of aspiration, having risen gradually through the practice of awakening, a mine of all <s>dharma</s>-jewels — he will become the supreme essence of knowledge.

body.text: bodhi-citta-bhuja-ga-indra-saṃbhavo dharma-dhātu-gagane samudgataḥ | dharma-megha-yugapat-pravarṣaṇaḥ sarva-śukla-phala-śasya-vardhanaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Born from the serpent-king of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), risen in the sky of the <s>dharma-dhātu</s>, raining <s>Dharma</s>-clouds simultaneously, increasing all wholesome fruits and crops —

body.text: śuddhi vartti tri-mala-ttamo * apy ahaṃ maitri-sneha-smṛti-bhājanaṃ dṛḍham | bodhi-citta-vi-mala-agni-su-prabham dharma-dīpa samujjvālayiṣyati ||
body.translated_text: Though I am the most defiled by the three impurities, [I am] a firm vessel of the oil of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and mindfulness. He will kindle the <s>Dharma</s>-lamp, bright with the stainless fire of <s>bodhicitta</s>.

body.text: bodhi-citta-kalalaḥ kṛpā-arbudo maitra-peśir a-cala-āśayo ghanaḥ | bodhi aṅgam anupūrva-saṃbhavo buddha-garbha ayu saṃpravardhate ||
body.translated_text: The embryo (<s>kalala</s>) of <s>bodhicitta</s>, the lump (<s>arbuda</s>) of compassion, the flesh (<s>peśī</s>) of friendliness, the solid mass (<s>ghana</s>) of unwavering aspiration, the limbs of awakening gradually forming — this <s>buddha-garbha</s> (buddha-embryo) grows and develops.

body.text: puṇya-garbham abhivarddhayiṣyati prajña-garbham abhiśodhayiṣyati | jñāna-garbha samudeśyate ayaṃ yādṛśaḥ praṇidhi-garbha-saṃbhavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: He will increase the womb of merit, he will purify the womb of wisdom. He is designated as the womb of knowledge — such is his birth from the womb of aspiration.

body.text: īdṛśāḥ karuṇa-maitra-dharmitāḥ satva-mocana matī hita-āśayāṃ | dur-labhā jagi s-deva-mānuṣe yādṛśo * ayu viśuddha-mānasaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Those endowed with compassion and loving-kindness, with the intention to liberate beings, with a beneficent disposition — such ones of purified mind are rare in the world with its gods and humans.

body.text: īdṛśa-āśaya-su-mūla-saṃsthito īdṛśo dṛḍha-prayoga-varddhitaḥ | īdṛśas tri-bhava-chādana-prabho jñāna-vṛkṣa-phala-daḥ su-dur-labhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Established in the good root of such aspiration, nurtured by such firm exertion, covering the three realms with such radiance — the knowledge-tree that bears fruit is supremely rare.

body.text: eṣa sarva-guṇa-saṃbhava-arthikaḥ sarva-dharma-paripṛcchana-arthikaḥ | sarva-saṃśaya-vidāraṇa-arthikaḥ sarva-mitra bhajate a-tandritaḥ ||
body.translated_text: He, desiring the arising of all qualities, desiring to investigate all <s>dharmas</s>, desiring to resolve all doubts, serves all spiritual friends without sloth.

body.text: eṣa māra-kali-kleśa-sūdano eṣa dṛṣṭi-mala-kleśa-śodhanaḥ | eṣa sarva-jaga-mokṣaṇa-udyato eṣa te sada viśeṣa paṇḍitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: He is the destroyer of <s>Māra</s>, strife, and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions); he is the purifier of the stain and defilement of [wrong] views; he is the one who strives for the liberation of the entire world — he is always your supreme sage.

body.text: eṣa dur-gati viśodhayiṣyati svarga-mārgam upadarśayiṣyati | mokṣa-mārgam upaneṣyate jagad yādṛśe guṇa-pathe pratiṣṭhitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: He will purify the lower realms, he will reveal the path to heaven, he will lead the world to the path of liberation — established as he is on such a path of virtues.

body.text: eṣa sarvata-duṣkha-mocako | eṣa sarva-gati-saukhya-dāyakaḥ | eṣa sarva-bhaya-pāśa-chedako | bheṣyate bhagavatī-nisūdana | iti ||
body.translated_text: He is the liberator from all suffering everywhere; he is the giver of happiness in all destinies; he is the cutter of the bonds of all fears; he will become the destroyer [of obstacles] of the Blessed Lady.

body.text: evam anayā bhāvanayā + an-artha-vivarjanaṃ su-karaṃ bhavati | tathā + adhyāśaya-sañcodana-sūtre * apy an-artha-vivarjanam uktaṃ | caturbhir maitreya dharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhi-satva-yānikaḥ pudgalaḥ paścimāyāṃ pañcaśatyāṃ sad-dharma-vipralope vartamāne * a-kṣato * an-upahataḥ svastinā parimokṣyate ||
body.translated_text: Thus, by this cultivation, the avoidance of harmful consequences becomes easy. Likewise, in the <s>Adhyāśayasaṃcodana-sūtra</s> (Sūtra Urging Superior Intention), the avoidance of harmful consequences is stated: "Endowed with four <s>dharmas</s>, O <s>Maitreya</s>, a person following the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle, when the final five hundred [years] of the deterioration of the true <s>Dharma</s> have arrived, will be unharmed, uninjured, and will be safely liberated."

body.text: katamaiś caturbhiḥ | ātma-skhalita-pratyavekṣaṇatayā | pareṣāṃ bodhi-satva-yānikānāṃ pudgalānām āpattya-codanatayā | mitra-kula-bhikṣād a-kula-an-avalokanatayā | a-manaska-vacana-prativiramaṇatayā | ebhir maitreya caturbhir iti pūrva-vat ||
body.translated_text: "With which four? Through self-examination of one's own stumbles; through admonishing other persons following the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle regarding their transgressions; through not looking down upon the families from which one's friends and fellow monks [come]; and through abstaining from careless speech. With these four, O <s>Maitreya</s>" — as before.

body.text: a-paraiś caturbhiḥ | katamaiḥ | alpa-śruta-satva-parivarjanatayā | parṣad-an-upādānatayā | prānta-śayyā-āsana-niṣevaṇatayā ca | ātma-dama-śamatha-yogam anuyuktatayā ca | ebhiś caturbhir iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: "With four more. Which? Through avoiding beings of little learning; through not being attached to assemblies; through resorting to secluded beds and seats; and through being devoted to the yoga of self-restraint and tranquility. With these four" — and so on in detail.

body.text: punar atra + eva + āha | ādi-karmikeṇa maitreya bodhi-satvena prajñā-bala-ādhāna-prāptena lābha-sat-kāra-parivarjitena lābha-sat-kāra-doṣa-darśinā bhavitavyaṃ || pe ||
body.translated_text: And further in the same [text] it says: "A beginner <s>bodhisattva</s>, O <s>Maitreya</s>, who has attained the foundation of the power of wisdom, should be one who avoids gain and honor, who sees the faults in gain and honor." [Abbreviated.]

body.text: saṃgaṇikā-ārāma-parivarjitena saṃgaṇikā-ārāma-doṣa-darśinā bhavitavyaṃ | bhāṣya-ārāma-parivarjitena bhāṣya-ārāma-doṣa-darśinā bhavitavyaṃ | nidrā-ārāma-varjitena nidrā-ārāma-doṣa-darśinā bhavitavyaṃ | karma-ārāma-varjitena karma-ārāma-doṣa-darśinā bhavitavyaṃ | prapañca-ārāma-varjitena prapañca-ārāma-doṣa-darśinā bhavitavyaṃ || pe ||
body.translated_text: "He should be one who avoids delight in socializing, who sees the faults in delight in socializing. He should be one who avoids delight in talking, who sees the faults in delight in talking. He should be one who avoids delight in sleeping, who sees the faults in delight in sleeping. He should be one who avoids delight in busyness, who sees the faults in delight in busyness. He should be one who avoids delight in conceptual proliferation (<s>prapañca</s>), who sees the faults in delight in conceptual proliferation." [Abbreviated.]

body.text: iha maitreya bodhi-satvena mahā-satvena rāga-saṃjanano lābha-sat-kāraḥ pratyavekṣitavyaḥ | smṛti-vidhvaṃsana-karo lābha-sat-kāraḥ pratyavekṣitavyaḥ | lābha-a-lābhatayā unnāma-avanāma-karo lābha-sat-kāraḥ pratyavekṣitavyaḥ | moha-utpādano lābha-sat-kāraḥ pratyavekṣitavyaḥ | kula-mātsarya-adhyavasāno lābha-sat-kāraḥ pratyavekṣitavyaḥ | ātma-artha-niṣpādanatayā śāṭhya-utpādano lābha-sat-kāraḥ pratyavekṣitavyaḥ | catur-ārya-vaṃśa-parivarjanatayā āhrīkya-an-apatrāpya-saṃjanano lābha-sat-kāraḥ pratyavekṣitavyaḥ | evaṃ sarva-buddha-an-anujñāno lābha-sat-kāraḥ pratyavekṣitavyaḥ | māna-mada-utpādano lābha-sat-kāraḥ pratyavekṣitavyaḥ | gurūṇām avamānano lābha-sat-kāraḥ | māra-pakṣo lābha-sat-kāraḥ | eka-anta-pramāda-mūlaḥ kuśala-mūla-apaharaṇo lābha-sat-kāraḥ | vidyuc-cakra-aśani-sadṛśo lābha-sat-kāraḥ | bahu-paligodha-paliguddho mitra-kula-bhikṣād a-kula-avalokano daurmanasya-saṃjananaḥ | buddhi-vibhrāmaṇo lābha-sat-kāraḥ priya-vastu-pariṇāmanatayā śoka-bhājano lābha-sat-kāraḥ |catuḥ-smṛty-upasthāna-saṃmoṣaṇaḥ śukla-dharma-dur-balī-karaṇaḥ catuḥ-samyak-prahāṇa-parihāṇa-karaṇo lābha-sat-kāraḥ | ṛddhy-abhijñā-parihāṇa-karaṇaḥ | pūrvaṃ sat-kāra-paścād a-sat-kāra-karaṇaḥ | a-mitra-sat-karaṇa-mitra-prahāṇo lābha-sat-kāraḥ | para-abhisaṃdhānatayā gaṇikā-sadṛśaḥ | dhyana-a-pramāṇa-parivarjanaḥ | naraka-tiryag-yoni-yama-loka-prapātano lābha-sat-kāraḥ | devadatta-udraka-samācāro lābha-sat-kāraḥ pratyavekṣitavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: "Here, O <s>Maitreya</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> should reflect that gain and honor generate passion. He should reflect that gain and honor destroy mindfulness. He should reflect that gain and honor cause elation and dejection through gain and non-gain. He should reflect that gain and honor generate delusion. He should reflect that gain and honor produce clinging to the miserliness of family. He should reflect that gain and honor generate deceit through the accomplishment of selfish purposes. He should reflect that gain and honor, through the abandonment of the four noble lineages, generate shamelessness and absence of moral dread. Likewise, he should reflect that gain and honor are not sanctioned by all <s>Buddhas</s>. He should reflect that gain and honor generate pride and intoxication. Gain and honor are a disrespect to teachers. Gain and honor are the party of <s>Māra</s>. Gain and honor are exclusively the root of heedlessness, robbing one of roots of virtue. Gain and honor are like a circle of lightning and thunderbolts. Gain and honor, entangled in many obstacles, looking down upon the families of friends and fellow monks, generate depression. Gain and honor confuse the intellect. Gain and honor, through the transformation of cherished things, make one a vessel of grief. Gain and honor destroy the four foundations of mindfulness, weaken wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, and cause the decline of the four right exertions. Gain and honor cause the decline of supernatural powers and superknowledges. Gain and honor cause honor first and dishonor later. Gain and honor cause the honoring of enemies and the abandonment of friends. Gain and honor, through scheming against others, are like a courtesan. Gain and honor cause the abandonment of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and the immeasurables. Gain and honor cause the fall into hell, the animal realm, and the world of <s>Yama</s>. He should reflect that gain and honor are the conduct of <s>Devadatta</s> and <s>Udraka</s>."

body.text: ime evaṃ-rūpā maitreya lābha-sat-kāre ādīnavā ye bodhi-satvena pratyavekṣitavyāḥ | pratyavekṣya ca + alpa-icchatāyāṃ rantavyaṃ na paritaptavyaṃ | tat kasya hetoḥ | alpa-icchasya hi maitreya imae evaṃ-rūpā doṣā na bhavanti na ca + asya + antarāyā bhavanti buddha-dharmāṇāṃ | a-nirviṇṇaś ca bhavati gṛhi-pravrajitebhyaḥ | anurakṣaṇīyaś ca bhavati deva-manuṣyāṇāṃ pariśuddha-āśaya-sthitaḥ | a-saṃtrastaś ca bhavati sarva-dur-gati-nipātebhyaḥ | an-abhibhūtaś ca bhavati tarjanā-vigataḥ | a-saṃhāryaś ca bhavati māra-viṣaya-vimuktaḥ | a-dharṣaṇīyaś ca bhavati sarva-vyasanaiḥ | abhilaṣaṇīyaś ca bhavati deva-manuṣyāṇāṃ dhyāna-abhyāsa-avasthitaḥ

children.text: | spaṣṭaś ca bhavati māyā-śāṭhya-prahīṇo * a-pramattaś ca bhavati pañca-kāma-guṇa-doṣa-darśī yathā-vādī tathā-kārī bhavaty ārya-vaṃśe sthitaḥ | abhilaṣitaś ca bhavati vidvadbhiḥ sa-brahma-cāribhiḥ | imāṃ maitreya evaṃ-rūpām anuśaṃsāṃ viditvā paṇḍitena bodhi-satvena + adhyāśayena + alpa-icchatāyāṃ rantavyaṃ | alpa-icchatā āsevitavyā sarva-lābha-sat-kara-prahāṇāya + iti ||
children.translated_text: "And he is transparent, having abandoned deceit and guile. And he is vigilant, seeing the faults of the five strands of sensual pleasure. He is one whose words match his deeds, established in the noble lineage. And he is desired by the learned and those leading the holy life. Knowing these kinds of benefits, O <s>Maitreya</s>, a wise <s>bodhisattva</s> should delight in contentment with little through superior aspiration. Contentment with little should be cultivated for the abandonment of all gain and honor."

body.translated_text: "These, O <s>Maitreya</s>, are the dangers of such gain and honor that should be examined by a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Having examined them, one should delight in contentment with little (<s>alpecchatā</s>) and not be tormented. For what reason? For one who is content with little, O <s>Maitreya</s>, these kinds of faults do not occur, nor do obstacles to the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> arise for him. And he is not disenchanted with householders and renunciants. And he is worthy of being protected by gods and humans, being established in pure aspiration. And he is unafraid of all falls into lower realms. And he is unoppressed, free from threats. And he is unshakable, liberated from the domain of <s>Māra</s>. And he is invincible against all misfortunes. And he is desirable to gods and humans, being established in the practice of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation)."

body.text: saṃgaṇikām adhikṛtya + āha | vijahya rāgaṃ vijahya doṣaṃ na tiṣṭhate saṃgaṇikāsu yogī | bhavaty asau tat-pravaṇas tan-nimnaḥ | etena doṣeṇa ratiṃ na kuryāt | auddhatya hāsyaṃ ca tathā vitarkā | bhavanty amī saṃgaṇikāsu sarve ||
body.translated_text: Regarding socializing, it says: "Having abandoned passion, having abandoned hatred, the practitioner does not remain in social gatherings. He becomes inclined toward that, flowing toward that. Through this fault, one should not take delight [in socializing]. Restlessness, laughter, and likewise discursive thoughts — all these arise in social gatherings."

body.text: saṃkīrṇa-cārī hi bhavaty a-saṃvṛtaḥ | karoti yaḥ saṃgaṇikām a-sārām ||
body.translated_text: "For one who lives mingling [with others] becomes unrestrained. He who engages in worthless socializing —"

body.text: lokasya mantreṣu ramanti bālā | hīyanti ca + iha + agra-kathāsu bālāḥ | pradoṣa vardhenti vitarka utsadā | etena doṣeṇa na tatra rājate ||
body.translated_text: "Fools delight in worldly conversations and fools decline from the highest discourses. They increase aversion and discursive thoughts grow — through this fault, one does not shine there."

body.text: na vardhate ca + api śrutena bhikṣuḥ | a-yukta-mantreṣu ratiṃ janitvā | tasmāt parityajya a-yukta-mantrān | dharme ratiṃ vindatha nitya-kālam ||
body.translated_text: "The monk does not grow in learning, having generated delight in inappropriate conversations. Therefore, having abandoned inappropriate conversations, find delight in the <s>Dharma</s> at all times."

body.text: sahasraśo * aṣṭhāni mayā svakāni | tyaktāni bodhiṃ pratikāṅkṣa tarhi | na ca + asmi tṛptaḥ śṛṇumāna dharmaṃ | te khedam eṣyanti śṛṇonta dharmam ||
body.translated_text: "Thousands of my own bones have I cast away, seeking awakening then. And I am not sated hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. Will they grow weary hearing the <s>Dharma</s>?"

body.text: sarveṇa sarvaṃ parivarjanīyā | a-yukta-mantrāś ca a-śiṣṭa-mantrāḥ | dharme vare tatra ratiṃ janetha | yo dur-labhaḥ kalpa-śatair an-ekaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: "Entirely and completely should inappropriate conversations and undisciplined conversations be avoided. Generate delight in that excellent <s>Dharma</s> which is difficult to obtain in many hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons)."

body.text: vane vasantena guṇa-arthikena | parasya doṣā na hi vīkṣitavyāḥ | ahaṃ viśiṣṭo * aham eva śreṣṭho | na eva cittaṃ samupādanīyam ||
body.translated_text: "For one dwelling in the forest, seeking virtuous qualities, the faults of others should not be examined. The thought 'I am distinguished, I alone am the best' — such a mind should never be taken up."

body.text: mado * ayaṃ sarva-pramāda-mūlo | na hīna-bhikṣū avamanyitavyāḥ | anupūrva eṣo iha śāsanasya | na + ekena janmena labhate bodhim ||
body.translated_text: "This pride is the root of all heedlessness. Inferior monks should not be despised. This is the gradual [path] in this teaching — one does not obtain awakening in a single birth."

body.text: atra + iva bhāṣya-ārāmam adhikṛtya + āha | a-gauravo bhoti śrutena matto | vivāda-mantreṣu niviṣṭa bhoti | muṣita-śrutiś ca + api a-saṃprajanyo | bhāṣye ramantasya ime hi doṣāḥ ||
body.translated_text: And here, regarding delight in talking, it says: "He becomes disrespectful, intoxicated with learning, and becomes attached to contentious conversations. He becomes one whose learning is stolen, lacking clear comprehension — these are the faults of one who delights in talking."

body.text: adhyātma-cintā + atta

children.text: su-dūra bhotī | cittaṃ na kāyaś ca prasanna bhoti | unnāma-nāmāni bahūni gacchatī | bhāṣye ramantasya ime hi doṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "... becomes very far away. Neither the mind nor the body becomes serene. He undergoes many ups and downs — these are the faults of one who delights in talking."

body.translated_text: Contemplation of the inner [nature] ...

body.text: sad-dharma-cittāt tu praṇaṣṭu bālāḥ | su-karkaśo bhoti a-snigdha-cittaḥ | vipaśyanāyāḥ śamathāc ca dūre | bhāṣye ramantasya ime hi doṣāḥ ||
body.translated_text: "Fools lose the mind [directed toward] the true <s>Dharma</s>. He becomes extremely harsh, with an unaffectionate mind. He becomes far from <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) and <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) — these are the faults of one who delights in talking."

body.text: a-gauravo bhoti sadā gurūṇāṃ | paligodha-mantreṣu ratiṃ janitvā | a-sāra-sthāyī parihīṇa-prajño | bhāṣye ramantasya ime hi doṣāḥ ||
body.translated_text: "He becomes always disrespectful to teachers. Having generated delight in obstructive conversations, he remains in what is insubstantial, with diminished wisdom — these are the faults of one who delights in talking."

body.text: a-mānito deva-guṇaiḥ sa bhoti | na + apy asya tasmin spṛha saṃjananti | pratisaṃvidāto bhavatī vihīno | bhāṣye ramantasya ime hi doṣāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'He is not honored with divine qualities. Nor does longing arise in him for that [goal]. He becomes deficient in analytical knowledge. These are the faults of one who delights in talk.'

body.text: paribhāṣyate ca + api sa paṇḍitebhiḥ | ye ka-cid astī pṛthakāya-sākṣī

children.text: | nir-arthakaṃ jīvitu tasya bhotī | bhāṣye ramantasya ime hi doṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'his life becomes purposeless. These are the faults of one who delights in talk.'

body.translated_text: 'And he is reviled by the wise. Whoever there is who is a witness of the solitary [path] —'

body.text: sa śocate kālu karotu bālaḥ | pratipatti hīno * asmi kim adya kuryāṃ | su-duṣkhito bhoti a-labdha-gādho | bhāṣye ramantasya ime hi doṣāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'He grieves: "Alas, I have been a fool! I am deficient in practice — what should I do now?" He becomes deeply distressed, having found no foothold. These are the faults of one who delights in talk.'

body.text: cala-a-calo bhoti tṛṇaṃ yathā + īritaṃ | vicikitsate evam asau na saṃśayaḥ | na tasya jātū dṛḍha buddhi bhotī | bhāṣye ramantasya ime hi doṣāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'He becomes unsteady like grass blown by the wind. He doubts in this way, without a doubt. A firm resolve never arises in him. These are the faults of one who delights in talk.'

body.text: naṭā yathā tiṣṭhati raṅga-madhye | anyāna śūrāṇa guṇān prabhāṣate | svayaṃ ca bhotī pratipatti-hīno | bhāṣye ramantasya ime hi doṣāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Like an actor standing in the middle of a stage, he proclaims the virtues of other heroes, but he himself is devoid of practice. These are the faults of one who delights in talk.'

body.text: śaṭhaś ca so bhoti laghu-nir-āśaḥ | punaḥ punaś ca + ārabhate vivādam | so dūrato ārya-dharmasya bhotī | bhāṣye ramantasya ime hi doṣāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'And he becomes deceitful, fickle, and without hope. Again and again he engages in disputes. He becomes far from the noble <s>Dharma</s>. These are the faults of one who delights in talk.'

body.text: saṃhṛṣyate sat-krṭa alpa-sthāmaḥ | prakampate viprakṛto * ajānī | kapir yathā cañcala-citta bhotī | bhāṣye ramantasya ime hi doṣāḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'He becomes elated when honored, [but is] of little strength. He trembles when treated with contempt, ignoble. He becomes fickle-minded like a monkey. These are the faults of one who delights in talk.' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: ramitva bhāṣyasmi ciraṃ pi kālaṃ | na vindate prītim iha + ātma-saukhyaṃ | varaṃ hi ekasya padasya cintanā | prītiṃ pade yatra labhed an-antam ||
body.translated_text: 'Though one has delighted in talk for a long time, one finds no joy here, no happiness for oneself. Better indeed is the contemplation of a single word — where one would find infinite joy in that word.'

body.text: na + ikṣu-tvace sāram iha + asti kiñ-cin | madhye * asti tat-sāra su-premaṇīyaḥ | bhuktvā tvacaṃ na + iha punaḥ saśakyaṃ | labdhuṃ nareṇa + ikṣu-rasaṃ pradhānam ||
body.translated_text: 'There is nothing of substance in the outer husk of sugarcane; the essence within is most delightful. Having consumed the husk, a person cannot then obtain the excellent sugarcane juice.'

body.text: yathā tvacaṃ tad-vad avaihi bhāṣyaṃ | yathā rasas tad-vad iha + artha-cintā

children.text: | tasmād * dhi bhāṣye tu ratiṃ vihāya | cintetha arthaṃ sada a-pramattāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, abandoning delight in talk, always contemplate the meaning, heedfully.'

body.translated_text: 'As the husk, so understand talk to be; as the juice, so is the contemplation of meaning here —'

body.text: nidrā-ārāmam adhikṛtya + āha | mahac ca so vardhati moha-jālaṃ | vicikitsako bhoti sa dṛṣṭi-prāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Regarding delight in sleep (<s>nidrā</s>), [the sūtra] says: 'And a great net of delusion grows in him. He becomes one who doubts, arrived at [wrong] views.'

body.text: dṛṣṭī-kṛtāny asya bahūni bhontī | yasmāna middhe * abhiratiṃ prayāti ||
body.translated_text: 'Many view-based [errors] arise in him, since he takes delight in torpor.'

body.text: prajñā ca teṣāṃ bhavatī su-dur-balā | parihīyate buddhi na tasya bhoti | jñānāc ca so hīyati nitya-kālaṃ | yasmāna middhe * abhiratiṃ prayāti ||
body.translated_text: 'And their wisdom becomes exceedingly weak. Intelligence diminishes; it does not arise in him. He declines from knowledge at all times, since he takes delight in torpor.'

body.text: kusīda a-jño * a-laso * a-prajño * a-manuṣya avatāra labhenti tasya | viheṭhayante ca vane vasantaṃ yasmāna middhe * abhiratiṃ prayāti ||
body.translated_text: 'Lazy, ignorant, slothful, unwise — they attain a non-human rebirth. And wild creatures harass him as he dwells in the forest, since he takes delight in torpor.'

body.text: kuśalena cittena sadā an-arthiko | dharme ca chando na hi bhoti tasya | a-dharma-kāyaś ca sa bhoti bhūyo yasmāna middhe * abhiratiṃ prayāti ||
body.translated_text: 'Always indifferent to wholesome states of mind, desire for the <s>Dharma</s> does not arise in him. And he increasingly becomes one whose body is [given to] what is contrary to <s>Dharma</s>, since he takes delight in torpor.'

body.text: sad-dharma-chandena vihīna-mūḍhaḥ parihoyate sarva-guṇehi bālaḥ | śuklaṃ ca ghāteti tamo * adhigacchatī | yasmāna middhe * abhiratiṃ prayāti ||
body.translated_text: 'The deluded fool, devoid of desire for the true <s>Dharma</s>, declines from all good qualities. He destroys the bright [deeds] and falls into darkness, since he takes delight in torpor.'

body.text: a-viśārado bhoti pralīna-cittaḥ | prāmodya tasya + u bhavatī na nityaṃ | nidrayā + apagrastaḥ śithila-aṅga bhotī | yasmāna middhe * abhiratiṃ prayāti ||
body.translated_text: 'He becomes timid, with a sunken mind. Joy does not constantly arise in him. Seized by sleep, his limbs become slack, since he takes delight in torpor.'

body.text: ātmā tu jñātvā ca kusīda-prāptaḥ īrṣyāyate vīrya-balair upetān | vīrya-anvitānāṃ ca a-varṇa bhāṣate yasmāna middhe * abhiratiṃ prayāti || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'Knowing himself to be lazy, he becomes envious of those endowed with the strength of vigor. And he speaks ill of those possessed of vigor, since he takes delight in torpor.' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: yat sarva-duṣkhasya tamasya nāśanaṃ | apāya-parivarjanatayā mūlaṃ | sarvehi buddhair hi sadā praśastaṃ | taṃ vīryam āryaṃ satataṃ bhajasva ||
body.translated_text: 'That which is the destruction of all suffering and darkness, which is the root of avoidance of lower realms, which is always praised by all the <s>Buddhas</s> — that noble vigor, cultivate it constantly!'

body.text: karma-ārāmam adhikṛtya + āha ||
body.translated_text: Regarding delight in worldly activity (<s>karma</s>), [the sūtra] says:

body.text: su-dur-vaco bhoti gurūbhi coditaḥ | pradakṣiṇaṃ gṛhṇati na + anuśāsanaṃ | vipanna-śīlaś ca sa bhoti kṣipraṃ | doṣā amī karma-rate bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: 'He becomes very hard to admonish, even when urged by teachers. He does not receive instruction favorably. And his morality quickly becomes corrupted. These are the faults of one who delights in worldly activity.'

body.text: utkaṇṭhito bhoti sa nitya-kālaṃ | gṛha-stha-karmāṇi sadā vicintayan | dhyāna-prahāṇaiś ca na tasya kṛtyaṃ | doṣā amī karma-rate bhavati ||
body.translated_text: 'He becomes distressed at all times, always thinking about household tasks. He has no concern for meditation and spiritual exertion. These are the faults of one who delights in worldly activity.'

body.text: tīvraś ca saṃjāyati tasya rāgo | rasa-a-raseṣu grasitaḥ sa mūrcchitaḥ | na tuṣyate * asāv itara-itareṇa | doṣā amī karma-rate bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: 'And intense attachment arises in him. Swallowed up by pleasant and unpleasant flavors, he is intoxicated. He is not satisfied with one thing after another. These are the faults of one who delights in worldly activity.'

body.text: mahatyā ca bhotī pariṣāya tuṣṭho | sa duṣkhito bhoti tayā vihīnaḥ | saṃkīrṇa bhotī sayathā + iha gardabho | doṣā amī karma-rate bhavanti || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'He is pleased with a large assembly, but becomes distressed when deprived of it. He becomes mixed up, like a donkey. These are the faults of one who delights in worldly activity.' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: divā ca rātrau ca an-anya-citto | bhakte ca coḍe ca bhavaty abhīkṣṇaṃ | sv-an-arthiko bhoti guṇaiḥ sa sarvadā | doṣā amī karma-rate bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: 'Day and night, his mind is single-pointedly [fixed] on food and robes, constantly. He is always indifferent to [spiritual] qualities. These are the faults of one who delights in worldly activity.'

body.text: kṛtyāny asau pṛcchati laukikāni | a-yukta-mantraiś ca ratiṃ prayāti | yuktaiś ca mantraiḥ sa na vindate ratiṃ | doṣā amī karma-rate bhavanti || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'He inquires about worldly tasks and takes delight in improper deliberations. But he finds no delight in proper deliberations. These are the faults of one who delights in worldly activity.' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: atha khalu maitreyo bodhi-satvo mahā-satvo bhagavantam etad avocat | su-parītta-prajñās te bhagavan bodhi-satvā bhaviṣyanti vihīna-prajñā ye * agra-dharmān varjayitvā hīnāni karmāṇy ārapsyante ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> said to the Blessed One: 'Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> will be of very little wisdom, O Blessed One, of deficient wisdom, who, abandoning the supreme <s>dharmas</s>, will undertake inferior activities.'

body.text: evam ukte bhagavān maitreyaṃ bodhi-satvaṃ mahā-satvam etad avocat | evam etan maitreya | evam etad yathā vadasi su-parītta-prajñās te bodhi-satvā bhaviṣyanti ye * agra-dharmān parivarjayitvā hīnāni karmāṇy ārapsyante | api tv ārocayāmi te maitreya prativedayāmi te | na te bodhi-satvās tathāgata-śāsane pravrajitā yeṣāṃ na + asti yogo na + asti dhyānaṃ na + asti prahāṇaṃ na + asty adhyayanaṃ na + asti bāhuśrutya-paryeṣṭiḥ | api tu maitreya dhyāna-prahāṇa-prabhāvitaṃ tathā-gata-śāsanaṃ jñāna-saṃskṛtaṃ jñāna-samāhitaṃ abhiyoga-prabhāvitaṃ | na gṛhi-karma-anta-vaiyāpṛtya-prabhāvitaṃ | a-yukta-yogānām etat karma saṃsāra-abhiratānāṃ yad uta vaiyāpṛtyaṃ laukika-kṛtya-paligodhaḥ | na tatra bodhi-satvena spṛhā + utpādayitavyā | sacen maitreya vaiyāpṛtya-abhirato bodhi-satvaḥ sapta-ratna-mayaiḥ stūpair imaṃ tri-sāhasra-mahā-sāhasraṃ loka-dhātuṃ pūrayet | na + ahaṃ tena + ārādhito bhaveyaṃ na mānito na + api sat-kṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One said to the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>: 'So it is, <s>Maitreya</s>! It is just as you say — those <s>bodhisattvas</s> will be of very little wisdom who, abandoning the supreme <s>dharmas</s>, will undertake inferior activities. But I declare to you, <s>Maitreya</s>, I announce to you: those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have no practice (<s>yoga</s>), no meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), no spiritual exertion (<s>prahāṇa</s>), no study, no quest for great learning — they have not gone forth in the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching. Moreover, <s>Maitreya</s>, the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is made powerful by meditation and spiritual exertion, constructed by knowledge, established in knowledge, made powerful by application — not made powerful by household tasks and worldly business. This work — namely, worldly business and preoccupation with mundane tasks — belongs to those unyoked to practice, to those who delight in <s>saṃsāra</s>. A <s>bodhisattva</s> should not generate longing for that. If, <s>Maitreya</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who delights in worldly business were to fill this trichiliocosm with <s>stūpas</s> made of the seven treasures — I would not be pleased by that, nor honored, nor respected.'

body.text: pe | tatra jambū-dvīpaḥ pūritaḥ syād vaiyāpṛtya-karair bodhi-satvaiḥ | sarvais tair ekasya + uddeśa-sva-adhyāya-abhiyuktasya bodhi-satvasya + upasthāna-paricaryā karaṇīyā | jambū-dvīpa-pramāṇaiś ca + uddeśa-sva-adhyāya-abhiyuktair bodhi-satvair ekasya pratisaṃlayana-abhiyuktasya bodhi-satvasya + upasthāna-paricaryā kartavyā || pe ||
body.translated_text: [Abbreviated.] 'Therein, suppose <s>Jambudvīpa</s> were filled with <s>bodhisattvas</s> engaged in worldly business — all of them should perform attendance and service to a single <s>bodhisattva</s> devoted to recitation and study. And <s>bodhisattvas</s> devoted to recitation and study, equal in number to [the population of] <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, should perform attendance and service to a single <s>bodhisattva</s> devoted to solitary meditation.' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: tat kasya hetoḥ | duṣ-karam etat karma yad uta prajñā-karma | uttaraṃ nir-uttaraṃ sarva-trailokya-prativiśiṣṭam abhyudgataṃ tasmāt tarhi maitreya bodhi-satvena yoga-arthikena vīryam ārabdhu-kāmena prajñāyām abhiyoktavyam iti ||
body.translated_text: 'For what reason? Because this is a difficult task — namely, the task of wisdom. It is supreme, unsurpassed, distinguished above all the three worlds, exalted. Therefore, <s>Maitreya</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> who seeks practice and wishes to undertake vigor should apply himself to wisdom.'

body.text: prapañca-ārāmam adhikṛtya + āha | aṣṭa-a-kṣaṇā tasya na bhonti dūre | kṣaṇa-saṃpadā tasya na bhoti śreṣṭhā | ete an-arthā sya bhavanti nityaṃ | doṣā amī tasya prapañca-cāriṇaḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: Regarding delight in proliferation (<s>prapañca</s>), [the sūtra] says: 'The eight inopportune conditions are not far from him. The excellence of opportune conditions does not arise for him. These misfortunes constantly befall him. These are the faults of one who engages in proliferation.' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: doṣān imān samyag avetya paṇḍitaḥ sarvān prapañcān parivarjīta | su-labhā an-arthā hi prapañca-cāriṇaḥ | tasmāt prapañcena na saṃvaseta ||
body.translated_text: 'Having rightly understood these faults, the wise person abandons all proliferations. For misfortunes are easily obtained by one who engages in proliferation. Therefore one should not dwell with proliferation.'

body.text: yāyāc * chataṃ yojanakaṃ paraṃ varaṃ | yatra prapañco stiya vigraho vā | na tatra vāsaṃ na niketu kuryān muhūrtta-mātraṃ stiya yatra kleśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Better to go a hundred <s>yojanas</s> away — wherever there is proliferation or quarrel, one should not make a dwelling or abode there, not even for a moment, wherever there is <s>kleśa</s> (affliction).'

body.text: na + artha-arthikāḥ pravrajitā guṇa-arthikā | mā vigraha kurvatha dusta-cittāḥ | na vo * asti kṣetraṃ na kṛṣir vaṇijyā | syur yasya arthāya prapañca ete ||
body.translated_text: 'Renunciants are not seekers of wealth but seekers of virtue. Do not engage in quarrels with corrupt minds! You have no fields, no farming, no trade — for whose sake would these proliferations be?'

body.text: na putra dhītā na ca vo * asti bhāryā | na ca + asya mitraṃ na ca bandhu-vargaḥ | dāsyo na dāsā na ca īśvaratvaṃ | mā vigrahaṃ kurvatha pravrajitvā ||
body.translated_text: 'You have no sons, no daughters, no wife; he has no friend, no group of relatives; no female servants, no male servants, no sovereignty. Do not engage in quarrels, having gone forth!'

body.text: kāṣāya-vastrāṇi gṛhītva śraddhayā | śānta-praśāntair hi niṣevitāni | śānta-praśāntā upaśānta bhotha | prapañca varjitva janetha kṣāntim ||
body.translated_text: 'Having taken up the ochre robes with faith — [robes] that are worn by the calm and tranquil — be calm, tranquil, and serene! Abandoning proliferation, generate patience!'

body.text: āśī-viṣān rakṣatha raudra-cittān | narakāś ca tiryag viṣayo yamasya | prapañca-cārasya na bhonti dūre | tasmād * dhi kṣāntau janayeta vīryam || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'Guard against the terribly-minded poisonous serpents! The hells, the animal realm, and the domain of <s>Yama</s> are not far from one who engages in proliferation. Therefore generate vigor in patience!' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: imena yogena labheta śuddhiṃ | kṣapayitva karma-āvaraṇaṃ a-śeṣaṃ | dharṣeti māraṃ sa-calaṃ sa-vāhanaṃ yo dhīru tasya + eva janeti kṣāntim | iti ||
body.translated_text: 'By this practice one obtains purity, having destroyed all <s>karmāvaraṇa</s> (karmic obstructions) without remainder. He vanquishes <s>Māra</s> together with his army and vehicles — whoever, being resolute, generates that very patience.'

body.text: saṃkṣepatas tatra + an-artha-vivarjanam uktaṃ | tasmāt tarhi maitreya bodhi-satva-yānikena kula-putreṇa vā kula-duhitrā vā paścimāyāṃ pañca-śatyāṃ sad-dharma-pralope vartamāne * a-kṣatana-an-upahatena svastinā parimoktu-kāmena sarva-karma-āvaraṇāni kṣapayitu-kāmena + a-saṃsarga-abhiratena bhavitavyam araṇya-vana-prānta-vāsinā + an-abhiyukta-satva-parivarjitena + ātma-skhalita-gaveṣiṇā para-skhalita-a-gaveṣiṇā tuṣṇī-bhāva-abhiratena prajñā-pāramitā-vihāra-abhiratena + iti ||
body.translated_text: In brief, the avoidance of harmful things is stated therein: 'Therefore, <s>Maitreya</s>, the son of good family or daughter of good family who follows the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle, in the final five-hundred-year period when the decline of the true <s>Dharma</s> is occurring, wishing to be liberated unharmed and uninjured, in safety, wishing to destroy all <s>karmāvaraṇas</s> (karmic obstructions) — should be one who delights in non-association, dwelling in forest and woodland borders, avoiding persons who are not devoted [to practice], seeking out one's own faults, not seeking out the faults of others, delighting in silence, delighting in the abiding of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.'

body.text: ārya-ratna-meghe * apy an-artha-varjanam uktaṃ | tāvat piṇḍāya carati yāvad asya kāryasya prāptir bhavati | anyatra yeṣu sthāneṣu caṇḍā vā kukkurās taruṇa-vatsā vā gāvaḥ prakṛti-duḥ-śīlā vā tiryag-yoni-gatā | viheṭhana-abhiprāyā vā strī-puruṣa-dāraka-dārikā jugupsitāni vā sthānāni | tāni sarveṇa sarvaṃ varjayati + iti ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Ratnamegha</s> also, the avoidance of harmful things is stated: 'He goes for alms only so long as the accomplishment of his purpose requires. But those places where there are fierce dogs, or cows with young calves, or naturally ill-tempered animals, or men, women, boys, and girls with harmful intent, or disgusting places — he avoids all of those entirely.'

body.text: anena + etad darśitaṃ bhavati yad dṛṣṭe * api bādhā-kara evaṃ-vidhe | tad a-varjayata āpattir bhavati + iti ||
body.translated_text: By this it is shown that even when harm of this kind is merely visible, not avoiding it constitutes a transgression.

body.text: atha yad evam-ādy an-artha-varjanam uktaṃ kena + etal labhyate sarva-niṣ-phala-syanda-varjanāt | phalam atra para-arthaṃ | tad-arthaṃ yaḥ syando na saṃvartate | sa niṣ-phalatvād varjayitavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Now, as the avoidance of harmful things of this kind has been stated — by what is it obtained? By avoiding all fruitless activity. The fruit here is the benefit of others. That activity which does not conduce to that purpose — it should be avoided as fruitless.

body.text: yathā candra-pradīpa-sūtre kāya-saṃvara-madhye paṭhyate | na hasta-lolupo bhavati na pāda-lolupaḥ hasta-pāda-saṃyata iti ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Candrapradīpasūtra</s>, in the section on bodily restraint: 'He is not restless with his hands, not restless with his feet — restrained in hands and feet.'

body.text: tathā daśa-dharmaka-sūtre * api deśitaṃ hasta-vikṣepaḥ pāda-vikṣepo * a-dhāvanaṃ paridhāvanaṃ laṅghanaṃ plavanam idam ucyate kāya-dauṣṭhulyam iti ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, in the <s>Daśadharmakasūtra</s> also it is taught: 'Flinging of the hands, flinging of the feet, not running, running about, jumping, leaping — this is called bodily restlessness.'

body.text: ārya-dharma-saṃgīti-sūtre tu yathā bodhi-satvānāṃ para-arthād anyat karma na kalpate | tathā spaṣṭam eva paridīpitaṃ yat kiñ-cid bhagavan bodhi-satvānāṃ kāya-karma yat kiñ-cid vāk-karma yat kiñ-cin manas-karma tat sarvaṃ satva-avekṣitaṃ pravartate mahā-karuṇā-adhipateyaṃ satva-hita-adhiṣṭhāna-nimittaṃ sarva-satva-hita-sukha-adhyāśaya-pravṛttaṃ | sa evaṃ hita-āśayaḥ evaṃ saṃjñī-bhavati | sa mayā pratipattiḥ pratipattavyayā sarva-satvānāṃ hita-āvahā sukha-āvahā ca || pe ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Dharmasaṃgīti-sūtra</s>, it is clearly illuminated that no action other than benefiting others is fitting for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: "Whatever bodily action of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, whatever verbal action, whatever mental action — all of that proceeds with regard for beings, under the sovereignty of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), motivated by the establishment of benefit for beings, proceeding from the intention of welfare and happiness for all beings. One of such benevolent intention thus conceives: 'That practice which is to be practiced by me should bring benefit and happiness to all beings.'" And so forth.

body.text: āyataneṣu śūnya-grāma-vat pratyavekṣaṇā pratipattiḥ | na ca + āyatana-parityāgaṃ spṛhayati + iti ||
body.translated_text: The practice is the contemplation of the sense-bases (<s>āyatanas</s>) as like an empty village; yet one does not desire the abandonment of the sense-bases.

body.text: ārya-gagana-gañja-sūtre * apy uktaṃ | tad yathā + api nāma chidrān mārutaḥ praviśati | evam eva yato yata eva cittasya chidraṃ bhavati tatas tata eva māro * avatāraṃ labhate | tasmāt sadā + a-chidra-cittena bodhi-satvena bhavitavyaṃ |tatra + iyam a-chidra-cittatā yad idaṃ sarva-ākāra-jñatāyāḥ śūnyatāyāḥ paripūrir iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Gaganagañja-sūtra</s> it is also said: "Just as wind enters through an opening, so wherever there is an opening in the mind, there <s>Māra</s> finds an entrance. Therefore, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should always maintain a mind without openings. Therein, this state of having a mind without openings is the fulfillment of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) in all its aspects."

body.text: kā punar iyaṃ sarva-ākāra-vara-upetā śūnyatā | yā + iyaṃ bodhi-satva-caryāyā a-parityāgena + abhyasyamānā | abhyastā vā | sarva-bhāva-śūnyatā | eṣā ca ratna-cūḍa-sūtre vistareṇa + ākhyātā ||
body.translated_text: What then is this <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) endowed with all excellent aspects? It is that which is practiced without abandoning the <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct, or which, having been practiced, is the emptiness of all existents. This is explained at length in the <s>Ratnacūḍa-sūtra</s>.

body.text: tathā + akṣayamati-sūtre * api darśitaṃ | pāpakānām a-kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prahāṇāya chandaṃ janayati + ity atra prastāve yāni ca + anyāni punaḥ kāni-cid anyāny api citta-vikṣepa-karāṇi yāni samādhi-skandhasya vipakṣāya saṃvartante | ayam ucyate samādhi-vipakṣaḥ | yāvad ime ucyante pāpakā a-kuśalā dharmā iti ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, in the <s>Akṣayamati-sūtra</s> it is also shown, in the context of the passage 'one generates zeal for the abandonment of evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>': "And whatever other things cause distraction of the mind and conduce to opposition against the aggregate of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) — this is called the opposition to <s>samādhi</s>. These are called evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>."

body.text: śikṣā-samuccaye śīla-pāramitāyām an-artha-vivarjanaṃ pañcamaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>, the fifth chapter on the avoidance of harm in the <s>Śīla-pāramitā</s> (perfection of moral discipline).

body.text: ātma-bhāva-rakṣā ṣaṣṭhaḥ paricchedaḥ | uktaṃ niṣ-phala-syanda-varjanaṃ | katham etat sidhyed ity āha | etat sidhyet sadā smṛtyā + iti ||
body.translated_text: The sixth chapter is on the protection of one's own being (<s>ātmabhāvarakṣā</s>). The avoidance of fruitless outflow has been stated. How is this to be accomplished? He says: "This is accomplished through constant <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness)."

body.text: dvādaśa + imāḥ smṛtayo niṣ-phala-syanda-varjanayā saṃvartante | yad uta | tathā-gata-ājñā-an-atikrama-anupālana-vipāka-gaurava-smṛtiḥ | sarva-kāyasya niś-cala-sva-bhāvatā-pratiṣṭhitatā-anusmṛtiḥ | sati satva-arthe yad aṅgam an-upayogi tad dṛḍhatara-smṛty-apekṣā-niś-cala-mādhya-chanda-para-āpattī-kṛtaṃ sarva-dhīra-ceṣṭā-smṛtiḥ | na ca + asya bhaya-utsava-ādi-saṃbandha-saṃbhrame * aṅga-mukta-smṛtiḥ | īryā-patha-catuṣka-ākṣepa-nirūpaṇa-smṛtiḥ | antara-antarā ca + īryā-patha-vikopa-ārakṣaṇa-artham īryā-patha-saṃpad-avalokana-smṛtiḥ | bhāṣaṇa-kāle ca + ati-prasāda-auddhatya-saṃrambha-pakṣa-pāta-ādi-vaśād ati-mātra-a-prāsādika-hasta-pāda-śiro-mukha-vikāra-niyamana-smṛtiḥ | yaḥ śrotā vaktavyaḥ sa yāvan-mātreṇa dhvaninā + arthaṃ jānāti | tad-an-atirekeṇa svareṇa bhāṣaṇa-smṛtir anyatra para-āśaṅkā-doṣa-saṃbhavāt | a-śikṣita-jana-samāgama-saṅkaṭe sva-citta-tac-citta-prasādana-ādi-tātparya-smṛtiḥ | citta-matta-dvi-pasya śamatha-stambhe nitya-baddha-smṛtiḥ | muhur muhuś ca citta-avasthā-pratyavekṣaṇā-smṛtiḥ | mahā-jana-saṃpātaṃ prāyo * anya-kārya-tyāgena + api yathā-ukta-smṛti-rakṣā-tātparya-smṛtir iti ||
body.translated_text: These twelve forms of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) conduce to the avoidance of fruitless outflow, namely: mindfulness of the gravity of the consequences of not transgressing the command of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; recollection of the immovable nature and stability of the entire body (<s>kāya</s>); when there is a purpose for beings, mindfulness of all steady conduct through firmness of mindfulness with respect to whatever limb is not being employed, attended by unwavering, balanced intention and vigilance against the faults of others; mindfulness of not releasing one's limbs in the confusion of fear, excitement, and the like; mindfulness of examining the four modes of deportment (<s>īryāpatha</s>); mindfulness of observing the proper conduct of deportment at intervals for the purpose of guarding against its disruption; mindfulness of restraining excessive gestures of hands, feet, head, and face during speech due to excessive approval, excitement, agitation, or partiality; mindfulness of speaking with a voice not exceeding the volume by which the listener can understand the meaning, except where there might arise the fault of suspicion in others; mindfulness of the purpose of pleasing one's own mind and the minds of others when in a gathering of untrained people; mindfulness constantly bound to the post of <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) for the wild elephant of the mind; mindfulness of repeatedly examining the state of the mind; and mindfulness of the purpose of guarding the aforementioned forms of mindfulness, even by abandoning other tasks, in a great assembly of people.

body.text: evam etābhiḥ smṛtibhir niṣ-phala-syandana-varjanaṃ sidhyati | sā ca smṛtis tīvra-ādarād bhavet | tatra + ādaraḥ kāryeṣu sarva-bhāvena + abhimukhyam | avajñā-prati-pakṣaḥ | ayaṃ ca + ādaraḥ śamatha-māhātmyaṃ jñātvā tātparyeṇa jāyate | kas tāvad ayaṃ śamo nāma | ya ārya-akṣayamati-sūtre śamatha uktaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus through these forms of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), the avoidance of fruitless outflow is accomplished. And that <s>smṛti</s> arises from intense earnestness (<s>ādara</s>). Therein, earnestness means wholeheartedly facing one's duties — it is the antidote to negligence. And this earnestness arises with dedication from knowing the greatness of <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility). What then is this <s>śamatha</s>? It is what is called <s>śamatha</s> in the <s>Ārya-Akṣayamati-sūtra</s>.

body.text: tatra katamā śamatha-a-kṣayatā | yā cittasya śāntir upaśāntir a-vikṣepa-kendriya-saṃyamaḥ | an-uddhatatā | an-unnahanatā a-capalatā a-cañcalatā saumyatā guptatā karmaṇyatā ājāneyatā eka-agratā eka-ārāmatā saṃgaṇikā-varjanatā viveka-ratiḥ kāya-vivekaś citta-a-vibhramo * araṇya-mukha-manasi-kāratā + alpa-icchatā | yāvad īryā-patha-guptiḥ kāla-jñatā samaya-jñatā mātra-jñatā mukti-jñatā | su-bharatā su-poṣatā + ity-ādi ||
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the inexhaustibility of <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility)? It is the peace of mind, its pacification, non-distraction, sense-restraint (<s>indriyasaṃyama</s>), non-agitation, non-conceit, non-fickleness, non-restlessness, gentleness, self-guardedness, workableness, tractability, one-pointedness, delight in solitude, avoidance of company, joy in seclusion, bodily seclusion, non-confusion of mind, mental orientation toward the wilderness, fewness of desires; up to: guarding of deportment, knowledge of the proper time, knowledge of the occasion, knowledge of the measure, knowledge of liberation, being easy to support, being easy to maintain, and so forth.

body.text: kiṃ punar asya śamasya māhātmyaṃ yathā-bhūta-jñāna-janana-śaktiḥ | yasmāt samāhito yathā-bhūtaṃ prajānāti + ity avadan muniḥ ||
body.translated_text: What then is the greatness of this <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility)? It is the power to generate knowledge of things as they truly are (<s>yathābhūta-jñāna</s>). For the <s>Muni</s> (the Sage) has said: "One who is concentrated knows things as they truly are."

body.text: yathā + uktaṃ dharma-saṃgītau | samāhita-manaso yathā-bhūta-darśanaṃ bhavati | yathā-bhūta-darśino bodhi-satvasya satveṣu mahā-karuṇā pravartate | evaṃ ca + asya bhavati | idaṃ mayā samādhi-mukhaṃ sarva-dharma-yathā-bhūta-darśanaṃ ca sarva-satvānāṃ niṣpādayitavyaṃ | sa tayā mahā-karuṇayā saṃcodyamāno * adhi-śīlam adhi-cittam adhi-prajñaṃ ca śikṣāṃ paripūryāṃ caturāṃ samyak-saṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyate | tasmān mayā śīla-su-sthitana-a-prakampena + a-śithilena bhavitavyam iti | idaṃ śamatha-māhātmyam ātmanaḥ pareṣāṃ ca + an-anta-apāya-ādi-duḥkha-samatikrama-an-anta-laukika-loka-uttara-sukha-saṃpat-prakarṣa-pāra-prāpty-ātmakam avagamya tad-abhilāṣeṇa + ātāpo bhāvayitavyaḥ | ādīpta-gṛha-anta-gatena + iva śītala-jala-abhilāṣiṇā | tena tīvra ādaro bhavati śikṣāsu | tena + api smṛtir upatiṣṭhati | upasthita-smṛtir niṣ-phalaṃ varjayati | yaś ca niṣ-phalaṃ varjayati tasya + an-arthā na saṃbhavanti | tasmād ātma-bhāvaṃ rakṣitu-kāmena smṛti-mūlam anviṣya nityam upasthita-smṛtinā bhavitavyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Dharmasaṃgīti</s>: "For one whose mind is concentrated, there is seeing of things as they truly are. For a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who sees things as they truly are, great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) toward beings arises. And thus he thinks: 'I must bring about for all beings this gateway of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and the seeing of all <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are.' Impelled by that great compassion, he fulfills the training in higher morality (<s>adhiśīla</s>), higher mind (<s>adhicitta</s>), and higher wisdom (<s>adhiprajñā</s>), and attains supreme perfect awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Therefore I must be well-established in <s>śīla</s> (moral discipline), unshakable and unslackening." This greatness of <s>śamatha</s> — understanding it to consist in the transcendence of the endless suffering of lower rebirths and the attainment of the supreme culmination of endless worldly and supramundane happiness, for oneself and others — one should cultivate ardor through longing for it, like one inside a burning house longing for cool water. From that arises intense earnestness in the trainings. From that, <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) becomes established. One with established mindfulness avoids the fruitless. And for one who avoids the fruitless, misfortunes do not arise. Therefore, one who wishes to protect one's own being, having sought the root of <s>smṛti</s>, should always remain with established mindfulness.

body.text: ata eva + ugra-paripṛcchāyāṃ gṛhiṇaṃ bodhi-satvam adhikṛtya + uktaṃ | surā-maireya-madya-pramāda-sthānāt prativiratena bhavitavyam a-mattena + an-unmattena + a-capalena + a-cañcalena + a-saṃbhrāntena + a-mukhareṇa + an-unnaḍena + an-uddhatena + upasthiti-smṛti-saṃprajanyena + iti ||
body.translated_text: For this very reason, in the <s>Ugra-paripṛcchā</s>, with reference to the householder <s>Bodhisattva</s>, it is said: "One should abstain from the basis of heedlessness that is liquor, spirits, and intoxicants; one should be non-intoxicated, non-deranged, non-fickle, non-restless, non-confused, non-garrulous, non-conceited, non-agitated, and endowed with established <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) and <s>saṃprajanya</s> (clear comprehension)."

body.text: atra + eva ca pravrajita-bodhi-satvam adhikṛtya + uktaṃ smṛti-saṃprajanyasya + a-vikṣepa iti ||
body.translated_text: And in this very context, with reference to the renunciant <s>Bodhisattva</s>, it is said: "Non-distraction of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) and <s>saṃprajanya</s> (clear comprehension)."

body.text: tatra smṛtiḥ ārya-ratna-cūḍa-sūtre * abhihitā | yayā smṛtyā sarva-kleśānāṃ prādur-bhāvo na bhavati | yayā smṛtyā sarva-māra-karmaṇām avatāraṃ na dadāti | yayā smṛtyā utpathe vā ku-mārge vā na patati | yayā smṛtyā dauvārika-bhūtayā sarveṣām a-kuśalānāṃ citta-caitasikānāṃ dharmāṇām avakāśaṃ dadāti + iyam ucyate samyak-smṛtir iti ||
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is described in the <s>Ārya-Ratnacūḍa-sūtra</s>: "That mindfulness by which the arising of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) does not occur; that mindfulness by which one does not give entrance to any of <s>Māra's</s> deeds; that mindfulness by which one does not fall into a wrong path or an evil road; that mindfulness which, standing as a gatekeeper, gives no opportunity to any unwholesome mental and associated <s>dharmas</s> — this is called right mindfulness (<s>samyak-smṛti</s>)."

body.text: saṃprajanyaṃ tu prajñā-pāramitāyām uktaṃ | caraṃś carāmi + iti prajān-ti | sthitaḥ sthito * asmi + iti prajānāti | śayanaḥ śayita iti prajānāti | niṣaṇṇo niṣaṇṇo * asmi + iti prajānāti | yathā yathā ca + asyaḥ

children.text: kāyaḥ sthito bhavati tathā tathā + eva prajānāti ||
children.translated_text: body is positioned, one clearly knows it accordingly.

body.translated_text: Clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajanya</s>), however, is described in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>: "When walking, one clearly knows 'I am walking'; when standing, one clearly knows 'I am standing'; when lying down, one clearly knows 'I am lying down'; when sitting, one clearly knows 'I am sitting'; and in whatever way one's

body.text: pe||
body.translated_text: And so forth.

body.text: so * atikrāman vā pratikrāman vā saṃprajānaṃś cārī bhavati | ālokite vilokite saṃmiñjite prasārite saṃghāṭī-paṭṭa-pātra-cīvara-dhāraṇe | aśite pīte khādite nidrā-klama-prativinodane āgate gate sthite niṣaṇṇe supte jāgarite bhāṣite tuṣṇī-bhāve pratisaṃlayane saṃprajānaṃś cārī bhavati + iti ||
body.translated_text: "Whether going forward or turning back, one acts with clear comprehension; in looking ahead and looking around, in bending and stretching, in wearing the outer robe, the inner robe, and carrying the bowl and robes; in eating, drinking, chewing, in dispelling drowsiness and fatigue; in coming, going, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, being silent, and in meditation — one acts with clear comprehension."

body.text: śīlaṃ hi samādhi-saṃvartanīyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: For <s>śīla</s> (moral discipline) conduces to <s>samādhi</s> (concentration).

body.text: yathā + uktaṃ candra-pradīpa-sūtre | kṣipraṃ samādhiṃ labhate nir-aṅgaṇaṃ | viśuddha-śīle * asminn ānuśaṃsa iti ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Candrapradīpa-sūtra</s>: "One quickly attains <s>samādhi</s> that is free from defilement — this is the benefit of pure <s>śīla</s> (moral discipline)."

body.text: ato * avagamyate ye ke-cit samādhi-hetavaḥ prayogās te śīla-antar-gatā iti | tasmāt samādhy-arthinā smṛti-saṃprajanya-śīlena bhavitavyaṃ | tathā śīla-arthinā + api samādhau yatnaḥ kāryaḥ tatra + eva sūtre vacanāt | dhyāna-anuśaṃseṣu hi paṭhyate | na + asau bhoti an-ācāro ācāro su-pratiṣṭhitaḥ | go-care carate yogī vivarjeti a-gocaraṃ ||
body.translated_text: From this it is understood that whatever practices are causes of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), they are included within <s>śīla</s> (moral discipline). Therefore, one who seeks <s>samādhi</s> should be endowed with <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), <s>saṃprajanya</s> (clear comprehension), and <s>śīla</s>. Likewise, one who seeks <s>śīla</s> should also make effort in <s>samādhi</s>, as stated in that very sūtra. For among the benefits of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) it is recited: "Such a one is not of bad conduct; one's conduct is well-established. The <s>yogī</s> (practitioner) moves in the proper domain and avoids the improper domain."

body.text: niṣ-paridāha-vihārī gupta indriya-saṃvṛta | iti ||
body.translated_text: "One dwells without burning, guarded, with senses restrained."

body.text: etābhyāṃ ca śīla-samādhibhyām anyo-nya-saṃvardhana-karābhyāṃ citta-karma-pariniṣpattiḥ etāvatī ca + iyaṃ bodhi-satva-śikṣā yad uta citta-parikarma | etan-mūlatvāt sarva-satva-arthānāṃ ||
body.translated_text: And through these two — <s>śīla</s> (moral discipline) and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) — which mutually enhance each other, the perfection of the work of the mind is accomplished. And this entire training of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is nothing but the purification of the mind (<s>citta-parikarma</s>), since it is the root of all purposes for beings.

body.text: uktaṃ hy ārya-ratna-meghe | citta-pūrvaṅ-gamāś ca sarva-dharmāḥ | citte parijñāte sarva-dharmāḥ parijñātā bhavanti | api tu cittena nīyate lokaḥ cittaṃ cittaṃ na paśyati | cittena cīyate karma śubhaṃ vā yadi vā + a-śubham ||
body.translated_text: For it is said in the <s>Ārya-Ratnamegha</s>: "All <s>dharmas</s> are preceded by the mind. When the mind is fully understood, all <s>dharmas</s> are fully understood. Moreover, the world is led by the mind; the mind does not see the mind. By the mind is accumulated <s>karma</s> (action), whether wholesome or unwholesome."

body.text: cittaṃ bhramate * alāta-vat | cittaṃ bhramate turaṅ-ga-vat | cittaṃ dahate deva-agni-vat | cittaṃ harate mahā-ambu-vat ||
body.translated_text: "The mind whirls like a firebrand; the mind gallops like a horse; the mind burns like a forest fire; the mind carries away like a great flood."

body.text: sa evaṃ vyupaparīkṣamāṇaś citte su-upasthita-smṛtir viharati na cittasya vaśaṃ gacchati | ap tu cittam eva + asya vaśaṃ gacchati | cittena + asya vaśī-bhūtena sarva-dharmā vaśī-bhavanti + iti ||
body.translated_text: "Thus examining, one dwells with well-established <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) regarding the mind; one does not come under the power of the mind. Rather, the mind comes under one's own power. When the mind has been brought under control, all <s>dharmas</s> come under one's control."

body.text: tathā + ārya-dharma-saṅgīti-sūtre * apy uktaṃ | mati-vikramo bodhi-satva āha | yo * ayaṃ dharmo dharma ity ucyate na + ayaṃ dharmo deśa-stho na pradeśa-stho * anyatra sva-citta-adhīno dharmaḥ tasmān mayā sva-cittaṃ sv-ārādhitaṃ sv-adhiṣṭhitaṃ su-samārabdhaṃ su-nigṛhītaṃ kartavyaṃ | tat kasya hetoḥ | yatra cittaṃ tatra guṇa-doṣāḥ | na + asti niś-cittatāyāṃ guṇa-doṣaḥ | tatra bodhi-satvo doṣebhyaś cittaṃ nivārya guṇeṣu pravartayati ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, in the <s>Ārya-Dharmasaṅgīti-sūtra</s> it is also said: "The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mativikrama</s> said: 'This thing called <s>dharma</s> — this <s>dharma</s> is not located in any place or region; rather, <s>dharma</s> is dependent on one's own mind. Therefore I must make my own mind well-controlled, well-governed, well-undertaken, and well-restrained. For what reason? Because where there is mind, there are virtues and faults. In the absence of mind, there are no virtues or faults. Therein, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> turns the mind away from faults and directs it toward virtues.'"

body.text: tad ucyate | citta-adhīno dharmo dharma-adhīnā bodhir iti ||
body.translated_text: It is therefore said: "<s>Dharma</s> depends on the mind; awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) depends on <s>dharma</s>."

body.text: ayaṃ bhagavan dharmaṃ samādānaḥ sukha-abhisaṃbodhāya saṃvartatae iti ||
body.translated_text: "This, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, is the undertaking of <s>dharma</s> that conduces to the ease of full awakening."

body.text: ārya-gaṇḍa-vyūha-sūtre * api varṇitaṃ | sva-citta-adhiṣṭhānaṃ sarva-bodhi-satva-caryā sva-citta-adhiṣṭhānaṃ sarva-satva-paripāka-vinayaḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Gaṇḍavyūha-sūtra</s> it is also described: "The governance of one's own mind is the entire conduct of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>; the governance of one's own mind is the ripening and discipline of all beings." And so forth.

body.text: tasya mama kula-putra + evaṃ bhavati | sva-cittam eva + upastambhayitavyaṃ sarva-kuśala-mūlaiḥ | sva-cittam eva + abhiṣyandayitavyaṃ dharma-meghaiḥ | sva-cittam eva pariśodhayitavyam āvaraṇāya dharmebhyaḥ | sva-cittam eva dṛḍhī-kartavyaṃ vīryeṇa + ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: He thinks thus, O son of good family: 'One's own mind alone is to be supported by all wholesome roots; one's own mind alone is to be suffused with the clouds of <s>Dharma</s>; one's own mind alone is to be purified from obstructive <s>dharmas</s>; one's own mind alone is to be made firm through vigor,' and so forth.

body.text: tathā + atra + eva māyā-devy--a-darśana-ākulī-bhūte ārya-sudhane ratna-netrāyā nagara-devatāyās tad-darśana-artham iyam anuśāsanī | citta-nagara-paripālana-kuśalena te kula-putra bhavitavyaṃ sarva-saṃsāra-viṣaya-raty-a-saṃvasanatayā | citta-nagara-alaṃ-kāra-prayuktena te kula-putra bhavitavyaṃ daśa-tathā-gata-bala-adhyālambanatayā | citta-nagara-pariśodhana-prayuktena te kula-putra bhavitavyam īrṣyā-mātsarya-śāṭhya-apanayanatayā | citta-nagara-vivardhana-abhiyuktena te kula-putra bhavitavyaṃ sarva-jñatā-saṃbhāra-mahā-vīrya-vega-vivardhanatayā | citta-nagara-dur-yodhana-dur-āsadatā-abhinirhāra-prayuktena te kula-putra bhavitavyaṃ sarva-kleśa-māra-kāyika-pāpa-mitra-māra-cakra-an-avamardanatayā | citta-nagara-pravistaraṇa-prayuktena te kula-putra bhavitavyaṃ mahā-maitrī-sarva-jagat-sphuraṇatayā | citta-nagara-praticchādana-prayuktena te kula-putra bhavitavyaṃ vipula-dharma-cchatra-sarva-a-kuśala-dharma-pratipakṣa-abhinirharaṇatayā | citta-nagara-vivaraṇa-prayuktena te kula-putra bhavitavyaṃ ādhyātmika-bāhya-vastu sarva-jagat-saṃprāpaṇatayā | citta-nagara-dṛḍha-sthāma-abhinirhara-prayuktena te kula-putra bhavitavyaṃ sarva-a-kuśala-dharma-sva-santaty-a-vasanatayā | yāvad evaṃ citta-nagara-viśuddhy-abhiyuktena kula-putra bodhi-satvena śakyaṃ sarva-kuśala-mūla-samārjanam anuprāptuṃ | tat kasya hetoḥ | tathā hi tasya bodhi-satvasya + evaṃ citta-nagara-pariśuddhaysa sarva-āvaraṇāni purato na saṃtiṣṭhante | buddha-darśana-āvaraṇaṃ vā dharma-śravaṇa-āvaraṇaṃ vā + ity ādi | tasmād vyavasthitam evaṃ | citta-parikarma + eva bodhi-satva-śikṣā + iti | tac ca + a-capala-cetasaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, in this same [sūtra], when the noble <s>Sudhana</s> was distressed at not seeing <s>Māyā Devī</s>, the city-goddess <s>Ratnanetrā</s> gave him this instruction for the purpose of seeing her: 'You should, O son of good family, be skilled in guarding the city of the mind, through not dwelling in delight in the objects of all <s>saṃsāra</s>. You should, O son of good family, be engaged in adorning the city of the mind, through relying on the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. You should, O son of good family, be engaged in purifying the city of the mind, through removing envy, jealousy, and hypocrisy. You should, O son of good family, be devoted to expanding the city of the mind, through increasing the great vigorous energy of the accumulations of omniscience. You should, O son of good family, be engaged in making the city of the mind unconquerable and unapproachable, through not being crushed by the armies of all afflictions, <s>Māra</s>, evil bodily friends, and <s>Māra</s>'s hosts. You should, O son of good family, be engaged in extending the city of the mind, through pervading all the world with great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>). You should, O son of good family, be engaged in sheltering the city of the mind, through producing the great umbrella of <s>Dharma</s> as the antidote to all unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>. You should, O son of good family, be engaged in opening the city of the mind, through making all the world attain both inner and outer things. You should, O son of good family, be engaged in producing firm strength in the city of the mind, through not allowing any unwholesome <s>dharma</s> to dwell in one's own continuum.' And so on: 'Thus, O son of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s> devoted to the purification of the city of the mind is able to attain the accumulation of all wholesome roots. Why? For indeed, when the city of the mind of that <s>bodhisattva</s> is thus purified, no obstructions stand before him — neither obstructions to seeing the <s>Buddha</s> nor obstructions to hearing the <s>Dharma</s>,' and so forth. Therefore it is established thus: the training of the mind (<s>citta-parikarma</s>) alone is the <s>bodhisattva</s> training. And that [belongs to one] whose mind is not fickle.

body.text: śamāc ca na calec cittaṃ bāhya-ceṣṭā-nivartanāt ||
body.translated_text: And the mind should not waver from calm (<s>śama</s>), through the cessation of outward activities.

body.text: a-saṃprajanya-para-tantrasya muṣita-smṛteś ca cittaṃ calati samīhitād ālambanād anyatra nīyamānatvāt | yadā tu smṛti-saṃprajanyena bāhyāś ceṣṭā nivartitā bhavanti tadā tad-vaśatvād ekasminn ālambane nibaddhaṃ yāvad iṣyate tāvat tiṣṭhati | tataś ca pūrva-vad anuśaṃsa-vistaraḥ | adyatve * api ca satva-artha-kṣamo bhavaty eva prasāda-karatvāt | kathaṃ ||
body.translated_text: For one who is under the control of non-awareness (<s>asaṃprajanya</s>) and whose mindfulness is impaired, the mind wavers — since it is led away from its intended object elsewhere. But when outward activities have been restrained by mindfulness and awareness, then, being under [their] control, the mind, bound to a single object, remains as long as one wishes. And from that, the enumeration of benefits follows as before. And even in the present, one becomes capable of benefiting beings, by being one who inspires faith. How?

body.text: sarvatra + a-capala-manda-mita-snigdha-abhibhāṣaṇāt | āvarjayej janaṃ bhavyam ādeyaś ca + api jāyate ||
body.translated_text: By speech that is everywhere steady, gentle, measured, and affectionate, one wins over suitable people, and one becomes esteemed.

body.text: etad eva ca bodhi-satvasya kṛtyam yad uta satva-a-varjanaṃ | yathā + ārya-dharma-saṃgīti-sūtre | ārya-priyadarśena bodhi-satvena paridīpitaṃ | tathā tathā bhagavan bodhi-satvena pratipattavyaṃ yat saha-darśanena + eva satvāḥ prasīdeyuḥ | tat kasmād * dhetoḥ | na bhagavan bodhi-satvasya + anyat karaṇīyam asty anyatra satva-a-varjanāt | satva-paripāka eva + iyaṃ bhagavan bodhi-satvasya dharma-saṃgītir iti ||
body.translated_text: And this alone is the task of a <s>bodhisattva</s> — namely, winning over beings. As in the <s>Ārya-Dharmasaṃgīti Sūtra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Ārya-Priyadarśana</s> explained: 'The <s>bodhisattva</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, should practice in such a way that beings are inspired with faith at the very sight [of him]. Why? For the <s>bodhisattva</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, has no other task than winning over beings. This ripening of beings alone, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Dharma</s>-assembly.'

body.text: evaṃ punar a-kriyamāṇe ko doṣa ity āha | an-ādeyaṃ tu taṃ lokaḥ paribhūya jina-aṅkuraṃ | bhasma-channo yathā vahniḥ pacyeta naraka-ādiṣu ||
body.translated_text: And when [one does] not act thus, what is the fault? [Śāntideva] says: But the world, having disregarded the unesteemed one — that sprout of the <s>Jina</s> — like a fire covered by ashes, will be cooked in the hells and so forth.

body.text: yathā prāg upadarśitaṃ ||
body.translated_text: As was shown previously.

body.text: yena ca + asya paribhava evam an-artho ratna-meghe jinena + uktas tena saṃkṣepa-saṃvaraḥ |yena + a-prasādaḥ satvānāṃ tad yatnena vivarjayed iti ||
body.translated_text: And since this contempt brings such harm [to beings], as stated by the <s>Jina</s> in the <s>Ratnamegha</s>, therefore the summary restraint is: 'Whatever causes the lack of faith of beings — that one should diligently avoid.'

body.text: yathā + āha | katame ca te bodhi-satva-samudācārāḥ | yāvad iha bodhi-satvo na + a-sthāne viharati na + a-kāle | na + a-kāla-bhāṇī bhavati na + a-kāla-jño bhavati na + a-deśa-jño bhavati | yato nidānam asya + antike satvā a-prasādaṃ prativedayeyuḥ | sa sarva-satva-anurakṣayā | ātmanaś ca bodhi-saṃbhāra-paripūraṇa-arthaṃ saṃpanna-īryā-patho bhavati mṛdu-bhāṇī manda-bhāṇī | a-saṃsarga-bahulaḥ | praviveka-abhimukhaḥ | su-prasanna-mukha iti ||
body.translated_text: As it says: 'And what are the conducts of a <s>bodhisattva</s>? [Among other things,] here a <s>bodhisattva</s> does not dwell in an improper place, nor at an improper time; he does not speak at an improper time, nor is he ignorant of the proper time, nor is he ignorant of the proper place — so that beings would not experience a lack of faith toward him. He, out of care for all beings, and for the purpose of completing his own accumulations of awakening (<s>bodhisaṃbhāra</s>), is endowed with proper deportment, speaks gently and softly, is mostly without worldly associations, is inclined toward seclusion, and has a very serene face.'

body.text: ata eva dharma-saṃgīti-sūtre deśitaṃ | yaḥ satvān rakṣati sa śīlaṃ rakṣati + iti | anayā kanīyena mātṛ-grāmeṇa saha raho-avasthā-ādiṣu loka-rakṣā ca kṛtā syāt | evaṃ bhogyeṣu jala-sthaleṣu mūtra-purīṣa-śleṣma-pūya-ādīnāṃ kutsitānāṃ rahasy a-rahasi ca + utsargaṃ na kuryād deva-manuṣya-citta-rakṣā-arthaṃ ||
body.translated_text: For this very reason it is taught in the <s>Dharmasaṃgīti Sūtra</s>: 'He who protects beings protects moral conduct.' And by this [principle], with regard to the youngest women, seclusion and other [potentially compromising situations] would [constitute] the guarding of worldly [opinion]. Likewise, in places of enjoyment, on water and on land, one should not discharge urine, excrement, phlegm, pus, and other repulsive [substances], whether in private or in public — for the sake of protecting the minds of gods and humans.

body.text: sad-dharma-smṛty-upasthāne ca raha utsiṣṭaṃ kṛtvā + an-utsiṣṭa-āhāreṣv a-dadataḥ preta-gatiḥ paṭhyate ||
body.translated_text: And in the <s>Saddharmasm​ṛtyupasthāna</s>, it is read that for one who, having discharged waste in private, does not wash [before] giving [food] that has not been wasted, the <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost) destiny [results].

body.text: tathā bodhi-satva-prātimokṣe * apy a-prasāda-parihāra uktaḥ | na purato danta-kāṣṭhaṃ khāditavyaṃ na purataḥ kheṭe nikṣiptavya iti | eṣa ca gaurava-lajjā-vidhiḥ sarva-draṣṭavyo na brahma-cāriṣv eva | atra tu sūtre brahma-cāry--adhikāraḥ teṣu gurutara-āpatti-bhaya-saṃdarśana-arthaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, in the <s>Bodhisattva-prātimokṣa</s> too, the avoidance of [causing] lack of faith is taught: 'One should not chew a tooth-stick in front of [others]; one should not spit in front of [others].' And this rule of reverence and modesty is to be observed toward all, not just toward fellow celibates. But in this <s>sūtra</s>, the section pertains to fellow celibates, for the purpose of showing that toward them the fault of transgression is even more serious.

body.text: yathā + atra + eva + āha | na + uccair-bhāṣiṇā bhavitavyam iti ||
body.translated_text: As it also says here: 'One should not be a loud speaker.'

body.text: na ca + ayaṃ vidhiḥ prādeśikaḥ | tathā brahma-paripṛcchāyām apy uktaṃ na ca vadha-sadṛśena bodhi-satvena bhavitavyam iti | tathā prātimokṣād api loka-a-prasāda-karam anveṣya varjanīyaṃ | tan na tāvad ||
body.translated_text: And this rule is not limited [to one context]. Likewise, in the <s>Brahmaparipṛcchā</s> it is also said: 'A <s>bodhisattva</s> should not be like a slayer.' Likewise, from the <s>prātimokṣa</s> too, having searched out what causes the lack of faith of the world, one should avoid it. Therefore, at least [this much should be observed]:

body.text: mukha-pūraṃ na bhuñjīta sa-śabdaṃ prasṛta-ānanaḥ | pralamba-pādaṃ na + āsīta na bāhuṃ mardayet samam ||
body.translated_text: One should not eat with the mouth full, noisily, with the face stretched forward; one should not sit with legs dangling, nor should one rub both arms together.

body.text: evaṃ svayam apy utprekṣya dṛṣṭvā śrutvā ca loka-a-prasādaṃ rakṣeta | a-prasāda-kara-vacana-varjanaṃ tu na su-karam iti smaraṇa-bodhana-artham upadarśyate | ārya-sāgaramati-sūtre deśitaṃ | na + avalīna-vacano bhavati | na vyavakīrṇa-vacanaḥ | na + avasyandana-vacanaḥ | na + ujjvālana-vacanaḥ | na rāga-anunīta-vacanaḥ | na prākṛta-vacanaḥ | na + a-saṃrakṣita-vacanaḥ | na vyāpāda-saṃdhukṣaṇa-vacanaḥ | na cañcala-vacanaḥ | na capala-vacanaḥ | na raṭa-raṅga-vacanaḥ | na mukha-sākṣy--avaropaṇa-vacano bhavati + iti ||
body.translated_text: Thus, even by inferring for oneself, and by seeing and hearing what causes the world's lack of faith, one should guard [against it]. But since avoiding speech that causes lack of faith is not easy, [the following] is shown for the purpose of reminding and awakening [attention]. In the <s>Ārya-Sāgaramati Sūtra</s> it is taught: 'He is not one of withdrawn speech, nor one of scattered speech, nor one of insinuating speech, nor one of inflammatory speech, nor one whose speech is led by passion, nor one of vulgar speech, nor one of unguarded speech, nor one whose speech fans hatred, nor one of wavering speech, nor one of frivolous speech, nor one of noisy theatrical speech, nor one who imputes the testimony of the face [to others].'

body.text: ārya-tathā-gata-guhya-sūtre * apy āha | na khalu punaḥ kula-putra bodhi-satvasya vāg raktā vā duṣṭā vā mūḍhā vā kliṣṭā vā | kṣuṇṇa-vyākaraṇā vā sva-pakṣa-utkarṣaṇa-vacanā vā | para-pakṣa-nigraha-vacanā vā | ātma-varṇa-anunaya-vacanā vā | para-varṇa-pratigha-vacanā vā | pratijñā-uttāraṇa-vacanā vā | ābhimānika-vyākaraṇa-vacanā vā + iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Tathāgataguhya Sūtra</s> it also says: 'Moreover, O son of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s>'s speech is not colored by passion, nor by hatred, nor by delusion, nor by affliction; it is not of confused exposition, nor speech that exalts one's own side, nor speech that defeats the other's side, nor speech that praises one's own virtues, nor speech hostile to the virtues of others, nor speech that refutes a thesis, nor speech that proclaims with conceit.'

body.text: ārya-daśa-bhūmaka-sūtre * apy uktaṃ | yā + iyaṃ vāga-mano-jñā sva-santāna-para-santāna-vināśanī tathā-rūpāṃ vācaṃ prahāya | yā + iyaṃ vāk snigdhā mṛdvī mano-jñā madhurā priya-karaṇī mana-apakaraṇī

children.text: hita-karaṇī karṇa-sukhā hṛdayaṃ-gamā premaṇī varṇa-viṣpaṣṭā vijñeyā śravaṇīyā a-niśritā bahu-jana-kāntā bahu-jana-priyā bahu-jana-mana-āpā
children.translated_text: 'conducive to welfare, pleasing to the ear, going to the heart, loving, clear in expression, intelligible, worth hearing, not dependent, desired by many people, dear to many people, agreeable to many people,'

children.text: vijña-praśastā sarva-satva-hita-sukha-āvahā mana-utplāva-karī manaḥ-prahlādana-karī sva-para-santāna-pramodana-karī rāga-dveṣa-moha-sarva-kleśa-āpraśāmanī tathā-rūpāṃ vācaṃ niścārayati | yāvad itihāsa-pūrvakam api vacanaṃ parihārya pariharati + iti ||
children.translated_text: 'praised by the wise, bringing welfare and happiness to all beings, causing elation of mind, causing delight to the mind, causing joy to one's own and others' continuum, pacifying attachment, hatred, delusion, and all afflictions — such speech he utters. He avoids and refrains from speech that even has the character of legend,' and so forth.

body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Daśabhūmaka Sūtra</s> it is also said: 'Having abandoned that speech which, though pleasant, destroys one's own and others' continuum — that speech which is affectionate, gentle, pleasant, sweet, endearing, pleasing to the mind,'

body.text: ārya-gagana-gañja-sūtre tu + uktaṃ | guru-vacana-an-avamardanatayā | para-vacana-an-ācchindanatayā ca + ādeya-grāhya-vacano bhavati + iti ||
body.translated_text: But in the <s>Ārya-Gaganagañja Sūtra</s> it is said: 'Through not disregarding the words of teachers, and through not interrupting the words of others, one becomes esteemed and trusted in speech.'

body.text: dharma-saṃgīti-sūtre * apy uktaṃ | gaganagañjo bodhi-satva āha | na bodhi-satvena + eṣā vāg bhāṣitavyā yayā + a-paro vyāpadyeta | na sā vāg bhāṣitavyā yayā + a-paraṃ tāpayet | na bodhi-satvena sā vāg bhāṣitavyā yat paro jānīyāt | na sā vāg bhāṣitavyā yayā + arthā nir-arthā | na bodhi-satvena sā vāg bhāṣitavyā yayā na vidyām utpādayet | na sā vāg bhāṣitavyā yā satvānāṃ na hṛdayaṃ-gamā na paurī na karṇa-sukhā na sā vāg bhāṣitavyā + iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Dharmasaṃgīti Sūtra</s> it is also said: 'The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Gaganagañja</s> said: "A <s>bodhisattva</s> should not speak that speech by which another would be harmed. He should not speak that speech by which another would be distressed. A <s>bodhisattva</s> should not speak that speech which another would [merely] know [but not benefit from]. He should not speak that speech by which the meaning becomes meaningless. A <s>bodhisattva</s> should not speak that speech by which he does not generate knowledge. He should not speak that speech which does not go to the hearts of beings, which is not urbane, which is not pleasant to the ear."'

body.text: saṃkṣepatas tu para-a-prasāda-rakṣā ārya-sāgaramati-sūtre deśitā | a-para eka dharmo mahā-yāna-saṃgrahāya saṃvartate sva-skhalita-pratyavekṣaṇatayā sarva-satva-anurakṣā + iti ||
