body.translated_text: In summary, the guarding against causing others' lack of faith is taught in the <s>Ārya-Sāgaramati Sūtra</s>: 'Another single <s>dharma</s> conduces to the embrace of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — the care of all beings through observing one's own faults.'

body.text: eṣā rakṣā + ātma-bhāvasya | yathā + a-parair na nāśyeta | yathā na parān na nāśayet | asya tu grantha-vistarasya + ayaṃ piṇḍa-artho bodhi-satvena manasā nityaṃ dhārayitavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: This is the protection of one's own body — [both] so that one is not destroyed by others, and so that one does not destroy others. And the essential meaning of this extensive text is to be constantly held in mind by the <s>bodhisattva</s>:

body.text: su-niś-calaṃ su-prasannaṃ dhīraṃ sa-ādara-gauravaṃ | sa-lajjaṃ sa-bhayaṃ śāntaṃ para-ārādhana-tat-param ||
body.translated_text: Very steady, very serene, resolute, with respect and reverence, with modesty, with fear [of wrongdoing], peaceful, intent upon pleasing others —

body.text: ātma-satva-vaśaṃ nityam an-avadyeṣu vastuṣu | nirmāṇam iva nir-mānaṃ dhārayāmy eṣa mānasam | iti ||
body.translated_text: 'I shall always hold this mind, in blameless matters, [as] subject to myself and to [all] beings, like a magical creation, free from pride.' Thus.

body.text: kim etāvatī ātma-bhāva-rakṣā | na hi | kiṃ tarhi bhaiṣajya-vasana-ādibhiḥ saha | tatra dvi-vidhaṃ bhaiṣajyaṃ | satata-bhaiṣajyaṃ glāna-pratyaya-bhaiṣajyaṃ ca | tatra satata-bhaiṣajyam adhikṛtya + ārya-ratna-meghe * abhihitaṃ | tasmāt piṇḍa-pātrād ekaṃ praty-aṃśaṃ sa-brahma-cāriṇāṃ sthāpayati | dvitīyaṃ duṣkhitānāṃ tṛtīyaṃ vinipatitānāṃ caturtham ātmanā paribhuṅkte | paribhuñjāno na raktaḥ paribhuṅkte a-sakto * a-gṛddho * an-adhyavasitaḥ | anyatra yāvad eva kāyasya sthitaye | yāpanāyai | tathā paribhuṅkte yathā na + ati-saṃlikhito bhavati | na + ati-guru-kāyaḥ | tat kasya hetoḥ | ati-saṃlikhito hi kuśala-pakṣa-parāṅ-mukho bhavati | ati-guru-kāyo middha-avaṣṭabdho bhavati | tena taṃ piṇḍa-pātaṃ paribhujya kuśala-pakṣa-abhimukhena bhavitavyam ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: Is this the extent of the protection of one's own body? No indeed. What then? It includes medicine, clothing, and the like. Therein, medicine is twofold: regular medicine and medicine for illness. Regarding regular medicine, in the <s>Ārya-Ratnamegha</s> it is stated: 'Therefore, from the alms-food, he sets aside one portion for fellow celibates, a second for the distressed, a third for the destitute, and consumes the fourth himself. And when consuming it, he consumes without attachment, without clinging, without greed, without being absorbed [in it] — only for the maintenance of the body, for its sustenance. He consumes in such a way that he is neither excessively emaciated nor excessively heavy in body. Why? For one who is excessively emaciated turns away from the side of wholesomeness; one who is excessively heavy is oppressed by torpor. Therefore, having consumed that alms-food, he should be inclined toward the side of wholesomeness,' and so forth.

body.text: ārya-ratna-rāśāv apy uktaṃ | tena grāmaṃ vā nagaraṃ vā nigamaṃ vā piṇḍāya caratā dharma-saṃnāhaṃ saṃnahya piṇḍāya cartavyaṃ | tatra katamo dharma-saṃnāhaḥ | a-mana-āpāni

children.translated_text: forms, one should not become averse. Having seen agreeable
[forms], one should not be drawn [toward them]. Likewise, regarding agreeable and disagreeable

children.text: śabda-gandha-rasa-spraṣṭavyeṣu vijñapteṣu na + anunetavyaṃ na pratihantavyaṃ | indriya-su-saṃvṛtena + an-utkṣipta-cakṣuṣā yuga-mātra-prekṣiṇā | dānta-ājāneya-cittena pūrva-dharma-manasi-kāram an-utsṛjatā na + āmiṣa-prakṣiptayā santatyā piṇḍāya cartavyaṃ sa-avadāna-cāriṇā ca bhavitavyaṃ | yataś ca piṇḍa-pāto labhyate tatra + anunayo na kartavyaḥ yataś ca na labhyate tatra pratighāto na + utpādayitavyaḥ | daśa-kula-praveśe na ca + ekādaśāt kulād bhikṣā na labhyate | tathā + api na paritaptavyaṃ evaṃ ca cittam utpādayitavyam | evaṃ bahu-kṛtyā hy ete śramaṇa-brāhmaṇa-gṛha-patayo na tair a-vaśyaṃ mama dātavyaṃ | idaṃ tāvad āścaryaṃ yan mām ete samanvāharanti | kaḥ punar vādo yad bhikṣāṃ dāsyanti | tena + evam a-paritapatā piṇḍāya cartavyaṃ ||
children.translated_text: sounds, smells, tastes, tangibles, and cognizable objects — one should neither be drawn [toward them] nor become averse. With the sense-faculties well-restrained, with unraised eyes, looking only a yoke's length ahead, with a mind [tamed] like a trained thoroughbred, not abandoning the prior mental application to <s>Dharma</s>, not with a mind attracted by material things — one should go for alms, and one should conduct oneself with moral propriety. Where alms are obtained, there one should not make attachment; where they are not obtained, there one should not generate aversion. After entering ten families, even if alms are not obtained from an eleventh, still one should not be distressed. And this thought should be generated: "For indeed these householders, ascetics, and brahmins are very busy people; they are not obligated to give to me. This much itself is wonderful — that they pay attention to me at all. What need be said of their giving alms?" Thus, without being distressed, one should go for alms.'

body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Ratnarāśi</s> too it is said: 'By him, going for alms in a village, city, or town, one should go for alms having girded oneself with the armor of <s>Dharma</s>. Therein, what is the armor of <s>Dharma</s>? Having seen disagreeable

body.text: ye ca + asya satvāś cakṣuṣu ābhāsam āgacchanti strī-puruṣa-dāraka-dārikāḥ | antaśas tiryag-yoni-gatās tatra maitrī-karuṇā-cittam utpādayitavyaṃ | tathā + ahaṃ kariṣyāmi yathā ye me satvāś cakṣuṣā ābhāsam āgacchanti piṇḍa-pātaṃ vā dāsyanti tān su-gati-gāminaḥ kariṣyāmi | tādṛśaṃ yogam āpatsye | tena lūhaṃ vā praṇītaṃ vā piṇḍa-pāta saṃgṛhya samantāc catur-diśaṃ vyavalokayitavyaṃ | ka iha grāma-nagara-nigame daridraḥ satvaḥ | yasya + asmāt piṇḍa-pātāt saṃvibhāgaṃ kariṣyāmi | yadi daridraṃ satvaṃ paśyati tena tat-piṇḍa-pātāt saṃvibhāgaḥ kartavyaḥ | atha na kañ-cit satvaṃ daridraṃ paśyati | tena + evaṃ cittam utpādayitavyaṃ | santy an-ābhāsa-gatāḥ satvā ye mama cakṣuṣu ābhāsaṃ na + āgacchanti | teṣām itaḥ piṇḍa-pātād agraṃ praty-aṃśaṃ niryātayāmi | datta-ādānāḥ paribhuñjatāṃ | tena tat piṇḍa-pātaṃ gṛhītvā tad araṇya-āyatanam abhiruhya dhauta-pāṇinā śobhana-samācāreṇa śramaṇa-cāritra-kalpa-samatva-āgatena + adhiṣṭhāna-adhiṣṭhitena paryaṅkaṃ baddhvā sa-piṇḍa-pātaḥ paribhoktavyaḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'And whatever beings come into the range of his sight — women, men, boys, girls, and even those born in animal realms — toward them a mind of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) should be generated: "I shall act in such a way that those beings who come into the range of my sight, or who will give me alms, I shall make them travelers to a good destiny. I shall undertake such a practice." By him, having received the alms-food, whether coarse or fine, he should look around in all four directions: "Who here in this village, city, or town is a poor being with whom I shall share this alms-food?" If he sees a poor being, he should share from that alms-food. But if he does not see any poor being, he should generate this thought: "There are beings not in the range [of my sight] who do not come into the range of my eyes. To them, from this alms-food, I offer the first portion and individual share. May the recipients consume what is given!" Having taken that alms-food, he should ascend to that forest-hermitage, and with washed hands, with proper conduct, in accordance with the standard of a renunciant's way of life, established in meditative composure, having crossed his legs, he should eat that alms-food.' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: paribhuñjatā ca + evaṃ manasi-kāra utpādayitavyaḥ | santy asmin kāye * aśītiḥ krimi-kula-sahasrāṇi | tāny anena + eva + ojasā sukhaṃ phāsuṃ viharantu | idānīṃ ca + eṣām āmiṣeṇa saṃgrahaṃ kariṣyāmi | bodhi-prāptaś ca punar dharmeṇa saṃgrahaṃ kariṣyāmi | yadi punar asya lūhaṃ piṇḍa-pātaṃ bhavati tena + evaṃ cittam utpādayitavyaṃ | lūha-āhāratayā me laghuḥ kāyo bhaviṣyati prahāṇa-kṣama uccāra-prasrāva-niṣyandanaś ca me parītto bhaviṣyati | śraddhā-deyaṃ ca parīttaṃ bhaviṣyati | kāya-laghutā citta-laghutā ca me bhaviṣyati | alpa-mlāna-middhaś ca me bhaviṣyati | yadā punar asya prabhūtaḥ piṇḍa-pāto bhavati tatra + api mātra-ābhojinā bhavitavyaṃ utsarjana-dharmiṇā ca | tataḥ piṇḍa-pātād anyatarāyāṃ śilāyām avatīrya + evaṃ cittam utpādayitavyaṃ | ye ke-cin mṛga-pakṣi-saṃgā āmiṣa-bhojanena + arthikās te datta-ādānāḥ paribhuñjatām iti ||
body.translated_text: 'And while eating, this mental application should be generated: "There are in this body eighty thousand families of worms. May they live happily and comfortably with this very nourishment! Now I shall gather them together with material [sustenance]; and having attained awakening, I shall gather them together with <s>Dharma</s>." If, however, his alms-food is coarse, he should generate the thought: "Through eating coarse food, my body will become light, fit for exertion; and my discharge of excrement and urine will be small. And the consumption of what was given in faith will be small. And I shall have lightness of body and lightness of mind. And I shall have little torpor and drowsiness." When, however, his alms-food is abundant, even then he should eat only moderately and should be one whose principle is to leave [some over]. Then, having descended from the alms-food to some rock, this thought should be generated: "Whatever herds of deer and birds desire food — may the recipients consume what is given!"'

body.text: punar āha | tena sarveṇa rasa-saṃjñā na + utpādayitavyā || pe ||
body.translated_text: Again it says: 'By him, the perception of flavor should not be generated.' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: caṇḍāla-kumāra-sadṛśena mayā bhavitavyaṃ | citta-kāya-caukṣeṇa | na bhojana-caukṣeṇa | tat kasmād * dhetoḥ | kiyat-praṇītam api bhojanaṃ bhuktaṃ | sarvaṃ tat pūti-niṣyanda-paryavasānaṃ dur-gandha-paryavasānaṃ pratikūla-paryavasānaṃ | tasmān mayā na praṇīta-bhojana-ākāṅkṣiṇā bhavitavyaṃ | tena na + evaṃ cittam utpādayitavyaṃ |puruṣo me piṇḍa-pātaṃ dad-ti na strīḥ | strī me piṇḍa-pātaṃ dadāti na puruṣaḥ | dārako me piṇḍa-pātaṃ dadāti na dārikā | dārikā me piṇḍa-pātaṃ dadāti na dārakaḥ | praṇītaṃ labhe * ahaṃ na lūhaṃ | sat-kṛtya labhe * ahaṃ na + a-sat-kṛtya | capalaṃ labhe * ahaṃ na kṛcchreṇa praviṣṭa-mātraṃ ca māṃ samanvāhareyuḥ | na me kaś-cid vikṣepo bhavet | su-nihitāṃl labhe * ahaṃ praṇītān nānā-rasāṃl labhe * aham | na hīna-daridra-bhojanaṃ labhe * ahaṃ pratyudgaccheyur māṃ strī-puruṣa-dāraka-dārikāḥ | ime te sarve * a-kuśalā manasi-kārā na + utpādayitavyaḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'I should be like a <s>caṇḍāla</s> youth — pure in mind and body, not pure in food. For what reason? However fine the food that is eaten, all of it ends in foul discharge, ends in bad smell, ends in what is repulsive. Therefore, I should not be one who craves fine food.' 'By him, this thought should not be generated: "A man gives me alms-food, not a woman. A woman gives me alms-food, not a man. A boy gives me alms-food, not a girl. A girl gives me alms-food, not a boy. I receive fine [food], not coarse. I receive [it] with respect, not without respect. I receive [it] quickly, not with difficulty — and upon my mere entry, they should attend to me. May there be no disturbance for me! May I receive well-prepared, fine foods of various flavors! May I not receive poor, humble food! May women, men, boys, and girls come out to meet me!" All these are unwholesome mental applications and should not be generated.' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: prāyeṇa hi satvā rasa-gṛddhā bhojana-hetoḥ pāpāni karmāṇi kṛtvā narakeṣu + upapadyante | ye ye punaḥ saṃtuṣṭā a-gṛddhā a-lulopā rasa-pratiprasrabdhā jihva-indriya-saṃtuṣṭāḥ kiyal-lūhena + api bhojanena jñāpayanti | teṣāṃ cyutānāṃ kāla-gatānāṃ svarga-upapattir bhavati | su-gati-gamanaṃ bhavati deva-manuṣyeṣu | te deva-upapannāḥ sudhāṃ paribhuñjate | evaṃ kāśyapa piṇḍa-cārikeṇa bhikṣuṇā rasa-tṛṣṇāṃ vinivartayitvā nidhyapta-cittena su-paripakvān kulmāṣān paribhuñjatā na paritaptavyam | tat kasmād * dhetoḥ | kāya-saṃdhāraṇa-arthaṃ mārga-saṃdhāraṇa-arthaṃ mayā bhojanaṃ paribhoktavyaṃ || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'For beings who are greedy for flavors, having performed evil <s>karmas</s> for the sake of food, are mostly reborn in the hells. But those who are content, not greedy, not avaricious, who have subsided [the craving for] flavors, who are satisfied in the sense-faculty of the tongue, who manage with however coarse the food — for them, upon dying and passing away, there is rebirth in heaven; there is a going to a good destiny among <s>devas</s> and humans. Those reborn among <s>devas</s> consume <s>sudhā</s> (ambrosia). Thus, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>bhikṣu</s> who goes on alms-round, having turned away the craving for flavors, eating with a settled mind even well-cooked coarse grains, should not be distressed. For what reason? "Food is to be consumed by me for the purpose of maintaining the body, for the purpose of maintaining the [spiritual] path."' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: yadi punaḥ kāśyapa piṇḍa-cāriko bhikṣur megha-ākula-vṛṣṭi-kāla-samaye vartamāne na śaknuyāt piṇḍāya + avatartuṃ | tena maitryā + āhāra-saṃnaddhena dharma-cintā-manasi-kāra-pratiṣṭhitena dvi-rātraṃ tri-rātraṃ vā bhakta-cchada-cchinnena evaṃ saṃjñā + utpādayitavyā | santi yāma-laukikāḥ pretā duṣ-kara-karma-kāriṇo ye varṣa-śatena kheṭa-piṇḍam apy āhāraṃ na pratilabhante | tan mayā dharma-yoniśaś cintā-pratiṣṭhitena kāya-daurbalyaṃ vā citta-daurbalyaṃ vā na + utpādayitavyaṃ | adhivāsayiṣyāmi kṣut-pipāsāṃ | na punar ārya-mārga-bhāvanāyāṃ vīryaṃ sraṃsayiṣyāmi || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'If, however, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the alms-round <s>bhikṣu</s>, when a time of cloudy, rainy weather prevails, is unable to go down for alms, he should — armed with <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) in regard to food, established in the mental application of reflecting on <s>Dharma</s> — whether deprived of food for two nights or three nights, generate this perception: "There are worldly <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), performers of difficult deeds, who do not obtain even a ball of spittle as food in a hundred years. By me, established in reflection on the <s>Dharma</s> and its source, neither bodily weakness nor mental weakness should be generated. I shall endure hunger and thirst. But I shall not let my vigor slacken in the cultivation of the noble path."' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: yatra kule piṇḍa-pātaṃ śuciṃ kārayet tatra kule āsane niṣadya dhārmī kathā kartavyā | yāvan na sa piṇḍa-pātaḥ śucī-krṭo bhavet tena piṇḍa-pātaṃ gṛhītvā utthāya + āsanāt prakramitavyaṃ | piṇḍa-cārikeṇa kāśyapa bhikṣuṇā na + avabhāsa-kareṇa bhavitavyaṃ na lapanā na kuhanā kartavyā ||
body.translated_text: 'In whatever family he has his alms-food prepared, in that family, having sat on a seat, a <s>Dharma</s>-conversation should be conducted. Until that alms-food is prepared, having taken the alms-food, he should rise from the seat and depart. The alms-round <s>bhikṣu</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, should not be one who makes impressions; neither flattery nor hypocrisy should be performed.'

body.text: tatra katamo * avabhāsaḥ | yat pareṣām evaṃ vācaṃ bhāṣate | lūho me piṇḍa-pāto rukṣo me piṇḍa-pāta āsīn na ca me yāvad-arthaṃ bhuktaṃ | bahu-jana-sādhāraṇaś ca me piṇḍa-pātaḥ kṛtaḥ | alpaṃ me bhuktaṃ jighatsito * asmi + iti | yat kiñ-cid evaṃ-rūpam avabhāsa-nimittaṃ | iyam ucyate citta-kuhanā | sarvam etat piṇḍa-cārikeṇa bhikṣuṇā na kartavyaṃ | upekṣaka-bhūtena | yat pātre patitaṃ lūhaṃ vā praṇītaṃ vā śubhaṃ vā + a-śubhaṃ vā tat paribhoktavyam a-paritapyamānena + āśaya-śuddhena dharma-nidhyapti-bahulena | kāya-jāpana-artham ārya-mārgasya + upastambha-arthaṃ sa piṇḍa-pātaḥ paribhoktavya iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Therein, what is "making impressions"? When he speaks such words to others: "My alms-food is coarse; my alms-food was rough; I did not eat as much as I needed; my alms-food was shared among many people; I ate little; I am hungry." Whatever expression of this kind is a sign for [soliciting] an impression — this is called mental hypocrisy. All of this should not be done by the alms-round <s>bhikṣu</s>. Being equanimous, whatever falls into his bowl — coarse or fine, good or bad — that should be eaten without distress, with purity of intention, with a mind intent on the contemplation of <s>Dharma</s>. That alms-food should be consumed for the purpose of sustaining the body and for the purpose of supporting the noble path.'

body.text: tathā + ārya-ugra-paripṛcchāyām apy uktaṃ | yasyāś ca + antike piṇḍa-pātaṃ paribhujya na śaknoty ātmanaḥ parasya ca + arthaṃ paripūrayitum anujānāmy ahaṃ tasya piṇḍa-cārikasya bodhi-satvasya nimantraṇam iti ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, in the <s>Ārya-Ugra-paripṛcchā</s> too it is said: 'For one who, having eaten the alms-food in her presence, is unable to fulfill the purpose of both self and other — I permit that alms-round <s>bodhisattva</s> to accept an invitation.'

body.text: evaṃ tāvat satata-bhaiṣajyena + ātma-bhāva-rakṣā kāryā | tatra + api na matsya-māṃsena laṅkā-avatāra-sūtre pratiṣiddhatvāt ||
body.translated_text: Thus, first, the protection of the body should be accomplished through constant [intake of] medicine [i.e., food]. And even in that, not through fish and meat, since it is prohibited in the <s>Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra</s>.

body.text: tathā hy uktaṃ | māṃsaṃ sarvam a-bhakṣyaṃ kṛpa-ātmāno bodhi-satvasya + iti vadāmi || pe ||
body.translated_text: For thus it is said: 'I declare that all meat is not to be eaten by the compassionate <s>bodhisattva</s>.' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: svājanyād vyabhicārāc ca śukra-śoṇita-saṃbhavāt | udvejanīyaṃ bhūtānāṃ yogī māṃsaṃ vivarjayet ||
body.translated_text: 'Because of the impurity of one's own birth, because of the deviation [from right conduct], and because [meat] arises from semen and blood — being revolting to beings ��� the <s>yogī</s> should avoid meat.'

body.text: māṃsāni ca palāṇḍūṃś ca madyāni vividhāni ca | gṛñjanaṃ laśunaṃ ca + eva yogī nityaṃ vivarjayet ||
body.translated_text: 'Meat, onions, and various kinds of intoxicants, garlic and leeks — the <s>yogī</s> should always avoid.'

body.text: mrakṣaṇaṃ varjayet tailaṃ śalya-viddheṣu na svapet | chidra-a-chidreṣu satvānāṃ yac ca sthānaṃ mahā-bhayam || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'He should avoid oil for anointing; he should not sleep in places infested with thorns; and wherever there is great danger to beings, in openings and non-openings [alike].' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: lābha-arthaṃ hanyate prāṇī māṃsa-arthaṃ dīyate dhanaṃ | ubhau tau pāpa-karmāṇau pacyete raurava-ādiṣu ||
body.translated_text: 'For the sake of profit, a living being is killed; for the sake of meat, wealth is given. Both of those performers of evil <s>karma</s> are cooked in the <s>Raurava</s> [hell] and the like.'

body.text: yāvat ||
body.translated_text: And so on.

body.text: yo * atikramya muner vākyaṃ māṃsaṃ bhakṣeta dur-matiḥ | loka-dvaya-vināśa-arthaṃ dīkṣitaḥ śākya-śāsane ||
body.translated_text: 'He who, transgressing the Sage's word, would eat meat — the evil-minded one — has taken initiation in the <s>Śākya</s>'s teaching for the destruction of both worlds.'

body.text: te yānti paramaṃ ghoraṃ narakaṃ pāpa-kaṝiṇaḥ | raurava-ādiṣu raudreṣu pacyante māṃsa-khādakāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Those performers of evil go to the most terrifying hell; in the terrible <s>Raurava</s> and the like, meat-eaters are cooked.'

body.text: tri-koṭi-kṣuddhaṃ māṃsaṃ vai a-kalpitam a-yācitaṃ | a-coditaṃ ca na + eva + asti tasmān māṃsaṃ na bhakṣyayet ||
body.translated_text: 'The three-fold purification of meat — [supposedly] not prepared [for oneself], not requested, and not incited — does not in fact exist. Therefore, meat should not be eaten.'

body.text: māṃsaṃ na bhakṣyayed yogī mayā buddhaiś ca garhitaṃ | anyo-nya-bhakṣaṇāḥ satvāḥ kravya-ada-kula-saṃbhavāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Meat should not be eaten by the <s>yogī</s> — it is condemned by me and by the <s>Buddhas</s>. Beings who eat one another are born in the family of flesh-eaters.'

body.text: yāvat ||
body.translated_text: And so on.

body.text: dur-gandhaḥ kutsanīyaś ca utmattaś ca + api jāyate | caṇḍāla-pukkasa-kule ḍombeṣu ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'He becomes foul-smelling, contemptible, and even mad. He is reborn again and again in the families of <s>ca��ḍālas</s>, <s>pukkasas</s>, and <s>ḍombas</s>.'

body.text: ḍākinī-jāti-yonau ca māṃsa-ade jāyate kule | ṛkṣa-mārjara-yonau ca jāyate * asau nara-adhamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'In the womb of the <s>ḍākinī</s> race, the meat-eater is born in [such] a family. In the womb of bears and cats is born that lowest of men.'

body.text: hasti-kakṣye mahā-meghe nirvāṇa-aṅgulimālike | laṅkā-avatāra-sūtre ca mayā māṃsaṃ vigarhitaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'In the <s>Hastikakṣya</s>, the <s>Mahāmegha</s>, the <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, the <s>Aṅgulimālika</s>, and the <s>Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra</s> — by me, meat has been condemned.'

body.text: buddhaiś ca bodhi-satvaiś ca śrāvakaiś ca vigarhitaṃ | khādate yadi nir-lajja unmatto jāyate sadā ||
body.translated_text: 'By <s>Buddhas</s>, by <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and by <s>Śrāvakas</s> it is condemned. If one eats [it] shamelessly, one is always born mad.'

body.text: brāhmaṇeṣu ca jāyante atha vā yogināṃ kule | prajñāvān dhanavāṃś ca + eva māṃsa-adyānāṃ vivarjanāt ||
body.translated_text: 'One is born among <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, or in the family of <s>yogīs</s>, possessed of wisdom and wealth — through the avoidance of meat-eating.'

body.text: dṛṣṭa-śruta-viśaṅkābhiḥ sarvaṃ māṃsaṃ vivarjayet | tārkikā na + avabudhyante kravya-ada-kula-saṃbhavāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Through the suspicions of what is seen and heard, all meat should be avoided. Logicians do not understand [this] — [they who are] born in the family of flesh-eaters.'

body.text: yathā + eṣa rāgo mokṣasya antarāya-karo bhavet | tathā + eva māṃsa-madya-ādi antarāya-karaṃ bhavet ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as passion becomes an obstruction to liberation, so too does meat, intoxicants, and the like become obstructions.'

body.text: vakṣanty an-āgate kāle māṃsa-adā moha-vādinaḥ | kalpikaṃ nir-avadyaṃ ca māṃsaṃ buddha-anuvarṇitaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'In the future time, meat-eaters, speakers of delusion, will say: "Meat is permissible, blameless, and praised by the <s>Buddha</s>."'

body.text: bheṣajyam iva āhāraṃ putra-māṃsa-upamaṃ punaḥ | mātrayā pratikūlaṃ ca yogī piṇḍaṃ samācaret ||
body.translated_text: The practitioner should partake of alms-food as medicine, like the flesh of one's own son, in [proper] measure and [with a sense of] aversion.

body.text: maitrī-vihāriṇā nityaṃ sarvathā garhitaṃ mayā | siṃha-vyāghra-mṛga-ādyaiś ca saha ekatra saṃbhavet ||
body.translated_text: "By one who constantly abides in loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), [meat-eating] has been condemned by me in every way. One may find oneself in the company of lions, tigers, deer, and other [animals]."

body.text: tasmān na bhakṣayen māṃsam udveja-janakaṃ nṛṇāṃ | mokṣa-dharma-niruddhatvād āryāṇām eṣa vai dhvajaḥ ||
body.translated_text: "Therefore one should not eat meat, which generates alarm in people. Because the <s>dharma</s> of liberation is obstructed thereby — this indeed is the banner of the noble ones."

body.text: yat tu jñānavatī-parivarte māṃsa-bhakṣaṇaṃ paṭhyate tan mahā-artha-sādhakatvān nir-doṣam ||
body.translated_text: But the eating of meat that is described in the <s>Jñānavatī-parivarta</s> (Chapter on the Wise Woman) is blameless, because it accomplishes a great purpose.

body.text: evaṃ hi tathā + uktaṃ | eṣo * akariṣyad yadi bhikṣu kālaṃ | samādhi-śabdo * api hi jambu-dvīpe | niruddhu satvāna sadā + abhaviṣyad | cikitsite asmi samādhi labdhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: For thus it is said there: "If this monk had died, even the word '<s>samādhi</s>' (concentration) would have ceased in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. It would have been forever unavailable to sentient beings. Through his treatment, <s>samādhi</s> was obtained."

body.text: na ca mahā-karuṇā-abhiyuktam | tena asmin na maitrī śaṅkā + api na + asti + ity a-doṣaḥ ||
body.translated_text: And it is not the case that one who is devoted to great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) [would be faulted]; therefore there is no suspicion of [lack of] loving-kindness in this [case] — hence it is blameless.

body.text: yady apy ārya-ratna-meghe * abhihitaṃ | śmāśānikena nir-āmiṣeṇa bhavitavyam iti ||
body.translated_text: Although in the noble <s>Ratnamegha</s> (Cloud of Jewels) it is said: "One who [dwells] in charnel grounds should be one who is free from attachment to material bait" —

body.text: tad anyatra + evaṃ jātīya-satva-artha-saṃdarśana-arthaṃ | vinaye * api yad anujñātaṃ tat tu tri-koṭi-pariśuddha-bhakṣaṇe na prahāṇa-antarāya iti | tat parityāgena śuddha-dṛṣṭīnām abhimāna-nirāsa-arthaṃ | tad vṛddhatayā ca bhavyānāṃ śāsana-an-avatāra-parihāra-arthaṃ ||
body.translated_text: that [statement] is for the purpose of demonstrating [the ideal] to beings of such a kind elsewhere. And what is permitted in the <s>Vinaya</s> (Monastic Discipline) — that concerns the eating of what is pure in three respects, which is no obstacle to abandonment. The renunciation of that [three-fold pure meat] is for the purpose of removing the conceit of those with [overly] pure views. And by the prevalence of that [practice], it is for the purpose of averting the non-entry into the teaching of those who are spiritually mature.

body.text: tathā hy uktaṃ laṅkā-avatāra-sūtre | tatra tatra deśanā pāṭhe śikṣā-padānām ānupūrvīṃ bandhan niśreṇī-pada-vinyāsa-yogena | tri-koṭiṃ baddhvā | tatra uddiṣya krṭāni pratiṣiddhāni tato * antaśaḥ prakṛti-mṛtāny api pratiṣiddhāni + iti ||
body.translated_text: For thus it is said in the <s>Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra</s>: "In those various teachings, binding the gradual sequence of training-rules by the method of progressive steps as in climbing a ladder, establishing the triple purity — therein, first he prohibited [meat] that was designated [i.e., specially prepared for one], then ultimately even that which has died naturally was prohibited."

body.text: uktaṃ satata-bhaiṣajyaṃ | glāna-pratyaya-bhaiṣajyaṃ tat sevyam eva ||
body.translated_text: The constant medicine has been mentioned; the medicine [taken] on account of illness — that should certainly be used.

body.text: śrāvaka-vinaye * api tāvad ātma-arthaṃ brahma-carya-vāsa-arthaṃ pātra-cīvaram api vikrīya | kāya-saṃdhāraṇam uktaṃ | kiṃ punar a-parimita-jana-paritrāṇa-hetor bodhi-satva-śarīrasya dur-labhā ca + īdṛśī kṣaṇa-pratilābha-utsava-sampad | iti tat-pradarśana-arthaṃ ca bhagavatā tatra svayaṃ bhaiṣajya-upayogaḥ pradarśitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Even in the <s>Śrāvaka-vinaya</s> (Hearers' Monastic Code), for one's own sake, for the sake of dwelling in the holy life, even the bowl and robe may be sold for the maintenance of the body. How much more so for the body of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, whose purpose is the protection of immeasurable beings! And such an occasion of gaining this [human life] is rare and a festive [opportunity]. To demonstrate this, the <s>Bhagavan</s> (Lord) himself showed the use of medicine there.

body.text: uktaṃ ca + ārya-ratna-megha-sūtre | tair yadā pracāritaṃ bhavati tadā satyāṃ velāyām a-satyāṃ vā teṣām imāny evaṃ-rūpāṇi kāya-upastambhanāny upakaraṇāni na labhyante * abhyavahartuṃ | yad uta sarpir vā tailaṃ vā mūla-raso vā gaṇḍa-raso vā phala-raso vā | na ca + anyān abhyavaharato dṛṣṭvā pratigha-cittam utpādayati | yadi punaḥ khalu paścād-bhaktiko bodhi-satvo vā glāno bhavati | yathā-rūpeṇa + asya glānyena jīvita-antarāyo bhavati kuśala-pakṣa-antarāyo vā tena niṣ-kaukṛtyena bhūtvā nir-vicikitsakena bhaiṣajya-cittam upasthāpya pratinisevyāni + iti ||
body.translated_text: And it is said in the noble <s>Ratnamegha-sūtra</s>: "When they are wandering about [for alms], at the proper time or at an improper time, they do not obtain such provisions for the support of the body — namely, ghee, oil, root-juice, trunk-juice, or fruit-juice — they should not generate a mind of hostility upon seeing others consuming them. If, however, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who eats [only] after the noon-meal becomes ill, and if by such illness his life would be endangered or there would be an obstacle to wholesome states — then, being free from remorse, free from doubt, establishing the thought of medicine, he should partake [of food]."

body.text: vasana-upabhoga-prayojanam ugra-paripṛcchā-sūtre * abhihitaṃ | hrīr-apatrāpya-kāpair niḥ-...

children.text: pracchādana-arthaṃ tu śramaṇa-liṅga-saṃdarśana-artham imāni ca kāṣāyāṇi deva-mānuṣa-asurasya lokasya caityam iti | caitya-arthaṃ samyag-dhāritavyāni | nirvṛti-virāga-raktāni
children.translated_text: ... for the purpose of covering [the body], for the purpose of displaying the marks of a renunciant, these saffron robes are a shrine (<s>caitya</s>) for the world of gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>" — and for the purpose of being a shrine they should be properly maintained. "These are dyed with the dye of cessation and dispassion,

children.text: etāni | na rāga-raktāni | upaśama-anukūlāny etāni | na saṃkleśa-saṃdhukṣaṇa-anukūlāni | ebhiś ca kāṣāyair vivṛta-pāpā bhaviṣyāmaḥ | su-kṛta-karma-kāriṇo na cīvara-maṇḍana-anuyogam anuyuktāḥ | etāni ca kāṣāyāṇy ārya-mārga-saṃbhāra-anukūlāni + iti kṛtvā tathā kariṣyāmo yathā na + eka-kṣaṇam api sa-kaṣāyāḥ kāye kāṣāyāṇi dhārayiṣyāma iti ||
children.translated_text: not dyed with the dye of passion. These are conducive to tranquility, not conducive to kindling defilement. And through these saffron robes we shall become those whose sins are laid bare, performers of good deeds, not devoted to the adornment of our robes. And regarding these saffron robes — they are conducive to the provisions of the noble path — we shall act in such a way that we will not, even for a single moment, wear the saffron robes on our bodies while afflicted by defilements (<s>kaṣāya</s>)."

body.translated_text: The purpose of clothing and its use is stated in the <s>Ugraparipṛcchā-sūtra</s>: "With garments of modesty and shame, free from ...

body.text: atra ca kāraṇaṃ ratna-rāśi-sūtre * abhihitaṃ | ye punas te kāśyapa vaidaryā a-saṃyatā itaḥ śramaṇa-guṇa-dharmād uddhurāḥ kāye kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇi dhārayanti | na ca + eteṣu gauravam utpādayanti | tatra kāśyapa śramaṇa-varṇa-prati-rūpakaṃ nāma praty-eka-narakaṃ | tatra kāśyapa praty-eka-narake śramaṇa-rūpa-prati-rūpeṇa tāḥ kāraṇāḥ kāryante ādīpta-cailā ādīpta-śīrṣā ādīpta-pātrā ādīpta-āsanā ādīpta-śayanāḥ | yaḥ kaś-cit tatra teṣām upabhoga-paribhogaḥ sa sarva ādīptaḥ saṃprajvalita eka-jvālī-bhūtaḥ | tatra taiḥ śramaṇa-varṇa-rūpeṇa duṣkhāṃ vedanām anubhavanti + iti ||
body.translated_text: And the reason for this is stated in the <s>Ratnarāśi-sūtra</s> (Heap of Jewels Sūtra): "But those, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, who are of the deficient kind, unrestrained, who have departed from the qualities and <s>dharmas</s> of a renunciant, who wear saffron robes on their bodies but do not generate reverence for them — there, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is a particular hell called <s>Śramaṇavarṇapratirūpaka</s> (Counterfeit of the Renunciant's Appearance). In that particular hell, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, in the counterfeit form of a renunciant, those torments are inflicted: blazing robes, blazing heads, blazing bowls, blazing seats, blazing beds. Whatever use and enjoyment they have there — all of it is blazing, flaming, become a single mass of fire. There, in the appearance of a renunciant, they experience painful feelings."

body.text: ārya-ratna-meghe * apy uktaṃ | yadi bhaved abhyavakāśiko bodhi-satvo glāna-kāyo * a-prati-bala-kāyas tena vihāra-kṣitena + evaṃ cittam utpādayitavyaṃ | kleśa-prati-pakṣa-arthaṃ tathā-gatena dhuta-guṇāḥ prajñaptāḥ | tathā + ahaṃ kariṣyāmi yathā vihārasya eva kleśānāṃ prahāṇāya ghaṭiṣyāmi | tatra ca vihāre na gṛddhim utpādayāmi na + adhyavasānaṃ | evaṃ ca + asya bhavati | kartavyo dāna-patīnām anugraho na + asmābhir ātmambharibhir bhavitavyam iti ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Ratnamegha</s> it is also said: "If a <s>bodhisattva</s> who lives in the open is ill in body, with weakened strength, he should, [while staying] in a dwelling-place, generate this thought: 'The <s>dhutaguṇas</s> (ascetic practices) were prescribed by the <s>Tathāgata</s> for the purpose of counteracting <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). I shall act in such a way that I will strive for the abandonment of <s>kleśas</s> even while in the dwelling. And in that dwelling I shall not generate greed or attachment.' And he should think: 'We should show gratitude to the donors; we should not be self-serving.'"

body.text: punar atra + eva + āha | te śayyāṃ kalpayanto dakṣiṇena pārśvena śayyāṃ kalpayanti | pādasya + upari pādam ādhāya cīvaraiḥ a-saṃvṛta-kāyāḥ smṛtāḥ | saṃprajānānā utthāna-saṃjñina āloka-saṃjñinaḥ śayyāṃ kalpayanti | na ca nidrā-sukham āsvādayanti | na pārśva-sukham anytra yāvad eva + eṣāṃ mahā-bhūtānāṃ sthitaye jāpanāyai | ity anayā diśā sarva-paribhogāḥ satva-artham adhiṣṭhātavyāḥ | ātma-tṛṣṇā-upabhogāt tu kliṣṭa-āpattiḥ prajāyate ||
body.translated_text: And further in the same [text] it says: "When they prepare their bed, they lie down on the right side, placing foot upon foot, with bodies not completely covered by robes, mindful, clearly comprehending, with the perception of rising, with the perception of light, they prepare their bed. They do not savor the pleasure of sleep, nor the pleasure of the side [they lie on] — only so long as is necessary for the maintenance and sustenance of these great elements." In this manner, all enjoyments should be consecrated for the benefit of sentient beings. But from enjoyment motivated by craving for self, a defiled transgression arises.

body.text: yathā + uktaṃ candra-pradīpa-sūtre | te bhojanaṃ svādu-rasaṃ praṇītaṃ | labdhvā ca bhuñjanti a-yukta-yogāḥ | teṣāṃ sa āhāru badhāya bhotī | yatha hasti-potāna viṣā a-dhautā ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Candrapradīpa-sūtra</s>: "Those who, having obtained delicious and excellent food, eat it without proper practice — for them that food becomes a bond, like unwashed poison for young elephants."

body.text: iti ||
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: ārya-ratna-rāśi-sūtre * api bhagavatā śraddhā-deya-paribhoge parikīrtite | atha tasyām eva parṣadi yoga-ācārāṇāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ dve śate imaṃ dharma-paryāyaṃ śrutvā prarudite | evaṃ ca vācam abhāṣanta | kālaṃ vayaṃ bhagavan kariṣyāmo | na punar a-prāpta-phalā eka-piṇḍa-pātam api śraddhā-deyasya paribhokṣyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Ratnarāśi-sūtra</s> also, when the <s>Bhagavan</s> had described the enjoyment of what is given in faith, at that very assembly, two hundred monks who were practitioners of yoga, having heard this <s>Dharma</s> discourse, wept. And they spoke these words: "We shall die, O <s>Bhagavan</s>! But we will never again, without having attained the fruit, partake of even a single morsel of what is given in faith."

body.text: bhagavān āha | sādhu sādhu kula-putrā evaṃ-rūpair lajjābhiḥ kaukṛtya-saṃpannaiḥ para-loka-a-vadya-bhaya-darśibhir idaṃ pravacanaṃ śobhate ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavan</s> said: "Excellent! Excellent, sons of good family! By those endowed with such a sense of shame, conscience, and fear of blame in the next world, this teaching is adorned."

body.text: api tu ||
body.translated_text: "Moreover:"

body.text: dvayor ahaṃ kāśyapa śraddhā-deyam anujānāmi | katamayor dvayoḥ | yuktasya muktasya ca | yadi bhikṣavo bhikṣur yukto yoga-ācāro mama śikṣāyāṃ pratipannaḥ sarva-saṃskāreṣv a-nitya-darśī | sarva-saṃskāra-duḥkha-viditaḥ sarva-dharmeṣv an-ātma-adhimuktiḥ śānta-nirvāṇa-abhikāṅkṣī sumeru-mātrair ālopaiḥ śraddhā-deyaṃ bhuñjīta | atyanta-pariśuddhā + eva tasya sā dakṣiṇā bhavati | yeṣāṃ ca dāyakānāṃ dāna-patīnāṃ sakāśāc * chraddhā-deyaṃ paribhuktaṃ tatas teṣāṃ dāyaka-dāna-patīnāṃ maha-rddhikaḥ puṇya-vipāko bhavati | mahā-dyutikaḥ | tat kasmād * dhetoḥ | agram idam aupadhikānāṃ puṇya-kriyā-vastūnāṃ yā + iyaṃ maitra-citta-samāpattiḥ | tatra kāśyapa yo bhikṣur dāyakasya dāna-pater antikāc cīvara-piṇḍa-pātaṃ paribhujya-a-pramāṇaṃ cetaḥ-samādhiṃ samāpadyate * a-pramāṇas tasya dāyakasya dāna-pateḥ puṇya-kriyā-vipākaḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyaḥ | syāt kāśyapa tri-sāhasra-mahā-sāhasrāyāṃ loka-dhātau mahā-samudrāṇāṃ kṣayo na tv eva tasya puṇya-niṣyandanasya kaś-cit kṣaya iti ||
body.translated_text: "I permit the enjoyment of what is given in faith for two [kinds of persons], O <s>Kāśyapa</s>. Which two? For one who is yoked [to practice] and for one who is liberated. If, O monks, a monk who is yoked [to practice], a practitioner of yoga, who has entered upon my training, who sees impermanence in all <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations), who knows the suffering of all <s>saṃskāras</s>, who has the aspiration of non-self in all <s>dharmas</s>, who longs for peaceful <s>nirvāṇa</s> — were to partake of what is given in faith in morsels as large as Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, even so, that offering would be utterly purified for him. And for those donors and patrons from whom what is given in faith has been enjoyed, the karmic ripening of merit for those donors and patrons is of great supernatural power, of great splendor. For what reason? Because this is the supreme among meritorious acts that are based on [individual] foundations — namely, the attainment of the meditation of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī-citta-samāpatti</s>). Therein, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, whatever monk, having partaken of robe and alms-food from a donor, enters into the immeasurable mental concentration — immeasurable is the fruition of meritorious action to be expected for that donor and patron. Suppose, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, in this trichiliocosm the great oceans were to be exhausted — but there would be no exhaustion whatsoever of that outflow of merit."

body.text: tad evaṃ piṇḍa-pāta-gamanaārambhe bhojana-ārambhe vā triṣu sthāneṣu smṛtir upasthāpyā dāyaka-anugrahe | kāya-krimi-saṃgrahe | sarva-satva-artha-sādhake ca sad-dharma-parigrahe ||
body.translated_text: Thus, at the commencement of going for alms-food or at the commencement of eating, mindfulness should be established in three areas: in gratitude toward the donor; in the nourishment of the worms of the body; and in the embrace of the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharma-parigraha</s>) which accomplishes the welfare of all sentient beings.

body.text: tathā-gata-ājñā-saṃpādane tu sarva-kāryeṣu smṛtiḥ kāryā | ādi-śabdān mantrair api rakṣā kāryā ||
body.translated_text: For the accomplishment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s command, mindfulness should be maintained in all activities. From the initial syllables [of the mantras], protection should be performed through mantras as well.

body.text: tatra + api tāvad imāṃ tri-samaya-rāja-uktāṃ vidyāṃ maṇḍala-samaya-artham uccārayet | namaḥ sarva-buddha-bodhi-satvānāṃ oṃ viraji mahā-cakra-viraji | sata sārata trapi vidhamani | sabhajani | saṃbhajani | taramati | siddha agre tvaṃ svāhā ||
body.translated_text: Therein, one should first recite this <s>vidyā</s> (sacred formula) taught in the <s>Trisamayarāja</s> for the purpose of the <s>maṇḍala</s>-commitment: <s>Namaḥ sarva-buddha-bodhisatvānāṃ oṃ viraji mahā-cakra-viraji sata sārata trapi vidhamani sabhajani saṃbhajani taramati siddha agre tvaṃ svāhā</s>.

body.text: anena sarva-maṇḍala-praviṣṭo bhavati ||
body.translated_text: By this one becomes initiated into all <s>maṇḍalas</s> (sacred circles).

body.text: atha-vā tathā-gata-hṛdayam aṣṭa-sahastraṃ japet sa-laukika-loka-uttara-maṇḍala-praviṣṭo bhavati | katamac ca tat ||
body.translated_text: Alternatively, one should recite the <s>Tathāgatahṛdaya</s> (Heart of the <s>Tathāgata</s>) eight thousand times — [thereby] one becomes initiated into both worldly and supramundane <s>maṇḍalas</s>. And what is that?

body.text: namas traiyabdhikānāṃ tathā-gatānāṃ | sarvatra-a-pratihata-avāpti-dharmatā-balināṃ | āṃ a-sama-sama samantato * an-antana-avāpti-śāsani | hara smara smaraṇa vigata-rāga-buddha-dharmate | sara sama-balā | hasa | traya | gagana mahā-a-cala-rakṣaṇa | jvala jvalana sāgare svāhā ||
body.translated_text: <s>Namas traiyabdhikānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ sarvatrāpratihata-avāpti-dharmatā-balinām āṃ asama-sama samantato anantanāvāpti-śāsani hara smara smaraṇa vigata-rāga-buddhadharmate sara sama-balā hasa traya gagana mahā-acala-rakṣaṇa jvala jvalana sāgare svāhā</s>.

body.text: ayaṃ sarva-tathā-gatānām ātma-bhāvaḥ | atra + an-uttaraṃ gauravaṃ bhāvayitavyaṃ | anena + ādi-karmikā api satveṣv anantaṃ buddha-kṛtyaṃ kurvanti | ayam eva paramāṃ rakṣāṃ māra-ādibhyaḥ sarva-duṣṭebhyaḥ karoti | hasta-tāḍena bhasmanā sarṣapair udakena dṛṣṭyā manasā vā sīmā-bandhaṃ karoti ||
body.translated_text: This is the self-nature of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Herein, the highest reverence should be cultivated. By this, even beginners perform infinite <s>Buddha</s>-activity among sentient beings. This very [mantra] provides the supreme protection from <s>Māra</s> and all malevolent beings. It creates a boundary-protection through a hand-clap, ashes, mustard seeds, water, gaze, or mind.

body.text: vyādhiṣu bhaiṣajyam udakaṃ ca + abhimantrya + upayojyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: For illnesses, water should be consecrated [with the mantra] and medicine should be applied.

body.text: vana-kusumāni vā caitye pratimāyāṃ sad-dharma-pustake vā samāhito nivedayet ||
body.translated_text: Or one should, in a state of meditative composure, offer forest flowers at a <s>caitya</s> (shrine), before an image, or at a manuscript of the true <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: pakṣa-prayogān mahā vyādhibhir abhimucyate | buddha-bodhi-satva-ālambanena sarva-satva-artha-abhilāṣiṇā ca cittena bhadra-cari-vidhi-pūrvakaṃ ca japtavyaḥ | ayaṃ vidhir asya kalpasya + avasāne draṣṭavyaḥ | tri-samaya-jāpinaś ca + āmnāyato na doṣaḥ | utsiṣṭasya + apy a-śucer na doṣaḥ | mudrā-ākārā na bhakṣaṇīyā na laṅghanīyā | na mañca-ārohaḥ kartavyaḥ | na madyaṃ pātavyaṃ | adhimukti-caryā śikṣā-padeṣv a-calasya nir-vicikitsasya duḥ-śīla-pūrvasya + api sidhyati | paṇḍitasya + a-paṇḍitasya vā niyataṃ sidhyati ||
body.translated_text: By a fortnight's practice, one is freed from great illnesses. [The mantra] should be recited with a mind focused on the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s>, aspiring to the welfare of all sentient beings, preceded by the method of the <s>Bhadracarī</s> (Prayer of Good Conduct). The procedure for this should be observed at the conclusion of the <s>kalpa</s> (chapter/period). And for one who recites the <s>Trisamaya</s> according to tradition, there is no fault. Even for one who has remnants of food or is impure, there is no fault. Mudrā-forms should not be eaten or stepped over. One should not climb onto a bed [with mudra items]. Intoxicants should not be consumed. For one of aspiring conduct who is steadfast in the training-rules, who is free from doubt — even if formerly of poor moral conduct — [the mantra] succeeds. For the learned or the unlearned alike, it certainly succeeds.

body.text: tathā ca + atra + eva + uktaṃ | bodhi-cittaṃ dṛḍhaṃ yasya niḥ-saṃgā ca matir bhavet | vicikitsā na + eva kartavyā tasya + idaṃ sidhyati dhruvam | iti ||
body.translated_text: And thus it is said right here: "For one whose <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening) is firm and whose mind is unattached, no doubt should be entertained — for this [practice] will surely succeed for him."

body.text: bodhi-citta-dṛḍhatā ca + atra pṛthag-jana-cala-cittatāyā niyama-artham uktā na tu bhūmi-praviṣṭam adhikṛtya ||
body.translated_text: And the firmness of the <s>bodhicitta</s> (thought of awakening) is stated here for the purpose of restraining the fickleness of mind of ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjanas</s>), not with reference to one who has entered the [bodhisattva] stages.

body.text: yasmād atra + uktaṃ | pratyuddhāratām avabhāsatāṃ ca pratilabdhu-kāmena |mahā-andha-kārād ālokaṃ praveṣṭu-kāmena | yad bhūyasā vinipatitena sādhyaṃ | tathā kuto mama + alpa-puṇyasya siddhir iti nīca-citta-pratiṣedhaḥ | na ca + atikrānta-dur-gater utsāha-ūrmi-bahulasya + upacita-a-prameya-puṇya-skandhasya bhūmi-praviṣṭasya + ayaṃ pūrva-ukto doṣaḥ saṃbhavati | atra ca mantrāṇām a-jñānān na + adhika-akṣara-pāṭhe doṣo * asti | na + api nyūnatā-doṣaḥ | na + api vidhi-bhraṃsa-doṣaḥ | kiṃ-tu śraddhā-vegaṃ bodhi-citta-vegaṃ sarva-utsarga-vegaṃ ca pramāṇī-kṛtya + a-vicārataḥ pravartitavyam a-vaśyaṃ buddha-bodhi-satvam iha + eva yathā-iṣṭa-siddhiś ca bhavati ||
body.translated_text: Since it is stated here: 'For one who wishes to attain deliverance and illumination, who wishes to enter the light from the great darkness — that which is to be accomplished mostly by one who has fallen [into error] — how then shall there be success for me, of little merit?' — this is the prohibition against the lowly mind. And for one who has entered the [bodhisattva] stages, who has passed beyond the lower realms, who is abundant in waves of enthusiasm, who has accumulated immeasurable masses of merit — the previously stated fault does not arise. And here, due to ignorance of the <s>mantras</s>, there is no fault in reciting with extra syllables, nor is there the fault of deficiency, nor the fault of deviation from the prescribed method. Rather, one should proceed unhesitatingly, taking as authoritative the force of faith, the force of <s>bodhicitta</s>, and the force of complete relinquishment — and inevitably, the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s> will bring about the accomplishment of whatever is wished for, right here.

body.text: atha-vā + anena sarva-vajra-dhara-mantreṇa rakṣāṃ kuryāt | namas traiyabdhikānāṃ tathā-gatānāṃ sarva-vajra-dharāṇāṃ caṇḍāla | cala | vajra | śāntana | phalana | cara | māraṇa | vajra-ḍāla-phaṭa | lalita-śikhara samanta-vajriṇi | jvala | namo * astu te agra-ugra-śāsānānāṃ raṇa haṃ phula sphāṭa vajra-uttame svāhā ||
body.translated_text: Alternatively, one should make protection with this <s>Sarvavajradhara-mantra</s>: '<s>Namas traiyabdhikānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ sarvavajradhārāṇāṃ caṇḍāla cala vajra śāntana phalana cara māraṇa vajra-ḍāla-phaṭ lalita-śikhara samantavajriṇi jvala namo'stu te agraugra-śāsānānāṃ raṇa haṃ phula sphāṭa vajrottame svāhā</s>.'

body.text: anena paṭhita-mātreṇa sarva-vighna-vināyakā na + upasaṃkrāmanti | deva-nāga-ādayo na prasahante | bhojana-pāna-śayana-āsana-vasana-pūjā-upakaraṇāni ca + abhimantritena jalena dṛṣṭyā manasā vā rakṣeta | a-cala-hṛdayena vā sarvam etat kuryāt ||
body.translated_text: By merely reciting this, all obstacle-creators (<s>vighna-vināyakas</s>) do not approach. Gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, and others cannot prevail. One should protect food, drink, bedding, seats, clothing, and worship implements with water consecrated [by this mantra], or by sight, or by mind. Or one should do all this with the heart[-mantra] of <s>Acala</s>.

body.text: idaṃ ca tat ||
body.translated_text: And this is that [mantra]:

body.text: namaḥ samanta-vajrāṇāṃ trāṭa | a-mogha caṇḍa-mahā-roṣaṇa sphāṭaya hūṃ | bhrāmaya hūṃ | trāṭa hūṃ | māṃ | oṃ balaṃ dade tejo-mālini svāhā ||
body.translated_text: '<s>Namaḥ samantavajrāṇāṃ trāṭ amoghacaṇḍamahāroṣaṇa sphāṭaya hūṃ bhrāmaya hūṃ trāṭ hūṃ māṃ oṃ balaṃ dade tejomālini svāhā</s>.'

body.text: anena prathamaṃ piṇḍam aṣṭa-abhimantritaṃ bhuñjīta bhaiṣajya-rājatāṃ buddha-bodhi-satvānām anusmṛtya ||
body.translated_text: With this [mantra], one should first eat the alms-food consecrated eight times, recollecting the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s> as the king of medicines.

body.text: viṣa-pratīkāras tu ||
body.translated_text: Now, for the antidote against poison:

body.text: tad yathā | ilimitte | tilimitte | ilitilimitte | dumbe | duḥse | duḥsālīye | dumbālīye | takke | tarkkaraṇe | marmme | marmaraṇe | kaśmīre | kaśmīra-mukte | aghane | aghanaghane | ilimilīye | akhāpye | apāpye śvete | śveta-tuṇḍe | anānurakṣe svāhā ||
body.translated_text: Namely: '<s>Ilimitte tilimitte ilitilimitte dumbe duḥse duḥsālīye dumbālīye takke tarkkaraṇe marmme marmaraṇe kaśmīre kaśmīramukta aghane aghanaghane ilimilīye akhāpye apāpye śvete śvetatuṇḍe anānurakṣe svāhā</s>.'

body.text: ya imāṃ vidyāṃ sakṛc * chṛṇoti sa sapta varṣāṇy ahinā na daśyate | na ca + asya kāye viṣaṃ krāmati | yaś ca + enaṃ ahir daśati saptadhā + asya sphuṭen mūrddhā arjakasya + iva mañjarī ||
body.translated_text: Whoever hears this <s>vidyā</s> (spell) even once is not bitten by a snake for seven years, nor does poison course through his body. And if a snake bites him, its head splits into seven pieces, like the blossom of the <s>arjaka</s> plant.

body.text: ya imāṃ vidyāṃ dhārayati sa yāvaj-jīvam ahinā na daśyate | na ca + asya kāye viṣaṃ krāmati | imāni ca mantra-padāni sarpasya purato na vaktavyāni yat-kāraṇaṃ sarpo mriyate ||
body.translated_text: Whoever holds this <s>vidyā</s> is not bitten by a snake for his entire life, nor does poison course through his body. And these <s>mantra</s>-words should not be spoken in front of a snake, for the reason that the snake would die.

body.text: tad yathā | illā | cillā | cakko | bakko | koḍā koḍeti | nikuruḍā nikuruḍeti | poḍā poḍeti | moḍā | moḍeti | puruḍā puruḍeti | phaṭa rahe | phuṭṭaṇḍa rahe | nāga rahe | nāgaṭṭaṇḍarahe | sarpa rahe | sarpaṭṭaṇḍarahe | acche | chala viṣaśāte | śītavattāle | halale | halale | taṇḍi | taḍa | tāḍi | mala | sphuṭa | phuṭu | svāhā ||
body.translated_text: Namely: '<s>Illā cillā cakko bakko koḍā koḍeti nikuruḍā nikuruḍeti poḍā poḍeti moḍā moḍeti puruḍā puruḍeti phaṭa rahe phuṭṭaṇḍa rahe nāga rahe nāgaṭṭaṇḍarahe sarpa rahe sarpaṭṭaṇḍarahe acche chala viṣaśāte śītavattāle halale halale taṇḍi taḍa tāḍi mala sphuṭa phuṭu svāhā</s>.'

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo jāṅgulyāṃ vidyāyāṃ udāhṛtāyāṃ sarva-bhūta-samāgate sarvaṃ tathā-a-vitathā-an-anyathā-bhūtaṃ satyam a-viparītam a-viparyastaṃ | idaṃ viṣam a-viṣaṃ bhavatu | dātāraṃ gacchatu | daṃṣṭrāraṃ gacchatu | agniṃ gacchatu | jalaṃ gacchatu | sthalaṃ gacchatu | stambhaṃ gacchatu | kuḍyaṃ gacchatu | bhūmiṃ saṃkrāmatu | śāntiṃ gacchatu svāhā ||
body.translated_text: 'Thus, O monks, when the <s>Jāṅgulī vidyā</s> has been recited, in the presence of all beings, all is true, not false, not otherwise, real, not inverted, not perverted. Let this poison become non-poison! Let it go to the giver [of the poison]! Let it go to the biter! Let it go to fire! Let it go to water! Let it go to dry land! Let it go to a pillar! Let it go to a wall! Let it pass into the earth! Let it go to peace! <s>Svāhā</s>!'

body.text: cora-ādi-pratīkāre mārīcīṃ japet ||
body.translated_text: For the antidote against thieves and so forth, one should recite the [dhāraṇī of] <s>Mārīcī</s>.

body.text: tad yathā | parākramasi | udayam asi | vairam asi arkam asi | markam asi | vanam asi | antar-ddhānam asi | pathe me rakṣa | utpathe me rakṣa | janato me rakṣa | caurato me rakṣa | rājato me rakṣa | siṃhato me rakṣa | vyāghrato me rakṣa | nāgato me rakṣa | sarpato me rakṣa | sarvato me rakṣa | rakṣa māṃ sarva-satvāṃś ca sarva-bhayebhyaḥ sarva-upāye sa-upasargebhyaḥ svāhā ||
body.translated_text: Namely: '<s>Parākramasi udayamasi vairamasi arkamasi markamasi vanamasi antardhānamasi</s>. Protect me on the path! Protect me off the path! Protect me from people! Protect me from thieves! Protect me from kings! Protect me from lions! Protect me from tigers! Protect me from <s>Nāgas</s>! Protect me from serpents! Protect me from everything! Protect me and all beings from all fears, from all dangers and calamities! <s>Svāhā</s>!'

body.text: uṃvaḍili sarva-duṣṭānāṃ granthiṃ vandāmi svāhā ||
body.translated_text: '<s>Uṃvaḍili</s> — I bind the knot of all evil-doers! <s>Svāhā</s>!'

body.text: namo ratna-trayāya | namo mārīcyai devatāyai | mārīcyā devatāyā hṛdayam āvartayiṣyāmi ||
body.translated_text: 'Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the deity <s>Mārīcī</s>! I shall recite the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart-mantra) of the deity <s>Mārīcī</s>.'

body.text: ta yathā | battāli | badāli | badāli | barāli | varāha-mukhi | sarva-duṣṭānāṃ nivāraya | bandha mukhaṃ svāhā ||
body.translated_text: Namely: '<s>Battāli badāli badāli barāli varāhamukhi</s> — ward off all evil-doers! Bind [their] mouths! <s>Svāhā</s>!'

body.text: imām api vidyām an-anta-jāti-smara-hetuṃ mahā-prabhāvāṃ sapta-pañcāśad-akṣarāṃ vidyā-dhara-piṭaka-upanibaddhāṃ sarva-bhaya-rakṣā-arthaṃ prayuñjīta ||
body.translated_text: One should also employ this <s>vidyā</s> — which is the cause of remembering innumerable past births, of great power, consisting of fifty-seven syllables, included in the <s>Vidyādhara-piṭaka</s> — for the purpose of protection against all fears.

body.text: tad yathā | aṭṭe | baṭṭe | naṭṭe | kunaṭṭe | ṭake | ṭhake | ṭharake | urumati | rurumati | turu | hili mili | sarva-jña-udupadagga

children.text: | namo sabba-samma-saṃbuddhāṇaṃ sijjhantu me manta-padāḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: '— <s>Namo sabba-samma-saṃbuddhāṇaṃ</s> (Homage to all perfectly awakened ones). May these <s>mantra</s>-words be efficacious for me! <s>Svāhā</s>!'

body.translated_text: Namely: '<s>Aṭṭe baṭṭe naṭṭe kunaṭṭe ṭake ṭhake ṭharake urumati rurumati turu hili mili sarvajña-udupadagga</s> —'

body.text: eṣā rakṣā + ātma-bhāvasya bhaiṣajya-vasana-ādibhiḥ | satva-artha-smṛti-pūrvakam eva vaktavyā ||
body.translated_text: This protection of one's own body — through medicine, clothing, and so forth — should be undertaken with mindfulness of the benefit of [other] beings.

body.text: ātma-tṛṣṇā-upabhogāt tu kliṣṭa-āpattiḥ prajāyate ||
body.translated_text: But from enjoying [things] with craving for oneself, a defiled transgression arises.

body.text: sarvaṃ hi bodhi-satvena + utsṛṣṭaṃ sarva-satvebhyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: For everything has been relinquished by the <s>bodhisattva</s> to all beings.

body.text: tatra yadi vismṛtya para-dravyam ātma-bharaṇa-tṛṣṇayā paribhuṅkte kliṣṭa-āpattim āpadyate | atha vi-tṛṣṇo * a-nyāsakto vā satva-kāryam anusmṛtya bhuṅkte na kliṣṭām āpattim āpadyate | para-dravya-saṃjñī sva-arthena bhuṅkte steya-āpattim āpadyate | pūra-argheṇa prātimokṣe pārājiko bhavati | satva-svāmikais tu bhogaiḥ satva-svāmika eva + ātma-bhāvaḥ saṃrakṣata ity a-doṣaḥ | na hi dāsasya nityaṃ svāmi-karma-vyāpṛtasya sva-dravyam asti yena varteta ||
body.translated_text: Therein, if, having forgotten, one consumes what belongs to others with craving for one's own sustenance — one incurs a defiled transgression. But if one consumes without craving, without attachment, recollecting the task of [benefiting] beings — one does not incur a defiled transgression. One who consumes for one's own sake with the perception of [using] what belongs to others incurs the transgression of theft. At full value, in the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>, one becomes <s>pārājika</s> (defeated). But since enjoyments belong to [all] beings as their owners, one's own body — which also belongs to [all] beings as its owners — is maintained [through them] — therefore there is no fault. For a servant, constantly engaged in the master's work, has no property of his own by which he would sustain himself.

body.text: uktaṃ ca dharma-saṅgīti-sūtre | dāsa-upamena bodhi-satvena bhavitavyaṃ sarva-satva-kiṅ-karaṇīya-prāpaṇatayā + iti ||
body.translated_text: And it is stated in the <s>Dharmasaṅgītisūtra</s>: 'The <s>bodhisattva</s> should be like a servant, in the sense of accomplishing whatever needs to be done for all beings.'

body.text: na ca + eka-anta-svāmy-artha-parasya dāsasya vyādhy-ādi-viklava-mateḥ svāminam an-anujñāpya + api bhuñjānasya kaś-cid doṣaḥ | na + apy evaṃ kurvāṇasya bodhi-satvasya + antike kasya-cid vidita-vṛttā-antasya + apy a-prasādo yujyate mātsarya-tyāga-citta-a-parijñānāt ||
body.translated_text: And for a servant who is entirely devoted to his master's purpose, who is confused in mind due to illness and so forth — there is no fault even if he eats without asking the master's permission. Nor is displeasure appropriate toward a <s>bodhisattva</s> who acts in this way, even on the part of someone who knows his circumstances, because of the failure to understand his mind of renouncing avarice.

body.text: na ca + atra nyāye kaś-cit saṃdeho yuktaḥ | sarva-utsargo hi pūrvam eva bhagavat-kaṇṭha-uktyā pratipāditaḥ | tathā ca + ātma-bhāva-rakṣā satva-artham eva + uktā | tasya spaṣṭa-avabodha-artham ayaṃ nyāyo * abhiyukto na tu sva-artha-apekṣayā + iti ||
body.translated_text: And here there should be no doubt about this principle. For the complete relinquishment [of everything to all beings] has already been established by the very words of the Blessed One. And similarly, the protection of one's own body has been stated to be for the sake of beings alone. This principle has been set forth for the purpose of clearly understanding that — not with regard to self-interest.

body.text: iti śikṣā-samuccaye ātma-bhāva-rakṣā ṣaṣṭhaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the sixth chapter of the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>: the protection of one's own body (<s>ātmabhāva-rakṣā</s>).

children.translated_text: VII. Protection of enjoyments and merit (<s>bhoga-puṇya-rakṣā</s>)

body.text: bhoga-puṇya-rakṣā saptamaḥ paricchedaḥ evaṃ tāvad ātma-bhāva-rakṣā veditavyā | bhoga-rakṣā tu vaktavyā | tatra su-kṛta-ārambhiṇā bhāvyaṃ mātra-jñena ca sarvata iti śikṣā-padād asya bhoga-rakṣā na duṣ-karā ||
body.translated_text: Protection of enjoyments and merit — the seventh chapter. Thus the protection of one's own body is to be understood as explained. But the protection of enjoyments must now be discussed. Therein, 'one should be well-intentioned in one's undertakings and moderate in all respects' — from this training-rule, the protection of enjoyments is not difficult for him.

body.text: ugra-paripṛcchāyāṃ hi śikṣā-padam uktaṃ | su-samīkṣita-karma-kāritā su-kṛta-karma-kāritā ca | tena bhogānāṃ dur-nyāsā pretyavekṣā | avajñā-pratiṣedhaḥ siddho bhavati | śamatha-prastāvena ca mātra-jñatā yukti-jñatā ca + uktā ||
body.translated_text: For in the <s>Ugraparipṛcchā</s>, the training-rule is stated: 'Acting with well-considered deeds and well-performed deeds.' By that, the examination of the misplacement of enjoyments with regard to the next life, and the prohibition against contempt, are established. And in the context of <s>śamatha</s> (calm), moderation and knowledge of what is proper have also been stated.

body.text: tena + idaṃ siddhaṃ bhavati | yad idaṃ | alpa-adhama-bhogena + api kārya-siddhau satyāṃ svayam anyair vā bahūttama-bhoga-nāśana-upekṣā na kāryā + iti ||
body.translated_text: By that, this is established: namely, that even when the accomplishment of one's purpose is achieved through small and lowly enjoyments, indifference toward the destruction of many excellent enjoyments — whether by oneself or by others — should not be maintained.

body.text: ata eva + ugra-paripṛcchāyām uktaṃ | putra-bhāryā-dāsī-dāsa-karma-kara-pauruṣeyāṇāṃ samyak-paribhogena + iti | tathā sva-para-bodhi-pakṣa-śruta-ādy-antarāya-karau tyāga-a-tyāgau na kāryau | adhika-satva-artha-śaktes tulya-śakter vā bodhi-satvasya + adhika-tulya-kuśala-antarāya-karau tyāga-a-tyāgau na kāryāv iti siddhaṃ bhavati + iti ||
body.translated_text: For this very reason, it is stated in the <s>Ugraparipṛcchā</s>: 'Through the proper use of sons, wives, female servants, male servants, workers, and attendants.' Likewise, giving and not-giving should not be done when they would create obstacles to one's own or others' factors of awakening, learning, and so forth. For a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has greater or equal capacity for the benefit of beings, giving and not-giving should not be done when they would create obstacles to greater or equal wholesome [activities] — this is established.

body.text: idaṃ ca saṃdhāya bodhi-satva-prātimokṣe * abhihitaṃ | yas tu khalu punaḥ śāriputra + abhiniṣkrānta-gṛha-āvāso bodhi-satvo bodhy-aṅgair abhiyuktas tena kathaṃ dānaṃ dātavyaṃ | kataraṃ dānaṃ dātavyaṃ | kiyad-rūpaṃ dānaṃ dātavyaṃ || pe ||
body.translated_text: And with this in mind, it is stated in the <s>Bodhisattvaprātimokṣa</s>: 'Now, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, for the <s>bodhisattva</s> who has gone forth from the household life and is devoted to the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅgas</s>) — how should he give? What kind of gift should he give? How much should he give?' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: dharma-dāyakena bhavitavyaṃ dharma-dāna-patinā | yaś ca śāriputra gṛhī bodhi-satvo gaṅgā-nadī-vālikā-samāni buddha-kṣetrāṇi sapta-ratna-pratipūrṇāni kṛtvā tathā-gatebhyo * arhadbhyaḥ samyak-saṃbuddhebhyo dānaṃ dadyād | yaś ca śāriputra pravrajyā-paryāpanno bodhi-satva ekāṃ catuṣ-padikāṃ gāthāṃ prakāśayed ayam eva tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati | na śāriputra tathā-gatena pravrajitasya + āmiṣa-dānam anujñātaṃ || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'He should be a giver of <s>Dharma</s>, a master of <s>Dharma</s>-giving. O <s>Śāriputra</s>, if a householder <s>bodhisattva</s>, having filled <s>Buddha</s>-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges with the seven treasures, were to give them to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s>, the perfectly awakened ones; and if, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has gone forth were to explain a single verse of four lines — this [latter one] produces far more merit than that [former one]. O <s>Śāriputra</s>, material giving (<s>āmiṣa-dāna</s>) has not been permitted by the <s>Tathāgata</s> for one who has gone forth.' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: yasya khalu punaḥ śāriputra pātra-āgataḥ pātra-paryāpanno lābho bhaved dhārmiko dharma-labdhaḥ | tena sādhāraṇa-bhojinā bhavitavyaṃ sārddhaṃ sa-brahma-cāribhiḥ | sacet punaḥ kaś-cid eva + āgatya pātraṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā yāceta | tasya + atiriktaṃ bhaved buddha-anujñātāt tri-cīvarād | yathā parityaktaṃ dātavyaṃ | sacet punas tasya + ūnaṃ cīvaraṃ bhaved yan niśritya brahma-carya-vāsaḥ | tan na parityaktavyaṃ | tat kasya hetoḥ | a-visarjanīyaṃ tri-cīvaram uktaṃ tathā-gatena | sacet punaḥ śāriputra bodhi-satvaḥ tri-cīvaraṃ parityajya yācanaka-guruko bhaven na tena + alpa-icchatā āsevitā bhavet | yas tu khalu punaḥ śāriputra + abhiniṣkrānta-gṛha-āvāso bodhi-satvas tena dharma āsevitavyaḥ | tan na tena + abhiyuktena bhavitavyam iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Now, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, for one whose gain — righteous and obtained through the <s>Dharma</s> — has come into his bowl and is contained within his bowl: he should be one who shares food together with his fellow practitioners of the holy life. If someone comes and asks for his bowl or his robe — if he has more than the three robes authorized by the <s>Buddha</s>, he should give the surplus as if it were already relinquished. But if his robe is less [than what is needed] — that upon which the life of celibacy depends — that should not be given up. For what reason? The <s>Tathāgata</s> has said that the three robes are not to be relinquished. If, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> were to give up the three robes and become one burdened by begging — by that, contentment with little would not be cultivated. Now, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> who has gone forth from the household life should cultivate the <s>Dharma</s>; he should not be devoted to that [begging].'

body.text: anyathā hy eka-saṃgraha-arthaṃ mahataḥ satva-rāśes tasya ca satvasya bodhi-satva-āśaya-parikarma-antarāyān mahato * arthasya hāniḥ kṛtā syād | ata eva + udāra-kuśala-pakṣa-vivarjanatā + apakṣāla ity ucyate | evaṃ tāvat tyāga-pratiṣedhaḥ | a-tyāga-pratiṣedho * api ||
body.translated_text: For otherwise, for the sake of gathering a single [person], the loss of a great purpose would be done — [namely,] the obstruction to the preparation of the <s>bodhisattva</s>-intention of a great multitude of beings, and of that being [himself]. For this very reason, the abandoning of the side of excellent wholesome [deeds] is called 'stain.' Thus the prohibition against giving [is stated]. The prohibition against not-giving also [follows]:

body.text: yathā + ārya-sāgaramati-sūtre mahā-yāna-antarāyeṣu bahu-lābhatā paṭhyate | yo * ayaṃ vidhir ātmany uktaḥ so * anyasminn api bodhi-satve pratipādya iti kuto gamyate | ārya-ugra-paripṛcchāyāṃ deśitatvāt | para-kṛtya-kāritaḥ sva-kārya-parityāga iti ||
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Ārya-Sāgaramati Sūtra</s>, obtaining many material gains is read [as an obstacle] among the hindrances to the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. That the procedure stated with regard to oneself should also be applied to another <s>bodhisattva</s> — whence is this understood? Because it is taught in the <s>Ārya-Ugraparipṛcchā</s>: 'Abandoning one's own interests for the sake of [fulfilling the tasks] of others.'

body.text: tathā + ārya-vimalakīrti-nirdeśe * apy uktaṃ | saṃsāra-bhaya-bhītena kiṃ pratisartavyam | āha | saṃsāra-bhaya-bhītena mañjuśrīr bodhi-satvena buddha-māhātmyaṃ pratisartavyaṃ | āha | buddha-māhātmya-sthātu-kāmena kutra sthātavyaṃ | āha | buddha-māhātmye sthātu-kāmena sarva-satva-samatāyāṃ sthātavyaṃ | āha | sarva-satva-samatāyāṃ sthātu-kāmena kutra sthātavyaṃ | āha |sarva-satva-samatāyāṃ sthātu-kāmena sarva-satva-pramokṣāya sthātavyam iti ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, in the <s>Ārya-Vimalakīrtinirdeśa</s> it is also said: 'What should one who fears the terror of <s>saṃsāra</s> resort to?' He says: 'O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who fears the terror of <s>saṃsāra</s> should resort to the greatness of the <s>Buddha</s>.' He says: 'One who wishes to abide in the greatness of the <s>Buddha</s> — where should he abide?' He says: 'One who wishes to abide in the greatness of the <s>Buddha</s> should abide in the equality of all beings.' He says: 'One who wishes to abide in the equality of all beings — where should he abide?' He says: 'One who wishes to abide in the equality of all beings should abide in the liberation of all beings.'

body.text: tathā ca dharma-saṅgītau sārthavāho bodhi-satva āha | yo bhagavan bodhi-satvaḥ sarva-satvānāṃ prathamataraṃ bodhim icchati na + ātmanaḥ | yāvad iyaṃ bhagavan dharma-saṅgītir iti ||
body.translated_text: And likewise, in the <s>Dharmasaṅgīti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sārthavāha</s> said: 'The <s>bodhisattva</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, who desires awakening for all beings first, rather than for himself — this, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the <s>Dharma</s>-assembly.'

body.text: utsargād eva ca + asya sva-artha-a-bhāvaḥ siddhaḥ | kiṃ tu satva-artha-hāni-bhayād a-yogye satve su-bharaṃ na + āropayati | yatra tu satva-artha-hāniṃ na paśyati tatra svayaṃ kṛtam anyena vā jagad * dhitam ācaritam iti ko viśeṣo | yad ayam a-para-bodhi-satva-kuśala-siddhaye na sva-kuśalam utsṛjati | atha sva-dur-gati-duṣkha-d bibheti | dvitīyasya + api tad eva duṣkhaṃ | atha tad-duṣkhena me bādhā na + asti + ity upekṣate | yathā + uktaiḥ sūtraiḥ sa-āpattiko bhavati ||
body.translated_text: And by the very act of relinquishment, the absence of self-interest is established. However, out of fear of harming the interests of beings, one does not place a heavy burden upon an unsuitable being. But where one does not see harm to the interests of beings, then what difference does it make whether what is done by oneself or by another is conducted for the benefit of the world? [One might ask:] 'Why does he not abandon his own wholesomeness for the accomplishment of another <s>bodhisattva</s>'s wholesomeness?' If he fears the suffering of his own bad destiny, [he should reflect:] 'That other [being] has exactly the same suffering.' If he remains indifferent, [thinking:] 'That suffering causes me no harm' — then by the <s>sūtras</s> stated [above], he incurs a transgression.

body.text: yathā ca ratna-kūṭa-sūtre | catvāra ime kāśyapa bodhi-satva-prati-rūpakā ity ārabhya + uktaṃ | ātma-sukha-arthiko bhavati na sarva-satva-duṣkha-apanayana-arthika iti ||
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Ratnakūṭa Sūtra</s>: 'There are these four, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, who are counterfeits of <s>bodhisattvas</s>' — beginning thus it is said — 'one who seeks happiness for himself and does not seek to remove the suffering of all beings.'

body.text: tasmād ugra-paripṛcchā-vidhinā pūrva-vad ātmā garhaṇīyaḥ eṣā tu bodhi-satva-śikṣā yathā + ārya-nir-ārambheṇa dharma-saṅgīti-sūtre nirdiṣṭā | kathaṃ kula-putrāḥ pratipatti-sthīta veditavyāḥ | āha | yadā satveṣu na vipratipadyante | āha | kathaṃ satveṣu na vipratipadyante | āha | yan maitrīṃ ca mahā-karuṇāṃ ca na tyajanti | subhūtir āha | katamā bodhi-satvānāṃ mahā-maitrī | āha | yat kāya-jīvitaṃ ca sarva-kuśala-mūlaṃ ca sarva-satvānāṃ niryātayanti na ca pratikāraṃ kāṅkṣanti | āha | katamā bodhi-satvānāṃ mahā-karuṇā | yat pūrvataraṃ satvānāṃ bodhim icchanti na + ātmana iti ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, in the manner [prescribed in] the <s>Ugraparipṛcchā</s>, one should censure oneself as before. But this <s>bodhisattva</s> training is as the noble <s>Nirārambha</s> expounded it in the <s>Dharmasaṅgīti Sūtra</s>: 'How should sons of good family who abide in practice be understood?' He says: 'When they do not go wrong with regard to beings.' He says: 'How do they not go wrong with regard to beings?' He says: 'When they do not abandon loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>).' <s>Subhūti</s> says: 'What is the great loving-kindness of <s>bodhisattvas</s>?' He says: 'That they hand over their body, life, and all wholesome roots to all beings, and do not expect anything in return.' He says: 'What is the great compassion of <s>bodhisattvas</s>?' 'That they desire awakening for beings first, rather than for themselves.'

body.text: atra + eva ca + āha | mahā-karuṇā-mūlāḥ sarva-bodhi-satva-śikṣā iti | a-vaśyaṃ ca bhagavatā + idaṃ na nivāraṇīyaṃ | anyatara-bodhi-satva-arthe na + arthitvād a-vaśyaṃ tu + upadiśati + iti niścīyate | yena dātur mahā-dakṣiṇīye mahā-artha-dānān mahā-puṇya-sāgara-vistaro dṛśyate | anyathā tu kevalam eva vighātino maraṇaṃ syāt ||
body.translated_text: And in this same [sūtra] it says: 'All <s>bodhisattva</s> trainings have great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) as their root.' And the <s>Bhagavān</s> must certainly not prohibit this — it is determined that he does not seek [anything] for the sake of some [particular] <s>bodhisattva</s>, but instructs all without exception. By this, the vast ocean of great merit is seen from the gift of great value by a donor to a supremely worthy recipient. Otherwise, it would be merely the death of one who destroys [himself].

body.text: yat tu praśānta-viniścaya-prātihārya-sūtre deśitam | ya eṣa te mahā-rāja varṣa-śata-sahasreṇa parivyayo * atra praviṣṭaḥ sa sarvaḥ piṇḍī-kṛtya + ekasya bhikṣor yātrā bhaved evaṃ praty-ekaṃ sarva-bhikṣūṇāṃ | yaś ca + uddeśa-sva-adhyāya-abhiyukto bodhi-satvaḥ sa-gauravo dharma-ka-maḥ śraddhā-deyam āhāraṃ parigṛhya + evaṃ cittam utpādayet | anena + ahaṃ dharma-paryeṣṭim āpatsyae iti | asya kuśalasya + eṣa deya-dharma-parityāgaḥ śatatamīm api kalāṃ na + upaiti + iti ||
body.translated_text: As taught in the <s>Praśāntaviniścayaprātihārya Sūtra</s>: 'O great king, all the expenditure you have incurred over a hundred thousand years — all of that, collected together, would [only] amount to the sustenance of a single monk, and likewise for each and every monk individually. But a <s>bodhisattva</s> who is devoted to recitation and study, who reveres the <s>Dharma</s> and is desirous of it, having accepted food given out of faith, should generate the thought: "By this, I shall pursue the quest for <s>Dharma</s>." The relinquishment of what is to be given for the sake of this wholesomeness does not amount to even a hundredth part [of the merit of that Dharma-quest].'

body.text: tad gṛha-sukha-paliśuddham adhikṛtya + uktaṃ | na tu pūrva-ukta-vidhinā kaś-cid doṣaḥ ||
body.translated_text: That was stated with reference to the impurity [associated with] household pleasures. But there is no fault in the procedure stated previously [for monks].

body.text: ukto samāsatā bhoga-rakṣā | puṇya-rakṣā vācyā | tatra sva-artha-vipāka-vaitṛṣṇyāc * chubhaṃ saṃrakṣitaṃ bhavet ||
body.translated_text: The protection of enjoyments has been stated in summary. The protection of merit is to be stated. Therein: through freedom from craving for the fruit of one's own benefit, the wholesome [merit] becomes protected.

body.text: yathā + uktaṃ nārāyaṇa-paripṛcchāyāṃ | sa na + ātma-hetoḥ śīlaṃ rakṣati | na svarga-hetoḥ | na śakratva-hetoḥ | na bhoga-hetoḥ | na + aiśvarya-hetoḥ | na rūpa-hetor na varṇa-hetor na yaśo-hetoḥ | pe ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Nārāyaṇaparipṛcchā</s>: 'He does not guard moral conduct for his own sake; not for the sake of heaven; not for the sake of becoming <s>Śakra</s>; not for the sake of enjoyments; not for the sake of sovereignty; not for the sake of beauty, not for complexion, not for fame.' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: na niraya-bhaya-bhi-taḥ śīlaṃ rakṣati | pe ||
body.translated_text: 'He does not guard moral conduct out of fear of the hells.' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: evaṃ na tiryag-yoni-bhaya-bhītaḥ śīlaṃ rakṣati | anyatra buddha-netrī-pratiṣṭhāpanāya śīlaṃ rakṣati | yāvat sarva-satva-hita-sukha-yoga-kṣema-arthikaḥ śīlaṃ rakṣati ||
body.translated_text: 'Likewise, he does not guard moral conduct out of fear of the animal realm. Rather, he guards moral conduct for the purpose of establishing the <s>Buddha</s>-vision. He guards moral conduct as one who seeks the welfare, happiness, and security of all beings.'

body.text: sa evaṃ-rūpeṇa śīla-skandhena samanvāgato bodhi-satvo daśabhir dharmair na hīyate | katamair daśabhiḥ | yad uta na cakra-varti-rājyāt parihīyate | tatra ca bhavaty a-pramatto bodhi-pratikāṅkṣī buddha-darśanam abhikāṅkṣate | evaṃ brahmatvād buddha-darśana-a-bhedya-pratilambhād dharma-śravaṇān na parihīyate | yāvad yathā-śruta-pratipatti-saṃpādanāya bodhi-satva-saṃvara-samādānān na parihīyate | an-āchedya-pratibhānāt sarva-kuśala-dharma-prārthana-dhyānān na parihīyate ||
body.translated_text: 'The <s>bodhisattva</s> endowed with such an aggregate of moral conduct (<s>śīla-skandha</s>) does not fall away from ten <s>dharmas</s>. Which ten? Namely, he does not fall away from the kingship of a <s>cakravartin</s>; and therein he is diligent, aspiring toward <s>bodhi</s>, longing for the sight of the <s>Buddha</s>. Likewise, [he does not fall away] from the state of <s>Brahmā</s>, from the attainment of unbroken <s>Buddha</s>-vision, [nor] from hearing the <s>Dharma</s>; he does not fall away from undertaking the <s>bodhisattva</s> vow for the sake of accomplishing practice in accord with what he has heard; he does not fall away from <s>dhyāna</s> that aspires to all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, [resulting in] unbroken eloquence.'

body.text: evaṃ śīla-skandha-pratiṣṭhito bodhi-satvo mahā-satvaḥ sadā namas-kṛto bhavati devaiḥ | sadā praśaṃsito bhavati nāgaiḥ | sadā namas-kṛto bhavati yakṣaiḥ | sadā pūjito bhavati gandharvaiḥ sadā + apacāyitaś ca bhavati nāga-indra-asura-indraiḥ | sadā su-mānitaś ca bhavati brāhmaṇa-kṣatriya-śreṣṭhi-gṛha-patibhiḥ | sadā + abhigamanīyaś ca bhavati paṇḍitaiḥ | sadā samanvāhṛtaś ca bhavati buddhaiḥ | śāstṛ-saṃmataś ca bhavati sa-devakasya lokasya + anukampakaś ca bhavati sarva-satvānāṃ || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> thus established in the aggregate of moral conduct is always bowed to by the gods; always praised by the <s>nāgas</s>; always bowed to by the <s>yakṣas</s>; always worshipped by the <s>gandharvas</s>; always honored by the lords of the <s>nāgas</s> and lords of the <s>asuras</s>; always esteemed by <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, merchants, and householders; always approached by the wise; always remembered by the <s>Buddhas</s>; regarded as a teacher by the world with its gods; and compassionate toward all beings.' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: catasro gatīr na gacchati | katamāś catasro | yad uta + a-kṣaṇa-gatiṃ na gacchaty anyatra satva-paripākāt | buddha-śūnya-buddha-kṣetraṃ na gacchati | mithyā-dṛṣṭi-kula-upapattiṃ na gacchati | sarva-dur-gati-gatiṃ na gacchati ||
body.translated_text: 'He does not go to four destinies. Which four? He does not go to the destiny of unfavorable conditions, except for the sake of ripening beings. He does not go to a <s>Buddha</s>-field devoid of a <s>Buddha</s>. He does not go to birth in a family of wrong views. He does not go to any lower destiny.'

body.text: evaṃ pūrva-utsṛṣṭasya + api puṇyasya kleśa-vaśāt punar upādīyamānasya rakṣā kāryā | puṇya-dānād api yat puṇyaṃ tato * api na vipākaḥ prārthanīyo * anyatra para-arthāt | kiṃ ca puṇyaṃ rakṣitu-kāmaḥ | paścāt tāpaṃ na kurvīta ||
body.translated_text: Thus, even merit previously relinquished, when taken up again through the power of the afflictions, should be protected. Even from the giving away of merit, whatever merit [results] — even from that, the fruit should not be desired, except for the sake of others. Moreover, one who wishes to protect merit should not afterward generate remorse.

body.text: yathā + uktam ugra-paripṛcchāyāṃ | dattvā ca na vipratisāra-cittam utpādayitavyam iti ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Ugraparipṛcchā</s>: 'Having given, one should not generate a mind of regret.'

body.text: pṛṣṭha-daurbalyād daurbalyaṃ | vipratisārāt pāpa-vat puṇyasya + api kṣayaḥ syād ity abhiprāyaḥ | na ca kṛtvā prakāśayed | an-eka-paryāyeṇa hi bhagavatā prachanna-kalyāṇatā | vivṛta-pāpatā varṇitā | tatra vivṛtasay kṣayo gamyate | pāpasya daurmanasyena + eva puṇyasya saumanasyena + āpattiḥ satva-arthaṃ nir-āmiṣa-cittasya prakāśayataḥ ||
body.translated_text: From the weakness of the follow-through comes weakness. The intent is: from regret, even merit — like sin — would be diminished. And one should not publicize what one has done. For in many ways the <s>Bhagavān</s> has praised concealment of virtues and disclosure of sins. From that, it is understood that what is disclosed is diminished. Regarding sin, through despondency itself [it is diminished]; regarding merit, through elation [comes] the transgression — [except] for one who publicizes with a selfless mind for the sake of beings.

body.text: yathā ratna-meghe vaidya-dṛṣṭa-antena ātma-utkarṣo nir-doṣa uktaḥ | punaḥ puṇya-rakṣā kāmo lābha-sat-kāra-bhītaḥ syād unnatiṃ varjayet sadā | bodhi-satvo prasannaḥ syād dharme vimatim utsṛjet ||
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Ratnamegha</s>, self-exaltation using the analogy of a physician is said to be faultless. Furthermore, one who wishes to protect merit should be afraid of gain and honor, and should always avoid elation. A <s>bodhisattva</s> should be serene; he should abandon doubt regarding the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: idaṃ ca ratna-kūṭe * abhihitaṃ | caturbhiḥ kāśyapa dharmaiḥ samanvāgatasya bodhi-satvasya + utpanna-utpannāḥ kuśalā dharmāḥ parihīyante | yaiḥ caturbhir muktāḥ na vardhante kuśala-dharmaiḥ | katamaiś caturbhiḥ | yad uta + abhimānikasya loka-āyata-mantra-paryeṣṭyā | lābha-sat-kāra-adhyavasitasya kula-pratyavalokanena | bodhi-satva-vidveṣa-abhyākhyānena | a-śrutānām a-nirdiṣṭānāṃ ca sūtra-antānāṃ pratikṣepeṇa + iti ||
body.translated_text: And this is stated in the <s>Ratnakūṭa</s>: 'O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> endowed with four <s>dharmas</s> has his wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, as soon as they arise, diminished — freed from which four, wholesome <s>dharmas</s> do not increase. Which four? Namely: the pursuit of worldly treatises and <s>mantras</s> by one who is conceited; the scrutiny of families by one absorbed in gain and honor; malicious accusation against <s>bodhisattvas</s>; and rejection of <s>sūtra</s>-conclusions that one has not heard and that have not been expounded.'
