body.text: ārya-sarva-asti-vādānāṃ ca paṭhyate | paśyadhvaṃ bhikṣava etaṃ bhikṣuṃ keśa-nakha-stūpe sarva-aṅgena praṇipatya cittam abhiprasādayantam |evaṃ bhadanta | anena bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇā yāvatī bhūmir ākrāntā + adhara-śīti-yojana-sahasrāṇi yāvat kāñcana-cakraṃ | atra + antare yāvantyā vālikās tāvanty anena bhikṣuṇā cakra-varti-rājya-sahasrāṇi paribhoktavyāni | yāvad atha + āyuṣmān upālir yena bhagavān tena + añjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantam idam avocat | yad uktaṃ bhagavatā + asya bhikṣor evaṃ mahānti kuśala-mūlāni | kutra + imāni bhagavan kuśala-mūlāni tanutvaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gacchanti | na + aham upāle evaṃ kṣatiṃ ca + upahatiṃ ca samanupaśyāmi | yathā sa-brahma-cārī sa-brahma-cāriṇo * antike duṣṭa-cittam utpādayati | atra + upāle imāni mahānti kuśala-mūlāni tanutvaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gacchanti | tasmāt tarhy upāle evaṃ śikṣitavyaṃ yad dagdha-sthūṇāyām api cittaṃ na pradūṣayiṣyāmaḥ | prāg eva sa-vijñānake kāya iti ||
body.translated_text: And of the <s>Ārya-Sarvāstivādins</s> it is read: 'Look, O monks, at this monk generating faith in his mind by prostrating with his entire body at a <s>stūpa</s> of hair and nails. — Indeed so, Venerable One. — O monks, that monk, for as much ground as has been covered [by his body] — eighty thousand <s>yojanas</s> below down to the golden circle — however many grains of sand there are in that interval, that many thousands of <s>cakravartin</s> kingdoms will he enjoy.' And then the venerable <s>Upāli</s>, joining his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared such great wholesome roots for this monk. Where, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, do these wholesome roots go to diminution, exhaustion, and complete consumption?' — 'I do not, O <s>Upāli</s>, see such damage and injury as when a fellow celibate generates a hostile mind toward a fellow celibate. Here, O <s>Upāli</s>, these great wholesome roots go to diminution, exhaustion, and complete consumption. Therefore, <s>Upāli</s>, one should train thus: "We shall not corrupt our minds even toward a burnt post, how much less toward a body endowed with consciousness!"'

body.text: ārya-mañjuśrī-vikrīḍita-sūtre * apy āha | pratighaḥ pratigha iti kalpa-śata-upacitaṃ kuśala-mūlaṃ pratihanti tena + ucyate pratigha iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Mañjuśrīvikrīḍita Sūtra</s> it also says: '<s>Pratigha</s> (hostility), <s>pratigha</s> — it destroys wholesome roots accumulated over a hundred <s>kalpas</s>; therefore it is called <s>pratigha</s> (that which strikes back).'

body.text: ārya-gaṇḍa-vyūha-sūtre ca samanta-satva-paritrāṇy ojasaḥ striyā rātri-devatayā pūrva-avadānaṃ kathayantyā + abhihitaṃ | te tena + anyo-nya-avamanyana-a-samuditena + a-kuśala-mūlena + āyuḥ-pramāṇād api parihīyante sma | varṇād api balād api parihīyante sma + iti | atra ca na kadā-cid unnatiḥ kāryā + iti pradarśana-arthaṃ sadā + ity ucyate ||
body.translated_text: And in the <s>Ārya-Gaṇḍavyūha Sūtra</s>, the night-goddess <s>Samantasattvaparitṛāṇyojas</s>, while narrating a previous story, said: 'By that unwholesome root of mutual contempt which arose [among them], they declined even from their lifespan; they declined from their complexion and their strength.' And here, to show that one should never at any time be haughty, the word 'always' is used.

body.text: lābha-sat-kāras tu kadā-cid abhyupagamyate * api | yathā + uktaṃ ārya-ratna-meghe | iha kula-putra bodhi-satvaḥ sumeru-mātram api ratna-rāśiṃ labhamānaḥ pratigṛhṇāti | pratyavaram api vastu pratilabhamānaḥ | tat kasya hetoḥ | tasya + evaṃ bhavati | ete satvā matsariṇo lubdhā lobha-abhibhūtāḥ | tad-dhetoḥ tat-pratyayaṃ tan-nidānaṃ mahā-vāri-skandha-avaṣṭabdā iva saṃsāra-sāgare unmajja-nimajjanaṃ kurvanti | tad eṣāṃ bhaviṣyati dīrgha-rātram arthāya hitāya sukhāya | sarvaṃ pratigṛhya na svī-karoti | na lobha-cittam utpādayati | anyatra sarva-satva-sādhāraṇāṃ buddha-dharma-saṃgheṣu kārāṃ karoti | yathā duṣkhitānāṃ ca sarva-satvānām upajīvyaṃ karoti |taṃ ca dāna-patiṃ samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati + iti ||
body.translated_text: However, <s>lābhasatkāra</s> (gain and honor) is sometimes accepted. As stated in the <s>Ārya-Ratnamegha</s>: "Here, O son of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s>, even when obtaining a heap of jewels the size of <s>Sumeru</s>, accepts it; even when obtaining the most inferior thing, he accepts it. For what reason? He thinks thus: 'These beings are miserly, greedy, overcome by greed; on that account, for that reason, from that cause, as if weighed down by a great mass of water, they rise and sink in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>. This will be for their long-term welfare, benefit, and happiness.' Having accepted everything, he does not make it his own. He does not give rise to a mind of greed. Rather, he makes offerings to the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s> for the common benefit of all beings. Thus he makes it a means of sustenance for all suffering beings. And he encourages and delights that <s>dānapati</s> (patron of giving)."

body.text: tathā + atra + eva + uktaṃ | tena ca dānena na + unnato bhavati + iti ||
body.translated_text: And likewise it is stated in that very text: "And by that giving, he does not become elated."

body.text: punar atra + eva + āha | yadi punar asya tad-dhetos tat-pratyayaṃ tan-nidānaṃ kīrti-śabda-śloko bhavati tatra na + unnāma-jāto bhavati na māna-jāto na mada-jātaḥ | evaṃ ca + asya bhavati | na cireṇa kālena yasya ca + ayaṃ kīrti-śloka-śabdaḥ samutthito yaiś ca samutthāpito yaś ca kīrti-śabda-ślokas trayam apy etat sarveṇa sarvaṃ na bhaviṣyati | tatra kaḥ paṇḍita-jātīyo * a-nityeṣu na ca sthiteṣu dharmeṣv a-dhruveṣv an-āśvāsikeṣv anunaya-cittam utpādayed unnato bhaven māna-darpito vā | evaṃ hi bodhi-satvo lābha-sat-kāra-kīrti-śabda-ślokeṣu su-upasthita-smṛtir viharati + iti ||
body.translated_text: Again in that very text it says: "If, however, on that account, for that reason, from that cause, fame, renown, and praise arise for him, he does not become puffed up, does not become proud, does not become intoxicated. And he thinks thus: 'Before long, he from whom this fame, renown, and praise has arisen, those by whom it was raised up, and the fame, renown, and praise itself—all three will entirely cease to exist. What person of wise nature would, regarding things that are impermanent, unstable, unreliable, and not enduring, give rise to a mind of attachment, become elated, or be filled with pride and arrogance?' Thus the <s>bodhisattva</s> dwells with well-established mindfulness regarding gain, honor, fame, renown, and praise."

body.text: punar āha | caṇḍāla-kumāra-upamāś ca loke viharanti nīca-nīcena manasā | māna-mada-darpa-adhigatāś ca bhavanti paiśunya-saṃjñāyāḥ satata-samitaṃ pratyupasthitatvād iti ||
body.translated_text: Again it says: "And they dwell in the world like a <s>caṇḍāla</s> youth, with a lowly and humble mind; and they become free from pride, intoxication, and arrogance, because of constantly and continuously being on guard against the perception of slander."

body.text: punar apy uktaṃ | iha kula-putra + abhiniṣkrānta-gṛha-vāsaḥ pravrajito bodhi-satvo mṛtaka-sadṛśo * ahaṃ mitra-amātya-jñāti-sālohitānām iti nihatamāno bhavati | vairūpyaṃ me * abhyudgataṃ vi-varṇāni ca me vāsāṃsi prāvṛtāny anyaś ca me ākalpaḥ saṃvṛtta iti nihatamāno bhavati | muṇḍaḥ pātra-pāṇiḥ kulāt kulam upasaṃkramāmi bhikṣā-hetor bhikṣā-nidānam iti nihatamāno bhavati | nīca-nīcena cittena caṇḍāla-kumāra-sadṛśena piṇḍāya carāmi + iti nihatamāno bhavati | paiṇḍiliko * asmi saṃvṛtaḥ | para-pratibaddhā ca me jīvikā + iti nihatamāno bhavati | avadhūtam avajñātaṃ pratigṛhṇāmi + iti nihatamāno bhavati | ārādhanīyā me ācārya-guru-dakṣiṇīyā iti nihatamāno bhavati | saṃtoṣaṇīyā me sa-brahma-cāriṇo | yad uta tena tena + ācāra-go-cara-samudācāreṇa + iti nihatamāno bhavati | a-pratilabdha-anubaddha-dharmān pratipatsyae iti nihatamāno bhavati | kruddhānāṃ vyāpanna-cittānāṃ satvānāṃ madhye kṣānti-bahulo vihariṣyāmi + iti nihatamāno bhavati + iti ||
body.translated_text: Again it is stated: "Here, O son of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has gone forth from the household life and become a renunciant, dwells with humbled mind, thinking: 'I am as one dead to my friends, ministers, relatives, and kinsmen.' He dwells with humbled mind, thinking: 'Disfigurement has come upon me, and I wear discolored garments, and my appearance has become different.' He dwells with humbled mind, thinking: 'With shaven head, bowl in hand, I go from family to family for the sake of alms, on account of alms.' He dwells with humbled mind, thinking: 'With a lowly and humble mind, like a <s>caṇḍāla</s> youth, I go about for alms-food.' He dwells with humbled mind, thinking: 'I have become a mendicant, and my livelihood depends on others.' He dwells with humbled mind, thinking: 'I accept what is rejected and despised.' He dwells with humbled mind, thinking: 'I must please my teachers, elders, and those worthy of offerings.' He dwells with humbled mind, thinking: 'I must satisfy my fellow practitioners in the holy life, namely through proper conduct, practice, and deportment.' He dwells with humbled mind, thinking: 'I shall attain the teachings that I have not yet obtained and grasped.' He dwells with humbled mind, thinking: 'Among beings who are angry and hostile in mind, I shall dwell abounding in patience.'"

body.text: ārya-sāgaramati-sūtre * apy uktaṃ | sat-kāya-pariśuddhaś ca bhavati | lakṣaṇa-samalaṃ-kṛta-gātra-mṛdu-taruṇa-hasta-pādaḥ sva-vibhakta-puṇya-niṣyanda-gātro * a-hīna-indriyaḥ sarva-aṅga-praty-aṅga-paripūrṇaḥ | na ca rūpa-mada-matto bhavati | na kāya-maṇḍana-yoga-anuyuktaḥ | sa kiyad * dhīnānām api satvānāṃ rūpa-vikalānām apy avanamati praṇamati dharma-grāhyatām upādāya + iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Sāgaramati-sūtra</s> also it is stated: "And he becomes purified in body; with limbs adorned with the marks, with soft and tender hands and feet, with a body that is the outflow of well-distributed merit, with unimpaired faculties, complete in all major and minor limbs. Yet he does not become intoxicated with pride in his beauty, nor is he devoted to adorning the body. He bows down and pays respect even to beings who are greatly inferior and deficient in appearance, for the sake of receptivity to the <s>Dharma</s>."

body.text: punar atra + eva + uktaṃ | syād yathā + api nāma bhagavan yadā mahā-sāgaraḥ pratisaṃtiṣṭhate tadā nimne pṛthivī-pradeśe saṃtiṣṭhate | tasya nimnatvād alpa-kṛcchreṇa sarva-nadyaś ca sarva-praśravaṇāni ca prapatanti | evam eva bhagavan nir-mānasya guru-dakṣiṇīya-gauravasya bodhi-satvasya + alpa-kṛcchreṇa tāni gambhīrāṇi dharma-sukhāni śrota-indriyasya + ābhāsam āgacchanti | smṛtau ca + avatiṣṭhante | tasmāt tarhi bhagavan yo bodhi-satvo māna-unnato bhavati māna-stabdhaḥ na ca guru-dakṣiṇīyebhyo * avanamati na praṇamati veditavyaṃ bhagavan māra-aṅkuśa-āviddho vata + ayaṃ bodhi-satva iti ||
body.translated_text: Again in that very text it is stated: "Just as, Lord, when the great ocean comes to rest, it settles in the low-lying regions of the earth, and because of its low position, all rivers and all streams flow into it with little difficulty—even so, Lord, for a <s>bodhisattva</s> who is free from pride and who reveres his teachers and those worthy of offerings, those profound joys of the <s>Dharma</s> come within range of his faculty of hearing with little difficulty, and they remain in his mindfulness. Therefore, Lord, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who is elevated by pride, rigid with pride, and who does not bow down or pay respect to his teachers and those worthy of offerings—it should be understood, Lord, that this <s>bodhisattva</s> is pierced by the goad of <s>Māra</s>."

body.text: ārya-loka-uttara-parivarte ca + uktaṃ | daśa + imāni bho jina-putra bodhi-satvānāṃ māra-karmāṇi | katamāni daśa | yad idaṃ guru-dakṣiṇīya-ācārya-mātā-pitṛ-śramaṇa-brāhmaṇa-samyag-gata-samyak-pratipanneṣv a-gauravatā māra-karma | dharma-bhāṇakānāṃ viśiṣṭa-dharma-adhigatānām udāra-dharma-deśakānāṃ mahā-yāna-samārūḍhānāṃ nirvāṇa-patha-vidhi-jñānāṃ dhāraṇī-sūtra-anta-rāja-pratilabdhānāṃ na + avanamati | garvita-stabdhaś ca bhavati | dharma-bhāṇake na gauravam utpādayati | na śuśrūṣāṃ na citrī-kāraṃ karoti | māra-karma dharma-śravaṇa-sāṃkathye ca niṣaṇṇae udāra-dharma-vege samutpanne dharma-bhāṇakasya sādhu-kāraṃ na prayacchati mā kaś-cid asmin praśaṃsati + iti māra-karma ||
body.translated_text: And in the <s>Ārya-Lokottaraparivarta</s> it is stated: "There are these ten forms of <s>mārakarma</s> (works of Māra) for <s>bodhisattvas</s>, O son of the <s>Jina</s>. What are the ten? Namely: disrespect toward teachers, those worthy of offerings, preceptors, mother, father, <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and those who have rightly gone and rightly practiced—this is <s>mārakarma</s>. He does not bow down to preachers of the <s>Dharma</s>, to those who have attained distinguished <s>Dharma</s>, to noble teachers of the <s>Dharma</s>, to those who have mounted the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, to those who know the method of the path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, to those who have obtained the king of <s>dhāraṇī</s>-sūtras; and he is haughty and rigid. He does not show respect to the preacher of the <s>Dharma</s>, does not render service, does not show honor. This is <s>mārakarma</s>. And when seated at a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, when a noble surge of <s>Dharma</s> has arisen, he does not offer applause to the preacher of the <s>Dharma</s>, thinking 'Let no one praise him'—this is <s>mārakarma</s>."

body.text: abhimānaṃ ca + utpādya + ātmānaṃ pratigṛhṇāti | parāṃś ca na gṛhṇāti | ātma-jñatāṃ ca na + avatarati | citta-nidhyaptiṃ na + utpādayati | māra-karma ||
body.translated_text: "And having given rise to <s>abhimāna</s> (conceit), he clings to himself and does not acknowledge others. He does not enter into self-knowledge, and does not give rise to mental reflection. This is <s>mārakarma</s>."

body.text: adhimānaṃ ca + utpādya + a-jānann a-budhyamāno varṇa-arhāṇāṃ pudgalānāṃ varṇaṃ praticchādayati | a-varṇaṃ bhāṣate | na ca parasya guṇa-varṇena + ātta-manā bhavati | māra-karma ||
body.translated_text: "And having given rise to <s>adhimāna</s> (overweening pride), without knowing, without understanding, he conceals the virtues of persons worthy of praise, speaks ill of them, and does not rejoice in the praise of others' good qualities. This is <s>mārakarma</s>."

body.text: jānāti ca | ayaṃ dharmo * ayaṃ vinayo bhūtam idaṃ buddha-vacanam iti | pudgala-vidveṣeṇa dharma-vidveṣaṃ karoti | sad-dharmaṃ pratikṣipati | anyāṃś ca vigrāhayati | māra-karma ||
body.translated_text: "He knows: 'This is the <s>Dharma</s>, this is the <s>Vinaya</s>, this is true, this is the word of the <s>Buddha</s>.' Yet out of personal animosity he engenders hatred of the <s>Dharma</s>, rejects the true <s>Dharma</s>, and causes others to quarrel. This is <s>mārakarma</s>."

body.text: ucca-mānasaṃ prārthayate parihāra-dharmaṃ na mārgayati | para-upasthānaṃ so * abhiyāti | abhinandati | vṛddha-sthavirāṇāṃ cira-carita-brahma-caryāṇāṃ na pratyupatiṣṭhate na ca pratyudgacchati | māra-karma ||
body.translated_text: "He aspires to high honor, does not seek the <s>Dharma</s> of self-restraint. He goes to be attended upon by others, and delights in it. He does not rise up to receive or go out to meet the elders and seniors who have long practiced the holy life. This is <s>mārakarma</s>."

body.text: bhṛkuṭī-mukhaḥ khalu punar bhavati | na smita-mukhaḥ | na khila madhura-vacanaḥ | sadā kaṭhina-cittaś chidra-anveṣī ||
body.translated_text: "Moreover, he is frowning-faced, not smiling-faced, not sweet-spoken; always hard-hearted, searching for faults,"

body.text: avatāra-prekṣī | māra-karma ||
body.translated_text: "looking for openings to attack. This is <s>mārakarma</s>."

body.text: abhimānaṃ ca patitvā paṇḍitān na + upasaṃkrāmati | na sevate | na bhajate | na paryupāste | na paripraśnayati | na paripṛcchati | kiṃ kuśalaṃ kim a-kuśalaṃ kiṃ karaṇīyaṃ kiṃ kṛtaṃ dīrgha-rātram arthāya hitāya sukhāya bhavati | kiṃ vā + a-kṛtaṃ dīrgha-rātram an-arthāya + a-hitāya + a-sukhāya bhavati + iti | sajaḍaḥ sajaḍataro bhavati | moha-vyūho māna-grāhī | a-niḥsaraṇa-darśī | māra-karma ||
body.translated_text: "And having fallen into conceit, he does not approach the wise, does not attend upon them, does not serve them, does not honor them, does not inquire of them, does not ask: 'What is <s>kuśala</s> (wholesome)? What is <s>akuśala</s> (unwholesome)? What should be done? What, when done, leads to long-term welfare, benefit, and happiness? And what, when not done, leads to long-term harm, detriment, and suffering?' Being dull, he becomes even duller; entangled in delusion, gripped by pride, seeing no way out. This is <s>mārakarma</s>."

body.text: saa māna-abhibhūto buddha-utpādaṃ virāgayati | pūrva-kuśala-mūlaṃ kṣapayati | navaṃ na + utthāpayati | a-nirdeśaṃ nirdiśati | vigraham ārabhate vivāda-bahulaś ca bhavati | sa evaṃ dharma-vihārī sthānam etad vidyate yasmin mithyā mahā-prapātaṃ patet | atha ca punar bodhi-citta-bala-adhīnād aiśvaryaṃ pratilabhate | sa kalpa-śata-sahasreṣu buddha-utpādaṃ na + āsādayati | kutaḥ punar dharma-śravaṇam | idaṃ daśamaṃ māra-karma ||
body.translated_text: "He, overcome by pride, becomes disgusted with the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>. He exhausts his former <s>kuśalamūla</s> (roots of merit) and does not generate new ones. He teaches what should not be taught, engages in dispute, and becomes quarrelsome. It is possible that one who thus dwells in the <s>Dharma</s> falsely may fall into a great abyss. And yet, through the power of <s>bodhicitta</s>, he obtains sovereignty. But for a hundred thousand <s>kalpas</s> he does not encounter the arising of a <s>Buddha</s>—how much less the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>! This is the tenth <s>mārakarma</s>."

body.text: imāni bho jina-putra daśa māra-karmāṇi | yāni parivarjya bodhi-satvā daśa jñāna-karmāṇi pratilabhante | atra + eva ca jñāna-karmasu pacyate | nir-mānatā sarva-satveṣv iti ||
body.translated_text: "These, O son of the <s>Jina</s>, are the ten forms of <s>mārakarma</s>. Having abandoned them, <s>bodhisattvas</s> obtain the ten forms of <s>jñānakarma</s> (works of wisdom). And in these very works of wisdom, this is ripened: humility toward all beings."

body.text: ārya-rāṣṭrapāla-sūtre * apy uktaṃ | apāya-bhūmiṃ | gatim a-kṣaṇeṣu | daridratāṃ | nīca-kula-upapattim | jāty-andhya-daurbalyam atha + alpa-sthāmatāṃ | gṛhṇanti te māna-vaśena mūḍhāḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Rāṣṭrapāla-sūtra</s> also it is stated: "Rebirth in the realms of misfortune, in unfavorable states, poverty, birth in a low family, blindness from birth, weakness, and lack of stamina—these the deluded ones grasp through the power of pride."

body.text: iti ||
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: dharma-saṃgīti-sūtre * apy uktaṃ | satva-kṣetraṃ bodhi-satvasya buddha-kṣetraṃ yataś ca buddha-kṣetrād buddha-dharmāṇāṃ lābha-āgamo bhavati | na + arhāmi tasmin vipratipattum | evaṃ ca + asya bhavati | sarvaṃ su-caritaṃ duś-caritaṃ ca satvān niśritya pravartate | duś-carita-āśramāc ca + apāyāḥ pravartante | su-carita-āśrayād deva-manuṣyā iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Dharmasaṃgīti-sūtra</s> also it is stated: "The field of beings is the <s>Buddha</s>-field of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, since from the <s>Buddha</s>-field comes the acquisition of <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. I should not act wrongly toward it. And he thinks thus: 'All good conduct and bad conduct proceed in dependence on beings. From the basis of bad conduct, the unfortunate realms arise; from the basis of good conduct, gods and humans arise.'"

body.text: ata eva ratna-ulkā-dhāraṇyām apy uktaṃ | iha bho jina-putrāḥ prathama-citta-utpādiko bodhi-satvaḥ ādita eva sarva-satvānām antike daśa-prakāraṃ cittam utpādayati | katamad daśa-prakāraṃ | tad yathā | hita-cittatāṃ sukha-cittatāṃ dāyā-cittatāṃ snigdha-cittatāṃ priya-cittatāṃ anugraha-cittatāṃ ārakṣā-cittatāṃ sama-cittatāṃ ācārya-cittatāṃ śāstṛ-cittatāṃ | idaṃ daśa-prakāraṃ cittam utpādayati + iti ||
body.translated_text: For this very reason, in the <s>Ratnolkā-dhāraṇī</s> also it is stated: "Here, O sons of the <s>Jina</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has just generated the first aspiration to awakening, from the very beginning generates a tenfold mind toward all beings. What is this tenfold mind? Namely: a mind of benevolence, a mind of happiness, a mind of compassion, a mind of affection, a mind of love, a mind of helpfulness, a mind of protection, a mind of equanimity, a mind regarding them as teachers, and a mind regarding them as the <s>Śāstṛ</s> (Master). This is the tenfold mind that he generates."

body.text: śraddhā-bala-ādhāna-avatāra-mudrā-sūtre * apy uktaṃ | sarva-satvānāṃ śiṣyatva-abhyupagame sthito * asmi | parāṃś ca sarva-satva-śiṣyatva-abhyupagame pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyāmi + ity āśvāsaṃ pratilabhate ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Śraddhābalādhānāvatāramudrā-sūtra</s> also it is stated: "'I stand in the acceptance of discipleship toward all beings, and I shall establish others in the acceptance of discipleship toward all beings'—thus he gains confidence."

body.text: peyālaṃ ||
body.translated_text: And so forth.

body.text: sarva-satveṣv avanama-praṇamanatāyāṃ pratiṣṭhito * asmi + iti pūrva-vat ||
body.translated_text: "'I stand established in bowing down and paying respect to all beings'—as before."

body.text: tatra + avanamana-praṇamanatāyāṃ sarva-satveṣu nir-mānatā ||
body.translated_text: Therein, bowing down and paying respect to all beings means humility toward all beings.

body.text: tathā + ārya-vimalakīrti-nirdeśe | pariśuddha-buddha-kṣetra-upapattaye sarva-satveṣu śāstṛ-prema + uktaṃ | loka-prasāda-anurakṣā-arthaṃ tv āsana-pāda-prakhyālana-karma kurvatā + api cetasā strīṣu vā + a-kṣaṇa-prāpteṣu vā vinipatiteṣu bodhi-satvena prema-gaurava-abhyāsaḥ kāryaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Likewise in the <s>Ārya-Vimalakīrtinirdeśa</s>, for the sake of rebirth in a purified <s>Buddha</s>-field, love and respect toward the <s>Śāstṛ</s> (Master) in all beings is taught. For the sake of preserving the faith of the world, even while performing the act of washing the feet of a seat-occupant, a <s>bodhisattva</s> should cultivate the practice of love and reverence in his mind toward women, toward those who have reached unfavorable states, and toward those who have fallen.

body.text: uktaṃ hi gaṇḍa-vyūhe tasya samanantara-niṣaṇṇasya tasmin mahā-siṃha-āsane sarvaḥ sa jana-kāyo * abhimukhaḥ prāñjali-sthito * abhūt | tam eva rājānaṃ namasyamānaḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: For it is stated in the <s>Gaṇḍavyūha</s>: "No sooner had he sat down on that great lion-throne than that entire assembly of people stood facing him with palms joined together, paying homage to that very king." And so forth.

body.text: sa khalu sarva-dharma-nirnāda-cchatra-maṇḍala-nirghoṣo rājā teṣāṃ yācanakānāṃ saha darśanena + ātta-manaskataro rājñā + anena ca tri-sāhasra-cakra-varti-rājya-pratilābhena + a-sīma-āprāpta-kalpa-paryavasānena | yāvat śuddha-āvāsa-deva-śānti-vimokṣa-mukha-vihāreṇa + a-paryanta-kalpa-āvasānena | tad yathā kula-putra puruṣasya + eka-anta-tṛṣṇā-caritasya mātā-pitṛ-bhrātṛ-bhaginī-mitra-amātya-jñāti-sālohita-putra-duhitṛ-bhāryā-cira-kāla-viyuktasya + aṭavī-kāntāra-vipraṇaṣṭasya tad-darśana-kāmasya | teṣāṃ samavadhānena mahatī prītir adhyavasānam utpatet tad-darśana-a-vitṛptatayā | evam eva kula-putra rājñaḥ sarva-dharma-nirnāda-cchatra-maṇḍala-nirghoṣasya teṣāṃ yācanakānāṃ saha darśanena mahā-prīti-vegāḥ saṃjātāḥ | citta-tuṣṭi-sukham avakrāntaṃ mahāṃś citta-udagratā-vegaḥ prādur-bhūto yāvat teṣu sarva-yācanakeṣu eka-putraka-saṃjñā mātā-pitṛ-saṃjñā dakṣiṇīya-saṃjñā kalyāṇa-mitra-saṃjñā varṇa-saṃjñā dur-labha-saṃjñā duṣ-kara-kāraka-saṃjñā bahu-kara-saṃjñā parama-upakāri-saṃjñā bodhi-mārga-upastambha-saṃjñā ācārya-śāstṛ-saṃjñā + utpadyeta + iti ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, that King <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s>, at the very sight of those supplicants, became even more delighted than — by the attainment of the sovereignty of a universal monarch over the trichiliocosm extending to the boundary-edge of the <s>kalpa</s>'s end; and even more than by the abiding in the tranquility-liberation-door of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abode) <s>devas</s> for the limitless end of <s>kalpas</s>. Just as, O son of good family, for a man of single-minded longing, long separated from his mother, father, brothers, sisters, friends, ministers, relatives, kinsmen, sons, daughters, and wife, lost in a forest wilderness, desiring to see them — upon encountering them, a great joy and satisfaction would arise, due to his insatiable desire to see them — just so, O son of good family, for King <s>Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa</s>, at the very sight of those supplicants, great surges of joy arose; happiness and contentment of mind were entered; a great surge of mental elation appeared; and so on, up to: toward all those supplicants there arose the perception of [them as] an only son, the perception of [them as] mother and father, the perception of [them as] worthy recipients, the perception of [them as] spiritual friends, the perception of [them as being of] excellent [qualities], the perception of [them as] rare, the perception of [them as] performers of difficult deeds, the perception of [them as] those who do much, the perception of [them as] supreme benefactors, and the perception of [them as] supporters of the path to awakening, the perception of [them as] teachers and masters.'

body.text: evam anya-gata-bhāve satvānām agrato-gamana-upasthāna-ādi-prasaṅge sarva-utsargaṃ smaret | eṣām eva + ayam ātmīyaḥ kāyaḥ | yathā-iṣṭam atra vartantām | pṛthivī-śodhana-upalepana-ādiṣv iva sva-sukha-artham iti | atha-vā svāmy--a-prasāda-bhītena + iva tat-prasāda-arthinā + iva tad-ājñā-saṃpādanā manasi kartavyā | bhagavato * apy upasthānaṃ kurvato * anya-gaty-a-bhāvāt | bhikṣuṇā glānena + aṅgī-kṛtaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Thus, when the circumstance arises of going before beings, attending them, and the like — due to another's state [of need] — one should remember the complete relinquishment [of self]: 'This body of mine belongs to these very [beings]. Let them act in it as they wish — as with sweeping and anointing the ground and so forth, for one's own happiness.' Or alternatively, like a servant afraid of the master's displeasure, seeking his favor — the carrying out of his commands should be kept in mind. Even the Blessed One's performing of service — because there is no other course [when it comes to sick monks] — the acceptance [of that duty] by a <s>bhikṣu</s> who is sick.

body.text: yathā + uktaṃ bhikṣu-prakīrṇake | bhagavān āha | mā bhāya bhikṣu mā bhāya bhikṣu | ahaṃ te bhikṣu + upasthāsyaṃ | āhara bhikṣu cīvarāṇi yāvat te dhopāmi | evam ukte āyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam etad avocat | mā bhagavān etasya glānasya + a-śuci-mraks.itāni cīvarāṇi dhovatu | ahaṃ bhagavan dhoviṣyaṃ | bhagavān āha | tena hy ānanda tvam etasya bhikṣusya cīvarāṇi dhova | tathā-gato udakam āsiñciṣyati | atha khalv āyuṣmān ānando tasya glānasya bhikṣusya cīvarāṇi dhovati | bhagavān udakam āsiñcati || pe ||
body.translated_text: As it is said in the <s>Bhikṣu-prakīrṇaka</s>: 'The Blessed One said: "Do not fear, <s>bhikṣu</s>! Do not fear, <s>bhikṣu</s>! I, <s>bhikṣu</s>, shall attend you. Bring, <s>bhikṣu</s>, your robes — I shall wash them for you." When this was said, the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said to the Blessed One: "Let not the Blessed One wash the filth-smeared robes of this sick one. I, Blessed One, shall wash them." The Blessed One said: "Then, <s>Ānanda</s>, you wash this <s>bhikṣu</s>'s robes; the <s>Tathāgata</s> will pour the water." Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> washes the robes of that sick <s>bhikṣu</s>; the Blessed One pours the water.' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: atha khalv āyuṣmān ānandas taṃ glānaṃ bhikṣuṃ sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca + anuparigṛhya bahir-dhā haritvā snāpayet | bhagavān udakam āsiñcati + iti | āha ca| yān ārādhya mahat tvaṃ virādhya kaṣṭāṃ vipattim āpnoti | prāṇa-parityāgair api teṣāṃ nanu toṣaṇaṃ nyāyyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having well and properly tended that sick <s>bhikṣu</s>, brought him outside and bathed him; the Blessed One pours the water. And it is said: 'By propitiating whom, one gains the great [reward], and by offending whom, one meets with terrible ruin — is it not fitting that they should be gratified even by the sacrifice of one's life?'

body.text: ete te vai satvāḥ prasādya yān siddham āgatā bahavaḥ | siddhi-kṣetraṃ na + anyat satvebhyo vidyate jagati ||
body.translated_text: 'These indeed are the beings by propitiating whom many have attained perfection. There is no field of attainment other than beings in the world.'

body.text: ete cintā-maṇayo bhadra-ghaṭā dhenavaś ca kāma-dughāḥ | guru-vac ca devatā + iva ca tasmād ārādhanīyās te ||
body.translated_text: 'These are wish-fulfilling jewels, auspicious vessels, and wish-granting cows. Like elders, like deities — therefore they should be propitiated.'

body.text: kiṃ ca niś-chadma-bandhūnām a-prameya-upakāriṇām | satva-ārādhanam utsṛjya niṣ-kṛtiḥ kā parā bhavet ||
body.translated_text: 'Moreover, for those who are genuine kinsmen, of immeasurable benefit — abandoning the propitiation of beings, what greater atonement could there be?'

body.text: śirasā dhārayām āsa purā nātho yathā-īpsitam | jaṭā-sv-adhyuṣitān satvān bhūtvā yatnena niś-calaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'The Protector formerly bore upon his head, as [they] wished, beings who dwelt in his matted locks — having become steadfast with effort.'

body.text: bhindanti dehaṃ praviśanty avīcīm yeṣāṃ kṛte tatra kṛte kṛtaṃ syāt ||
body.translated_text: 'They split their bodies and enter <s>Avīci</s> [hell] — for whose sake? In serving them, one has done what is to be done.'

body.text: mahā-apakāriṣv api tena sarvaṃ kalyāṇam eva + ācaraṇīyam eṣu ||
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, toward even great harm-doers, all good alone should be practiced toward them.'

body.text: svayaṃ mama svāmina eva tāvad yad artham ātmany api nir-vyapekṣāḥ | ahaṃ kathaṃ svāmiṣu teṣu teṣu karomi mānaṃ na tu dāsa-bhāvam ||
body.translated_text: 'Since even my own masters, for whose sake they are indifferent even toward themselves — how could I display pride toward those very masters of mine, rather than servitude?'

body.text: yeṣāṃ sukhe yānti mudaṃ muni-indrāḥ yeṣāṃ vyathāyāṃ praviśanti manyum | tat-toṣaṇāt sarva-muni-indra-tuṣṭis tatra + apakāre * apakṛtaṃ munīnāṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'The Lords of Sages rejoice in their happiness; they become wrathful at their suffering. Through gratifying them, all the Lords of Sages are gratified; in harming them, the Sages are harmed.'

body.text: ādīpta-kāyasya yathā samantān | na sarva-kāmair api saumanasyam | satva-vyathāyām api tad-vad eva na prīty-upāyo * asti mahā-kṛpāṇām ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as for one whose body is ablaze on all sides, there is no joy even from all desirable objects — so too, when beings suffer, there is no means of delight for the greatly compassionate ones.'

body.text: tasmān mayā yaj-jana-duṣkhanena | duṣkhaṃ kṛtaṃ sarva-mahā-dayānāṃ | tad adya pāpaṃ pratideśayāmi yat-kheditās te munayaḥ kṣamantām ||
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, whatever suffering I have caused to all the greatly compassionate ones through harming people — I now confess that sin. May those Sages whom I have grieved forgive [me]!'

body.text: ārādhanāya + adya tathā-gatānāṃ sarva-ātmanā dāsyam upaimi loke | kurvantu me mūrdhni padaṃ jana-oghāḥ nighnantu vā tuṣyatu loka-nāthāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'For the propitiation of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, from this day forth, I enter into servitude to the world with my entire being. Let the masses of people place their feet upon my head or strike me — may the Protectors of the World be pleased!'

body.text: ātmī-kṛtaṃ sarvam idaṃ jagat taiḥ kṛpā-ātmabhir na + eva hi saṃśayo * atra | dṛśyantae ete nanu satva-rūpās | tae eva nāthāḥ kim an-ādaro * atra ||
body.translated_text: 'This entire world has been made their own by those compassionate ones — of this there is no doubt. Are not those seen in the form of beings those very Protectors themselves? Why then disrespect here?'

body.text: tathā-gata-ārādhanam etad eva sva-arthasya saṃsādhanam etad eva | lokasya duṣkha-apaham etad eva tasmān mama + astu vratam etad eva ||
body.translated_text: 'This alone is the propitiation of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>; this alone is the accomplishment of one's own purpose; this alone removes the suffering of the world — therefore, may this alone be my vow!'

body.text: yathā + eko rāja-puruṣaḥ pramathnāti mahā-janaṃ | vikaroti na śaknoti dīrgha-darśī mahā-janaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as a single king's agent overwhelms a great multitude — [the multitude] takes offense but is unable [to retaliate], being far-sighted —'

body.text: yasmān na + eva sa ekākī tasya rāja-balaṃ balaṃ | tathā na dur-balaṃ kaṃ-cid aparāddhaṃ vimānayet ||
body.translated_text: 'because he is not alone; the king's power is his power — so too, one should not despise any weak person who has committed an offense.'

body.text: yasmān naraka-pālāś ca kṛpāvantaś ca tad-balaṃ | tasmād ārādhayet satvān bhṛtyaś caṇḍa-nṛ-paṃ yathā ||
body.translated_text: 'Because the guardians of hell and the compassionate ones are his power. Therefore one should propitiate beings as a servant [propitiates] a wrathful king.'

body.text: kupitaḥ kiṃ nṛ-paḥ kuryād yena syān naraka-vyathā | yat-satva-daurmanasyena kṛtena hy anubhūyate ||
body.translated_text: 'What could an angered king do that would equal the suffering of hell — which is experienced as a result of causing displeasure to beings?'

body.text: tuṣṭaḥ kiṃ nṛ-patir dadyād yad buddhatva-samaṃ bhavet | yat satva-saumanasyena kṛtena hy anubhūyate ||
body.translated_text: 'What could a pleased king give that would equal <s>Buddhahood</s> — which is experienced as a result of causing joy to beings?'

body.text: āstāṃ bhaviṣyad-buddhatvaṃ satva-ārādhana-saṃbhavaṃ | iha + eva saubhāgya-yaśaḥ sausthityaṃ kiṃ na paśyasi ||
body.translated_text: 'Setting aside the future <s>Buddhahood</s> arising from the propitiation of beings — do you not see, even here [in this life], good fortune, fame, and well-being?'

body.text: prāsādikatvam ārogyam prāmodyaṃ cira-jīvitaṃ | cakra-varti-sukhaṃ sphītaṃ kṣamī prāpnoti saṃsaran ||
body.translated_text: 'Graciousness, health, cheerfulness, long life — the abundant happiness of a universal monarch: the patient one obtains [these] while wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s>.'

body.text: maitrā-āśayaś ca yat pūjyaḥ satva-māhātmyam eva tat | buddha-prasādād yat puṇyaṃ buddha-māhātmyam eva tat ||
body.translated_text: 'That a mind of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) is to be honored — that is the greatness of beings. That there is merit from faith in the <s>Buddha</s> — that is the greatness of the <s>Buddha</s>.'

body.text: ata eva hi candra-pradīpa-sūtre maitrī-bhāva-phalam udbhāvitam | yāvanti pūjāṃ bahu-vidha a-prameyāḥ | kṣetraṃ śateṣu niyuta ca bimbareṣū | tāṃ pūja kṛtvā a-tuliya-nāyakānāṃ | saṃkhyā-kalāpī
body.translated_text: For this very reason, in the <s>Candrapradīpa-sūtra</s>, the fruit of the state of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) is proclaimed: 'However many and varied and immeasurable offerings [are made] in hundreds of fields and billions [of <s>Buddha</s>-fields] — having made that worship of the incomparable Leaders, not even a fraction —'

body.text: tasmād evaṃ-vidheṣu mahā-dakṣiṇīyeṣu + unnatiṃ varjayet sadā | eṣā ca + unnatir a-yoniśo-manas-kārāt saṃbhavati + iti ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, toward such supremely worthy recipients, one should always avoid arrogance. And this arrogance arises from improper mental attention (<s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>).

body.text: tasya + an-avatāre yatnaḥ kāryaḥ | yathā + uktaṃ ratna-meghe | kathaṃ ca kula-putra bodhi-satvo * a-yoniśo-manas-kāra-apagato bhavati | iha bodhi-satva ekākī raho-gataḥ praviveka-sthito na + evaṃ cittam utpādayati | ahaṃ a-saṃkīrṇa-vihārī | ahaṃ praviveka-sthitaḥ | ahaṃ pratipannas tāthāgate dharma-vinaye | ye tv anye śramaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā sarve te saṃkīrṇa-vihāriṇaḥ | saṃsarga-bahulā uddhurās tāthāgatād dharma-vinayāt ||
body.translated_text: Effort should be made to prevent its arising. As it is said in the <s>Ratnamegha</s>: 'And how, O son of good family, does the <s>bodhisattva</s> become free from improper mental attention? Here, the <s>bodhisattva</s>, alone, secluded, dwelling in solitude, does not generate the thought: "I am one who dwells apart from the crowd. I am one established in solitude. I am one who has entered the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharma-vinaya</s>. But all those other <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — they dwell in the crowd, are abundant in association, unruly, [fallen] from the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharma-vinaya</s>."'

body.text: evaṃ hi bodhi-satvo * a-yoniśo-manas-kāra-apagato bhavati ||
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>bodhisattva</s> becomes free from improper mental attention.

body.text: punar atra + eva + uktam | iha bodhi-satvo vīryam ārabhamāṇo na tan mahad vīryam āsvādayati | na ca tena vīryeṇa + ātmānam utkarṣayati | na parān paṃsayati | tasya + evaṃ bhavati | ko hi nāma sa-prajña-jātīyaḥ sva-karma-abhiyuktaḥ parāṃś codayet ||
body.translated_text: Again, right here it is said: 'Here, the <s>bodhisattva</s>, when arousing vigor, does not savor that vigor as great. And he does not exalt himself by that vigor; he does not denigrate others. His thought is thus: "What wise person, devoted to his own task, would urge others [to be like him]?"'

body.text: evaṃ hi bodhi-satvo * an-unnata-vīryo bhavati ||
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>bodhisattva</s> becomes one whose vigor is free from arrogance.

body.text: eṣa tu puṇya-rakṣāyāḥ saṃkṣepo yad bodhi-pariṇāmanā ||
body.translated_text: But this is the summary of the protection of merit: namely, the dedication to awakening (<s>bodhi-pariṇ��manā</s>).

body.text: tathā hy uktam ārya-akṣayamati-sūtre | na hi bodhi-pariṇāmitasya kuśala-mūlasya + antarā kaś-cit parikṣayo yāvad bodhi-maṇḍa-niṣadanāt | tad yathā + api nāma bhadanta śāradvatīputra mahā-samudra-patitasya + udaka-bindor na + antarā + asti kṣayo yāvan na kalpa-paryavasāna | iti ||
body.translated_text: For thus it is said in the <s>Ārya-Akṣayamati-sūtra</s>: 'For indeed, of a wholesome root that has been dedicated to awakening, there is no diminution in the interim, until the sitting at the seat of awakening. Just as, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, of a drop of water that has fallen into the great ocean, there is no diminution in the interim until the end of the <s>kalpa</s>.'

body.text: iti śikṣā-samuccaye bhoga-puṇya-rakṣā saptamaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the seventh chapter of the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>: the Protection of Enjoyments and Merit.

body.text: pāpa-śodhanaṃ aṣṭamaḥ paricchedaḥ | uktā trayāṇām apy ātma-bhāva-ādīnāṃ rakṣā | śuddhir adhunā vaktavyā | kim artham | śodhitasya + ātma-bhāvasya bhogaḥ pathyo bhaviṣyati | samyak-siddhasya bhaktasya niṣ-kaṇasya + iva dehinām ||
body.translated_text: Purification of sin — the eighth chapter. The protection of all three — the body and so forth — has been stated. Purification must now be discussed. For what purpose? 'For one whose body has been purified, the enjoyment will be wholesome — like food that is properly prepared, free from husks, for embodied beings.'

body.text: yathā + uktam ārya-tathā-gata-guhya-sūtre | yāni ca tāni mahā-nagareṣu mahā-śmaśānāni bhavanty an-eka-prāṇi-śata-sahasra-ākīrṇāni | tatra + api sa bodhi-satvo mahā-satvo mahāntam ātma-bhāvaṃ mṛtaṃ kāla-gatam upadarśayati | tatra te tiryag-yoni-gatāḥ satvā yāvad arthaṃ māṃsaṃ paribhujya + āyuḥ-paryante mṛtāḥ kāla-gatāḥ su-gatau svarga-loke deveṣu + upapadyante | sa ca + eva teṣāṃ hetur bhavati yāvat parinirvāṇāya | yad idaṃ | tasya + eva bodhi-satvasya pūrva-praṇidhāna-pariśuddhyā | yena dīrgha-rātram evaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ | ye me mṛtasya kāla-gatasya māṃsaṃ paribhuñjīran | sa eva teṣāṃ hetur bhavet svarga-utpattaye yāvat parinirvāṇāya tasya śīlavataḥ | ṛdhyati cetanā | ṛdhyati prārthanā | ṛdhyati praṇidhānam iti ||
body.translated_text: As it is said in the <s>Ārya-Tathāgataguhya-sūtra</s>: 'And whatever great charnel grounds exist in the great cities, filled with many hundreds of thousands of living beings — there too, that <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> displays a great dead body, one that has passed away. There, those beings born in animal realms, having eaten as much flesh as they need, upon dying and passing away at the end of their lifespan, are reborn in the fortunate destiny, in the heavenly world among the <s>devas</s>. And he himself becomes the cause for them, up until final <s>nirvāṇa</s>. How? Through the purification of that very <s>bodhisattva</s>'s former aspiration, by which he made this vow over a long time: "May those who eat my flesh when I have died and passed away — may he himself become the cause for their heavenly rebirth, up until final <s>nirvāṇa</s>." Of that virtuous one, the intention succeeds; the prayer succeeds; the aspiration succeeds.'

body.text: punar atra + eva + uktaṃ | sa dharma-kāya-prabhāvito darśanena + api satvānām arthaṃ karoti | śravaṇena + api sparśanena + api satvānām arthaṃ karoti | tad yathā + api nāma śāntamate jīvakena vaidya-rājena sarva-bhaiṣajyāni samudānīya bhaiṣajya-taru-saṃhātam ayaṃ dārikā-rūpaṃ kṛtaṃ prāsādikaṃ darśanīyaṃ su-kṛtaṃ su-niṣṭhitaṃ su-parikarma-kṛtaṃ | sā + āgacchati gacchati tiṣṭhati niṣīdati śayyāṃ ca kalpayati | tatra ye āgacchanty āturā mahā-ātmāno rājāno vā rāja-mātrā vā śreṣṭhi-gṛha-paty-amātya-koṭṭa-rājāno vā | tān sa jīvako vaidya-rājas tayā bhaiṣajya-dārikayā sārddhaṃ saṃyojayati | teṣāṃ samanantara-saṃyogam āpannānāṃ sarva-vyādhayaḥ prasrabhyante * a-rāgāś ca bhavanti sukhino nir-vikārāḥ | paśya śāntamate jīvakasya vaidya-rājasya laukika-vyādhi-cikitsā-jñānaṃ yady anyeṣāṃ vaidyānāṃ saṃvidyate | evam eva śāntamate tasya dharma-kāya-prabhāvitasya bodhi-satvasya yāvantaḥ satvāḥ strī-puruṣa-dāraka-dārikā rāga-doṣa-moha-saṃtaptāḥ kāyaṃ spṛśanti | teṣāṃ saṃspṛṣṭa-mātrāṇāṃ sarva-kleśāḥ prasrabhyante vigata-saṃtāpaṃ ca kāyaṃ saṃjānanti ||
body.translated_text: And further in the same [text] it is said: "He, being empowered by the <s>dharma-kāya</s> (truth-body), benefits sentient beings even by sight. He benefits sentient beings even by hearing, even by touch. Just as, O <s>Śāntamati</s>, the physician-king <s>Jīvaka</s>, having gathered all medicines, fashioned an assemblage of medicinal trees into the form of a maiden — graceful, beautiful, well-made, well-finished, well-adorned. She comes and goes, stands, sits, and lies down. There, those who come — the great-souled, afflicted kings, or those of royal rank, or chief merchants, householders, ministers, and provincial rulers — the physician-king <s>Jīvaka</s> brings them into union with that medicinal maiden. As soon as they enter into contact with her, all their diseases are alleviated, and they become free from passion, happy, and without disturbance. See, O <s>Śāntamati</s>, whether the worldly knowledge of healing diseases of the physician-king <s>Jīvaka</s> exists in other physicians! Just so, O <s>Śāntamati</s>, whatever sentient beings — men, women, boys, or girls — scorched by passion, hatred, and delusion, touch the body of that <s>bodhisattva</s> empowered by the <s>dharma-kāya</s>, as soon as they touch him, all their <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are alleviated, and they experience their bodies as free from torment."

body.text: yad idaṃ tasya + eva bodhi-satvasya pūrva-praṇidhāna-su-pariśuddhatvāt | etad-artham ātma-bhāvaḥ śodhyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: This is because of the thorough purification of the former aspirations of that very <s>bodhisattva</s>. For this purpose, one's own self should be purified.

body.text: kiṃ ca a-śodhane doṣam āha |tṛṇa-channaṃ yathā śasyaṃ rogaiḥ sīdati na + edhate | buddha-aṅkuras tathā vṛddhiṃ kleśa-channo na gacchati ||
body.translated_text: And what is the fault in not purifying? "Just as grain covered by weeds sickens and does not thrive, so the sprout of <s>Buddhahood</s>, covered by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), does not grow."

body.text: prati-pakṣa-nirāsena vṛddhy-arthaṃ ca + ity abhiprāyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The intention is: for the purpose of growth through the removal of the antidotes' [obstacles].

body.text: ātma-bhāvasya kā śuddhiḥ | pāpa-kleśa-viśodhanaṃ | saṃbuddha-ukty-artha-sāreṇa | yatna-a-bhāve tv apāya-gaḥ ||
body.translated_text: What is the purification of the self? The purification of sins and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), by means of the essence of what the perfectly awakened one has taught. But without effort, one is destined for the lower realms.

body.text: tatra pāpa-śodhanaṃ catur-dharmaka-sūtre deśitaṃ | caturbhir maitreya dharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhi-satvo mahā-satvaḥ kṛta-upacitaṃ pāpam abhibhavati | katamaiś caturbhiḥ | yad uta | vidūṣaṇa-a-samudācāreṇa prati-pakṣa-samudācāreṇa | praty-āpatti-balena | āśraya-balena ca ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the purification of sin is taught in the <s>Caturdharmaka-sūtra</s> (Sūtra of the Four Dharmas): "Endowed with four <s>dharmas</s>, O <s>Maitreya</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> overcomes sin that has been committed and accumulated. With which four? Namely: through the practice of censure, through the practice of the antidote, through the power of restraint, and through the power of the foundation."

body.text: tatra vidūṣaṇa-a-samudācāro * a-kuśalaṃ karma + adhyacārati tatra tatra + eva ca vipratisāra-bahulī bhavati ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the practice of censure is: having committed an unwholesome action, one becomes full of remorse regarding that very [action].

body.text: tatra prati-pakṣa-samudācāraḥ kṛtvā + apy a-kuśalaṃ karma kuśale karmaṇy aty-artha-abhiyogaṃ gataḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the practice of the antidote is: having committed an unwholesome action, one engages most intensely in wholesome action.

body.text: praty-āpatti-balaṃ saṃvara-samādānād a-karaṇa-saṃvara-lābhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The power of restraint is: through undertaking the vow of restraint, the attainment of the restraint of non-commission.

body.text: tatra + āśraya-balaṃ buddha-dharma-saṃgha-śaraṇa-gamanam an-utsṛṣṭa-bodhi-cittatā ca | su-balavat-saṃniśrayeṇa na śakyate pāpena + abhibhavituṃ | ebhir maitreya caturbhir dharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhi-satvo mahā-satvaḥ kṛta-upacitaṃ pāpam abhibhavati + iti ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the power of the foundation is: taking refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s>, and not abandoning <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening). Through reliance on a powerful foundation, one cannot be overcome by sin. "Endowed with these four <s>dharmas</s>, O <s>Maitreya</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> overcomes sin that has been committed and accumulated."

body.text: tatra kathaṃ vidūṣaṇa-a-samudācāro bhāvayitavyaḥ | yathā suvarṇa-prabhāsa-uttama-sūtre * abhihitaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, how should the practice of censure be cultivated? As stated in the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra</s> (Supreme Golden Light Sūtra):

body.text: samanvāharantu māṃ buddhāḥ kṛpā-kāruṇya-cetasaḥ | ye ca daśa-diśi loke tiṣṭhanti dvi-pada-uttamāḥ ||
body.translated_text: "May the <s>Buddhas</s> be mindful of me, with minds of pity and compassion — those supreme among bipeds who abide in the ten directions of the world."

body.text: yac ca me pāpakaṃ karma kṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ su-dāruṇaṃ | tat sarvaṃ deśayiṣyāmi sthito daśa-bala-agrataḥ ||
body.translated_text: "Whatever terrible sinful <s>karma</s> I have committed in the past — all that I shall confess, standing before the lords of the ten powers."

body.text: mātā-pitṝn a-jānatā buddhānām a-prajānatā | kuśalaṃ ca + a-prajānatā yat tu pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā ||
body.translated_text: "Not knowing my mother and father, not understanding the <s>Buddhas</s>, not understanding what is wholesome — whatever sin was committed by me —"

body.text: aiśvarya-mada-mattena kula-bhoga-madena ca | tāruṇya-mada-mattena yat tu pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā ||
body.translated_text: "Intoxicated by the pride of authority, by the pride of family and wealth, intoxicated by the pride of youth — whatever sin was committed by me —"

body.text: duś-cintitaṃ dur-uktaṃ ca duṣ-kṛtena + api karmaṇā | an-ādīnava-darśinā yat tu pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā ||
body.translated_text: "Through wrongly thought, wrongly spoken, and wrongly done actions, by one who does not see the danger — whatever sin was committed by me —"

body.text: bāla-buddhi-pracāreṇa a-jñāna-āvṛta-cetasā | pāpa-mitra-vaśāc ca + eva kleśa-vyākula-cetasā ||
body.translated_text: "Through the course of a foolish mind, with consciousness obscured by ignorance, under the influence of bad friends, with consciousness agitated by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) —"

body.text: krīḍā-rati-vaśāc ca + eva śoka-roga-vaśena vā | a-tṛpta-dhana-doṣeṇa yat tu pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā ||
body.translated_text: "Under the influence of sport and pleasure, or under the influence of grief and disease, through the fault of insatiable desire for wealth — whatever sin was committed by me —"

body.text: an-ārya-jana-saṃsargair īrṣyā-mātsarya-hetunā | śāṭhya-dāridrya-doṣeṇa yat tu pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā ||
body.translated_text: "Through association with ignoble people, through the cause of envy and miserliness, through the fault of deceit and poverty — whatever sin was committed by me —"

body.text: vyasana-āgama-kāle * asmin kāmānāṃ bhaya-hetunā | an-aiśvarya-gatena + api yat tu pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā ||
body.translated_text: "In this time when misfortune approaches, through the cause of fear of sensual desires, and even through the state of lacking authority — whatever sin was committed by me —"

body.text: cala-citta-vaśena + eva kāma-krodha-vaśena vā | kṣut-pipāsa-ārditena + api yat tu pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā ||
body.translated_text: "Under the influence of a fickle mind, or under the influence of desire and anger, tormented by hunger and thirst — whatever sin was committed by me —"

body.text: pāna-arthaṃ bhojana-arthaṃ ca vastra-arthaṃ strīṣu hetunā | vicitraiḥ kleśa-saṃtāpair yat tu pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā ||
body.translated_text: "For the sake of drink, for the sake of food, for the sake of clothing, on account of women, through various torments of affliction — whatever sin was committed by me —"

body.text: kāya-vāṅ-manasāṃ pāpaṃ tridhā duś-caritaṃ cittaṃ | yat kṛtam īdṛśai rūpais tat sarvaṃ deśayāmy aham ||
body.translated_text: "The sin of body, speech, and mind — the threefold misconduct of thought — whatever was committed of such forms — all that I confess."

body.text: yat tu buddheṣu dharmeṣu śrāvakeṣu tathā + eva ca | a-gauravaṃ kṛtaṃ syād * dhi tat sarvaṃ deśayāmy aham ||
body.translated_text: "Whatever disrespect I may have shown toward the <s>Buddhas</s>, toward the <s>Dharma</s>, and likewise toward the <s>Śrāvakas</s> (Hearers) — all that I confess."

body.text: yat tu praty-eka-buddheṣu bodhi-satveṣu vā punaḥ |a-gauravaṃ kṛtaṃ syād * dhi tat srvaṃ deśayāmy aham ||
body.translated_text: "Whatever disrespect I may have shown toward the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (Solitary Buddhas) and again toward the <s>bodhisattvas</s> — all that I confess."

body.text: sad-dharma-bhāṇakeṣv eva anyeṣu guṇavatsu vā | a-gauravaṃ kṛtaṃ syād * dhi tat sarvaṃ deśayāmy aham ||
body.translated_text: "Whatever disrespect I may have shown toward the preachers of the true <s>Dharma</s> and toward others endowed with virtues — all that I confess."

body.text: sad-dharmaḥ pratikṣiptaḥ syād a-jñānaṃ tena me sadā | mātā-pitṛṣv a-gauravaṃ tat sarvaṃ deśayāmy aham ||
body.translated_text: "If I have rejected the true <s>Dharma</s> — through that, ignorance is always mine. If I have shown disrespect to my mother and father — all that I confess."

body.text: mūrkhatvena bālatvena māna-darpa-āvṛtena ca | rāga-dveṣeṇa mohena tat sarvaṃ deśayāmy aham ||
body.translated_text: "Through stupidity, through foolishness, through being covered by pride and arrogance, through passion, hatred, and delusion — all that I confess."

body.text: vyavalokayantu māṃ buddhāḥ samanvāhṛta-cetasaḥ | atyayaṃ pratigṛhṇantu kāruṇya-arpita-cetasaḥ ||
body.translated_text: "May the <s>Buddhas</s> look upon me with attentive minds! May they accept my transgression with minds directed to compassion!"

body.text: yat tu pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ mayā kalpa-śateṣu ca | tasya + arthaṃ śoka-citto * ahaṃ krpaṇīyo bhaya-ārditaḥ ||
body.translated_text: "Whatever sin was committed by me in the past, over hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) — on account of that I am grief-stricken, pitiable, terrified."

body.text: bhavāmi pāpa-karmāṇāṃ satataṃ dīna-mānasaḥ | yatra yatra cariṣyāmi na ca + asti me balaṃ kva-cit ||
body.translated_text: "I am always downcast in mind regarding my sinful actions. Wherever I shall go, I have no strength anywhere."

body.text: sarve kāruṇikā buddhāḥ sarve bhaya-harā jage | atyayaṃ pratigṛhṇantu mocayantu ca māṃ bhayāt ||
body.translated_text: "All the compassionate <s>Buddhas</s>, all who remove fear in the world — may they accept my transgression and liberate me from fear!"

body.text: kleśa-karma-phalaṃ mahyaṃ pravāhayantu tathā-gatāḥ | snāpayantu ca māṃ buddhāḥ kāruṇya-sarita-udakaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: "May the <s>Tathāgatas</s> wash away from me the fruit of afflictions and <s>karma</s>! May the <s>Buddhas</s> bathe me with the waters of the river of compassion!"

body.text: sarvaṃ pāpaṃ deśayāmi yat tu pūrvaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā | yac ca etarhi me pāpaṃ tat sarvaṃ deśayāmy aham ||
body.translated_text: "All the sin that was committed by me in the past — I confess it all. Whatever present sin I have — all that I confess."

body.text: āyatyāṃ saṃvaram āpadye sarva-duṣ-kṛta-karmaṇām | na chādayāmi tat pāpaṃ yad bhaven mama duṣ-kṛtam ||
body.translated_text: "For the future I undertake the vow of restraint from all wrongly done actions. I do not conceal that sin — whatever wrongdoing of mine there may be."

body.text: tri-vidhaṃ kāyikaṃ karma vacasā ca catur-vidham | manasā tri-prakāreṇa tat sarvaṃ deśayāmy aham ||
body.translated_text: "The threefold action of the body, the fourfold [action] of speech, the threefold [action] of the mind — all that I confess."

body.text: kāya-kṛtaṃ vāca-kṛtaṃ manasā ca vicintitaṃ | kṛtaṃ daśa-vidhaṃ karma tat sarvaṃ deśayāmy aham ||
body.translated_text: "Action done by body, done by speech, and conceived by mind — the tenfold action — all that I confess."

body.text: yac ca me pāpakaṃ karma an-iṣṭa-phala-dāyakaṃ | tat sarvaṃ deśayiṣyāmi buddhānāṃ purataḥ sthitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: "Whatever sinful <s>karma</s> of mine that gives undesired fruit — all that I shall confess, standing before the <s>Buddhas</s>."

body.text: bhava-gati-saṃkaṭe bāla-buddhinā pāpaṃ yan me kṛtaṃ su-dāruṇam | daśa-balam agrataḥ sthitaḥ tat sarvaṃ pāpaṃ pratideśayāmi | deśayāmi ca tat pāpaṃ yan mayā saṃcitaṃ janma-saṃkaṭe vividhaiḥ kāya-pracāra-saṃkaṭair bhava-saṃkaṭa-loka-saṃkaṭe cāpala-cala-citta-saṃkaṭe mūrkha-bāla-kṛta-kleśa-saṃkaṭe | pāpa-mitra-āgama-saṃkaṭe ca | bhaya-saṃkaṭa-rāga-saṃkaṭe doṣa-moha-tama-saṃkaṭair api kṣaṇa-saṃkaṭe kāla-saṃkaṭe puṇya-upārjana-saṃkaṭair api | jina-saṃkaṭa-saṃmukha-sthitaḥ | tat sarva-pāpaṃ pratideśayāmi ||
body.translated_text: "In the narrow passage of existence, with a foolish mind, whatever terrible sin was committed by me — standing before the lords of the ten powers, I confess all that sin. And I confess that sin which was accumulated by me in the narrow passage of birth, through various bodily actions in the narrow passage, in the narrow passage of existence and of the world, in the narrow passage of a fickle and wavering mind, in the narrow passage of afflictions created by foolishness and ignorance, in the narrow passage of encountering evil friends, in the narrow passage of fear, in the narrow passage of passion, and through the narrow passages of hatred, delusion, and darkness, in the narrow passage of [this] moment, in the narrow passage of time, and through the narrow passages of gathering merit. Standing face to face before the Victorious Ones in [all] narrow passages — I confess all that sin."

body.text: viśeṣatas tu bodhi-satva-āpattīnāṃ gurvīṇāṃ laghvīnāṃ deśanā + ārya-upāli-paripṛcchāyām uktā | kā punar gurvī mūla-āpattiḥ ||
body.translated_text: In particular, the confession of <s>bodhisattva</s> transgressions, both heavy and light, is stated in the noble <s>Upāliparipṛcchā</s> (Questions of <s>Upāli</s>). What then is a heavy root transgression?

body.text: sāmānyatas tu tatra + uktaṃ | saced upāle mahā-yāna-saṃprasthito bodhi-satvo mahā-satvo gaṅgā-nadī-vālika-upamā rāga-pratisaṃyuktā āpattīr āpadyeta | yāṃ ca + ekato dveṣa-saṃprayuktām āpattim āpadyeta bodhi-satva-yānaṃ pramāṇī-kṛtya || pe ||
body.translated_text: In general, it is stated there: "If, O <s>Upāli</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> who has set forth upon the <s>Mahāyāna</s> were to commit transgressions connected with passion as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River — and if he were to commit a single transgression connected with hatred, taking the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle as his standard —" [abbreviated]

body.text: iyaṃ tābhyo gurutarā āpattir yā + iyaṃ dveṣa-saṃyuktā | tat kasya hetoḥ | yo * ayaṃ dveṣa upāle satva-parityāgāya saṃvartate | rāgaḥ satva-saṃgrahāya saṃvartate | tatra + upāle yaḥ kleśaḥ satva-saṃgrahāya saṃvartate | na tatra bodhi-satvasya chalaṃ na bhayaṃ || pe ||
body.translated_text: "this [latter] transgression connected with hatred is heavier than those [former ones]. For what reason? Because hatred, O <s>Upāli</s>, leads to the abandonment of sentient beings, whereas passion leads to the gathering of sentient beings. Therein, O <s>Upāli</s>, whatever <s>kleśa</s> (affliction) leads to the gathering of sentient beings — in that, there is no deception for the <s>bodhisattva</s>, no fear." [Abbreviated.]

body.text: tasmāt tarhi tvām upāle yāḥ kāś-cana rāga-pratisaṃyuktā āpattayaḥ sarva-s tā an-āpattaya iti vadāmi | ko * atra + abhiprāyaḥ | satva-saṃgrahasya + eva pūrvam eva viśeṣitatvād | adhyāśaya-kṛpāvato hy ayam upadeśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: "Therefore, O <s>Upāli</s>, whatever transgressions connected with passion there may be — I declare all of them to be non-transgressions." What is the intent here? Because the gathering of sentient beings has been given priority from the very beginning. For this teaching is for one who has superior aspiration and compassion.

body.text: yasmād an-antaram āha | tatra + upāle ye * an-upāya-kuśalā bodhi-satvās te rāga-pratisaṃyuktābhya āpattibhyo bibhyati | ye punar upāya-kuśalā bodhi-satvās te dveṣa-saṃprayuktābhya āpattibhyo bibhyati na rāga-pratisaṃyuktābhya iti ||
body.translated_text: For immediately after, [the sūtra] says: "Therein, O <s>Upāli</s>, those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are unskilled in means fear transgressions connected with passion. But those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are skilled in means fear transgressions connected with hatred, not those connected with passion."

body.text: ke punar upāya-kuśalāḥ | ye prajñā-kṛpābhyāṃ satva-tyāgān nivāryante | ubhayathā hi satva-tyāgo bhavati | kevala-prajñayā duṣkha-śūnyatā-avabodhāt | kevalayā ca kṛpayā kleśa-balād a-cireṇa kṛpā-hāniḥ ||
body.translated_text: Who then are the ones skilled in means? Those who are prevented from abandoning sentient beings by [the combination of] wisdom and compassion. For the abandonment of sentient beings occurs in both ways: through wisdom alone, by realizing the emptiness of suffering; and through compassion alone, [because] through the power of afflictions, compassion is quickly lost.

body.text: yad uktam upāya-kauśalya-sūtre | tad yathā kula-putra maṃtra-vidyā-dharaḥ puruṣo rājñā pañca-pāśakena bandhanena baddhaḥ syāt | sa yadā kāṅkṣeta prakramaṇāya tadā + eka-mantra-vidyā-balena sarva-bandhanāni chittvā prakramet | evam eva kula-putra + upāya-kuśalo bodhi-satvaḥ pañcabhiḥ kāma-guṇai ratiṃ vindati taiś ca + ākīrṇo viharati | yadā ca punar ākāṅkṣate tadā prajñā-bala-adhīnena ekena ca sarva-jñatā-cittena sarva-kāma-guṇān prabhujya cyuto brahma-lokae upapadyatae iti ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Upāyakauśalya-sūtra</s> (Sūtra on Skill in Means): "Just as, O son of good family, a man who holds a spell of sacred knowledge, bound by a king with five-fold chains — whenever he wishes to depart, by the power of a single spell of sacred knowledge he cuts through all bonds and departs. Just so, O son of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s> skilled in means finds delight in the five strands of sensual pleasure and dwells surrounded by them. But whenever he wishes, by the power dependent on wisdom and by a single mind directed toward omniscience, having enjoyed all the strands of sensual pleasure, he departs and is reborn in the <s>Brahma</s>-world."

body.text: dveṣe * api kiṃ na + evam iṣyate | prakṛti-mahā-sa-avadyatvāt | kṛpā-vaikalye ca + upāyasya + eva + a-saṃbhavāt ||
body.translated_text: But regarding hatred — why is the same [leniency] not accepted? Because it is inherently greatly blameworthy, and because when compassion is lacking, [skillful] means itself is impossible.

body.text: para-artha-siddhiṃ vā sva-arthād gurutarām adhimucyamānaḥ kopa-paravattayā + api param anuśāsya-anutāpa-pūrvakam āyatyāṃ saṃvaram utpadyate | a-hita-nivārake krodhe ko doṣaḥ | avakāśa-dānena tad-vāsanā-doṣāt kṛpā-hāni-doṣaḥ | tac-chedena mūla-ccheda-doṣa iti paścād darśayiṣyāmaḥ | yady api tasya satvasya tad-dhitaṃ tathā + api bodhi-satva-kṛpā-hānyā mahataḥ satva-artha-anubandhasya hāniḥ syāt ||
body.translated_text: Or, accepting that the accomplishment of others' welfare is weightier than one's own welfare, even when one who is controlled by anger admonishes another with [subsequent] remorse, restraint for the future arises. What fault is there in anger that averts harm? [The fault is:] through giving it room, by the fault of its latent tendency, there is the fault of loss of compassion. And through cutting it off [entirely], we shall show later that there is the fault of cutting the root.

body.text: ārya-satyake parivartte * api putra-dṛṣṭa-antaḥ karuṇā-adhiṣṭhita eva veditavyaḥ | yaś ca tatra + api kṛpā-pratiṣedhaḥ sa loka-artha-pāṇḍityena loka-āvarjana-arthaṃ | nivāryamāṇaś ca yadi hita-kāme bodhi-satve pratighaṃ labheta sa bodhi-satvaḥ syād ubhayor an-arthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Satyaka-parivarta</s> also, the perspective of seeing [beings] as one's children should be understood as established in compassion. And whatever prohibition against compassion is found there — that is for the purpose of winning over the world, through skill in worldly benefit. And if, despite being restrained, one were to generate hostility toward a <s>bodhisattva</s> who wishes [one's] benefit — that <s>bodhisattva</s> would be [causing] harm to both [himself and the other].

body.text: rāge * api tarhi doṣaḥ paṭhyate | kāma-anuṣevaṇi bhoti andha manu-jo | mātā-pitṛ-ghātayī | kāmān sevatu śīlavantu vadhayī | tasmād vivarjet sadā iti ||
body.translated_text: But the fault regarding attachment is also taught: 'One who indulges in sensual pleasures becomes a blind man. He is a slayer of mother and father. Let him who indulges in pleasures kill the virtuous! Therefore one should always abstain [from them].'

body.text: sva-saukhya-saṃgena ca para-duṣkha-upekṣā dṛṣṭā ||
body.translated_text: And through attachment to one's own happiness, indifference to the suffering of others is observed.

body.text: satyaṃ dṛṣṭā | yena para-duṣkhaṃ sva-duṣkhatayā na + abhyastaṃ | yena tv abhyastaṃ | tasya + ubhaya-doṣa-a-saṃbhavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: True, it is observed. [But only] by one who has not practiced [seeing] the suffering of others as one's own suffering. For one who has practiced thus, the arising of both faults is impossible.

body.text: yathā + uktaṃ candra-pradīpa-sūtre | tad yathā + api nāma + ānanda kaś-cid eva puruṣo * adhastāt pāda-talam ādāya yāvan murddhany ādīpto bhavet | saṃprajvalita eka-jvalī-bhu-tas taṃ kaś-cid eva puruṣa upasaṃkramya evaṃ vaded | ehi tvāṃ bhoḥ puruṣa nirvāpitena + ātma-bhāvena pañcabhiḥ kāma-guṇaiḥ samarpitaḥ samanvaṅgī-bhūtaḥ krīḍasva ramasva paricārayasva + iti | tat kiṃ manyase ānanda | api tu sa puruṣo * a-nirvāpitena + ātma-bhāvena pañcabhiḥ kāma-guṇaiḥ krīḍeta ramet paricaret ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Candrapradīpasūtra</s>: 'Suppose, <s>Ānanda</s>, a certain man were ablaze from the soles of his feet up to the crown of his head — burning, a single mass of flame. And suppose someone were to approach that man and say: "Come, good sir! With your body unextinguished, enjoy yourself, delight, and amuse yourself with the five strands of sensual pleasure." What do you think, <s>Ānanda</s> — would that man, with his body unextinguished, play, delight, and amuse himself with the five strands of sensual pleasure?'

body.text: ānanda āha ||
body.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s> said:

body.text: na + u hi + idaṃ bhagavan ||
body.translated_text: 'Certainly not, O Blessed One.'

body.text: g
body.translated_text: [Abbreviated passage marker]

body.text: bhagavān āha | krīḍeta + ānanda sa puruṣo ramet paricaret parikalpam upādāya + a-parinirvāpitena + ātma-bhāvena pañcabhiḥ kāma-guṇaiḥ samarpitaḥ samanvaṅgī-bhūto | na tv evaṃ tathā-gatasya pūrvaṃ bodhi-satva-caryāṃ caramāṇasya satvān tribhir apāyair duṣkhitān dṛṣṭvā daridrān abhūt saumanasyaṃ vā citta-prasādo vā + iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'By supposition, <s>Ānanda</s>, that man would play, delight, and amuse himself — equipped and endowed with the five strands of sensual pleasure while his body is unextinguished. But for the <s>Tathāgata</s>, previously, when practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, having seen beings suffering in the three lower realms, impoverished — there never arose mental well-being or joyful serenity of mind.' And so on in detail.

body.text: loke * api putre śūlam āropyamāṇe | paśyator mātā-pitror na sva-saukhya-saṃgo dṛṣṭaḥ sva-anurūpa-kṛpā-vaśāt | pracchannas tarhi sa-svāmikāsu ni-svāmikāsu bāhula-dharma-dhvaja-rakṣitāsu kāma-mithyā-ācāro na syāt | sati satva-arthe satva-an-upaghāte ca + anubandhaṃ nirūpya + a-doṣaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Even in the world, when a son is being impaled upon a stake before the eyes of his mother and father, attachment to one's own happiness is not observed — on account of the force of compassion appropriate [to the relationship]. 'Then, secretly, with women who have husbands or who have no husbands, protected by the banner of [monastic] discipline, would there not be sexual misconduct?' When there is benefit to beings and no harm to beings, having examined the consequences, there is no fault.

body.text: samyag-brahma-cāriṇīṣu kṛta-arthatvād dūrāt parihāraḥ | pūjyā ca mātṛ-bhaginy--ādi-vat | evaṃ tarhi bhikṣor apy evam āpannaṃ | na tasya + a-pareṇa brahma-carya-prakāreṇa satva-artha-sādhanāt ||
body.translated_text: With women who are properly celibate, avoidance [should be maintained] from afar, since one's purpose [with them] is already accomplished. And they should be honored like mothers, sisters, and so forth. 'Then the same would apply even to a monk?' Not so, since his purpose of benefiting beings is accomplished through another mode of celibacy.

body.text: tathā hy uktam ārya-akṣayamati-sūtre | kāla-a-kāle punar anena + upekṣā karaṇīyā + iti ||
body.translated_text: For thus it is stated in the noble <s>Akṣayamatisūtra</s>: 'Furthermore, he should exercise equanimity at the right and wrong time.'

body.text: atha tato * apy adhikaṃ satva-arthaṃ paśyet | śikṣāṃ nikṣipet ||
body.translated_text: But if he sees an even greater benefit to beings than that — he should lay down the training.

body.text: upāya-kauśalya-sūtre jyotir-māṇavakaṃ dvācatvāriṃśad-varṣa-sahasra-brahma-cāriṇam adhikṛtya saptame pade sthitasya kāruṇyam utpadyeta | kiṃ ca + apy aham idaṃ vrataṃ khaṇḍayitvā niraya-parāyaṇaḥ syāṃ | tathā + apy utsahe * ahaṃ nairayikaṃ duṣkhaṃ prativedayitum atha ca + iyaṃ strī sukhitā bhavatu | mā kālaṃ karotu | iti hi kula-putra jyotir-māṇavakaḥ paścān-mukho nivartya tāṃ striyaṃ dakṣiṇena pāṇinā gṛhītvā + evam āha | uttiṣṭha bhagini yathā-kāma-karaṇīyas te bhavāmi + iti || pe ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Upāyakauśalyasūtra</s>, regarding the youth <s>Jyotis</s>, who had been celibate for forty-two thousand years, when he stood at the seventh step, compassion arose: 'Even if by breaking this vow I become destined for hell — even so, I am prepared to experience the suffering of hell; but let this woman be made happy! Let her not meet her death!' Thus, O son of good family, the youth <s>Jyotis</s>, turning back, took that woman by his right hand and said: 'Rise, sister! I shall do whatever you wish.' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: so * ahaṃ kula-putra mahā-kāruṇya-citta-utpādena + itvareṇa kāma-upasaṃhitena daśa-kalpa-sahasrāṇi paścān-mukham akārṣam | paśya kula-putra yad anyeṣāṃ niraya-saṃvartanīyaṃ karma | tad upāya-kuśalasya bodhi-satvasya brahma-loka-upapatti-saṃvartanīyam iti ||
body.translated_text: 'I, O son of good family, through that trifling generation of the thought of great compassion — though connected with desire — went backward for ten thousand <s>kalpas</s>. Behold, O son of good family: that which for others would be <s>karma</s> leading to hell — for the <s>bodhisattva</s> who is skilled in means, that very [act] leads to rebirth in the <s>Brahmaloka</s>.'

body.text: punar atra + eva + āha | yadi bodhi-satva ekasya satvasya kuśala-mūlaṃ saṃjanayet tathā-rūpāṃ ca + āpattim āpadyeta yathā-rūpayā + āpattyā + āpannayā kalpa-śata-sahasraṃ niraye pacyeta | utsoḍhavyam eva bhagavan bodhi-satvena + āpattim āpattuṃ tac ca nairayikaṃ duṣkhaṃ | na tv eva tasya + ekasay satvasya kuśalaṃ parityaktum iti ||
body.translated_text: And again in the same [sūtra] it is stated: 'If a <s>bodhisattva</s> were to generate a wholesome root in a single being, and were to incur such a transgression — a transgression by which, having been committed, one would be cooked in hell for a hundred thousand <s>kalpas</s> — even so, O Blessed One, the <s>bodhisattva</s> should endure incurring the transgression and that hellish suffering. But he should never abandon the wholesome [root] of that single being.'

body.text: punar atra + eva + āha | iha kula-putra + upāya-kuśalo bodhi-satvo yadā kadā-cit kasmiṃś-cit pāpa-mitra-vaśena + āpattim āpadyeta | sa itaḥ pratisaṃśikṣate | na mayā + ebhiḥ skandhaiḥ parinirvāpayitavyaṃ | mayā punar evaṃ saṃnāhaḥ saṃnaddhavyaḥ | a-para-anta-koṭiḥ saṃsaritavyā satvānāṃ paripācana-hetor iti | na mayā citta-dāhaḥ karaṇīyo | yathā yathā saṃsariṣyāmi tathā tathā satvān paripācayiṣyāmi | api tv etāṃ ca + āpattiṃ yathā-dharmaṃ pratikariṣyāmi | āyatyāṃ saṃvaram āpatsye | sacet kula-putra pravrajito bodhi-satvaḥ parikalpam ādāya sarvāś catasro mūla-āpattīr atikramed anena ca + upāya-kauśalyena vinodayed | an-āpattiṃ bodhi-satvasya vadāmi + iti ||
body.translated_text: And again in the same [sūtra] it is stated: 'Here, O son of good family, when the <s>bodhisattva</s> skilled in means at some time or other incurs a transgression through the power of a bad companion — he trains again from this [point onward, thinking]: "I should not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> with these <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates). Rather, I should don armor thus: I shall wander in <s>saṃsāra</s> to the very end, for the sake of maturing beings. I should not cause burning in my mind. As much as I shall wander [in saṃsāra], to that extent I shall ripen beings. Moreover, I shall counteract this transgression according to the <s>Dharma</s>. In the future I shall undertake the restraint." If, O son of good family, a renunciant <s>bodhisattva</s>, by supposition, were to transgress all four root offenses — but were to dispel [their effects] through this skillful means — I declare that there is no transgression for the <s>bodhisattva</s>.'

body.text: sphuṭaṃ ca + ārya-ratna-meghe ānantarya-cikīrṣu-puruṣa-māraṇa-anujñānāt ||
body.translated_text: And it is clearly [shown] in the noble <s>Ratnamegha</s>, from the permission to kill a man who intends to commit an <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) crime.

body.text: śrāvaka-vinaye * api mūla-āpatti-sthānae eva kāruṇyān mṛga-ādi-mokṣaṇe * an-āpattir uktā + eva ||
body.translated_text: Even in the <s>Śrāvaka Vinaya</s>, at the very point of root offense, non-transgression has been stated for the release of deer and so forth, out of compassion.

body.text: ayaṃ ca rāge guṇo yad bodhi-satve rāgam utpādya su-gatir labhyate | na tu krodhena ||
body.translated_text: And this is the virtue of attachment: that by generating attachment toward a <s>bodhisattva</s>, a good rebirth is obtained — but not through anger.

body.text: yathā + uktam upāya-kauśalya-sūtre | priyaṃkare bodhi-satve raktā ... dhavyottarāṃ dārikām adhikṛtya | priyaṃkarasya praṇidheḥ punaḥ punar yā istri prekṣeta sa-rāga-cittā | sā istri-bhāvaṃ parivarjayitvā puruṣo bhavet yādṛg udāra-satvaḥ ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Upāyakauśalyasūtra</s>, regarding the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Priyaṃkara</s> and the maiden <s>Dhavyottarā</s>, who was attached [to him]: 'The woman who looks again and again at <s>Priyaṃkara</s> with a passionate mind — that woman, abandoning womanhood, becomes a man, a being of noble character.'

body.text: paśyasva ānanda guṇā + asya īdṛśāḥ | yena + anya-satvā nirayam vrajanti | tena + eva śūreṣu janitva rāgaṃ gacchanti svargaṃ puruṣatvam eva ca || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'Behold, <s>Ānanda</s>, his virtues are of such a kind! That by which other beings go to hell — by generating attachment toward those heroes through that very [feeling], they go to heaven and [attain] manhood itself.' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: bhaiṣajya-rājeṣu mahā-yaśeṣu | ko bodhi-satveṣu janayeta dveṣam | yesāṃ kileśo * api sukhasya dāyakaḥ | kiṃ vā punar yaḥ tān sat-kareyā | iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Among those glorious kings of medicine, who would generate hatred toward <s>bodhisattvas</s> — for whom even affliction (<s>kleśa</s>) is a bestower of happiness? How much more, then, for one who would honor them!'

body.text: evam anyasmin satva-artha-upāye sati rāga-ja-āpattir an-āpattir uktā ||
body.translated_text: Thus, when there is another means for the benefit of beings, a transgression born of attachment is declared to be non-transgression.

body.text: upāya-kauśalya-sūtre ca gaṇikā-vat kṛta-artho bodhi-satvo nir-apekṣas taṃ satvaṃ tyajati + iti vistareṇa + uktam ||
body.translated_text: And in the <s>Upāyakauśalyasūtra</s>, it is stated in detail that the <s>bodhisattva</s>, having accomplished his purpose like a courtesan, abandons that being without attachment.

body.text: a-labdha-bhūmeś ca ṣaṭ-pāramitāsu caritavata iyaṃ cintā | na + itarasya + ity āstāṃ prāsaṅgikam ||
body.translated_text: And this consideration [applies] to one who has not attained the [bodhisattva] stages but has practiced the six <s>pāramitās</s> — not to another. But enough with what is incidental.

body.text: tasmād dveṣasya + avakāśo na deya | uktaṃ hy upāli-paripṛcchāyāṃ | bodhi-satvānāṃ śāriputra dve mahā-sa-avadye āpattī | katame dve | dveṣa-saha-gatā moha-saha-gatā ca + iti | tatra śāriputra prathamā āpattir daśa-varge ṛjukena deśayitavyā | hasta-āpattiḥ pañca varge gurvī deśayitavyā | striyā hasta-grahaṇaṃ cakṣur-darśanaṃ | duṣṭa-citta-āpattir eka-pudgalasya dvayor vā śāriputra tāṃ gurvīṃ daśayet | pañca + ānantarya-samanvāgatā + āpattir bodhi-satvena stry--āpattir dārikā-āpattir hasta-āpattiḥ stūpa-āpattiḥ saṃgha-āpattis tathā + anyāś ca + āpattayo bodhi-satvena na pañcatriṃśatāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatām antike rātriṃ-divaṃ ekākinā gurvyo deśayitavyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therefore no room should be given to hatred. For it is stated in the <s>Upāliparipṛcchā</s>: 'For <s>bodhisattvas</s>, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, there are two greatly blameworthy transgressions. What are the two? One accompanied by hatred, and one accompanied by delusion. Therein, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, the first transgression should be confessed straightforwardly before a group of ten. A hand-transgression should be confessed as a grave [offense] before a group of five. The grasping of a woman's hand, the gazing with the eyes — a transgression of corrupt mind should be confessed to one or two persons, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, as grave. A transgression connected with the five <s>ānantaryas</s> (heinous crimes), a woman-transgression, a maiden-transgression, a hand-transgression, a <s>stūpa</s>-transgression, a <s>Saṃgha</s>-transgression, and other such transgressions — the <s>bodhisattva</s> should confess these grave [offenses] alone, day and night, before the thirty-five <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones.'

body.text: tatra + iyaṃ deśanā | aham evaṃ-nāmā buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi | dharmaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi | saṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi ||
body.translated_text: 'Therein, this is the confession: "I, named so-and-so, go for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s>. I go for refuge to the <s>Dharma</s>. I go for refuge to the <s>Saṃgha</s>."'

body.text: namaḥ śākya-munaye tathā-gatāya + arhate samyak-saṃbuddhāya | namo vajra-pramardine | namo ratna-arciṣe | namo nāga-īśvara-rājāya | namo vīra-senāya | namo vīra-nandine | namo ratna-śriye | namo ratna-candra-prabhāya | namo * a-mogha-darśine | namo ratna-candrāya | namo nir-malāya | namo vi-malāya | namaḥ śūra-dattāya | namo brahmaṇe | namo brahma-dattāya | namo varuṇāya | namo varuṇa-devāya | namo bhadra-śriye | namaś chandana-śriye | namo * an-anta-ojase | namaḥ prabhāsa-śriye | namo * a-śoka-śriye | namo nārāyaṇāya | namaḥ kusuma-śriye | namo brahma-jyotir-vikrīḍita-abhijñāya tathā-gatāya | namo dhana-śriye | namaḥ smṛti-śriye | namaḥ su-parikīrtita-nāma-dheya-śriye | nama indra-ketu-dhvaja-rājāya | namaḥ su-vikrānta-śriye | namo vicitra-saṃkramāya | namo vikrānta-gāmine | namaḥ samanta-avabhāsa-vyūha-śriye | namo ratna-padma-vikrāmiṇe | namo ratna-padma-su-pratiṣṭhita-śaila-indra-rājāya tathā-gatāya + arhate samyak-saṃbuddhāya ||
body.translated_text: 'Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened <s>Śākyamuni</s>. Homage to <s>Vajrapramardin</s>. Homage to <s>Ratnārcis</s>. Homage to <s>Nāgeśvararāja</s>. Homage to <s>Vīrasena</s>. Homage to <s>Vīranandin</s>. Homage to <s>Ratnaśrī</s>. Homage to <s>Ratnacandraprabhā</s>. Homage to <s>Amoghadarśin</s>. Homage to <s>Ratnacandra</s>. Homage to <s>Nirmala</s>. Homage to <s>Vimala</s>. Homage to <s>Śūradatta</s>. Homage to <s>Brahman</s>. Homage to <s>Brahmadatta</s>. Homage to <s>Varuṇa</s>. Homage to <s>Varuṇadeva</s>. Homage to <s>Bhadraśrī</s>. Homage to <s>Candanaśrī</s>. Homage to <s>Anantaojas</s>. Homage to <s>Prabhāsaśrī</s>. Homage to <s>Aśokaśrī</s>. Homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. Homage to <s>Kusumaśrī</s>. Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Brahmajyotirvikrīḍitābhijña</s>. Homage to <s>Dhanaśrī</s>. Homage to <s>Smṛtiśrī</s>. Homage to <s>Suparikīrtitanāmadheyaśrī</s>. Homage to <s>Indraketudhvajarāja</s>. Homage to <s>Suvikrāntaśrī</s>. Homage to <s>Vicitrasaṃkrama</s>. Homage to <s>Vikrāntagāmin</s>. Homage to <s>Samantāvabhāsavyūhaśrī</s>. Homage to <s>Ratnapadmavikrāmin</s>. Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened <s>Ratnapadmasupratiṣṭhitaśailendrarāja</s>.'

body.text: evaṃ-pramukhā yāvantaḥ sarva-loka-dhātuṣu tathā-gata-arhantaḥ samyak-saṃbuddhās tiṣṭhanti dhriyante yāpayanti | te māṃ samanvāharantu buddhā bhagavanto yan mayā + asyāṃ jātau anyāsu vā jātiṣv an-avara-agre jāti-saṃsāre saṃsaratā
