children.text: pāpakaṃ karma kṛtaṃ syāt kāritaṃ vā kriyamāṇaṃ vā + anumoditaṃ bhavet | staupikaṃ vā sāṅghikaṃ vā dravyam apahṛtaṃ syāt hāritaṃ vā hriyamāṇaṃ vā + anumoditaṃ bhavet | pañca-an-antaryāṇi kṛtāni syuḥ kāritāni vā kriyamāṇāni vā + anumoditāni bhaveyuḥ | daśa-a-kuśalān karma-pathān samādāya vartitaṃ syāt pare vā samādāpitāḥ syur vartamānā vā + anumoditā bhaveyur yena karma-āvaraṇena + āvṛto * ahaṃ nirayaṃ vā gaccheyaṃ tiryag-yoniṃ vā yama-viṣayaṃ vā gaccheyaṃ praty-anta-jana-padeṣu mleccheṣu vā pratyājāyeyaṃ dīrgha-āyuṣkeṣu deveṣu + upapadyeyam indriya-vikalatāṃ vā + adhigaccheyaṃ mithyā-dṛṣṭiṃ vā + upagṛhṇīyāṃ buddha-utpādaṃ vā virāgayeyaṃ | tat sarvaṃ karma-āvaraṇaṃ teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ jñāna-bhūtānāṃ cakṣur-bhūtānāṃ sa-akṣi-bhūtānāṃ pramāṇa-bhūtānāṃ jānatāṃ paśyatām agrataḥ pratideśayāmi āviṣ-karomi na praticchādayāmy āyatyāṃ saṃvaram āpadye | samanvāharantu māṃ te buddhā bhagavanto yan mayā + asyāṃ jātāv anyāsu vā jātiṣv an-avara-agre vā jāti-saṃsāre saṃsaratā dānaṃ dattaṃ bhaved antaśas tiryag-yoni-gatāya + apy ālopaḥ śīlaṃ vā rakṣitaṃ bhaved yac ca me brahma-carya-vāsa-kuśala-mūlaṃ yac ca me satva-paripāka-kuśala-mūlaṃ yac ca me bodhi-citta-kuśala-mūlaṃ yac ca me * an-uttara-jñāna-kuśala-mūlaṃ tat sarvam aikadhyaṃ piṇḍayitvā tulayitvā + abhisaṃkṣipya + an-utt arāyāṃ samyak-saṃbodhau uttara-uttarayā pariṇāmanayā yathā pariṇāmitam atītair buddhair bhagavadbhir yathā pariṇāmayiṣyanty an-āgatā buddhā bhagavanto yathā pariṇamanty etarhi daśasu dikṣu praty-utpannā buddhā bhagavantaḥ | tathā + aham api pariṇāmayāmi | sarvaṃ puṇyam anumodayāmi | sarvān buddhān adhyeṣayāmi | bhavatu me jñānam an-uttaram | ye ca + abhyatītās tathā + api ca ye an-āgatā ye ca + api tiṣṭhanti nara-uttamā jināḥ | an-anta-varṇān guṇa-sāgara-upamān upaimi sarvān śaraṇaṃ kṛta-añjaliḥ | ye bodhi-satvāḥ karuṇa-balair upetā vicarati loke satva-hitāya śūrāḥ trāyantu te māṃ sada-pāpa-kāriṇaṃ
children.translated_text: Whether sinful <s>karma</s> has been committed, caused to be committed, is being committed, or has been approved; whether property belonging to a <s>stūpa</s> or to the <s>Saṅgha</s> has been taken, caused to be taken, is being taken, or has been approved [of its taking]; whether the five heinous acts (<s>ānantarya</s>) have been committed, caused to be committed, are being committed, or have been approved; whether one has lived having undertaken the ten unwholesome courses of action, or has caused others to undertake them, or has approved of those who are [so] living — whatever karmic obstruction by which I might go to the hells, or to the animal realm, or to the domain of <s>Yama</s>, or be reborn among border peoples and barbarians, or be reborn among long-lived gods, or attain deficiency of faculties, or take up wrong views, or be averse to the arising of a <s>Buddha</s> — all that karmic obstruction I confess, make manifest, and do not conceal before those <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s> who are knowledge-beings, who are eye-beings, who are witnesses, who are authorities, who know and see; and for the future I undertake restraint. May those <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s> take note of me: whatever gift I may have given in this birth or in other births, while wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s> without beginning or end — even a morsel to one born in the animal realm; whatever moral conduct I may have guarded; whatever wholesome root of celibate living I have; whatever wholesome root of ripening beings I have; whatever wholesome root of <s>bodhicitta</s> I have; whatever wholesome root of unsurpassed knowledge I have — all of that, gathered together, weighed, and collected, I dedicate to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) with ever higher dedication, just as the <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s> of the past have dedicated, as the <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s> of the future will dedicate, as the <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s> of the present in the ten directions dedicate. Just so do I also dedicate. I rejoice in all merit. I beseech all <s>Buddhas</s>. May unsurpassed knowledge be mine! Those <s>Jinas</s>, supreme among men, who have passed, who are yet to come, and who abide — of infinite virtues, like oceans of qualities — I go to all of them for refuge with palms joined. Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> endowed with the power of compassion who wander in the world, heroes for the welfare of beings — may they rescue me, the constant evil-doer,
I go to those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> for refuge.

body.translated_text: 'These and others — as many <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones as abide, endure, and live in all the world-realms — may those blessed <s>Buddhas</s> attend to me! Whatever, in this birth or in other births, throughout beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, while wandering —'

body.text: iti hi śāriputra bodhi-satvena + imān pañcatriṃśato buddhān pramukhān kṛtvā sarva-tathā-gata-anugatair manasi-kāraiḥ pāpa-śuddhiḥ kāryā | tasya + evaṃ sarva-pāpa-viśuddhasya tatra ca buddhā bhagavanto mukhāny upadarśayanti satva-vimokṣa-artham eva | nānā-vyañjana-ākāram upadarśayanti vibhrānta-bāla-pṛthag-janānāṃ paripācanā-hetoḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s>, having placed these thirty-five <s>Buddhas</s> at the forefront, should perform the purification of sin through mental activities that follow all the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. When all his sins have been thus purified, those <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s> show [him their] faces for the very purpose of liberating beings. They show [him forms of] various characters and appearances, for the purpose of ripening deluded, confused ordinary persons. [Abbreviation.]

body.text: na śakyaṃ sarva-śrāvaka-praty-eka-buddha-nikāyair āpatti-kaukṛtya-sthānaṃ viśodhayituṃ yad bodhi-satvas teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ nāma-dheya-dhāraṇa-parikīrtanena rātriṃ-divaṃ tri-skandhaka-dharma-paryāya-pravartanena + āpatti-kaukṛtyān niḥsarati samādhiṃ ca pratilabhate ||
body.translated_text: It is not possible for the entirety of <s>śrāvaka</s> and <s>pratyekabuddha</s> assemblies to purify the ground of transgression and remorse [as effectively as] a <s>bodhisattva</s> who, through retaining and proclaiming the names of those <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s> and practicing the <s>triskandha</s> (three-section) <s>Dharma</s>-discourse day and night, emerges from transgression and remorse and attains <s>samādhi</s>.

body.text: ukto vidūṣaṇa-a-samudācāraḥ | prati-pakṣa-samudācāra ucyate | tatra gambhīra-sūtra-anta-paricayāt pāpa-kṣayo bhavati ||
body.translated_text: The conduct of non-defilement has been stated. The conduct of the antidote is now stated. Therein, through familiarity with the profound <s>sūtra</s>-conclusions, the destruction of sin occurs.

body.text: yathā vajra-cchedikāyām uktaṃ | ye te subhūte kula-putrā vā kula-duhitaro vā imān evaṃ-rūpān sūtra-antān udgrahīṣyanti yāvat paryavāpsyanti | te paribhūtā bhaviṣyanti su-paribhūtāḥ | tat kasya hetoḥ | yāni teṣāṃ satvānāṃ paurva-janmikāni karmāṇi kṛtāny apāya-saṃvartanīyāni | tāni tayā paribhūtatayā dṛṣṭae eva dharme kṣapayiṣyanti buddha-bodhiṃ ca prāpsyanti + iti ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Vajracchedikā</s> (Diamond Cutter): 'Those sons or daughters of good family, O <s>Subhūti</s>, who will take up and master such <s>sūtra</s>-conclusions as these — they will be scorned and greatly scorned. Why? Because those sinful actions performed by those beings in previous births, which would have led to lower realms — by that very condition of being scorned, in this very life they will exhaust [those past actions], and they will attain the awakening of the <s>Buddha</s>.'

body.text: śūnyatā-adhimuktyā + api pāpa-śuddhir bhavati tathā-gata-koṣa-sūtre vacanāt | yaḥ kāśyapa pitā ca syāt praty-eka-buddhaś ca taṃ jīvitād vyaparopayed idam agraṃ prāṇa-atipātānāṃ | idam agram a-datta-ādānānāṃ yad uta tri-ratna-dravya-apaharaṇatā | idam agraṃ kāma-mithyā-ācārāṇāṃ yad uta mātā syād arhantī ca | idam agraṃ mṛṣā-vādānāṃ yad uta tathā-gatasya + abhyākhyānaṃ | idam agraṃ paiśunyānāṃ yad uta + ārya-saṃghasya + a-varṇaḥ | idam agraṃ pāruṣyāṇāṃ yad uta + āryāṇām avasphaṇḍanaṃ | idam agraṃ saṃbhinna-pralāpānāṃ yad uta dharma-kāmānāṃ vikṣepaḥ | idam agraṃ vyāpādānāṃ yad uta + ānantarya-parikarṣaṇam | idam agram abhidhyānāṃ yad uta samyag-gatānāṃ lābha-haraṇa-cittatā | idam agraṃ mithyā-dṛṣṭīnāṃ yad uta gahanatā-dṛṣṭiḥ | ime kāśyapa daśa + a-kuśalāḥ karma-pathā mahā-sa-āvadyāḥ | sacet kāśyapa eka-satva ebhir evaṃ mahā-sa-āvadyair daśabhir a-kuśalaiḥ karma-pathaiḥ samanvāgato bhavet | sa ca tathā-gatasya hetu-pratyaya-saṃyuktāṃ dharma-deśanām avataren | na + atra kaś-cid ātmā vā satvo vā jīvo vā pudgalo vā yaḥ karoti pratisaṃvedayate iti hy a-kṛtām an-abhisaṃskārāṃ māyā-dharmatām a-saṃkleśa-dharmatāṃ prakṛti-prabhāsvaratāṃ sarva-dharmāṇām avataraty ādi-śuddhān sarva-dharmān abhiśraddadhāty adhimucyate | na + ahaṃ tasya satvasya + apāya-gamanaṃ vadāmi + iti ||
body.translated_text: Through conviction in emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) too, purification of sin occurs, as stated in the <s>Tathāgatakoṣa Sūtra</s>: 'O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, if one who is both a father and a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> — and one deprives him of life — this is the supreme among killings. This is the supreme among thefts — namely, the stealing of the property of the Three Jewels. This is the supreme among sexual misconducts — when the [victim] is both one's mother and an <s>arhat</s> (worthy one). This is the supreme among false speeches — namely, defamation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. This is the supreme among slanders — namely, speaking ill of the noble <s>Saṅgha</s>. This is the supreme among harsh words — namely, the derision of noble ones. This is the supreme among idle talks — namely, the distraction of those who desire the <s>Dharma</s>. This is the supreme among ill-wills — namely, the cultivation of the conditions for the heinous acts. This is the supreme among covetousness — namely, the mentality of seizing the gains of those rightly progressing. This is the supreme among wrong views — namely, the view of impenetrability. These, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the ten unwholesome courses of action that are greatly blameworthy. If, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a single being endowed with these ten greatly blameworthy unwholesome courses of action were to enter the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> connected with causes and conditions — [understanding] that "here there is no self, no being, no life-force, no person, who acts or experiences" — thus penetrating the uncreated, unfabricated, illusion-like nature, the nature free from defilement, the nature of primordial luminosity of all <s>dharmas</s>; and if he trusts and aspires to all <s>dharmas</s> as primordially pure — I do not declare that that being will go to a lower realm.'

body.text: karma-āvaraṇa-viśuddhi-sūtre * apy uktaṃ | punar a-paraṃ mañjuśrīr yo bodhi-satva āpattim an-āpattiṃ paśyati | a-vinayaṃ vinayaṃ paśyati | saṃkleśaṃ vyavadānaṃ paśyati | saṃsāra-dhātuṃ nirvāṇa-dhātuṃ paśyati | sa karma-āvaraṇa-viśuddhiṃ pratilabhatae iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Karmāvaraṇaviśuddhi Sūtra</s> (Sūtra on the Purification of Karmic Obstructions) it is also said: 'Furthermore, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who sees transgression as non-transgression, who sees indiscipline as discipline, who sees defilement as purification, who sees the realm of <s>saṃsāra</s> as the realm of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — he attains the purification of karmic obstructions.'

body.text: tri-samaya-rāje * api pāpa-prati-pakṣa-samudācāra uktaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Trisamayarāja</s> too, the conduct of the antidote to sin is stated.

body.text: akṣiṇī nimīlya buddha-bodhi-satva-ālambana-cittaḥ śata-akṣaram aṣṭa-sahasraṃ japet | nimīlita-akṣa eva buddha-bodhi-satvān paśyati vigata-pāpo bhavati | atha-vā caityaṃ pradakṣiṇī-kurvann aṣṭa-sahasraṃ japec caitya-pratimāyāḥ sad-dharma-pustakānāṃ ca + ekatamaṃ puras-kṛtya + ayam eva vidhir iti ||
body.translated_text: Closing one's eyes, with the mind focused on <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s>, one should recite eight thousand [times] the hundred-syllable [mantra]. With eyes still closed, one sees the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s> and becomes free of sin. Alternatively, while circumambulating a <s>caitya</s> (shrine), one should recite eight thousand [times], placing before oneself one of the following: an image of a <s>caitya</s>, or books of the true <s>Dharma</s> — this is the procedure.

body.text: cundā-dhāraṇīṃ vā tāvaj japed yāvat pāpa-kṣaya-nimittāni paśyati svapne | tad yathā krandana-ādi-chardana-dadhi-kṣīra-ādi-bhojanāt tu vigata-pāpo bhavati | vamanād vā candra-sūrya-darśanād ākāśa-gamanāj jvalita-anala-mahiṣa-kṛṣṇa-puruṣa-parājayād bhikṣu-bhikṣuṇī-saṃgha-darśanāt kṣīra-vṛkṣa-gaja-vṛṣa-giri-siṃha-āsana-prāsādana-avarohaṇād dharma-śravaṇāc ca pāpa-kṣayaḥ saṃlakṣayitavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Or one should recite the <s>Cundā-dhāraṇī</s> until one sees signs of the destruction of sin in dreams. Such as: weeping and the like, vomiting, eating yogurt, milk, and the like — by these one becomes free of sin. Or from vomiting, from seeing the sun and moon, from traveling through the sky, from defeating a blazing fire, a buffalo, a dark person; from seeing an assembly of monks and nuns; from descending from a milk-tree, an elephant, a bull, a mountain, a lion-throne, or a mansion; and from hearing the <s>Dharma</s> — the destruction of sin should be recognized.

body.text: tathā-gata-bimba-parivarte * api prati-pakṣa-samudācāra uktaḥ | tad yathā puruṣo mīḍha-avaliptaḥ su-dhautu-snānaṃ kṛtvā gandhair vilipyate | tasya tad daurgandhyaṃ vāntaṃ vigataṃ syād evaṃ pañca-ānantarya-kāriṇas tat pāpaṃ vigacchati | yo * api daśa-a-kuśala-karma-patha-samanvāgatas tathā-gate śraddhāṃ pratilabhya tathā-gata-bimbaṃ kārayet tasya + api tat pāpaṃ na prajñāyate viśeṣato bodhi-citta-samanvāgatasya | viśeṣato * abhiniṣkrānta-gṛha-āvāsasya śīlavata iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Tathāgatavimbaparivarta</s> (Chapter on the Image of the Tathāgata) too, the conduct of the antidote is stated: 'Just as a man smeared with excrement, having washed and bathed thoroughly, anoints himself with fragrances — and that foul smell of his would be gone and vanished — just so, the sin of one who has committed the five heinous acts departs. And one endowed with the ten unwholesome courses of action, having obtained faith in the <s>Tathāgata</s> and having had an image of the <s>Tathāgata</s> made — his sin too is no longer apparent, especially for one endowed with <s>bodhicitta</s>; especially for one who has gone forth from the household life and is virtuous.'

body.text: puṣpa-kūṭa-dhāraṇyām apy uktaṃ | yaś ca khalu punaḥ siṃha-vikrīḍita-tathā-gataṃ saṃmukhaṃ varṣaṃ vā varṣa-sahasraṃ vā varṣa-śata-sahasraṃ vā sarva-sukha-upadhānair upatiṣṭhed | yaś ca parinirvṛtasya tathā-gatasya caitye bodhi-citta-saṃgṛhīta eka-puṣpam āropayet tathā-gata-pūjāyai jana-añjaliṃ ca + upanāmayej jalena vā siñcayed iṣikā-padaṃ vā dadyān nir-mālyaṃ ca + apanayed upalepana-pradānaṃ vā puṣpa-pradānaṃ vā dīpa-pradānaṃ vā kuryād ātta-manāḥ eka-krama-vyatihāraṃ vā + atikramya vācaṃ bhāṣate | namas tasmai buddhāya bhagavata iti-mātre * atra siṃha-vikrīḍita-kāṅkṣā vā vi-matir vā vicikitsā vā yad asau kalpaṃ vā kalpa-śataṃ vā kalpa-sahasraṃ vā dur-gati-vinipātaṃ gacchen na + idaṃ sthānaṃ vidyatae iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Puṣpakūṭadhāraṇī</s> it is also said: 'If someone were to attend upon the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Siṃhavikrīḍita</s> face-to-face for a year, or a thousand years, or a hundred thousand years, with every provision of comfort; and if another, with a mind embraced by <s>bodhicitta</s>, were to place a single flower upon the <s>caitya</s> of that <s>Tathāgata</s> who has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, for the worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and offer a public salutation, or sprinkle it with water, or give a measure of reed, or remove withered offerings, or make an offering of ointment, or flowers, or a lamp, and with a joyful mind, even crossing [the ground] with a single step, utters the words: "Homage to that <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>!" — as for doubt, hesitation, or uncertainty about this <s>Siṃhavikrīḍita</s> [<s>Tathāgata</s>], that he would go to a lower realm or ruin for a <s>kalpa</s>, a hundred <s>kalpas</s>, or a thousand <s>kalpas</s> — such a thing is not possible.'

body.text: bhaiṣajya-guru-vaidūrya-prabha-rāja-sūtre * apy uktaṃ | ye pañca śikṣā-padāni dhārayanti | ye daśa śikṣā-padāni dhārayanti | ye ca bodhi-satva-saṃvaraṃ caturthaṃ śataṃ śikṣā-padānāṃ dhārayanti | ye punar abhiniṣkrānta-gṛha-āvāsā bhikṣavaḥ pañcāśa-adhike dve śikṣā-pada-śate dhārayanti | yāś ca bhikṣuṇyaḥ pañca-śikṣā-pada-śatāni dhārayanti | ye ca yathā-parigṛhītāc * chikṣā-saṃvarād anyatarāc * chikṣā-padād bhraṣṭā bhavanti | sacet te dur-gati-bhaya-bhītās tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajya-guru-vaiḍūrya-prabha-rājasya tathā-gatasya nāma-dheyaṃ dhārayeyur yathā-vibhavataś ca pūjāṃ kuryuḥ | na bhūyas teṣām apāya-gatiḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyā ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Bhaiṣajyaguru-Vaiḍūryaprabharāja Sūtra</s> it is also said: 'Those who maintain the five training rules; those who maintain the ten training rules; those who maintain the <s>bodhisattva</s> vow of four hundred training rules; those monks who have gone forth from the household life and maintain two hundred and fifty training rules; those nuns who maintain five hundred training rules — and those who have lapsed from any training rule of whatever vow they have undertaken — if those who fear the terror of lower realms retain the name of that <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguru-Vaiḍūryaprabharāja</s> and perform worship according to their means, then a lower realm destiny is no longer to be expected for them.'

body.text: atha bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate sma | śraddadhāsi tvam ānanda | pattīyasi | yad ahaṃ tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajya-guru-vaiḍūrya-prabha-rājasya tathā-gatasya guṇān varṇayāmi | atha te kāṅkṣā vā vi-matir vā vicikitsā vā + atra gambhīre buddha-go-care ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Do you believe, O <s>Ānanda</s>? Do you trust? That I am praising the virtues of that <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguru-Vaiḍūryaprabharāja</s>? Is there any doubt, hesitation, or uncertainty in you regarding this profound domain of the <s>Buddha</s>?'

body.text: atha + āyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam etad avocat | na me bhadanta bhagavan kāṅkṣā vā vi-matir vā vicikitsā vā tathā-gata-bhāṣiteṣu sūtra-anteṣu | tat kasya hetoḥ | na + asti tathā-gatānām a-pariśuddha-kāya-vāṅ-manaḥ-samudācāratā | imau bhagavan candra-sūryāv evaṃ maha-rddhikāv evaṃ mahā-anubhāvau pṛthivyāṃ patetāṃ | sumeruḥ parvata-rājā sthānāc calet | na tu buddhānāṃ vacanam anyathā bhavet ||
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'O venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, I have no doubt, no hesitation, no uncertainty regarding the <s>sūtra</s>-conclusions spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Why? Because the <s>Tathāgatas</s> do not have impure conduct of body, speech, or mind. O <s>Bhagavān</s>, these sun and moon, of such great power and might, might fall to the earth; <s>Sumeru</s>, king of mountains, might move from its place — but the word of the <s>Buddhas</s> would never become otherwise.'

body.text: kiṃ-tu bhadanta bhagavan santi satvāḥ śraddhā-indriya-vikalā ye buddha-go-caraṃ śrutvā na śraddadhati | teṣām evaṃ bhavati | katham idaṃ nāma-dheyaṃ smaraṇa-mātreṇa tasya tathā-gatasya ettakā guṇa-anuśaṃsā bhavati | te na śraddadhati | na pattīyanti | pratikṣipanti | teṣāṃ dīrgha-rātram an-arthāya + a-hitāya + a-sukhāya vinipātāya bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: 'However, Venerable Blessed One, there are beings deficient in the faculty of faith who, upon hearing the domain of the <s>Buddha</s>, do not have faith. Their thought is thus: "How can it be that merely by remembering the name of that <s>Tathāgata</s>, such great benefits of virtues arise?" They do not believe; they do not trust; they reject [it]. For them, it will be for their long-term harm, non-benefit, unhappiness, and downfall.'

body.text: bhagavān āha | a-sthānam ānanda + an-avakāśo yeṣāṃ tasya nāma-dheyaṃ nipatet karṇe teṣāṃ dur-gaty-apāya-gamanaṃ bhaved iti | duḥ-śraddhānīyaś ca + ānanda buddhānāṃ buddha-go-caraḥ |yac ca tvam ānanda śraddadhāsi pattīyasi | tathā-gatasya + eṣo * anubhāvo draṣṭavyaḥ | a-bhūmiś ca + atra śrāvaka-praty-eka-buddhānāṃ sthāpayitvā eka-jāti-pratibaddhān bodhi-satvān mahā-satvān iti ||
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'It is impossible, <s>Ānanda</s>, there is no occasion, that for those in whose ears that name would fall, there would be a going to the lower realms and evil destinies. And, <s>Ānanda</s>, the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s> is difficult to believe in. That you, <s>Ānanda</s>, do believe and trust — this should be seen as the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And this is not the ground of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, except for <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who are bound to one more birth.'

body.text: atra + eva ca + uktaṃ | ye ca + anye śrāddhāḥ kula-putrā vā kula-duhitaro vā + aṣṭa-aṅga-samanvāgatam upavāsam upavasanti | eka-vārṣikaṃ vā traivārṣikaṃ vā śikṣā-padaṃ dhārayanti | yeṣām evam abhiprāyaḥ evaṃ praṇidhānaṃ | anena vayaṃ kuśala-mūlena paścimāyāṃ diśāyāṃ sukhāvatyāṃ loka-dhātau upapadyema yatra + amitābhas tathāgataḥ | yaiḥ śrutaṃ bhaviṣyati tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajya-guru-vaiḍūrya-prabhava-rājasya tathā-gatasya nāma-dheyaṃ | teṣāṃ maraṇa-kāla-samaye * aṣṭau bodhi-satvā ṛddhyā + āgatya mārgam upadarśayanti | te tatra nānā-raṅgeṣu padmeṣu + upapādukāḥ prādur-bhavanti | ke-cit punar deva-lokae upapadyante | teṣāṃ tatra + upapannānāṃ tat pūrvakaṃ kuśala-mūlaṃ na kṣīyate | dur-gati-vinipāta-bhayaṃ ca na bhaviṣyati | te tataś cyutā iha manuṣya-loke rājāno bhavanti | catur-dvīpa-īśvarāś cakra-vartinaḥ | an-ekāni satva-koṭī-niyuta-śata-sahasrāṇi daśa kuśaleṣu karma-patheṣu pratiṣṭhāpayanti | a-pare punaḥ kṣatriya-mahā-śāla-kuleṣu + upapadyante | brāhmaṇa-mahā-śāla-kuleṣu + upapadyante | gṛha-pati-mahā-śāla-kuleṣu prabhūta-dhana-dhānya-koṣa-koṣṭha-āgāra-kuleṣu + upapadyante | te rūpa-saṃpannā bhavanti | parivāra-sampannā bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: And right here it is said: 'And whatever other faithful sons of good family or daughters of good family observe the eight-limbed fasting vow, or maintain the training rule for one year or for three years — whose intention and aspiration is thus: "By this wholesome root, may we be reborn in the western direction, in the <s>Sukhāvatī</s> world-system, where the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s> [dwells]" — those who will have heard the name of that Blessed One, <s>Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabharāja Tathāgata</s>: for them, at the time of death, eight <s>bodhisattvas</s> come by miraculous power and show the path. They appear by spontaneous birth upon lotuses of various colors. Some, however, are reborn in the world of the <s>devas</s>. For those reborn there, the former wholesome root is not exhausted; and there will be no fear of falling into lower destinies. Having fallen from there, they become kings here in the human world — sovereigns of the four continents, universal monarchs. They establish innumerable billions of beings in the ten wholesome courses of action. Others, moreover, are reborn in great <s>kṣatriya</s> families, in great <s>brāhmaṇa</s> families, in great householder families — families with abundant riches, grain, treasuries, and storehouses. They become endowed with beauty; they become endowed with a retinue.'

body.text: tatra + eva + uktaṃ | yena ca punar mātṛ-grāmeṇa tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajya-guru-vaiḍūrya-prabha-rājasya tathā-gatasya nāma-dheyaṃ śrutaṃ bhaviṣyati | udgṛhītaṃ vā | sa tasya paścimo mātṛ-grāma-bhāvaḥ pratikāṅkṣitavya iti ||
body.translated_text: Right there it is said: 'And whatever woman will have heard the name of that Blessed One, <s>Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabharāja Tathāgata</s>, or will have grasped it — her state of being a woman should be expected to be the last.'

body.text: mañjuśrī-buddha-kṣetra-guṇa-vyūha-alaṃ-kāra-sūtre * apy uktaṃ | jñāna-uttara-prabhā-ketuṃ praṇidhāna-matiṃ tathā | śānta-indriyaṃ mañju-ghoṣaṃ bhaktitaḥ praṇamāmy aham ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Mañjuśrī-buddhakṣetra-guṇavyūhālaṅkāra-sūtra</s> too it is said: '<s>Jñānottaraprabhāketu</s>, <s>Praṇidhānamati</s>, likewise <s>Śāntendriya</s>, <s>Mañjughoṣa</s> — with devotion I bow to them.'

body.text: ya eṣāṃ bodhi-satvānāṃ nāma-dheyaṃ tu dhārayet | etasya mātṛ-grāmasya strī-bhāvo na bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: 'Whoever retains the names of these <s>bodhisattvas</s> — for that woman, the state of being female will no longer exist.'

body.text: uktaḥ saṃkṣepāt prati-pakṣa-samudācāraḥ ||
body.translated_text: The practice of the counter-agent has been stated in summary.

body.text: praty-āpatti-balam adhunā + ucyate ||
body.translated_text: The power of restoration (<s>pratyāpatti-bala</s>) is now stated.

body.text: yathā + uktam ārya-kṣitigarbha-sūtre | prāṇa-atipātāt prativirato bhavati bodhi-satvo mahā-satvaḥ sarva-satvānām a-bhayaṃ-dadaḥ | an-uttrāso * an-upāyāso * a-loma-harṣaḥ sa tena kuśala-mūlena karma-vipākena | yat pūrva-anta-koṭi-pañca-gati-cakra-āruḍhena saṃsāra-nady--udyātena prāṇa-atipāta-hetunā kāya-vāṅ-manasā karma-āvaraṇaṃ kleśa-āvaraṇaṃ dharma-āvaraṇaṃ kṛtaṃ vā syāt kāritaṃ vā + anumoditaṃ syāt | tat sarvaṃ tena prāṇa-atipāta-vairamaṇa-cakreṇa sarva-an-arthaṃ mardayati | yāvad a-śeṣam a-vipākaṃ kurute | sa-nikāya-sa-bhāge deva-manuṣyāṇāṃ priyo bhavati nir-ātaṅko dīrgha-āyuṣka iti ||
body.translated_text: As it is said in the <s>Ārya-Kṣitigarbha-sūtra</s>: 'The <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abstains from taking life, giving fearlessness to all beings — without terror, without distress, without hair-raising. By that wholesome root, by that ripening of <s>karma</s>: whatever obstruction of <s>karma</s>, obstruction of afflictions, obstruction of <s>Dharma</s> was done, caused to be done, or rejoiced in by body, speech, or mind — due to having mounted the wheel of the five destinies from the beginning-edge of the former limit, [and being] carried along by the river of <s>saṃsāra</s>, through the cause of taking life — all of that he crushes with the wheel of abstaining from taking life, [crushing] all calamity, until he renders it completely without ripening. He becomes dear to the <s>devas</s> and humans of his own group and similar class; free from affliction; of long life.'

body.text: yāvat punar a-paraṃ kula-putra yo bodhi-satvo yāvaj-jīvam a-datta-ādānāt prativirato bhavati sa sarva-satvānām a-bhayam dadāti anyatra + a-sa-yatnena + a-saṃkṣobheṇa sva-lābhena saṃtuṣṭo viharati | a-dhārmika-bhoga-an-abhilāṣī sa tena kuśala-mūlena yāvad a-datta-ādāna-hetukaṃ karma-āvaraṇaṃ mardayati pramardayati yāvad a-śeṣam a-vipākaṃ kurutae iti || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, O son of good family, whatever <s>bodhisattva</s> abstains for life from taking what is not given — he gives fearlessness to all beings; by another's effort alone, without agitation, he dwells content with his own gains; not desiring unlawful wealth — by that wholesome root, and so on, he crushes and completely crushes the obstruction of <s>karma</s> caused by taking what is not given, until he renders it completely without ripening.' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: evaṃ daśa + api kuśalāḥ karma-pathāḥ sva-vipakṣa-a-kuśala-ghātakās tatra paṭhyante ||
body.translated_text: Thus, all ten wholesome courses of action are read there as destroying their respective opposite unwholesome [courses].

body.text: tathā candra-pradīpa-sūtre * api vyāpāda-viratyā sarva-pāpa-kṣayaḥ śrūyate | yathā + āha | sahiṣyāmy atra bālānām a-bhūtāṃ paribhāṣaṇāṃ | ākrośanaṃ tarjanāṃ ca adhivāsiṣya nāyakaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, in the <s>Candrapradīpa-sūtra</s> too, the destruction of all sin through abstention from ill-will is heard. As it says: 'I shall endure here the unfounded abuse of fools — their reviling and threatening — the Leader shall forbear.'

body.text: kṣapayiṣye pāpakaṃ karma yan mayā purime kṛtam | anyeṣu bodhi-satveṣu vyāpādo janito mayā + iti ||
body.translated_text: 'I shall exhaust the evil <s>karma</s> that was formerly done by me: ill-will that was generated by me toward other <s>bodhisattvas</s>.'

body.text: uktaṃ praty-āpatti-balam ||
body.translated_text: The power of restoration has been stated.

body.text: āśraya-balaṃ tu vaktavyam ||
body.translated_text: But the power of the support (<s>āśraya-bala</s>) must be stated.

body.text: atra sūkarika-avadānam udāhāryam | ye buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ yānti na te gacchanti dur-gatiṃ | prahāya mānuṣān kāyān divyān kāyāṃl labhanti te ||
body.translated_text: Here the <s>sūkarika-avadāna</s> (story of the pig-keeper) should be cited: 'Those who go to the <s>Buddha</s> for refuge do not go to the lower destinies. Having left human bodies, they obtain divine bodies.'

body.text: ity evaṃ dharmaṃ saṃghaṃ ca + adhikṛtya pāpa-kṣayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus, with reference to the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Saṃgha</s> likewise, the destruction of sin [is stated].

body.text: ārya-maitreya-vimokṣe tu bodhi-cittena pāpa-viśuddhir uktā | kalpa-uddāhā-agni-bhūtaṃ sarva-duṣ-kṛta-nirdahanatayā | pātāla-bhūtaṃ sarva-a-kuśala-dharma-paryādāna-karaṇatayā || pe ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Maitreya-vimokṣa</s>, however, the purification of sin through <s>bodhicitta</s> is stated: [<s>bodhicitta</s> is] 'like the fire of the <s>kalpa</s>-conflagration, through its burning of all evil deeds; like the netherworld, through its capacity to completely absorb all unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>.' And so on in abbreviation.

body.text: tad yathā kula-putra hāṭaka-prabhāsaṃ nāma rasa-jātaṃ | tasya + ekaṃ palaṃ loha-pala-sahasraṃ suvarṇī-karoti | na ca tatra tat palaṃ śakyate tena loha-pala-sahasreṇa paryādātuṃ | na lohī-kartuṃ | evam eva + ekaḥ sarva-jñatā-citta-utpāda-rasa-dhātuḥ kuśala-mūla-pariṇāmanā-jñāna-saṃgṛhītaḥ sarva-karma-kleśa-āvaraṇa-lohāni paryādāya sarva-dharmān sarva-jñatā-varṇān karoti | na ca sarva-jñatā-citta-utpāda-rasa-dhātuḥ śakyaḥ sarva-karma-kleśa-lohaiḥ saṃkleśayituṃ paryādātuṃ vā | tad yathā kula-putra + ekaḥ pradīpo yādṛśe gṛhe vā layane vā praveśyate sa saha praveśito varṣa-sahasra-saṃcitam api tamo-ndha-kāraṃ vidhamayati | avabhāsaṃ ca karoti | evam eva + ekaḥ sarva-jñatā-citta-utpāda-pradīpo yādṛśe satva-āśaye gahane * a-vidyā-tamo-ndha-kāra-anugate praveśyate sa saha praveśito * an-abhilāpya-kalpa-śata-sahasra-saṃcitam api karma-kleśa-āvaraṇa-tamo-ndha-kāraṃ vidhamati | jñāna-ālokaṃ ca karoti ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as, O son of good family, there is a chemical substance called <s>hāṭakaprabhāsa</s> — one <s>pala</s> (measure) of it turns a thousand <s>palas</s> of iron into gold; and that [one] <s>pala</s> cannot be overcome by those thousand <s>palas</s> of iron, nor can it be turned into iron — just so, a single elixir-element of the generation of the mind of omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā-cittotpāda</s>), sustained by the knowledge of the dedication of wholesome roots, overcomes all the iron of obstructions due to <s>karma</s> and afflictions, and makes all <s>dharmas</s> into the color of omniscience. And that elixir-element of the generation of the mind of omniscience cannot be defiled or overcome by all the iron of <s>karma</s> and afflictions. Just as, O son of good family, a single lamp, in whatever house or cave it is brought, immediately upon being brought in, dispels even the darkness accumulated over a thousand years and produces illumination — just so, a single lamp of the generation of the mind of omniscience, in whatever thicket of a being's disposition, pervaded by the darkness of the blindness of ignorance, it is brought — immediately upon being brought in, it dispels even the darkness of the obstruction of <s>karma</s> and afflictions accumulated over unspeakably many hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, and produces the light of knowledge.'

body.text: tad yathā kula-putra cintā-maṇi-rāja-mukuṭānāṃ mahā-nāga-rājñāṃ na + asti para-upakrama-bhayaṃ | evam eva bodhi-citta-mahā-karuṇā-cintā-maṇi-rāja-mukuṭa-avabaddhānāṃ bodhi-satvānāṃ na + asti dur-gaty-apāya-para-upakrama-bhayam iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as, O son of good family, for the great <s>Nāga</s>-kings who wear the crest-jewel of the wish-fulfilling gem, there is no fear of hostile attack — just so, for <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are bound with the crest-jewel of the wish-fulfilling gem of <s>bodhicitta</s> and great compassion, there is no fear of the hostile attack of the lower destinies and evil paths.'

body.text: ārya-upāli-paripṛcchāyām apy uktaṃ | iha + upāle mahā-yānaṃ saṃprasthito bodhi-satvaḥ sacet pūrva-ahṇa-kāla-samaye āpattim āpadyeta | madhya-ahna-kāla-samaye sarva-jñatā-cittena + a-virahito vihared a-paryanta eva bodhi-satvasya śīla-skandhaḥ | sacen madhya-ahna-kāla-samaye āpattim āpadyate sāya-ahna-kāla-samaye sarva-jñatā-cittena + a-virahito bhaved a-paryanta eva bodhi-satvasya śīla-skandhaḥ | evaṃ yāme yāme vidhir uktaḥ | evaṃ hy upāle sa-parihārā śikṣā mahā-yāna-saṃprasthitānāṃ bodhi-satvānāṃ | tatra bodhi-satvena na + ati-kaukṛtya-paryutthānam utpādyaṃ na + ati-vipratisāriṇā bhavitavyaṃ | sacet punaḥ śrāvaka-yānīyaḥ pudgalaḥ punaḥ punar āpattim āpadyeta | naṣṭaḥ śrāvakasya pudgalasya śīla-skandho veditavyaḥ | iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Upāli-paripṛcchā</s> too it is said: 'Here, <s>Upāli</s>, if a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has set out in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> commits a transgression in the morning period, [and] in the midday period he dwells not separated from the mind of omniscience — the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s aggregate of moral conduct is still unlimited. If he commits a transgression in the midday period, [and] in the evening period he is not separated from the mind of omniscience — the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s aggregate of moral conduct is still unlimited.' Thus the rule is stated for each watch [of the day]. 'For thus, <s>Upāli</s>, the training of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have set out in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is one with remedy. Therein, the <s>bodhisattva</s> should not generate excessive remorse and agitation; he should not become excessively regretful. But if a person of the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle were to commit a transgression again and again — the aggregate of moral conduct of that <s>Śrāvaka</s> person should be known as destroyed.'

body.text: iti śikṣā-samuccaye pāpa-śodhanam aṣṭamaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the eighth chapter of the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>: the Purification of Sin.

body.text: kṣānti-pāramitā navamaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Kṣānti-pāramitā</s> (Perfection of Patience) — the ninth chapter.

body.text: tad evam a-virata-pravṛttāṃ bahu-sukhāṃ dauḥś-lya-utpattiṃ rakṣann evaṃ ca karma-āvaraṇa-vibandham apanayan kleśa-viśodhane prayateta ||
body.translated_text: Thus, while protecting [oneself] from the arising of immorality, which operates without cessation and which [would yield] much suffering — and while thus removing the bondage of the obstruction of <s>karma</s> — one should exert oneself in the purification of the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>).

body.text: tatra + adau tāvat kṣameta | a-kṣamasya hi śruta-ādau vīryaṃ pratihanyate * a-kheda-sahatvāt | a-śrutavāṃś ca na samādhy-upāyaṃ jānāti | na + api kleśa-śodhana-upāyam | tasmād a-khinnaḥ śrutam eṣeta | jñānato * api saṃkīrṇa-cāriṇaḥ samādhānaṃ duṣ-karam iti | saṃśrayeta vanaṃ tataḥ | tatra + api vikṣepa-praśamana-an-abhiyuktasya cittaṃ na samādhīyatae iti | samādhānāya yujyeta | samāhitasya ca na kiñ-cit phalam anyatra kleśa-śodhanād iti | bhāvayed a-śubha-ādikaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, first, one should be patient. For without patience, vigor in study and the like is obstructed, due to the inability to bear hardship. And one who has not studied does not know the method of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), nor the method of purifying the afflictions. Therefore, without weariness, one should seek learning. And for one of mixed conduct, even with knowledge, composure is difficult — therefore one should resort to the forest. Even there, without being devoted to the pacification of distraction, the mind is not composed — therefore one should apply oneself to composure. And for one who is composed, there is no fruit other than the purification of afflictions — therefore one should cultivate [meditations such as] the unlovely (<s>aśubha</s>) and the like.

body.text: ity etāni tāvat kleśa-śuddher uddeśa-padāni ||
body.translated_text: These, then, are the summary-topics of the purification of afflictions.

body.text: idānīṃ nirdeśa ucyate | tatra kṣāntis tri-vidhā dharma-saṃgīti-sūtre * abhihitā | duṣkha-adhivāsana-kṣāntiḥ | dharma-nidhyāna-kṣāntiḥ | para-apakāra-marṣaṇa-kṣāntiś ca + iti | tatra duṣkha-adhivāsana-kṣānti-vipakṣo * an-iṣṭa-āgama-prāpta-duṣkha-bhīrutā | iṣṭa-vighāta-prāptaś ca sukha-abhiṣvaṅgas tābhyāṃ daurmanasyaṃ | tato dveṣo līnatā ca ||
body.translated_text: Now the detailed exposition is stated. Therein, patience is threefold, as stated in the <s>Dharmasaṃgīti-sūtra</s>: the patience of enduring suffering (<s>duḥkhādhivāsana-kṣānti</s>); the patience of contemplating the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmanidhyāna-kṣānti</s>); and the patience of forbearing the harm of others (<s>parāpakāramarṣaṇa-kṣānti</s>). Therein, the opponent of the patience of enduring suffering is: the fearfulness regarding suffering that comes with the arrival of the undesirable; and the attachment to pleasure that comes with the obstruction of the desirable. From both of these [comes] despondency (<s>daurmanasya</s>); from that, hatred and torpor.

body.text: ata eva + āha candra-pradīpa-sūtre | sukhe * an-abhiṣvaṅgaḥ | duṣkhe * a-vaimukhyam iti ||
body.translated_text: For this very reason, it says in the <s>Candrapradīpa-sūtra</s>: 'Non-attachment to pleasure; non-aversion to suffering.'

body.text: ratna-megha-sūtre * apy uktaṃ | yae ime ādhyātmikāḥ śoka-parideva-duṣkha-daurmanasya-upāyāsās tān kṣamate * adhivāsayati + iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ratnamegha-sūtra</s> too it is said: 'He endures and bears those internal sorrows, lamentations, sufferings, despondencies, and distresses.'

body.text: ārya-ugradatta-paripṛcchāyām apy uktaṃ | punar a-paraṃ gṛha-pate gṛhiṇā bodhi-satvena + anunaya-pratighā-apagatena bhavitavyam aṣṭa-loka-dharma-an-anuliptena | tena bhoga-lābhena vā bhāryā-putra-lābhena vā dhana-dhānya-vitta-lābhena vā na + unnamitavyaṃ na praharṣitavyaṃ | sarva-vipattiṣu ca + anena na + avanamitavyaṃ | na dur-manasā bhavitavyaṃ evaṃ ca + anena pratyavekṣitavyaṃ | māyā-kṛtaṃ sarva-saṃskṛtaṃ viṭhapana-pratyupasthāna-lakṣaṇaṃ | karma-vipāka-nirvṛttā hy ete | yad idaṃ mātā-pitṛ-putra-bhāryā-dāsī-dāsa-karma-kara-pauruṣeya-mitra-amātya-jñāti-sālohitā | na + ete mama svakāḥ | na + aham eteṣām iti ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Ugradattaparipṛcchā</s> it is also said: "Furthermore, O householder, a householder <s>bodhisattva</s> should be free from favoritism and hostility, unstained by the eight worldly <s>dharmas</s>. He should not be elated or overjoyed by the gain of wealth, the gain of wife and sons, or the gain of riches, grain, and possessions. And in all misfortunes he should not be downcast; he should not become despondent. And he should reflect thus: 'All that is conditioned is like a magical creation, characterized by deception and semblance. For these — mother, father, sons, wife, female and male servants, workers, attendants, friends, ministers, relatives, and kinsmen — arise from the ripening of <s>karma</s>. They are not truly mine; I am not truly theirs.'"

body.text: api ca | yady asty eva pratīkāro daurmanasyena tatra kim | pratīkāre * api muhyeta dur-manāḥ krodha-mūrcchitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Moreover: "If there is indeed a remedy, what use is despondency in that case? Even [when there is a remedy], one who is despondent, stupefied by anger, would be confused about the remedy."

body.text: līnatvād vā hata-utsāho gṛhyate parayā + āpadā | tac-cintayā mudhā yānti hrasvam āyur muhur muhuḥ ||
body.translated_text: "Or, with a sunken spirit and destroyed enthusiasm, he is seized by an overwhelming calamity. Through fruitless worry over that, the brief span of life constantly passes away."

body.text: tena + abhyāsāt tyajed etaṃ nir-arthakam an-artha-vat ||
body.translated_text: "Therefore, through practice, one should abandon this [despondency] — worthless and harmful."

body.text: kathaṃ ca daurmanasya-tyāgo * abhyasyate | laghu-su-kumāra-citta-utsargāt ||
body.translated_text: And how is the abandonment of despondency to be practiced? Through the relinquishment of a light and tender-minded disposition.

body.text: yathā + uktam ugradatta-paripṛcchāyāṃ | apagata-tūla-picu-upamatā-cittasya + iti ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Ugradattaparipṛcchā</s>: "Of one whose mind has departed from the likeness of cotton-floss."

body.text: ārya-gaṇḍa-vyūhe * apy uktaṃ | dur-yodhanaṃ cittaṃ te dārike utpādayitavyaṃ sarva-kleśa-nirghātāya | a-parājita-cittaṃ sarva-abhiniveśa-vinirbhedāya | a-kṣobhya-cittaṃ viṣama-āśayatva-sāgara-āvarta-prayāteṣv iti ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Gaṇḍavyūha</s> it is also said: "You should generate, O maiden, an unconquerable mind for the destruction of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions); an undefeatable mind for the penetration of all attachments; an unshakable mind toward those who have gone into the whirlpool-ocean of perverse dispositions."

body.text: na ca + abhyāsasya duṣ-karaṃ nāma kiñ-cid asti | tathā hi mūḍhatarāṇām api tāvad bhāra-hāraka-kaivartaka-rṣaka-ādīnāṃ duṣkha-abhyāsāt kṣudratara-phale * api vastuni saṃrūḍha-kiṇa-aṅkitaṃ cittam avasādena na paribhūyate | kiṃ punaḥ sarva-saṃsāra-sukha-sarva-bodhi-satva-sukha-an-uttara-pada-samadhigama-phale karmaṇi | tathā prākṛtā api kiñ-cid apakāriṣv ātma-duṣkṛtena + eva hateṣu svayaṃ mṛtyuṣu prahartuṃ gāḍha-prahāra-vedanā api saṃgrāmayanty eva | ki.ṃ punar drāghiṣṭha-kāla-apakāriṣu duṣkha-upātta-kuśala-dhana-lava-stainyeṣu narakeṣu na + avadhya-ghātakeṣu bhava-cāraka-pālakeṣu niḥ-saraṇa-dvāra-dig-nāśakeṣv ānukūlye * api dṛḍhatara-vādhā-kareṣv an-apakṛta-vairiṣv an-avadhi-kalpa-ābaddha-dṛḍha-vaireṣu kleśa-śatruṣu prahartum utsāho duṣkha-sahanaṃ vā na bhavet | viśeṣatas tri-bhuvana-vijayayā baddha-parikarasya māra-śavara-pratigṛhīta-jagad-bandi-mokṣāya saṃgrāmayataḥ | tatra + ātma-duṣkha-abhyāsa-pūrvakaṃ kaṣṭaṃ kaṣṭatara-abhyāsaḥ sidhyati | yathā ca + abhyāsa-vaśāt satvānāṃ duṣkha-sukha-sa/mjñā | tathā sarva-duṣkha-utpādeṣu sukha-saṃjñā pratyupasthāna-abhyāsāt sukha-saṃjñā + eva pratyupatiṣṭhate | etan niṣyanda-phalaṃ ca sarva-dharma-sukha-ākrāntaṃ nāma samādhiṃ pratilabhate ||
body.translated_text: And there is nothing that is truly difficult for one who practices. For even the most deluded — such as porters, fishermen, ploughmen, and the like — through habitual endurance of suffering, even for a result that is trifling, their minds, bearing the marks of hardened calluses, are not overcome by despondency. How much more so in an endeavor whose fruit is the attainment of the supreme state — the happiness of all <s>saṃsāra</s> and the happiness of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>! Likewise, even ordinary worldly people, against those who have caused them some harm — who are themselves slain by their own misdeeds, who are themselves subject to death — they engage in battle, ready to strike, even enduring the pain of heavy blows. How much more should there be enthusiasm or endurance of suffering against the <s>kleśa</s>-enemies (affliction-enemies) who cause harm over the longest period, who steal even a morsel of the wealth of virtue acquired through suffering, who are slayers that cannot be slain, who are guardians and wardens of the prison of existence, who destroy the direction of the door of escape, who cause ever more severe harm even when treated favorably, who are enemies without having been harmed, whose enmity is firmly bound for limitless <s>kalpas</s> (aeons)! Especially for one who has girded his armor for the conquest of the three worlds, who is fighting for the liberation of the world's captives seized by the <s>Māra</s>-bandits! Therein, through prior habituation to one's own suffering, the habituation to harder and harder [sufferings] succeeds. And just as, through the power of habituation, the perception of suffering and happiness [changes] for sentient beings — so too, through the habituation of establishing the perception of happiness in all occasions of suffering, the perception of happiness alone arises. And as a natural outflow of this, one attains the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) called <s>Sarvadharmsukhākrānta</s> (Pervaded by the Happiness of All Dharmas).

body.text: uktaṃ hi pitā-putra-samāgame | asti bhagavan sarva-dharma-sukha-krānto nāma samādhiḥ | yasya samādheḥ pratilambhād bodhi-satvaḥ sarva-ārambaṇa-vastuṣu sukhām eva vedanāṃ vedayate | na + a-duṣkha-a-sukhāṃ | tasya nairayikām api kāraṇāṃ kāryamāṇasya sukha-saṃjñā + eva pratyupasthitā bhavati | mānuṣīm api kāraṇāṃ kāryamāṇasya hasteṣv api chidyamāneṣu pādeṣv api karṇeṣv api nāsāsv api sukha-saṃjñā + eva pratyupasthitā bhavati | vetrair api tāḍyamānasya + arddha-vetrair api kaśābhir api tāḍyamānasya sukha-saṃjñā + eva pravartate bandhana-āgāreṣv api praks.iptasya || pe ||
body.translated_text: For it is said in the <s>Pitāputrasamāgama</s> (Meeting of Father and Son): "There is, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, a <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvadharmasukhākrānta</s> (Pervaded by the Happiness of All Dharmas). By attaining this <s>samādhi</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> experiences only pleasant feelings in all objects and occasions — not feelings that are neither painful nor pleasant. Even when the torments of hell are being inflicted upon him, the perception of happiness alone is present. Even when human torments are being inflicted upon him — even when his hands are being cut off, even his feet, even his ears, even his nose — the perception of happiness alone is present. Even when he is being beaten with rods, with half-rods, with whips — the perception of happiness alone arises. Even when he is thrown into prison —" [abbreviated]

body.text: taila-pācikaṃ vā kriyamāṇasya | ikṣu-kuṭṭitavad vā kuṭṭhyamānasya | naḍa-cippitikaṃ vā cipyamānasya taila-pradyotikaṃ vā + ādīpyamānasya sarpiḥ-pradyotikaṃ vā dadhi-pradyotikaṃ vā + ādīpyamānasya sukha-saṃjñā + eva pratyupasthitā bhavati | ulkā-mukhaṃ vā hriyamāṇasya siṃha-mukhaṃ vā hriyamāṇasya śuṣka-varttikāṃ vā vartyamānasya || pe ||
body.translated_text: "Even when being boiled in oil; even when being crushed like sugarcane; even when being peeled like a reed; even when being set ablaze as an oil-lamp, or set ablaze as a ghee-lamp, or set ablaze as a curd-lamp — the perception of happiness alone is present. Even when being dragged by a torch-mouth; even when being dragged by a lion-mouth; even when being wound with a dry wick —" [abbreviated]

body.text: kārṣāpaṇa-cchedikaṃ vā chidyamānasya piṣṭa-pācanikaṃ vā pācyamānasya hastibhir vā mardyamānasya sukha-saṃjñā + eva pravartate | akṣiṇy--utpāṭhyamāne jīva-śūlikam api kriyamāṇasya sarvaśo vā + a-ghātaṃ nirṇīya śirasi vā prapātyamāne sukha-saṃjñā + eva pravartate | na duṣkha-saṃjñā | na + a-duṣkha-a-sukha-saṃjñā ||
body.translated_text: "Even when being cut as in the coin-cutting [punishment]; even when being cooked as in the flour-cooking [punishment]; even when being trampled by elephants — the perception of happiness alone arises. Even when his eyes are being torn out; even when the impaling-on-a-stake [punishment] is being carried out; even when being led out to complete execution or when his head is being struck off — the perception of happiness alone arises. Not the perception of suffering. Not the perception of neither-suffering-nor-happiness."

body.text: tat kasya hetoḥ | tathā hi bodhi-satvasya mahā-satvasya dīrgha-rātraṃ caryāṃ carata etat praṇidhānam abhūt | ye māṃ bhojayeran | te upaśama-śama-sukhasya lābhino bhaveyuḥ | ye māṃ pālayeyuḥ sat-kuryur guru-kuryur mānayeyuḥ pūjayeyuḥ sarve te upaśama-sukhasya lābhino bhaveyuḥ | ye * api mām ākrośeyur visparśeyus tāḍayeyuḥ śastreṇa + āchindyur yāvat sarvaśo jīvitād vyaparopayeyuḥ sarve te saṃbodhi-sukhasya lābhino bhaveyuḥ | an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyerann iti ||
body.translated_text: "For what reason? Because that <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, during his long career of practice, had this aspiration: 'May those who feed me obtain the happiness of tranquility and peace. May those who protect me, honor me, revere me, respect me, worship me — may they all obtain the happiness of tranquility. May those who revile me, abuse me, strike me, cut me with weapons, and even deprive me of life — may they all obtain the happiness of complete awakening. May they attain supreme perfect awakening.'"

body.text: sa ebhir manas-kāraiḥ samanvāgata etena karmaṇā | ebhiḥ praṇidhibhiḥ samanvāgataḥ sarva-satva-anugatāṃ sukha-saṃjñām āsevate nisevate bhāvayati bahulī-karoti | sa tasya karmaṇo vipākena sarva-dharma-sukha-ākrāntaṃ nāma samādhiṃ pratilabhate | yasmin samaye bodhi-satvena sarva-dharma-sukha-ākrānto nāma samādhiḥ pratilabdho bhavati tasmin samaye a-kṣobhyo bhavaty a-saṃhāryaḥ sarva-māra-karmabhir iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: "He, endowed with these mental attitudes, by this <s>karma</s>, endowed with these aspirations, cultivates, practices, develops, and makes abundant the perception of happiness that follows all sentient beings. By the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, he attains the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvadharmasukhākrānta</s>. At the time when the <s>bodhisattva</s> attains the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvadharmasukhākrānta</s>, he becomes unshakable, unassailable by all works of <s>Māra</s>" — and so on in detail.

body.text: ayaṃ hi prayogaḥ sarva-parityāga-pūraṇaḥ | sarva-caryā-duṣ-kara-caryā-sādhanaḥ sarva-kṣānti-dṛḍhī-karaṇaḥ sarva-vīrya-āsaṃsādanaḥ | sarva-dhyāna-prajñā-aṅga-saṃbhāraḥ | tasmān nitya-muditaḥ syāt ||
body.translated_text: For this practice fulfills complete relinquishment, accomplishes the difficult practice of all conducts, strengthens all forms of patience, makes all vigor unwavering, and gathers the equipment for all <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). Therefore one should be always joyful.

body.text: yathā + āha candra-pradīpa-sūtre | sa-gauravaḥ prīta-manāḥ sadā bhavet | saumyāya dṛṣṭīya sadā sthito bhaved | iti ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Candrapradīpa-sūtra</s>: "He should always be reverential and of delighted mind. He should always be established in a gentle gaze."

body.text: uktaṃ ca + akṣayamati-sūtre | tatra katamā muditā | yāvad dharma-anusmaraṇāt prītiḥ prasādaḥ prāmodyaṃ cittasya + an-avalīnatā + an-avamṛdyatā + a-paritarṣaṇā | sarva-kāma-ratīnām apakarṣaṇā sarva-dharma-ratīnāṃ pratiṣṭhānaṃ | cittasya prāmodyaṃ kāyasya + audbilyaṃ buddheḥ saṃpraharṣaṇaṃ manasa utplavaḥ | tathā-gata-kāya-abhinandana-ratir lakṣaṇa-anuvyañjana-vibhūṣaṇa-paryeṣṭi-kauśalyaṃ | kuśala-dharma-śravaṇa-a-parikhedatā | tatva-dharma-pratiśaraṇa-pratipatti-prīti-prasāda-pramodyaṃ muditasya dharma-utplavaḥ | satataṃ satveṣv a-pratihata-buddhitā | tīvra-cchandatā | buddha-dharma-paryeṣṭiṣu tasya ca dharma-cchandasya + an-utsṛjanatā | udāreṣu buddha-dharmeṣv adhimuktiḥ | vimuktiḥ prādeśika-yāna-apakṛṣṭa-citta-utpādaḥ | mātsarya-a-saṃkucitaś citta-utpādaḥ | yācitasya dātu-kāmatā | dadato dattvā ca tri-maṇḍala-pariśodhitaṃ dāna-prāmodyaṃ | śīlavatsu sadā prasādaḥ | duḥ-śīleṣv anugraha-prītiḥ | sva-śīla-pariśuddhyā sarva-dur-gandham atikrama-āśvāsanaṃ | tathā-gata-śīla-pariṇāmanatā | dṛḍha-a-bhedyatā | para-dur-ukta-dur-āgateṣu vacana-patheṣv a-pratihata-cittatā | kṣānti-sauratyaṃ | nir-mānatā | guruṣu gaurava-avanāmaś citrī-kāraḥ | sadā smita-mukhatā bhṛkuṭi-vigatatā | pūrva-abhilāpitā + a-kuhanatā + an-eṣyaiṣikatā śuddha-āśayatā citta-a-karkaśatā + a-kuṭilatā | sarvatra + anuśaṃsa-darśitā ātma-skhalita-pratyavekṣitā | āpattiṣv a-codanatā saṃrañjanīya-dharmeṣv anuvartanatā | śāstṛ-prema bodhi-satveṣu | ātma-prema dharmeṣu | jīvita-prema tathā-gateṣu | mātā-pitṛ-prema guruṣu | putra-prema satveṣu | buddha-prema ācārya-upādhyāyeṣu | uttama-aṅga-śiraḥ-prema pratipattiṣu | hasta-pāda-prema pāramitāsu | sarva-ratna-prema dharma-bhāṇakeṣu | sarva-rati-krīḍā-prema + anuśāsanīṣu | ārogya-prema saṃtuṣṭau | bhaiṣajya-prema dharma-paryeṣṭiṣu | vaidya-prema codaka-smārakeṣu | iti hi yā sarva-indriyeṣv an-avalīna-indriyatā iyam ucyate muditā + ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: And it is stated in the <s>Akṣayamati-sūtra</s>: "Therein, what is joy (<s>muditā</s>)? It extends to: delight arising from the recollection of the <s>Dharma</s>; faith; gladness; non-depression of mind; non-crushing of mind; non-parching. The withdrawal from all delights in sensual pleasures and the establishment in all delights in the <s>Dharma</s>. Gladness of mind; elation of body; delight of intelligence; buoyancy of mind. Delight and pleasure in the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; skill in the quest for adornment with the [major] marks and minor marks. Non-weariness in hearing wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Delight, faith, and gladness in the practice of taking refuge in the true <s>Dharma</s> — the joyous buoyancy of the joyful one. Constant unobstructed understanding toward sentient beings. Intense desire. In the quests for the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> — the non-relinquishment of that desire for the <s>Dharma</s>. Aspiration toward the lofty <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. Liberation — the generation of a mind that is drawn away from the lowly, partial vehicles. The generation of a mind not contracted by miserliness. The desire to give when asked. While giving and after having given — the gladness of giving purified in the three spheres. Constant faith in those endowed with moral conduct. Joyful beneficence toward those of poor moral conduct. The confidence, through the purity of one's own moral conduct, to overcome all bad odors. The dedication [of merit] toward the moral conduct of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Firm unbreakability. An unobstructed mind toward the verbal paths of others' harsh and hostile words. The gentleness of patience. Freedom from pride. Reverent bowing, esteem, and wonder toward teachers. Constant smiling face, free from frowning. Speaking first [in greeting]; non-deceit; non-selfish seeking; purity of aspiration; non-harshness of mind; non-crookedness. Showing the benefits everywhere. Examining one's own faults. Non-censure regarding transgressions. Conformity in <s>dharmas</s> that generate harmony. Love for the Teacher toward <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Love for oneself toward the <s>Dharma</s>. Love for life toward the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Love as for mother and father toward teachers. Love as for a son toward sentient beings. Love for the <s>Buddha</s> toward preceptors and instructors. Love as for the chief limb, the head, toward practices. Love as for hands and feet toward the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections). Love as for all jewels toward <s>Dharma</s>-preachers. Love as for all sport and play toward admonitions. Love as for health toward contentment. Love as for medicine toward the quests for the <s>Dharma</s>. Love as for a physician toward those who admonish and remind. Indeed, that non-sinking of all the faculties — this is called joy (<s>muditā</s>)" — and so forth.

body.text: atra ca śikṣitān bodhi-satvān idaṃ vacanam alaṃ-karoti yad uktam ārya-mahā-meghe | niraya-gati-citta-nitya-samādhāna-śīlāś ca niraya-gati-priyāś ca niraya-gati-pattana-vaṇijaś ca bhavanti | niraya-lolāś ca bhavanti niraya-lobha-matsariṇaś ca niraya-agni-citta-praguṇṇāḥ bhavanti + iti ||
body.translated_text: And here, for trained <s>bodhisattvas</s>, this statement is fitting, as declared in the noble <s>Mahāmegha</s> (Great Cloud): "They are those whose minds are constantly composed toward the destination of the hells, and who are fond of the destination of the hells, and who are merchants traveling to the port of the destination of the hells. They are eager for the hells, and they are covetous of the hells with the covetousness of the hells, and their minds are inclined toward the fire of the hells."

body.text: uktā duṣkha-adhivāsanā kṣāntiḥ ||
body.translated_text: The patience of enduring suffering has been stated.

body.text: ārya-sāgaramati-sūtre tu tri-vidhā + api kṣāntir uktā | iha sāgaramate bodhi-satvo mahā-satvaḥ sarva-jñatā-citta-utpāda-ratne | an-āryair duḥ-śīlaiḥ satvair mārair māra-kāyikābhir vā devatābhir māra-adhiṣṭhitair vā māra-dūtair vā viheṭhyamānaḥ samīryamāṇaḥ kṣobhyamānas tarjyamānas tāḍyamāno na bhidyate tato | adhyāśaya-citta-utpādo na bhidyate sarva-satva-pramokṣa-mahā-karuṇā-vīrya-ārambhāt | na bhidyate tri-ratna-vaṃśa-an-upaccheda-parākramāt | na bhidyate sarva-dharma-samudānayana-kuśala-prayogāt | na bhidyate lakṣaṇa-anuvyañjana-pariniṣpatti-gatāt puṇya-saṃbhāra-upacayāt | na bhidyate buddha-kṣetra-pariśuddhy-abhinirhāra-āhṛtād autsukyāt | na bhidyate sarva-dharma-a-parigraha-abhiyuktāt kāya-jīvita-utsargāt | na bhidyate sarva-satva-paripācana-abhiyuktād ātma-saukhya-an-adhyavasānāt | sa evam adhyāśaya-saṃpanna eva samānaḥ sarva-satvānām antikād ucca-ghanāṃ sahate | unmananāṃ kutsanāṃ sahate sarva-satvānām ākrośa-paribhāṣāṃ dur-ukta-dur-āgatān vacana-pathān sahate | sarva-satva-pīḍāṃ sahate | sarva-satva-bhārāṃś ca sahate uttārayati vā na ca khidyate | na ca līyate | na saṃlīyate | na viṣīdati | balam upadarśayati | sthāma saṃjanayati | vīryam ārabhate | parākramaṃ parākramate | utsāhaṃ janayati | unmūḍha-cittaṃ nigṛhṇāti | sa ākruṣṭo na pratyākrośati | tāḍito na pratitāḍayati | roṣito na pratiroṣayati | kruddhāya na pratikrudhyati | evaṃ citta-gaṇanā-saṃnāhaṃ saṃnahyati | ... sacet punar ete satvā yāvanto daśasu dikṣu prabhāvyamānāḥ prabhāvyante te sarve * asi-śakti-tomara-pāli-yogena māṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhato * anubadhnīyuḥ | yatra + eṣa pṛthivī-pradeśe sthito vā niṣaṇṇo vā caṅkramyamāṇo vā śayāno vā bodhi-cittam utpādayiṣyati dāna-cittaṃ vā yāvat prajñā-cittaṃ vā śruta-kuśala-mūla-cittaṃ vā + utpādayiṣyati tatra + asya pṛthivī-pradeśe śata-dhā-badarī-pattra-pramāṇaṃ kāyaṃ chetsyāmo vikariṣyāmo vidhvaṃsayiṣyāmas | te cet sarva-satvā mām ākrośayeyuḥ paribhāṣeran kutsayeyuḥ paṃsayeyur a-satyābhir vāgbhiḥ paruṣābhir vāgbhiḥ samuccareyur adhiṣṭhitā an-artha-karmāṇaḥ śata-dhā-badarī-pattra-pramāṇaṃ mama kāyaṃ chindhyur bhindyur vikareyur vidhvaṃsayeyuḥ | evaṃ mayā na kasya-cit satvasya + antike kṣobha-cittam utpādayitavyaṃ | tat kasya hetoḥ | pūrvā koṭiḥ saṃsārasya + a-pramāṇī-kṛtā yatra me * ayam ātma-bhāvo naraka-gatasya + api tiryag-yoni-gatasya + api yama-loka-gatasya + api manuṣya-gatasya + api kāma-āhāra-paliguddhasya dharmān a-śrutavato viṣama-ājīva-go-carasya nir-arthaka-jīvinaḥ aṅga-praty-aṅgasya śata-dhā chinno bhinno nikṛtto vividhābhiś ca kāraṇābhiḥ kārito na ca mayā tato nidānam ātma-arthaṃ kṛto na para-arthaḥ | sacet punar punar mama + ete sarva-satvā a-para-anta-koṭiṃ chindyur bhindyur vikireyur vidhvaṃsayeyus tathā + api mayā + a-parityaktā + eva sarva-jñatā | a-parityaktā eva sarva-satvāḥ | a-parityaktaḥ kuśalo charma-chandaḥ | tat kasya hetoḥ | sarvā hy eṣā kāya-pīḍā kāya-vivartanā | nairayikasya duṣkhasya śatatamīm api kalāṃ na + upaiti yāvad upaniṣadam api na kṣamate | naraka-āvāsam apy aham utsahe | na punar mayā buddha-dharmāḥ parityaktavyā na sarva-satva-ārambaṇā mahā-karuṇā || pe ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Sāgaramatisūtra</s>, all three kinds of patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) are stated: 'Here, O <s>Sāgaramati</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, with respect to the jewel of generating the thought of omniscience — when being harassed, disturbed, agitated, threatened, and struck by ignoble, immoral beings, by <s>Māras</s>, by deities belonging to <s>Māra</s>'s host, by those controlled by <s>Māra</s>, or by <s>Māra</s>'s emissaries — does not break from that [resolve]. His generation of the thought of high aspiration does not break, because of undertaking the vigor of great compassion for the liberation of all beings. He does not break, because of the exertion to maintain the uninterrupted lineage of the Three Jewels. He does not break, because of the skillful application of assembling all <s>dharmas</s>. He does not break, because of the accumulation of the collection of merit that leads to the perfection of the [thirty-two major] marks and the [eighty minor] signs. He does not break, because of the eagerness drawn from the determination to purify <s>Buddha</s>-fields. He does not break, because of the relinquishment of body and life, devoted to non-attachment to all <s>dharmas</s>. He does not break, because of the absence of attachment to personal happiness, devoted to the ripening of all beings. He, being thus endowed with high aspiration, endures harsh and abusive language from all beings; he endures contempt, censure, abuse, and reviling from all beings; he endures cruel and hostile verbal assaults; he endures the affliction of all beings; he bears and delivers the burdens of all beings and is not wearied, does not withdraw, does not shrink, does not despair. He displays strength, generates fortitude, undertakes vigor, exerts heroism, generates enthusiasm, and restrains a confused mind. When abused, he does not abuse in return. When struck, he does not strike back. When angered, he does not anger in return. He does not become angry at one who is angry. He dons the armor of mental reckoning thus: ... "And if all those beings who are being tormented in the ten directions were to pursue me from behind with swords, spears, javelins, and bludgeons — wherever on this spot of earth I stand, or sit, or walk, or lie down, I shall generate the thought of <s>bodhi</s>, or the thought of giving, up to the thought of wisdom, or the thought of wholesome roots through learning — and even there, on that spot of earth, they will cut my body into pieces the size of a hundred jujube leaves, tear it apart, and destroy it. Even if all those beings were to abuse me, revile me, censure me, disparage me, utter false and harsh words — influenced by agents of harm, they may cut, break, tear apart, and destroy my body into pieces the size of a hundred jujube leaves. Even so, I shall not generate a thought of agitation toward any being. For what reason? The beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s> is immeasurable, wherein this body of mine — even when in hell, even when in the animal realm, even when in <s>Yama</s>'s world, even when among humans — greedy for sensual food, not having heard the <s>Dharma</s>, living by wrong livelihood, living a purposeless life — has been cut limb by limb, broken into a hundred pieces, tortured by various punishments; and yet from all that, I accomplished nothing for myself, nor for the benefit of others. But if these beings were to cut, break, scatter, and destroy me endlessly, even so, I shall never abandon omniscience, never abandon all beings, never abandon the wholesome desire for the <s>Dharma</s>. For what reason? Because all this bodily affliction and bodily torment does not equal even a hundredth part of the suffering of hell, does not even approach it. I am able to endure even dwelling in hell — but the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities shall never be abandoned by me, nor shall the great compassion directed toward all beings."' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: yan nidānaṃ punar vyāpāda utpadyeta | taṃ vayaṃ dharmaṃ prahāsyāmaḥ | katamaś ca sa dharmo | yad uta kāya-prema kāya-niketaḥ kāya-adhyavasānaṃ | utsṛṣṭaś ca kāya utsṛṣṭo vyāpādaḥ | evaṃ dharma-gaṇanā-āviṣṭaḥ sāgaramate bodhi-satvaḥ sarva-satva-pīḍāṃ sahate || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'And furthermore, he reflects thus: "We shall abandon that <s>dharma</s> which is the cause from which ill-will arises. And what is that <s>dharma</s>? Namely: attachment to the body, abiding in the body, being absorbed in the body. When the body is relinquished, ill-will is relinquished." Thus, O <s>Sāgaramati</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s>, engaged in this reckoning of <s>dharmas</s>, endures the affliction from all beings.' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: yaḥ kāyasya + utsargaḥ kāya-parityāgaḥ kāya-an-avekṣā | iyam asya dāna-pāramitā ||
body.translated_text: 'His relinquishment of the body, his abandonment of the body, his non-regard for the body — this is his <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving).'

body.text: yat kāye chidyamāne sarva-satvān maitryā spharati | vedanābhiś ca na saṃhriyate | iyam asya śīla-pāramitā ||
body.translated_text: 'That when his body is being cut, he pervades all beings with loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), and is not overcome by painful sensations — this is his <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of morality).'

body.text: yat kāye chidyamāne ya eva + asya kāyaṃ chindati teṣām eva pramokṣa-arthaṃ kṣamate | na ca cittena kṣaṇyate kṣānti-balaṃ ca + upadarśayati + iyam asya kṣānti-pāramitā ||
body.translated_text: 'That when his body is being cut, he endures [it] for the very sake of liberating those who cut his body, and his mind is not shaken, and he displays the power of patience — this is his <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience).'

body.text: yena vīryeṇa taṃ sarva-jñatā-chandaṃ na + utsṛjati citta-bala-ādhīnaṃ ca pratigṛhṇāti | saṃsāram eva ca + anubadhnāti | kuśala-mūla-ārambham eva ca + ārabhate | iyam asya vīrya-pāramitā ||
body.translated_text: 'That vigor by which he does not abandon his desire for omniscience, and takes hold of the power of mind, and binds himself to <s>saṃsāra</s> itself, and undertakes the effort of [developing] wholesome roots — this is his <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor).'

body.text: yat kāye vikīryamāṇe tat sarva-jñatā-citta-utpāda-ratnaṃ kartuṃ na saṃmuhyati bodhim eva + apekṣate śānta-praśāntam eva pratyavekṣate | iyam asya dhyāna-pāramitā ||
body.translated_text: 'That when his body is being scattered, he does not become confused about producing that jewel of generating the thought of omniscience, and he looks only toward <s>bodhi</s>, and he reflects only on what is calm and tranquil — this is his <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation).'

body.text: yat kāye chidyamāne kāyasya tṛṇa-kāṣṭha-kuḍyavat-pratibhāsa-upamatāṃ pratyavekṣate māyā-dharmatāṃ ca kāyasya + avatarati | bhūta-a-nityatāṃ ca bhūta-duṣkhatāṃ ca bhūta-an-ātmatāṃ ca bhūta-śāntatāṃ ca kāyasya + upanidhyāyati | iyam asya prajñā-pāramitā + iti vistaraḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'That when his body is being cut, he reflects on the body's likeness to the appearance of grass, wood, and a wall, and he enters into the <s>māyā</s>-nature (illusory nature) of the body, and he contemplates the body's true impermanence, true suffering, true selflessness, and true peace — this is his <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom).' And so on in detail. [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: punar a-param asya + evaṃ bhavati | eṣa satvaḥ kusīdaḥ śukla-dharma-rahitaḥ | sa mām ākrośayati paribhāṣate | hanta vayam ārabdha-vīryā bhaviṣyāmaḥ | a-tṛptāḥ kuśala-mūla-paryeṣaṇa-abhiyuktā | eṣa eva tāvan mayā satvaḥ pūrvataraṃ bodhi-maṇḍe niṣādayitavyaḥ | paścān mayā + an-uttarā samyak-saṃbodhir abhisaṃboddhavyā + iti || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'And furthermore, he reflects thus: "This being is lazy, devoid of wholesome qualities. He abuses and reviles me. Come then, I shall be one of vigorous effort, unsatisfied, devoted to the quest for wholesome roots. This very being must first be established by me at the seat of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). Afterward, I shall attain supreme, perfect <s>bodhi</s>."' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: īdṛśānām asmābhiḥ satvānām a-dāntānām a-guptānām an-upaśāntānām arthāya saṃnāhāḥ saṃnaddhavyāḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: '"For the sake of such beings as these — untamed, unguarded, unquiet — armor must be donned by us."' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: hanta vayaṃ dharmatāṃ pratisariṣyāmaḥ | ko * atra + ākrośati vā ākruśyate vā | sa parigaveṣamāṇo na taṃ dharmam upalabhate | ya ākrośati vā ākruśyate vā | sa ātma-para-an-upalabdha-upalambha-dṛṣṭi-vigataḥ kṣamatae iti ||
body.translated_text: '"Come, we shall resort to the true nature of things (<s>dharmatā</s>). Who here abuses, and who is abused?" Searching thus, he does not apprehend that <s>dharma</s> which abuses or which is abused. He, freed from the view of apprehending self and other as unobtainable, endures [it all].'

body.text: bhagavatyām apy uktaṃ | evaṃ cittam utpādayati | yena mayā sarva-satvānāṃ vivāda utsārayitavyaḥ | so * ahaṃ svayam eva vivadāmi | lābhā me dur-labdhā yo * ahaṃ jalpite pratijalpāmi | yena mayā sarva-satvānāṃ saṃkrama-bhūtena bhavitavyaṃ so * ahaṃ parasya tvam ity api vācaṃ bhāṣe | paruṣaṃ vā prati-vāco dadāmi | idaṃ mayā na + eva vaktavyaṃ jaḍa-samena | eḍaka-mūka-samena mayā kalaha-vivādeṣu bhavitavyaṃ | parato dur-uktān dur-āgatān dur-bhāṣitān bhāṣyamāṇān vacana-pathān śṛṇvatā cittaṃ na + āghātayitavyaṃ | pareṣām antike na mama + etat sādhu na prati-rūpaṃ yo * ahaṃ parasya doṣa-antaraṃ saṃjanayeyam | etan na mama prati-rūpaṃ yad ahaṃ pareṣāṃ doṣa-antaram api saṃśrotavyaṃ manye | tat kasya hetoḥ | na mayā + āśayo vikopayitavyo yena mayā sarva-satvāḥ sarva-sukha-upadhānena sukhayitavyāḥ parinirvāpayitavyāś ca + an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhya tatra nāma + ahaṃ vyāpadye | na ca mayā pareṣāṃ sv-aparāddhānām api vyāpattavyaṃ | sa nāma + ahaṃ mohaṃ kṣobhaṃ gacchāmi | idaṃ tu mayā karaṇīyaṃ | dṛḍha-parākramatayā parākrāntavyaṃ | na mayā jīvita-antarāye * api kriyamāṇe kṣobhaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | na mayā bhṛkuṭī mukhe
body.translated_text: In the <s>Bhagavatī</s> (Prajñāpāramitā) also it is stated: 'He generates this thought: "I, who should dispel the quarrels of all beings — I myself am quarreling! Poorly have I gained who retort when spoken to! I, who should be a bridge for all beings — I utter even the word 'you' to another, or I give harsh replies! This should not at all be spoken by me, who should be like one who is dumb, like a mute sheep. In quarrels and disputes, I should remain so. When hearing cruel, hostile, abusive verbal assaults spoken by others, the mind should not be made resentful. It is not good or fitting for me to generate faults toward others. It is not fitting that I should think even others' faults worth hearing. For what reason? My intention should not be corrupted — I who should make all beings happy with every source of happiness and bring them to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, having attained supreme, perfect <s>bodhi</s> — that I should become malicious! And I should not bear ill-will even toward others who have offended me — that I should go to delusion and agitation! But this I should do: I should exert myself with firm heroism. Even when my life is being threatened, I should not be agitated. I should not produce a frown upon my face —"'

body.text: bodhi-satva-prātimokṣe * apy uktam | ye kruddhāḥ satvās tān āśvāsayati kṣamāpayati | anulomayati dharmeṇa toṣayati + iti ||
body.translated_text: It is also stated in the <s>Bodhisattvaprātimokṣa</s>: 'He consoles those beings who are angry, causes them to ask forgiveness, accommodates them, and satisfies them through the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: iti śikṣā-samuccaye kṣānti-pāramitā paricchedo navamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the ninth chapter of the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>: the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>).

body.text: vīrya-pāramitā daśamaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The perfection of vigor — the tenth chapter.

body.text: evaṃ kṣānti-pratisthitaḥ śrute vīryam ārabheta | anyathā śrutam eva + asya vināśāya saṃpadyate ||
body.translated_text: Thus, established in patience, one should undertake vigor in learning. Otherwise, learning itself turns to his destruction.

body.text: yathā + uktaṃ candra-pradīpa-sūtre | kiyad-bahū dharma-paryāyuṇeyā

children.text: śīlaṃ na rakṣeta śrute namanta | na bāhuśrutyena sa śakyu trāyituṃ duḥ-śīlayena vrajamāna dur-gatim ||
children.translated_text: '— he does not guard morality, while bowing to learning. He who is immoral, going to a lower rebirth, cannot be saved by great learning.'

body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Candrapradīpasūtra</s>: 'However many <s>Dharma</s>-discourses one may learn —'

body.text: śruta-anuśaṃsās tu nārāyaṇa-paripṛcchāyām uktāḥ | tathā hi kula-putrāḥ śrutavataḥ prajñā-āgamo bhavati | prajñāvataḥ kleśa-praśamo bhavati | niḥ-kleśasya māro * avatāraṃ na labhate ||
body.translated_text: But the benefits of learning are stated in the <s>Nārāyaṇaparipṛcchā</s>: 'For thus, O sons of good family, for one who possesses learning, there is the advent of wisdom. For one who possesses wisdom, there is the pacification of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). For one who is free from <s>kleśas</s>, <s>Māra</s> finds no entry.'

body.text: atra ca maha-rṣer uttarasya jātakaṃ vistareṇa kṛtvā + āha | dharma-kāmānāṃ hi | vi-mala-tejaḥ | bodhi-satvānāṃ mahā-satvānāṃ sa-gauravāṇāṃ sa-pratīśānāṃ anya-loka-dhātu-sthitā api buddhā bhagavanto mukham upadarśayanti dharmaṃ ca + anuśrāvayanti | dharma-kāmānāṃ | vi-mala-tejaḥ | bodhi-satvānāṃ mahā-satvānāṃ parvata-kandara-vṛkṣa-madhyeṣu dharma-nidhānāni nikṣiptāni | dharma-mukhāny an-antāni pustaka-gatāni kara-tala-gatāni bhavanti | dharma-kāmānāṃ vi-mala-tejaḥ bodhi-satvānāṃ pūrva-buddha-darśinyo devatā buddha-pratibhānam upasaṃharanti || pe ||
body.translated_text: And here, after relating in detail the <s>jātaka</s> (birth-story) of the great sage <s>Uttara</s>, [the sūtra] says: 'For <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s> who desire the <s>Dharma</s>, O <s>Vimalatejas</s> — who are reverent and respectful — <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, even those dwelling in other world-realms, show their faces and cause the <s>Dharma</s> to be heard. For <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s> who desire the <s>Dharma</s>, O <s>Vimalatejas</s> — in mountain caves and in the midst of trees, treasuries of the <s>Dharma</s> are deposited; infinite gateways to the <s>Dharma</s>, in written form, come into the palm of [their] hands. For <s>bodhisattvas</s> who desire the <s>Dharma</s>, O <s>Vimalatejas</s> — deities who have seen former <s>Buddhas</s> bring forth the eloquence of the <s>Buddha</s>.' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: parikṣīṇa-āyuṣkāṇāṃ buddhā bhagavanto devatāś ca + āyur-balaṃ ca + upasaṃharanti | buddha-adhiṣṭhānena devatā-adhiṣṭhānena ca kāṅkṣāmāṇā varṣa-sahasram avatiṣṭhante || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'For those whose lifespan has become exhausted, the blessed <s>Buddhas</s> and the deities bring the power of life. Through the empowerment of the <s>Buddha</s> and the empowerment of the deities, those who desire [to live longer] remain for a thousand years.' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: yāvat kalpaṃ vā kalpa-avaśeṣaṃ vā yāvad vā ākāṅkṣanti dharma-gaurava-jātānāṃ bodhi-satvānāṃ buddhā bhagavanto jarām apy apanayanti | vyādhīn apanayanti | smṛtim upasaṃharati | gatiṃ matiṃ pratibhānaṃ ca + upasaṃharanti || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'For as long as a <s>kalpa</s> or a remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>, or for as long as they wish — for <s>bodhisattvas</s> in whom reverence for the <s>Dharma</s> has arisen, the blessed <s>Buddhas</s> remove even old age, remove diseases, bring forth memory, and bring forth understanding, intellect, and eloquence.' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: dṛṣṭi-kṛtāni vinodayanti | samyag-dṛṣṭiṃ ca + upasaṃharanti | dharma-gauraveṇa | vi-mala-tejaḥ | bodhi-satvānāṃ mahā-satvānāṃ sarva-upakrama-bhayāni na bhavanti | tasmāt tarhi vi-mala-tejaḥ śruta-saṃbhāra-kauśalya-abhiyuktena bodhi-satvena bhavitavyam iti ||
body.translated_text: They dispel what has been done through [wrong] views, and they bring about right view. By reverence for the <s>Dharma</s>. O <s>Vimalatejas</s>, for <s>bodhisattvas</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s>, there are no fears from any attacks. Therefore, O <s>Vimalatejas</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> should be devoted to skill in the accumulation of learning.

body.text: kim ākāraṃ śrutaṃ bodhi-satva-vinaye praśastaṃ | yathā ārya-akṣayamati-sūtre * abhihitaṃ | aśīty-ākāra-praveśaṃ śrutaṃ | tad yathā | chanda-ākāram āśaya-ākāram adhyāśaya-ākāraṃ prayoga-ākāraṃ nirmāṇa-ākāram a-pramāṇa-ākāraṃ kalyāṇa-mitra-ākāraṃ gaurava-ākāraṃ pradakṣiṇa-ākāraṃ su-vacana-ākāraṃ paryupāsana-ākāram avahita-śrotra-ākāraṃ manas-kāra-ākāram a-vikṣepa-ākāram avasthāna-ākāraṃ ratna-saṃjñā-ākāraṃ bhaiṣajya-saṃjñā-ākāraṃ sarva-vyādhi-śamana-ākāraṃ smṛti-bhajana-ākāraṃ gati-bodhana-ākāraṃ mati-rocana-ākāraṃ buddhi-praveśa-āk āram a-tṛpta-buddha-dharma-śravaṇa-ākāraṃ tyāga-vṛṃhaṇa-ākāraṃ dānta-ājāneya-ākāraṃ bahu-śruta-sevanā-ākāraṃ satya-kṛtya-prīty-anubhavana-ākāraṃ kāya-audbilya-ākāraṃ citta-prahlādana-ākāram a-parikheda-śravaṇa-ākāraṃ dharma-śravaṇa-ākāraṃ pratipatti-śravaṇa-ākāraṃ para-deśanā-śravaṇa-ākāraṃ a-śruta-śravaṇa-ākāraṃ abhijñā-śravaṇa-ākāram anya-yāna-a-spṛhaṇā-śravaṇa-ākāraṃ prajñā-pāramitā-śravaṇa-ākāraṃ bodhi-satva-piṭaka-śravaṇa-ākāraṃ saṃgraha-vastu-śravaṇa-ākāram upāya-kauśalya-śravaṇa-ākāraṃ brahma-vihāra-śravaṇa-ākāraṃ smṛti-saṃprajanya-śravaṇa-ākāraṃ gaurava-ākāraṃ utpāda-kauśalya-śravaṇa-ākāram an-utpāda-kauśalya-śravaṇa-ākāram a-śubha-ākāraṃ maitryāḥ śravaṇa-ākāraṃ pratītya-samutpāda-ākāraṃ a-nitya-ākāraṃ duṣkha-ākāram an-ātmā-ākāraṃ śānta-ākāraṃ śūnyatā-nimitta-a-praṇihita-ākāraṃ an-abhisaṃs kāra-ākāraṃ kuśala-abhisaṃskāra-ākāraṃ satva-adhiṣṭhāna-ākāraṃ a-vipraṇāśa-ākāraṃ sva-adhīna-ākāraṃ sva-citta-ārakṣaṇa-ākāraṃ vīryasya + āśraṃsana-ākāraṃ dharma-nidhyapty-ākāraṃ kleśa-vipakṣa-ākāraṃ sva-pakṣa-parikarṣaṇa-ākāraṃ para-pakṣa-kleśa-nigraha-ākāraṃ sapta-dhana-samavaśaraṇa-ākāraṃ sarva-dāridrya-upacheda-ākāraṃ sarva-vidvat-praśasta-ākāraṃ paṇḍita-abhinandana-ākāraṃ ārya-saṃmata-ākāraṃ an-ārya-prasādana-ākāraṃ satya-darśana-ākāraṃ skandha-doṣa-vivarjana-ākāraṃ saṃskṛta-doṣa-paritulana-ākāram artha-pratiśaraṇa-ākāraṃ dharma-pratiśaraṇa-ākāraṃ sarva-pāpa-a-karaṇa-ākāraṃ ātma-para-hita-ākāraṃ su-kṛta-karma-an-anutapyana-ākāraṃ viśeṣa-gamana-ākāraṃ sarva-buddha-dharma-pratilābha-ākāram iti ||
body.translated_text: What form of learning is praised in the <s>bodhisattva</s> discipline? As stated in the <s>Ārya-Akṣayamati Sūtra</s>: 'Learning has eighty modes of entry. Namely: the mode of desire, the mode of intention, the mode of higher intention, the mode of effort, the mode of emanation, the mode of the immeasurable, the mode of spiritual friends, the mode of reverence, the mode of circumambulation, the mode of receptive speech, the mode of attendance, the mode of attentive hearing, the mode of mental attention, the mode of non-distraction, the mode of remaining [in the teaching], the mode of perceiving [Dharma] as a jewel, the mode of perceiving [it] as medicine, the mode of quelling all diseases, the mode of cultivating mindfulness, the mode of awakening to the course [of things], the mode of illuminating the intellect, the mode of entering into wisdom, the mode of insatiable hearing of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, the mode of strengthening generosity, the mode of a tamed thoroughbred, the mode of attending upon the learned, the mode of experiencing joy from truthful conduct, the mode of bodily elation, the mode of mental delight, the mode of unwearied hearing, the mode of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, the mode of hearing the practice, the mode of hearing others' teachings, the mode of hearing what has not been heard, the mode of hearing about higher knowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), the mode of hearing [about] non-aspiration for other vehicles, the mode of hearing the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>), the mode
