of hearing the <s>bodhisattva</s> collection, the mode of hearing the means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>), the mode of hearing skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>), the mode of hearing the divine abidings (<s>brahmavihāra</s>), the mode of hearing mindfulness and awareness (<s>smṛtisaṃprajanya</s>), the mode of reverence, the mode of hearing skill in arising, the mode of hearing skill in non-arising, the mode of the unpleasant (<s>aśubha</s>), the mode of hearing about loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), the mode of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), the mode of impermanence, the mode of suffering, the mode of non-self, the mode of peace, the mode of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (<s>śūnyatā-nimitta-apraṇihita</s>), the mode of non-fabrication, the mode of wholesome fabrication, the mode of the support of beings, the mode of non-loss, the mode of self-reliance, the mode of guarding one's own mind, the mode of relaxation of vigor, the mode of reflection on the <s>Dharma</s>, the mode of the antidote to the afflictions, the mode of cultivating one's own side, the mode of subduing the afflictions of the other's side, the mode of the convergence of the seven treasures, the mode of cutting off all poverty, the mode of being praised by all the learned, the mode of being celebrated by the wise, the mode of being approved by the noble, the mode of inspiring faith in the ignoble, the mode of seeing the truth, the mode of avoiding the faults of the aggregates, the mode of weighing the faults of the conditioned, the mode of relying on meaning, the mode of relying on the <s>Dharma</s>, the mode of non-commission of all sins, the mode of benefiting self and others, the mode of not regretting well-done actions, the mode of attaining distinction, the mode of attaining all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text: punar atra + eva + āha | yaś ca dharma-saṃbhāra-yogaḥ sa eva + asya jñāna-saṃbhāro bhavati | tatra katamo dharma-saṃbhāra-yogo yā + iyam alpa-arthatā + alpa-kṛtyatā + alpa-bhāṣatā + alpa-pariṣkāratā pūrva-rātra-a-para-rātraṃ jāgarikā-yogam anuyuktasya śruta-artha-paritulanatā | bhūyo bhūyaḥ paryeṣaṇatā | cittasya + an-āvilatā | nīvaraṇānāṃ viṣkambhanatā | āpattiṣu niḥ-śaraṇa-jñānaṃ | a-kaukṛtyatā | a-paryutthānatā | pratipatti-sāratā | dharma-nimnatā dharma-pravaṇatā dharma-prāg-bhāratā | parākrama-saṃpannatā ādīpta-śiraś-caila-upamatā jñāna-paryeṣṭyā | tan-maya-vihāritā | a-śithila-śīlatā + a-nikṣipta-dhuratā viśeṣa-gāmitā saṃgaṇikā-vivarjanam eka-ārāmatā + araṇya-abhimukha-manas-kāratā ārya-vaṃśa-santuṣṭiḥ dhuta-guṇeṣv a-calanatā dharma-ārāma-rati-ratatā laukika-mantra-a-smaraṇatā loka-uttara-dharma-paryeṣṭitā smṛty-a-pramoṣatā | artha-gaty-anugamatā | matyā mārga-anulomatā | dhṛtyā saṃvara-pratyayair jñāna-anugamaḥ | hrīr-apatrāpya-alaṃ-kāratā | jñāna-anugamana-sāratā | a-jñāna-vidhamanatā | a-vidyā-moha-tamas-timira-paṭala-paryavanaddhasya prajñā-cakṣur-viśuddhiḥ | su-viśuddha-buddhitā | buddhi-vistīrṇatā | a-saṃkucita-buddhitā prabhinna-buddhitā | praty-akṣa-buddhitā | a-para-adhīna-guṇatā | sva-guṇair a-manyanatā | para-guṇa-parikīrtanatā | su-kṛta-karma-kāritā | karma-vipāka-an-uddhuratā | karma-pariśuddhi-jñānam iti ||
body.translated_text: And further in this same [sūtra] it says: 'The practice of the <s>Dharma</s>-accumulation becomes his knowledge-accumulation. Therein, what is the practice of the <s>Dharma</s>-accumulation? It is having few wants, few tasks, few words, few requisites; being devoted to the practice of wakefulness in the first and last watches of the night; weighing the meaning of what has been heard; ever-renewed investigation; clarity of mind; suppression of the hindrances; knowledge of escape from transgressions; absence of remorse; absence of mental disturbance; essence being practice; inclining toward the <s>Dharma</s>, flowing toward the <s>Dharma</s>, tending toward the <s>Dharma</s>; endowed with exertion, likened to one whose head-turban is on fire in the quest for knowledge; dwelling immersed in that; non-lax morality, non-abandonment of the burden, going toward distinction; avoidance of groups, delight in solitude; mental inclination toward the forest; contentment in the noble lineage (<s>āryavaṃśa</s>); steadfastness in the ascetic virtues (<s>dhutaguṇa</s>); delighting in the garden of <s>Dharma</s>; not remembering worldly <s>mantras</s>; pursuit of supramundane <s>dharmas</s>; non-forgetfulness of mindfulness; following the course of meaning; conformity to the path through intellect; through resolution, following knowledge through the supports of restraint; adornment with moral shame and dread (<s>hrī-apatrāpya</s>); essence being the following of knowledge; destruction of ignorance; purification of the eye of wisdom for one enveloped by the thick veil of darkness of ignorance, delusion, and gloom; well-purified understanding; breadth of understanding; uncontracted understanding; penetrating understanding; direct understanding; not depending on others for qualities; not being conceited about one's own qualities; proclaiming the qualities of others; performing well-done actions; not being agitated by the ripening of <s>karma</s>; knowledge of the purification of <s>karma</s>.'

body.text: kiṃ śrotavyaṃ | uktaṃ bhagavatā jñāna-vaipulya-sūtre | sa-arthakāni śāstrāṇi śikṣitavyāni | apa-arthakāni parivarjayitavyāni | tad yathā | loka-āyata-śāstrāṇi daṇḍa-nīti-śāstrāṇi kārkheda-śāstrāṇi vāda-vidyā-śāstrāṇi kumāra-krīḍā-śāstrāṇi jambhaka-vidyā-śāstrāṇi || pe ||
body.translated_text: What should be studied? The <s>Bhagavān</s> has said in the <s>Jñānavaipulya Sūtra</s>: 'Treatises that have meaning should be studied. Those that lack meaning should be avoided. Namely: treatises on worldly philosophy (<s>lokāyata</s>), treatises on statecraft (<s>daṇḍanīti</s>), treatises on accounting (<s>kārkheda</s>), treatises on the art of debate (<s>vādavidyā</s>), treatises on children's games (<s>kumārakrīḍā</s>), treatises on the yawning-spell art (<s>jambhakavidyā</s>).' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: yāny api tad anyāni kāni-cin mokṣa-prati-kūlāni śāstrāṇi saṃmohāya saṃvartante tāni sarvāṇi bodhi-satva-yāna-saṃprasthitena parivarjayitavyāni + iti ||
body.translated_text: 'And whatever other treatises there may be that are contrary to liberation and conduce to delusion — all of these should be avoided by one who has set out on the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle.'

body.text: evaṃ śrutavatā cittaṃ śodhayitum araṇyam āśrayaṇīyaṃ | kathaṃ punar āśaya-saṃpannasya + apy ugradatta-paripṛcchāyāṃ gṛham anujñātaṃ | yatnavato * apy a-sāmarthyāt | para-dāra-ādiṣv api tarhi na + āpattiḥ syāt | na teṣām a-sāmarthye * api prakṛti-duṣṭatvād gṛha-āvāsasya ca prajñapti-sa-avadyatvād iti ||
body.translated_text: Thus, one who has [the requisite] learning should resort to the forest to purify the mind. But how is it that in the <s>Ugradattaparipṛcchā</s>, the household life is permitted even for one endowed with [proper] intention? [Answer:] Because of incapacity, even when one makes effort. But then there would be no transgression even regarding the wives of others [for the same reason of incapacity]? No — because [those acts] are inherently corrupt, and because the household life is blameworthy by convention.

body.text: iti śikṣā-samuccaye vīrya-pāramitā paricchedo daśamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>, the tenth chapter on the Perfection of Vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>).

body.text: araṇya-saṃvarṇanaṃ nāma + ekādaśaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The eleventh chapter, called the Praise of the Forest (<s>araṇyasaṃvarṇana</s>).

body.text: tad evam ugradatta-paripṛcchā-vidhinā gṛha-doṣān bhāvayitvā śrutavatā cittaṃ śodhayitum araṇyam āśrayaṇīyam iti sthitaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Thus, having contemplated the faults of the household life in the manner of the <s>Ugradattaparipṛcchā</s>, it is established that one who has learning should resort to the forest to purify the mind.

body.text: tathā ca + uktaṃ candra-pradīpa-sūtre | na jātu kāmān pratiṣevamāṇaḥ putreṣu dāreṣu janitva tṛṣṇāṃ | gṛhaṃ ca sevitva jugupsanīyam an-uttarāṃ prāpsyati so * agra-bodhim ||
body.translated_text: And thus it is said in the <s>Candrapradīpa Sūtra</s>: 'One who continually indulges in pleasures, having generated craving for sons and wives, and frequents the repulsive household — he will never attain unsurpassed, supreme awakening.'

body.text: ye kāma varjenti yathā + agni-karṣūṃ putreṣu dāreṣu janitva tṛṣṇāṃ | uttasta gehād abhiniṣkramanti na dur-labhā teṣv iyam agra-bodhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Those who abandon pleasures as [one avoids] a pit of fire, having [overcome] craving for sons and wives, who rise up and go forth from the house — for them this supreme awakening is not difficult to attain.'

body.text: na kaś-ci buddhaḥ purimeṇa āsīd an-āgato bheṣyati yo * avatiṣṭhate | yehi sthitair eva agāra-madhye prāptā iyaṃ uttama agra-bodhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'There has never been any <s>Buddha</s> in the past, nor will there be in the future, nor is there one now abiding, who, while remaining within the household, has attained this supreme, unsurpassed awakening.'

body.text: prahāya rājyaṃ yatha kheṭa-piṇḍaṃ vased araṇyeṣu viveka-kāmaḥ | kleśān prahāya vinihatya mānaṃ budhyanti bodhiṃ vi-rajām a-saṃskṛtām || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'Having abandoned kingship like a lump of spittle, one who dwells in forests desiring seclusion, having abandoned the afflictions and crushed pride — they awaken to <s>bodhi</s>, stainless and unconditioned.' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: annehi pānehi ca cīvarehi puṣpehi gandhehi vilepanehi | na + upasthitā bhonti nara-uttamā jinā yatha pravrajitvā caramāṇa-dharmān ||
body.translated_text: 'Not with foods and drinks and robes, with flowers, fragrances, and ointments, have the supreme among men, the <s>Jinas</s>, been attended — rather, having gone forth, they practice the <s>dharmas</s> of the wanderer.'

body.text: yaś ca + eva bodhiṃ pratikāṅkṣamāṇaḥ satva-artha nirviṇṇa ku-saṃskṛtātaḥ | araṇya-abhimukha sapta padāni gacched ayaṃ tataḥ puṇya-viśiṣṭa bhoti ||
body.translated_text: 'And one who aspires to <s>bodhi</s>, for the benefit of beings, disgusted with the corrupt conditioned [world], who takes even seven steps toward the forest — that one thereby becomes distinguished in merit.'

body.text: yadi punar visabhāga-satva-anunayāt pariṣat-kāmatayā vā lābha-ādi-kāmatayā vā viveka-praveśe vilambeta | tad-artham atra + eva + uktaṃ | na vijña bālehi karonti vigrahaṃ sat-kṛtya bālān parivarjayanti | mama + antike ca + iti praduṣṭa-cittā na bāla-dharmehi karonti saṃstavam ||
body.translated_text: But if, through attachment to beings of dissimilar disposition, or through desire for assemblies, or through desire for gain and the like, one delays in entering seclusion — for that purpose it is said in this very [sūtra]: 'The wise do not quarrel with fools; having honored fools, they avoid them. And [thinking,] "Those of corrupted minds are near me" — they do not praise the ways of fools.'

body.text: na vijña bālāna karoti sevanāṃ viditva bālāna sva-bhāva-saṃtatim | kiyac-ciraṃ bāla-su-sevitā pi puno * api te bhonti a-mitra-sannibhāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'The wise do not attend upon fools, having known the nature and continuity of fools; even those long served by fools again become like enemies.'

body.text: na vijña bāleṣv iha viśvasanti vijñāya bālāna sva-bhāva-saṃtatim | sva-bhāva-bhinnā prakṛtīya bālāḥ kuto * asti mitraṃ hi pṛthag-janānāṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'The wise do not trust fools here, having understood the nature and continuity of fools; fools are by nature different, of base disposition — whence would there be friendship among ordinary persons?'

body.text: saha-dhārmikeno vacanena uktāḥ krodhaṃ ca doṣaṃ ca a-pratyayaṃ ca | prāviṣkaronti imi bāla-dharmā imam artha vijñāya na viśvasanti ||
body.translated_text: 'When addressed with a word in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, they manifest anger, fault-finding, and disbelief — these are the ways of fools; understanding this meaning, [the wise] do not trust them.'

body.text: bālā hi bālehi samaṃ samenti yathā a-medhyena a-medhya sārddham | vijñaḥ punar vijña-janena sārddhaṃ samenti sarpir yatha sarpi-maṇḍe ||
body.translated_text: 'For fools associate with fools, just as filth [mixes] with filth; but the wise [associate] with the wise, just as clarified butter [blends] with the cream of clarified butter.'

body.text: tathā ca punar atra + evam āha | sū-sukhitāḥ sada te nara-loke yeṣu priya-a-priya na + asti kahiṃ-cit | ye ca na kandarake * abhiramante śrāmaṇakaṃ su-sukhaṃ anubhonti ||
body.translated_text: And further, in this same [sūtra] it says: 'Very happy always are they in the world of men, for whom there is nothing dear or unpleasant anywhere, who do not delight in discord — they experience the supreme happiness of the ascetic life.'

body.text: yeṣu mama + api tu na + asti kahiṃ-cit | yeṣu parigrahu sarvaśu na + asti | khaḍga-samā vicaranti mu lokaṃ gagane pavana yathā + iva vrajanti ||
body.translated_text: 'Those for whom there is nothing of "mine" anywhere, who have no possessions whatsoever, who wander in the world like rhinoceroses, who go like the wind in the sky.'

body.text: syuḥ sukhitā vata te nara-loke yeṣu na sajjati mānasa loke | vāyu-samaṃ sada teṣv iha cittaṃ na + u ca priya-a-priya vidyati saṃgo ||
body.translated_text: 'Happy indeed are they in the world of men, for whom the mind is not attached to the world, whose mind is always like the wind herein — for them there is no attachment to the dear or unpleasant.'

body.text: a-priya ye dukhitehi nivāso ye * api priyā dukhitehi viyogo | anta ubhe api tehi jahitvā te sukhitā naraye rata dharme ||
body.translated_text: 'Those for whom dwelling with the unpleasant is suffering, and separation from the dear is also suffering — having abandoned both extremes, they are happy, delighting in the <s>Dharma</s>, the noble ones.'

body.text: punar atra + eva + uktam | bhavati satatam alpa-kṛtya-yogī pṛthu guṇa doṣata sarvi varjayitvā | na vivadati kadā-ci yukta-yogī imi guṇa tasya bhavanty araṇya-vāse ||
body.translated_text: And further, in this same [sūtra] it is said: 'He is always devoted to having few tasks, having abandoned all faults from wide [entanglements]; he never quarrels, being devoted to practice — these are the virtues of forest-dwelling.'

body.text: sada bhavati niviṇṇa saṃskṛte * asau na bhavati tasya pṛhā kahiṃ-ci loke | na ca bhavati vivṛddhir āsravāṇāṃ vana-vasato * asya bhavanti ānuśaṃsāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'He is always disenchanted with the conditioned; he has no craving anywhere in the world; and the increase of the outflows (<s>āsrava</s>) does not occur — these are the benefits of dwelling in the forest.'

body.text: adhikaraṇa na tasya jātu bhotī sada upaśānta-rato viveka-cārī | vacaci manasi kāya saṃvṛta-syo bahu-guṇa tasya bhavanty araṇya-vāse ||
body.translated_text: 'Disputes never arise for him; always delighting in peace, practicing seclusion; restrained in speech, mind, and body — many are the virtues of his forest-dwelling.'

body.text: bhavati anukūla tasya mokṣo laghu pratividhyati so * adhimukti śāntām | vani-cari dhimukti sevate * asya imi guṇa bhonty araṇya-vāsi sarve ||
body.translated_text: 'Liberation becomes favorable for him; swiftly he penetrates the peaceful conviction; practicing in the forest, his conviction is cultivated — all these virtues belong to the forest-dweller.'

body.text: punar āha | vana-ṣaṇḍa sevatha vivikta sadā vijahitva grāma-nagareṣu ratim | a-dvitīya-khaḍga-sama bhotha sadā na cireṇa lapsyatha samādhi-varam | iti ||
body.translated_text: And further it says: 'Frequent the forest groves, always secluded, having abandoned delight in villages and cities; be always solitary like the rhinoceros — before long you will attain the supreme <s>samādhi</s>.'

body.text: ārya-rāṣṭrapāla-sūtre * apy āha | tyaktvā geham an-anta-doṣa-gahanaṃ cintā-an-apekṣāḥ sadā | te * araṇye ratim āpnuvanti guṇinaḥ śānta-indriyāḥ sūratāḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Rāṣṭrapāla Sūtra</s> it also says: 'Having abandoned the household, a thicket of endless faults, always free from anxiety and care, those virtuous ones, with senses pacified and resolute, find delight in the forest.'

body.text: na strī-saṃbhava na + eva ca + api puruṣais teṣāṃ kva-cid vidyate | ekākī viharanti khaḍga-sadṛśāḥ śuddha-āśayā nir-malāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Among them there is nothing born of woman, nor even anything [associated] with men anywhere; they dwell alone like rhinoceroses, of pure intent, stainless.'

body.text: lābhair na + api ca teṣu harṣa sva-mano līyanty a-lābhair na ca | alpa-icchā itara-itarair abhiratā māyā-kuhā-varjitāḥ | ti ||
body.translated_text: They are not elated by gains, nor do their minds cling to them; they are not [dismayed] by non-gains; they are of few desires, delighting in one thing after another, free from deceit and guile.

body.text: ugradatta-paripṛcchāyām apy āha | satva-saṃsargo me na kartavyo na hi mayā + eka-satvasya kuśala-mūlāni saṃjanayitavyāni + ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ugradattaparipṛcchā</s> also it is said: "I should not engage in association with beings; for it is not for me to generate the <s>kuśalamūla</s> (wholesome roots) of a single being" — and so forth.

body.text: yadi punaḥ śrutavān imāṃ kṣaṇa-saṃpadam āsādya lābha-ādau saktaḥ cittaṃ na śodhayet sa eva + ekaḥ | sa-devake loke vañcitaḥ syād ||
body.translated_text: But if one who has heard [the teaching], having obtained this opportunity of a moment, remains attached to gain and the rest and does not purify the mind, he alone would be the one deceived in the world with its <s>devas</s> (gods).

body.text: uktaṃ hy ārya-ratna-kūṭe | tad yathā kāśyapa kaś-cid eva puruṣo mahatā udaka-arṇavena + uhyamāna udaka-tṛṣṇayā kālaṃ kuryād | evam eva kāśyapa iha + eke śramaṇa-brāhmaṇā bahūn dharmān udgṛhya paryavāpya na rāga-tṛṣṇāṃ vinodayanti | na dveṣa-tṛṣṇāṃ | na moha-tṛṣṇāṃ vinodayanti | te mahatā dharma-arṇavena + uhyamānāḥ kleśa-tṛṣṇayā kāla-gatā | dur-gati-vinipāta-gāmino bhavanti + iti ||
body.translated_text: For it is said in the <s>Ārya-Ratnakūṭa</s>: "Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a certain man, being carried along by a great flood of water, might die of thirst for water — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, here some <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (brahmins), having learned and mastered many <s>dharmas</s> (teachings), do not dispel the thirst of <s>rāga</s> (passion), do not dispel the thirst of <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred), do not dispel the thirst of <s>moha</s> (delusion). Being carried along by the great flood of <s>dharma</s>, they die of the thirst of <s>kleśa</s> (affliction) and go to unfortunate destinies and downfall."

body.text: tasmād a-vaśyam araṇyam āśrayet ||
body.translated_text: Therefore one must necessarily resort to the <s>araṇya</s> (forest/wilderness).

body.text: tādṛśāni ca sthānāni āśrayet | yeṣu ca sthāneṣu na + ati-dūre piṇḍa-pāta-go-caro bhavati na + ati-saṃnikṛṣṭe | yeṣu pānīyāni bhavanty acchāni śucīni nir-malāny alpa-āyāsāni mukha-paribhogāni yāni ca sthānāni vṛkṣa-saṃpannāni bhavanti puṣpa-saṃpannāni phala-saṃpannāni pattra-saṃpannāny apagata-duṣṭa-śvā-padāni guhā-saṃpannāni prāg-bhāra-saṃpannāni sukha-parisarpyakāṇi śāntāny a-dvitīyāni tādṛśāni sthānāny āśrayet | sa teṣu sthāneṣv āśrito yad anena pūrva-paṭhitaṃ bhavati tat tribhī rātrais trir-divasasya sva-adhyāyati na + aty-uccena svareṇa na + ati-nīcena na + uddhatair indriyair na bahir-gatena cittena prasādam upajīvan grantham upadhārayan nimittāny udgṛhṇan middham apakrāman | saced āraṇyakasya bhikṣo rājā vā + upasaṃkrāmati rāja-mātro vā + anye vā brāhmaṇa-kṣatriya-naigama-jānapadāḥ | tena teṣām ādareṇa sv-āgata-kriyā kartavyā | evaṃ ca + anena vaktavyaṃ | niṣīda mahā-rāja yathā prajñaptae āsane | saced upaviśati dvābhyām apy upaveṣṭavyaṃ | sacen na + upaviśati ubhābhyām api na + upaveṣṭavyaṃ | sacec cañcala-indriyo bhavati utkarṣayitavyaṃ | tasya te mahā-rāja lābhāḥ su-labdhā yasya te bhū-pradeśe śīlavanto guṇavanto bahu-śrutāḥ śramaṇa-brāhmaṇāḥ prativasanti | an-upadrutāś caura-bhaṭa-ādibhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: And one should resort to such places where the alms-round is neither too far nor too close; where the water is clear, pure, spotless, easily obtainable, and fit for drinking; where the places are endowed with trees, endowed with flowers, endowed with fruits, endowed with leaves, free from dangerous wild animals, endowed with caves, endowed with sheltering overhangs, easy to walk about in, peaceful, and solitary — one should resort to such places. Dwelling in those places, whatever he has previously studied, he should recite three times during the three watches of the day — not with too loud a voice, not with too low a voice, not with agitated senses, not with a mind directed outward, cultivating serenity, grasping the meaning of the text, apprehending the key points, and warding off drowsiness. If a king approaches the forest-dwelling <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), or a person of royal rank, or other <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, townspeople, or country-folk, he should respectfully offer them a welcome. And he should say thus: "Be seated, great king, upon the prepared seat." If he sits down, both should sit. If he does not sit, neither should sit. If he is of restless senses, he should be uplifted [with teachings]. "It is a gain well-gained for you, great king, that in your territory virtuous, meritorious, and learned <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> dwell, untroubled by thieves, soldiers, and the like."

body.text: sacet sthiro bhavati vinītaḥ praśānta-indriyaḥ bhavyaś ca bhavati dharma-deśanāyāḥ tato * asya vicitrā dharma-deśanā upasaṃhartavyā | saced vicitrāṃ na priyāyate | saṃvega-anukūlā dharma-deśanā upasaṃhartavyā | sacet saṃvega-anukūlāṃ na priyāyate udāra-udārāṇi tathā-gata-māhātmyāni upadeṣṭavyāni | brāhmaṇa-kṣatriya-naigama-jānapadānām apy upasaṃkrāmatāṃ yathā-anurūpāḥ kriyā upasaṃhartavyā | sa evaṃ bahu-śrutaḥ san prati-balo bhavati dhārma-śravaṇikānāṃ cittam ārādhayituṃ | te ca satvās tasya + antike prītiṃ ca prasādaṃ ca prāmodyaṃ ca pratilabhantae iti ||
body.translated_text: If he is steadfast, disciplined, with tranquil senses, and receptive to the teaching of <s>Dharma</s>, then a varied teaching of <s>Dharma</s> should be offered to him. If he does not delight in a varied [teaching], a teaching of <s>Dharma</s> conducive to <s>saṃvega</s> (spiritual urgency) should be offered. If he does not delight in one conducive to <s>saṃvega</s>, the sublime and exalted glories of the <s>Tathāgata</s> should be taught to him. For <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, townspeople, and country-folk who approach, appropriate conduct should be employed [according to their nature]. Being thus learned, he becomes capable of gladdening the minds of those who come to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. And those beings attain joy, serenity, and gladness in his presence.

body.text: ugradatta-paripṛcchāyām apy āha | punar a-paraṃ gṛha-pate pravrajitena bodhi-satvena + araṇye prativasatā evam upaparīkṣitavyaṃ | kim artham aham araṇye prativasāmi | na kevalam araṇya-vāsena śramaṇo bhavati | bahavo * apy atra + a-dāntā a-vinītā a-yuktā an-abhiyuktāḥ prativasanti | tad yathā | mṛga-vānara-pakṣi-saṃgha-caura-caṇḍālāḥ prativasanti | na ca te śramaṇa-guṇa-samanvāgatā bhavanti | api tu khalu punar ahaṃ yasya + arthāya + araṇye prativasāmi sa mayā + arthaḥ paripūrayitavyo yad uta śrāmaṇya-arthaḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ugradattaparipṛcchā</s> also it is said: "Furthermore, householder, a renunciant <s>bodhisattva</s> dwelling in the <s>araṇya</s> (wilderness) should reflect thus: 'For what purpose do I dwell in the wilderness? One does not become a <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic) merely by dwelling in the wilderness. Many who are untamed, undisciplined, unyoked, and not diligent also dwell here — such as herds of deer, monkeys, flocks of birds, bandits, and outcasts — and they are not endowed with the qualities of a <s>śramaṇa</s>. Rather, the purpose for which I dwell in the wilderness must be fulfilled by me, namely the purpose of the ascetic life.'" And so forth.

body.text: punar a-paraṃ gṛha-pate pravrajitena bodhi-satvena + araṇye viharatā evam upaparīkṣitavyaṃ | kim artham aham araṇym āgataḥ | tena + evaṃ mīmāṃsayitavyaṃ | bhaya-bhīto * asmy aham araṇyam āgataḥ | kuto bhaya-bhītaḥ | saṃgaṇikā-bhaya-bhītaḥ | saṃsarga-bhaya-bhīto rāga-dveṣa-moha-bhaya-bhīto māna-mada-mrakṣa-paridāha-bhaya-bhīto lobha-īrṣyā-mātsarya-bhaya-bhītaḥ rūpa-śabda-gandha-rasa-sparṣṭavya-bhaya-bhītaḥ | so * ahaṃ-kāra-mama-kāra-bhaya-bhītaḥ | auddhatya-vicikitsā-bhaya-bhītaḥ | skandha-māra-bhaya-bhītaḥ | kleśa-māra-bhaya-bhīto | mṛtyu-māra-bhaya-bhīto | deva-putra-māra-bhaya-bhītaḥ | a-nitye nitya iti viparyāsa-bhaya-bhīto * an-ātmany ātmā + iti viparyāsa-bhaya-bhīto * a-śucau śucir iti viparyāsa-bhaya-bhīto | duṣkhe sukham iti viparyāsa-bhaya-bhītaḥ | citta-mano-vijñāna-bhaya-bhīto | nivaraṇa-āvaraṇa-paryutthāna-bhaya-bhītaḥ | sat-kāya-dṛṣṭi-bhaya-bhītaḥ pāpa-mitra-bhaya-bhīto | lābha-sat-kāra-bhaya-bhīto * a-kāla-mantra-bhaya-bhīto * a-dṛṣṭe dṛṣṭam iti bhaya-bhīto * a-śrute śrutam iti bhaya-bhīto * a-mate matam iti bhaya-bhīto * a-vijñāte vijñātam iti bhaya-bhīto * a-śramaṇe śramaṇa-mada-bhaya-bhīto * anyo-nya-vidveṣaṇa-bhaya-bhītaḥ kāma-dhātu-rūpa-dhātv-a-rūpya-dhātu-bhaya-bhītaḥ sarva-bhava-gaty-upapatti-bhaya-bhīto niraya-tiryag-yoni-pitṛ-viṣaya-bhaya-bhītaḥ saṃkṣepeṇa sarvebhyo * a-kuśalebhyo manasi-kārebhyo bhaya-bhī ta ebhyo hy aham evaṃ-rūpebhyo bhaya-bhairavebhyo bhīto * araṇya-āvāsam upagataḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: "Furthermore, householder, a renunciant <s>bodhisattva</s> dwelling in the <s>araṇya</s> (wilderness) should reflect thus: 'For what purpose have I come to the wilderness?' He should investigate thus: 'I have come to the wilderness frightened by fear. Frightened by what fear? Frightened by fear of social gatherings, frightened by fear of association, frightened by fear of <s>rāga</s> (passion), <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred), and <s>moha</s> (delusion), frightened by fear of pride, intoxication, resentment, and inner torment, frightened by fear of greed, envy, and jealousy, frightened by fear of forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangibles, frightened by fear of the conceits "I" and "mine," frightened by fear of restlessness and doubt, frightened by fear of the <s>Māra</s> of the aggregates, frightened by fear of the <s>Māra</s> of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), frightened by fear of the <s>Māra</s> of death, frightened by fear of the <s>Māra</s> who is a <s>devaputra</s> (son of a god), frightened by fear of the perversion of seeing permanence in the impermanent, frightened by fear of the perversion of seeing a self in what is without self, frightened by fear of the perversion of seeing purity in the impure, frightened by fear of the perversion of seeing happiness in what is suffering, frightened by fear of mind, thought, and consciousness, frightened by fear of hindrances, obstructions, and latent afflictions, frightened by fear of the view of a personal self, frightened by fear of evil companions, frightened by fear of gain and honour, frightened by fear of untimely death, frightened by fear of [claiming] "I have seen" what has not been seen, frightened by fear of [claiming] "I have heard" what has not been heard, frightened by fear of [claiming] "I have thought" what has not been thought, frightened by fear of [claiming] "I have known" what has not been known, frightened by fear of the pride of being an ascetic when one is not an ascetic, frightened by fear of mutual hostility, frightened by fear of the desire realm, form realm, and formless realm, frightened by fear of all states of existence, destinies, and rebirths, frightened by fear of the hells, animal realm, and realm of the departed — in short, frightened by fear of all <s>akuśala</s> (unwholesome) mental activities. Frightened by these fearful terrors, I have entered the forest dwelling.'" And so forth.

body.text: punar a-paraṃ gṛha-pate pravrajitena bodhi-satvena + araṇya-vāsa-sthitena bhītena vā trastena vā evaṃ śikṣitavyaṃ | yāni kāni-cid bhayāny utpadyante sarvāṇi tāny ātma-grāhata utpadyante || pe ||
body.translated_text: "Furthermore, householder, a renunciant <s>bodhisattva</s> established in forest dwelling, whether afraid or terrified, should train thus: 'Whatever fears arise, they all arise from grasping at a self.'" And so forth.

body.text: sacet punar aham araṇye prativasan na + ātma-grāhaṃ parityajeyaṃ na + ātma-abhiniveśaṃ na + ātma-parigrahaṃ na + ātma-nidānaṃ na + ātma-tṛṣṇāṃ na + ātma-saṃjñāṃ na + ātma-vāda-upādānaṃ na + ātma-dṛṣṭiṃ na + ātma-adhiṣṭhānaṃ na + ātma-parikalpanāṃ na + ātma-rakṣāṃ parityajeyaṃ | nir-arthako me * araṇya-vāsaḥ syād | api tu khalu punar gṛha-pate na + asty ātma-saṃjñino * araṇya-vāso | na + asti para-saṃjñinaḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: "If, moreover, while dwelling in the wilderness I do not abandon the grasping at a self, the clinging to a self, the appropriation of a self, the basis of a self, the thirst for a self, the notion of a self, the attachment to the doctrine of a self, the view of a self, the foundation of a self, the false construction of a self, the protection of a self — then my wilderness dwelling would be purposeless. But indeed, householder, there is no wilderness dwelling for one who has the notion of a self, nor for one who has the notion of another." And so forth.

body.text: araṇya-vāso nāma gṛha-pate ucyate sarva-dharmeṣv a-saṃbhava-vāsaḥ sarva-dharmeṣv a-saṃga-vāsaḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: "Wilderness dwelling, householder, is said to be dwelling in the non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena), dwelling in non-attachment to all <s>dharmas</s>." And so forth.

body.text: tad yathā gṛha-pate * araṇye tṛṇa-gulma-auṣadhi-vanas-patayaḥ prativasanto na bibhyati na + uttrasyanti na saṃtrasyanti na saṃtrāsam āpadyante | evam eva gṛha-pate pravrajitena bodhi-satvena + araṇye viharatā tṛṇa-gulma-auṣadhi-vanas-pati-kāṣṭha-kuḍya-vad ātma-pratibhāsa-vat saṃjñā kāye utpādayitavyā | māyā-samatā cittasya + utpādayitavyā | ko * atra bibheti | ko * asminn uttrasyati |tena bhaya-bhītena vā trastena vā evaṃ yoniśaḥ kāya upaparīkṣitavyaḥ | na + asty atra kāye ātmā vā satvo vā jīvo vā poṣo vā pudgalo vā manu-jo vā mānavo vā | a-bhūta-parikalpa eṣa yad uta bhayaṃ nāma | sa mayā + a-bhūta-parikalpo na parikalpayitavyaḥ | tena yathā + araṇye tṛṇa-gulma-auṣadhi-vanas-patayaḥ prativasanti a-mamā a-parigrahāḥ | evam eva + a-mamena + a-parigraheṇa + araṇyam eva sarva-dharmā iti jñātvā upasampadya vihartavyaṃ | tat kasya hetoḥ | raṇa-chedo * araṇya-vāso * a-mamo * a-parigrahaḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: "Just as, householder, grasses, shrubs, herbs, and trees dwelling in the wilderness are not afraid, do not tremble, do not quake, and do not fall into terror — even so, householder, a renunciant <s>bodhisattva</s> dwelling in the wilderness should generate the perception of the body as being like grass, shrubs, herbs, trees, wood, and walls — as a mere appearance of a self. He should generate in the mind the equality of illusion. Who is afraid here? Who trembles in this? Whether afraid or terrified, he should thus wisely examine the body: 'There is no self in this body, no being, no life-force, no person, no individual, no human, no man. This so-called fear is a false construction. That false construction should not be constructed by me.' Therefore, just as grasses, shrubs, herbs, and trees dwell in the wilderness without possessiveness and without appropriation, even so, without possessiveness and without appropriation, knowing that all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are indeed wilderness, one should attain [this realization] and dwell [accordingly]. For what reason? Because wilderness dwelling is the cutting off of conflict — without possessiveness, without appropriation." And so forth.

body.text: punar a-paraṃ gṛha-pate pravrajitena bodhi-satvena buddha-anujñāto * araṇya-vāsa iti jñātvā + araṇye vastavyaṃ | atra hi śukla-dharma-paripūrir bhavati | upastabdha-kuśala-mūlaḥ paścād-grāma-nagara-nigama-rāṣṭra-rāja-dhānīṣv avatīrya dharmaṃ deśayiṣyāmi || pe ||
body.translated_text: "Furthermore, householder, a renunciant <s>bodhisattva</s>, knowing that wilderness dwelling is authorized by the <s>Buddha</s>, should dwell in the wilderness. For therein is the fulfilment of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> (qualities). Having strengthened the <s>kuśalamūla</s> (wholesome roots), afterwards I shall descend to villages, cities, towns, kingdoms, and royal capitals and teach the <s>Dharma</s>." And so forth.

body.text: sacet punar gṛha-pate pravrajito bodhi-satva uddeśa-sva-adhyāya-arthaṃ gaṇam avatarati | tena tatra sa-gauraveṇa bhavitavyaṃ sa-pratīsena + ācārya-upādhyāyeṣu sthavira-madhya-navakeṣu bhikṣuṣu pradakṣiṇa-bhavitavyam an-alasena svayaṃ-kāriṇā + a-para-upatāpinā na ca tena + upasthāna-gurukeṇa bhavitavyaṃ | evaṃ ca + anena + upaparīkṣitavyaṃ | tathā-gato * apy arhan samyak-saṃbuddhaḥ sa-devasya lokasya sa-mārakasya sa-brahmakasya sa-śramaṇa-brāhmaṇikāyāḥ prajāyāḥ pūjito dakṣiṇīyaḥ sarva-satvānāṃ | so * api tāvan na kasya-cit sakāśād upasthānaṃ svī-karoti | kiṃ punar asmābhir a-śikṣitaiḥ śikṣitu-kāmaiḥ | api tu vayam eva sarva-satvānām upasthāyakā bhaviṣyāmaḥ | vayam eva pareṣām upasthāna-paricaryāṃ kariṣyāmo na ca punaḥ kasya-cit sakāśād upasthāna-paricaryāṃ svī-kariṣyāmaḥ | tat kasya hetoḥ | upasthāna-gurukasya hi gṛha-pate bhikṣor guṇa-dharma-anugraho naśyati | yeṣāṃ ca saṃgrahaṃ karoti teṣām evaṃ bhavati | upasthāna-hetor eṣo * asmākaṃ saṃgrahaṃ karoti ||
body.translated_text: "If, moreover, householder, a renunciant <s>bodhisattva</s> enters the community for the purpose of recitation and study, he should conduct himself there with respect and deference toward teachers and preceptors; he should show circumspection toward senior, middle, and junior <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), being diligent, doing things himself, not causing distress to others. And he should not be one who is eager for personal service. He should reflect thus: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully Awakened One, who is worthy of worship and offerings from the whole world with its <s>devas</s>, <s>Māras</s>, and <s>Brahmās</s>, with its <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — even he does not accept personal service from anyone. How much less should we, who are untrained but wish to train? Rather, we ourselves shall be attendants of all beings. We ourselves shall perform service and attendance for others, and we shall not accept service and attendance from anyone. For what reason? Because, householder, for a <s>bhikṣu</s> who is eager for personal service, the benefit of virtuous qualities is lost. And those whose favour he curries will think: He serves us for the sake of personal service.'"

body.text: punar atra + eva + āha | sacet punar gṛha-pate āraṇyako bodhi-satvo dharma-śravaṇa-arthika ācārya-upādhyāya-darśana-arthiko vā glāna-paripṛcchako vā grāma-antikaṃ śayana-āsanam āgacchet tena sā + ayam āgamanāya prakramaṇāya ca cittam utpādayitavyaṃ | sacet punar asya para-pratibaddha uddeśaḥ sva-adhyāyo vā tena vihāre prativasatā + araṇya-pravaṇa-cittena bhavitavyaṃ | eṣa eva tasya + araṇya-vāso yat sarva-vastuṣv araṇya-saṃjñā dharma-paryeṣṭyā ca + ātṛptā + iti ||
body.translated_text: Further, in the same [<s>sūtra</s>] it is said: "If, moreover, householder, a forest-dwelling <s>bodhisattva</s>, wishing to hear the <s>Dharma</s>, or wishing to see his teachers and preceptors, or to visit the sick, comes to a lodging near a village, he should generate the intention to return [to the forest]. If, however, his recitation or study depends on others [being present], then while dwelling in the monastery he should maintain a mind inclined toward the wilderness. This itself is his wilderness dwelling — that he has the perception of wilderness with regard to all things, and is insatiable in the pursuit of the <s>Dharma</s>."

body.text: ārya-ratna-rāśi-sūtre * apy uktaṃ | yadi punar asya tatra + araṇya-āyatane viharato * a-prāpta-phala-pṛthag-janasya vyāḍa-mṛgā āgaccheyuḥ | tena tatra na bhayaṃ na trāsa utpādayitavyaḥ | evaṃ ca cittam utpādayitavyaṃ | pūrvam eva + aham utsṛṣṭa-kāya-jīvito * araṇya-vāsam upagato | na mayā + atra bhetavyaṃ | na + uttrasitavyaṃ | api tu maitrīm utpādayitvā doṣaṃ vivarjayiṣyāmi bhayam apanayiṣyāmi | yady evam api kṛtvā te vyāḍa-mṛgā māṃ jīvitād vyaparopya bhuñjīran | tena mayā + evaṃ cittam utpādayitavyaṃ | lābhā me su-labdhā yasya me * a-sārāt kāyāt sāram ādattaṃ bhaviṣyati | na punar ime vyāḍa-mṛgāḥ śakyā mayā + āmiṣeṇa toṣayituṃ mama māṃsaṃ bhakṣayitvā sukha-sparśaṃ vihariṣyanti || pe ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Ratnarāśi-sūtra</s> (Heap of Jewels Sūtra) it is also said: "If, while dwelling in that forest retreat, wild beasts should approach this ordinary person who has not yet attained the fruit — he should not generate fear or alarm there. And he should generate this thought: 'I came to dwell in the forest having already relinquished body and life. I should not be afraid here. I should not be alarmed. Rather, having generated loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), I will avoid hostility and remove fear.' If, even after doing thus, those wild beasts should kill me and devour me, then I should generate this thought: 'It is a gain for me, well-gained, that the essence will have been extracted from this essenceless body. For I cannot satisfy these wild beasts with material food — having devoured my flesh, they will dwell in pleasant contact.'" [Abbreviated.]

body.text: yadi punas tatra + araṇya-āyatane viharato * a-manuṣyā upasaṃkramiṣyanti su-varṇā vā dur-varṇā vā | tena na tatra + anunetavyaṃ na pratihantavyaṃ | yadi pūrva-buddha-darśinyo devatā āraṇyakaṃ bhikṣum upasaṃkramya praśnaṃ paripṛccheyuḥ | tatra tena + āraṇyakena bhikṣuṇā yathā-śakti yathā-balaṃ yathā-dharma + adhigamāya tāsāṃ devatānāṃ dharmo deśayitavyaḥ | yadi punas tāvaṅ gambhīrān praśnān paripṛccheyur yān sa āraṇyako bhikṣur na śaknuyād visarjayituṃ | tena nir-mānena bhūtvā vāg bhāṣitavyā + a-śikṣito na paribhavitavyaḥ | yuñjiṣyāmi ghaṭiṣye buddha-śāsane | bhaviṣyati sa kālaḥ sa samayo yadā + adhigatān dharmān śrutvā sarva-kathāṃ visarjayiṣyāmi | api tu pratibhātu te | vayaṃ dhārma-śravaṇikā iti || pe ||
body.translated_text: "If, while dwelling in that forest retreat, non-human beings should approach — whether of beautiful or ugly form — he should neither be attracted to them nor repel them. If deities who have seen former <s>Buddhas</s> approach the forest-dwelling monk and ask questions, then that forest-dwelling monk should teach the <s>Dharma</s> to those deities according to his ability, according to his strength, for the comprehension of the <s>Dharma</s>. If they ask such profound questions that the forest-dwelling monk is unable to answer, then, being free from pride, he should speak these words — [for] one who is unlearned should not be despised: 'I will apply myself and strive in the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching. The time and occasion will come when, having attained and heard the <s>dharmas</s>, I will answer all questions. But may it please you — we are listeners of the <s>Dharma</s>.'" [Abbreviated.]

body.text: tena tatra + araṇya-āyatane prativasatā tṛṇa-gulma-auṣadhi-vanas-patīnāṃ nimittaṃ grahītavyaṃ | katham ete bhavanti | yathā + eṣāṃ bhāvanām a-svāmikānām a-mamānām a-parigrahāṇām evaṃ niś-ceṣṭānāṃ nir-vyāpārāṇāṃ bhavaty utpādo bhaṅgaś ca | na ca + eṣāṃ kaś-cid utpādayitā | na nirodhayitā | evam eva + ayaṃ kāyas tṛṇa-kāṣṭha-kuḍya-pratibhāsa-upamo * a-svāmiko * a-mamo * a-parigraho niś-ceṣṭo nir-vyāpāro hetu-pratyaya-yuktyā utpadyate | hetu-pratyaya-vaikalyān nirudhyate | na punar atra kaś-cid dharmaḥ parama-arthata utpadyate vā nirudhyate vā + iti ||
body.translated_text: "While dwelling in that forest retreat, he should take note of grasses, shrubs, herbs, and forest trees — how they come into being. Just as their arising and perishing occurs — ownerless, not belonging to anyone, without attachment, without effort, without activity — and no one produces them and no one destroys them — just so, this body, resembling grass, wood, and a wall-reflection, is ownerless, not belonging to anyone, without attachment, without effort, without activity. It arises through the conjunction of causes and conditions; it ceases through the deficiency of causes and conditions. And herein, ultimately, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever arises or ceases."

body.text: punaś ca + uktaṃ | tena tatra + araṇya-āyatane viharatā evaṃ cittam utpādayitavyaṃ | yady apy aham araṇyam āgata eko * a-dvitīyo | na me kaś-cit sahāyo yo māṃ su-kṛtaṃ duṣ-kṛtaṃ vā codayet | api tu khalu punaḥ santi + ime deva-nāga-yakṣā buddhāś ca bhagavanto ye mama citta-āśayaṃ jānanti | te mama sākṣiṇaḥ | so * aham iha + araṇya-āyatane prativasann a-kuśala-cittasya vaśaṃ gacchāmi | yadi punar aham iyad-dūram āgata eko * a-dvitīyo * a-saṃstabdho * a-mamo * a-parigrahaḥ kāma-vitarkaṃ vā vitarkayeyaṃ | vyāpaādaṃ vihinsā-vitarkaṃ vā vitarkayeyam anyaṃ vā + a-kuśala-vitarkaṃ vitarkayeyaṃ | nir-viśeṣo bhaveyaṃ saṃsarga-saṃgaṇikābhir etaiḥ satvaiḥ | te ca me deva-nāga-yakṣā visaṃvāditāḥ buddhāś ca bhagavanto * an-abhirāddhā bhaviṣyanti + iti ||
body.translated_text: And further it is said: "While dwelling in that forest retreat, he should generate this thought: 'Although I have come to the forest alone, without a companion — there is no one who would admonish me for good or bad conduct. But indeed, there are these gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, who know the disposition of my mind. They are my witnesses. If I, dwelling here in this forest retreat, were to come under the power of unwholesome mind — if I, having come this far, alone, without a companion, unsupported, without possessiveness, without attachment, were to entertain a thought of sensual desire, or a thought of ill-will or harm, or any other unwholesome thought — I would be no different from those beings [immersed in] socializing and gatherings. And those gods, <s>nāgas</s>, and <s>yakṣas</s> would be deceived by me, and the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, would be displeased.'"

body.text: iti śikṣā-samuccaye araṇya-saṃvarṇano nāma + ekādaśaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the eleventh chapter of the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>, called the Praise of the Forest (<s>araṇya-saṃvarṇana</s>).

body.text: citta-parikarma dvādaśaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Mental preparation — the twelfth chapter.

body.text: tad evam araṇye vasan samādhānāya yujyate ||
body.translated_text: Thus, dwelling in the forest, one applies oneself to mental composure (<s>samādhāna</s>).

body.text: uktaṃ hi bhagavatyāṃ | sa teṣām eva satvānām arthāya dhyāna-pāramitāyāṃ carann a-vikṣipta-citto bhavati | tat kasya hetoḥ | tathā hy asya + evaṃ bhavati | laukikī dhyāna-upapattir api tāvad vikṣipta-cittasya dur-labhā | kaḥ punar vādo * an-uttarā samyak-saṃbodhiḥ | tasmān mayā + a-vikṣipta-cittena bhavitavyam | yāvann an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddheyam iti ||
body.translated_text: For it is said in the <s>Bhagavatī</s> [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>]: "He, practicing the <s>dhyāna-pāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation) for the sake of those very sentient beings, becomes one of undistracted mind. For what reason? For thus he reflects: 'Even a worldly meditative attainment is difficult to obtain for one whose mind is distracted. What need to speak of supreme perfect awakening! Therefore I must become one of undistracted mind, until I am fully awakened to supreme perfect awakening.'"

body.text: punar asyām uktaṃ | punar a-paraṃ subhūte bodhi-satvo mahā-satvaḥ prathama-citta-utpādam upādāya dhyāna-pāramitāyāṃ caran sarva-ākāra-jñatā-pratisaṃyuktair manasi-kārair dhyānaṃ samāpadyate | sa cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā na nimitta-grāhī bhavati na + anuvyañjana-grāhī | yato * adhikaraṇam asya cakṣur-indriyeṇa + a-saṃvara-saṃvṛtasya viharato * abhidhyā-daurmanasye anye vā pāpakā a-kuśalā dharmāś cittam anuprāpnuyuḥ | teṣāṃ saṃvarāya pratipadyate | rakṣati cakṣur-indriyam | evaṃ śrotreṇa śabdān śrutvā | ghrāṇena gandhān ghrātvā | jihvayā rasān āsvādya | kāyena spraṣṭavyāni spṛṣṭvā | manasā dharmān vijñāya na nimitta-grāhī bhavati | na + anuvyañjana-grāhī | yato * adhikaraṇam asya mana indriyeṇa + a-saṃvara-saṃvṛtasya pāpakāś cittam anuprāpnuyuḥ | teṣāṃ saṃvarāya pratipadyate | rakṣati mana indriyaṃ | sa gacchann api tiṣṭhann api niṣaṇṇo * api śayāno * api bhāṣamāṇo * api samāhita-avasthām a-samāhita-avasthāṃ na vijahāti | sa bhavaty a-hasta-lolaḥ | a-pāda-lolo * a-mukha-lolo * a-prakīrṇa-vāk | a-vikṣipta-indriyo * an-uddhato * an-unnato * a-capalo * an-alaso * a-saṃbhrānta-kāyo * a-saṃbhrānta-cittaḥ | śānta-kāyaḥ śānta-vāk śānta-cittaḥ | rahasy a-rahasi vā kalpita-īryā-pathaḥ saṃtuṣṭaḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: And further in the same [text] it is said: "Furthermore, O <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing the <s>dhyāna-pāramitā</s> from the very first generation of the mind, enters <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) with mental attitudes connected with the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākāra-jñatā</s>). Having seen forms with the eye, he does not grasp at signs, does not grasp at secondary characteristics. Since, by reason of dwelling with the eye-faculty unrestrained, covetousness and mental distress, or other evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, would overtake his mind — he undertakes the restraint against those, and guards the eye-faculty. Likewise, having heard sounds with the ear, having smelled odors with the nose, having tasted flavors with the tongue, having touched tangibles with the body, having cognized <s>dharmas</s> with the mind — he does not grasp at signs, does not grasp at secondary characteristics. Since, by reason of dwelling with the mind-faculty unrestrained, evil [dharmas] would overtake his mind — he undertakes the restraint against those, and guards the mind-faculty. Whether going, standing, sitting, lying down, or speaking, he does not abandon the state of composure or the state of non-composure. He is not restless with his hands, not restless with his feet, not restless with his face, not scattered in speech, not with distracted faculties, not agitated, not elated, not fickle, not lazy, not with an agitated body, not with an agitated mind. Calm in body, calm in speech, calm in mind. Whether in private or in public, his deportment is proper; he is content." [Abbreviated.]

body.text: su-bharaḥ su-poṣaḥ | su-upāsyaḥ kalyāṇa-ācāra-go-caraḥ | saṃgaṇikayā + api viveka-go-caraḥ | lābhe * a-lābhe ca samo nir-vikāraḥ | an-unnato * an-avanataḥ | evaṃ sukhe duṣkhe | stutau nindāyāṃ | yaśasy a-yaśasi | jīvite maraṇe ca samo nir-vikāro * an-unnato * an-avanataḥ | evaṃ śatrau mitre ca | mana-apavartini ... | āryeṣv an-āryeṣu | śabdeṣu saṃkīrṇeṣv a-saṃkīrṇeṣu | priya-a-priyeṣu ca rūpeṣu samo nir-vikāraḥ | an-unnato * an-avanataḥ | anurodha-virodha-apagataḥ | tat kasya hetoḥ | tathā hi sa sva-lakṣaṇa-śūnyān a-saṃbhūtān a-niṣpannān an-abhinirvṛttān sarva-dharmān paśyati + iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: "He is easy to support, easy to nourish, easy to attend upon, of virtuous conduct and activity. Even in a group, his activity is that of seclusion. He is the same and unperturbed whether in gain or non-gain; likewise in happiness and suffering; in praise and blame; in fame and disrepute; and in life and death — the same, unperturbed, neither elated nor dejected. Likewise toward enemy and friend; ... toward the noble and the ignoble; toward sounds mixed and unmixed; toward pleasant and unpleasant forms — the same, unperturbed, neither elated nor dejected, free from attachment and aversion. For what reason? Because he sees all <s>dharmas</s> as empty of own-characteristics, unarisen, unaccomplished, unproduced" — and so on in detail.

body.text: tatra līne manasi muditā bhāvanayā + uttejanaṃ kuryāt | uddhate tv a-nityatā-manasi-kāraiḥ praśamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, when the mind is sluggish, one should rouse it through the cultivation of joy (<s>muditā</s>). When it is restless, [one should achieve] calm through reflections on impermanence.

body.text: ubhaya-prati-pakṣa-arthaṃ ca + ārya-rāṣṭrapāla-uktāṃ gāthāṃ smaret | bahu kalpa-koṭībhi kadā-ci buddho utpadyate loka-hito maha-rṣi | labdho * adhunā sa pravaraḥ kṣaṇo * adya tyajati pramādaṃ yadi moktu-kāma | iti ||
body.translated_text: And for the antidote to both, one should remember the verse spoken by the noble <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>: "After many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, sometimes a <s>Buddha</s> arises — the great sage who benefits the world. That supreme moment has now been obtained — let him who wishes for liberation abandon heedlessness!"

body.text: tathā | mayā + upamaṃ vitatham etat svapna-upamaṃ ca saṃskṛtam avekṣya na cirād bhaviṣyati viyogaḥ sarva-priyaiḥ | na nityam iha kaś-cit | udyujya yathā ghaṭata nityaṃ pāramitāsu bhūmiṣu baleṣu | mā jātu sraṃsaya vīryaṃ yāvan na budhyathā pravara-bodhim | iti ||
body.translated_text: Likewise: "Having considered that this [life] is false, like an illusion, and that the conditioned is like a dream, and that separation from all that is dear will come before long — nothing here is permanent — exert yourselves and strive always in the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), the <s>bhūmis</s> (stages), and the powers (<s>balas</s>). Never let your vigor slacken until you are awakened to the supreme awakening!"

body.text: ārya-lalita-vistare * apy uktaṃ | jvalitaṃ tri-bhuvaṃ jara-vyādhi-dukhair maraṇa-agni-pradīptam a-nātham idam | bhava-niḥ-śaraṇe sada mūḍha jagad bhramati bhramaro yathā kumbha-gataḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Lalitavistara</s> it is also said: "The three worlds are ablaze, tormented by old age, disease, and suffering, alight with the fire of death, without a protector. The world, forever deluded in this shelterless existence, wanders like a bee trapped in a jar."

body.text: a-dhruvaṃ tri-bhuvaṃ śarad-abhra-nibhaṃ naṭa-raṅga-samā jagi janma-cyutiḥ | giri-nadya-samaṃ laghu-śīghra-javaṃ vrajatāyu jage yatha vidyu nabhe ||
body.translated_text: "The three worlds are impermanent, like an autumn cloud. The birth and death of beings in the world is like a performance on a stage. The course of life passes swiftly, like a mountain torrent — rushing rapidly, like lightning in the sky."

body.text: bhuvi deva-pure tri-apāya-pathe bhava-tṛṣṇa-a-vidya-vaśā janatā | parivarttiṣu pañca-gatiṣv a-budhā yatha kumbha-karasya hi cakra bhramī ||
body.translated_text: "On earth, in the divine realm, and on the paths of the three lower destinies — beings are under the power of craving for existence and ignorance. The unwise revolve through the five changing destinies like the wheel of a potter."

body.text: priya-rūpa-varaiḥ sada snigdha-rutaiḥ śubha-gandha-rasair vara-sparśa-sukhaiḥ | pariṣiktam idaṃ kali-pāśa jagat mṛga-lubdhaka-pāśi yathā + eva kapi ||
body.translated_text: "With beautiful forms and colors, with sweet sounds always, with pleasant fragrances and flavors, with the happiness of excellent touch — this world is sprinkled with the snare of <s>Kali</s> (strife), like a monkey in the trap of a hunter."

body.text: sa-bhayāḥ sa-raṇāḥ sada vaira-karāḥ bahu-śoka-upadrava kāma-guṇāḥ | asi-dhāra-samā viṣa-pattra-nibhāḥ jahita-ārya-janair yatha mīḍha-ghaṭaḥ ||
body.translated_text: "Full of fear, full of conflict, always producing enmity — the strands of sensual pleasure are full of much grief and tribulation. Like the edge of a sword, like poisonous leaves — they are abandoned by noble people like a pot of filth."

body.text: smṛti-moṣa-karās tamasī-karaṇā bhaya-hetu-karā dukha-mūla sadā | bhava-tṛṣṇa-latāya vivṛddhi-karāḥ sa-bhayāḥ sa-raṇā sada kāma-guṇāḥ ||
body.translated_text: "Stealing away mindfulness, creating darkness, causing fear, always the root of suffering, increasing the creeper of craving for existence — always full of fear, full of conflict, are the strands of sensual pleasure."

body.text: yatha agni-khadāḥ jvalitāḥ sa-bhayāḥ tatha kāma ime viditā + ārya-janaiḥ | maha-paṅka-samā aśi-śūla-samā madhu-digdha iva kṣura-dhāra-samā ||
body.translated_text: "Like blazing fire-pits, full of danger — so are these desires, as understood by noble people. Like great mud, like the point of a spear, like honey smeared on the edge of a razor."

body.text: yatha sarpa-śiro yatha mīḍha-ghaṭaḥ tatha kāma ime viditā viduṣām | tatha śūla-sāmā dvi-ja-peśi-samā yatha śvāna-karaṃ kiśa-vaira tathā + udaka-candra-nibhā imi kāma-guṇāḥ pratibimba ivā giri-ghoṣa yathā | pratibhāsa-samā naṭa-raṅga-nibhā tatha svapna-samā viditā + ārya-janaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: "Like the head of a serpent, like a pot of filth — so are these desires, as understood by the wise. Like the point of a spear, like a piece of flesh [fought over by] birds, like the bone gnawed by a dog, like a quarrel of the lean. Like the moon in water are these strands of sensual pleasure, like a reflection, like an echo in the mountains, like an illusion, like a performance on a stage, like a dream — so they are understood by noble people."

body.text: kṣaṇikā-vasikā imi kāma-guṇāḥ tatha māya-marīci-samā alika-udaka-budbuda-phena-samā vitathāḥ parikalpa-samutthita buddha budhaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: "Momentary and transient are these strands of sensual pleasure, like a magical illusion, like a mirage, like false water, like a bubble, like foam — unreal, arisen from conceptual construction, as understood by the awakened ones."

body.text: prathame vayase vara-rūpa-dharaḥ priya iṣṭa-mato iya bāla-cārī | jara-vyādhi-dukhair hata-teja-vapuṃ vijahanti mṛgā iva śuṣka-nadīm ||
body.translated_text: "In the prime of youth, bearing excellent beauty, dear and beloved — this is the way of fools. Struck by old age, disease, and suffering, with luster and beauty destroyed — they abandon him like deer abandoning a dried-up river."

body.text: dhana-dhānya-varo bahu-dravya-balī priya iṣṭa-mato iya bāla-cārī | parihīṇa-dhanaṃ puna kṛcchra-gataṃ vijahanti narā iva śūnya-ṭavīm ||
body.translated_text: "Possessing the best of wealth and grain, powerful with many riches, dear and beloved — this is the way of fools. When his wealth is lost and he has fallen into difficulty — people abandon him like an empty wilderness."

body.text: yatha puṣpa-drumo sa-phalo va drumo naru-dāna-rataḥ tatha prīti-karaḥ | dhana-hīnu jarā-arditu yācanako bhavate tada a-priya-gṛdhra-samaḥ ||
body.translated_text: "Like a flowering tree, or a tree bearing fruit — so a man devoted to giving is a source of delight. Devoid of wealth, afflicted by old age, begging — he then becomes as unwelcome as a vulture."

body.text: prabhu-dravya-balī vara-rūpa-dharaḥ priya-saṅga-mana-indriya-prīti-karaḥ | jarā-vyādhi-dukha-arditu kṣīṇa-dhano bhavate tada a-priya-mṛtyu-samaḥ ||
body.translated_text: "Powerful in possessions, bearing excellent beauty, a source of delight to the senses, dear in companionship. Afflicted by old age, disease, and suffering, with wealth exhausted — he then becomes as unwelcome as death."

body.text: jarayā jaritaḥ samatīta-vayo druma vidyu-hato va yathā bhavati | jara-jīrṇa agāra yathā sa-bhayo jara-niḥ-śaraṇaṃ laghu brūhi mune ||
body.translated_text: "Worn out by old age, with life-span elapsed — he becomes like a tree struck by lightning. Like a house crumbling with age, full of danger — O sage, declare quickly the shelterlessness of old age!"

body.text: jara śoṣayate nara-nāri-gaṇaṃ yatha mālu-latā ghana śāla-vanam | jara vīrya-parākrama-vega-harī jara paṅka-nimagna yathā puruṣo ||
body.translated_text: "Old age withers the multitude of men and women, as the <s>mālu</s> (parasitic) vine [withers] a dense <s>śāla</s>-forest. Old age steals vigor, power, and momentum. Old age is like a man sunk in mud."

body.text: jara rūpa su-rūpa-vi-rūpa-karī jara teja-harī bala-sthāma-harī | sada saukhya-harī paribhāva-karī jara mṛtyu-karī jara oja-harī ||
body.translated_text: 'Old age disfigures the beautiful and makes beautiful forms ugly; old age steals radiance, steals strength and fortitude; old age always steals happiness and brings contempt; old age causes death, old age steals vitality.'

body.text: bahu-roga-śatair ghana-vyādhi-dukhaiḥ upasṛṣṭu jagaj jvalanā + iva mṛgāḥ | jara vyādhi-gataṃ prasamīkṣya jagat dukha-niḥ-śaraṇaṃ laghu deśaya hī ||
body.translated_text: 'The world is assailed by hundreds of diseases, by dense afflictions and sufferings, like deer by a forest fire. Having observed the world stricken by old age and disease, suffering and without refuge — teach the <s>Dharma</s> swiftly!'

body.text: śiśirehi yathā hima-dhātu mahaṃ tṛṇa-gulma-vana-auṣadhi oja-haro | tatha oja-haro * ayu vyādhi jage parihīyati indriya-rūpa-balam ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as in winter, the great mass of frost robs the vitality of grasses, shrubs, forests, and herbs — so disease in the world robs vitality and lifespan; the faculties, form, and strength decline.'

body.text: dhana-dhānya-mahā-artha-kṣaya-anta-karaḥ paribhāva-karaḥ sad vyādhi jage | pratighāta-karaḥ priya-dveṣa-karaḥ paridāha-karo yatha sūryu nabhe ||
body.translated_text: 'Disease in the world causes the destruction of wealth, grain, and great prosperity; it causes contempt; it constantly causes obstruction; it causes the hatred of loved ones; it causes burning, like the sun in the sky.'

body.text: maraṇaṃ cyavanaṃ cyuti kāla-kriyā priya-dravya-janena viyogu sadā | a-puna-āgamanaṃ ca a-saṃgamanaṃ druma-pattra-phalā nadi-śrotu yathā ||
body.translated_text: 'Death, passing away, decease, the making of time — always the separation from loved ones, possessions, and people; no returning, no reunion — like the leaves and fruit of a tree, like the current of a river.'

body.text: maraṇaṃ vaśitān a-vaśī-kurute maraṇaṃ harate nadi dāru yathā | a-sahāya-naro vrajate * a-dvitīyaḥ svaka-karma-phala-anugato vi-vaśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Death makes the powerful powerless; death carries [one] away like a river carries wood. A man goes alone, without a companion, without a second, helpless, followed [only] by the fruit of his own <s>karma</s>.'

body.text: maraṇaṃ grasate bahu prāṇi-śatān makaro va jala-ākari bhūta-gaṇān | garuḍo ura-gaṃ mṛga-rāja gaja jvalano va tṛṇa-auṣadhi-bhūta-gaṇam | iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Death devours hundreds of living beings, like a sea-monster [devours] hosts of creatures in a body of water, like <s>Garuḍa</s> [devours] a serpent, like the king of beasts [devours] an elephant, like fire [consumes] hosts of grasses, herbs, and creatures.'

body.text: rāja-avavādaka-sūtre * apy āha | tad yathā mahā-rāja catasṛbhyo digbhyaś catvāraḥ parvatā āgaccheyur dṛḍhāḥ | sāravanto * a-khaṇḍā a-cchidrā a-suṣirāḥ su-saṃvṛtā eka-ghanā nabhaḥ spṛśantaḥ pṛthivīṃ ca + ullikhantaḥ sarva-tṛṇa-kāṣṭha-śākhā-parṇa-palāśa-ādi sarva-satva-prāṇi-bhūtāni nirmathnantas tebhyo na su-karaṃ javena vā palāyituṃ balena vā dravya-mantra-auṣadhibhir vā nivartayitum | evam eva mahā-rāja catvāri + imāni mahā-bhayāny āgacchanti yeṣāṃ na su-karaṃ javena vā palāyituṃ balena dravya-mantra-auṣadhair vā nivartanaṃ kartum | katamāni catvāri | jarā vyādhir maraṇaṃ vipattiś ca ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Rāja-avavādaka-sūtra</s> (Sūtra of Admonition to the King) also it is said: 'Suppose, O great king, from the four directions, four mountains were to come — solid, substantial, unbroken, without fissures, without hollows, well-compacted, of one mass — touching the sky and scraping the earth, crushing all grasses, wood, branches, leaves, foliage, and all beings, living creatures. Against these it would not be easy to flee by speed, or to turn them back by strength, or by substances, <s>mantras</s>, or medicines. Even so, O great king, these four great terrors approach, against which it is not easy to flee by speed, or to turn them back by strength, substances, <s>mantras</s>, or medicines. What are the four? Old age, disease, death, and calamity.'

body.text: jarā mahā-rāja āgacchati yauvanaṃ pramathamānā | vyādhir mahā-rāja āgacchaty ārogyaṃ pramathamānaḥ | maraṇam āgacchati jīvitaṃ pramathamānaṃ | vipattir mahā-rāja + āgacchati sarvāḥ saṃpattīḥ pramathamānā | tat kasya hetoḥ | tad yathā mahā-rāja siṃho mṛga-rājo rūpa-saṃpanno java-saṃpannaḥ su-jāta-nakha-daṃṣṭrā-karālo mṛga-gaṇam anupraviśya mṛgaṃ gṛhītvā yathā-kāma-karaṇīyaṃ karoti | sa ca mṛgo * ati-balaṃ vyāḍa-mukham āsādya vi-vaśo bhavati | evam eva mahā-rāja viddhasya mṛtyu-śalyena + apagata-madasya + a-parāyaṇasya marmasu chidyamāneṣu mucyamāneṣu sandhiṣu māṃsa-śoṇite pariśuṣyamāṇe paritapta-tṛṣita-vihvala-vadanasya kara-caraṇa-vikṣepa-abhiyuktasya + a-karmaṇyasya + a-samarthasya lālā-siṅghāṇaka-pūya-mūtra-purīṣa-upaliptasya īṣaj-jīvita-avaśeṣasya karma-bhavāt punar bhavam ālambānasya yama-puruṣa-bhaya-bhītasya kāla-rātri-vaśa-gatasya carama-āśvāsa-praśvāseṣu + uparudhyamāneṣu e kākino * a-dvitīyasya + a-sahāyasya + imaṃ lokaṃ jahataḥ para-lokam ākrāmato mahā-pathaṃ vrajato mahā-kāntāraṃ praviśato mahā-gahanaṃ samavagāhamānasya mahā-andha-kāraṃ pratipadyamānasya mahā-arṇavena + urjyamānasya karma-vāyunā + āhriyamāṇasya + a-nimittī-kṛtāṃ diśaṃ gacchato na + anyat trāṇaṃ na + anyac * charaṇaṃ na + anyat parāyaṇam ṛte dharmāt | dharmo hi mahā-rāja tasmin samaye trāṇaṃ layanaṃ śaraṇaṃ parāyaṇaṃ bhavati | tad yathā śīta-ārttasya + agni-pratāpaḥ | agnim apagatasya + a-nirvāpaṇaṃ | uṣṇa-ārttasya śaityaṃ | adhvānaṃ pratipannasya śītalaṃ chāyā-upavanaṃ | pipāsitasya śītala-jalaṃ | bubhukṣitasya vā praṇītam annaṃ | vyādhitasya vaidya-oṣadhi-paricārakāḥ | bhaya-bhītasya balavantaḥ sahāyāḥ | sādhavaḥ prati-śaraṇā bhavanti | evam eva mahā-rāja viddhasya mṛtyu-śalyena + apagata-madasya + a-trāṇasya + a-śaraṇasya + a-parāyaṇasya na + anyat trāṇaṃ na + anyat parāyaṇam anyatra dharmāt | tasmāt tarhi te mahā-rāja + a-nityatā-anudarśinā bhavitavyaṃ kṣaya-vyaya-anudarśinā bhavitavyaṃ maraṇa-bhaya-bhītena | dharmeṇa + eva te mahā-rāja rājyaṃ kārayitavyaṃ na + a-dharmeṇa | tat kasya hetoḥ | asya + api te mahā-rāja + ātma-bhāvasya + evaṃ su-ciram api parirakṣitasya su-ciram api śucinā praṇītena khādanīya-bhojanīya-āsvādanīyena saṃtarpitasya saṃpravāritasya | kṣuta-pipāsā-parigatasya kāla-kriyā bhaviṣyati | evaṃ kāśi-kauśeya-dūkūla-pattra-ūrṇā-kṣauma-ādibhir vastra-viśeṣair ācchāditasya carama-śayana-avasthitasya vividha-sveda-ambu-klinna-malina-vasana-āvṛtasya kāla-kriyā bhaviṣyati | evam api te mahā-rāja snāna-anulepana-vāsa-dhūpa-puṣpa-surabhi-gandhasya + ātma-bhāvasya na cireṇa dur-gandhatā bhaviṣyati | evaṃ stry--āgāra-madhya-gatasya + api te strī-gaṇa-parivṛtasya nānā-vādya-gīta-tūrya-nādyair upagīyamānasya su-manasaḥ krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayato maraṇa-bhaya-bhītasya + atīva duṣkha-daurmanasyābhyāṃ kāla-kriyā bhaviṣyati | evam api te mahā-rāja gṛheṣu + upalepana-upalipteṣu su-sthāpita-argaleṣu su-pihita-vāta-āyaneṣu bahu-gandha-dhūpa-puṣpa-taila-varti-prajvāliteṣv āsakta-paṭṭa-dāma-kalāpeṣu mukta-kusuma-avakīrṇeṣu gandha-ghaṭikā-nirdhūpiteṣu a-nyasta-pāda-pīṭha-paṭikā-āstaraṇa-goṇikā-āstaraṇa-kāca-lindika-prāvaraṇa-sa-antara-uchada-paṭikā-ubhaya-kṛta-upadhāneṣu paryaṅkeṣu śayitvā | punaś ca śṛgāla-kāka-gṛdhra-mṛtaka-ḍevara-māṃsa-asthi-keśa-rudhira-vaśa-ākule parama-bībhatse śmaśāne gata-ceṣṭasya + ātma-bhāvaḥ pṛthivyām a-vaśaḥ śeṣyate | evam api te mahā-rāja gaja-skandha-aśva-pṛṣṭha-ratha-abhirūḍhasya śaṅkha-paṭaheṣv āhanyamāneṣu chatreṇa dhāryamāṇena bāla-vyajanena vījayamānasya + an-eka-hasty-aśva-ratha-padātibhir anuyātasya + añjali-śata-sahasrair namas-kriyamāṇasya | nirgamanam anubhūya na cirān niś-ceṣṭasya mṛta-śayana-abhirūḍhasya caturbhiḥ puruṣair utkṣiptasya dakṣiṇena nagara-dvāreṇa nirṇītasya mātā-pitṛ-bhrātṛ-bhaginī-bhāryā-putra-duhitṛ-vayasya-dāsī-dāsa-karma-kara-pauruṣeyaiḥ śoka-gata-hṛdayair vikṣipta-keśair utkṣipta-bhujaiḥ sa-uras-tāḍaṃ parama-karuṇaṃ | hā putra hā nātha hā tāta hā svāminn ity ākrandamānaiḥ paura-jānapadaiḥ sa-paribhāva-dṛśyamānasya śmaśānaṃ nītasya punaḥ kāka-gṛdhra-śva-śṛgāla-ādibhir bhakṣitasya tāny asthīny agninā vā dagdhāni pṛthivyāṃ vā nikhānitāni adbhir vā klinnāni vāta-ātāpa-varṣair vā cūrṇī-kṛtāni dig-vi-dikṣu prakṣiptāni tatra + eva pūta-bhavam āyāsyanti | evam a-nityāḥ sarva-saṃskārā evam a-dhruvā iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Old age, O great king, approaches, crushing youth. Disease, O great king, approaches, crushing health. Death approaches, crushing life. Calamity, O great king, approaches, crushing all prosperity. For what reason? Just as, O great king, a lion, the king of beasts — endowed with beauty, endowed with swiftness, with well-grown claws and fangs, terrible — entering a herd of deer, seizing a deer, does with it whatever he wishes; and that deer, encountering the powerful and ferocious jaws, becomes helpless — even so, O great king, for one pierced by the arrow of death, whose pride has departed, who has no refuge, whose vital points are being severed, whose joints are loosening, whose flesh and blood are drying up, whose face is burning with thirst, confused and distressed, whose hands and feet are flinging about, who is incapable and powerless, smeared with saliva, mucus, pus, urine, and excrement, with barely a trace of life remaining, grasping at another existence from the existence of <s>karma</s>, terrified by the fear of <s>Yama</s>'s messengers, fallen under the power of the night of death, whose final inhalations and exhalations are being obstructed — alone, without a second, without a companion, leaving this world, proceeding to the next world, traveling the great highway, entering the great wilderness, plunging into the great thicket, arriving at the great darkness, carried along by the great ocean, swept by the wind of <s>karma</s>, going to a directionless direction — there is no other protection, no other refuge, no other resort, apart from the <s>Dharma</s>. For the <s>Dharma</s>, O great king, at that time becomes the protection, the shelter, the refuge, the resort. Just as the warmth of fire for one afflicted by cold; quenching for one afflicted by fire; coolness for one afflicted by heat; a shady grove for one who has taken to the road; cool water for one who is thirsty; excellent food for one who is hungry; a physician, medicine, and attendants for one who is sick; powerful companions for one who is frightened by fear — virtuous ones become the refuge. Even so, O great king, for one pierced by the arrow of death, whose pride has departed, who has no protection, no refuge, no resort — there is no other protection, no other resort, apart from the <s>Dharma</s>. Therefore, O great king, you should be one who contemplates impermanence, who contemplates decay and destruction, who is frightened by the fear of death. You should govern your kingdom through the <s>Dharma</s>, O great king, not through what is contrary to the <s>Dharma</s>. For what reason? Even this body of yours, O great king — though protected for so long, though nourished for so long with pure and excellent food, solid and liquid — when afflicted by hunger and thirst, the time of death will come. Even when clothed in special garments of <s>Kāśī</s> silk, Chinese silk, fine muslin, and wool — when lying on the final bed, covered in soiled garments damp with various sweat — the time of death will come. Even this body of yours, O great king, fragrant with baths, ointments, perfumes, incense, and flowers — before long, foulness of smell will come. Even for you, O great king, dwelling in the midst of the women's quarters, surrounded by a host of women, serenaded by various instrumental music, song, and cymbals, happy in mind, playing, delighting, being attended upon — terrified by the fear of death, with extreme suffering and mental distress, the time of death will come. Even for you, O great king, having slept in houses plastered and decorated, with well-fastened bolts, with well-closed ventilation openings, lit with many incense-sticks, flowers, oil-lamps, and candles, with silk ribbons and garlands fastened, strewn with loose flowers, perfumed with incense-balls, on couches with foot-stools and mats of various kinds, coverlets, and pillows arranged on both sides — even then, your body, motionless, will lie helplessly upon the earth in the supremely loathsome cremation ground, crowded with jackals, crows, vultures, corpses, and bones, hair, blood, and fat. Even for you, O great king — having mounted elephant-back, horse-back, and chariot, with conches and drums being sounded, with a parasol held [over you], fanned with a <s>bālavyajana</s> (yak-tail fan), followed by many elephants, horses, chariots, and foot-soldiers, being saluted by hundreds of thousands of joined palms — having experienced departure, before long, motionless, mounted on the death-bed, lifted by four men, carried out through the southern gate of the city, while mothers, fathers, brothers, sisters, wives, sons, daughters, friends, female servants, male servants, workers, and attendants — grief-stricken, with disheveled hair, with arms raised, beating their chests, crying out most pitifully: "Alas, my son! Alas, my lord! Alas, my father! Alas, my master!" — while the townsfolk and countryfolk look on with contempt, carried to the cremation ground, then eaten by crows, vultures, dogs, jackals, and others — those bones are burned by fire, or buried in the earth, or dissolved by water, or ground to dust by wind, heat, and rain, scattered in all directions, and right there they will come to a state of putrefaction. Thus all conditioned things are impermanent, thus they are unstable' — and so on in detail.

body.text: tatra kleśāḥ prādhānyena rāga-dveṣa-mohā yasya + eṣām ekatarasya tāvat prati-pakṣam ādau bhāvayet tan-nidānaṃ ca varjayet ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are primarily attachment, hatred, and delusion. With respect to whichever of these is predominant, one should first cultivate its antidote and avoid its cause.

body.text: tatra + ārya-ratna-meghe tāvad āha | sa rāgasya prati-pakṣaṃ bhajate | rāga-utpatti-pratyayāṃś ca varjayati | katamaś ca sa rāgasya prati-pakṣaḥ | katame ca te rāga-utpatti-pratyayāḥ | a-śubhā-bhāvanā + a-rāgasya prati-pakṣaḥ | jana-pada-kalyāṇī-rāga-utpatti-pratyayaḥ | katamā ca sā + a-śubhā-bhāvanā | yad uta santy asmin kāye keśā romāṇi nakhā dantā rajo malaṃ tvak māṃsa-asthi snāyuḥ śirā vṛkkā hṛdayaṃ plīhakaḥ klomakaḥ | antrāṇy antra-guṇa āma-āśayaḥ pakva-āśayaḥ | audaryakaṃ yakṛt purīṣam aśru svedaḥ kheṭaḥ siṅghāṇakaṃ vasā lasikā majjā medaḥ pittaṃ śleśmā pūyaṃ śoṇitaṃ mastakaṃ mastaka-luṅgaṃ prasrāvaḥ | eṣu ca vastuṣu bodhi-satva upaparīkṣaṇa-jātīyo bhavati | tasya + evam upaparīkṣamāṇasya + evaṃ bhavati | yo * api tāvat syād bālo mūḍhaḥ a-bhavyo * a-kuśalaḥ so * api tāvad etāni vastūni jñātvā rāga-cittaṃ na + utpādayet | prāg eva sa-prajña-jātīyaḥ | evaṃ hi bodhi-satvo * a-śubhā-bhāvanā-bahulo bhavati + iti ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the noble <s>Ratnamegha</s> says: 'He resorts to the antidote of attachment and avoids the conditions that give rise to attachment. And what is the antidote of attachment? And what are the conditions that give rise to attachment? The contemplation of the impure (<s>aśubhā-bhāvanā</s>) is the antidote of non-attachment. A beautiful woman of the countryside is the condition that gives rise to attachment. And what is that contemplation of the impure? Namely: in this body there are head-hairs, body-hairs, nails, teeth, dirt, filth, skin, flesh, bones, sinews, veins, kidneys, heart, spleen, lung, intestines, intestinal mesentery, the undigested [food], the digested [food], stomach contents, liver, excrement, tears, sweat, phlegm, mucus, fat, lymph, marrow, adipose tissue, bile, mucous, pus, blood, brain, brain-membrane, and urine. And regarding these substances, the <s>bodhisattva</s> becomes one who investigates. As he investigates thus, this [thought] arises: "Even a foolish, deluded, incapable, unskillful person, having understood these substances, would not generate a thought of attachment — how much less one of a wise nature!" Thus the <s>bodhisattva</s> becomes one who is abundant in the contemplation of the impure.'

body.text: bhagavatyām apy uktaṃ | punar a-paraṃ subhūte bodhi-satvo mahā-satvaḥ prajñā-pāramitāyāṃ carann imam evaṃ kāyaṃ yathā-bhūtaṃ prajānāti | tad yathā + api nāma subhūte go-ghātako vā go-ghātaka-ante-vāsī vā gāṃ hatvā tīkṣṇena śastreṇa catvāri phalakāni kṛtvā pratyavekṣate sthito * atha-vā niṣaṇṇaḥ | evam eva subhūte bodhi-satvaḥ prajñā-pāramitāyāṃ carann imam eva kāyaṃ dhātuśo yathā-bhūtaṃ prajānāti | asty asmin kāye pṛthivī-dhātur ab-dhātur api tejo-dhātur api vāyu-dhātur api + iti | pe ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Bhagavatī</s> (Prajñāpāramitā) also it is stated: 'Furthermore, O <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, knows this body as it truly is. Just as, O <s>Subhūti</s>, a butcher or a butcher's apprentice, having killed a cow and having cut it into four portions with a sharp knife, examines [them] while standing or sitting — even so, O <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s>, practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, knows this very body according to its elements as it truly is: "In this body there is the earth element, the water element, the fire element, and the wind element."' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: punar apy āha | tad yathā + api subhūte karṣakasya mūtoḍī pūrṇā nānā-dhānyānāṃ śālīnāṃ vrīhīṇāṃ tilānāṃ taṇḍulānāṃ mudrānāṃ māṣāṇāṃ yavānāṃ go-dhūmānāṃ maśūrāṇāṃ sarṣapāṇāṃ |tān etān cakṣuṣmān puruṣaḥ pratyavekṣamāṇaḥ | evaṃ-jātīyād ayaṃ śālir ayaṃ vrīhir amī tilā amī taṇḍulā amī mudrā amī māṣā yavā amī go-dhūmā amī maśūrā amī sarṣapā iti ||
body.translated_text: And again it says: 'Just as, O <s>Subhūti</s>, a farmer's granary is full of various grains — rice, unhusked rice, sesame seeds, husked rice, kidney beans, black beans, barley, wheat, lentils, and mustard seeds — and a man with eyes, examining them, [would say]: "This is of such a kind — this is rice, this is unhusked rice, these are sesame seeds, these are husked rice grains, these are kidney beans, these are black beans, this is barley, this is wheat, these are lentils, these are mustard seeds."'

body.text: evam eva bodhi-satvo mahā-satvaḥ prajñā-pāramitāyāṃ carann imam eva kāyam ūrddhvaṃ pāda-talād adhaḥ keśa-mastaka-nakha-roma-tvak roma-paryantaṃ pūrṇaṃ nānā-prakārasya + a-śucer yathā-bhūtaṃ pratyavekṣate | santy asmin kāye keśā romāṇi nakhā yāvan mastakaṃ mastaka-luṅgam akṣi-gūthaṃ karṇa-gūtham iti || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'Even so, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, examines this very body as it truly is — upward from the soles of the feet, downward from the crown of the head and the tips of the nails and hairs — full of various kinds of impurity: "In this body there are head-hairs, body-hairs, nails, up to brain and brain-membrane, eye-excrement, ear-excrement."' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: punar a-paraṃ subhūte bodhi-satvaḥ śmaśāna-gataḥ paśyati nānā-rūpāṇi mṛta-śarīrāṇi śmaśāne * apaviddhāni śava-śayane ujjhitāni eka-aha-mṛtāni vā dvy-aha-mṛtāni vā try-aha-mṛtāni vā catur-aha-mṛtāni vā pañca-aha-mṛtāni vā vyādhmātakāni vinīlakāni vipūyakāni vipaṭhyakāni | sa imam eva kāyaṃ tatra + upasaṃharati | ayam api kāya evaṃ-dharmā evaṃ-sva-bhāvaḥ | etāṃ dharmatām a-vyativṛttae iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, O <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s>, having gone to a charnel ground, sees various kinds of dead bodies cast aside in the charnel ground, abandoned on the corpse-bed — dead one day, two days, three days, four days, or five days — swollen, discolored, festering, and decomposing. He applies [this observation] to his own body: "This body too is of such a nature, of such a character; it has not gone beyond this condition."'

body.text: evaṃ hi subhūte bodhi-satvo mahā-satvaḥ prajñā-pāramitāyāṃ caran bahir-dhā kāye kāya-anudarśī viharati || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'Thus, O <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing the Perfection of Wisdom (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>), dwells externally contemplating the body in the body.' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: punar a-paraṃ yadā mṛta-śarīrāṇi śmaśāne utsṛṣṭāni paśyati | ṣaḍ-rātra-mṛtāni kākair vā khādyamānāni kurarair vā gṛdhrair vā śvabhir vā śṛgālair vā tato * anyair vā nānā-vidhaiḥ prāṇaka-jātaiḥ khādyamānāni sa imam eva kāyaṃ tatra + upasaṃharati | ayam api kāya evaṃ-dharmā evaṃ-sva-bhāvaḥ | etāṃ dharmatāṃ na vyativṛttae iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, when he sees dead bodies abandoned in the charnel ground — dead six nights — being devoured by crows, or hawks, or vultures, or dogs, or jackals, or by various other kinds of living creatures — he applies [this observation] to his own body: "This body too is of such a nature, of such a character; it has not gone beyond this condition."'

body.text: punar a-paraṃ yadā mṛta-śarīrāṇi paśyati śmaśāne utsṛṣṭāni vikhāditāny a-śucīni dur-gandhāni | sa imam eva kāyaṃ tatra + upasaṃharati + iti pūrva-vat || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, when he sees dead bodies abandoned in the charnel ground — gnawed, impure, foul-smelling — he applies this very body thereto,' as before. [Abbreviation.]

body.text: punar a-paraṃ yadā paśyati mṛta-śarīrāṇi śiva-pathikāyām asthi-saṃkalikāṃ māṃsa-śoṇita-mrakṣitāṃ snāyu-vinibaddhāṃ |sa tatra + imam eva kāyam iti pūrva-vat ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, when he sees dead bodies on the cremation path — a chain of bones smeared with flesh and blood, bound together by sinews — he applies this very body thereto,' as before.

body.text: punar a-paraṃ yadā mṛta-śarīrāṇi paśyati śiva-pathikāyām asthi-saṃkalī-bhūtāni apagata-māṃsa-śoṇita-snāyu-bandhanāni | sa imam eva kāyam iti pūrva-vat ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, when he sees dead bodies on the cremation path — become a chain of bones, devoid of flesh, blood, and sinew-bindings — he applies this very body thereto,' as before.

body.text: punar a-paraṃ yadā paśyati śiva-pathikāyām asthīni dig-vi-dikṣu kṣiptāni | yad uta + anyena pāda-asthīni | anyena jaṅgha-asthīni | anyena ca + ūrv-asthīni | anyena śroṇi-kaṭāhakaṃ | anyena pṛṣṭha-vaṃśam anyena pārśvaka-asthīni | anyena grīva-asthīni | anyena bāhv-asthīni | sa imam eva kāyam upasaṃharati + iti pūrva-vat || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, when he sees on the cremation path bones scattered in the cardinal and intermediate directions — here the foot-bones, there the shin-bones, elsewhere the thigh-bones, elsewhere the hip-socket, elsewhere the spine, elsewhere the rib-bones, elsewhere the neck-bones, elsewhere the arm-bones — he applies this very body thereto,' as before. [Abbreviation.]

body.text: punar a-paraṃ yadā paśyati śiva-pathikāyām asthīny an-eka-vārṣikāṇi vāta-anupariśoṣitāni śaṅkha-sannibhāni | imam eva kāyaṃ tatra + upasaṃharati + iti pūrva-vat | ayam api kāya evaṃ-dharmā evaṃ-sva-bhāva etāṃ dharmatāṃ na vyativṛttae iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, when he sees on the cremation path bones many years old, dried out by the wind, resembling conch-shells — he applies this very body thereto,' as before: 'This body too is of such a nature, of such a character; it has not gone beyond this condition.'

body.text: punar a-paraṃ subhūte bodhi-satvo mahā-satvaḥ prajñā-pāramitāyāṃ caran yadā paśyati śiva-pathikāyām asthīny an-eka-vārṣikāṇi tiro-bhūtāni nīlāni kapota-varṇāni pūtīni cūrṇaka-jātāni pṛthivyāṃ pāṃsunā a-sama-samī-bhūtāni sa imam eva kāyaṃ tatra + upasaṃharati ayam api kāya evaṃ-dharmā evaṃ-sva-bhāvaḥ | etāṃ dharmatāṃ na vyativṛttae iti ||
