body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, O <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing the Perfection of Wisdom (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>), when he sees on the cremation path bones many years old, hidden away, bluish, pigeon-colored, putrid, crumbled, become level with the earth and dust — he applies this very body thereto: "This body too is of such a nature, of such a character; it has not gone beyond this condition."'

body.text: eṣa tāvat samāsato rāgasya samudācāra-prati-pakṣaḥ | dveṣasya maitrī prati-pakṣaḥ | a-priya-satva-a-darśanaṃ ca | tena vā saha bhojana-ādy-eka-arthatayā + a-prīty-utpādanaṃ tatra para-sukhasya + āśaṃsā prārthanā tṛṣṇā + abhinandanaṃ maitrī | kāma-rāga-praty-upakāra-hetubhyām a-kliṣṭaḥ sneha ity arthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: This, then, is in brief the antidote to the arising of attachment (<s>rāga</s>). The antidote to hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>) is loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) — and [also] the non-seeing of disagreeable beings; or the non-arising of displeasure through sharing food and other things with them. Therein, the wish, aspiration, craving, and delight for the happiness of others is <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). [It is] an undefiled affection, [arising] from causes other than sensual desire and reciprocal benefit — this is the meaning.

body.text: sā tri-vidhā + ārya-akṣayamati-sūtre * abhihitā | satva-ārambaṇā maitrī prathama-citta-utpādikānāṃ bodhi-satvānāṃ | dharma-ārambaṇā caryā-pratipannānāṃ bodhi-satvānāṃ | an-ārambaṇā maitrī an-utpattika-dharma-kṣānti-pratilabdhānāṃ bodhi-satvānām iti ||
body.translated_text: That [loving-kindness] is threefold, as stated in the <s>Ārya-Akṣayamati Sūtra</s>: '<s>Maitrī</s> that takes beings as its object belongs to <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have first generated the mind [of awakening]. <s>Maitrī</s> that takes <s>dharmas</s> as its object belongs to <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have entered the practice. <s>Maitrī</s> without object belongs to <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have attained the patience of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>).'

body.text: punar buddha-ārambaṇā bodhi-satva-ārambaṇā śrāvaka-praty-eka-buddha-ārambaṇā satva-ārambaṇā ca | tatra satva-ārambaṇāyāḥ pūrvaṃ priye satve hita-sukha-upasaṃhārān na dhyānam abhyasya | tat-same maitrīm upasaṃharet | tataḥ pariciteṣu | tata udāsīneṣu | tataḥ samīpa-vāsiṣu | tataḥ sva-grāma-vāsiṣu | evaṃ para-grāme ca | evaṃ yāvad ekāṃ diśam adhimucya spharitvā + upasaṃpadya viharati | evaṃ daśasu dikṣu | buddha-ādy-ārambaṇāyās tv ayaṃ prayāso na + asti ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, [maitrī may take as its object] the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, or beings. Among these, for <s>maitrī</s> taking beings as its object: first, without having practiced <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) through applying [the wish for] welfare and happiness to a dear being, one should extend <s>maitrī</s> to one who is equal to that [dear person]; then to acquaintances; then to neutral persons; then to nearby dwellers; then to one's own village; and likewise to other villages; and so on, until, having resolved upon and pervaded one direction, one dwells [in maitrī]. Likewise in the ten directions. But for <s>maitrī</s> taking <s>Buddhas</s> and others as its object, this exertion is not required.

body.text: sā ca vajra-dhvaja-pariṇāmanāyām uktā | sa bodhi-satva-caryāyāṃ caran yāvanti kāni-cid dṛśyante rūpāṇi mano-jñāni vā prati-kūlāni vā | evaṃ śabdā gandhā rasā spraṣṭavyā dharmā mano-jñā vā prati-kūlā vā | an-avadyā viśuddhāḥ kalyāṇa-udāra-prabhāsvarā vā yena saumanasyaṃ jāyate | sukham avakrāmati | prasādo jāyate | prītiḥ saṃbhavati | prāmodyaṃ saṃtiṣṭhate | harṣaḥ prādur-bhavati | daurmanasyaṃ nivartate | citta-kalyatā prādur-bhavati | cittaṃ karmaṇyaṃ bhavati | āśayo mṛdu-bhavati | indriyāṇi prahlādaṃ gacchanti | satata-sukhaṃ saṃvedayamāna evaṃ pariṇāmayati | sarva-buddhānām etayā pariṇāmanayā bhūyasyā mātrayā te buddhā bhagavanto * a-cintyena buddha-vihāra-sukhena samanvāgatā bhavantv a-tulyena buddha-samādhi-sukhena su-saṃgṛhītā bhavantv an-anta-sukhena bhūyasyā mātrayā + upastabdhā bhavantu | a-pramāṇena buddha-vimokṣa-sukhena samanvāgatā bhavantu | a-prameyeṇa buddha-prātihārya-sukhena su-saṃgṛhītā bhavantu | a-cintyena buddha-a-saṃga-vihāra-sukhena su-parigṛhītā bhavantu | dur-āsadena buddha-vṛṣabhita-sukhena + abhichannā bhavantu | a-prameyeṇa buddha-bala-sukhena + ātyanta-sukhitā bhavantu | sarva-vedita-śāntena + an-utpatti-sukhena + adhikāra-sukhā bhavantu | a-saṃga-vihāra-satata-samāhitena tathā-gata-sukhena + a-dvaya-samudācāreṇa + a-vikopita-sukhā bhavantu ||
body.translated_text: And that [dedication] is stated in the <s>Vajradhvajapariṇāmanā</s>: 'The <s>bodhisattva</s> practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct — whatever forms are seen, whether pleasant or disagreeable; likewise sounds, smells, tastes, tangible objects, and mental objects, whether pleasant or disagreeable; or those that are blameless, pure, beautiful, noble, and luminous — by which joy arises, happiness descends, faith arises, gladness is born, delight is established, exhilaration appears, despondency ceases, mental health appears, the mind becomes workable, the intention becomes soft, the faculties reach refreshment — experiencing constant happiness, he dedicates thus: "By this dedication, may all <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s> be endowed all the more with the inconceivable happiness of the <s>Buddha</s>'s abiding; may they be well-sustained by the incomparable happiness of the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>samādhi</s>; may they be supported all the more by infinite happiness; may they be endowed with the immeasurable happiness of the <s>Buddha</s>'s liberation; may they be well-sustained by the inconceivable happiness of the <s>Buddha</s>'s miraculous display; may they be well-held by the inconceivable happiness of the <s>Buddha</s>'s unattached abiding; may they be covered by the unapproachable happiness of the <s>Buddha</s>'s sovereignty; may they be supremely happy through the immeasurable happiness of the <s>Buddha</s>'s powers; may they have the happiness of mastery through the happiness of non-arising in which all experience has been pacified; may they have unimpaired happiness through the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s happiness that is constantly concentrated in unattached abiding, with the conduct of non-duality."'

body.text: evaṃ bodhi-satvas tat-kuśala-mūlaṃ tathā-gateṣu pariṇamayya bodhi-satveṣu pariṇamayati | yad idam a-paripūrṇānām abhiprāyāṇāṃ paripūrṇāya pariṇamayati | a-pariśuddhānāṃ sarva-jñatā-adhyāśayānāṃ pariśuddhaye | a-pariniṣpannānāṃ sarva-pāramitānāṃ pariniṣpattaye | vajra-upamasya bodhi-citta-utpādasya + adhiṣṭhānāya | a-nivartyasya sarva-jñatā-saṃnāhasya + a-pratiprasrabdhaye | bodhi-satvānāṃ kuśala-mūlānāṃ mārgaṇatāyai | sarva-jagat-samatā-sthitasya mahā-praṇidhānasya paripūraye | sarva-bodhi-satva-vihārāṇām adhigamāya | sarva-bodhi-satva-indriyāṇāṃ tīkṣṇa-abhijñatāyai | sarva-bodhi-satva-kuśala-mūlānāṃ sarva-jñatā-sparśanatāyai ||
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>bodhisattva</s>, having dedicated that wholesome root to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, dedicates it to the <s>bodhisattvas</s> — for the fulfillment of their unfulfilled intentions; for the purification of their impure aspirations toward omniscience; for the completion of their incomplete perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>); for the establishment of the diamond-like arising of <s>bodhicitta</s>; for the non-relaxation of the irreversible armor of omniscience; for the quest of the wholesome roots of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>; for the fulfillment of the great aspiration that abides in the equality of the entire world; for the attainment of all <s>bodhisattva</s> abodes; for the sharpness and direct knowledge of the faculties of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>; for all wholesome roots of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> to touch omniscience.

body.text: sa evaṃ tat-kuśala-mūlaṃ bodhi-satvānām arthāya pariṇamayya buddha-śāsana-avacareṣu sarva-śrāvaka-praty-eka-buddheṣu tat-kuśala-mūlam evaṃ pariṇāmayati | te ke-cit satvā eka-acchaṭa-a-saṃhāta-mātram api buddha-śabdaṃ sṛṇvati | dharma-śabdaṃ vā + ārya-saṃgha-paryupāsanaṃ vā kurvanti teṣāṃ tat-kuśala-mūlam an-uttarāyai samyak-saṃbodhaye pariṇāmayati buddha-anusmṛti-paripūryai pariṇāmayati | dharma-anusmṛti-prayogatāyai pariṇāmayati | ārya-saṃgha-gauravāya pariṇāmayati | a-cira-hita-buddha-darśanatāyai pariṇāmayati | citta-pariśuddhaye pariṇāmayati | buddha-dharma-prativedhāya pariṇāmayati | a-prameya-guṇa-pratipattaye pariṇāmayati | sarva-abhijñā-kuśala-pariśuddhaye pariṇāmayati | dharma-vi-mati-vinivartanāya pariṇāmayati | yathā buddha-śāsana-avacareṣu pariṇāmayati | śrāvaka-praty-eka-buddheṣu ca tathā bodhi-satvaḥ sarva-satveṣu tat-kuśala-mūlaṃ pariṇāmayati ||
body.translated_text: Having thus dedicated that wholesome root for the sake of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, he dedicates that wholesome root thus to all <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> who follow the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching: 'Those beings who hear even a single moment's snap of the word "<s>Buddha</s>," or the word "<s>Dharma</s>," or who attend upon the noble <s>Saṅgha</s> — their wholesome root he dedicates to unsurpassed perfect awakening; he dedicates it for the fulfillment of <s>Buddha</s>-recollection; he dedicates it for the practice of <s>Dharma</s>-recollection; he dedicates it for reverence toward the noble <s>Saṅgha</s>; he dedicates it for the swift seeing of the <s>Buddha</s>; he dedicates it for the purification of mind; he dedicates it for the penetration of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>; he dedicates it for the practice of immeasurable virtues; he dedicates it for the purification of all higher knowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) and wholesome [qualities]; he dedicates it for the removal of doubts about the <s>Dharma</s>.' Just as he dedicates to those who follow the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching and to the <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, so too the <s>bodhisattva</s> dedicates that wholesome root to all beings.

body.text: yad idaṃ nairayika-mārga-vinivartanāya pariṇāmayati | tiryag-yoni-vyavacchedāya pariṇāmayati | yama-loka-upaccheda-sukhāya pariṇāmayati | nir-avaśeṣa-sarva-apāya-gaty-upapatti-vyavacchedāya pariṇāmayati ||
body.translated_text: Namely, he dedicates it for turning back from the path of the hells; he dedicates it for cutting off [rebirth in] the animal realm; he dedicates it for the happiness of eliminating the world of <s>Yama</s>; he dedicates it for the complete cutting off of birth in all lower destinies without remainder.

body.text: teṣāṃ ca sarva-satvānām an-uttara-bodhi-chanda-vivardhanatāyai pariṇāmayati | adhyāśaya-sarva-jñatā-citta-lābhāya pariṇāmayati | sarva-buddha-dharma-a-pratikṣepāya pariṇāmayati | aty-anta-sukha-sarva-jñatā-bhūmi-saṃvartanāya pariṇāmayati | aty-anta-sarva-satva-viśuddhaye pariṇāmayati | sarva-satvānām an-anta-jñāna-adhigamāya pariṇāmayati | pe ||
body.translated_text: And he dedicates it for the increase of the aspiration toward unsurpassed awakening of all those beings; he dedicates it for the attainment of the mind of omniscience through higher aspiration; he dedicates it for the non-rejection of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>; he dedicates it for reaching the stage of omniscience that brings about supreme happiness; he dedicates it for the supreme purification of all beings; he dedicates it for the attainment of infinite knowledge by all beings. [Abbreviation.]

body.text: tasya yat kiñ-cic cīvara-piṇḍa-pāta-śayana-āsana-glāna-pratyaya-bhaiṣajya-gamana-āgamana-śarīra-upasthāna-niṣadya-ādi-niṣevaṇa-āyatanānāṃ pravartana-karma īryā-patha-adhiṣṭhānam īryā-pathasya + a-vikopanaṃ kāya-karma vāk-karma manas-karma sa-curitaṃ ṣaṇṇām indriyāṇāṃ saṃvaraḥ sva-śarīra-āchādana-mardana-snāna-karma | aśita-pīta-khāditaṃ saṃmiñjita-prasārita-avalokita-vilokita-supta-jāgarita-sva-śarīra-gata-upasthānaṃ sarvam etad bodhi-satvasya sarva-jñatā-ālambana-prayuktasya na kiñ-cid a-pariṇāmitaṃ sarva-jñatāyāṃ sarva-satva-hita-sukha-cittasya || pe ||
body.translated_text: Whatever activities he undertakes — robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, medicine as requisites for illness, coming and going, attending to the body, sitting and the like, engaging in the domains [of the senses], the performance of activities, the establishment of deportment, the non-disruption of deportment, bodily action, verbal action, mental action and conduct, the restraint of the six faculties, the covering, rubbing, and bathing of his own body; eating, drinking, and chewing, bending and stretching, looking forward and looking around, sleeping and waking, attending to his own body — all of this for the <s>bodhisattva</s> who is engaged with omniscience as his object, who has the mind of welfare and happiness for all beings — nothing is left undedicated to omniscience. [Abbreviation.]

body.text: sarva-jagat-paritrāṇa-manaso nitya-udyukta-kuśala-mūlasya mada-pramāda-vyativṛttasya || pe ||
body.translated_text: For one whose mind is intent on the rescue of the entire world, who is ever exerting himself in wholesome roots, who has gone beyond intoxication and heedlessness — [Abbreviation.]

body.text: sarva-kleśa-parāṅ-mukhasya sarva-bodhi-satva-anuśikṣaṇa-cetasaḥ sarva-jñatā-mārga-a-pratihatasya jñāna-bhūmi-niṣevaṇasya paṇḍita-saṃvāsa-abhiratasya | pe ||
body.translated_text: For one who has turned away from all afflictions, whose mind follows the training of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, who is unobstructed on the path of omniscience, who dwells on the ground of knowledge, who delights in the company of the wise — [Abbreviation.]

body.text: madhu-kara iva kuśala-mūla-saṃbharaṇasya sarva-jagad-uccalita-santānasya + an-abhiniviṣṭa-sarva-saṃskārasya | pe ||
body.translated_text: For one who gathers wholesome roots like a honey-bee, whose continuum is stirred by the entire world, who is unattached to all formations — [Abbreviation.]

body.text: antaśaḥ śvasv api tad anyeṣv api tiryag-yoni-gateṣv eka-odana-unmiñjitam eka-ālopaṃ vā parityajati | su-gatāv upapattiṣu tat sarvaṃ teṣām eva hitāya teṣām eva parimocanāya pariṇāmayati | tasyās tiryag-yones tasmād duṣkha-ārṇavāt tasmād duṣkha-upādānāt tasmād duṣkha-skandhāt tasmād duṣkhā-vedanāyāḥ | tasmād duṣkha-upacayāt tasmād duṣkha-abhisaṃskārāt tasmād duṣkha-nidānāt tato duṣkha-mūlāt tasmād duṣkha-āyatanāt teṣāṃ satvānāṃ vinivartanāya pariṇāmayati tad-ārambaṇena ca sarva-satva-ārambaṇī-karoti manasi-karoti | tatra kuśala-mūle pūrvaṅ-gamī-karoti | yad idaṃ sarva-jñatāyāṃ pariṇāmayati | bodhi-citta-utpādena pratigṛhṇāti | tatra kuśala-mūlam upanayati | saṃsāra-kāntārād vinivartayati | an-āvaraṇena buddha-sukhena + abhimukhī-karoti | saṃsāra-sāgarād unmajjayati | buddha-dharma-prayuktāya maitryā spharati + ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: Even to a dog, or to other beings gone to animal births, he gives a single morsel of rice or a single mouthful. He dedicates all [merit from] rebirths in happy destinies for the benefit of those very [beings], for the liberation of those very [beings]. From that animal birth, from that ocean of suffering, from that clinging to suffering, from that aggregate of suffering, from that feeling of suffering, from that accumulation of suffering, from that formation of suffering, from that cause of suffering, from that root of suffering, from that base of suffering — he dedicates [the merit] for turning those beings away [from suffering], and with that as the object, he makes all beings the object [of his practice] and attends to them mentally. Therein, he makes the wholesome root primary — namely, he dedicates it to omniscience. He embraces it with the generation of <s>bodhicitta</s>. He leads [beings] toward that wholesome root. He turns [them] away from the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>. He directs [them] toward unobstructed <s>Buddha</s>-happiness. He lifts [them] out of the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>. He pervades [them] with <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) yoked to the <s>Buddha-dharma</s>.' And so on.

body.text: imāś ca suvarṇa-bhāsa-uktā maitrī-karuṇā-garbhā gāthāḥ sarvā ādarataḥ samanvāhṛtya bhāvayitavyā antaśo vacasā + api ||
body.translated_text: And these verses spoken in the <s>Suvarṇabhāsottama</s>, pregnant with <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) — all of them should be respectfully taken up and cultivated, even if only verbally.

body.text: suvarṇa-bhāsa-uttama-dundubhena śāmyantu duṣkhās tri-sahasra-loke | apāya-duṣkhā yama-loka-duṣkhā dāridrya-duṣkhāś ca iha tri-loke ||
body.translated_text: By the supreme drum of the <s>Suvarṇabhāsa</s>, may sufferings be pacified in the three-thousandfold world — the sufferings of the lower destinies, the sufferings of <s>Yama</s>'s realm, and the sufferings of poverty here in the triple world.

body.text: anena ca + u dundubhi-ghoṣa-nādinā śāmyantu sarva-vyasanāni loke | bhavantu satvā hy a-bhaya-āhatā tathā yathā + a-bhayāḥ śānta-bhayāḥ muni-indrāḥ ||
body.translated_text: And by the sound of this drum's resounding, may all calamities in the world be pacified. May beings become free from the strike of fear, just as the Lords of Sages are fearless, with fears stilled.

body.text: yathā + eva sarva-ārya-guṇa-upapannāḥ saṃsāra-sarva-jña-mahā-samudrāḥ | tathā + eva bhontū guṇa-sāgarāḥ prajāḥ samādhi-bodhy-aṅga-guṇair upetāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Just as [the <s>Buddhas</s>] are endowed with all noble qualities, oceans of omniscience in <s>saṃsāra</s> — just so, may beings become oceans of virtues, endowed with the qualities of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and the limbs of awakening.

body.text: anena ca + u dundubhi-ghoṣa-nādinā bhavantu brahma-svara sarva-satvāḥ | spṛśantu buddhatva-vara-agra-bodhiṃ pravartayantū śubha-dharma-cakram ||
body.translated_text: And by the sound of this drum's resounding, may all beings become possessed of <s>Brahma</s>-voice. May they reach the supreme, foremost awakening of <s>Buddhahood</s>, and may they set in motion the auspicious <s>Dharma</s>-wheel!

body.text: tiṣṭhantu kalpāni a-cintiyāni deśentu dharmaṃ jagato hitāya | hanantu kleśān vidhamantu duṣkhān samentu rāgaṃ tatha doṣa moham ||
body.translated_text: May they remain for inconceivable <s>kalpas</s>; may they teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the welfare of the world. May they destroy the afflictions; may they dispel suffering; may they pacify desire, and likewise hatred and delusion.

body.text: ye satva tiṣṭhanti apāya-bhūmau ādīpta-saṃprajvalita-asthi-gātrāḥ | śṛṇvantu te dundubhi-saṃpravāditaṃ namo * astu buddhāya bhaṇantu vācam ||
body.translated_text: Whatever beings abide in the realms of lower destinies, their bones and limbs ablaze and burning — may they hear this sounding of the drum and utter the words: 'Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>!'

body.text: jāti-smarāḥ satvā bhavantu sarve jātī-śataṃ jāti-sahasra-koṭyaḥ | anusmarantū satataṃ muni-indrān śṛṇvantu teṣāṃ vacanaṃ hy udāraṃ ||
body.translated_text: May all beings become those who remember their [past] births — hundreds of births, thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of births. May they constantly recall the Lords of Sages and hear their noble words.

body.text: anena ca + u dundubhi-ghoṣa-nādinā labhantu buddhehi samāgamaṃ sadā | vivarjayantū khalu pāpa-karma carantu kuśalāni śubha-kriyāṇi ||
body.translated_text: And by the sound of this drum's resounding, may they always obtain the encounter with <s>Buddhas</s>. May they abandon evil <s>karma</s> and practice wholesome, auspicious deeds.

body.text: sarvatra kṣetreṣu ca sarva-prāṇināṃ sarve ca duṣkhāḥ praśamantu loke | ye satva vi-kala-indriya aṅga-hīnāḥ te sarvi sa-kala-indriya bhontu sāṃpratam ||
body.translated_text: In all fields, may all the sufferings of all living beings in the world be pacified. Whatever beings have impaired faculties or are missing limbs — may all of them become complete in their faculties right now.

body.text: ye vyādhitā dur-bala-kṣīṇa-gātrā nis-trāṇa-bhūtāḥ śayitā diśāsu | te sarvi mucyantu ca vyādhito laghu labhantu ca + ārogya bala-indriyāṇi ||
body.translated_text: Whatever beings are sick, weak, with wasted limbs, lying helpless in various directions — may all of them be swiftly freed from illness and may they obtain health, strength, and [vigorous] faculties.

body.text: ye rāja-caura-bhaṭa tarjita vadhya-prāptā nānā-vidhair bhaya-śatair vyasana-upapannāḥ | te sarvi satva vyasana-āgata-duṣkhitā hi mucyantu tair bhaya-śataiḥ paramaiḥ su-ghoraiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Those who are threatened by kings, thieves, and soldiers, who have reached the point of execution, afflicted by hundreds of various fears and calamities — may all those beings, afflicted and come to calamity, be freed from those hundreds of supremely terrible fears.

body.text: ye tāḍitā bandhana-baddha-pīḍitā vividheṣu vyasaneṣu ca saṃsthitāhi | an-eka āyāsa-sahasra ākulā vicitra-bhaya-dāruṇa-śoka-prāptāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Those who are beaten, bound in fetters and oppressed, situated in various calamities, bewildered by thousands of manifold troubles, stricken with diverse, terrible, and dreadful sorrows —

body.text: te sarvi mucyantv iha bandhanebhyaḥ saṃtāḍitā mucyiṣu tāḍanebhyaḥ | vadhyāś ca saṃyujyiṣu jīvitena vyasana-āgatā nir-bhaya bhontu sarve ||
body.translated_text: may all of them here be freed from bondage; may those who are beaten be freed from beatings; may those condemned to death be reunited with life; and may all who have fallen into calamity become fearless.

body.text: ye satva kṣut-tarṣa-pipāsa-pīḍitā labhantu te bhojana-pāna-citram | andhāś ca paśyantu vicitra-rūpāṃ badhirāś ca śṛṇvantu mano-jña-ghoṣān ||
body.translated_text: Whatever beings are afflicted by hunger, thirst, and craving — may they obtain varied food and drink. May the blind see varied forms, and may the deaf hear delightful sounds.

body.text: nagnāś ca vastrāṇi labhantu citrāṃ daridra-satvāś ca nidhiṃ labhantu | prabhūta-dhana-dhānya-vicitra-ratnaiḥ sarve ca satvāḥ sukhino bhavantu ||
body.translated_text: May the naked obtain fine garments; may destitute beings obtain treasure. May all beings become happy, with abundant wealth, grain, and various jewels.

body.text: mā kasya-cid bhāvatu duṣkha-vedanāḥ saukhya-anvitāḥ satva bhavantu sarve | abhirūpa-prāsādika-saumya-rūpā an-eka sukha saṃcita nitya bhontu ||
body.translated_text: May no one experience painful feelings; may all beings be attended by happiness. May they be beautiful, gracious, and gentle in form; may they always be endowed with manifold accumulated joys.

body.text: manasa-anna-pānāḥ su-samṛddha-puṇyāḥ saha citta-mātreṇa bhavantu teṣāṃ | vīṇā mṛdaṅgāḥ paṇavāḥ su-ghoṣakāḥ utsā sarāḥ puṣkariṇī taḍāgāḥ ||
body.translated_text: May food and drink [appearing] by mental [wish], and merit abundantly flourishing, arise for them by the mere [power of] thought. May <s>vīṇās</s>, <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, and sweetly-sounding drums, springs, pools, lotus ponds, and lakes —

body.text: suvarṇa-padma-utpala-padminīś ca saha citta-mātreṇa bhavantu teṣām | gandhaṃ ca mālyaṃ ca vilepanaṃ ca vāsaś ca cūrṇaṃ kusumaṃ vicitram ||
body.translated_text: and golden lotuses, blue lotuses, and lotus-groves arise for them by the mere [power of] thought; and fragrance, garlands, ointments, clothes, powder, and varied flowers.

body.text: triṣ-kāla-vṛkṣebhi pravarṣayantu gṛhṇantu te satva bhavantu hṛṣṭāḥ | kurvantu pūjāṃ daśasū diśāsu a-cintiyāṃ sarva-tathā-gatānām ||
body.translated_text: May trees bearing fruit in all three seasons rain [their bounty] down; may those beings take [of it] and become joyful. May they make inconceivable worship of all the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the ten directions.

body.text: sa bodhi-satvān atha śrāvakāṇāṃ dharmasya bodhi pratisṛṣṭi tasya | nīcāṃ gatiṃ satva vivarjayantu bhavantu aṣṭa-akṣaṇa-vīti-vṛttāḥ ||
body.translated_text: And [may they worship] the <s>bodhisattvas</s> and the <s>Śrāvakas</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the awakening and the gift thereof. May beings avoid the lower destinies and become free from the eight inopportune states.

body.text: āsādayantū jina-rājam uttamaṃ labhantu buddhehi samāgamaṃ sadā | sarvā striyo nitya narā bhavantu śūrāś ca vīrā vidu-paṇḍitāś ca ||
body.translated_text: May they attain the supreme King of Conquerors; may they always obtain encounter with <s>Buddhas</s>. May all women always become men — heroic, brave, learned, and wise.

body.text: te sarvi bodhāya carantu nityaṃ carantu te pāramitāsu ṣaṭsu | paśyantu buddhān daśasū diśāsu ratna-druma-indreṣu sukha-upaviṣṭān | vaiḍūrya-ratna-āsana-saṃniṣaṇṇān dharmāṃś ca śṛṇvantu prakāśyamānān | iti ||
body.translated_text: May they all constantly practice for awakening; may they practice the six <s>pāramitās</s>. May they behold the <s>Buddhas</s> in the ten directions, seated happily upon jewel-trees, seated upon thrones of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> gems, and may they hear the <s>Dharma</s> being proclaimed.

body.text: eṣā saṃkṣepato maitrī ||
body.translated_text: This is <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) in summary.

body.text: dveṣa-samudācāra-prati-pakṣaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The counter-agent to the active arising of hatred.

body.text: moha-anuśayasya pratītya-samutpāda-darśanaṃ prati-pakṣaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The counter-agent to the latent tendency of delusion is the seeing of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination).

body.text: tatra pratītya-samutpādaḥ śāli-stamba-sūtre * abhihitaḥ | tatra + ādhyātmikasya pratītya-samutpādasya hetu-upanibandhaḥ katamaḥ | yad idam a-vidyā-pratyayāḥ saṃskārā yāvaj jāti-pratyayaṃ jarā-maraṇam iti | a-vidyā cen na + abhaviṣyan na + eva saṃskārāḥ prājñāsyanta | evaṃ yāvad yadi jātir na + abhaviṣyan na jarā-maraṇaṃ prājñāsyata | atha satyām a-vidyāyāṃ saṃskārāṇām abhinirvṛttir bhavati | evaṃ yāvaj jātyāṃ satyāṃ jarā-maraṇasya + abhinirvṛttir bhavati | tatra + a-vidyāyā na + evaṃ bhavati | ahaṃ saṃskārān abhinirvartayāmi + iti | saṃskārāṇām apy evaṃ na bhavati | vayam a-vidyayā + abhinirvṛttā iti | evaṃ yāvaj jātyā na + evaṃ bhavati | ahaṃ jarā-maraṇam abhinirvartayāmi + iti | jarā-maraṇasya + api na + evaṃ bhavati | ahaṃ jātyā nirvṛtta iti |atha ca satyām a-vidyāyāṃ saṃskārāṇām abhinirvṛttir bhavati prādur-bhāvaḥ | evaṃ yāvaj jātyāṃ satyāṃ jarā-maraṇasya + abhinirvṛttir bhavati prādur-bhāvaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) is stated in the <s>Śālistamba-sūtra</s>. Therein, what is the causal connection (<s>hetu-upanibandha</s>) of internal dependent origination? It is this: conditioned by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) are <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), and so on up to: conditioned by <s>jāti</s> (birth) are <s>jarā-maraṇa</s> (old age and death). If <s>avidyā</s> did not exist, <s>saṃskāras</s> would not at all be known. Likewise, up to: if <s>jāti</s> did not exist, <s>jarā-maraṇa</s> would not be known. But when <s>avidyā</s> exists, the arising of <s>saṃskāras</s> occurs. Likewise, up to: when <s>jāti</s> exists, the arising of <s>jarā-maraṇa</s> occurs. Therein, <s>avidyā</s> does not think thus: 'I produce <s>saṃskāras</s>.' Nor do the <s>saṃskāras</s> think thus: 'We are produced by <s>avidyā</s>.' Likewise, up to: <s>jāti</s> does not think thus: 'I produce <s>jarā-maraṇa</s>.' Nor does <s>jarā-maraṇa</s> think thus: 'I am produced by <s>jāti</s>.' But when <s>avidyā</s> exists, the arising, the manifestation, of <s>saṃskāras</s> occurs. Likewise, up to: when <s>jāti</s> exists, the arising, the manifestation, of <s>jarā-maraṇa</s> occurs.

body.text: evam ādhyātmikasya pratītya-samutpādasya hetu-upanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus should the causal connection of internal dependent origination be seen.

body.text: katham ādhyātmikasya pratītya-samutpādasya pratyaya-upanibandho draṣṭavya iti | ṣaṇṇāṃ dhātūnāṃ samavāyāt | katam eṣāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ dhātūnāṃ samavāyāt | yad idaṃ pṛthivy--ap-tejo-vāyv-ākāśa-vijñāna-dhātūnāṃ samavāyād ādhyātmikasya pratītya-samutpādasya pratyaya-upanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: How should the conditional connection (<s>pratyaya-upanibandha</s>) of internal dependent origination be seen? Through the coming together of the six <s>dhātus</s> (elements). Through the coming together of which six <s>dhātus</s>? Namely, through the coming together of the <s>pṛthivī</s> (earth), <s>ap</s> (water), <s>tejas</s> (fire), <s>vāyu</s> (wind), <s>ākāśa</s> (space), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) <s>dhātus</s> should the conditional connection of internal dependent origination be seen.

body.text: tatra + ādhyātmikasya pratītya-samutpādasya pṛthivī-dhātuḥ katama iti | yo * ayaṃ kāyasya saṃśleṣataḥ kaṭhina-bhāvam abhinirvartayaty ayam ucyate pṛthivī-dhātuḥ | yaḥ kāyasya + anuparigrahaṃ kṛtyaṃ karoti ayam ucyate * ab-dhātuḥ | yaḥ kāyasya + aśita-pīta-bhakṣitaṃ paripācayati ayam ucyate tejo-dhātuḥ | yaḥ kāyasya + āśvāsa-praśvāsa-kṛtyaṃ karoty ayam ucyate vāyu-dhātuḥ | yaḥ kāyasya + antaḥ-sauṣirya-bhāvam abhinirvartayaty ayam ucyate ākāśa-dhātuḥ | yo nāma-rūpam abhinirvartayati naḍa-kalāpa-yogena pañca-vijñāna-kāya-saṃprayuktaṃ sa-āsravaṃ ca mano-vijñānam ayam ucyate vijñāna-dhātuḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the <s>pṛthivī-dhātu</s> (earth element) of internal dependent origination? That which, by cohering in the body, produces the quality of hardness — this is called the <s>pṛthivī-dhātu</s>. That which performs the function of holding the body together — this is called the <s>ap-dhātu</s> (water element). That which digests what is eaten, drunk, and consumed by the body — this is called the <s>tejo-dhātu</s> (fire element). That which performs the function of inhalation and exhalation in the body — this is called the <s>vāyu-dhātu</s> (wind element). That which produces the quality of internal hollowness in the body — this is called the <s>ākāśa-dhātu</s> (space element). That which produces <s>nāma-rūpa</s> (name-and-form), through the conjunction [functioning like] a bundle of reeds, comprising the five sense-consciousness groups and the defiled mental consciousness — this is called the <s>vijñāna-dhātu</s> (consciousness element).

body.text: a-satsu pratyayeṣu kāyasya + utpattir na bhavati | yadā + ādhyātmikaḥ pṛthivī-dhātur a-vikalo bhavaty evam ap-tejo-vāyv-ākāśa-vijñāna-dhātavaś ca + a-vikalā bhavanti | tataḥ sarveṣāṃ samavāyāt kāyasya + utpattir bhavati ||
body.translated_text: When the conditions are absent, the arising of the body does not occur. When the internal <s>pṛthivī-dhātu</s> is complete, and likewise the <s>ap</s>, <s>tejas</s>, <s>vāyu</s>, <s>ākāśa</s>, and <s>vijñāna-dhātus</s> are complete — then, from the coming together of all of them, the arising of the body occurs.

body.text: tatra pṛthivī-dhātor na + evaṃ bhavati | ahaṃ kāyasya kaṭhina-bhāvam abhinirvartayāmi + iti | ab-dhātor na + evaṃ bhavati | ahaṃ kāyasya + anuparigraha-kṛtyaṃ karomi + iti | tejo-dhātor na + evaṃ bhavati | ahaṃ kāyasya + aśita-pīta-khāditaṃ paripācayāmi + iti | vāyu-dhātor na + evaṃ bhavati | ahaṃ kāyasya + āśvāsa-praśvāsa-kṛtyaṃ karomi + iti | ākāśa-dhātor na + evaṃ bhavati | ahaṃ kāyasya + antaḥ saurṣiryaṃ karomi + iti | vijñāna-dhātor na + evaṃ bhavati | aham ebhiḥ pratyayair janita iti | atha ca satsv eṣu pratyayeṣu kāyasya + utpattir bhavati | tatra pṛthivī-dhātur na + ātmā na satvo na jīvo na jantur na manu-jo na mānavo na strī na pumān na na-puṃsakaṃ | na ca + ahaṃ | na mama | na ca apy anyasya kasya-cit | evam ab-dhātus tejo-dhātur vāyu-dhātur ākāśa-dhātur vijñāna-dhātur na satvo na jīvo na jantur na manu-jo na mānavo na strī na pumān na na-puṃsakaṃ na ca + ahaṃ na mama na ca + apy anyasya kasya-cit ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the <s>pṛthivī-dhātu</s> does not think thus: 'I produce the quality of hardness in the body.' The <s>ap-dhātu</s> does not think thus: 'I perform the function of holding the body together.' The <s>tejo-dhātu</s> does not think thus: 'I digest what is eaten, drunk, and consumed by the body.' The <s>vāyu-dhātu</s> does not think thus: 'I perform the function of inhalation and exhalation in the body.' The <s>ākāśa-dhātu</s> does not think thus: 'I produce internal hollowness in the body.' The <s>vijñāna-dhātu</s> does not think thus: 'I am produced by these conditions.' But when these conditions exist, the arising of the body occurs. Therein, the <s>pṛthivī-dhātu</s> is not a self, not a being, not a living being, not a creature, not a human, not a person, not a woman, not a man, not neuter; it is not 'I,' not 'mine,' and not anyone else's either. Likewise, the <s>ap-dhātu</s>, <s>tejo-dhātu</s>, <s>vāyu-dhātu</s>, <s>ākāśa-dhātu</s>, and <s>vijñāna-dhātu</s> are not a being, not a living being, not a creature, not a human, not a person, not a woman, not a man, not neuter; they are not 'I,' not 'mine,' and not anyone else's either.

body.text: tatra + a-vidyā katamā | yā eṣv eva ṣaṭsu dhātuṣv eka-saṃjñā piṇḍa-saṃjñā nitya-saṃjñā dhruva-saṃjñā śāśvata-saṃjñā sukha-saṃjñā ātma-saṃjñā satva-jīva-manu-ja-mānava-saṃjñā | ahaṃ-kāra-mama-kāra-saṃjñā | evam-ādi vividham a-jñānam iyam ucyate * a-vidyā + iti | evam a-vidyāyāṃ satyāṃ viṣayeṣu rāga-dveṣa-mohāḥ pravartante | tatra ye rāga-dveṣa-mohā viṣayeṣv amī ucyante saṃskārā iti | vastu-prati-vijñaptir vijñānaṃ | vijñāna-saha-jāś catvāro * a-rūpiṇa upādāna-skandhās tan nāma-rūpaṃ | catvāri ca mahā-bhūtāni ca + upādāya upādāya r ūpam aikadhyam abhisaṃkṣipya tan nāma-rūpaṃ | nāma-rūpa-saṃniśritāni + indriyāṇi ṣaḍ-āyatanaṃ | trayāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ saṃnipātaḥ sparśaḥ | sparśa-anubhavanā vedanā | vedanā-adhyavasānaṃ tṛṣṇā | tṛṣṇā vaipulyam upādānaṃ | upādāna-nirjātaṃ punar-bhava-janakaṃ karma | bhavaḥ | tad-dhetuka-skandha-prādur-bhāvo jātiḥ | skandha-paripāko jarā vināśo maraṇaṃ | mriyamāṇasya mūḍhasya sva-abhiṣvaṅgasya + antar-dāhaḥ śokaḥ | lālapyanaṃ paridevaḥ | pañca-vijñāna-kāya-saṃprayuktam a-śāta-anubhavanaṃ duṣkhaṃ | manasi-kāra-saṃprayuktaṃ mānasaṃ duṣkhaṃ daurmanasyam | ye ca + anyae evam-ādaya upakleśās tae upāyāsāḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: Therein, what is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance)? It is, with regard to these very six elements, the perception of unity, the perception of a solid mass, the perception of permanence, the perception of stability, the perception of eternality, the perception of happiness, the perception of a self, the perception of a being, a living being, a person, a human. It is the perception of 'I' and 'mine'. Such manifold ignorance is called <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). Thus, when <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) exists, attachment, aversion, and delusion arise with regard to objects. Therein, those attachment, aversion, and delusion with regard to objects are called <s>saṃskārāḥ</s> (formations). The cognition of an object is <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). The four formless aggregates of clinging that arise together with <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) — that is <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form). And the four great elements and the form derived from them, compressed into a unity — that is <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form). The sense faculties dependent on <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) are <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (the six sense-bases). The conjunction of three factors is <s>sparśa</s> (contact). The experience of <s>sparśa</s> (contact) is <s>vedanā</s> (feeling). The attachment to <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) is <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving). The proliferation of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) is <s>upādāna</s> (clinging). The action born from <s>upādāna</s> (clinging) that generates renewed existence is <s>bhava</s> (becoming). The manifestation of the aggregates caused by that is <s>jāti</s> (birth). The maturation of the aggregates is aging, their destruction is death. The inner burning of one who is dying, deluded, and attached to self — that is grief. Lamentation is wailing. The experience of displeasure connected with the five sense-consciousness groups is <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering). Mental suffering connected with mental attention is dejection. And whatever other such secondary afflictions — those are miseries. And so forth.

body.text: punar a-paraṃ tatve * a-pratipattiḥ mithyā pratipattiḥ a-jñānam a-vidyā | evam a-vidyāyāṃ satyāṃ tri-vidhāḥ saṃskārāḥ abhinirvartante | puṇya-upagā a-puṇya-upagā āniñjya-upagāś ca + imae ucyante * a-vidyā-pratyayāḥ saṃskārā iti | puṇya-upagānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ puṇya-upagam eva vijñānaṃ bhavati | a-puṇya-upagānāṃ saṃskārāṇām a-puṇya-upagam eva vijñānaṃ bhavati | āniñjya-upagānāṃ saṃskārāṇām āniñjya-upagam eva vijñānaṃ bhavati | idam ucyate saṃskāra-pratyayaṃ vijñānam iti | evaṃ nāma-rūpaṃ | nāma-rūpa-vivṛddhyā ṣaḍbhir āyatana-dvāraiḥ kṛtya-kriyāḥ pravartante | tan nāma-rūpa-pratyayaṃ ṣaḍ-āyatanam ity ucyate | ṣaḍbhya āyatanebhyaḥ ṣaṭ sparśa-kāyāḥ pravartante * ayaṃ ṣaḍ-āyatana-pratyayaḥ sparśa ity ucyate | yaj-jātīyaḥ sparśo bhavati taj-jātīyā vedanā pravartate | iyaṃ sparśa-pratyayā vedanā + ity ucyate | yas tāṃ vedayati viśeṣeṇa + āsvādayati | abhinandaty adhyavasyaty atyadhitiṣṭhati | sā vedanā-pratyayā tṛṣṇā + ity ucyate | āsvādana-abhinandana-adhyavasānaṃ | mā me priya-rūpa-śāta-rūpair viyogo bhavatv iti | a-parityāgo bhūyo bhūyaś ca prārthanā | idaṃ tṛṣṇā-pratyayam upādānam ity ucyate | evaṃ prārthayamānaḥ punar-bhava-janakaṃ karma samutthāpayati kāyena vācā manasā | ayam upādāna-pratyayo bhava ity ucyate | yā karma-nirjātānāṃ skandhānām abhinirvṛttiḥ sā bhava-pratyayā jātir ity ucyate | yo jāty-abhinirvṛttānāṃ skandhānām upacaya-paripākād vināśo bhavati | tad idaṃ jāti-pratyayaṃ jarā-maraṇam ucyate || pe ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, non-comprehension of reality, wrong comprehension, ignorance — that is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). Thus, when <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) exists, three kinds of <s>saṃskārāḥ</s> (formations) are produced: those tending toward merit, those tending toward demerit, and those tending toward the imperturbable — these are called '<s>saṃskārāḥ</s> (formations) conditioned by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).' For formations tending toward merit, the <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) itself tends toward merit. For formations tending toward demerit, the <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) itself tends toward demerit. For formations tending toward the imperturbable, the <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) itself tends toward the imperturbable. This is called '<s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) conditioned by <s>saṃskārāḥ</s> (formations).' Likewise <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form). Through the development of <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form), activities proceed through the six sense-base doors — that is called '<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (the six sense-bases) conditioned by <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form).' From the six sense-bases, six groups of contact arise — this is called '<s>sparśa</s> (contact) conditioned by <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (the six sense-bases).' Whatever the kind of contact, that kind of <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) arises — this is called '<s>vedanā</s> (feeling) conditioned by <s>sparśa</s> (contact).' One who feels it especially relishes it, delights in it, adheres to it, and clings to it — that is called '<s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) conditioned by <s>vedanā</s> (feeling).' The relishing, delighting, and adhering — 'May I not be separated from what is dear and pleasant!' — the non-relinquishing and repeated longing — this is called '<s>upādāna</s> (clinging) conditioned by <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving).' Thus longing, one generates action that produces renewed existence by body, speech, and mind — this is called '<s>bhava</s> (becoming) conditioned by <s>upādāna</s> (clinging).' The production of the aggregates born from action — that is called '<s>jāti</s> (birth) conditioned by <s>bhava</s> (becoming).' The destruction that occurs from the growth and maturation of the aggregates produced by <s>jāti</s> (birth) — that is called '<s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (aging-and-death) conditioned by <s>jāti</s> (birth).' And so forth.

body.text: evam ayaṃ dvādaśa-aṅgaḥ pratītya-samutpādo * anyo-nya-hetuko * anyo-nya-pratyayato | na + eva + a-nityo na nityo | na saṃskṛto na + a-saṃskṛto | na vedayitā | na kṣaya-dharmo na nirodha-dharmo | na vi-rāga-dharmo | an-ādi-kāra-pravṛtto * an-udbhinno * anupravartate nadī-srota-vat ||
body.translated_text: Thus this twelve-limbed <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), mutually caused and mutually conditioned, is neither impermanent nor permanent, neither conditioned nor unconditioned, without an experiencer, neither subject to destruction nor subject to cessation, nor subject to dispassion; it has been proceeding since beginningless time, uninterrupted, continuing like the current of a river.

body.text: atha ca + imāny asya dvādaśa-aṅgasya pratītya-samutpādasya catvāri aṅgāni saṃghāta-kriyāyai hetutvena pravartante | katamāni catvāri | yad uta | a-vidyā tṛṣṇā karma vijñānaṃ ca | tatra vijñānaṃ bīja-sva-bhāvatvena hetuḥ | karma kṣetra-sva-bhāvatvena hetuḥ | a-vidyā tṛṣṇā ca kleśa-sva-bhāvatvena hetuḥ | karma-kleśā vijñāna-bījaṃ saṃjanayanti | tatra karma vijñāna-bījasya kṣetra-kāryaṃ karoti | tṛṣṇā vijñāna-bījaṃ snehayati | a-vidyā vijñāna-bījam avakirati | a-satāṃ yeṣāṃ pratyayānāṃ bījasya + abhinirvṛttir na bhavati ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, four limbs of this twelve-limbed <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) function as causes for the activity of combination. Which four? Namely: <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), <s>karma</s> (action), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). Therein, <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is a cause by virtue of being a seed in nature. <s>Karma</s> (action) is a cause by virtue of being a field in nature. <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) and <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) are causes by virtue of being afflictions in nature. Action and afflictions generate the seed of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). Therein, <s>karma</s> (action) performs the function of a field for the seed of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). <s>Tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) moistens the seed of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) scatters the seed of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). When these conditions are absent, the seed does not come into being.

body.text: tatra karmaṇo na + evaṃ bhavati | ahaṃ vijñāna-bījasya kṣetra-kāryaṃ karomi + iti | tṛṣṇāyā api na + evaṃ bhavati |ahaṃ vijñāna-bījaṃ snehayāmi + iti | a-vidyāyā api na + evaṃ bhavati | ahaṃ vijñāna-bījam avakirāmi + iti | vijñāna-bījasya + api na + evaṃ bhavaty aham ebhiḥ pratyayair janita iti | api tu vijñāna-bīje karma-kṣetra-pratiṣṭhite tṛṣṇā-sneha-abhiṣyandite * a-vidyā-avakīrṇe tatra tatra + utpatty-āyatana-sandhau mātuḥ kukṣau virohati | nāma-rūpa-aṅkurasya + abhinirvṛttir bhavati | sa ca nāma-rūpa-aṅkuro na svayaṃ-kṛto na para-kṛto na + ubhaya-kṛto na + īśvara-ādi-nirmito na kāla-pariṇāmito na ca + eka-kāraṇa-adhīno na + apy a-hetu-samutpannaḥ | atha ca mātā-pitṛ-saṃyogād ṛtu-samavāyād anyeṣāṃ ca pratyayānāṃ samavāyād āsvāda-anupraviddhaṃ vijñāna-bījaṃ mātuḥ kukṣau nāma-rūpa-aṅkura-bījam abhinirvartayati | a-svāmikeṣu dharmeṣv a-mameṣv a-parigraheṣv a-praty-arthikeṣv ākāśa-sameṣu māyā-lakṣaṇa-sva-bhāveṣu hetu-pratyayānām a-vaikalyāt ||
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>karma</s> (action) does not think thus: 'I perform the function of a field for the seed of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness).' <s>Tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) too does not think thus: 'I moisten the seed of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness).' <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) too does not think thus: 'I scatter the seed of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness).' The seed of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) too does not think: 'I am generated by these conditions.' But when the seed of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is established in the field of <s>karma</s> (action), moistened by the moisture of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), and scattered by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), then at the juncture of the place of birth, here and there, it sprouts in the mother's womb. The sprout of <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) comes into being. And that sprout of <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) is not self-made, not other-made, not made by both, not created by <s>Īśvara</s> (a lord) or the like, not transformed by time; it does not depend on a single cause, nor does it arise without a cause. But from the union of mother and father, from the conjunction of the season, and from the conjunction of other conditions, the seed of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) infused with relishing produces the sprout-seed of <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) in the mother's womb — in <s>dharmas</s> that are ownerless, without 'mine,' without possessor, without opponent, equal to space, having the nature of an illusion — through the non-deficiency of causes and conditions.

body.text: tad yathā pañcabhiḥ kāraṇaiś cakṣur-vijñānam utpadyate | katamaiḥ pañcabhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Just as eye-consciousness arises from five causes — which five?

body.text: cakṣuś ca pratītya rūpaṃ ca + ālokaṃ ca + ākāśaṃ taj-jaṃ ca manasi-kāraṃ ca pratītya + utpadyate cakṣur-vijñānaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Dependent on the eye, form, light, space, and the mental attention born from them, eye-consciousness arises.

body.text: tatra cakṣur-vijñānasya cakṣur-āśraya-kṛtyaṃ karoti | rūpam ārambaṇa-kṛtyaṃ karoti | āloko * avabhāsa-kṛtyaṃ karoti | ākāśam an-āvaraṇa-kṛtyaṃ karoti | taj-ja-manasi-kāraḥ samanvāhāra-kṛtyaṃ karoti | asatsv eṣu pratyayeṣu cakṣur-vijñānaṃ na + utpadyate ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the eye performs the function of support for eye-consciousness. Form performs the function of the object. Light performs the function of illumination. Space performs the function of non-obstruction. The mental attention born from them performs the function of bringing together. When these conditions are absent, eye-consciousness does not arise.

body.text: yadā cakṣur ādhyātmikam āyatanam a-vikalaṃ bhavati | evaṃ rūpa-āloka-ākāśa-taj-ja-manasi-kārāś ca + a-vikalā bhavanti | tataḥ sarva-samavāyāc cakṣur-vijñānasya + utpattir bhavati ||
body.translated_text: When the internal sense-base of the eye is intact, and likewise form, light, space, and the mental attention born from them are intact, then from the conjunction of all these, the arising of eye-consciousness occurs.

body.text: tatra cakṣuṣo na + evaṃ bhavati | ahaṃ cakṣur-vijñānasya + āśraya-kṛtyaṃ karomi + iti | rūpasya + api na + evaṃ bhavati | ahaṃ cakṣur-vijñānasya + ārambaṇa-kṛtyaṃ karomi + iti | ālokasya + api na + evaṃ bhavati | aham avabhāsa-kṛtyaṃ karomi + iti | ākāśasya + api na + evaṃ bhavati | ahaṃ cakṣur-vijñānasya + an-āvaraṇa-kṛtyaṃ karomi + iti | taj-ja-manasi-kārasya + api na evaṃ bhavati | ahaṃ cakṣur-vijñānasya samanvāhāra-kṛtyaṃ karomi + iti | cakṣur-vijñānasya + api na + evaṃ bhavati | aham ebhiḥ pratyayair janita iti | atha ca punaḥ satsv eṣu pratyayeṣu cakṣur-vijñānasya + utpattir bhavati prādur-bhāvaḥ | evaṃ śeṣāṇām indriyāṇāṃ yathā-āyogaṃ kartavyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the eye does not think thus: 'I perform the function of support for eye-consciousness.' Form too does not think thus: 'I perform the function of the object for eye-consciousness.' Light too does not think thus: 'I perform the function of illumination.' Space too does not think thus: 'I perform the function of non-obstruction for eye-consciousness.' The mental attention born from them too does not think thus: 'I perform the function of bringing together for eye-consciousness.' Eye-consciousness too does not think thus: 'I am generated by these conditions.' But when these conditions exist, the arising, the manifestation of eye-consciousness occurs. In the same way, one should apply this to the remaining sense faculties as appropriate.

body.text: tatra na kaś-cid dharmo * asmāl lokāt paraṃ lokaṃ saṃkrāmati | asti ca karma-phala-prativijñaptiḥ | hetu-pratyayānām a-vaikalyāt | yathā + agnir upādāna-vaikalyān na jvalati | evam eva karma-kleśa-janitaṃ vijñāna-bījaṃ tatra tatra + utpatty-āyatana-prati-sandhau mātuḥ kukṣau nāma-rūpa-aṅkuram abhinirvartayati | a-svāmikeṣu dharmeṣv a-mameṣv a-parigraheṣv a-praty-arthikeṣv ākāśa-sameṣu māyā-lakṣaṇa-sva-bhāveṣu hetu-pratyayānām a-vaikalyāt ||
body.translated_text: Therein, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever transmigrates from this world to the next world. Yet there is the cognition of the fruit of action, through the non-deficiency of causes and conditions. Just as fire does not blaze when fuel is lacking — in the same way, the seed of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), generated by action and afflictions, produces the sprout of <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) in the mother's womb at the juncture of the place of birth, here and there — in <s>dharmas</s> that are ownerless, without 'mine,' without possessor, without opponent, equal to space, having the nature of an illusion — through the non-deficiency of causes and conditions.

body.text: tan na + ādhyātmikaḥ pratītya-samutpādaḥ pañcabhiḥ kāraṇair draṣṭavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The internal <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) should be seen through five characteristics.

body.text: katamaiḥ pañcabhiḥ | na śāśvatato na + ucchedato na saṃkrāntitaḥ | parītta-hetuno vipula-phala-abhinirvṛttitas tat-sadṛśa-anuprabandhataś ca + iti ||
body.translated_text: Which five? Not from the standpoint of eternalism, not from the standpoint of annihilationism, not from the standpoint of transmigration, from the production of extensive fruit from a limited cause, and from the continuity of what is similar to that.

body.text: kathaṃ na śāśvatataḥ | yasmād anye māraṇa-antikāḥ skandhā anyae aupapatty-aṃśikāḥ | na tu yae eva māraṇa-antikāḥ skandhās tae eva + aupapatty-aṃśikāḥ skandhā | api tu māraṇa-antikāś ca skandhā nirudhyamānā aupapatty-aṃśikāḥ skandhāś ca prādur-bhavanti | ato na śāśvatataḥ ||
body.translated_text: How not from the standpoint of eternalism? Because the aggregates at the time of death are different from the aggregates at the moment of rebirth. It is not that the very aggregates at the time of death are the aggregates at the moment of rebirth. Rather, the aggregates at the time of death cease and the aggregates at the moment of rebirth manifest. Therefore, not from the standpoint of eternalism.

body.text: kathaṃ na + ucchedataḥ | na ca niruddheṣu skandheṣu aupapatty-aṃśikāḥ skandhāḥ prādur-bhavanti na + apy a-niruddheṣu | api tu māraṇa-antikāś ca skandhā nirudhyante aupapatty-aṃśikāś ca prādur-bhavanti | tulā-daṇḍa-unnāma-avanāma-vat | ato na + ucchedataḥ ||
body.translated_text: How not from the standpoint of annihilationism? The aggregates at the moment of rebirth do not manifest when the aggregates have ceased, nor when they have not ceased. Rather, the aggregates at the time of death cease and the aggregates at the moment of rebirth manifest — like the rising and falling of the beam of a balance. Therefore, not from the standpoint of annihilationism.

body.text: kathaṃ na saṃtrāntitaḥ | vi-sadṛśāt satva-nikāyād * dhi sa-bhāgāḥ skandhā jāty-antare * abhinirvartante | ato na saṃkrāntitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: How not from the standpoint of transmigration? Because from a dissimilar class of beings, homogeneous aggregates are produced in another birth. Therefore, not from the standpoint of transmigration.

body.text: kathaṃ parītta-hetuto vipula-phala-abhinirvṛttitaḥ parīttaṃ karma kriyate | vipulaḥ phala-vipāko * anubhūyate | ataḥ parītta-hetuto vipula-phala-abhinivṛttiḥ ||
body.translated_text: How is there production of extensive fruit from a limited cause? A limited action is performed, yet an extensive ripening of fruit is experienced. Therefore, the production of extensive fruit from a limited cause.

body.text: kathaṃ tat-sādṛśa-anuprabandhataḥ | yathā vedanīyaṃ karma kriyate | tathā vedanīyo vipāko * anubhūyate | atas tat-sadṛśa-anuprabandhataś ca + iti ||
body.translated_text: How from the continuity of what is similar? As the action is performed to be experienced, so a similar ripening is experienced. Therefore, from the continuity of what is similar.

body.text: yaḥ kaś-cid bhadanta śāriputra + imaṃ pratītya-samutpādaṃ bhagavatā samyak-praṇītam evaṃ yathā-bhūtaṃ samyak-prajñayā satata-samitam a-jīvaṃ nir-jīvaṃ yathā-vad a-viparītam a-jātam a-bhūtam a-kṛtam a-saṃskṛtam a-pratigham an-āvaraṇaṃ śivam a-bhayam a-hāryam a-vyayam a-vyupaśamam a-sva-bhāvaṃ paśyati | a-satyatas tucchata ṛktato * a-sārato * aghato * a-nityato duṣkhataḥ śūnyato * an-ātmanaś ca samanupaśyati | sa na pūrva-antaṃ pratisarati | kim aham abhūvam atīte * adhvany āho svin na + abhūvam atīte * adhvani | ko nv aham abhūvam atīte * adhvani ||
body.translated_text: Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, whoever sees this <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), well set forth by the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One), as it truly is, with right <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), constantly and continuously, as lifeless, without a living being, as it really is, without error, as unborn, as not having come into being, as unmade, as unconditioned, as unobstructed, as unimpeded, as auspicious, as fearless, as indestructible, as imperishable, as unceasing, as without own-nature — and sees it as unreal, as hollow, as empty, as without essence, as a misfortune, as impermanent, as <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), as <s>śūnya</s> (empty), and as <s>anātman</s> (without self) — that one does not run after the past, thinking: 'Did I exist in the past or did I not exist in the past? What was I in the past?'

body.text: a-para-antaṃ vā punar na pratisarati | kiṃ nu bhaviṣyāmy an-āgate * adhvany āho svin na bhaviṣyāmy an-āgate * adhvani | ko nu bhaviṣyāmi + iti | praty-utpannaṃ vā punar na pratisarati | kiṃ svid idaṃ kathaṃ svid idaṃ | ke santaḥ ke bhaviṣyāma iti ||
body.translated_text: Nor does he speculate about the future: 'Will I exist in the future, or will I not exist in the future? What will I become?' Nor does he speculate about the present: 'What indeed is this? How indeed is this? Who are we? What shall we become?'

body.text: ārya-daśa-bhūmake * apy uktaṃ | tatra + a-vidyā-tṛṣṇā-upādānaṃ ca kleśa-vartmano * a-vyavacchedaḥ | saṃskārā bhavaś ca karma-vartmano * a-vyavacchedaḥ | pariśeṣaṃ duṣkha-vartmano * a-vyavacchedaḥ | api tu khalu punar yad ucyate * avidyā-pratyayāḥ saṃskārā iti | eṣā pūrva-antiky apekṣā ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Daśabhūmika</s> (Ten Stages) it is also said: "Therein, ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), and grasping (<s>upādāna</s>) are the non-interruption of the path of afflictions. Formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) and becoming (<s>bhava</s>) are the non-interruption of the path of <s>karma</s>. The remaining [links] are the non-interruption of the path of suffering. Moreover, when it is said: 'Conditioned by ignorance are formations' — this is the consideration regarding the past."

body.text: vijñānaṃ yāvad vedanā + iti | eṣā pratyutpannā + apekṣā | tṛṣṇā yāvad bhava iti | eṣā + a-para-antiky apekṣā + ata ūrddhvam asy pravṛttir iti || pe ||
body.translated_text: "'Consciousness up to feeling' — this is the consideration regarding the present. 'Craving up to becoming' — this is the consideration regarding the future. Beyond this is its continuation." [Abbreviated.]

body.text: tasya + evaṃ bhavati | saṃyogāt saṃskṛtaṃ pravartate | vi-saṃyogān na pravartate | sāmagryāḥ saṃskṛtaṃ pravartate | vi-sāmagryā na pravartate | hanta vayam evaṃ bahu-doṣa-duṣṭaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ viditvā + asya saṃyogasya + asyāś ca sāmagryā vyavacchedaṃ kariṣyāmo | na ca + atyanta-upaśamaṃ sarva-saṃskārāṇām adhigamiṣyāmaḥ satva-paripācanatāyai | iti ||
body.translated_text: "He reflects thus: 'Through conjunction, the conditioned proceeds; without conjunction, it does not proceed. Through the completeness [of conditions], the conditioned proceeds; without the completeness [of conditions], it does not proceed. Come, having understood the conditioned to be so full of faults and defects, let us bring about the interruption of this conjunction and this completeness of conditions. But we shall not attain the ultimate cessation of all <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) — for the sake of maturing sentient beings.'"

body.text: idaṃ saṃkṣepān moha-śodhanaṃ ||
body.translated_text: This is, in brief, the purification of delusion.

body.text: iti śikṣā-samuccaye citta-parikarma paricchedo dvādaśamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the twelfth chapter of the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>: the chapter on Mental Preparation (<s>citta-parikarma</s>).

children.translated_text: Chapter XIII: The Foundation of Mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>)

body.text: smṛty-upasthāna-paricchedaḥ trayodaśaḥ | evaṃ karmaṇya-cittaḥ smṛty-upasthānāny avataret ||
body.translated_text: The thirteenth chapter: the Foundation of Mindfulness. Thus, with a mind made pliable, one should enter into the foundations of mindfulness.

body.text: tatra + a-śubha-prastāvena kāya-smṛty-upasthānam uktam ||
body.translated_text: Therein, contemplation of the body as the foundation of mindfulness is stated through the topic of the impure (<s>aśubha</s>).

body.text: tad eva ca bheda-leśena dharma-saṃgīti-sūtre * abhihitaṃ | punar a-paraṃ kula-putra bodhi-satva evaṃ kāye smṛtim upasthāpayati | ayaṃ kāyaḥ pāda-pāda-aṅguli-jaṅgha-ūru-trika-udara-nābhi-pṛṣṭha-vaṃśa-hṛdaya-pārśva-pārśvakā-hasta-kalācī-bāhv-aṃśa-grīvā-hanu-lalāṭa-śiraḥ-kapāla-mātra-samūhaḥ karma-bhava-kāraka-upacito nānā-kleśa-saṃkalpa-vikalpa-śata-sahasrāṇām āvāsa-bhūto | bahūni ca + atra dravyāṇi samavahitāni | yad uta | keśa-roma-nakha-danta-asthi-carma-piśita-vapā-snāyu-medo-vaśā-lasīkā-yakṛn-mūtra-purīṣa-āma-āśaya-rudhira-kheṭa-pitta-pūya-siṅghāṇaka-mastaka-luṅgāni | evam bahu-dravya-samūhaḥ | tat ko * atra kāyaḥ | tasya pratyavekṣamāṇasya + evaṃ bhavati | ākāśa-samo * ayaṃ kāyaḥ | sa ākāśa-vat kāye smṛtim upasthāpayati | sarvam etad ākāśam iti paśyati | tasya kāya-parijñāna-hetor na bhūyaḥ kva-cit smṛtiḥ prasarati | na visarati | na pratisarati + iti ||
body.translated_text: And that very [contemplation], with a partial distinction, is stated in the <s>Dharmasaṃgīti-sūtra</s>: "Furthermore, O son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> establishes mindfulness regarding the body thus: 'This body is merely an assemblage of feet, toes, calves, thighs, hips, belly, navel, back, spine, heart, sides, flanks, hands, wrists, arms, shoulders, neck, chin, forehead, skull, and cranium — accumulated through the activity of <s>karma</s> and becoming, being the dwelling-place of hundreds of thousands of various afflictive thoughts, intentions, and discriminations. And herein many substances are deposited — namely: hair of the head, hair of the body, nails, teeth, bones, skin, flesh, membrane, sinews, fat, marrow, lymph, liver, urine, feces, stomach contents, blood, phlegm, bile, pus, mucus, brain, and lungs.' Thus it is an assemblage of many substances. What then is 'body' therein? As he examines it, it occurs to him: 'This body is like space.' He establishes mindfulness of the body as like space. He sees all of it as space. Through his comprehension of the body, his mindfulness no longer flows out anywhere, does not scatter, does not speculate."

body.text: punar uktaṃ | ayaṃ kāyo na pūrva-antād āgato | na para-ante saṃkrānto na pūrva-anta-a-para-anta-avasthito * anyatra + a-sad-viparyāsa-saṃbhūtaḥ kāraka-vedaka-rahito na + ādy-anta-madhye pratiṣṭhita-mūlaḥ | a-svāmikaḥ | a-mamaḥ | a-parigrahaḥ | āgantukair vyavahārair vyavahriyate kāya iti deha iti bhoga iti āśraya iti śarīram iti kuṇapa iti āyatanam iti | a-sārako * ayaṃ kāyo mātā-pitṛ-śoṇita-śukra-saṃbhūto * a-śuci-pūti-dur-gandha-sva-bhāvo rāga-dveṣa-moha-bhaya-viṣāda-taskara-ākulo nityaṃ śatana-patana-bhedana-vikiraṇa-vidhvansana-dharmā | nānā-vyādhi-śata-sahasra-nīta iti ||
body.translated_text: And further it is said: "This body has not come from the past, has not passed on to the future, is not established in the past or the future — it has arisen from nothing other than the false inversion of what is non-existent. It is devoid of agent and experiencer. Its root is not established in beginning, end, or middle. It is ownerless, belonging to no one, without attachment. It is designated by adventitious conventions as 'body,' 'frame,' 'enjoyment,' 'support,' 'corporeal form,' 'corpse,' 'sphere.' This body is essenceless, arisen from the blood and semen of mother and father, its nature being impure, putrid, and foul-smelling, beset by the thieves of passion, hatred, delusion, fear, and despair, always subject to the law of crumbling, falling, breaking, scattering, and destruction, assailed by hundreds of thousands of various diseases."

body.text: ārya-ratna-cūḍe * apy āha | a-nityo vata + ayaṃ kāyo * a-cira-sthitiko maraṇa-paryavasāna iti jñātvā na kāya-hetor viṣamayā jīvati | sāraṃ ca + eva + ādatte | sa trīṇi sārāṇy ādatte |katamāni trīṇi | kāya-sāraṃ bhoga-sāraṃ jīvita-sāraṃ ca | so * a-nityaḥ kāya iti sarva-satvānāṃ dāsatva-śiṣyatvam abhyupagamya kiṅ-karaṇīyatāyai utsuko bhavati | a-nityaḥ kāya iti sarva-kāya doṣa-vaṅka-śāṭhya-kuhanāṃ na karoti | a-nityaḥ kāya iti jīvitena + āśvāsa-prāpto jīvita-hetor api pāpaṃ karma na karoti | a-nityaḥ kāya iti bhogeṣu tṛṣṇā-adhyavasānaṃ na karoti | sarvasva-parityāgī + iva bhavati + iti ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Ratnacūḍa</s> (Jewel Crest) it is also said: "Knowing that 'this body is indeed impermanent, of brief duration, ending in death,' one does not live poisonously for the sake of the body, but extracts the essence. He extracts three essences. Which three? The essence of the body, the essence of possessions, and the essence of life. [Reflecting] 'the body is impermanent,' he undertakes servanthood and discipleship to all sentient beings and is eager for their service. [Reflecting] 'the body is impermanent,' he does not practice any crookedness, deceit, or guile with regard to the body. [Reflecting] 'the body is impermanent,' having found confidence in life, he does not commit evil action even for the sake of [preserving] life. [Reflecting] 'the body is impermanent,' he does not cling with craving to possessions — he becomes one who relinquishes everything."

body.text: punar a-paraṃ kula-putra bodhi-satvaḥ kāye kāya-anudarśana-smṛty-upasthānaṃ bhāvayan sarva-satva-kāyāṃs tatra sva-kāyae upanibadhnāti | evaṃ ca + asya bhavati | sarva-satva-kāyā mayā buddha-kāya-pratiṣṭhāna-pratiṣṭhitāḥ kartavyāḥ | yathā ca tathā-gata-kāye na + āśravas tathā sva-kāya-dharmatāṃ pratyavekṣate | so na + āśrava-dharmatā-kuśalaḥ sarva-satva-kāyān api tal-lakṣaṇān eva prajānāti + ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: "Furthermore, O son of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s>, cultivating the foundation of mindfulness of contemplating the body in the body, connects the bodies of all sentient beings with his own body. And he reflects thus: 'The bodies of all sentient beings must be established by me in the establishment of the <s>Buddha</s>-body.' And just as there are no outflows (<s>āśravas</s>) in the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, so he examines the nature of his own body. Being skilled in the nature of non-outflow, he comprehends the bodies of all sentient beings as having those very characteristics" — and so forth.

body.text: vīradatta-paripṛcchāyām apy uktam | yad uta + ayaṃ kāyo * anupūrva-samudāgato * anupūrva-vināśo parama-aṇu-saṃcayaḥ śuṣira unnāma-avanāmau nava-vraṇa-mukha-roma-kūpa-srāvī valmī-kava-dāsī-viṣa-nivāsaḥ

children.text: | a-jāta-śatruḥ | markaṭa-van mitra-drohī | ku-mitra-vad vi-saṃvādana-ātmakaḥ | phena-piṇḍa-vat prakṛti-dur-balaḥ | udaka-budbuda-vad utpanna-bhagna-vilīnaḥ | marīci-vad vipralambha-ātmakaḥ | kadalī-van nibhujyamānā-sārakaḥ | māyā-vad vañcana-ātmakaḥ | rāja-vad ājñā-bahulaḥ | śatru-vad avatāra-prekṣī | cora-vad a-viśvasanīyaḥ | vadhya-ghātaka-vad an-anuvītaḥ | a-mitra-vad a-hita-eṣī | vadhaka-vat prajñā-jīvita-antarāya-karaḥ | śūnya-grāma-vad ātma-virahitaḥ | kulāla-bhāṇḍa-vad bhedana-paryantaḥ | mūtoḍī-van nānā-a-śuci-paripūrṇaḥ | medaka-sthālī-vad a-śuci-srāvī || pe ||
children.translated_text: an enemy from birth; treacherous like a monkey; deceitful in nature like a bad friend; inherently weak like a mass of foam; arising, breaking, and dissolving like a water-bubble; deceptive in nature like a mirage; essenceless when peeled like a plantain stem; fraudulent in nature like a magical illusion; full of commands like a king; watching for an opening like an enemy; untrustworthy like a thief; never to be accompanied like one condemned to death; ill-wishing like a foe; creating obstacles to the life of wisdom like an assassin; devoid of self like an empty village; ending in destruction like a potter's vessel; filled with various impurities like a cesspool; oozing impurity like a vat of dregs." [Abbreviated.]

body.translated_text: In the <s>Vīradattaparipṛcchā</s> it is also said: "This body is gradually assembled and gradually destroyed — a collection of atoms, hollow, subject to rise and fall, oozing from nine wound-openings and pores, a dwelling for swarms of vermin like an anthill, a house of poison,

body.text: vraṇa-vad ghaṭṭana-a-sahiṣṇuḥ | śalya-vat tudana-ātmakaḥ | jīrṇa-gṛha-vat prati-saṃskāra-dhāryaḥ | jīrṇa-yāna-pātra-vat prati-saṃskāra-vāhyaḥ | āma-kumbha-vad yatna-anupālyaḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: "Unable to bear being touched, like a wound; piercing in nature, like a thorn; to be maintained through constant repair, like a dilapidated house; to be carried through constant repair, like a worn-out vessel; to be preserved with care, like an unfired pot." [Abbreviated.]

body.text: nadī-taṭa-vṛkṣa-vac cala-a-calaḥ | mahā-nadī-sroto-van maraṇa-samudra-paryavasānaḥ | āgantuka-āgāra-vat sarva-duṣkha-nivāsaḥ | a-nātha-śālā-vad a-parigṛhītaḥ | cāraka-pāla-vad utkoca-sādhyaḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: "Unsteady, like a tree on a riverbank; ending in the ocean of death, like the current of a great river; a dwelling of all sufferings, like a guest-house; uncared for, like a poorhouse; to be won over by bribes, like a prison guard." [Abbreviated.]

body.text: bāla-dāraka-vat satata-paripālyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: "Constantly needing to be watched over, like a small child."

body.text: punar āha | evaṃ-vidhaṃ kāyam a-caukṣa-rāśiṃ | rūpa-abhimānī bahu manyate yaḥ | prajñāyamānaḥ sa hi bāla-buddhiḥ viṣṭhā-ghaṭaṃ yāti vahan vi-cetāḥ ||
body.translated_text: And further it says: "One who, being proud of beauty, highly esteems this body — this heap of impurity — he is indeed known to be of childish intellect, senseless, carrying a pot of excrement."

body.text: pūya-prakāraṃ vahate * asya nāsā | vaktraṃ ku-gandhaṃ vahate sadā ca | cikkās tathā + akṣṇoḥ krimi-vac ca jantoḥ | kas tatra rāgo bahu-mānatā vā ||
body.translated_text: "His nose carries forth pus; his mouth always carries a foul smell; likewise eye-discharge from the eyes, like worms from a creature — what passion or conceit could there be regarding that?"

body.text: aṅgāram ādāya yathā hi bālo | ghṛṣyed ayaṃ yāsyati śukla-bhāvam | yāti kṣayaṃ na + eva tu śukla-bhāvaṃ bālasya buddhir vitathā + abhimānā ||
body.translated_text: "Just as a fool, having taken a charcoal, rubs it [thinking] 'this will become white' — it goes to destruction but never becomes white. The fool's understanding is a false conceit."

body.text: evaṃ hi yaḥ caukṣa-matir manuṣyaḥ caukṣaṃ kariṣye * aham idaṃ śarīram | su-udvartitaṃ tīrtha-śata-abhiṣiktaṃ yāti kṣayaṃ mṛtyu-vaśād a-caukṣam ||
body.translated_text: "Just so, whoever with the idea of cleanliness thinks 'I will make this body clean' — well-bathed, anointed at a hundred bathing-places — it goes to destruction under the power of death, unclean."

body.text: tathā prabhaṅguraḥ | prasravan bodhi-satvena kāyaḥ pratyavekṣitavyo nava vraṇa-mukhair yāvat | āvāso bodhi-satvena kāyaḥ pratyavekṣitavyaḥ | aśīti-krimi-kula-sahasrāṇām || pe ||
body.translated_text: "Likewise, the body should be examined by the <s>bodhisattva</s> as fragile, oozing from nine wound-openings and so on. The body should be examined by the <s>bodhisattva</s> as a dwelling for eighty thousand families of worms." [Abbreviated.]

body.text: para-bhojano bodhi-satvena kāyaḥ pratyavekṣitavyaḥ | vṛka-śṛgāla-śva-piśita-aśināṃ | yantra-upamo bodhi-satvena kāyaḥ pratyavekṣitavyaḥ | asthi-snāyu-yantra-saṃghāta-vinibaddhaḥ | a-sva-adhīno bodhi-satvena kāyaḥ pratyavekṣitavyaḥ anna-pāna-saṃbhūta iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: "The body should be examined by the <s>bodhisattva</s> as food for others — for wolves, jackals, dogs, and flesh-eating [creatures]. The body should be examined by the <s>bodhisattva</s> as like a machine — bound together as an assemblage of the mechanism of bones and sinews. The body should be examined by the <s>bodhisattva</s> as not under one's own control — arising from food and drink" — and so on in detail.

body.text: tatra + eva jñeyaṃ | vedanā smṛty-upasthānaṃ tu yathā tāvad ārya-ratna-cūḍa-sūtre | iha kula-putra bodhi-satvo vedanāsu vedanā-anupaśyanā-smṛty-upasthānaṃ bhāvayan vedita-sukha-āśriteṣu satveṣu mahā-karuṇāṃ pratilabhate | evaṃ ca pratisaṃśikṣate | tat sukhaṃ yatra veditaṃ na + asti sa sarva-satva-vedita-prahāṇāya vedanāsu vedanā-smṛty-upasthānaṃ bhāvayati | vedita-nirodhāya ca satvānāṃ saṃnāhaṃ saṃnahyati | ātmanā ca vedita-nirodhaṃ na + arpayati | sa yāṃ kāṃ-cid vedanāṃ vedayate tāṃ sarvāṃ mahā-karuṇā-parigṛhītāṃ vedayate | sa yadā sukhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayate tadā rāga-cariteṣu satveṣu mahā-karuṇāṃ pratilabhate ātmanaś ca rāga-anuśayaṃ pratijahāti | yadā duṣkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayate tadā dveṣa-cariteṣu satveṣu mahā-karuṇāṃ pratilabhate ātmanaś ca doṣa-anuśayaṃ prajahāti | yadā + a-duṣkha-a-sukhāṃ vedanāṃ moha-cariteṣu satyeṣu mahā-karuṇāṃ pratilabhate | ātmanaś ca moha-anuśayaṃ prajahāti | sa sukhāyāṃ vedanāyāṃ na + anunīyate | anunaya-samudghātaṃ ca + arjayati | duṣkhāyāṃ vedanāyāṃ na pratihanyate pratigha-samudghātaṃ ca + arjayati | a-duṣkha-a-sukhāyāṃ vedanāyāṃ na + a-vidyā-gato bhavati | a-vidyā-samudghātaṃ ca + arjayati | sa yāṃ kāñ-cid vedanāṃ vetti sarvāṃ tām a-nitya-veditāṃ vetti | sarvāṃ tāṃ duṣkha-veditāṃ vetti | an-ātma-veditāṃ vetti | sa sukhāyāṃ vedanāyām a-nitya-vedito bhavati | duṣkhāyāṃ vedanāyāṃ śalya-vedito bhavati | a-duṣkha-a-sukhāyāṃ vedanāyāṃ śānti-vedito bhavati | iti hi yat sukhaṃ tad a-nityaṃ yad duṣkhaṃ sukham eva tat | yad a-duṣkha-a-sukhaṃ tad an-ātmakam ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: Therein, one should also know the foundation of mindfulness of feelings. First, as in the noble <s>Ratnacūḍa-sūtra</s>: "Here, O son of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s> cultivating the foundation of mindfulness of contemplating feelings in feelings, obtains great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) toward sentient beings who are dependent on feelings of happiness. And he trains thus: 'That happiness — where it is felt — does not [truly] exist.' He cultivates the foundation of mindfulness of feelings in feelings for the abandonment of the feelings of all sentient beings. He dons the armor for the cessation of feelings for sentient beings. Yet he himself does not apply the cessation of feelings. Whatever feeling he feels, he feels it all as encompassed by great compassion. When he feels a pleasant feeling, he obtains great compassion toward sentient beings of passionate disposition and abandons his own latent tendency of passion. When he feels a painful feeling, he obtains great compassion toward sentient beings of hateful disposition and abandons his own latent tendency of aversion. When he feels a feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant, [he obtains great compassion] toward sentient beings of deluded disposition and abandons his own latent tendency of delusion. In a pleasant feeling he is not attracted; and he achieves the eradication of attraction. In a painful feeling he is not repelled; and he achieves the eradication of repulsion. In a feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant he does not become [a victim of] ignorance; and he achieves the eradication of ignorance. Whatever feeling he knows, he knows it all as impermanently felt. He knows it all as felt with suffering. He knows it as felt with non-self. In a pleasant feeling he becomes one who perceives impermanence. In a painful feeling he becomes one who perceives a barb. In a feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant he becomes one who perceives peace. Thus indeed: what is pleasant is impermanent; what is painful is [itself truly a form of] happiness; what is neither painful nor pleasant is without self" — and so forth.

body.text: ārya-akṣayamati-sūtre * apy uktaṃ | duṣkhayā vedanayā spṛṣṭaḥ sarva-pāpa-a-kṣaṇa-upapanneṣu satveṣu mahā-karuṇām utpādayati || pe ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Akṣayamati-sūtra</s> it is also said: "Touched by a painful feeling, he generates great compassion toward all sentient beings born in unfortunate states of non-leisure." [Abbreviated.]

body.text: api tu khalu punar abhiniveśo vedanā parigraho vedanā + upādānaṃ vedanā + upalambho vedanā viparyāso vedanā vikalpo vedanā + ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: "Moreover: attachment is feeling; grasping is feeling; clinging is feeling; perception is feeling; inversion is feeling; conceptual construction is feeling" — and so forth.

body.text: dharma-saṃgīti-sūtre * apy uktaṃ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Dharmasaṃgīti-sūtra</s> it is also said:

body.text: vedanā-anubhavaḥ proktaḥ | kena + asāv anubhūyate | vedako vedanād anyaḥ pṛthag-bhūto na vidyate ||
body.translated_text: "The experience of feeling has been declared — but by whom is it experienced? An experiencer separate from, distinct from feeling is not found."

body.text: evaṃ smṛtir upastheyā vedanāyāṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ | yathā bodhis tathā hy eṣā śāntā śuddhā prabhāsvarā ||
body.translated_text: "Thus should mindfulness of feeling be established by the discerning. For this [feeling], like awakening, is peaceful, pure, and luminous."

body.text: etat samāsato vedanā-smṛty-upasthānam ||
body.translated_text: This, in brief, is the foundation of mindfulness of feelings (<s>vedanā-smṛtyupasthāna</s>).

body.text: citta-smṛty-upasthānaṃ tu yathā + ārya-ratna-kūṭe | sa evaṃ cittaṃ parigaveṣate | katarat tu cittaṃ | rajyati vā duṣyati vā muhyati vā | kim atītam an-āgataṃ praty-utpannaṃ vā + iti | tatra yad atītaṃ tat kṣīṇaṃ | yad an-āgataṃ tad a-saṃprāptaṃ | pratyutpannasya sthitir na + asti | cittaṃ hi kāśyapa na + adhyātmaṃ na bahir-dhā na + ubhayam antareṇa + upalabhyate | cittaṃ hi kāśyapa + a-rūpam a-nidarśanam a-pratigham a-vijñaptikam a-pratiṣṭham a-niketaṃ | cittaṃ hi kāśyapa sarva-buddhair na dṛṣṭaṃ | na paśyanti na drakṣyanti yat sarva-buddhair na dṛṣṭaṃ |na paśyanti na drakṣyanti | kīdṛśas tasya pracāro draṣṭavyaḥ | anyatra vitatha-patitayā saṃjñayā dharmāḥ pravartante | cittaṃ hi kāśyapa māyā-sadṛśam a-bhūta-parikalpanayā vividhām upapattiṃ parigṛhṇāti || pe ||
body.translated_text: The foundation of mindfulness of the mind (<s>citta-smṛtyupasthāna</s>) is as [stated] in the noble <s>Ratnakūṭa</s>: 'He searches for the mind: "Which, then, is the mind? That which is attached, that which is hostile, or that which is deluded? Is it past, future, or present?"'

body.text: cittaṃ hi kāśyapa nadī-srotaḥ-sadṛśam an-avasthitam utpanna-bhagna-vilīnaṃ | cittaṃ hi kāśyapa dīpa-arcciḥ-sadṛśaṃ hetu-pratyayatayā pravartate | cittaṃ hi kāśyapa vidyut-sadṛśaṃ kṣaṇa-bhaṅga-an-avasthitam | cittaṃ hi kāśyapa + ākāśa-sadṛśam āgantukaiḥ kleśair upakliśyate | pe ||
body.translated_text: 'For the mind, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like the current of a river — unsteady, arisen and broken and dissolved. The mind, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like the flame of a lamp — it proceeds through causes and conditions. The mind, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like —'

body.text: cittaṃ hi kāśyapa pāpa-mitra-sadṛśaṃ sarva-duṣkha-saṃjananatayā | pe | cittaṃ hi kāśyapa matsya-baḍiśa-sadṛśaṃ duṣkhe sukha-saṃjñayā | tathā nīla-makṣikā-sadṛśam a-śucau śuci-saṃjñayā | cittaṃ hi kāśyapa praty-arthika-sadṛśaṃ vividha-kāraṇa-ākaraṇatayā | cittaṃ hi ojo-hāra-yakṣa-sadṛśaṃ sadā vivara-gaveṣaṇatayā | evaṃ cora-sadṛśaṃ sarva-kuśala-mūla-muṣaṇatayā | cittaṃ hi kāśyapa rūpa-ārāmaṃ pataṅ-ga-netra-sadṛśaṃ | cittaṃ hi kāśyapa śabda-ārāmaṃ saṃgrāma-bherī-sadṛśaṃ | cittaṃ hi kāśyapa gandha-ārāmaṃ varāha iva + a-śuci-madhye | cittaṃ hi kāśyapa rasa-ārāmaṃ ratha-avaśeṣa-bhoktṛ-ceṭī-sadṛśaṃ | cittaṃ hi kāśyapa sparśa-ārāmaṃ makṣikā + iva taila-pātre | cittaṃ hi kāśyapa parigaveṣyamāṇaṃ na labhyate | yan na labhyate tan na + upalabhyate | yan na + upalabhyate tan na + eva + atītaṃ na + an-āgataṃ na praty-utpannaṃ | yan na + eva + atītaṃ na + an-āgataṃ na praty-utpannaṃ tat try-adhva-samatikrāntaṃ | yat try-adhva-samatikrāntaṃ tan na + iva + asti na na + asti + ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: 'The mind, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like a bad friend — through its generating all suffering. [Abbreviated.] The mind, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like a fish-hook — through perceiving pleasure in what is suffering. Likewise, it is like a blue fly —'

body.text: ārya-ratna-cūḍa-sūtre * apy āha | sa cittaṃ parigaveṣamāṇo na + ādhyātmaṃ cittaṃ samanupaśyati | na bahir-dhā cittaṃ samanupaśyati |na skandheṣu cittaṃ samanupaśyati | na dhātuṣu cittaṃ samanupaśyati | na + āyataneṣu cittaṃ samanupaśyati | sa cittam a-samanupaśyaṃś citta-dhārāṃ paryeṣate | kutaḥ cittasya + utpattir iti | tasya + evaṃ bhavati ālambane sati cittam utpadyate | tat kim anyad ālambanam | atha yad eva + ālambanaṃ tad eva cittaṃ | yadi tāvad anyad ālambanam anyac cittaṃ | tad dvi-cittatā bhaviṣyati | atha yad eva + ālambanaṃ tad eva cittaṃ | tat kathaṃ cittaṃ cittaṃ samanupaśyati | na hi cittaṃ cittaṃ samanupaśyati | tad yathā na tayā + eva + asi-dhārayā sā + eva + asi-dhārā śakyate chettum | na tena + eva + aṅguly--agreṇa tad eva + aṅguly--agraṃ spraṣṭuṃ śakyate | na + eva cittena tad eva cittaṃ śakyate draṣṭum || pe ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Ratnacūḍasūtra</s> also it is said: 'He, searching for the mind, does not perceive the mind internally; he does not perceive the mind externally; he does not perceive the mind in the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) —'

body.text: punar a-paraṃ kula-putra yad upadruta-pradruta-an-avasthita-pracārasya vānara-māruta-sadṛśasya | pe | dūraṃ-gama-cāriṇo * a-śarīrasya laghu-parivartino viṣaya-lolasya ṣaḍ-āyatana-go-carasya + a-para-a-para-saṃprayuktasya cittasya + avasthānām eka-agratā + a-śaraṇam a-viśaraṇaṃ śamathā + eka-agratā + a-vikṣepa ity ucyate cittasya smṛtir iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, O son of good family — of [the mind] whose course is harassed, agitated, and unsteady, resembling a monkey or the wind — [abbreviated] — far-ranging, bodiless, quick to turn, longing for sense-objects —'

body.text: ārya-akṣayamati-sūtre * apy uktaṃ |viṭhapanāyāṃ mayā yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | iyaṃ ca citta-dharmatā na vihātavyā | tatra katamā citta-dharmatā | katamā viṭhapanā | māyā-upamaṃ cittam iyam ucyate citta-dharmatā | yat punaḥ sarvasvaṃ parityajya sarva-buddha-kṣetra-pariśuddhaye pariṇāmayati + iti + iyam ucyate viṭhapanā + ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Akṣayamatisūtra</s> also it is stated: 'I should make an effort in establishing [the mind]. And this nature of the mind (<s>citta-dharmatā</s>) should not be abandoned. And what is the nature of the mind? And what is the establishing? The mind should not —'

body.text: dharma-smṛty-upasthānaṃ tu ||
body.translated_text: The foundation of mindfulness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharma-smṛtyupasthāna</s>) is as follows:

body.text: yathā tāvad atra + āha | dharme dharma-anudarśī viharan bodhi-satvo na kañ-cid dharmaṃ samanupaśyati | yato na buddha-dharmā yato na bodhiḥ | yato na mārgo yato na niḥ-saraṇaṃ | sa sarva-dharma-a-niḥ-saraṇam iti viditvā + an-āvaraṇaṃ nāma mahā-karuṇā-samādhiṃ samāpadyate | sa sarva-dharmeṣu sarva-kleśeṣu ca kṛtrima-saṃjñāṃ pratilabhate | niḥ-kleśā ete dharmā | na + ete sa-kleśāḥ | tat kasya hetoḥ | tathā hy ete nīta-arthe samavasaranti | na + asti kleśānāṃ saṃcayo | na rāśī-bhāvaḥ | na rāga-bhāvo na dveṣa-bhāvo na moha-bhāva | eṣām eva kleśānām avabodhād bodhiḥ | yat sva-bhāvāś ca kleśās tat sva-bhāvā bodhir ity evaṃ smṛtim upasthāpayati + iti ||
