body.translated_text: As [the sūtra] states here: 'The <s>bodhisattva</s>, dwelling as one who contemplates <s>dharmas</s> among <s>dharmas</s>, does not perceive any <s>dharma</s> — wherefrom there would be <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, wherefrom there would be <s>bodhi</s>, wherefrom there would be a path, wherefrom —'

body.text: ārya-ratna-cūḍe * apy uktam | iha kula-putra bodhi-satvasya dharme dharma-anupaśyanā smṛty-upasthānena viharata evaṃ bhavati | dharmā eva + utpadyamānā utpadyante | dharmā eva nirudhymānā nirudhyante ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Ratnacūḍa</s> also it is stated: 'Here, O son of good family, for the <s>bodhisattva</s> dwelling in the foundation of mindfulness of contemplating <s>dharmas</s> among <s>dharmas</s>, this [reflection] arises: "<s>Dharmas</s>, in arising, simply arise —"'

body.text: na punar atra kaś-cid ātma-bhāve satvo vā jīvo vā jantur vā poṣo vā puruṣo vā pudgalo vā manu-jo vā yo jāyate vā jīryate vā cyavate vā + utpadyate vā | eṣā dharmāṇāṃ dharmatā | yadi samudānīyante | samudāgacchanti | atha na samudānīyante na samudāgacchanti | yādṛśāḥ samudānīyante tādṛśāḥ samudāgacchanti kuśalā vā + a-kuśalā vā aniñjyā vā | na + asti dharmāṇāṃ samudānetā | na ca + a-hetukānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ kā-cid utpattir ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: 'But herein there is no self, no being, no soul, no creature, no person, no individual, no human — who is born, who ages, who passes away, or who arises. This is the nature of <s>dharmas</s> —'

body.text: tatra + eva + āha | sa kiyad-gambhīrān api dharmān pratyavekṣamāṇas tāṃ sarva-jñatā-bodhi-citta-anusmṛtiṃ na vijahāti ||
body.translated_text: In the same [sūtra] it says: 'He, even while examining <s>dharmas</s> of however great profundity, does not abandon that recollection of the thought of omniscience and <s>bodhi</s>.'

body.text: ārya-lalita-vistara-sūtre * apy uktam | saṃskāra a-nitya a-dhruvā āma-kumbha-upama-bhedana-ātmakāḥ | para-kelika-yācita-upamāḥ pāṃśu-nagara-upamatā ca kālikā ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Lalitavistarasūtra</s> also it is stated: 'Conditioned things (<s>saṃskāras</s>) are impermanent, unstable, like unfired pots — whose nature is to break; like things borrowed for a festival; comparable to a sand-castle — and temporal.'

body.text: saṃskāra pralopa dharmime varṣa-kāli calitaṃ vilepanaṃ | nadi-kūla iva sa-vālukaṃ pratyaya-adhīna sva-bhāva-dur-balāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Conditioned things are subject to decay, like a rain-cloud's dissolution, like ointment [that fades]; like a sandy river-bank — dependent on conditions, weak in their own nature.'

body.text: saṃskāra pradīpa arci-vat kṣipra-utpatti nirodha-dharmakāḥ | an-avasthita-māruta-upamāḥ phena-piṇḍā-vad a-sāra-dur-balāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Conditioned things are like the flame of a lamp — of swift arising and subject to cessation; comparable to the unsteady wind; like a mass of foam — insubstantial and weak.'

body.text: saṃskāra nir-īha śūnyakāḥ kadalī-skandha-samā nirīkṣataḥ | māyā-upama citta-mohanā bāla-ullāpana-rikta-muṣṭi-vat ||
body.translated_text: 'Conditioned things are without effort, empty; like the trunk of a banana tree when examined; like an illusion, deluding the mind; like an empty fist [shown] to amuse a child.'

body.text: hetūbhi ca pratyayebhi vā sarva saṃskāra-gataṃ pravartate | anyo-nya-pratītya-hetutaḥ tad idaṃ bāla-jano na budhyate ||
body.translated_text: 'Through causes and conditions, everything that pertains to conditioned things proceeds; dependent on one another as causes — this the foolish do not understand.'

body.text: yathā muñja pratītya balba-jaṃ rajju vyāyāma-balena vartitā | ghaṭi-yantra sa-cakra vartate teṣv eka-ekaśu na + asti vartanā ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as, dependent on <s>muñja</s> grass and <s>balbaja</s> reed, a rope twisted by the effort of the hands — a water-wheel with its wheel turns; but in each one individually there is no turning.'

body.text: tatha sarva-bhava-aṅga-vartanī anyo-nya-upacayena niḥśritā | eka-ekaśu teṣu vartanī pūrva-a-para-antato na + upalabhyate ||
body.translated_text: 'Even so, the turning of all the limbs of existence proceeds, dependent on the accumulation of one another; the turning is not found in each one individually, neither from the prior nor from the later end.'

body.text: bījasya sato yathā + aṅkuro na ca yo bīja sa ca + eva aṅkuro | na ca anya tato na ca + eva tat | evam an-uccheda a-śāśvata dharmatā ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as, when the seed exists, there is the sprout — yet that which is the seed is not itself the sprout; it is neither different from it, nor is it that very thing — thus is the nature of things: neither annihilation nor eternity.'

body.text: saṃskāra a-vidya-pratyayāḥ te ca saṃskāra na santi tatvataḥ | saṃskāra a-vidya ca + eva hi śūnya ete prakṛtī nir-īhakāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Conditioned things are conditioned by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), and those conditioned things do not truly exist; conditioned things and ignorance are indeed empty — these are [their] natures, without effort.'

body.text: mudrāt prati-mudra dṛśyate mudra-saṃkrānti na ca + upalabhyate | na ca tatra na ca + eva sānyato evaṃ saṃskār-an-uccheda-śāśvatāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'From a seal, an impression is seen, but no transference of the seal is apprehended; it is neither there [in the impression] nor from elsewhere — thus conditioned things are neither annihilated nor eternal.'

body.text: cakṣuś ca pratītya rūpataḥ cakṣu vijñānam iha + upajāyate | na ca cakṣuṣi rūpa-niśritaṃ rūpa-saṃkrānti na ca + eva cakṣuṣi ||
body.translated_text: 'Dependent on the eye and on form, eye-consciousness arises herein; but form does not reside in the eye, and no transference of form into the eye [occurs].'

body.text: nairātmya-śubhāś ca dharmime te punar ātmā + iti śubhāś ca kalpitāḥ | viparītam a-sad-vikalpitaṃ cakṣu-vijñāna tato upajāyate ||
body.translated_text: 'And these <s>dharmas</s> are selfless and pure; yet they are imagined as self and pure — what is inverted and falsely imagined: from that, eye-consciousness arises.'

body.text: vijñāna nirodha-saṃbhavaṃ vijña utpāda-vyayaṃ vipaśyati | a-kahiñ-ci gatam an-āgataṃ śūnya māyā-upama yogi paśyati ||
body.translated_text: 'Consciousness is subject to cessation and arising; the wise one sees the arising and passing away [of consciousness]; gone nowhere, not having come — the <s>yogin</s> sees it as empty, like an illusion.'

body.text: araṇiṃ yatha ca + uttara-araṇiṃ hasta-vyāyāma-trayebhi saṃgatiṃ | iti pratyayato * agni jāyate jātu kṛtu-kāryu laghū nirudhyate ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as from a fire-stick and an upper fire-stick, through the conjunction of three — hand-effort [and the two sticks] — fire is born from conditions; once its task is done, it quickly ceases.'

body.text: atha paṇḍitu kaś-ci mārgate kuta yam āgatu kutra yāti vā | vidiśo diśi sarva mārgato na gatir na + apy a-gatiś ca labhyate ||
body.translated_text: 'Then some wise person searches: "Whence has it come? Where does it go?" — searching in every direction and quarter, neither its going nor its not-going is found.'

body.text: skandha-āyatanāni dhātavaḥ tṛṣṇa a-vidyā iti karma-pratyayāḥ | sāmagri tu satva-sūcanā sā ca parama-arthatu na + upalabhyate ||
body.translated_text: 'The <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), and <s>dhātus</s> (elements); craving, ignorance, and <s>karma</s> as conditions — [their] aggregate indicates a "being," but that [being] is not found in the ultimate sense.'

body.text: kaṇṭha-oṣṭha pratītya tālukaṃ jihva parivartir avarti akṣarā | na ca kaṇṭha-gatā na tālukaiḥ akṣara-eka-eka tu na + upalabhyate ||
body.translated_text: 'Dependent on the throat, lips, palate, and the turning of the tongue — syllables [arise]; but they do not reside in the throat, nor in the palate; each syllable individually is not found.'

body.text: sāmagri-pratītyaś ca sā vācam anubudhi-vaśena niścarī | mana-vāca a-dṛśya-rūpiṇī bāhyato * abhyantari na + upalabhyate ||
body.translated_text: 'And dependent on the aggregate [of conditions], speech issues forth through the power of volition; [but] speech, of invisible form in mind and words, is not found externally or internally.'

body.text: utpāda-vyayaṃ vipaśyato vāca-ruta-ghoṣa-svarasya paṇḍitāḥ | kṣaṇikāṃ vaśikāṃ tad īdṛśīṃ sarva-vācaḥ pratiśrutaka-upamāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'The wise, seeing the arising and passing away of speech, sounds, calls, and voice — [see them as] momentary and dependent; all speech is like an echo.'

body.text: yatha tantri pratītya dāru ca hasta-vyāyāma-trayebhi saṃgatim | tuṇa-vīṇa-su-ghoṣaka-ādibhiḥ śabdo niścarate tad-udbhavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as, dependent on strings and wood, and through the conjunction of three — hand-effort [and the two] — from a <s>tuṇa-vīṇā</s> and well-sounding [instruments] and the like, sound issues forth, born from those [conditions].'

body.text: atha paṇḍitu kaś-ci mārgate kuto * ayam āgatu kutra yāti vā | vidiśo diśa sarva-mārgataḥ śabdam an-āgamanaṃ na labhyate ||
body.translated_text: 'Then some wise person searches: "Whence has this come? Where does it go?" — searching in every direction and quarter, the non-coming of sound is [all that] is found.'

body.text: tatha hetubhi pratyayebhi ca sarva-saṃskāra-gataṃ pravartate | yogī puna bhūta-darśanāt śūnya saṃskāra nir-īha paśyati ||
body.translated_text: 'Even so, through causes and conditions, everything that pertains to conditioned things proceeds; but the <s>yogin</s>, from seeing things as they truly are, sees conditioned things as empty and without effort.'

body.text: skandha-āyatanāni dhātavaḥ śūnya-adhyātmika śūnya-bāhyakāḥ | satva-ātma-viviktana-ālayāḥ dharma-ākāśa-sva-bhāva-lakṣaṇāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'The <s>skandhas</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>dhātus</s> — empty internally, empty externally; their abode is the separation from being and self; their nature is characterized as <s>dharma</s>-space.'

body.text: loka-nātha-vyākaraṇe * apy uktam ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Lokanāthavyākaraṇa</s> also it is stated:

body.text: śūnyā a-nāmakā dharmāḥ nāma kiṃ paripṛcchasi | śūnyatā na kva-cid devā na nāgā na + api rākṣasāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'The <s>dharmas</s> are empty, nameless — what name do you ask about? Emptiness is not anywhere among gods, nor among <s>nāgas</s>, nor among <s>rākṣasas</s>.'

body.text: manuṣyā vā + a-manuṣyā vā sarve tu eṣa vidyate | nāmnā hi nāmatā śūnyā nāmni nāma na vidyate ||
body.translated_text: 'Whether humans or non-humans — all this exists. By name, names are empty; in a name, no name is found.'

body.text: a-nāmakāḥ sarve dharmāḥ nāmnā tu paridīpitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are nameless; by names they are [merely] illuminated.'

body.text: yo hi sva-bhāvo nāmno vai na sa dṛṣṭo na ca śrutaḥ | na ca + utpanno niruddho vā kasya nāma + iha pṛcchasi ||
body.translated_text: 'For the intrinsic nature of a name has neither been seen nor heard; it has neither arisen nor ceased — whose name do you ask about here?'

body.text: vyavahāra-kṛtaṃ nāma prajñaptir nāma-darśitā | ratna-citro hy ayaṃ nāmnā ratna-uttama-para iti ||
body.translated_text: 'A name is made by convention; designation is shown through naming. For this one is called by name "<s>Ratnacitra</s>" (Jewel-Splendor), supreme among the best of jewels.'

body.text: iti śikṣā-samuccaye smṛty-upasthāna-paricchedas trayodaśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>, the thirteenth chapter on the Foundations of Mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>).

body.text: ātma-bhāva-pariśuddhiḥ paricchedaś caturdaśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The fourteenth chapter: Purification of the Self (<s>ātmabhāvapariśuddhi</s>).

body.text: uktāni smṛty-upasthānāni | evaṃ yogya-citto daśasu dikṣu śeṣasya jagato duṣkha-sāgara-uddharaṇa-abhisaṃbodhy-upāyo vyoma-paryanta-traikālya-sarva-dharma-vaśa-vartitvāya + eva tu punaḥ sarva-dharma-śūnyatām avataret | evaṃ hi pudgala-śūnyatā siddhā bhavati | tataś ca chinna-mūlatvāt kleśā na samudācaranti ||
body.translated_text: The foundations of mindfulness have been stated. Thus, one whose mind is prepared should, for the sake of drawing the remainder of the world from the ocean of suffering, [practice] the means of awakening to mastery over all <s>dharmas</s> of the three times extending to the limits of space — and for this very purpose he should enter the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s> (<s>sarvadharmśūnyatā</s>). For thus the emptiness of the person (<s>pudgalaśūnyatā</s>) is established; and from that, since the root is cut, the afflictions do not arise.

body.text: yathā + uktam ārya-tathā-gata-guhya-sūtre | tad yathā + api nāma śāntamate vṛkṣasya mūla-chinnasya sarva-śākhā patra-palāśāḥ śuṣyanti | evam eva śāntamate sat-kāya-dṛṣṭy-upaśamāt sarva-kleśā upaśāmyanti + iti ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Ārya-Tathāgataguhya Sūtra</s>: 'O <s>Śāntamati</s>, just as when the root of a tree is cut, all its branches, leaves, and foliage wither — just so, O <s>Śāntamati</s>, through the pacification of the view of the personal aggregate (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), all afflictions are pacified.'

body.text: śūnyatā-bhāvanā-anuśaṃsās tv a-paryantāḥ ||
body.translated_text: But the benefits of cultivating emptiness (<s>śūnyatābhāvanā</s>) are boundless.

body.text: yathā tāvac candra-pradīpa-sūtre | so * asau śikṣa na jātu traśatī su-gatānāṃ | so * asau śūru na jātu istriṇāṃ vaśam etī | so * asau sāsani prīti vindate su-gatānāṃ | yo * asau dharma-sva-bhāva jānatī su-praśāntaṃ ||
body.translated_text: As, to begin with, in the <s>Candrapradīpa Sūtra</s>: 'He never trembles at the teaching of the <s>Sugatas</s>; that hero never falls under the power of women; he finds delight in the teaching of the <s>Sugatas</s> — he who knows the nature of <s>dharmas</s> to be utterly peaceful.'

body.text: so * asau na + iha cireṇa bheṣyate dvi-pada-indraḥ | so * asau vaidya-bhiṣak bheṣyate sukha-dātā | so * asau uddhari śalya sarvaśo dukhitānāṃ |yo * asau dharma-sva-bhāva jānatī su-praśāntaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'He will before long become the lord among bipeds; that physician-healer will become a giver of happiness; he will extract the thorns [of suffering] completely from the afflicted — he who knows the nature of <s>dharmas</s> to be utterly peaceful.'

body.text: so * asau kṣānti-balena udgato nara-candraḥ | so * asau loṣṭaka-daṇḍa tāḍito na ca kupyī | so * asau chidyati aṅgam aṅgaśo na ca kṣubhyo | yo * asau dharma-sva-bhāva jānatī su-praśāntaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'That moon among men has risen through the power of patience; that one, struck by clods and sticks, does not become angry; that one, having his limbs severed piece by piece, is not agitated — he who knows the nature of <s>dharmas</s> to be utterly peaceful.'

body.text: na + asau durgatiṣū patiṣyatī anuvyañjana | nityaṃ lakṣaṇa-dhāri bheṣyatī abhirūpaḥ | pañcyo tasya abhijña bhāvitā ima nityaṃ | purataḥ so su-gatāna sthāsyatī sa ca śūra | ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: 'He will not fall into the lower realms; always bearing the [auspicious] marks, he will become handsome [with the minor marks]; the five higher knowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) will always be cultivated by him; that hero will stand in the presence of the <s>Sugatas</s>,' and so forth.

body.text: bhagavatyām apy uktaṃ | punar a-paraṃ śāriputra bodhi-satvena mahā-satvena buddha-kāyaṃ niṣpādayitu-kāmena dvātriṃśan-mahā-puruṣa-lakṣaṇāny aśītiṃ ca + anuvyañjanāni pratilabdhu-kāmena sarvatra jātau jāti-smaratāṃ bodhi-citta-a-vipraṇāśatāṃ bodhi-satva-caryā + a-saṃpramoṣatāṃ pratilabdhu-kāmena sarva-pāpa-mitra-pāpa-sahāyān vivarjayitu-kāmena sarva-buddha-bodhi-satva-kalyāṇa-mitrāṇy ārāgayitu-kāmena sarva-māra-māra-kāyika-devatā-nirjetu-kāmena sarva-āvaraṇī yāni śodhayitu-kāmena sarva-dharma-an-āvaraṇatāṃ pratilabdhu-kāmena prajñā-pāramitāyāṃ śikṣitavyaṃ | punar a-paraṃ śāriputra bodhi-satvena mahā-satvena ye daśasu dikṣu buddhā bhagavantas tiṣṭhanti te me varṇaṃ bhāṣerann iti prajñā-pāramitāyāṃ śikṣitavyaṃ | punar a-paraṃ śāriputra bodhi-satvena mahā-satvena + eka-citta-utpādena pūrvasyāṃ diśi gaṅgā-nadī-vālukā-upamān loka-dhātūn samatikramitu-kāmena | pe | evaṃ sarva-dikṣu prajñā-pāramitāyāṃ śikṣitavyam ity ādy iti
body.translated_text: In the <s>Bhagavatī</s> [Prajñāpāramitā] it is also said: 'Furthermore, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> who wishes to accomplish the <s>Buddha</s>-body, who wishes to obtain the thirty-two marks of a great being and the eighty minor marks, who wishes to obtain in every birth the memory of past births, the non-loss of <s>bodhicitta</s>, and the non-forgetfulness of the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct; who wishes to avoid all evil friends and evil companions; who wishes to please all the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s> as spiritual friends; who wishes to conquer all <s>Māra</s> and the <s>Māra</s>-host deities; who wishes to purify all obstructions; who wishes to attain the unobstructedness of all <s>dharmas</s> — should train in the Perfection of Wisdom (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>). Furthermore, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, [thinking:] "May the <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s> abiding in the ten directions speak in praise of me," should train in the Perfection of Wisdom. Furthermore, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> who wishes, by a single arising of the mind, to traverse world-realms in the eastern direction as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river — [Abbreviation] — likewise in all directions, should train in the Perfection of Wisdom,' and so on. Thus —

body.text: tatra yathā nir-ātmānaś ca sarva-dharmāḥ | karma-phala-saṃbandha-a-virodhaś ca niḥ-sva-bhāvatā ca yathā-dṛṣṭa-sarva-dharma-a-virodhaś ca | tathā pitṛ-putra-samāgame darśitam | ṣaḍ-dhātur ayaṃ mahā-rāja puruṣaḥ ṣaṭ-sparśa-āyatanaḥ | aṣṭādaśa-mana-upavicāraḥ | ṣaḍ-dhātur ayaṃ mahā-rāja puruṣa iti | na khalu punar etad yuktaṃ | kiṃ vā + etad pratītya + uktaṃ ṣaḍ ime mahā-rāja dhātavaḥ | katame ṣaṭ | tad yathā pṛthivī-dhātur ab-dhātus tejo-dhātur vāyu-dhātur ākāśa-dhātur vijñāna-dhātuś ca | ime mahā-rāja ṣaḍ dhātavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein — how all <s>dharmas</s> are without self, how there is no contradiction with the connection of <s>karma</s> and its fruit, how all <s>dharmas</s> are without intrinsic nature, and how there is no contradiction with all <s>dharmas</s> as they are seen — this is shown in the <s>Pitṛputrasamāgama</s> (Meeting of Father and Son): 'This person, O great king, consists of six elements and six bases of contact, with eighteen mental explorations.' 'This person consists of six elements, O great king' — this, however, is not proper [if taken literally]. What is meant by this? These, O great king, are six elements. Which six? Namely: the earth element, the water element, the fire element, the wind element, the space element, and the consciousness element. These, O great king, are the six elements.

body.text: yāvat ṣaḍ imāni mahā-rāja sparśa-āyatanāni | katamāni ṣaṭ | cakṣuḥ sparśa-āyatanaṃ rūpāṇāṃ darśanāya | śrotraṃ sparśa-āyatanaṃ śabdānāṃ śravaṇāya | ghrāṇaṃ sparśa-āyatanaṃ gandha-ārāma-āghrāṇāya | jihvā sparśa-āyatanaṃ rasānām āsvādanāya | kāya-sparśa-āyatanaṃ spraṣṭavyānāṃ sparśanāya | manaḥ-sparśa-āyatanaṃ dharmāṇāṃ vijñānāya | imāni ca mahā-rāja ṣaṭ sparśa-āyatanāni || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'These, O great king, are six bases of contact. Which six? The eye as a base of contact, for seeing forms. The ear as a base of contact, for hearing sounds. The nose as a base of contact, for smelling fragrances. The tongue as a base of contact, for tasting flavors. The body as a base of contact, for touching tangibles. The mind as a base of contact, for cognizing <s>dharmas</s>. These, O great king, are the six bases of contact.' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: aṣṭādaśa + ime mahā-rāja mana-upavicārāḥ | katame * aṣṭādaśa | iha puruṣaś cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā | saumanasya-daurmanasya-upekṣā-sthānīyāny upavicarati | evaṃ śrotra-ādiṣu vācyaṃ | tena praty-ekam indriya-ṣaṭkena saumanasya-ādi-trayāṇāṃ bhedād aṣṭādaśa mana-upavicārā bhavanti | pe | katamaś ca mahā-rāja + ādhyātmikaḥ pṛthivī-dhātuḥ | yat kiñ-cid asmin kāye * adhyātmaṃ kakkhaṭatvaṃ khara-gatam upāttaṃ | tat punaḥ katamat | tad yathā | keśā romāṇi nakhā dantā ity ādi | ayam ucyate + ādhyātmikaḥ pṛthivī-dhātuḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'These, O great king, are eighteen mental explorations. Which eighteen? Here, a person, having seen forms with the eye, explores those that pertain to pleasure, displeasure, and equanimity.' Likewise for the ear and the rest. Thus, by the division of the three — pleasure and so on — for each of the six faculties, there arise eighteen mental explorations. [Abbreviation.] 'And what, O great king, is the internal earth element? Whatever in this body is internal, solid, of a hard nature, and appropriated. What is that? Namely: hair of the head, body hair, nails, teeth,' and so forth. 'This is called the internal earth element.'

body.text: katamaś ca mahā-rāja bāhyaḥ pṛthivī-dhātuḥ | yat kiñ-cid bāhyaṃ kakkhaṭvaṃ khara-gatam anupāttam ayam ucyate bāhyaḥ pṛthivī-dhātuḥ | tatra mahā-rāja + ādhyātmikaḥ pṛthivī-dhātur utpadyamāno na kutaś-cid āgacchati nirudhyamāno na kva-cit saṃnicayaṃ gacchati | bhavati mahā-rāja sa samayo yat strī adhyātmam ahaṃ strī + iti kalpayati | sā + adhyātmam ahaṃ strī + iti kalpayitvā bahir-dhā puruṣaṃ puruṣa iti kalpayati | sā bahir-dhā puruṣaṃ puruṣa iti kalpayitvā saṃraktā satī bahir-dhā puruṣeṇa sārdhaṃ saṃyogam ākāṅkṣate | puruṣo * adhyātmaṃ puruṣo * asmi + iti kalpayati + iti pūrva-vat | tayoḥ saṃyoga-ākāṅkṣayā saṃyogo bhavati | saṃyoga-pratyayāt kalalaṃ jāyate | tatra mahā-rāja yaś ca saṃkalpo yaś ca saṃkalpayitā | ubhayam etan na saṃvidyate | striyāṃ strī na saṃvidyate | puruṣe puruṣo na saṃvidyate | iti hy a-sann a-sad-bhūtaḥ saṃkalpo jātaḥ | so * api saṃkalpā-sva-bhāvena na saṃvidyate | yathā saṃkalpas tathā saṃyogo * api kalalam api sva-bhāvena na saṃvidyate | yaś ca sva-bhāvato na saṃvidyate tat kathaṃ kakkhaṭatvaṃ janayiṣyati | iti hi mahā-rāja saṃkalpaṃ jñātvā kakkhaṭatvaṃ veditavyaṃ yathā kakkhaṭatvam utpadyamānaṃ na kutaś-cid āgacchati | nirudhyamānaṃ na kva-cit saṃnicayaṃ gacchati + iti | bhavati mahā-rāja samayo yad ayaṃ kāyaḥ śmaśāna-paryavasāno bhavati | tasya tat kakkhaṭatvaṃ saṃklidyamānaṃ nirudhyamānaṃ na pūrvāṃ diśaṃ gacchati | na dakṣiṇāṃ | na paścimāṃ | na + uttarāṃ | na + ūrdhvaṃ | na + adho | na tu vi-diśaṃ gacchati | evaṃ mahā-rāja + ādhyātmikaḥ pṛthivī-dhātur draṣṭavyaḥ | bhavati mahā-rāja sa samayo yadā + ākāśī-bhūte loka-saṃniveśe brāhmaṃ vimānaṃ saṃtiṣṭhate mahā-ratna-mayaṃ | tan mahā-rāja kakkhaṭatvam utpadyamānaṃ na kutaś-cid āgacchati | cakra-vāḍa-mahā-cakra-vāḍāḥ saṃtiṣṭhante dṛḍhāḥ sārā eka-ghanā vajra-mayās teṣām api kakkhaṭatvam utpadyamānaṃ na kutaś-cid āgacchati | sumeravaḥ parvata-rājāno yugaṃ-dharā nimiṃ-dharā īśā-dharā yāvat kāla-parvatāḥ saṃtiṣṭhante | sarvaś ca tri-sāhasra-mahā-sāhasro loka-dhātuḥ saṃtiṣṭhate | catur-aśītir yojana-sahasrāṇy udvedhena | madhye ca + aṣṭaṣaṣṭiṃ yojana-śata-sahasraṃ mahā-pṛthivī saṃtiṣṭhate | tad api mahā-rāja kakkhaṭatvaṃ samudāgacchat kutaś-cid āgacchati | bhavati mahā-rāja sa samayo yadā + ayaṃ lokaḥ saṃvartate | tadā + iyaṃ mahā-pṛthivī agninā vā dahyate * adbhir vā klidyate vāyunā vā vikīryate | tasyā agninā dahyamānāyā maṣir api na prajāyate tad yathā + api nāma sarpiṣo vā tailasya vā + agninā dahyamānasya na maṣir na chāyikā prajñāyate evam eva + asyās tri-sāhasra-mahā-sāhasrāyā loka-dhātor agninā dahyamānāyā na + eva maṣir na chāyikā + avaśiṣṭā prajñāyate | evam adbhir lavaṇa-vilaya-vad vāyunā vairambha-vāta-abhihata-śakunta-vat pṛthivyāṃ na kiñ-cid avaśiṣṭaṃ prajñāyatae iti paṭhyate | tatra mahā-rāja pṛthivī-dhātor utpādo * api śūnyaḥ vyayo * api śūnya utpanno * api pṛthivī-dhātuḥ sva-bhāva-śūnya | iti hi mahā-rāja pṛthivī-dhātuḥ pṛthivī-dhātutvena na + upalabhyate * anyatra vyavahārāt | so * api vyavahāro na strī na puruṣaḥ | evam eva + etan mahā-rāja yathā-bhūtaṃ samyak-prajñayā draṣṭavyaṃ | tatra katamo * ab-dhātuḥ | yad idam asmin kāye * adhyātmaṃ praty-ātmam āpaḥ | ab-gataṃ | aptvaṃ snehaḥ | sneha-gataṃ snehatvaṃ dravatvam upagatam upāttaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'And what, O great king, is the external earth element? Whatever is external, solid, of a hard nature, and unappropriated — this is called the external earth element. Therein, O great king, the internal earth element, when arising, does not come from anywhere; when ceasing, it does not go to any place of accumulation.' 'There is a time, O great king, when a woman internally imagines "I am a woman." Having imagined internally "I am a woman," she externally imagines a man to be "a man." Having imagined externally a man to be "a man," being attached, she desires union with a man externally. A man internally imagines "I am a man" — likewise as before. From the desire for union of those two, union occurs. From the condition of union, the embryo (<s>kalala</s>) is born. Therein, O great king, both the imagination and the imaginer — neither of these is found. In a woman, no woman is found; in a man, no man is found. Thus indeed, from what is non-existent, from what does not truly exist, the imagination is born. And that too, by its nature as imagination, is not found. Just as the imagination, so too the union and the embryo are not found by their intrinsic nature. And what is not found by intrinsic nature — how will it produce solidity?' 'Thus indeed, O great king, having understood the imagination, solidity should be known — that solidity, when arising, does not come from anywhere; when ceasing, it does not go to any place of accumulation.' 'There is a time, O great king, when this body reaches its end in the charnel ground. Its solidity, when decomposing and ceasing, does not go to the eastern direction, nor to the southern, nor to the western, nor to the northern, nor upward, nor downward, nor to the intermediate directions. Thus, O great king, is the internal earth element to be seen.' 'There is a time, O great king, when in the cosmic realm that has become empty space, the <s>Brahmā</s> palace, made of great jewels, comes into being. That solidity, O great king, when arising, does not come from anywhere. The <s>Cakravāḍa</s> and <s>Mahācakravāḍa</s> mountains come into being — firm, solid, compact, made of diamond — and their solidity too, when arising, does not come from anywhere. Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, the <s>Yugaṃdhara</s>, <s>Nimiṃdhara</s>, <s>Īśādhara</s>, up to the <s>Kāla</s> mountains come into being. And the entire three-thousand great-thousand world-system comes into being — eighty-four thousand <s>yojanas</s> in height; and in the middle, the great earth extends sixty-eight hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>. That solidity too, O great king, when coming into being, does not come from anywhere.' 'There is a time, O great king, when this world disintegrates. Then this great earth is either burnt by fire, or dissolved by water, or scattered by wind. When it is being burnt by fire, not even ash appears — just as when butter or oil is being burnt by fire, neither ash nor shadow appears — just so, when this three-thousand great-thousand world-system is being burnt by fire, neither ash nor shadow remains. Likewise, by water — like the dissolution of salt; by wind — like a bird struck by a whirlwind; nothing of the earth remains.' Thus it is read. 'Therein, O great king, the arising of the earth element is empty; the decay is also empty; even the arisen earth element is empty of intrinsic nature. Thus, O great king, the earth element is not apprehended as earth-element-ness, except through convention. And that convention too is neither female nor male. Just so, O great king, this should be seen as it truly is, with right wisdom.' 'Therein, what is the water element? Whatever in this body is internal, personal — water, of the nature of water, wetness, moisture, of the nature of moisture, liquidity — that is appropriated.'

body.text: tat punaḥ katamat | tad yathā | aśru svedaḥ kheṭaḥ siṅghāṇakaṃ vaśā lasikā majjā medaḥ pittaṃ śleṣmā pūyaḥ śoṇitaṃ kṣīraṃ prasrāva ity ādir ayam ucyante ādhyātmiko * ab-dhātuḥ | pe ||
body.translated_text: 'What is that? Namely: tears, sweat, phlegm, mucus, fat, synovial fluid, marrow, lard, bile, mucus, pus, blood, milk, urine,' and so forth. 'This is called the internal water element.' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: bhavati mahā-rāja sa samayo yat priyaṃ dṛṣṭvā + aśru pravartate | duṣkhena ca + abhyāhatasya dharma-saṃvegena vā + aśru pravartate | vātena vā + akṣi prasyandate | yāvat sa mahā-rāja + ab-dhātur na kutaś-cid āgacchati | bhavati mahā-rāja sa samayo yadā + ādhyātmiko * ab-dhātuḥ pariśuṣyati | sa pariśuṣyan nirudhyamāno na kva-cid gacchati | pe | vivartamāne khalu punar loke samantād dvātriṃśat paṭalā abhra-ghanāḥ saṃtiṣṭhante saṃsthāya sarvāvantaḥ | tri-sāhasra-mahā-sāhasraṃ loka-dhātuṃ chādayanti | yataḥ pañca-antara-kalpān īṣādhāro devo varṣati | evaṃ pañca gaja-prameho devo varṣati | pañca-ācchinna-dhāraḥ |pañca sthūla-bindukaḥ | tata iyaṃ mahā-pṛthivī yāvad brahma-lokād udakena sphuṭā bhavati | sa mahā-rāja tāvan mahān ab-dhātur utpadyamāno na kutaś-cid āgacchati | bhavati mahā-rāja sa samayo yad ayaṃ lokaḥ saṃvartate | saṃvartamāne khalu punar loke dvitīyasya sūryasya prādur-bhāvo bhavati | dvitīyasya sūryasa loke prādur-bhāvād utsāḥ sarāṃsi kunadyaś ca śuṣyanti | evaṃ tṛtīyasya mahā-utsā mahā-nadyaḥ | caturthasya + an-avataptaṃ mahā-saraḥ sarveṇa sarvam ucchuṣyati | caturthasya sūryasya prādur-bhāvān mahā-samudrasya yojanikam apy udakaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gacchati | dvi-yojanikam api tri-catuḥ-pañca-daśa-viṃśati-triṃśac-catvāriṃśat-pañcāśad-yojanikam api yāvac catvāriṃśad-yojana-sahasram udakam avaśiṣṭaṃ bhavati | yāvad dvi-tāla-mātraṃ |yāvat kaṇṭha-mātraṃ | yāvad goṣpada-mātram udakam avaśiṣṭaṃ bhavati | bhavati mahā-rāja sa samayo yan mahā-samudre pṛthita-pṛthitāny avaśiṣṭāni bhavanti | pe ||
body.translated_text: There is an occasion, O Great King, when tears flow upon seeing what is dear. And tears flow for one struck by suffering, or through spiritual urgency (<s>dharma-saṃvega</s>). Or the eye waters due to wind. Up to: That <s>ap-dhātu</s> (water element), O Great King, does not come from anywhere. There is an occasion, O Great King, when the internal <s>ap-dhātu</s> dries up. When it dries up and ceases, it does not go anywhere. [In abbreviation.] When the world is evolving, thirty-two layers of dense clouds gather from all sides and, having formed, cover the entire trichiliocosm (<s>tri-sāhasra-mahā-sāhasra loka-dhātu</s>). Then for five intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, the rain-god rains down a shower [as fine as] a yoke-pin. Likewise for five [kalpas] it rains an elephant-stream. For five, an unbroken torrent. For five, thick drops. Then this great earth becomes flooded with water up to the <s>Brahma</s>-world. That great <s>ap-dhātu</s>, O Great King, when arising in such magnitude, does not come from anywhere. There is an occasion, O Great King, when this world dissolves. When the world is dissolving, a second sun appears. With the appearance of a second sun in the world, springs, ponds, and small rivers dry up. Likewise, with the third [sun], great springs and great rivers [dry up]. With the fourth, the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s> dries up completely and entirely. With the appearance of a fourth sun, even a <s>yojana</s>'s depth of water in the great ocean is exhausted and consumed. Even two <s>yojanas</s>, even three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty <s>yojanas</s> — up to forty thousand <s>yojanas</s> of water remain. Up to only two palm-trees' depth. Up to only throat-depth. Up to only a cow's hoofprint of water remains. There is an occasion, O Great King, when in the great ocean only scattered puddles remain. [In abbreviation.]

body.text: bhavati mahā-rāja sa samayo yan mahā-samudre * aṅguli-sneha-mātram apy udakaṃ na + avaśiṣṭaṃ bhavati | sa mahā-rāja tāvān ab-dhātur nirudhyamāno na kva-cid gacchati | pe | tasya khalu punar mahā-rāja + ab-dhātor utpādo * api śūnyaḥ | vyayo * api śūnyaḥ tiṣṭhann api so * ab-dhātuḥ sva-bhāva-śūnya iti hi mahā-rāja + ab-dhātur ab-dhātutvena + upalabhyate * anyatra vyavahāra-mātrāt | so * api vyavahāro na strī na puruṣaḥ pūrva-vat ||
body.translated_text: There is an occasion, O Great King, when not even a finger-tip's worth of moisture remains in the great ocean. That great <s>ap-dhātu</s>, O Great King, when ceasing in such magnitude, does not go anywhere. [In abbreviation.] Moreover, the arising of that <s>ap-dhātu</s>, O Great King, is empty. Its cessation is also empty. That <s>ap-dhātu</s>, even while persisting, is empty of inherent nature. For thus, O Great King, the <s>ap-dhātu</s> is apprehended as <s>ap-dhātu</s> only through conventional designation. And that convention is neither woman nor man — as stated before.

body.text: ādhyātmikas tejo-dhātuḥ katamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: What is the internal <s>tejo-dhātu</s> (fire element)?

body.text: yat kiñ-cid asmin kāye tejas tejo-gatam ūṣma-gatam upagatam upāttaṃ | tat punaḥ katamat | yena + ayaṃ kāya ātapyate saṃtapyate | yena vā + asya + asita-pīta-khāditāni samyak-sukhena paripākaṃ gacchati | yasya ca + utsadatvāj jvarito jvarita iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati || pe ||
body.translated_text: Whatever in this body is heat, of the nature of heat, of the nature of warmth, that has been taken up and appropriated. And what is that? It is that by which this body is heated and warmed; and that by which what is eaten, drunk, and consumed is properly and comfortably digested; and due to whose excess one is called 'feverish.' [In abbreviation.]

body.text: bāhyas tejo-dhātuḥ katamaḥ | yad bāhyaṃ tejas tejo-gatam ūṣma-gatam upagatam upāttaṃ | tat punaḥ katamat | yan manuṣyā araṇī-sahagatebhyo garbhala-sahagatebhyo vā go-maya-cūrṇena vā kārpāsa-picunā + āvāsam anveṣante yad utpannaṃ grāmam api dahati grāma-pradeśam api dahati yāvad dvīpaṃ vā kakṣaṃ tṛṇānāṃ vā dāvaṃ vā kāṣṭhaṃ vā yāvad dahan paraiti + ity ādi |tatra mahā-rāja + ādhyātmikas tejo-dhātur utpadyate na kutaś-cid āgacchati nirudhyamāno na kva-cit saṃnicayaṃ gacchati | iti hy a-bhūtvā bhavati bhūtvā ca prativigacchati sva-bhāva-rahitatvāt ||
body.translated_text: What is the external <s>tejo-dhātu</s> (fire element)? Whatever external fire is of the nature of heat, of the nature of warmth, that has been taken up and appropriated. And what is that? [For instance,] humans seek fire from fire-sticks, from tinder, or with cow-dung powder or cotton wadding — and [that fire] once produced burns a village, burns a village district, even an island, or a thicket of grass, or a forest, or wood, and so on, burning as it advances. Therein, O Great King, the internal <s>tejo-dhātu</s>, when arising, does not come from anywhere; when ceasing, it does not go to any repository. For indeed, not having existed it comes to be, and having existed it passes away — due to the absence of inherent nature.

body.text: evaṃ yat kiñ-cid asmin kāye vāyur vāyu-gataṃ laghutvaṃ samudīraṇatvaṃ | tat punaḥ katamat | tad yathā ūrdhva-gamā vāyavo * adho-gamāḥ pārśva-āśrayāḥ pṛṣṭha-āśrayāḥ kukṣi-gamāḥ śastrakāḥ kṣurakāḥ sūcakāḥ pippalakā vāta-aṣṭhīlā vāta-gulmā āśvāsa-praśvāsā aṅga-anusāriṇo vāyava ity ādi | santi bahir-dhā pūrve vāyavo dakṣiṇāḥ paścimā uttarā vāyavaḥ sa-rajasaḥ a-rajasaḥ parīttā mahad-gatā vāyava iti | bhavati mahā-rāja sa samayo yan mahā-vāyu-skandhaḥ samudāgataḥ | vṛkṣa-agrān api pātayati | kuḍyān api parvata-agrān api pātayati | pātayitvā nir-upādāno vigacchati | yaṃ satvāś cīvara-karṇikena vā vidhamanakena vāta-anuvṛttena vā paryeṣyante | yāvad ayam ucyate bāhyo vāyu-dhātuḥ | tasya + apy utpattiḥ pūrva-vat ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, whatever in this body is wind, of the nature of wind — lightness and impulsion. And what is that? Namely: upward-moving winds, downward-moving winds, winds dwelling in the sides, winds dwelling in the back, winds moving through the belly, winds [sharp] like swords, winds [sharp] like razors, winds [sharp] like needles, winds like pippala[-berries], wind-stones (<s>vāta-aṣṭhīlā</s>), wind-tumors (<s>vāta-gulma</s>), inhalation and exhalation, and winds coursing through the limbs — and so on. Externally, there are eastern winds, southern, western, and northern winds; dusty winds, dust-free winds; minor and great winds. There is an occasion, O Great King, when a great mass of wind arises. It topples treetops, topples walls and mountaintops. Having toppled [them], it departs without support. [And that wind] which beings seek with the corner of a robe, or with a fan, or by following a breeze — up to: this is called the external <s>vāyu-dhātu</s> (wind element). Its arising too is as stated before.

body.text: ādhyātmika ākāśa-dhātuḥ katamaḥ | yat kiñ-cid asmin kāye * adhyātmaṃ praty-ātmam upagatam upāttam ākāśa-gatam iha + abhyantara-saṃkhyā-bhūtaṃ | a-sphuṭam a-spharaṇīyaṃ tvaṅ-mānsa-śoṇitena | tat punaḥ katamat | yad asmin kāye cakṣuḥ suṣiram iti vā yāvan mukhaṃ vā mukha-dvāraṃ vā kaṇṭhaṃ vā kaṇṭha-nāḍyā vā yena ca + abhyavaharati yatra ca + avatiṣṭhate | yena ca + asya + aśita-pīta-khādita-āsvāditam adhastāt pragharati | ayam ucyatae ādhyātmika ākāśa-dhātuḥ | evaṃ bāhye * api yad a-sphuṭam a-spharaṇīyaṃ rūpa-gatena + a-paliguddhaṃ suṣira-bhāvaś chidraṃ | ayam ucyate bāhyaḥ ākāśa-dhātuḥ ||
body.translated_text: What is the internal <s>ākāśa-dhātu</s> (space element)? Whatever in this body is internal, personal, taken up and appropriated, of the nature of space, counted as internal emptiness — that which is not solid, not spread through [by] skin, flesh, and blood. And what is that? Whatever in this body is the eye-socket, and so on up to: the mouth, the mouth-opening, the throat, the throat-tube, and that [passage] through which one swallows, and that where [food] settles, and that through which what has been eaten, drunk, consumed, and tasted passes downward — this is called the internal <s>ākāśa-dhātu</s>. Likewise externally: whatever is not solid, not spread through, and not enclosed by form — [that] quality of being hollow, an opening — this is called the external <s>ākāśa-dhātu</s>.

body.text: bhavati mahā-rāja sa samayo yat karma-pratyayād āyatanāni prādur-bhavanti tāny ākāśa-dhātuṃ paricārayanti | tatra saṃkhyā bhavaty ādhyātmika ākāśa-dhātur iti | sa na kutaś-cid āgacchati | bhavati samayo yad rūpaṃ bibharti sarvam ākāśī-bhavati | tat kasya hetoḥ | a-kṣayo hy ākāśa-dhātuḥ sthiro * a-calaḥ | tad yathā mahā-rāja + a-saṃskṛto nirvāṇa-dhātuḥ | evam eva + ākāśa-dhātuḥ sarvatra + anugato draṣṭavyaḥ | tad yathā + api nāma mahā-rāja puruṣa utthale deśe uda-pānaṃ vā kuṭakaṃ vā kūpaṃ vā puṣkariṇīṃ vā khānayet | tat kiṃ manyase mahā-rāja yat tatra + ākāśaḥ kutas tad āgatam iti | āha | na kutaś-cid bhagavan | bhagavān āha | tad yathā + api nāma mahā-rāja sa puruṣaḥ punar eva tad uda-pānaṃ vā yāvat puṣkariṇīṃ vā pūrayet | tat kiṃ manyase mahā-rāja yat tad ākāśaṃ kva-cid gatam iti | āha | na kva-cid gataṃ bhagavan | tat kasya hetoḥ | na hy ākāśa-dhātur gamane vā āgamane vā pratyupasthitaḥ | na strī-bhāvena na puruṣa-bhāvena pratyupasthitaḥ | bhagavān āha | iti hi mahā-rāja bāhya-ākāśa-dhātur a-calaḥ |a-vikāraḥ |tat kasya hetoḥ | śūnyo hy ākāśa-dhātur ākāśa-dhātutvena | virahita ākāśa-dhātur ākāśa-dhātutvena | na puruṣa-bhāvena na strī-bhāvena pratyupasthitaḥ | evam eva yathā-bhūtaṃ samyak-prajñayā draṣṭavyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: There is an occasion, O Great King, when, due to the condition of <s>karma</s>, the sense-bases come into being and they operate within the <s>ākāśa-dhātu</s>. There the designation 'internal <s>ākāśa-dhātu</s>' arises. It does not come from anywhere. There is an occasion when all form that it bears becomes space. For what reason? Because the <s>ākāśa-dhātu</s> is inexhaustible, stable, and unmoving. Just as, O Great King, the unconditioned <s>nirvāṇa</s>-element [is such] — just so, the <s>ākāśa-dhātu</s> should be seen as pervading everywhere. Just as, O Great King, a man in a barren place might dig a well, or a cistern, or a pit, or a pool — what do you think, O Great King: that space there — where did it come from? He said: 'From nowhere, Blessed One.' The Blessed One said: 'Just as, O Great King, that man might fill up again that well, or up to that pool — what do you think, O Great King: has that space gone anywhere?' He said: 'It has not gone anywhere, Blessed One. For what reason? Because the <s>ākāśa-dhātu</s> is not established in going or in coming. It is not established as being female or being male.' The Blessed One said: 'Thus, O Great King, the external <s>ākāśa-dhātu</s> is unmoving, unchanging. For what reason? Because the <s>ākāśa-dhātu</s> is empty of <s>ākāśa-dhātu</s>-ness. The <s>ākāśa-dhātu</s> is devoid of <s>ākāśa-dhātu</s>-ness. It is not established as being male or being female. Just so should it be seen as it truly is, with right wisdom.'

body.text: tatra katamo vijñāna-dhātur yā cakṣur-indriya-adhipateyā | rūpa-ārambaṇa-prativijñaptiḥ | yāvad iti hi mahā-rāja yā kā-cid varṇa-saṃsthāna-prativijñaptir ayam ucyate cakṣur-vijñāna-dhātuḥ | pe | iti hi yā ṣaḍ-indriya-adhipateyā ṣaḍ-viṣaya-ārambaṇā viṣaya-vijñaptir ayam ucyate vijñāna-dhātuḥ | sa khalu punar ayaṃ mahā-rāja vijñāna-dhātur na + indriya-niśrito na viṣayebhya āgato na madhye * antara-sthāyī sa na + adhyātma bahir-dhā na + ubhayam antareṇa | sa khalu punar ayaṃ mahā-rāja vijñāna-dhātur vastu prativijñapya niruddhaḥ | sa utpadyamāno na kutaś-cid āgacchati nirudhyamāno na kva-cid gacchati | tasya khalu punar vijñāna-dhātor utpādo * api śūnyaḥ | vyayo * api śūnyaḥ | utpanno * api vijñāna-dhātuḥ sva-bhāva-śūnyaḥ | iti mahā-rāja vijñāna-dhātur vijñāna-dhātutvena śūnyo na + upalabhyate * anyatra vyavahārāt | so * api vyavahāro na strī na puruṣaḥ | evam etad yathā-bhūtaṃ samyak-prajñayā draṣṭavyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the <s>vijñāna-dhātu</s> (consciousness element)? That which, with the eye-faculty as its governing [condition], is the cognition taking form as its object. Up to: Thus, O Great King, whatever cognition has the six faculties as governing [conditions], has the six objects as its domain, and is the discerning of objects — this is called the <s>vijñāna-dhātu</s>. Moreover, O Great King, this <s>vijñāna-dhātu</s> is not based in the sense-faculties, does not come from the objects, and does not stand in the interval between them. Moreover, O Great King, this <s>vijñāna-dhātu</s> is not internal, not external, and not in between the two. Moreover, O Great King, this <s>vijñāna-dhātu</s>, having discerned an object, ceases. When arising, it does not come from anywhere; when ceasing, it does not go anywhere. Moreover, the arising of that <s>vijñāna-dhātu</s> is empty. Its cessation is also empty. Even when arisen, the <s>vijñāna-dhātu</s> is empty of inherent nature. Thus, O Great King, the <s>vijñāna-dhātu</s> is empty of <s>vijñāna-dhātu</s>-ness; it is not apprehended except through convention. And that convention too is neither woman nor man. Just so should it be seen as it truly is, with right wisdom.

body.text: tatra mahā-rāja katamac cakṣur-āyatanaṃ | yac caturṇāṃ mahā-bhūtānāṃ prasādaḥ | tad yathā pṛthivī-dhātor ab-dhātos tejo-dhātor vāyu-dhātor yāvat | tatra pṛthivī-dhātu-prasādaś cakṣur-āyatanaṃ na + ab-dhātu-prasādo na tejo-dhātu-prasādo na vāyu-dhātu-prasādaś cakṣur-āyatanaṃ | tat kasya hetoḥ | na hi pṛthivī-dhātu-prasādaḥ kasya-cid dharma-āyatanaṃ vā āyatana-pratilambhena vā pratyupasthitaḥ | evaṃ yāvan na vāyu-dhātu-prasādaḥ kasya-cid dharmasya + āyatanaṃ vā āyatana-pratilambhena vā pratyupasthitaḥ | tat kasya hetoḥ | niś-ceṣṭā hy ete dharmā niṣṭhāpārā nirvāṇa-samā | iti hi mahā-rāja eka-ekato dharmān mṛgyamāṇān cakṣur-āyatanaṃ na + upalabhate * anyatra vyavahārāt | tat kasya hetoḥ | śūnyo hi pṛthivī-dhātu-prasādaḥ pṛthivī-dhātu-prasādena | yāvac * chūnyo vāyu-dhātu-prasādo vāyu-dhātu-prasādena | ye ca dharmāḥ sva-bhāvena śūnyāḥ kas teṣāṃ prasādo vā kṣobho vā | yeṣāṃ na prasādo na kṣobha upalabhyate | kathaṃ te rūpaṃ drakṣyanti | iti hy atyantatayā cakṣur-āyatanaṃ śūnyaṃ cakṣur-āyatana-sva-bhāvena tat pūrva-antato na + upalabhyate ||
body.translated_text: Therein, O Great King, what is the eye-base (<s>cakṣur-āyatana</s>)? It is the sensitive matter (<s>prasāda</s>) of the four great elements — namely, of the <s>pṛthivī-dhātu</s>, <s>ap-dhātu</s>, <s>tejo-dhātu</s>, and <s>vāyu-dhātu</s>. Up to: Therein, the sensitive matter of the <s>pṛthivī-dhātu</s> is the eye-base — not the sensitive matter of the <s>ap-dhātu</s>, nor of the <s>tejo-dhātu</s>, nor of the <s>vāyu-dhātu</s> is the eye-base. For what reason? Because the sensitive matter of the <s>pṛthivī-dhātu</s> is not established as any <s>dharma</s>'s base or as the obtaining of a base. Likewise, up to: the sensitive matter of the <s>vāyu-dhātu</s> is not established as any <s>dharma</s>'s base or as the obtaining of a base. For what reason? Because these <s>dharmas</s> are without activity, having cessation as their culmination, equal to <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Thus, O Great King, when <s>dharmas</s> are examined one by one, the eye-base is not apprehended except through convention. For what reason? Because the sensitive matter of the <s>pṛthivī-dhātu</s> is empty of the nature of the sensitive matter of the <s>pṛthivī-dhātu</s>. Up to: the sensitive matter of the <s>vāyu-dhātu</s> is empty of the nature of the sensitive matter of the <s>vāyu-dhātu</s>. And those <s>dharmas</s> that are empty by inherent nature — what clarity or disturbance could there be for them? For those in which neither clarity nor disturbance is apprehended — how can they see form? Thus, ultimately the eye-base is empty of the inherent nature of the eye-base; it is not apprehended from the former limit onward.

body.text: a-para-antato * api na + upalabhyate | an-āgamanatāṃ gamanatāṃ ca + upādāya sthānam apy asya na + upalabhyate sva-bhāva-virahitatvāt | yac ca sva-bhāvena na saṃvidyate | na tat strī na puruṣaḥ | tena kā manyanā | manyanā ca nāma mahā-rāja māra-go-caraḥ | a-manyanā buddha-go-caraḥ | tat kasya hetoḥ | manyanā + apagatā hi sarva-dharmāḥ | pe | tatra mahā-rāja katamac * chrotra-āyatanaṃ | yac caturṇāṃ mahā-bhūtānāṃ prasādo | yāvad iti hi mahā-rāja sarva-dharmā vimokṣa-abhimukhā dharma-dhātu-niyatā ākāśa-dhātu-paryavasānā a-prāptikā a-vyavahārā an-abhilāpyā an-abhilapanīyāḥ | yatra mahā-rāja indriyāṇi pratihanyante te viṣayā ity ucyante | cakṣur hi rūpe pratihanyate tasmād rūpāṇi cakṣur-viṣayā ity ucyante | evaṃ śrotraṃ śabdeṣv ity ādi | tatra cakṣū rūpe pratihanyata iti nipātaḥ | pratihanyanā teṣāṃ nirdiṣṭā | tathā hi cakṣū rūpeṣu tri-vidhaṃ nipatati + iti | anu-kūleṣu śubha-saṃjñayā | prati-kūleṣu pratigha-saṃjñayā | na + eva + anu-kūleṣu na prati-kūleṣu + upekṣayā | evaṃ mano dharmeṣv ity ādi | tae ime viṣayā mano-go-carā ity ucyante | atra hi manaś carati | upavicarati | tasmān mano-go-carā ity ucyante | yad etan mahā-rāja mano * a-prati-kūleṣu rūpeṣv anunītaṃ carati | tena + asya rāga utpadyate | prati-kūleṣu rūpeṣu pratihataṃ carati tena + asya dveṣa utpadyate | na + eva + anu-kūleṣu na prati-kūleṣu saṃmūḍhaṃ carati | tena + asya moha utpadyate | evaṃ śabda-ādiṣv api tri-vidham ārambaṇam anubhavati pūrva-vat ||
body.translated_text: Even ultimately, it is not apprehended. Taking into account both its non-coming and its going, even its abiding is not apprehended, because it is devoid of inherent nature. And that which does not exist by its own nature is neither woman nor man. Therefore, what is there to be proud about? And pride, O Great King, is the domain of <s>Māra</s>. Non-pride is the domain of the <s>Buddha</s>. For what reason? Because all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are free from pride. [abbreviated] In that case, O Great King, what is the ear sense-base (<s>śrotrāyatana</s>)? It is the refined [element] of the four great elements. And so on — for, O Great King, all <s>dharmas</s> face toward liberation, are determined by the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), terminate in the <s>ākāśadhātu</s> (realm of space), are unattainable, beyond convention, inexpressible, and ineffable. Where the sense-faculties (<s>indriyas</s>) are obstructed, O Great King, those are called 'objects' (<s>viṣayas</s>). For the eye is obstructed by form — therefore forms are called 'objects of the eye.' Similarly, the ear with sounds, and so forth. Now, regarding 'the eye is obstructed by forms' — this is a falling upon. Their obstruction has been indicated. For the eye falls upon forms in three ways: upon agreeable [forms] with the perception of the pleasant; upon disagreeable [forms] with the perception of aversion; and upon those that are neither agreeable nor disagreeable, with equanimity. Similarly, the mind with <s>dharmas</s> (mental objects), and so forth. Therefore, these objects are called 'the domain of the mind' (<s>manogocarā</s>). For the mind moves among them; it roams about. Therefore they are called 'the domain of the mind.' When, O Great King, the mind moves attracted toward forms that are not disagreeable, thereby attachment (<s>rāga</s>) arises in him. When it moves repelled toward disagreeable forms, thereby aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>) arises in him. When it moves bewildered toward those that are neither agreeable nor disagreeable, thereby delusion (<s>moha</s>) arises in him. Likewise, regarding sounds and other [objects], one experiences a threefold object-support, as before.

body.text: tatra mahā-rāja māyā-upamāni + indriyāṇi | svapna-upamā viṣayāḥ | tad yathā + api nāma mahā-rāja puruṣaḥ suptaḥ svapna-antare jana-pada-kalyāṇyā striyā sārdhaṃ paricaret | sa śayita-vibuddho jana-pada-kalyāṇīṃ striyam anusmaret | tat kiṃ manyase mahā-rāja saṃvidyate svapna-antare jana-pada-kalyāṇī strī | āha | na + u hi + idaṃ bhagavan | bhagavān āha | tat kiṃ manyase mahā-rāja + api nu sa puruṣaḥ paṇḍita-jātīyo bhavet | yaḥ svapna-antare jana-pada-kalyāṇīṃ striyam anusmaret | tayā vā sārdhaṃ krīḍitam abhiniveśet | āha | na + u hi + idaṃ bhagavan | tat kasya hetoḥ | aty-antatayā hi bhagavan svapna-antare jana-pada-kalyāṇī na saṃvidyate na + upalabhyate | kutaḥ punar anayā sārdhaṃ paricaraṇā | anyatra yāvad eva sa puruṣo vighātasya klamathasya bhāgī syāt | yas tām abhiniviśet ||
body.translated_text: In that regard, O Great King, the sense-faculties are like an illusion (<s>māyā</s>); the objects are like a dream. Just as, O Great King, a man who is asleep might in a dream consort with a woman who is the beauty of the land; and upon awakening from sleep, he would remember that woman, the beauty of the land. What do you think, O Great King — does the woman, the beauty of the land, exist in the dream? He said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavan</s>.' The <s>Bhagavan</s> said: 'What do you think, O Great King — would that man be of a wise nature, who would remember the woman, the beauty of the land, from the dream? Or who would cling to the sport enjoyed with her?' He said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavan</s>. For what reason? Because, <s>Bhagavan</s>, the woman, the beauty of the land, absolutely does not exist in the dream and is not apprehended. How then could there be consorting with her? Rather, that man would only be a partaker of frustration and weariness — he who would cling to that.'

body.text: bhagavān āha | evam eva mahā-rāja bālo * a-śrutavān pṛthag-janaś cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā saumanasya-sthānīyāny abhiniviśet | so * abhiniviṣṭaḥ sann anunīyate * anunītaḥ saṃrajyate | saṃrakto rāga-jaṃ karma + abhisaṃskaroti | tri-vidhaṃ kāyena catur-vidhaṃ vācā tri-vidhaṃ manasā | tac ca karma + abhisaṃskṛtam ādita eva kṣīṇaṃ niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇataṃ na pūrvāṃ diśaṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati | na dakṣiṇāṃ na paścimāṃ na + uttarāṃ na + ūrdhvaṃ na + adho na + anuvidiśaṃ | na + iha na tiryak | na ubhayam antarā | tat punaḥ kāla-antareṇa maraṇa-kāla-samaye pratyupasthite | jīvita-indriya-nirodhe āyuṣaḥ parikṣayāt tat-sa-bhāgasya karmaṇaḥ kṣīṇatvāc carama-vijñānasya nirudhyamānasya manasa ārambaṇī-bhavati | tad yathā + api nāma śayita-vibuddhasya jana-pada-kalyāṇī + iti manasa ārambaṇaṃ bhavati | iti hi mahā-rāja carama-vijñānena + adhipatinā tena ca karmaṇā ārambaṇena + aupapatty-aṃśika-dvaya-pratyayaṃ prathama-vijñānam utpadyate | yadi vā narakeṣu yadi vā tiryag-yonau yadi vā yama-loke yadi vā āsure kāye yadi vā manuṣyeṣu yadi vā deveṣu | tasya ca prathama-vijñānasya aupapatty-aṃśikasya samanantara-niruddhasya + an-antara-sa-bhāgā citta-saṃtatiḥ pravartate | yatra vipākasya pratisaṃvedanā prajñāyate | tatra yaś carama-vijñānasya nirodhas tatra cyutir iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati | yaḥ prathama-vijñānasya prādur-bhāvas tatra + upapattiḥ | iti hi mahā-rāja na kaś-cid dharmo * asmāl lokāt paraṃ lokaṃ gacchati | cyuty-upapattī ca prajāyete | tatra mahā-rāja carama-vijñānam utpadyamānaṃ na kutaś-cid āgacchati ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavan</s> said: 'In just this way, O Great King, the foolish, unlearned ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), having seen forms with the eye, clings to those that occasion a feeling of pleasure. Having thus clung, he is attracted; being attracted, he becomes impassioned; being impassioned, he produces <s>karma</s> born of passion — threefold through body, fourfold through speech, threefold through mind. And that <s>karma</s>, once produced, is from the very beginning exhausted, ceased, gone, transformed; it does not abide depending on the eastern direction, nor the southern, nor the western, nor the northern, nor above, nor below, nor in any intermediate direction, nor here, nor across, nor in between. But then, after an interval of time, when the moment of death is at hand, when the life-faculty (<s>jīvitendriya</s>) ceases, due to the exhaustion of the lifespan, and due to the exhaustion of <s>karma</s> of a similar class, when the final consciousness (<s>caramavijñāna</s>) is ceasing, it becomes the object-support of the mind. Just as, for one who has awakened from sleep, the thought of the beauty of the land becomes the object-support of the mind. Thus, O Great King, conditioned by the twofold cause of the rebirth-share — namely, the final consciousness as the dominant [condition] and that <s>karma</s> as the object-support — the first consciousness (<s>prathamavijñāna</s>) arises: whether in the hells, or in animal births, or in the world of <s>Yama</s>, or in a demonic body, or among humans, or among gods. And immediately after the cessation of that first consciousness belonging to the rebirth-share, a mental continuum (<s>cittasaṃtati</s>) of a similar class proceeds without interruption, wherein the experiencing of the ripening [of <s>karma</s>] is known. Therein, the cessation of the final consciousness is reckoned as 'death' (<s>cyuti</s>); the arising of the first consciousness is 'rebirth' (<s>upapatti</s>). Thus, O Great King, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever goes from this world to the next world; yet both death and rebirth occur. In that regard, O Great King, the final consciousness, when arising, does not come from anywhere;

body.text: nirudhyamānaṃ na kva-cid gacchati | karma + apy utpadyamānaṃ na kutaś-cid āgacchati | nirudhyamānaṃ na kva-cid gacchati | prathama-vijñānam apy utpadyamānaṃ na kutaś-cid āgacchati | nirudhyamānaṃ ca na kva-cid gacchati | tat kasya hetoḥ | sva-bhāva-virahitatvāt | carama-vijñānaṃ carama-vijñānena śūnyaṃ | karma karmaṇā śūnyaṃ | prathama-vijñānaṃ prathama-vijñānena śūnyaṃ | cyutiś cyutyā śūnyā | upapattir upapattyā śūnyā | karmaṇāṃ ca + a-bandhyatā prajāyate vipākasya ca pratisaṃvedanā na ca + atra kaś-cit kartā na bhoktā + anyatra nāma-saṃketāt | tad yathā + api nāma mahā-rāja puruṣaḥ suptaḥ svapna-antare śatruṇā sārdhaṃ saṃgrāmayet | sa śayita-vibuddhaḥ | tam eva + anusmaret | tat kiṃ manyase mahā-rāja saṃvidyate svapna-antare śatruḥ | śatruṇā vā sārdhaṃ saṃgrāma iti | āha | na + u hi + idaṃ bhagavan | bhagavān āha | tat kiṃ manyase mahā-rāja + api nu sa puruṣaḥ paṇḍita-jātīyo bhavet | yo * asau svapna-antare śatrum abhiniviśet | śatruṇā vā sārdhaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ | āha | na + u hi + idaṃ bhagavan | tat kasya hetoḥ | aty-antatayā hi bhagavan svapne śatrur na saṃvidyate kutaḥ punas tena sārdhaṃ saṃgrāmaḥ | anyatra yāvad eva sa puruṣo vighātasya klamathasya ca bhāgī syāt yas tam abhiniviśet | bhagavān āha | evam eva mahā-rāja bālo * a-śrutavān pṛthag-janaś cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā daurmanasyā-sthānīyāny abhiniviśate * abhiniviṣṭaḥ san pratihanyate | pratihataḥ saṃtuṣyati | duṣṭo doṣa-jaṃ karma + abhisaṃskaroti + iti pūrva-vat | tad yathā + api nāma mahā-rāja puruṣah suptaḥ svapna-antare piśācena paripātyamāno bhītaḥ saṃoham āpadyate | sa śayita-vibuddhas taṃ piśācaṃ taṃ ca saṃmoham anusmaret | tat kiṃ manyase mahā-rāja saṃvidyante svapne piśācaḥ saṃmoho vā | yāvad evam eva mahā-rāja bālo * a-śrutavān pṛthag-janaś cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā upekṣā-sthānīyāny abhiniviśate * abhiniviṣṭaḥ san muhyati mūḍho moha-jaṃ karma + abhisaṃskaroti + iti pūrva-vat | tad yathā + api nāma mahā-rāja puruṣaḥ suptaḥ svapna-antare jana-pada-kalyāṇyā gāyantyā madhuraṃ gīta-svaraṃ madhuraṃ ca tantrī-svaraṃ ca śṛṇuyāt | sā tena gīta-vāditena paricārayet | sa śayita-vibuddhas tad eva gīta-vāditam anusmaret | tat kiṃ manyase mahā-rāja + api nu sa puruṣaḥ paṇḍita-jātīyaḥ svapna-antare jana-pada-kalyāṇyā gīta-vāditam abhiniviśet | āha | na + u hi + idaṃ bhagavan | bhagavān āha | tat kasya hetoḥ | aty-antatayā hi bhagavan svapna-antare jana-pada-kalyāṇī strī na saṃvidyate na + upalabhyate | kutaḥ punar asyā gīta-vāditaṃ | anyatra yāvad eva sa puruṣo vighātasya klamathasya ca bhāgī syāt | yas tad abhiniviśet | bhagavān āha | evam eva mahā-rāja bālo * a-śrutavān pṛthag-janaḥ śrotreṇa śabdān śrutvā saumanasya-sthānīyāny abhiniviśate | iti pūrva-vat | evaṃ gandha-ādiṣu tri-dhā tri-dhā veditavyam || pe ||
body.translated_text: when ceasing, it does not go anywhere. <s>Karma</s> too, when arising, does not come from anywhere; when ceasing, it does not go anywhere. The first consciousness too, when arising, does not come from anywhere; and when ceasing, it does not go anywhere. For what reason? Because they are devoid of inherent nature. The final consciousness is empty of [being a] final consciousness. <s>Karma</s> is empty of [being] <s>karma</s>. The first consciousness is empty of [being a] first consciousness. Death (<s>cyuti</s>) is empty of death. Rebirth (<s>upapatti</s>) is empty of rebirth. Yet the non-barrenness of <s>karmas</s> occurs and the experiencing of their ripening [takes place], and herein there is no agent and no experiencer — apart from mere conventional designation.' 'Just as, O Great King, a man who is asleep might in a dream fight with an enemy. Upon awakening from sleep, he would remember that very [encounter]. What do you think, O Great King — does the enemy exist in the dream, or the battle with the enemy?' He said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavan</s>.' The <s>Bhagavan</s> said: 'What do you think, O Great King — would that man be of a wise nature, who would cling to the enemy in the dream, or to the battle with the enemy?' He said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavan</s>. For what reason? Because, <s>Bhagavan</s>, absolutely the enemy does not exist in the dream — how then could there be a battle with him? Rather, that man would only be a partaker of frustration and weariness, who would cling to that.' The <s>Bhagavan</s> said: 'In just this way, O Great King, the foolish, unlearned ordinary person, having seen forms with the eye, clings to those that occasion a feeling of displeasure. Having thus clung, he is repelled; being repelled, he is angered; being angered, he produces <s>karma</s> born of aversion' — as before. 'Just as, O Great King, a man who is asleep might in a dream be pursued by a <s>piśāca</s> (demon), becoming frightened and falling into bewilderment. Upon awakening from sleep, he would remember that <s>piśāca</s> and that bewilderment. What do you think, O Great King — do the <s>piśāca</s> or the bewilderment exist in the dream?' And so on — 'In just this way, O Great King, the foolish, unlearned ordinary person, having seen forms with the eye, clings to those that occasion a feeling of indifference. Having thus clung, he is bewildered; being bewildered, he produces <s>karma</s> born of delusion' — as before. 'Just as, O Great King, a man who is asleep might in a dream hear the sweet sound of song and the sweet sound of stringed instruments from a woman who is the beauty of the land, singing. She would entertain him with that singing and music. Upon awakening from sleep, he would remember that very singing and music. What do you think, O Great King — would that man be of a wise nature, who would cling to the singing and music of the beauty of the land in the dream?' He said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavan</s>.' The <s>Bhagavan</s> said: 'For what reason? Because, <s>Bhagavan</s>, the woman, the beauty of the land, absolutely does not exist in the dream and is not apprehended. How then could there be her singing and music? Rather, that man would only be a partaker of frustration and weariness, who would cling to that.' The <s>Bhagavan</s> said: 'In just this way, O Great King, the foolish, unlearned ordinary person, having heard sounds with the ear, clings to those that occasion a feeling of pleasure' — as before. Likewise, regarding odors and the rest, one should understand [the same] in three ways each. [abbreviated]

body.text: atra mahā-rāja mānasaṃ niveśayitavyaṃ | kim ity ahaṃ sa-devakasya lokasya cakṣur bhaveyaṃ | ulkā pradīpa āloka-bhūtaḥ | kūlaṃ naus tīrthaṃ | nāyakaḥ pariṇāyakaḥ daiśikaḥ sa-artha-vāhaḥ | puro javeyaṃ | mukto mocayeyam āśvasta āśvāsayeyaṃ parinirvṛttaḥ parinirvāpayeyam iti | pūrvā hi koṭir mahā-rāja na prajñāyate aiśvarya-ādhipatyānām anubhūya mānānāṃ | iti hi mahā-rāja māyā-upamāni + indriyāṇy a-tṛptāny a-tarṣaṇīyāni | svapna-upamā viṣayā a-tarṣakā a-tṛpti-karāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Herein, O Great King, one should direct the mind [thus]: 'How might I become the eye of the world together with its gods? A torch, a lamp, a source of light; a bank, a ship, a ford; a leader, a guide, a pathfinder, a caravan-leader. May I go forth; being liberated, may I liberate; being reassured, may I reassure; having attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, may I lead others to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.' For the prior limit, O Great King, of the lordships, sovereignties, and honors experienced [in the past] is not discernible. Thus, O Great King, the sense-faculties are like an illusion — unsatisfied and not to be craved for; the objects are like a dream — not thirst-quenching and not producing satisfaction.

body.text: atra + an-anta-yaśaś-cakravartinaḥ kathā svargāc ca patite tasmin sa-rājakaiḥ pauraiḥ parivṛta evaṃ paṭhyate | tad yathā + api nāma mahā-rāja sarpir-maṇḍo vā nava-nīta-maṇḍo vā taptāyāṃ vālukāyām upanikṣipto * avasīdati | na saṃtiṣṭhate | evam eva mahā-rāja + an-anta-yaśā avasīdati na saṃtiṣṭhate | atha rājā priyaṃkaro rājānam an-anta-yaśasaṃ tathā + avasīdantaṃ | upasaṃkramya + etad avocat | kiṃ vayaṃ mahā-rāja lokasya vyākuryāmaḥ | kiṃ rājño * an-anta-yaśasaḥ su-bhāṣitam iti | sa āha | vaktavyaṃ | mahā-rāja-an-anta-yaśāś catur-dvīpeṣu rājya-aiśvaryaṃ kārayitvā + a-bandhya-mano-rathatām anubhūya sarva-druma-a-kāla-phalatāṃ sarva-upadrava-prasrabdhi-sarva-satva-a-bandhya-mano-rathatāṃ gandha-udaka-varṣaṃ hiraṇya-varṣaṃ suvarṇa-varṣaṃ sarva-upakaraṇa-varṣaṃ ca + anubhūya caturo mahā-dvīpān adhyāvasitvā śakrasya + ardha-āsanam ākramyāti + icchayā na mukto * a-tṛpta eva kāmaiḥ kāla-gata iti | evaṃ tvaṃ mahā-rāja vyākuryā ity evam uktvā ca rājā + an-anta-yaśāḥ kālam akārṣīt | pe ||
body.translated_text: Herein is [told] the story of the emperor <s>Anantayaśas</s> (Infinite Glory), who, having fallen from heaven, is recited to [thus] while surrounded by princes and citizens: 'Just as, O Great King, a lump of clarified butter or a lump of fresh butter, when placed upon heated sand, sinks down and does not remain — in just this way, O Great King, <s>Anantayaśas</s> sinks down and does not remain.' Then King <s>Priyaṃkara</s> (the Beloved), approaching King <s>Anantayaśas</s> who was sinking down in this way, said: 'Shall we, O Great King, proclaim to the world? Shall we proclaim the noble speech of King <s>Anantayaśas</s>?' He said: 'It should be proclaimed. Great King <s>Anantayaśas</s>, having exercised sovereignty over the four continents, having experienced the non-barrenness of his wishes, having caused all trees to bear fruit out of season, having brought about the cessation of all calamities, the non-barrenness of all beings' wishes, rains of scented water, rains of silver, rains of gold, and rains of all provisions, having inhabited the four great continents, having ascended to the half-seat of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) — even with excessive desire was not freed, and unsatisfied with pleasures, has passed away.' 'Thus, O Great King, you should proclaim.' And having spoken thus, King <s>Anantayaśas</s> died. [abbreviated]

body.text: tasmāt tarhi te mahā-rāja marīcikāyām udaka-sva-bhāvo na + abhūn na bhaviṣyati na ca + etarhi vidyate | evam eva mahā-rāja rūpa-vedanā-saṃjñā saṃskāra-vijñanāṃ sva-bhāvo na + abhūn na bhaviṣyati na ca + etarhi vidyatae ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, O great king, in a mirage, the nature of water has never existed, will never exist, and does not exist now. Even so, O great king, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness —'

body.text: punar apy uktaṃ | etāvac ca + etat jñeyam | yad uta saṃvṛtiḥ parama-arthaś ca | tac ca bhagavatā śūnyataḥ su-dṛṣṭaṃ su-viditaṃ su-sākṣāt-kṛtaṃ | tena sa sarva-jña ity ucyate | tatra saṃvṛtir loka-pracāratas tathā-gatena dṛṣṭā | yaḥ punaḥ parama-arthaḥ so * an-abhilāpyaḥ | an-ājñeyo * a-vijñeyo * a-deśito * a-prakāśito yāvad a-kriyo yāvan na lābho na + a-lābho na sukhaṃ na duṣkhaṃ na yaśo na + a-yaśaḥ | na rūpaṃ na + a-rūpam ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: And again it is stated: 'And just this much is to be known: namely, the conventional (<s>saṃvṛti</s>) and the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>). And that has been well-seen, well-known, and well-realized by the Blessed One from [the standpoint of] emptiness. Therefore he is the Omniscient One —'

body.text: tatra jinena jagasya kṛtena saṃvṛti deśita loka-hitāya | yena jagat su-gatasya sakāśe saṃjanayīha prasāda-sukha-arthe ||
body.translated_text: 'Therein, the <s>Jina</s> (Victor), who has acted for the world, has taught the conventional for the welfare of the world — by which the world, in the presence of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), may generate here faith and happiness.'

body.text: saṃvṛti prajña-mayī nara-siṃhaḥ ṣaḍ-gatayo bhaṇi satva-gaṇānāṃ | naraka-tiraś ca tathā + eva ca pretān āsura-kāya narāṃś ca marūṃś ca ||
body.translated_text: 'The Lion among Men has taught, with conventional [truth] consisting of wisdom, the six destinies of the hosts of beings — hells, animals, <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), the <s>asura</s>-bodies, humans, and gods.'

body.text: nīca-kulāṃs tatha ucca-kulāṃś ca āḍhya-kulāṃś ca daridra-kulāṃś ca + ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: 'Those of low birth and those of high birth, those of wealthy families and those of poor families' — and so on.

body.text: punaś ca + uktaṃ | katama eṣa dharmo yo bhagavatā vyākṛto * an-uttarāyāṃ samyak-saṃbodhau | kiṃ rūpam uta vedanā āho śvit saṃjñā uta-āho saṃskārā atha vijñānaṃ bhagavatā vyākṛtam an-uttarāyāṃ samyak-saṃbodhāv iti | teṣām etad abhūt | na rūpaṃ yāvan na vijñānaṃ bhagavatā vyākṛtam an-uttarāyāṃ samyak-saṃbodhau | tat kasya hetoḥ | an-utpādo hi rūpam an-utpādo bodhiḥ | tat katham an-utpādo * an-utpādam abhisaṃbudhyate | evaṃ yāvad vijñānam || pe ||
body.translated_text: And again it is stated: 'What is this <s>dharma</s> that has been predicted by the Blessed One [to lead to] supreme, perfect <s>bodhi</s>? Is it form? Or feeling? Or perception? Or formations? Or consciousness? —'

body.text: tad evam an-upalabhyamāneṣu sarva-dharmeṣu katamo * atra buddhaḥ | katamā bodhiḥ | katamo bodhi-satvaḥ | katamad vyākaraṇam | śūnyaṃ hi rūpaṃ rūpeṇa yāvad vijñānaṃ || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'Thus, when all <s>dharmas</s> are unobtainable, what here is the <s>Buddha</s>? What is <s>bodhi</s>? What is the <s>bodhisattva</s>? What is the prediction? For form is empty of form — up to consciousness —'

body.text: yāvad eva vyavahāra-mātram etat | nāma-dhey-mātraṃ saṃketa-mātraṃ saṃvṛti-mātraṃ prajñapti-mātraṃ | na + alam atra paṇḍitair abhiniveśa utpādayitavya iti ||
body.translated_text: 'It is merely conventional usage; merely a name-designation; merely a sign; merely conventional [truth]; merely a designation. Herein the wise should not generate attachment.'

body.text: tathā + atra + eva + āhuḥ | nirmāṇa-ratayo devā yathā vayaṃ bhagavan | bhagavato bhāṣitasya + artham ājānīmaḥ | sarva-dharmā bhūta-koṭir an-anta-koṭir an-āvaraṇa-koṭir a-pratiṣṭhita-koṭir ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: And in the same [text], the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods say: 'Just as we, O Blessed One, understand the meaning of the Blessed One's teaching: all <s>dharmas</s> are the ultimate point of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>), the infinite point, without obstruction —'

body.text: sarva-dharmā bhagavan bodhiḥ | sva-bhāva-virahitā boddhavyāḥ | antaśa ānantaryāṇy api bodhiḥ | tat kasya hetoḥ | a-prakṛtikā hi bhagavan bodhir a-prakṛtikāni ca * pañca + ānantaryāṇi | tena + ucyate ānantaryāṇi bodhir iti | tathā vihasyante bhagavan ye ke-cit parinirvātu-kāmāḥ | tat kasya hetoḥ | yadi kaś-cit saṃsāra-pratipanno bhavet | sa nirvāṇaṃ paryeṣatae iti ||
body.translated_text: 'All <s>dharmas</s>, O Blessed One, are <s>bodhi</s>. They are to be understood as devoid of their own nature. Even the <s>ānantaryas</s> (heinous crimes) are <s>bodhi</s>. For what reason? Because <s>bodhi</s>, O Blessed One, is without inherent nature, and the <s>ānantaryas</s> too —'

body.text: punar uktaṃ | bhūta-koṭir iti bhagavan yad uktaṃ nirmāṇa-ratibhir devais tatra vayaṃ bhūtam api na + upalabhāmahe | kiṃ punar asya koṭim | tat kasya hetoḥ | yo hi kaś-cid bhagavan bhūtam upalabhate | koṭim api sa tasya + upalabhate dvaye ca + asau carati + iti ||
body.translated_text: And again it is stated: 'That which you, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, have called "the ultimate point of reality" (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) — therein we do not even apprehend "reality" (<s>bhūta</s>). How much less its "point" (<s>koṭi</s>)! For what reason? Whoever —'

body.text: tathā + atra + eva sahāṃpati-brahmaṇā śāstā stutaḥ ||
body.translated_text: And in the same [text], the Teacher is praised by <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>:

body.text: supiti yatha naraḥ kṣudhā + abhibhūtaḥ śata-rasa-bhojana-bhuñjino ca tṛptaḥ | na pi ca kṣudha na bhojanaṃ na satvaḥ supina yathā + eva nidṛṣṭa sarva-dharmāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as a man oppressed by hunger sleeps and [dreams of] eating food of a hundred flavors, and is satisfied — yet there is neither hunger, nor food, nor a being — so, as in a dream, all <s>dharmas</s> are [to be] seen.'

body.text: bhaṇi naru paṭhane mano-jña-vācaṃ priyu bhavatī na ca saṃkramo * asti vācaṃ | na ca vacana ca + asya rakta vācām upalabhase na ca tatra saṃśayo * asti ||
body.translated_text: 'A man speaks a pleasant word in recitation; it becomes dear, yet there is no transference of the word. You do not apprehend the word, nor one attached to words — and there is no doubt about this.'

body.text: śruṇati yatha mano-jña vīṇa-śabdaṃ madhura na ca + asti sva-bhāvataḥ sa śabdaḥ | tatha imi vidu skandha prekṣamāṇo na labhati bhāvu sva-bhāvataḥ su-medhāḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as one hears the pleasant sound of a <s>vīṇā</s>, sweet — yet that sound does not exist by its own nature — so the wise one, examining these <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), does not find any entity by its own nature.' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: yatha naru iha śaṅkha-śabda śrutvā vimṛśati vidva kuto ya prādu-bhūtaḥ | na ca labhati sva-bhāva śūnya-bhāvaṃ tatha tv aya dṛṣṭa nara-indra sarva-dharmāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as a man here, having heard the sound of a conch, investigates — "Whence has this appeared?" — and does not find its own nature, [finding only] the nature of emptiness — so, O Lord of Men, all <s>dharmas</s> are seen.'

body.text: yatha naru iha bhojanaṃ praṇītaṃ vimṛśati aṅgaśu siddham a-svabhāvam | yatha rasu tatha te * aṅga tat-sva-bhāvās tatha tv aya dṛṣṭa maha-rṣi sarva-dharmāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as a man here investigates excellent food — accomplished in its parts yet without own-nature — as the flavor, so those parts and their own natures — so, O Great Sage, all <s>dharmas</s> are seen.'

body.text: yatha naru iha indra-yaṣṭi dṛṣṭvā vimṛśati aṅgaśu niḥ-sva-bhāva śūnyam | vimṛśatu yatha yaṣṭi te * aṅga śūnyās tatha tv aya dṛṣṭa maha-rṣi sarva-dharmāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as a man here, having seen a rainbow, investigates it part by part — without own-nature, empty — investigate as you may, the rainbow and those parts are empty — so, O Great Sage, all <s>dharmas</s> are seen.'

body.text: pura-vara yatha aṅgaśo vibhajya nagaru sva-bhāvatu nāmato na labdham | yatha nagara tatha + aṅga sarva-śūnyās tatha tv aya dṛṣṭa nara-indra sarva-dharmāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as, having analyzed an excellent city part by part, the city is not found by its own nature even by name — as the city, so all those parts are empty — so, O Lord of Men, all <s>dharmas</s> are seen.'

body.text: mudita yatha narāga mukta bherī harṣa janeti sva-bhāva-śūnya-śabdā | svaru yatha tatha te * aṅga tat-svabhāvaṃ tatha tv aya dṛṣṭa maha-rṣi sarva-dharmāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as [when one] strikes a drum, free from attachment, with joy — it produces delight, [though] its sound is empty of own-nature — as the sound, so those parts and their own nature — so, O Great Sage, all <s>dharmas</s> are seen.'

body.text: ... ... hanatu yatha narasya tāṃ hi bherīṃ pratighu na vidyati na + api sneha-dhātuḥ | vimṛśatu bherī + iva te * aṅga tat-sva-bhāvās tatha tv aya dṛṣṭa nara-indra sarva-dharmāḥ ||
body.translated_text: '... When one strikes that drum for a man, neither hostility nor the element of affection is found [in it]. Investigate — like a drum, those parts and their own natures — so, O Lord of Men, all <s>dharmas</s> are seen.'

body.text: hanatu yatha narasya tāṃ hi bherīṃ svaru na sa manyati rāmayāmi lokam | svaru yatha tatha te * aṅga tat-sva-bhāvāḥ tatha tv aya dṛṣṭa nara-indra sarva-dharmāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'When one strikes that drum for a man, the sound does not think "I delight the world." As the sound, so those parts and their own natures — so, O Lord of Men, all <s>dharmas</s> are seen.'

body.text: hanatu yatha narasya tasya bheryāṃ na pi svaru aṅgaśu na + api sa sva-tantraḥ | svaru yatha tatha te * aṅga tat-sva-bhāvās tatha tv aya dṛṣṭa maha-rṣi sarva-dharmāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'When one strikes that drum, the sound is not found in its parts, nor is it self-governed. As the sound, so those parts and their own natures — so, O Great Sage, all <s>dharmas</s> are seen.'

body.text: punaś ca + uktaṃ | satva-ārambaṇa-nāyakena kathitā maitrī śubhā-bhāvanā | satvaś ca + asya vibhāvitaḥ su-viditaṃ niḥ-satva sarvaṃ jagat | tatra + evaṃ dvi-pada-uttamo * a-kaluṣo niḥ-saṃśayā mānasaḥ | tena tvā su-gataṃ vibhāvita-matiṃ pūjema pūjā-ariham ||
body.translated_text: And again it is stated: 'Loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and the contemplation of the pure (<s>śubhā-bhāvanā</s>) have been taught by the Guide who takes beings as his object. And a "being" has been conceptually constructed by him, [while] it is well-known that the entire world is devoid of beings. Therein, [the praise by] the <s>dvipada</s> (two-footed) best —'

body.text: duṣkhaṃ cā * su-gatā

children.text: daśa-ddiśi-gataṃ na + evaṃ parīdṛśyate | satveṣū karuṇā ca nāma bhaṇitā deva-ati-deva tvayā | evaṃ bho jina-puṅ-gavā jina-mataṃ ajñāta yathāvataḥ | tena tvāṃ dvi-pada-uttamā nara-varāḥ pūjema pūjā-ariham ||
children.translated_text: '— going in the ten directions, is not thus perceived. And compassion toward beings has been proclaimed by you, O god above gods. Thus, O bulls among <s>Jinas</s>, the doctrine of the <s>Jina</s> not being known as it truly is — therefore we, the best of two-footed [beings], the excellent among men, would worship you, who are worthy of worship.'

body.translated_text: 'And suffering, O <s>Sugata</s> —'

body.text: satvāna + eva na duṣkhaṃ śākya-muninā yasya + apanītaṃ dukhaṃ | jātās te muditāś ca hṛṣṭa-manaso * a-ratīś ca tair na + uditāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'There are no beings, and no suffering — [yet] the <s>Śākya</s> sage has removed suffering. Those [beings] are born joyful and glad of mind, and discontent does not arise in them.'

body.text: evaṃ buddha-nayaṃ a-cintiya-nayaṃ yāthāvato jānato | tasmāt pūjiya tvāṃ narāṇa pravaraṃ prāyema prāptaṃ phalaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'Thus, knowing the way of the <s>Buddha</s> — the inconceivable way — as it truly is, therefore, having worshipped you, the best of men, may we attain the fruit.'

body.text: kāyaḥ kāya-vivarjitena muninā na + āsādito mārgatāṃ | na + evaṃ te smṛti-nāyakā na bhaṇitā na + eva pramuṣṭā smṛtiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'The body has not been found by the Sage who is free from body. Nor have the foundations of mindfulness been proclaimed by you, nor has mindfulness been lost.'

body.text: uktaṃ ca + u su-gatena bhāva-pathimāḥ kāyaṃ gatā bhāvanāḥ | evaṃ buddha-nayaṃ viditva su-gatā pūjā kṛtā tāyinaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'And it has been stated by the <s>Sugata</s>: cultivations that follow the path of existence have gone to the body. Thus, knowing the way of the <s>Buddha</s>, worship has been made to the <s>Sugata</s>, the Protector.'

body.text: bhāvethaḥ śamathaṃ vipaśyanam ayaṃ mārgaṃ dukhā śāntaye | śāntās te bhagavan sa-vāsana-malā yehī jagat kliṣyate ||
body.translated_text: 'Cultivate <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) — this path for the cessation of suffering. Pacified, O Blessed One, are those stains together with their residual impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) by which the world is afflicted.'

body.text: śamathaś ca + atha vipaśyanā na ca malā sarve * ati śūnyā mune | asmin deva-gaṇā na kāṅkṣa kva-canā pūjentu tvāṃ nāyakaṃ | ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: 'Both <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>, and the stains too — all are utterly empty, O Sage. Herein, O hosts of gods, do not doubt anywhere! Worship the Guide!' And so on.

body.text: punar uktaṃ | śūnyaṃ hi cakṣuś cakṣuḥ-sva-bhāvena | yasya ca dharmasya sva-bhāvo na vidyate so * a-vastukaḥ | yo * a-vastukaḥ so * a-pariniṣpannaḥ yo * a-pariniṣpannaḥ sa na + utpadyate na nirudhyate | pe ||
body.translated_text: And again it is stated: 'For the eye is empty of the own-nature of the eye. And that <s>dharma</s> whose own-nature is not found is without substance (<s>avastuka</s>). What is without substance is not fully accomplished. What is not fully accomplished neither arises nor ceases.' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: yat triṣv apy adhvasu na + upalabhyate na tac cakṣur na + indriyaṃ kathaṃ tasya vyavahāro jñeyaḥ | tad yathā + api nāma rikta-muṣṭir a-līkaḥ | yāvad eva nāma-mātraṃ na + u tu khalu parama-arthato riktam upalabhyate na muṣṭiḥ | evaṃ cakṣuś ca + indriyaṃ ca rikte muṣṭi-sadṛśam a-līkam a-sad-bhūtaṃ tucchaṃ mṛṣā-moṣa-dharme bāla-upalāpanaṃ mūrkha-saṃmohanam yāvad eva nāma-mātram ||
body.translated_text: 'That which is not apprehended in any of the three times — that is not the eye, not a sense-faculty. How is its conventional usage to be understood? Just as an empty fist is not false — it is merely a name; but in the ultimate sense, neither "empty" nor "fist" is apprehended.
