Even so, the eye and the sense-faculty are like an empty fist — not false, not truly existent, hollow, of the nature of falsity and deception, an amusement for children, a delusion of the foolish — merely a name.'

body.text: punar atra + eva + āha | svapna-antare mahā-vṛṣṭir āsravāṇāṃ pravartanā | darśitā te mahā-vīra āsrava-utpatti-paṇḍitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: And again in the same [text] it says: 'A great rain within a dream — the operation of the <s>āsravas</s> (outflows) has been shown by you, O Great Hero, who are skilled in the arising of the outflows.'

body.text: svapne yathā śiraś-chedo dṛṣṭas te āsrava-kṣayaḥ | darśitaḥ sarva-vijñānāṃ sarva-darśin namo * astu te ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as in a dream, the cutting off of the head is seen — [so] the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s> has been shown by you to all who possess consciousness. O All-Seeing One, homage to you!'

body.text: atra + eva ca drumeṇa kinnara-rājena bhagavān pṛṣṭaḥ pratyāha | yad vadasi śūnyatāṃ ca vyākaraṇaṃ | ca + apy ahaṃ na jānāmi | syād yadi kiṃ-cid a-śūnyaṃ na bhavej jinena + asya vyākaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: And in the same [text], when the Blessed One was questioned by <s>Druma</s>, the king of the <s>Kinnaras</s>, he replied: 'You speak of both emptiness and prediction. Yet even I do not know [them as ultimately existing]. If there were anything non-empty, there would be a prediction of it by the <s>Jina</s>.'

body.text: kiṃ-kāraṇaṃ | tathā hi | sthitaṃ bhavet tat svake bhave | kūṭa-stha-nir-vikāraṃ | na tasya vṛddhir na parihāṇiḥ | na kriyā na ca kāraṇaṃ | yat sva-bhāva-śūnyam ādarśa-maṇḍale su-pariśuddhe saṃdṛśyate pratibimbam | tathā + eva druma jānīhi + imān dharmān | a-vi-kāraṃ dharma-dhātum imāṃ ca pūjāṃ druma + aṅgaśo vicārayasi | aṅgaśo nirīkṣya pūjāṃ | katame * a-vi-kāriṇo * aṅgāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'For what reason? For thus: that would remain in its own existence — immovable, unchanging. There would be no increase and no decline for it, no action and no cause. [But] that which is empty of own-nature — [is] like an image seen in a well-purified mirror-disc. Even so, <s>Druma</s>, understand these <s>dharmas</s>. The <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) is unchanging. And you, <s>Druma</s>, analyze this worship part by part. Having examined the worship part by part — what are the unchanging parts?'

body.text: yad api ca nir-īhakatvaṃ kriyāṃ ca na jānase mayā proktaṃ | śakaṭa-aṅga saṃnipātaṃ nirīkṣva śakaṭasya ca + eva kriyāṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'And as for the objection that you do not understand how there can be [both] effortlessness and action — what I have taught: look at the coming together of the parts of a cart, and [then] the function of the cart itself.'

body.text: karma ca me ākhyātaṃ kartā na vidyate daśasu dikṣu | vāta-īritād iva taror yathā hi nivartate vahniḥ ||
body.translated_text: '<s>Karma</s> has been declared by me, [yet] no doer is found in the ten directions — just as fire turns away from a tree blown by the wind.'

body.text: na ca māruto na ca taruś cetayati huta-aśanaṃ ca yajane | na nivartate vahnis tathā + eva karmasya kartāraḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Neither the wind nor the tree intends the fire [used] in sacrifice. The fire does not turn away [by itself] — even so [it is] with the doers of <s>karma</s>.'

body.text: yad api vadase na ca saṃcaya puṇyasya hi vidyate | su-caritasya samudāgamaś ca | bodhis tasya + api śṛṇu kramanta tvaṃ | yathā bhaṇasi manuṣyāṇām āyuḥ-parimāṇaṃ varṣa-śataṃ jīvin | na ca + asti varṣa-puñjī | ayam api samudāgamas tad-vad iti ||
body.translated_text: 'And as for your objection that no accumulation of merit is found, yet there is the attainment of good conduct and <s>bodhi</s> as well — listen to me, O <s>Druma</s>, as I explain: just as you say that the measure of human life is a hundred years — yet no heap of years exists — even so is this attainment.'

body.text: bhagavatyām apy uktaṃ | kiṃ punar āyuṣman subhūte utpanno dharma utpadyate uta + an-utpannaḥ | subhūtir āha | na + aham āyuṣman śāriputra utpannasya dharmasya + utpattim icchāmi na ca + an-utpannasya + iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Bhagavatī</s> (Prajñāpāramitā) also it is stated: 'Now, O Elder <s>Subhūti</s>, does an arisen <s>dharma</s> arise, or an unarisen one?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'I do not, O Elder <s>Śāriputra</s>, wish for the arising of an arisen <s>dharma</s>, nor of an unarisen one.'

body.text: dharma-saṃgītyām apy uktaṃ | tathatā tathatā + iti kula-putra śūnyatāyā etad adhivacanaṃ | sā ca śūnyatā na + utpadyate na nirudhyate | āha | yady evaṃ dharmāḥ śūnyā uktā bhagavatā tasmāt sarva-dharmā na + utpatsyante na nirotsyante | nir-ārambho bodhi-satvaḥ | āha | evam eva kula-putra tathā yathā + abhisaṃbudhyase sarva-dharmā na + utpadyante na nirudhyante | āha | yad etad uktaṃ bhagavatā | saṃskṛtā dharmā utpadyante nirudhyante ca + ity asya tathā-gata-bhāṣitasya ko * abhiprāyaḥ | āha | utpāda-nirodha-abhiniviṣṭaḥ kula-putra loka-saṃniveśaḥ | tatra tathā-gato mahā-kāruṇiko lokasya + uttrāsa-pada-parihāra-arthaṃ vyavahāra-vaśād uktavān utpadyante nirudhyante ca + iti | na ca + atra kasya-cid dharmasya + utpādo na nirodha iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Dharmasaṃgīti</s> also it is said: '<s>Tathatā</s>, <s>tathatā</s> (suchness, suchness) — O son of good family, this is a designation for emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>). And that emptiness neither arises nor ceases.' He said: 'If the <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared <s>dharmas</s> to be empty, then all <s>dharmas</s> will neither arise nor cease — the <s>bodhisattva</s> is without effort.' He replied: 'Exactly so, O son of good family, just as you have understood: all <s>dharmas</s> neither arise nor cease.' He said: 'As to what the <s>Bhagavān</s> has stated — "Conditioned <s>dharmas</s> arise and cease" — what is the intention of this <s>Tathāgata</s>-utterance?' He replied: 'The worldly convention, O son of good family, is fixated upon arising and cessation. Therein, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the Greatly Compassionate One, for the sake of removing the cause of fear from the world, has spoken in conformity with conventional usage, saying "they arise and they cease." But herein there is no arising of any <s>dharma</s>, nor cessation.'

body.text: punar atra + eva + uktaṃ | tatra bhagavaṃś cakṣū-rūpeṣu na raṇati śrotraṃ | śabdeṣu | yāvan mano-dharmeṣu na raṇati | sa dharmaḥ | tatra kathaṃ cakṣū-rūpeṣu na raṇati | saṃsarga-a-bhāvāt | na hi cakṣū-rūpeṇa saṃsṛjyate | yāvan na mano-dharmeṇa saṃsṛjyate | yan na saṃsṛjyate tan na raṇati | a-dvitīyasya bhagavan dharmasya raṇaṃ na + asti | a-dvitīyāś ca bhagavan sarva-dharmāḥ paras-paraṃ na jānanti na vijānanti | na kalpayanti na vikalpayanti | na saṃbhavanti na visaṃbhavanti | na hīyante na varddhante | na rajyanti | na virajyanti | na saṃsaranti na parinirvānti na + ete kasya-cit | na + eṣāṃ kaś-cit | na + ete bhagavan dharmā udvijante na saṃkliśyante na vyavadāyante | evam ahaṃ bhagavan jānāmy evam avabudhye | yad apy ahaṃ | bhagavann evaṃ vadāmi | evam ahaṃ jānāmy evam ahaṃ budhyāmi + iti | āyatanānām eṣa vi-kāraḥ | na ca bhagavann āyatanānām evaṃ bhavati | asmākam eṣa vi-kāra iti | yo hy evaṃ jānāti sa na kena-cit sārddhaṃ vivadati | yan na vivadati tac * chramaṇa-dharmam anusarati + iti | tathā dharma-darśanaṃ buddha-darśanaṃ sarva-satva-darśanaṃ sarva-satva-hetu-pratyaya-darśanaṃ śūnyatā-darśanaṃ śūnyatā-darśanam a-darśanaṃ | a-darśanaṃ bhagavan sarva-dharmāṇāṃ darśanaṃ samyag-darśanam iti ||
body.translated_text: Again, in this very [sūtra] it is said: 'Therein, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, the eye does not delight in forms; the ear [does not delight] in sounds; up to: the mind does not delight in <s>dharmas</s>. That is the <s>Dharma</s>. How does the eye not delight in forms? Because of the absence of contact — for the eye does not come into contact with form; up to: the mind does not come into contact with <s>dharmas</s>. That which does not come into contact does not delight. For a non-dual <s>dharma</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, there is no delight. And all <s>dharmas</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, are non-dual — they do not know each other, do not cognize each other; they do not construct, do not discriminate; they do not arise, do not decline; they do not decrease, do not increase; they do not become attached, do not become detached; they do not transmigrate, do not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — they do not belong to anyone, and no one belongs to them. These <s>dharmas</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, do not tremble, are not defiled, are not purified. Thus I know, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, thus I understand. And even that I say thus — "thus I know, thus I understand" — this is a modification of the sense-bases. And, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, it does not occur to the sense-bases thus: "this is our modification." For one who knows thus does not dispute with anyone. What is non-dispute — that follows the <s>śramaṇa-dharma</s> (ascetic's way).' Likewise: 'Seeing <s>dharma</s> is seeing the <s>Buddha</s>; seeing all beings; seeing the causes and conditions of all beings; seeing emptiness. And the seeing of emptiness is non-seeing. Non-seeing, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, of all <s>dharmas</s> is right seeing, true seeing.'

body.text: katham an-adhiṣṭhānā saṃvṛtir yuktā | kathaṃ punar a-yuktā | yathā + a-sati sthāṇau puruṣa-bhrāntiḥ | kasya punaḥ śūnyatā-vādinaḥ parama-arthataḥ sthāṇuḥ siddho yad-āśrayāt puruṣa-bhrāntiḥ syād | a-mūlā eva ca sarva-dharmās tatvato mūla-an-upapatteḥ ||
body.translated_text: How is convention (<s>saṃvṛti</s>) without a substrate fitting? How again is it unfitting? Just as, in the absence of a [real] post, there is the delusion of [seeing] a person — but for whom, the proponent of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā-vādin</s>), is the post ultimately established, on the basis of which the delusion of a person would occur? And all <s>dharmas</s> are indeed rootless, since a root is ultimately untenable.

body.text: tathā ca + uktam ārya-vimalakīrti-nirdeśe | a-bhūta-parikalpasya kiṃ mūlaṃ | āha | viparyastā saṃjñā mūlaṃ | āha | viparyastāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ kiṃ mūlaṃ | a-pratiṣṭhānaṃ mūlaṃ | āha | a-pratiṣṭhāyāḥ kiṃ mūlaṃ | āha | yan mañjuśrīr a-pratiṣṭhānaṃ na tasya kiñ-cin mūlam iti hy a-pratiṣṭhāna-mūla-pratiṣṭhitāḥ sarva-dharmā iti ||
body.translated_text: And thus it is said in the <s>Ārya-Vimalakīrtinirdeśa</s>: 'What is the root of false conceptual construction (<s>abhūta-parikalpa</s>)?' He said: 'Inverted perception (<s>viparyasta-saṃjñā</s>) is the root.' He said: 'What is the root of inverted perception?' 'Groundlessness (<s>apratiṣṭhāna</s>) is the root.' He said: 'What is the root of groundlessness?' He said: 'O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, that which is groundless has no root whatsoever. Thus, all <s>dharmas</s> are established upon the root of groundlessness.'

body.text: iyaṃ samāsataḥ prajñā-pāramitā citta-śuddhy-arthinā bhāvayitavyā | bhāvayitvā ca kleśa-ripu-raṇa-kuśalena bhavitavyaṃ | na sva-gṛha-śūreṇa ||
body.translated_text: This is, in summary, the Perfection of Wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) to be cultivated by one who seeks the purification of the mind. And having cultivated it, one should become skilled in the battle against the enemy of the afflictions — not merely a hero within one's own house.

body.text: yathā + uktam ārya-dharma-saṃgīti-sūtre | na śūnyatā-vādī loka-dharmaiḥ saṃhriyate * a-niśritatvāt | na sa lābhena saṃhṛṣyāti | a-lābhena na vi-manā bhavati | yaśasā na vismayate * a-yaśasā na saṃkucati | nindayā na + avalīyate | praśaṃsayā na + anunīyate | sukhena na rajyate duṣkhena na virajyate | yo hy evaṃ loka-dharmair na saṃhriyate sa śūnyatāṃ jānītae iti ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Ārya-Dharmasaṃgīti Sūtra</s>: 'One who speaks of emptiness is not overcome by worldly conditions (<s>lokadharmāḥ</s>), because of non-reliance. He does not rejoice at gain; he is not dejected at loss. He is not intoxicated by fame; he does not shrink from disgrace. He is not daunted by blame; he is not mollified by praise. He is not attached to pleasure; he is not repelled by suffering. For one who is not overcome by worldly conditions in this way — he knows emptiness.'

body.text: tathā śūnyatā-vādino na kva-cid anurāgo na vi-rāgaḥ | yasmin rajyeta tac * chūnyam eva jānīte | śūnyam eva paśyati | na + asau śūnyatāṃ jānīte yaḥ kva-cid dharme rajyate vā virajyate vā tathā na + asau śūnyatāṃ jānīte yaḥ kena-cit sārddhaṃ vi-grahaṃ vi-vādaṃ vā kuryāc * chūnyam eva jānīte tac * chūnyam eva paśyati + ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: Likewise: 'For one who speaks of emptiness, there is no attachment anywhere, nor aversion. Whatever he might be attached to — he knows it as empty; he sees it as empty. One who is attached to any <s>dharma</s> or is averse to it does not know emptiness. Likewise, one who enters into conflict or dispute with anyone does not know emptiness — he knows it as empty, he sees it as empty,' and so on.

body.text: etat saṃkṣepāc citta-śodhanam ||
body.translated_text: This is, in brief, the purification of the mind (<s>citta-śodhana</s>).

body.text: atha + evam api parama-viśuddhir dharma-darśane sati | iha pañca-kaṣāya-saṃkliṣṭasya kalyāṇa-mitra-avasāditasya vā saṃkṣepeṇa tāvat kutra yatnaṃ kṛtvā śīghraṃ citta-śuddhir bhavati | ātma-bahu-māna-para-avajñā-tyāge * anayor mūlam ātma-satva-dṛṣṭiḥ | sā ca + etad-abhyāsāt su-karaṃ prahīyatae iti para-gauravam ātma-avajñā ca + evaṃ bhāvanīyā ||
body.translated_text: Now, even thus, the supreme purification [comes] when there is the seeing of <s>Dharma</s>. Here, for one afflicted by the five corruptions (<s>pañcakaṣāya</s>), or for one who has been led astray by evil friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra-avasādita</s>) — in brief, where should one exert effort so that purification of mind occurs swiftly? In the abandonment of self-importance (<s>ātmabahu-māna</s>) and contempt for others (<s>parāvajñā</s>). The root of these two is the view of self and being (<s>ātma-satva-dṛṣṭi</s>). And that, through practice of this [teaching], is easily abandoned. Thus, reverence for others and self-deprecation should be cultivated in this manner:

body.text: yadi satvo yadi skandhāḥ kṣamatā sarvathā sthitā | ekasya hi para-ātmatvaṃ viruddhaṃ saṃbhavet kathaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Whether a [real] being or [merely] the aggregates (<s>skandhāḥ</s>) — forbearance applies in every case. For how could the contradictory [notions of] self and other arise for one [and the same entity]?

body.text: vinā + ālambanam apy etad ācaranty eva dehinaḥ | an-ādi-kalyāna-abhyāsāt kim abhyāsasya duṣ-karam ||
body.translated_text: Even without an [actual] object, embodied beings practice this indeed, through beginningless habituation to wholesome [conduct]. What is difficult for habituation [to accomplish]?

body.text: evam abhyāsa-vaśyatve tulye kasmāt sukha-udayam | para-gauravam utsṛjya sva-sukhāyān yad iṣyate ||
body.translated_text: When the susceptibility to habituation is equal [in both cases], why does one, abandoning reverence for others, choose what produces happiness for oneself?

body.text: cintā-maṇir yathā + uktāś ca santi gaurava-hetavaḥ | na tu me gauravāt saukhyam iha + api jana-dur-bhagāt ||
body.translated_text: Just as it has been said — and there are wish-fulfilling jewels (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>) and other causes of reverence — yet happiness does not come to me from one who is ill-fortuned among people, even from reverence.

body.text: tasmāt satva-antare yad-vad rūkṣa-matsara-māninaḥ | ātma-snehavato vṛttir bhāvayet tad-viparyayam ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, just as towards other beings one who is harsh, jealous, and proud [acts with] self-love — one should cultivate the opposite of that.

body.text: ātmano bahu-māno * ayaṃ stuti-nindā-ādi-sekataḥ | vardhate nāraka-vaśāt sekān naraka-vahni-vat ||
body.translated_text: This self-importance grows through the sprinkling of praise and blame and so forth, just as from the sprinkling of hellfire the hell-fires [grow] through the power of hell.

body.text: śabdas tāvad a-cittatvān māṃ stauti + iti na saṃbhavaḥ | paraḥ kila mayi prīta ity ayaṃ me mati-bhramaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Words, being without mind, cannot think "this one praises me" — that is impossible. This is my delusion of thought: "another is supposedly pleased with me."

body.text: tat-tuṣṭyā + eva mama prītiḥ sāmānye na sadā + astu sā | tat-sukhena na cet kāryaṃ tena tuṣṭena kiṃ mama ||
body.translated_text: My pleasure is only from his satisfaction — but should that be the same [toward] everyone? If there is nothing to be gained from his happiness, then what is his satisfaction to me?

body.text: anyatra mayi vā prītyā kiṃ hi me parakīyayā | na me pareṇa tuṣṭena kāye saukhyam iha + aṇv api ||
body.translated_text: Whether another's pleasure is in me or elsewhere — how does another's pleasure [benefit] me? Not even an atom of bodily well-being comes to me from another being satisfied.

body.text: evaṃ jñātvā prahātavyā kalpanā nir-vibandhanā | a-kīrti-nindā sat-kārā evaṃ jñeyāś ca niṣ-phalāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Having understood thus, the groundless imagining should be abandoned. Disrepute, blame, and honors — knowing them thus — are fruitless.

body.text: na dharmo na + āyur ārogyaṃ na balaṃ vandanā-ādibhiḥ | yad-vad utprāsyamānasya vikārair anya-kāyikaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Neither <s>dharma</s>, nor life-span, nor health, nor strength [comes] from homage and the like — just as for one who is being swept away, [nothing comes] from the physical transformations of another's body.

body.text: hṛṣṭasya + atha viṣaṇṇasya lābha-a-lābhau sama-udayau | vivarjya niṣ-phalaṃ tasmād bhaveyaṃ śaila-mānasaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Whether elated or dejected, gain and loss arise equally. Therefore, abandoning what is fruitless, I should become one whose mind is like a mountain.

body.text: saṃstava-tyāgāc ca śīghraṃ citta-viśuddhir bhavati | iti ||
body.translated_text: And from abandoning social attachments (<s>saṃstava</s>), purification of the mind occurs swiftly. Thus —

body.text: tatra + api cintyate | nimitta-udgraha-saṃbhūtā praty-abhijñā punaḥ punaḥ | utpādayaty anu-nayaṃ jāyate pratigho * apy ataḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein also it is considered: Recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>), arising from the grasping of signs (<s>nimitta-udgraha</s>), again and again produces affection (<s>anunaya</s>); from that, aversion (<s>pratigha</s>) is also born.

body.text: pratigha-anunayau yasya tasya pāpam a-vāritam | abhyākhyānāni citrāṇi mātsaryaṃ ca + īrṣyayā saha ||
body.translated_text: For one in whom there is aversion and affection, unhindered evil arises — various false accusations (<s>abhyākhyāna</s>), and miserliness (<s>mātsarya</s>) together with envy (<s>īrṣyā</s>).

body.text: lābha-ādi-kāmatā nāma ity ādy āvartate bahu | tasmāt sarva-prayatnena saṃstavaṃ praharen muniḥ ||
body.translated_text: The desire for gain and the like — thus it revolves extensively. Therefore, with every effort, the sage should strike down social attachment (<s>saṃstava</s>).

body.text: sādṛśyād anyad apy etad vāri-sroto-vad īkṣyate | tad eva + idam iti bhrāntyā tatve tiṣṭhāmy ato balāt ||
body.translated_text: Due to resemblance, something else too is seen — like a current of water. Through the delusion "this is that very thing," I forcibly remain in reality.

body.text: a-vastu ca + etat sādṛśyaṃ duṣkhaṃ ca janayiṣyati | ahaṃ ca + etac ca sarvaṃ ca na cirān na bhaviṣyati | iti ||
body.translated_text: And this resemblance is unreal and will produce suffering. Both I and this and all of it — before long, none will exist. Thus —

body.text: ātma-bhāva-pariśuddhiś caturdaśaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Purification of the Self (<s>ātmabhāvapariśuddhi</s>): the fourteenth chapter.

children.translated_text: XV. Purification of Enjoyments and Merit (<s>bhogapuṇyaśuddhi</s>)

body.text: bhoga-puṇya-śuddhiḥ pañcadaśaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Purification of Enjoyments and Merit (<s>bhogapuṇyaśuddhi</s>): the fifteenth chapter.

body.text: śikṣā-samuccayasya + ātma-śuddhy-an-antaraṃ bhoga-śuddhiḥ saṃcaya-a-bhāvāt | pṛthag iha lekhitā | bhoga-śuddhiṃ ca jānīyāt samyag-ājīva-śodhanāt ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>, immediately after purification of the self comes purification of enjoyments, because of the absence of accumulation. It is written here separately. One should know the purification of enjoyments through the purification of right livelihood (<s>samyag-ājīva</s>).

body.text: yathā + uktam ārya-ugra-paripṛcchāyām | iha gṛha-pate gṛhī bodhi-satvo dharmeṇa bhogān paryeṣate na + a-dharmeṇa | samena na vi-ṣameṇa | samyag-ājīvo bhavati na vi-ṣama-ājīva iti ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Ārya-Ugraparipṛcchā</s>: 'Here, O householder, a householder <s>bodhisattva</s> seeks enjoyments by <s>Dharma</s>, not by <s>adharma</s>; by fair means, not by unfair means. He is one of right livelihood (<s>samyag-ājīva</s>), not of wrong livelihood (<s>viṣama-ājīva</s>).'

body.text: ārya-ratna-meghe * apy uktaṃ | na bodhi-satvo dāyakaṃ dāna-patiṃ dṛṣṭvā + īryā-patham āracayati | kathaṃ na + īryā-patham āracayati | na śanair mandaṃ mandaṃ kramān utkṣipati na nikṣipati yuga-mātra-prekṣikayā sa-viśvasta-prekṣikayā + an-ābhoga-prekṣikayā | evaṃ kāya-kuhanāṃ na karoti | kathaṃ vāk-kuhanāṃ na karoti | na bodhi-satvo lābha-hetor lābha-nidānaṃ manda-bhāṇī mṛdu-bhāṇī na priya-bhāṇī bhavati | na + anuvartana-vacanāni niścārayati | pe ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Ratnamegha</s> also it is said: 'A <s>bodhisattva</s>, having seen a donor or <s>dānapati</s>, does not assume a [false] deportment. How does he not assume a deportment? He does not slowly and softly lift his steps or set them down, with a glance of only a yoke-length, with a look of trustworthiness, with an effortless gaze. Thus he does not engage in bodily hypocrisy (<s>kāya-kuhanā</s>). How does he not engage in verbal hypocrisy (<s>vāk-kuhanā</s>)? A <s>bodhisattva</s> does not, for the sake of gain or because of gain, speak softly, speak gently, or speak sweetly. He does not utter words of compliance.' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: kathaṃ na citta-kuhanāṃ kuroti | bodhi-satvo dāyakena dāna-patinā vā lābhena pravāryamāṇo vā ca + alpa-icchatāṃ darśayati | citte na spṛhām utpādayati | antar-dāha eṣa kula-putra yad vāca-alpa-icchatā cittena lābha-kāmatā | evaṃ hi kula-putra bodhi-satvaḥ kuhana-lapana-lābha-apagato bhavati | pe | na bodhi-satvo dāna-patiṃ vā dṛṣṭvā nimittaṃ karoti | vighāto me cīvareṇa | vighāto me pātreṇa | vighāto me glāna-bhaiṣajyena | na ca taṃ dāyakaṃ dāna-patiṃ vā kiṃ-cit prārthayate | na vācaṃ niścārayati | evaṃ hi bodhi-satvo nimitta-lābha-apagato bhavati | yāvan na bodhi-satvo dāyakaṃ dāna-patiṃ dṛṣṭvā evaṃ vācaṃ niścārayati | amukena + amukena vā me dāna-patinā + amukaṃ vastu pratipāditaṃ tasya ca mayā + amuka upakāraḥ kṛtaḥ | tena me śīlavān ayam iti kṛtvā idaṃ ca + idaṃ ca dattaṃ bahu-śruta iti | alpa-iccha iti kṛtvā | mayā ca tasya kāruṇya-cittam upasthāpya parigṛhītaṃ | pe ||
body.translated_text: How does he not engage in mental hypocrisy (<s>citta-kuhanā</s>)? 'When a <s>bodhisattva</s> is being pressed by a donor or <s>dānapati</s> with offerings, he shows few desires outwardly, but does not generate craving in his mind. This, O son of good family, is an internal burning — when there is verbal contentment but mental desire for gain. Thus, O son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> is free from the hypocrisy of flattery and pursuit of gain.' [Abbreviation.] 'A <s>bodhisattva</s>, having seen a <s>dānapati</s>, does not make hints. [He does not say:] "I am in need of a robe; I am in need of a bowl; I am in need of medicine for illness." He does not request anything from that donor or <s>dānapati</s>; he does not utter a word. Thus the <s>bodhisattva</s> is free from gain through hinting.' Up to: 'A <s>bodhisattva</s>, having seen a donor or <s>dānapati</s>, does not utter such words as: "Such-and-such <s>dānapati</s> gave me such-and-such a thing, and I did such-and-such a service for him. Therefore, thinking me virtuous, he gave this and that; [or] thinking me learned; [or] thinking me of few desires — and I, having aroused compassionate thoughts toward him, accepted [the gift]."' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: tatra kāya-kṣatir yad uta lābha-hetor lābha-nidānam ādhāvana-paridhāvanaṃ dauḥśīlya-samudācaraṇaṃ ca | citta-kṣatir yad uta prārthanā | lābhināṃ ca brahma-cāriṇām antike vyāpāda-bahulatā | evaṃ hi bodhi-satvo viṣama-paryeṣṭi-lābha-apagato bhavati | pe ||
body.translated_text: Therein, bodily harm is: running about and bustling for the sake of gain and because of gain, and the practice of misconduct (<s>dauḥśīlya</s>). Mental harm is: desire [for gain] and abundance of ill-will toward fellow practitioners who receive [offerings]. Thus the <s>bodhisattva</s> is free from gain through improper seeking.' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: iha bodhi-satvo na tulā-kūṭena na māna-kūṭena na visraṃbha-ghātikayā na dhūrtatayā lābham upārjayati | evaṃ hi bodhi-satvo * a-dharma-lābha-apagato bhavati | pe | ye te lābhā staupika-saṃsṛṣṭā vā dhārmika-saṃsṛṣṭā vā sāṃghika-saṃsṛṣṭā vā + a-dattā vā + an-anujñātā vā | tān na pratīcchati na svī-karoti | evaṃ hi bodhi-satvo * a-pariśuddha-lābha-apagato bhavati | yāval labdhā lābhaṃ na mamāyate | na dhanāyate | na saṃnidhiṃ karoti | kāla-anukālaṃ ca śramaṇa-brāhmaṇebhyo dadāti | mātā-pitṛ-mitra-amātya-jñāti-sālohitebhyaḥ kāla-anukālam ātmanā paribhuṅkte paribhuñjānaś ca + a-raktaḥ paribhuṅkte | sv-anadhyavasito na ca + ālabhyamāne lābhe kheda-cittam utpādayati | na paritapyati na ca dāyaka-dāna-patīnām antike * a-prasāda-cittam utpādayati + ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: 'Here a <s>bodhisattva</s> does not earn gain by false scales, nor by false measures, nor by breach of trust, nor by deceit. Thus the <s>bodhisattva</s> is free from unlawful gain.' [Abbreviation.] 'Whatever gains are mixed with <s>stūpa</s>-property, or mixed with <s>Dharma</s>-property, or mixed with <s>Saṅgha</s>-property, or ungiven, or unauthorized — these he does not accept, does not appropriate. Thus the <s>bodhisattva</s> is free from impure gain.' Up to: 'Having obtained gain, he does not treat it possessively, does not treasure it, does not hoard it. From time to time he gives to <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, to his mother, father, friends, ministers, relatives, and kinsmen. From time to time he himself enjoys it; and when enjoying, he enjoys without attachment, without being absorbed [in it]; and when gain is not obtained, he does not generate a mind of weariness, does not torment himself, and does not generate a mind of displeasure toward donors and patrons,' and so forth.

body.text: tatra + eṣa + apy asya bodhi-satvasya bhoga-śuddhir ātma-bhāva-śuddhi-vat para-hitāya bhavet ||
body.translated_text: Herein, this purity of enjoyments of the <s>bodhisattva</s> too should be for the benefit of others, like the purity of his own body.

body.text: yathā + uktam ārya-vimalakīrti-nirdeśe | punar a-paraṃ bhadanta śāriputra ye praviśanti + idaṃ gṛhaṃ teṣāṃ samanantara-praviṣṭānāṃ sarva-kleśā na bādhante * ayaṃ dvitīya āścarya-adbhuto dharmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Ārya-Vimalakīrtinirdeśa</s>: 'Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, those who enter this house — immediately upon entering, all their afflictions do not trouble [them]. This is the second wonderful and marvelous <s>dharma</s>.'

body.text: punar atra + eva + uktaṃ | atha tato bhojanāt sarvāvatī sā parṣat tṛptā bhūtā | na ca tat bhojanaṃ kṣīyate | yaiś ca bodhi-satvaiḥ śrāvakaiś ca śakra-brahma-loka-pālais tad anyaiś ca satvais tad bhojanaṃ bhuktaṃ teṣāṃ tādṛśaṃ sukhaṃ kāye * avakrāntaṃ yādṛśaṃ sarva-sukha-maṇḍitāyāṃ loka-dhātau bodhi-satvānāṃ sukhaṃ | sarva-roma-kūpebhyaś ca teṣāṃ tādṛśo gandhaḥ pravāti | tad yathā + api nāma tasyām eva sarva-gandha-su-gandhāyāṃ loka-dhātau vṛkṣāṇāṃ gandhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: And further in this same [sūtra] it is said: 'Then, from that food, the entire assembly was satisfied and fulfilled; yet that food was not diminished. And those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, the world-protectors, and other beings who ate that food — such happiness descended upon their bodies as the happiness of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> in a world-realm adorned with all happiness. And from all their pores there wafted such a fragrance as the fragrance of the trees in that very world-realm perfumed with all fragrances.'

body.text: punaś ca + uktaṃ | yaiś ca bhadanta + ānanda bhikṣubhir an-avakrānta-niyāmair etad bhojanaṃ bhuktaṃ teṣām eva + avakrānta-niyamānāṃ pariṇaṃsyati | pe | yair an-utpādita-bodhi-cittaiḥ satvaiḥ paribhuktaṃ teṣām utpādita-bodhi-cittānāṃ pariṇaṃsyati | yair utpādita-bodhi-cittair bhuktaṃ teṣāṃ na + a-pratilabdha-kṣāntikānāṃ pariṇaṃsyati + iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: And further it is said: 'O venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, those monks who have not yet entered the certainty [of the path] and who have eaten this food — it will be digested only when they have entered the certainty. [Abbreviation.] Those beings who have not yet generated <s>bodhicitta</s> and who have consumed [it] — it will be digested when they have generated <s>bodhicitta</s>. Those who have generated <s>bodhicitta</s> and have eaten [it] — it will not be digested until they have attained the patience [of the non-arising of dharmas],' thus in detail.

body.text: śūnyatā-karuṇā garbha-ceṣṭitāt puṇya-śodhanam ||
body.translated_text: Through activity whose essence is emptiness and compassion (<s>śūnyatā-karuṇā</s>), the purification of merit [is accomplished].

body.text: uktaṃ hy ārya-gagana-gañja-sūtre | yad uta + ahaṃ-kāra-viśuddhaṃ tad dānaṃ dadāti | mama-kāra-viśuddhaṃ tad dānaṃ dadāti | hetu-viśuddhaṃ tad dānaṃ dadāti | dṛṣṭi-viśuddhaṃ tad dānaṃ dadāti | nimitta-viśuddhaṃ tad dānaṃ dadāti | nānātva-viśuddhaṃ tad dānaṃ dadāti | vipāka-pratikāṅkṣaṇā-viśuddhaṃ tad dānaṃ dadāti | yathā gaganaṃ sama-viśuddhaṃ tad dānaṃ dadāti ||
body.translated_text: For it is stated in the <s>Ārya-Gaganagañja Sūtra</s>: 'He gives that gift purified of "I"-making (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>); he gives that gift purified of "mine"-making (<s>mamakāra</s>); he gives that gift purified of cause; he gives that gift purified of views; he gives that gift purified of signs; he gives that gift purified of diversity; he gives that gift purified of expectation of fruit; just as space is uniformly pure, he gives that gift.'

body.text: pe | yathā gaganam a-paryantam evam a-paryantī-kṛtena cittena tad dānaṃ dadāti | yathā gaganaṃ vistīrṇam an-āvaraṇam evaṃ bodhi-pariṇāmitaṃ tad dānaṃ dadāti | yathā gaganam a-rūpi evaṃ sarva-rūpa-a-niśritaṃ tad dānaṃ dadāti | yathā gaganam a-vedayitṛ | evaṃ sarva-vedita-pratiprasrabdhaṃ dānaṃ dadāti | evam a-saṃjñi a-saṃskṛtam a-vijñapti-lakṣaṇam evam a-pratijñānaṃ tad dānaṃ dadāti | yathā gaganaṃ sarva-buddha-kṣetra-spharaṇam evaṃ sarva-satva-maitrī-spharaṇaṃ tad dānaṃ dadāti | pe | yathā gaganaṃ sadā-prakāśam evaṃ citta-prakṛti-viśuddhaṃ tad dānaṃ dada-ti | yathā gaganaṃ sarva-satva-avakāśaṃ evaṃ sarva-satva-upajīvyaṃ tad dānaṃ dadāti | yāvad yathā nirmito nirmitāya dadāti nir-vikalpo * an-ābhogaḥ | citta-mano-vijñāna-vigataḥ sarva-dharma-niḥ-pratikāṅkṣī | evaṃ dvaya-vigamatayā māyā-lakṣaṇa-sva-bhāva-viśuddhaṃ bodhi-satvas tad dānaṃ dadāti | yasya + īdṛśo dāna-parityāgaḥ prajñā-jñānena ca sarva-satva-kleśa-parityāgaḥ | upāya-jñānena ca satva-a-parityāgaḥ | evaṃ tyāga-cittaḥ kula-putra bodhi-satvo gagana-sama-dāno bhavati ||
body.translated_text: [Abbreviation.] 'Just as space is boundless, so with a mind made boundless he gives that gift. Just as space is vast and unobstructed, so dedicated to awakening he gives that gift. Just as space is formless, so not relying on any form he gives that gift. Just as space does not experience, so with all experience relaxed he gives that gift. Likewise without perception, unconditioned, characterized by non-manifestation — thus without assertion he gives that gift. Just as space pervades all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, so pervading all beings with loving-kindness he gives that gift.' [Abbreviation.] 'Just as space is always luminous, so purified through the natural luminosity of the mind he gives that gift. Just as space gives room to all beings, so as a support for all beings he gives that gift.' Up to: 'Just as an emanation gives to an emanation — without discrimination, without deliberation, free from mind, thought, and consciousness, without expectation regarding any <s>dharma</s> — so, through the absence of duality, the <s>bodhisattva</s> gives that gift purified in its nature through the characteristic of illusion.' 'One whose relinquishment in giving is of this kind, and whose relinquishment of the afflictions of all beings is through the knowledge of wisdom, and whose non-abandonment of beings is through the knowledge of skillful means — a son of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s> of such a mind of generosity, becomes one whose giving is equal to space.'

body.text: ārya-akṣayamati-sūtre * apy uktaṃ | na + asti satva-utpīḍanā-dānam | yāvan na + asti yathā-ukte ūna-dānaṃ | yāvan na + asti sarva-satveṣu dakṣiṇīyā-avamanyanā-dānaṃ | pe | na + asti nikranda-dānaṃ yāvan na + asti yācanakeṣu + upatapta-dānaṃ na + asty uccagghana ullāpana-dānaṃ na + asti parāṅ-mukha-dānaṃ na + asty apaviddha-dānaṃ na + asty a-sva-hasta-dānaṃ | pe | na + asty a-kalpika-dānaṃ | na + asty a-kāla-dānaṃ na + asti viṣa-śastra-dānaṃ na + asti satva-viheṭhanā-dānam iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Akṣayamati Sūtra</s> it is also said: 'There is no giving that involves the oppression of beings; there is no giving that falls short of what has been promised; there is no giving that involves contempt toward those worthy of offerings among all beings.' [Abbreviation.] 'There is no giving with loud complaint; there is no giving that distresses the supplicants; there is no giving with mockery or ridicule; there is no giving with the face turned away; there is no giving that is thrown [contemptuously]; there is no giving not from one's own hand.' [Abbreviation.] 'There is no giving of what is improper; there is no giving at an improper time; there is no giving of poison or weapons; there is no giving that involves the harassment of beings.'

body.text: yat tarhy ugra-paripṛcchāyām uktaṃ | dāna-pāramitā-kālo * ayaṃ yasya yena + arthas tasya tat-pradāna-kālaḥ | api tu tathā + ahaṃ kariṣyāmi | madya-pebhya eva madya-pānaṃ dāsyāmi | tāṃs tān smṛti-saṃprajanye samādāpayiṣyāmi + iti ||
body.translated_text: As for what is said in the <s>Ugraparipṛcchā</s>: 'This is the time for the perfection of giving: the time for giving to him who needs something is [the time of] the giving of that [thing].' But [the bodhisattva thinks:] 'I shall act thus: I shall give liquor only to drunkards; [and then] I shall establish them in mindfulness and awareness.'

body.text: madya-pānād api nairāśya-kṛte bodhi-satve pratigho garīyān | satva-saṃgraha-hāniś ca + ato * anya-prasādana-upāya-a-saṃbhave madyaṃ deyam ity abhiprāyaḥ | śastra-ādiṣv api yady anubadha-gurula-ādy-avavicārād dānam āpadyeta | na + eva + āpattir ity ata eva gamyate | sūtreṣu tu sāmānyena pratiṣedha | ity uktā dāna-viśuddhi-dik ||
body.translated_text: Since hostility toward a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has been made to despair [by refusal of liquor] is more serious [than giving it]; and since there would be a loss of the attraction of beings — therefore, when there is no other possible means of inspiring [their] faith, liquor should be given — this is the intent. Regarding weapons and the like too, if one arrives at giving [them] after careful consideration that the harm involved is not grave — then there is indeed no transgression, as can be understood from this very [passage]. But in the <s>sūtras</s>, there is a general prohibition. Thus the direction of the purification of giving has been stated.

body.text: śīla-viśuddhir ārya-gagana-gañja-sūtre eva + abhihitā | a-virahita-bodhi-cittatā citta-viśuddhyai apagata-śrāvaka-praty-eka-buddha-cittatā prāmāṇika-viśuddhyai ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: The purification of moral conduct (<s>śīlaviśuddhi</s>) is stated in the <s>Ārya-Gaganagañja Sūtra</s> itself: 'Being inseparable from <s>bodhicitta</s>, for the purification of the mind; being free from the mentality of a <s>śrāvaka</s> or <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, for the purification of authority,' and so forth.

body.text: punar a-parā śīla-viśuddhiḥ | śuddhaṃ gaganaṃ śuddhaṃ tac-chīlaṃ |vi-malaṃ gaganaṃ vi-malaṃ tac-chīlaṃ | śāntaṃ gaganaṃ śāntaṃ tac-chīlaṃ | an-unnataṃ gaganam an-unnataṃ tac-chīlaṃ | anunītaṃ gaganam anunītaṃ tac-chīlam | yāvad a-chedya-a-bhedyaṃ gaganam a-chedya-a-bhedyaṃ tac-chīlam ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: And further, the purification of moral conduct: 'Pure is space, pure is that morality. Stainless is space, stainless is that morality. Peaceful is space, peaceful is that morality. Without elevation is space, without elevation is that morality. Without depression is space, without depression is that morality.' Up to: 'Unbreakable and indivisible is space, unbreakable and indivisible is that morality,' and so forth.

body.text: a-pratihataṃ gaganaṃ sarva-satva-a-pratigha-cittasya kṣānti-pariśuddhiḥ | sama-prayogaṃ gaganaṃ sarva-satva-sama-cittasya kṣānti-pariśuddhir ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: 'Unobstructed is space — the purification of patience for one whose mind is without hostility toward all beings. Of equal effort is space — the purification of patience for one whose mind is equal toward all beings,' and so forth.

body.text: tad yathā + api syān mahā-śāla-vanaṃ | tasmin kaś-cid eva + āgatya śālaṃ chindyāt | tatra teṣām avaśiṣṭānāṃ na + evaṃ bhavati | eṣa chinno vayam a-cchinnā iti | na teṣām anunayo na pratighaḥ | na kalpo na vikalpo na parikalpaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Suppose there were a great <s>śāla</s> forest. Someone comes and cuts down a <s>śāla</s> tree. Therein, the remaining [trees] do not think: "That one has been cut, but we have not." They have no attachment, no hostility; no thought, no discrimination, no fabrication.'

body.text: yā + evaṃ kṣāntir iyaṃ bodhi-satvasya paramā gagana-samā kṣāntir | iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Such patience is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s supreme patience, equal to space.'

body.text: ārya-ratna-cūḍa-sūtre vistaram uktvā āha | idam ucyate vīryaṃ | tasya kāya-pariśuddhiḥ | yat kāyasya pratibhāsa-pratibimba-jñānaṃ vāco * an-abhilāpya-jñānaṃ | cittasya + aty-anta-upaśama-jñānaṃ | tathā maitrī-saṃnāha-saṃnaddho mahā-karuṇā-adhiṣṭhāna-pratiṣṭhitaḥ | sarva-ākāra-vara-upetaṃ śūnyatā-ākāra-abhinirhṛtaṃ dhyānaṃ dhyāyati | tatra katamā sarva-ākāra-vara-upetā śūnyatā | yā na dāna-vi-kalā | yāvan na + upāya-vi-kalā | na mahā-maitrī-muditā-upekṣā-vi-kalā | na satya-jñāna-avatāra-vi-kalā | na bodhi-citta-satva-apekṣā-vi-kalā | na + āśaya-adhyāśaya-prayoga-vi-kalā | na dāna-priya-vadyatā + artha-kriyā samāna-arthatā-vi-kalā | na smṛti-saṃprajanya-vi-kalā | na smṛty-upasthāna-samyak-prahāṇa-rddhi-pāda-indriya-bala-bodhy-aṅga-aṣṭa-aṅga-mārga-vi-kalā na śamatha-vipaśyanā-vi-kalā | pe | upaśāntā ca sva-bhāvena | an-upaśāntā ca karma-kleśeṣu | upekṣikā ca sarva-dharmāṇāṃ | avekṣikā ca buddha-dharmāṇāṃ | jahā ca sva-lakṣaṇena | vikrāntā ca + adhiṣṭhāna-kāryatayā | a-vyāpṛtā ca sva-rasena | sadā vyāpṛtā ca buddha-kāryeṣu | śītī-bhūtā ca + upaśamena | sadā + ujjvalitā ca satva-paripāke | iyam ucyate sarva-ākāra-vara-upetā śūnyatā ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Ratnacūḍa Sūtra</s>, having spoken at length, it says: 'This is called vigor. Its purification of the body is the knowledge that the body is a reflection and mirror-image; of speech, the knowledge that it is inexpressible; of the mind, the knowledge of utter pacification. Likewise, armored with the armor of loving-kindness, established in the support of great compassion, he meditates on <s>dhyāna</s> endowed with all the best modes, produced through the mode of emptiness.' 'Therein, what is the emptiness endowed with all the best modes? That which is not deficient in giving; not deficient in skillful means; not deficient in great loving-kindness, sympathetic joy, and equanimity; not deficient in penetration of the knowledge of truth; not deficient in <s>bodhicitta</s> and care for beings; not deficient in intention, higher intention, and effort; not deficient in giving, kind speech, beneficial action, and shared purpose; not deficient in mindfulness and awareness; not deficient in the foundations of mindfulness, right efforts, bases of power, faculties, powers, factors of awakening, and the eightfold path; not deficient in calm (<s>śamatha</s>) and insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>).' [Abbreviation.] 'And it is pacified by its own nature; yet not pacified with regard to <s>karma</s> and the afflictions. It is equanimous toward all <s>dharmas</s>; yet watchful over the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. It has abandoned [all] by its own characteristic; yet it is powerful through the function of its establishment. It is unoccupied by its own essence; yet always occupied with the tasks of the <s>Buddha</s>. It is cooled through pacification; yet always ablaze in the ripening of beings. This is called emptiness endowed with all the best modes.'

body.text: yāvad iyaṃ kula-putra dhyāna-pāramitā caryā-pariśuddhir iti ||
body.translated_text: 'This, O son of good family, is the purification of conduct in the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>).'

body.text: etena prajñā-pariśuddhir veditavyā | evaṃ sarva-puṇyeṣv iti ||
body.translated_text: By this, the purification of wisdom is also to be understood. Likewise for all [forms of] merit.

body.text: tathā + ārya-vimalakīrti-nirdeśe * apy uktaṃ |sad-dharma-cakra-pravartana-mahā-parinirvāṇa-saṃdarśana-go-caraś ca bodhi-satva-caryā + a-tyajana-go-caraś ca + ayam api bodhi-satvasya go-cara | iti ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, in the <s>Ārya-Vimalakīrtinirdeśa</s> it is also said: 'The domain of displaying the turning of the wheel of the true <s>Dharma</s> and the great <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, and also the domain of not abandoning the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct — this too is the domain of the <s>bodhisattva</s>.'

body.text: bhoga-puṇya-śuddhiḥ pañcadaśaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The fifteenth chapter: Purification of Enjoyments and Merit (<s>bhogapuṇyaśuddhi</s>).

children.translated_text: XVI. The Method of Good Conduct (<s>bhadracaryāvidhi</s>)

body.text: bhadra-caryā-vidhiḥ ṣoḍaśaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The sixteenth chapter: The Method of Good Conduct (<s>bhadracaryāvidhi</s>).

body.text: idānīṃ trayāṇām api vṛddhir vācyā ||
body.translated_text: Now the increase of all three [— body, enjoyments, and merit —] is to be stated.

body.text: kim arthaṃ | grahītāraḥ su-bahavaḥ sv-alpaṃ ca + idam anena kiṃ | na ca + ati-tṛpti-janakaṃ vardhanīyam idaṃ tataḥ ||
body.translated_text: For what purpose? 'Those who would take [from us] are very many, and this [that we have] is little — what [use] is it? And since it does not generate supreme satisfaction, this should therefore be increased.'

body.text: ati-tṛpti buddhatvaṃ | tan na śrāvaka-sādhāraṇena śuddhi-mātreṇa satvānāṃ janyatae ity arthaḥ | ātma-bhāvasya kā vṛddhir bala-an-ālasya vardhanaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'Supreme satisfaction' means <s>Buddhahood</s>. The meaning is that it is not produced for beings by mere purification shared with <s>śrāvakas</s>. What is the increase of one's own body? The increase of strength and non-laziness.

body.text: tatra + ārya-ratna-meghe balam uktaṃ |na sa satvaḥ satva-nikāye saṃvidyate yo bodhi-satvasya balena balaṃ mardayed ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: Regarding that, in the <s>Ārya-Ratnamegha</s> the power [of a bodhisattva] is stated: 'No being in the entire assemblage of beings is found who could crush the power of a <s>bodhisattva</s> by power,' and so forth.

body.text: tasya kathaṃ vardhanam | yad uktam ārya-tathā-gata-guhya-sūtre ārya-vajrapāṇer bala-darśana-vismita-ajātaśatru-pṛṣṭena bhagavatā | daśabhir mahā-rāja dharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhi-satva evaṃ-rūpāṃ balavattāṃ pratilabhate |katamair daśabhiḥ | iha mahā-rāja bodhi-satvaḥ kāyaṃ jīvitaṃ ca parityajati | na ca punaḥ sad-dharmaṃ parityajati | sarva-satvānāṃ ca + avanamati na ca punar mānaṃ bṛṃhayati | dur-balānāṃ ca satvānāṃ kṣamate | na pratighaṃ karoti | jighatsitānāṃ ca satvānām agraṃ vara-bhojanaṃ dadāti | bhītānāṃ ca satvānām a-bhayaṃ dadāti | glānānāṃ ca satvānāṃ bhūta-cikitsāyai utsuko bhavati | daridrāṃś ca satvān bhogaiḥ saṃtarpayati | tathā-gata-caitye ca su-dhā-piṇḍa-lepanaṃ karoti | ānanda-vacanaṃ satvānāṃ śrāvayati | daridra-duṣkhitānāṃ ca satvānāṃ bhoga-saṃvibhāgaṃ karoti | śrānta-klāntānāṃ ca satvānāṃ bhāraṃ vahati | ebhir mahā-rāja daśabhir iti ||
body.translated_text: How is the increase of that [strength]? As it is said in the <s>Ārya-Tathāgataguhya-sūtra</s>, by the Blessed One when questioned by <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, who was astonished at the display of the power of <s>Ārya Vajrapāṇi</s>: 'Endowed with ten <s>dharmas</s>, O Great King, the <s>bodhisattva</s> obtains such great power. Which ten? Here, O Great King, the <s>bodhisattva</s> relinquishes body and life, but does not relinquish the true <s>Dharma</s>. He bows down to all beings, but does not nourish pride. He is patient with weak beings and does not generate hostility. He gives the choicest, excellent food to hungry beings. He gives fearlessness to frightened beings. He is eager to provide medical treatment for sick beings. He satisfies poor beings with material goods. He applies plaster to <s>Tathāgata</s> shrines (<s>caityas</s>). He makes beings hear words of joy. He shares material goods with poor and suffering beings. He carries the burdens of weary and exhausted beings. By these ten, O Great King.'

body.text: an-ālasya-vardhanaṃ katamat | yad vīrya-vardhanaṃ | yathā + uktaṃ sāgaramati-sūtre | ārabdha-vīryeṇa sāgaramate bodhi-satvena bhavitavyaṃ sadā dṛḍha-parākrameṇa | tīvra-cchandena bodhi-satvena bhavitavyam a-nikṣipta-dhureṇa | ārabdha-vīryāṇāṃ hi sāgaramate bodhi-satvānāṃ na dur-labhā bhavaty an-uttarā samyak-saṃbodhiḥ | tat kasya hetoḥ | yatra sāgaramate vīryaṃ tatra bodhiḥ | kusīdānāṃ punaḥ su-dūra-vidūre bodhiḥ | na + asti kusīdasya dānaṃ yāvan na + asti prajñā na + asti kusīdasya para-artha iti ||
body.translated_text: What is the increase of non-laziness? It is the increase of vigor (<s>vīrya</s>). As it is said in the <s>Sāgaramati-sūtra</s>: 'The <s>bodhisattva</s>, O <s>Sāgaramati</s>, should be one who has aroused vigor, always of firm exertion. The <s>bodhisattva</s> should be one of keen aspiration who has not laid down the burden. For <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have aroused vigor, O <s>Sāgaramati</s>, unsurpassed perfect awakening is not hard to obtain. For what reason? Where there is vigor, O <s>Sāgaramati</s>, there is awakening. But for the lazy, awakening is far, far away. There is no giving for the lazy; up to: there is no wisdom; there is no benefit for others for the lazy.'

body.text: candra-pradīpa-sūtre * apy āha | utpalaṃ vāri-madhye vā so * anupūrveṇa vardhatae |ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Candrapradīpa-sūtra</s> too it says: 'Like a lotus in the midst of water, he gradually grows.' And so on.

body.text: iyaṃ saṃkṣepād ātma-bhāva-vṛddhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: This is, in summary, the growth of one's own being (<s>ātma-bhāva-vṛddhi</s>).

body.text: śūnyatā karuṇā-garbhād dānād bhogasya vardhanaṃ ||
body.translated_text: From giving that is rooted in emptiness and compassion comes the increase of enjoyments.

body.text: yathā + uktaṃ vajra-cchedikāyāṃ | yo bodhi-satvo * a-pratiṣṭhito dānaṃ dadāti | tasya puṇya-skandhasya na su-karaṃ pramāṇam udgrahītum iti ||
body.translated_text: As it is said in the <s>Vajracchedikā</s>: 'The <s>bodhisattva</s> who gives a gift without being established [in anything] — of his aggregate of merit, the measure is not easy to grasp.'

body.text: mahatyām api prajñā-pāramitāyām uktaṃ | punar a-paraṃ śāriputra bodhi-satvena mahā-satvena + alpam api dānaṃ dadatā sarva-satveṣu sarva-ākāra-jñatāyām upāya-kauśalya-pariṇāmanatāyām a-prameyam a-saṃkhyeyaṃ kartu-kāmena prajñā-pāramitāyāṃ śikṣitavyam | tathā sarva-satvānāṃ mano-rathān paripūrayitu-kāmena | yāvaj jāta-rūpa-rajata-udyāna-rājya-ādibhir upakaraṇaiḥ prajñā-pāramitāyāṃ śikṣitavyam iti ||
body.translated_text: In the great <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> too it is said: 'Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who gives even a small gift, wishing to make it immeasurable and incalculable through the dedication skillful in means to omniscience of all aspects with respect to all beings — he should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Likewise, wishing to fulfill the heart's desires of all beings — up to: with gold, silver, parks, kingdoms, and other requisites — he should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.'

body.text: vinā ca karuṇayā na bodhi-satvānāṃ kiṃ-cic ceṣṭitam iti vakṣyāmaḥ | iti saṃkṣepād bhoga-vṛddhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: And we shall state that without compassion, <s>bodhisattvas</s> have no activity whatsoever. This is, in summary, the increase of enjoyments.

body.text: puṇya-vṛddhiḥ sarva-vṛddhīnāṃ mūlam iti tad-arthaṃ parikara-bandha ucyate ||
body.translated_text: The increase of merit is the root of all increases — for that purpose, the preparation (<s>parikara-bandha</s>) is stated.

body.text: kṛtvā + ādāv eva yatnena vyavasāya-āśāyau dṛḍhau | karuṇāṃ ca puras-kṛtya yateta śubha-vṛddhaye ||
body.translated_text: 'Having first made firm, with effort, one's resolve and aspiration, and having placed compassion at the forefront, one should strive for the increase of the wholesome.'

body.text: citta-śuddhi-kāla-bhāvitānāṃ vyavasāya-ādīnāṃ prayoga-ārambhe punar āmukhī-karaṇena dṛḍhatā + a-pādana-arthaḥ ślokaḥ | kṛtvā + ity ādi-pūrvaka eva ||
body.translated_text: The verse beginning with 'Having made' and so on has the purpose of making firm — through bringing [them] once more to the forefront at the commencement of practice — the resolve and other [qualities] that were cultivated at the time of purifying the mind, [so that] no slackening occurs.

body.text: āsanna-yuddha-kālānāṃ astra-kauśalya-ādara-vat prayoga-sama-kālaṃ dṛḍhī-kariṣyāmi + iti śaithilya-nivāraṇa-artham ādi-grahaṇam | tatra kathaṃ vyavasāyaṃ dṛḍhī-karoti ||
body.translated_text: The initial statement has the purpose of preventing laxity: 'I shall make [my resolve] firm at the very time of practice' — like the care for skill in weapons when the time of battle is near. Therein, how does he make his resolve firm?

body.text: yathā + ārya-sudhana ārya-maitreyam upasaṃprakrāntaḥ samyak-caryā-niḥ-samarthaḥ | pūrva-anta-koṭī-gata-kāya-praṇāmaḥ kāya-samanvāhāreṇa kāya-balaṃ dṛḍhī-kurvāṇaḥ | pūrva-anta-koṭī-gata-kāya citta-pariśuddhi-niṣ-kāraṇa-sāṃsārika-citta-pracāra-samanvāhāreṇa citta-manasi-kāraṃ nigṛhṇan | pūrva-anta-koṭy--a-sat-karma-laukika-kārya-prayukta-niṣ-prayojana-parisyanda-samanvāhāreṇa praty-utpanna-prayojana-mahā-sāmarthyaṃ vicintayan | pūrva-anta-a-bhūta-parikalpa-samutthita-vitatha-saṃkalpa-saṃdarśita-manasi-kāra-samanvāhāreṇa sarva-bodhi-satva-caryā-samyak-saṃkalpa-abhisaṃskāra-balaṃ samutthāpayan | atīta-ātma-bhāva-artha-prayoga-ārambha-viṣamatā-samanvāhāreṇa sarva-satva-ārambha-vaiśeṣikatayā + adhyāśaya-balaṃ dṛḍhī-kurvāṇaḥ | atīta-kāya-samudācāra-nir-āsvādatā-samanvāhāreṇa | sarva-buddha-dharma-pratilābha-prayoga-mahā-āśvāsa-pratilābha-indriya-vegān vivardhayamāno * atīta-adhva-viparyāsa-prayukta-mithyā-āśaya-prayoga-samanvāhṝeṇa | praty-utpanna-adhva-samyag-darśana-a-viparyāsa-saṃprayuktena bodhi-satva-praṇidhāna-samādānena saṃtatiṃ pariśodhayan | pūrva-anta-gata-āyoga-vīrya-ārambha-kārya-a-pariniṣpanna-ārya-samādāna-samanvāhāreṇa

children.text: | praty-utpanna-buddha-dharma-samudāgama-pratyupasthānena mahā-vīrya-ārambha-vikrameṇa kāya-citta-saṃpragrahaṃ saṃjanayamānaḥ | pūrva-anta-koṭī-pañca-gaty-apāya-nikṣipta-ātma-para-nir-upakaraṇa-ākhya-nir-upajīvya-samucchraya-parigraha-samanvāhāreṇa | sarva-buddha-dharma-utthāpaka-sarva-jagad-upajīvya-sarva-kalyāṇa-mitra-ārāgaṇa-samarthya-ātma-bhāva-parigrahaṇatayā vipula-prīti-prāmodya-vegān vivardhayamānaḥ praty-utpanna-janma-abhinirvṛttaṃ jarā-vyādhi-maraṇa-śoka-ākara-bhūtaṃ saṃyoga-viyoga-nidhāna-bhūtaṃ samucchrayaṃ | apara-anta-kalpa-koṭī-gata-bodhi-satva-caryā-ācaraṇa-prayuktasya satva-paripācana-buddha-dharma-parigraha-prayuktasya tathā-gata-saṃdarśana-sarva-buddha-kṣetra-anucaraṇa-sarva-dharma-bhāṇaka-upasthāna-sarva-tathā-gata-śāsana-samanvāharaṇa-prayuktasya sarva-dharma-paryeṣṭi-sahāya-bhūtasya sarva-kalyāṇa-mitra-darśana-sarva-buddha-dharma-samudānayana-prayuktasya bodhi-satva-praṇidhi-jñāna-śarīrasya hetu-pratyaya-bhūtam avalokya-a-cintya-kuśala-mūla-indriya-vegān viva rdhayamāna iti | ārya-akṣayamati-nirdeśe mahā-yāna-sūtre * apy uktaṃ | eko bodhi-satvo * a-dvitīyo * a-sahāyo * an-uttarāyāṃ samyak-saṃbodhau saṃnāhaṃ saṃnahyati | sa vīrya-bala-parigṛhītena + adhyāśayena + a-para-avakāśa-a-svayaṃ-kārī | sva-bala-bala-udgataḥ | sa evaṃ dṛḍha-saṃnāhaḥ saṃnaddho | yat kiñ-cit sarva-satvānāṃ pariprāpayitavyaṃ bhaviṣyati tad ahaṃ pariprāpayiṣyāmi | yat sarva-āryāḥ sarva-nava-yāna-saṃprasthitā bodhi-satvā na pariprāpayiṣyanti tad ahaṃ pariprāpayiṣyāmi | na mama dānaṃ sahāyakaṃ |ahaṃ punar dānasya sahāyaḥ | na mama śīla-kṣānti-vīrya-dhyāna-prajñāḥ sahāyikāḥ | ahaṃ punaḥ śīla-kṣānti-vīrya-dhyāna-prajñānāṃ sahāyo | na + ahaṃ pāramitābhir upasthātavyo mayā punaḥ pāramitā upasthātavyāḥ | evaṃ saṃgraha-vastuṣu sarva-kuśala-mūleṣu caleyam | yāvad ekākinā mayā + a-dvitīyena + a-sahāyena vajra-maye mahī-maṇḍale sthitena sa-balaṃ sa-vāhanaṃ māraṃ dharṣayitvā eka-citta-kṣaṇa-sama-āyuktayā prajñayā + an-uttarā samyak-saṃbodhir abhisaṃboddhavyā + iti ||
children.translated_text: generating bodily and mental self-discipline through the great vigorous exertion and prowess for the attainment of present <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, by reviewing past [conduct]; increasing the force of vast joy and delight through the grasping of a being capable of supporting all beings, capable of propitiating all spiritual friends, and capable of raising up all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, by reviewing the helpless and unsupported existence thrown into the five destinies and lower realms extending to the beginning-edge of the former limit; [contemplating] the present birth-arising, which is a mine of old age, sickness, death, and sorrow, and a repository of union and separation — as the causal condition for the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct extending to the end-edge of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> to come, which is engaged in the ripening of beings and the acquisition of <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, in seeing <s>Tathāgatas</s> and traversing all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, in attending all <s>Dharma</s>-preachers and maintaining the teaching of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, in seeking all <s>dharmas</s>, in seeing all spiritual friends and bringing together all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> — [and thus] increasing the force of inconceivable wholesome-root faculties by regarding [the present body] as the body of <s>bodhisattva</s> aspiration-knowledge, a cause and condition [for all this]. In the <s>Ārya-Akṣayamati-nirdeśa Mahāyāna-sūtra</s> too it is said: 'A single <s>bodhisattva</s>, alone, without a second, without a companion, girds on the armor for unsurpassed perfect awakening. With a higher aspiration sustained by the power of vigor, not making room for another, not acting on another's behalf — standing forth by one's own power alone. Thus firmly armored, he girds: "Whatever needs to be accomplished for all beings, I shall accomplish. What all noble ones, all <s>bodhisattvas</s> newly set out in the vehicles, will not accomplish — that I shall accomplish. Generosity is not my helper; rather, I am the helper of generosity. Moral conduct, patience, vigor, meditation, and wisdom are not my helpers; rather, I am the helper of moral conduct, patience, vigor, meditation, and wisdom. I am not to be served by the <s>pāramitās</s>; rather, by me the <s>pāramitās</s> are to be served." Likewise with the means of attraction and all wholesome roots. Up to: "Alone, without a second, without a companion, standing on the adamantine ground of the earth, having defeated <s>Māra</s> together with his forces and vehicles, with wisdom yoked in a single moment of thought, I shall fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening."'

body.translated_text: As the noble <s>Sudhana</s>, having approached the noble <s>Maitreya</s>, fully capable of right conduct: reflecting on the bodily prostrations extending to the beginning-edge of the former limit, making the body's power firm through the review of the body; restraining the mind's attention through the review of the bodily and mental purity extending to the beginning-edge of the former limit and of the purposeless courses of worldly thought in <s>saṃsāra</s>; contemplating the great capacity of present purpose through the review of the purposeless outflows of unwholesome and worldly activities extending to the beginning-edge of the former limit; generating the power of right intention and formation of all <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct through the review of the attention shown by false intentions arising from unreal imaginations extending to the beginning-edge of the former limit; making firm the power of higher aspiration through the excellence of endeavor for all beings by reviewing the unevenness of efforts undertaken for one's own sake in past lives; increasing the force of the faculties through the great confidence obtained in the practice of acquiring all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, by reviewing the tastelessness of past bodily conduct;

body.text: ārya-vajra-dhvaja-sūtre * apy āha | tad yathā + api nāma sūryo deva-putra udayamāno na tiṣṭhati | jāty-andha-doṣeṇa | na tiṣṭhati gandharva-nagara-doṣeṇa | na tiṣṭhati catur-dvīpa-loka-dhātu-bhūmi-rajo-doṣeṇa | na tiṣṭhati rāhv-asura-indra-doṣeṇa | na tiṣṭhati dhūma-maṇḍala-doṣeṇa | na tiṣṭhati jambū-dvīpa-kleśa-doṣeṇa | na tiṣṭhati nānā-chāyā-doṣeṇa | na tiṣṭhati vi-ṣama-parvata-doṣeṇa | evam eva bodhi-satvo mahā-satvaḥ smṛti-saṃprajanya-vipula-gambhīra-cetā a-dīna-satvo guṇa-caryā-jñāna-caryā-avasānaṃ yāvan na vivartate satva-drauhilya-doṣaiḥ | na vipravasati kuśala-mūla-pariṇāmaiḥ | satva-dṛṣṭi-kāluṣya-doṣair na vivartate | satva-kṣobha-cetobhir na dūrī-bhavati | satva-vinaṣṭa-saṃtatyā bodhi-saṃnāhaṃ na viṣkambhayati | sarva-jagat-paritrāṇa-praṇidhānasya satva-kali-kaluṣair na sraṃsanāṃ karoti yāvad bāla-jana-samavadhānena | na nirvidyate para-satva-doṣaiś ca | tat kasya hetoḥ | an-āvaraṇa-maṇḍalam etad udayati | yad uta sarva-jagad-viśuddhi-vinayāya | pe ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Vajradhvaja-sūtra</s> too it says: 'Just as the <s>deva</s>-son, the sun, when rising, does not stop because of the defect of those blind from birth; does not stop because of the defect of illusory cities (<s>gandharva-nagara</s>); does not stop because of the defect of the dust on the ground of the four-continent world-system; does not stop because of the defect of the <s>asura</s>-lord <s>Rāhu</s>; does not stop because of the defect of the mass of smoke; does not stop because of the defect of the afflictions of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>; does not stop because of the defect of various shadows; does not stop because of the defect of uneven mountains — just so, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, vast and profound in mind through mindfulness and clear comprehension, undaunted in spirit, until the end of the conduct of qualities and the conduct of knowledge, does not turn back because of the defects of beings' hostility; does not stray from the dedication of wholesome roots; does not turn back because of the defects of the impurity of beings' views; does not become distant because of the agitated minds of beings; does not loosen the armor of awakening because of beings whose continuity is destroyed; does not let go of the aspiration for the protection of all the world because of the corruption and impurity of beings; up to: does not become disheartened because of the assembly of childish folk and the faults of other beings. For what reason? Because this [sun-]disk rises unobstructed — namely, for the purification and discipline of all the world.' [In abbreviation.]

body.text: yaś ca teṣāṃ sarva-satvānāṃ duṣkha-skandho vividhaṃ ca + āvaraṇīyaṃ karma samutthitaṃ yena te āvaraṇīyena karmaṇā buddhān na paśyanti | dharmaṃ na śṛṇvanti | saṃghaṃ na jānanti | tad ahaṃ teṣāṃ tri-vidham āvaraṇīyaṃ karma + upacitaṃ duṣkha-skandhena svakena śarīreṇa + upādadāmi tāsu tāsu naraka-upapattiṣv apāya-bhūmiṣu saṃvāseṣu ca | te ca sarva-satvās tataś cyavantāṃ | ahaṃ ca duṣkha-upādānam upādadāmi vyavasyāmy utsahe | na nivarte na palāyāmi na + uttrasyāmi na saṃtrasyāmi na bibhemi na pratyudāvarte na viṣīdāmi | tat kasya hetoḥ | a-vaśyaṃ nirvāhayitavyo mayā sarva-satvānāṃ bhāro | na + eṣa mama kāma-kāraḥ | sarva-satva-uttāraṇa-praṇidhānaṃ mama | mayā sarva-satvāḥ parimocayitavyā | mayā sarva-jagat samuttārayitavyaṃ | jāti-kāntārāj jarā-kāntārād vyādhi-kāntārāc cyuty-upapati-kāntārāt sarva-āpatti-kāntārāt sarva-apāya-kāntārāt sarva-saṃsāra-kāntārāt sarva-dṛṣṭi-gahana-kāntārāt kuśala-dharma-praṇāśa-kāntārād a-jñāna-samutthita-kāntārāt tad ete mayā sarva-satvāḥ sarva-kāntārebhyaḥ parimocayitavyāḥ | tṛṣṇā-jāla-saktā a-vidyā-nivaraṇa-āvṛtā bhava-tṛṣṇā-saṃprayuktāḥ praṇāśa-paryavasānā duṣkha-pañjara-prakṣiptāś cāraka-saṃniśritā | a-budhāḥ pratijñā-viruddhāḥ saṃśaya-bhūtāḥ sadā vi-matayo * a-kṣema-darśinaḥ | a-niḥ-śaraṇa-kuśalā bhava-arṇave āvarta-maṇḍala-eka-caraṇāḥ | pe ||
body.translated_text: And whatever mass of suffering belongs to all those beings, and whatever manifold obstructive <s>karma</s> (action) has arisen by which, through that obstructive <s>karma</s>, they do not see the <s>Buddhas</s>, do not hear the <s>Dharma</s>, do not know the <s>Saṅgha</s> — I take upon myself with my own body that threefold obstructive <s>karma</s> accumulated together with the mass of suffering, in those various hell-rebirths, in the planes of misfortune and abodes. And may all those beings pass away from there, while I take on the burden of suffering. I resolve, I persevere; I do not turn back, I do not flee, I am not terrified, I am not frightened, I do not fear, I do not retreat, I do not despair. For what reason? The burden of all beings must inevitably be carried by me. This is not my arbitrary choice; my vow is for the deliverance of all beings. All beings must be liberated by me. The entire world must be rescued by me — from the wilderness of birth, the wilderness of old age, the wilderness of disease, the wilderness of death-and-rebirth, the wilderness of all calamities, the wilderness of all misfortunes, the wilderness of all <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), the wilderness of the thicket of all views, the wilderness of the destruction of wholesome qualities, the wilderness arisen from ignorance. All these beings must be liberated by me from all wildernesses. They are caught in the net of craving, enveloped by the obstruction of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), bound by craving for existence, destined for destruction, cast into the cage of suffering, dependent on wardens — unawakened, acting contrary to their professions, beset by doubt, always of wrong views, seeing no safety, unskilled in finding refuge, caught in the whirlpool of the ocean of existence, going round in circles. And so forth.

body.text: sarva-satvānām an-uttara-jñāna-rājya-pratiṣṭhāpana-artham ahaṃ carāmi | na + ahaṃ kevalam ātma-parimocana-abhiyuktaḥ | sarva-satvā hy ete mayā sarva-jñatā-citta-plavena saṃsāra-dur-gād * dhartavyā | mahā-prapātād abhyutkṣeptavyāḥ | sarva-upadravebhyaḥ parimocayitavyāḥ | saṃsāra-srotasaḥ pratārayitavyā ātmanā mayā sarva-satva-duṣkha-skandho * adhyavasitaḥ | yāvad utsahe * ahaṃ sarva-apāyeṣu sarva-loka-dhātu-paryāpanneṣu sarva-duṣkha-vāsam anubhavitum | na ca mayā sarva-satvāḥ kuśala-mūlair vañcitavyāḥ | vyavasyāmy aham eka-ekasminn apāye * apara-anta-koṭī-gatān kalpān saṃvasayituṃ | yathā ca eka-apāye tathā sarva-apāya-nir-avaśeṣa-sarva-loka-dhātu-paryāpanneṣu sarva-satva-parimocana-nidānaṃ |tat kasya hetoḥ | varaṃ khalu punar aham eko duṣkhitaḥ syāṃ na ca + ime sarva-satvāḥ apāya-bhūmi-prapatitāḥ | mayā tatra + ātmā bandhako dātavyaḥ | sarva-jagac ca niḥ-kretavyaṃ naraka-tiryag-yoni-yama-loka-kāntārād ahaṃ ca sarva-satvānām arthāya sarva-duṣkha-vedanā-skandham anena svakena śarīreṇa + anubhaveyam | sarva-satva-nidānam ahaṃ ca sarva-satvānāṃ prātibhāvyam utsahe satya-vādī pratyayito * a-visaṃvādakaḥ | na ca mayā sarva-satvāḥ parityaktāḥ | tat kasya hetoḥ | sarva-satva-ārambaṇo mama sarva-jñatā-citta-utpāda utpanno yad uta sarva-jagat-parimocanāya | na ca + ahaṃ rati-kāmatayā + an-uttarāyāṃ samyak-saṃbodhau saṃprasthito na + api pañca-kāma-guṇa-raty-anubhavanāya na + api kāma-viṣaya-niṣevaṇāya | na ca + aham anyo-nya-kāma-dhātu-paryāpanna-rati-vyūha-samudānayanāya carāmi bodhi-satva-caryāṃ | tat kasya hetoḥ | a-ratayo hy eṣā sarva-loka-ratayaḥ |māra-viṣaya eṣa yad uta kāma-viṣaya-niṣevaṇaṃ | dur-buddhi-sevito hy eṣa mārgaḥ |sarva-buddhi-vivarṇito hy ayam upadeśaḥ yad uta kāma-niṣevaṇaṃ |ataś ca + eṣa sarva-duṣkha-skandhasya + utpāda eva niṣevaṇaṃ ata eva ca naraka-tiryag-yoni-yama-lokānām utpādaḥ | kalaha-bhaṇḍana-vivāda-kṣobhāś ca satvānām ata eva prādur-bhavanti | ete ca satvāḥ kāmān niṣevamāṇāḥ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ sakāśād dūrī-bhavanti | svarga-upapatter apy ete kāmā antarāyāya saṃvartante | kiṃ punar an-uttarasya jñāna-rājasya sarva-satva-yoga-kṣemasya | so * aham evam a-pramāṇa-doṣān kāmānāṃ paśyan parīttān ādīptāṃs tasmād aham etan nidānam a-caraṇatāyāṃ pratipatsye || pe ||
body.translated_text: For the sake of establishing all beings in the unsurpassed kingdom of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), I practice. I am not devoted solely to my own liberation. All these beings must be carried by me on the boat of the mind set on <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) out of the difficult passage of <s>saṃsāra</s>; they must be lifted up from the great precipice; they must be freed from all calamities; they must be ferried across the stream of <s>saṃsāra</s>. By myself, the mass of suffering of all beings has been undertaken. As long as I am able, I will experience the abode of all suffering in all misfortunes throughout all world-realms. And beings must not be cheated by me of their roots of merit. I resolve to dwell for <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) reaching to the final limit in each and every misfortune. And just as in one misfortune, so in all misfortunes without remainder throughout all world-realms — this is the cause of the liberation of all beings. For what reason? It is far better indeed that I alone should suffer than that all these beings should fall into the planes of misfortune. There I must give myself as a hostage, and the entire world must be redeemed from the wilderness of hell, animal birth, and the realm of <s>Yama</s>. And I shall experience with this very body the entire mass of painful sensations for the sake of all beings. For the sake of all beings, I stand surety for all beings; I persevere, speaking truth, trustworthy, not deceiving. And beings must not be abandoned by me. For what reason? Because my arising of the mind set on <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) has arisen with all beings as its object — namely, for the liberation of the entire world. And I have not set out toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) out of desire for pleasure, nor for the experience of delight in the five strands of sensual pleasure, nor for the indulgence in sense-objects. Nor do I practice the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct for the sake of accumulating arrays of pleasure belonging to the realm of desire. For what reason? For all worldly pleasures are without true delight. This indulgence in sense-objects is the domain of <s>Māra</s>. This is a path followed by the foolish. This teaching — namely the indulgence in desires — is condemned by all the wise. Moreover, this indulgence is indeed the very arising of the entire mass of suffering, and from it arises rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the world of <s>Yama</s>. Quarrel, dispute, contention, and agitation among beings arise from this very source. And these beings, indulging in sensual pleasures, become far removed from the blessed <s>Buddhas</s>. These pleasures are an obstacle even to heavenly rebirth — how much more so to the unsurpassed kingdom of knowledge and the welfare of all beings! Therefore I, seeing these immeasurable faults of sensual pleasures — limited and ablaze — shall on this account devote myself to non-indulgence. And so forth.

body.text: tathā tathā + eva mayā kuśala-mūlaṃ pariṇāmayitavyaṃ yathā yathā + eva sarva-satvā aty-anta-sukham a-vedita-sukhaṃ yāvat sarva-jñatā-sukhaṃ pratilabheran | mayā sārathinā mayā pariṇāyakena mayā + ulkā-dhāriṇā mayā kṣema-gati-darśakena mayā kṣaṇa-gati-pratilabdhena mayā + upāya-jñena mayā + artha-viduṣā mayā saṃsāra-sāgare sarva-jña-jñāna-yāna-pātra-mahā-deśa-sthitena mayā pariṇāmana-kuśalena mayā pāra-darśakena || pe ||
body.translated_text: I must dedicate my roots of merit in such a way that all beings may obtain ultimate happiness, happiness beyond what has ever been experienced, even the happiness of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience). By me as charioteer, by me as guide, by me as torch-bearer, by me as the one who shows the path to safety, by me who has attained the opportune path, by me who is skilled in means, by me who knows the true purpose, by me who stands on the great ground of the vessel of the knowledge-vehicle of the Omniscient in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, by me who is skilled in dedication, by me who shows the further shore. And so forth.

body.text: na khalu punar asmiṃś cāturmahā-dvīpake loka-dhātau yāvantaḥ satvās tāvanta eva sūryā udāgacchanti cāturdvīpaka-loka-dhātv-avabhāsanāya | atha ca punar eka eva + eṣāṃ sūrya udāgacchati catur-dvīpa-avabhāsanāya | na ca teṣāṃ satvānāṃ catur-dvīpa-upapannānāṃ svaka-svakaiḥ śarīrair avabhāsaḥ prādur-bhavati | yena te divasa-saṃkhyāṃ jānīyuḥ | sva-kāryaṃ vā pariprāpayeyuḥ | sasyāni vā paripācayeyuḥ | ahar ahar vā udyāna-nagareṣu rati-krīḍā-paribhogam anubhaveyuḥ | diśo vā paśyeyuḥ | gamana-āgamanaṃ vā grāma-nagara-nigama-rāṣṭra-rāja-dhānīṣu kuryuḥ | vyavahāra-kāryeṣu prayujyeran |pe | atha ca punaḥ sūryasya deva-putrasya + udayata ekasya sūrya-maṇḍalasya + a-dvitīyasya cāturdvīpake loka-dhātau sarva-satvānām avabhāsaḥ prādur-bhavati | evam eva bodhi-satvasya mahā-satvasya kuśala-mūlāny upārpayamānasya kuśala-mūlaṃ pariṇāmayamānasya + evaṃ cittam utpadyate | na + eteṣāṃ satvānāṃ tat kuśala-mūlaṃ vidyate yena te ātmānaṃ paritrāyeran | kaḥ punar vādaḥ param | ahaṃ punaḥ sarva-satvānāṃ kṛtaśaḥ kuśala-mūlāni samudānayāmi kuśala-mūlaṃ pariṇāmayāmi | yad uta sarva-satva-mocanāya | sarva-satvānām avabhāsanāya sarva-satvānāṃ jñāpanāya sarav-satvānām avatāraṇāya sarva-satvānāṃ parigrahaṇāya sarva-satvānāṃ pariniṣpādanāya sarva-satvānāṃ prasādanāya sarva-satvānāṃ prahlādanāya sarva-satvānāṃ saṃśaya-cchedanāya āditya-maṇḍala-kalpair asmābhir bhavitavyaṃ | na paraḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyaḥ | na parasya + avakāśam utpādya satveṣu saṃnāha utsraṣṭavyaḥ | na ca sarva-satvānām antikāt sarva-satva-trāṇa-vyavaśāyo nivartayitavyaḥ | na pariṇāmanāyāḥ sarva-duṣkha-hatyā vinivartitavyaṃ | na parīttāni kuśala-mūlāni parigrahītavyāni | na parīttayā pariṇāmanayā tuṣṭir mantavyā ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: In this world-system of four great continents, it is not the case that as many suns rise as there are beings to illuminate the four-continent world-system. Rather, just one single sun rises to illuminate the four continents. And the illumination does not arise from the individual bodies of those beings born in the four continents, by which they might know the count of days, or accomplish their own tasks, or ripen their crops, or day after day enjoy the delights and pleasures of parks and cities, or see the directions, or travel to and from villages, towns, market-towns, kingdoms, and capital cities, or engage in affairs of commerce. And so forth. But rather, when the single sun-disc of the <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun) <s>devaputra</s> (divine prince) rises — that one sun-disc without a second — illumination arises for all beings in the four-continent world-system. Just so, when the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> (great being) offers up and dedicates roots of merit, this thought arises: these beings do not possess the roots of merit by which they could save themselves — to say nothing of saving others. But I shall systematically accumulate and dedicate roots of merit for all beings — namely, for the liberation of all beings, for the illumination of all beings, for the instruction of all beings, for leading all beings to the teaching, for the embrace of all beings, for the perfection of all beings, for gladdening all beings, for the delight of all beings, for cutting through the doubts of all beings. We must become like the disc of the sun. One must not look to another. One must not, having given opportunity to another, abandon one's armor toward beings. One must not turn back from the resolve to protect all beings in the presence of all beings. One must not turn away from the dedication that removes all suffering. One must not cling to limited roots of merit. One must not be satisfied with a limited dedication. And so on.

body.text: ārya-akṣayamati-sūtre * apy āha | sa na kalpa-gaṇanayā bodhiṃ paryeṣate | iyataḥ kalpān saṃnatsyāmi | iyataḥ kalpān saṃnatsyāmi + iti | api tu khalv a-cintyam eva saṃnāhaṃ saṃnahyati | yāvatī pūrvā-koṭiḥ saṃsārasya yady etāvad ekaṃ rātriṃ-divaṃ bhavet | evaṃ-rūpai rātriṃ-divaiḥ pañcadaśa-daivasikena pakṣeṇa triṃśad-daivasikena māsena dvādaśa-māsikena saṃvatsareṇa anayā varṣa-gaṇanayā yāvad varṣa-śata-sahasreṇa + ekaṃ bodhi-cittam utpādayeyam ekaṃ ca tathā-gatam arhantaṃ samyak-saṃbuddhaṃ paśyeyaṃ | anena praveśena + anayā gaṇanayā gaṅgā-nadī-vālukā-samaiś citta-utpādais tathā-gata-darśanaiś ca eka-ekasya + api satvasya citta-caritaṃ jānīyāṃ | anena + eva praveśena + anayā gaṇanayā sarva-satvānāṃ tāvadbhiś citta-utpādais tathā-gata-darśanaiḥ sva-citta-caritāni prajanīyām ity an-avalīnaḥ | saṃnāho * ayaṃ bodhi-satvasya + a-kṣayaḥ saṃnāhaḥ |evaṃ dāna-ādiṣu bodhi-pākṣika-mahā-puruṣa-lakṣaṇeṣu ca nayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Akṣayamatisūtra</s> (Noble Sūtra of Inexhaustible Intention) also it is said: He does not seek awakening by counting <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), thinking 'I shall put on armor for this many <s>kalpas</s>, I shall put on armor for this many <s>kalpas</s>.' Rather, he puts on truly inconceivable armor. If the entire beginningless extent of <s>saṃsāra</s> were to constitute a single day-and-night, then with such day-and-nights, in a fortnight of fifteen days, in a month of thirty days, in a year of twelve months, by this reckoning of years, up to a hundred thousand years — if I were to produce a single <s>bodhicitta</s> (thought of awakening) and behold a single <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One; by this method, by this reckoning, with aridings of <s>bodhicitta</s> and visions of <s>Tathāgatas</s> equal to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, I would come to know the mental conduct of each and every being; by this very method, by this reckoning, with that many arisings of <s>bodhicitta</s> and visions of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, I would come to know the mental conduct of all beings — thus undaunted. This armor of the <s>bodhisattva</s> is inexhaustible armor. The same method applies to <s>dāna</s> (generosity) and the other qualities conducive to awakening and the marks of a <s>mahāpuruṣa</s> (great being).

body.text: ārya-ratna-meghe * apy uktaṃ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Ratnamegha</s> (Noble Cloud of Jewels Sūtra) also it is said:

body.text: na bodhi-satvaḥ satva-khaṭuṅkatāṃ satva-dur-dāntatāṃ jñātvā | alam ebhiḥ satvair evaṃ khaṭuṅkair evaṃ dur-dāntair iti | tato nidānaṃ parikhinnaḥ parā-pṛṣṭhī-bhūtaḥ | pariśuddhāyāṃ loka-dhātau praṇidhānaṃ karoti | yatra + īdṛśānāṃ satvānāṃ nāma + api na śṛṇuyāt | na ca satva-artha-vaimukhyasya bodhi-satva-pariśuddhāyāṃ loka-dhātāv upapattir bhavati | tatra prājño bodhi-satva evaṃ cittam utpādayati | tasmāt satva-dhātor ye satvāḥ syuḥ pratyavarā dhajaḍa-eḍa-mūka-jātīyāḥ | a-parinirvāṇa-dharmakāḥ kṛtsnā satva-dhātau na cikitsitāḥ sarva-buddhaiḥ sarva-bodhi-satvaiś ca pratyākhyātāḥ | teṣāṃ madīye buddha-kṣetre saṃnipātaḥ syāt | tān ahaṃ sarvān bodhi-maṇḍe niṣīdya + an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhim abhisaṃbodhayeyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: A <s>bodhisattva</s>, having recognized the stubbornness and intractability of beings, does not think: 'Enough with these beings who are so stubborn, so intractable!' and thereby become disheartened and turn his back, making a vow for rebirth in a pure <s>lokadhātu</s> (world-realm) where he would not even hear the name of such beings. For one who turns away from the welfare of beings, there is no rebirth in the purified world-realm of a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Therein, the wise <s>bodhisattva</s> produces this thought: 'Therefore, whatever beings in the realm of beings are the lowest — the dull, the foolish, the deaf, the mute by nature, those whose nature is not to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation), who are not cared for in the entire realm of beings and are rejected by all <s>Buddhas</s> — may they gather in my <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field). Having sat at the seat of awakening, I shall awaken them all to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening).'

body.text: evaṃ hi bodhi-satvasya cintayataś citta-utpāde citta-utpāde sarva-māra-bhavanāni prakampante | sarva-buddhāś ca + asya varṇa-vādino bhavanti + iti ||
body.translated_text: For indeed, when the <s>bodhisattva</s> contemplates thus, at each arising of the thought, all the palaces of <s>Māra</s> tremble, and all the <s>Buddhas</s> become proclaimers of his praise.

body.text: evaṃ tāvat puṇya-vṛddhi-kāmena āśayo dṛḍhī-kartavyaḥ | āśaya-dṛḍhī-karaṇa-artham adhunā + ucyate | kiṃ punar anena dṛḍhī-kṛtena + iti | vimarṣa-nirāsāya dharma-saṃgīti-sūtre gaditaṃ |āśaye samyag bhagavan buddha-dharmāṇāṃ mūlaṃ | yasya punar āśayo na + asti sarve buddha-dharmās tasya dūre ||
body.translated_text: Thus, one who desires the increase of merit must first strengthen one's <s>āśaya</s> (intention/disposition). For the purpose of strengthening the <s>āśaya</s>, the following is now stated. But what is the use of this strengthened intention? To dispel doubt, it is declared in the <s>Dharmasaṃgītisūtra</s> (Sūtra of the Compilation of Dharma): 'O <s>Bhagavan</s> (Blessed One), right intention is the root of the <s>buddhadharmas</s> (qualities of a Buddha). For one who lacks this intention, all <s>buddhadharmas</s> are far away.'

body.text: āśaya-saṃpannasya punar bhagavan yadi buddhā na bhavanti gagana-talād dharma-śabdo niścarati kuḍma-vṛkṣebhyaś ca | āśaya-śuddhasya bodhi-satvasya sva-mano-jalpād eva sarva-avavāda-anuśāsanyo niścaranti | tasmāt tarhi bhagavan bodhi-satvena + āśaya-saṃpannena bhavitavyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: For one endowed with right <s>āśaya</s> (intention), O <s>Bhagavan</s>, even if <s>Buddhas</s> do not appear, the sound of the <s>Dharma</s> issues forth from the sky and from <s>kuḍma</s>-trees. For the <s>bodhisattva</s> whose <s>āśaya</s> is pure, all admonitions and instructions issue forth from his own mental discourse. Therefore, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> must be endowed with right <s>āśaya</s>.
