body.text: tad yathā bhagavan yasya pādau tasya gamanaṃ evaṃ bhagavan yasya + āśayas tasya buddha-dharmāḥ |tad yathā bhagavan yasya + uttama-aṅgaṃ tasya jīvitaṃ evam eva bhagavan yasya + āśayas tasya buddha-bodhiḥ | tad yathā bhagavan yasya jīvitaṃ tasya lābhaḥ | evam eva bhagavan yasya + āśayas tasya buddhatva-lābhaḥ | tad yathā bhagavan satītvena + agnir jvalati | a-satītvena na jvalati | evam eva bhagavann āśaye sati bodhi-satvasya sarva-buddha-dharmā jvalanti | a-saty āśaye na jvalanti | tad yathā bhagavan satsv abhra-megheṣu varṣaṃ varṣaty a-satsu na varṣati | evam eva bhagavann āśaye sati buddha-dharmāḥ pravartante | tad yathā bhagavan yasya vṛkṣasya mūlaṃ vipannaṃ tasya puṣpa-phalāni na bhūyaḥ prarohanti | evam eva bhagavan yasya + āśayo vipannas tasya sarve kuśalā dharmā na bhūyaḥ saṃbhavanti | tasmāt tarhi bhagavan bodhi-satvena buddha-bodhy-arthikena sva-āśayaḥ su-udgṛhītaḥ sv-ārakṣitaḥ su-śodhitaḥ sv-adhiṣṭhitaḥ kartavya iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as, O Blessed One, whoever has feet has walking — even so, O Blessed One, whoever has the [right] intention (<s>āśaya</s>) has the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. Just as, O Blessed One, whoever has a head has life — even so, O Blessed One, whoever has the [right] intention has <s>bodhi</s>. Just as, O Blessed One, whoever has life has gain — even so, O Blessed One, whoever has the [right] intention has the gain of <s>Buddhahood</s>. Just as, O Blessed One, when there is a wick, fire blazes, and when there is no wick, it does not blaze — even so, O Blessed One, when the intention exists, all the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities of the <s>bodhisattva</s> blaze; when the intention does not exist, they do not blaze. Just as, O Blessed One, when rain-clouds exist, rain falls, and when they do not exist, it does not fall — even so, O Blessed One, when the intention exists, the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities operate. Just as, O Blessed One, when the root of a tree is ruined, its flowers and fruits no longer sprout — even so, O Blessed One, when the intention is ruined, all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> no longer arise. Therefore, O Blessed One, the <s>bodhisattva</s> who seeks <s>Buddhabodhi</s> should make his own intention well-grasped, well-guarded, well-purified, and well-established.'

body.text: ko * ayam āśayo nāma | ārya-akṣayamati-sūtre * abhihitaḥ | sa khalu punar āśayo * a-kṛtrimaḥ a-kṛtakatvāt | a-kṛtako niḥ-sādhyatvāt | niḥ-sādhyaḥ su-viditatvāt | su-vidito nir-māyatvāt | nir-māyaḥ śuddhatvāt | śuddhaḥ ṛjukatvāt | ṛjukaḥ a-kuṭilatvāt | a-kuṭilaḥ spaṣṭatvāt | spaṣṭo * a-vi-ṣamatvāt | a-vi-ṣamaḥ sāratvāt | sāro * a-bhedyatvāt | a-bhedyo dṛḍhatvāt | dṛḍho * a-calitatvāt | a-calita a-niśritatvād ity ādi | ayam eva ca + adhika-adhika-guṇa-adhigama-pravṛtto * adhyāśaya ity ucyate ||
body.translated_text: What is this "intention" (<s>āśaya</s>)? It is described in the noble <s>Akṣayamatisūtra</s>: 'That intention is indeed unfeigned, because it is unfabricated. Unfabricated, because there is nothing to be accomplished. Without need of accomplishment, because it is well-known. Well-known, because it is free from deception. Free from deception, because it is pure. Pure, because it is straight. Straight, because it is not crooked. Not crooked, because it is clear. Clear, because it is not uneven. Not uneven, because it is substantial. Substantial, because it is unbreakable. Unbreakable, because it is firm. Firm, because it is unshaken. Unshaken, because it is independent.' And so on. And this same [intention], engaged in the attainment of ever-greater qualities, is called the high intention (<s>adhyāśaya</s>).

body.text: yathā + atra + eva + uktaṃ | uttaraṇa-adhyāśayo viśeṣa-gamanatayā ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the same [sūtra]: 'The high intention of deliverance consists in the going toward distinction' — and so on.

body.text: api ca + adhyāśaya ucyate | saumyatā bhūteṣu | maitratā satveṣu | hita-cittatā āryeṣu | kāruṇyam an-āryeṣu | gauravaṃ guruṣu | trāṇatā a-trāṇeṣu | śaraṇatā a-śaraṇeṣu | dvīpatā + a-dvīpeṣu | parāyaṇatā a-parāyaṇeṣu | sahāyatā a-sahāyeṣu | ṛjutā kuṭileṣu | spaṣṭatā khaṭuṅkeṣu | a-śaṭhatā śaṭheṣu | a-māyā āgahana-cariteṣu | kṛta-jñatā a-kṛta-jñeṣu | kṛta-veditā drohiṣu | upakāritā an-upakāriṣu | satyatā a-bhūta-gateṣu | nir-mānatā śrabdheṣu | a-ninditā su a-nindanā kṛteṣu

children.text: | an-ārocanatā para-skhaliteṣu | ārakṣaṇatā vipratipanneṣu | a-doṣa-darśanatā sarva-upāya-kauśalya-caryāsu | śuśrūṣaṇatā sarva-dakṣiṇīyeṣu | pradakṣiṇa-grāhitā + anuśāsanīṣv ity ādi ||
children.translated_text: Non-disclosure of others' faults; protectiveness toward those who have gone astray; not seeing fault in all conduct of skillful means; readiness to serve all who are worthy of offerings; receptiveness to instructions — and so on.

body.translated_text: Moreover, the high intention (<s>adhyāśaya</s>) is said to be: gentleness toward living creatures; friendliness toward beings; benevolent thought toward the noble; compassion toward the ignoble; reverence toward teachers; being a protector of the unprotected; being a refuge of the refugeless; being an island for those without an island; being a resort for those without a resort; being a companion for those without a companion; straightness toward the crooked; clarity toward the unrefined; non-deceit toward the deceitful; non-deception toward those of covert conduct; gratitude toward the ungrateful; acknowledgment toward the treacherous; helpfulness toward the unhelpful; truthfulness toward those who deal in falsehood; freedom from pride toward the faithful; non-censure and non-blaming of those who have acted [wrongly].

body.text: tad evaṃ vyavasāya-āśayau dṛḍhī-kṛtya kāruṇyaṃ puras-kṛtya yate śubha-vṛddhaye ||
body.translated_text: Thus, having made firm one's resolve and intention, and placing compassion at the forefront, one should strive for the increase of the wholesome.

body.text: yathā + uktam ārya-dharma-saṃgīti-sūtre | atha khalv avalokiteśvaro bodhi-satvo mahā-satvo bhagavantam etad avocat | na bhagavan bodhi-satvena + ati-bahuṣu dharmeṣu śikṣitavyaṃ | eko dharmo bhagavan bodhi-satvena sv-ārādhitaḥ su-pratividdhaḥ kartavyaḥ | tasya sarva-buddha-dharmāḥ kara-tala-gatā bhavanti | katama eka-dharmo | yad uta mahā-karuṇā | mahā-karuṇayā bhagavan bodhi-satvānāṃ sarva-buddha-dharmāḥ kara-tala-gatā bhavanti | tad yathā bhagavan yena rājñaś cakra-vartinaś cakra-ratnaṃ gacchati | tena sarvo bala-kāyo gacchati | evam eva bhagavan yena bodhi-satvasya mahā-karuṇā gacchati | tena sarve buddha-dharmā gacchanti | tad yathā bhagavann āditye udite satvāḥ karma-kriyāsu pracurā bhavanti | evam eva bhagavan mahā-karuṇā yatra + uditā bhavati tatra + anya-bodhi-karā dharmāḥ kriyāsu pracurā bhavanti | tad yathā bhagavan sarveṣām indriyāṇāṃ manasā + adhiṣṭhitānāṃ sva-sva-viṣaye grahaṇa-prācuryaṃ bhavati | evam eva bhagavan mahā-karuṇā-adhiṣṭhitānām anyeṣāṃ bodhi-karāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ svasmin svasmin karaṇīye prācuryaṃ bhavati | tad yathā bhagavan jīvita-indriye saty anyeṣām indriyāṇāṃ pravṛttir bhavati | evam eva bhagavan mahā-karuṇāyāṃ satyām anyeṣāṃ bodhi-karāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ pravṛttir bhavati + iti ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the noble <s>Dharmasaṅgītisūtra</s>: 'Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> said to the Blessed One: "The <s>bodhisattva</s> need not train in excessively many <s>dharmas</s>, O Blessed One. One single <s>dharma</s>, O Blessed One, should be well-practiced and well-penetrated by the <s>bodhisattva</s>. Through that, all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities come into the palm of his hand. What is that one <s>dharma</s>? Namely, great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>). Through great compassion, O Blessed One, all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities come into the palm of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' hands. Just as, O Blessed One, wherever the wheel-treasure of a <s>Cakravartin</s> king goes, the entire army follows — even so, O Blessed One, wherever the great compassion of the <s>bodhisattva</s> goes, all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities follow. Just as, O Blessed One, when the sun has risen, beings become active in their works — even so, O Blessed One, wherever great compassion has arisen, the other <s>bodhi</s>-producing <s>dharmas</s> become active in their functions. Just as, O Blessed One, when all the sense-faculties are governed by the mind, there is an abundance of apprehension in their respective domains — even so, O Blessed One, when the other <s>bodhi</s>-producing <s>dharmas</s> are governed by great compassion, there is an abundance in each of their respective tasks. Just as, O Blessed One, when the life-faculty exists, the other faculties operate — even so, O Blessed One, when great compassion exists, the other <s>bodhi</s>-producing <s>dharmas</s> operate."'

body.text: ārya-akṣayamati-sūtre * apy āha ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Akṣayamatisūtra</s> also it is said:

body.text: tad yathā + api nāma bhadanta sāradvatīputra puruṣasya jīvita-indriyasya + āśvāsāḥ praśvāsāḥ pūrvaṃ-gamāḥ | evam eva bhadanta sāradvatīputra bodhi-satvasya mahā-yāna-samudāgatasya mahā-karuṇā pūrvaṃ-gamāḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as, O Venerable <s>Sāradvatīputra</s> (<s>Śāriputra</s>), inhalations and exhalations precede a person's life-faculty — even so, O Venerable <s>Sāradvatīputra</s>, great compassion precedes the <s>bodhisattva</s> who has attained the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: syād yathā + api nāma śreṣṭhino vā gṛha-pater vā eka-putrake guṇavati majjā-gataṃ prema | evam eva mahā-karuṇā-pratilabdhasya bodhi-satvasya sarva-satveṣu majjā-gataṃ prema + iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as a wealthy merchant or householder has a marrow-deep love for his only virtuous son — even so, the <s>bodhisattva</s> who has attained great compassion has a marrow-deep love for all beings.'

body.text: katham eṣā bhāvayitavyā | svakam an-eka-vidhaṃ pūrva-anubhūtam anubhūyamānaṃ vā duṣkhaṃ bhayaṃ ca sva-ātmany aty-antam an-iṣṭaṃ bhāvayitvā | priya-ādiṣu maitrī maitrīvatā bhāvayitavyā praty-utpanna-duṣkha-vyādhiṣu mahā-duṣkha-sāgara-an-avadhi-dīrgha-saṃsāra-vyasana-anunīteṣu vā ||
body.translated_text: How should this [compassion] be cultivated? Having contemplated one's own manifold suffering and fear — previously experienced or being experienced — as utterly unwanted in oneself, loving-kindness should be cultivated through the quality of friendliness toward loved ones and others — whether they are afflicted by present suffering and disease, or whether they are brought low by the calamity of the boundless, long ocean of great suffering in <s>saṃsāra</s>.

body.text: yathā + uktam ārya-daśa-bhūmaka-sūtre | tasya + evaṃ bhavaty āścaryaṃ yāvad a-jñāna-saṃmūḍhā vata + ime bāla-pṛthag-janāḥ | yeṣām a-saṃkhyeyā ātma-bhāvā niruddhā nirudhyante nirotsyante ca | evaṃ ca kṣīyamāṇā kāye na nir-vedam utpādayanti | bhūyasyā mātrayā duṣkha-yantraṃ vivardhayanti | saṃsāra-śrotasaś ca mahā-bhayān na nivartante | skandha-ālayaṃ ca na + utsṛjanti | dhātu-ura-gebhyaś ca na nirvidyante | nandī-rāga-andhāś ca na + avabudhyante | ṣaḍ-āyatana-śūnya-grāmaṃ ca na vyavalokayanti | ahaṃ-kāra-mama-kāra-abhiniveśa-anuśayaṃ ca na prajahanti | māna-dṛṣṭi-śalyaṃ ca na + uddharanti | rāga-dveṣa-moha-jālaṃ ca na praśamayanti | a-vidyā-moha-andha-kāraṃ ca na vidhamayanti | tṛṣṇā-arṇavaṃ ca na + ucchoṣayanti | daśa-bala-sa-artha-vāhaṃ ca na paryeṣante | māra-āśaya-gahana-anugatāś ca saṃsāra-sāgare vividha-a-kuśala-vitarka-grāha-ākule pariplavante | a-prati-śaraṇāḥ tathā saṃvegam āpadyante bahūni duṣkhāni pratyanubhavantaḥ | yad idaṃ jāti-jarā-vyādhi-maraṇa-śoka-parideva-duṣkha-daurmanasya-upāyāsān | hanta + aham eṣāṃ satvānāṃ duṣkha-ārtānām a-nāthānām a-trāṇānām a-śaraṇānām a-layanānām a-a-parāyaṇānām andhānām a-vidyā-aṇḍa-koṣa-paṭala-paryavanaddhānāṃ tamo-abhibhūtānām arthāya + eko * a-dvitīyo bhūtvā tathā-rūpa-puṇya-jñāna-saṃbhāra-upacayaṃ bibharmi | yathā-rūpeṇa puṇya-jñāna-saṃbhāra-upacayena saṃbhṛtena ime sarva-satvā abhyanta-viśuddhim anuprāpnuyur iti ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the noble <s>Daśabhūmikasūtra</s>: 'This [thought] arises in him: "Alas, how extraordinary — these foolish ordinary persons are confused by ignorance! Their innumerable bodies have ceased, are ceasing, and will cease. And yet, even as they are being destroyed, they do not generate disenchantment with the body. They increasingly augment the mechanism of suffering. They do not turn back from the great terror of the current of <s>saṃsāra</s>. They do not relinquish the abode of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates). They are not disenchanted with the dwelling of the <s>dhātus</s> (elements). They do not awaken, blinded by delight and attachment. They do not observe the empty village of the six <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases). They do not abandon the underlying tendency of grasping at I-making and mine-making. They do not extract the thorn of pride and wrong views. They do not pacify the net of attachment, hatred, and delusion. They do not dispel the darkness of ignorance and delusion. They do not dry up the ocean of craving. They do not seek out the caravan-leader of the ten powers. Following the thicket of <s>Māra</s>'s intentions, they drift about in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, crowded with various crocodiles of unwholesome thoughts — without refuge, they fall into such distress, experiencing many sufferings: birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, mental distress, and anguish. Come, I shall become single, without a second, for the benefit of these beings — suffering, lordless, unprotected, without refuge, without shelter, without a resort, blind, enveloped in the covering-shell of the egg of ignorance, overcome by darkness — and I shall bear such an accumulation of the collection of merit and knowledge by which, having been assembled, all these beings may attain inner purity."'

body.text: tathā + atra + eva + āha | saṃsāra-aṭavī-kāntāra-mārga-prapannā vata + ime satvā niraya-tiryag-yoni-yama-loka-prapāta-abhimukhāḥ ku-dṛṣṭi-vi-ṣama-jāla-anuprāptāḥ moha-gahana-saṃchannā mithyā-mārga-vitatha-prayātā | andhī-bhūtāḥ pariṇāyaka-vi-kalāḥ || pe ||
body.translated_text: And in the same [sūtra] it is also said: 'Alas, these beings, set upon the path of the wilderness-desert of <s>saṃsāra</s>, face the precipice of the hells, the animal realm, and the world of <s>Yama</s>; they have entered the uneven net of wrong views; they are covered by the thicket of delusion; they have gone astray on the false path. Become blind, they are without a guide.' [And so on in abbreviated form.]

body.text: saṃsāra-śrota-anuvāhinaḥ tṛṣṇā-nadī-prapannāḥ | mahā-vega-grastā | avalokanā-a-samarthāḥ

children.text: kāma-vyāpāda-vicikitsā-vihiṃsā-vitarka-prapāta-anucaritāḥ | sva-kāya-dṛṣṭy-udaka-rākṣasa-gṛhītāḥ | kāma-gahana-āvartta-anupraviṣṭāḥ nandī-rāga-madhya-saṃsaktāḥ | asmi-māna-sthala-ucchannāḥ | a-parāyaṇāḥ | āyatana-grāma-an-ucchalitāḥ | kuśala-saṃbhāraka-virahitāḥ | te * asmābhir mahā-kuśala-mūla-balena + uddhṛtya nir-upadrave a-rajasi śiva-sarva-jñatā-ratna-dvīpe pratiṣṭhāpayitavyā | ruddhā vata + ime satvā bahu-duṣkha-daurmanasya-upāyāsa-bahula-anunaya-pratigha-priya-a-priya-vinibandhane sa-śoka-parideva-anucarite tṛṣṇā-nigaḍa-bandhane māyā-śāṭhya-a-vidyā-gahana-saṃchanne traidhātuka-cārake | te asmābhiḥ sarva-traidhātuka-viveke a-bhaya-pure sarva-duṣkha-upaśame
children.translated_text: '— accompanied by the precipice of thoughts of sensual desire, ill-will, doubt, and harmfulness; seized by the water-demon of the view of self-body (<s>svakāyadṛṣṭi</s>); having entered the whirlpool of the thicket of desire; caught in the midst of delight and attachment; cast up on the sandbank of the conceit "I am" (<s>asmimāna</s>); without a resort; unescaped from the village of the sense-bases; devoid of the provisions of wholesome [dharmas]. They should be rescued by us through the power of great wholesome roots and established on the jewel-island of omniscience — free from calamity, free from dust, and auspicious. Alas, these beings are obstructed — abundant in manifold sufferings, mental distress, and anguish, bound by the fetters of hostility and attraction to the pleasant and unpleasant, accompanied by sorrow and lamentation, bound in the shackles of craving, covered by the thicket of deception, guile, and ignorance, wandering in the three realms. They should be [rescued] by us [and established] in the fearless city, separated from all three realms, in the cessation of all suffering —'
'— and established in <s>Nirvāṇa</s> without obstruction.' And so on.

body.translated_text: 'They are carried along by the current of <s>saṃsāra</s>, set upon the river of craving, seized by a great torrent, unable to look back —'

body.text: evam ebhiḥ paras-para-dṛḍhī-kṛtyair vyavasāya-āśaya-kāruṇyaiḥ puṇya-vṛddhim ārabhet | tatra tāvad bhadra-ācāryā-vidhiḥ kāryā vandanā-ādiḥ sad-ādarāt ||
body.translated_text: Thus, through these mutually reinforcing [qualities] — resolve, intention, and compassion — one should undertake the increase of merit. Therein, first, the procedure of the virtuous conduct (<s>bhadrācārya</s>) — salutation and so forth — should be performed with constant reverence.

body.text: ārya-ugradatta-paripṛcchāyāṃ hi tri-rātre trir divasasya ca śuceḥ śuci-vastra-prāvṛtasya ca tri-skandhaka-pravartanam uktaṃ ||
body.translated_text: For in the noble <s>Ugradattaparipṛcchā</s>, the practice of the three sections (<s>triskandha</s>) is prescribed: three times by night and three times by day, for one who is pure and clad in clean garments.

body.text: tatra trayaḥ skandhāḥ pāpa-deśanā-puṇya-anumodanā-buddha-adhyeṣaṇa-ākhyāḥ puṇya-rāśitvāt | tatra vandanā pāpa-deśanāyām antar-bhavati | buddhān namas-kṛtya + upāli-paripṛcchāyāṃ deśanā + iti kṛtvā | yācanam adhyeṣaṇāyāṃ eka-arthatvāt | pūjā tu vibhava-a-bhāvād a-nityā + iti na + uktā | mānasī vācasī ca sūtra-antara-prasiddhatvān na + uktāḥ | trayāṇāṃ tu vacanāt prādhānyaṃ gamyate | tatra vandanā | sarva-buddhān namasyāmi + iti ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the three sections are called: confession of sins (<s>pāpadeśanā</s>), rejoicing in merit (<s>puṇyānumodanā</s>), and entreaty of the <s>Buddhas</s> (<s>buddhādhyeṣaṇā</s>) — because they constitute masses of merit. Therein, salutation is included within confession. Having paid homage to the <s>Buddhas</s>, [one confesses] as described in the <s>Upāliparipṛcchā</s> —

body.text: ārya-akṣayamati-sūtre tv ātma-para-pāpa-deśanā puṇya-saṃbhāre paṭhyate ||
body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Akṣayamatisūtra</s>, however, the confession of one's own and others' sins is recited as [part of] the collection of merit.

body.text: gāthā-catuṣṭayena ca yathā-gītaiś ca stotraiḥ | ārya-bhadra-caryā-ādi-gāthābhir vā pūjanā ca ||
body.translated_text: And worship [should be performed] with four verses and hymns of praise as appropriate, or with the verses of the noble <s>Bhadracarī</s> (Prayer of Good Conduct) and so forth.

body.text: ārya-ratna-meghe yathā + uktaṃ | iha bodhi-satvo yāni + imāni bhavanti puṣpa-jātāni vā phala-jātāni vā a-mamāny a-parigrahāṇi | tāni triṣ-kṛtvā rātrau triṣ-kṛtvā divase buddha-bodhisatvebhyo niryātayati || pe ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the noble <s>Ratnamegha</s>: 'Here the <s>bodhisattva</s> [takes] whatever flowers or fruits there are that are ownerless and unpossessed, three times by night and three times by day, [and] presents them to the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s> —'

body.text: sayathi + ime

children.text: dhūpa-vṛkṣā vā gandha-vṛkṣā vā ratna-vṛkṣā vā kalpa-vṛkṣā vā a-mamā a-parigrahās tān api triṣ-kṛtvā rātrau triṣ-kṛtvā divase buddha-bodhisatvebhyo niryātayati + iti ||
children.translated_text: '— incense-trees, or fragrant trees, or jewel-trees, or <s>kalpa</s>-trees (wish-fulfilling trees) that are ownerless and unpossessed — those too, three times by night and three times by day, he presents to the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s>.'

body.translated_text: 'Suppose these —'

body.text: ārya-tri-samaya-rāje * api sthala-jā ratna-parvatāḥ | jala-jā ratna-parvatā sthala-jala-jāni ratnāni daśa-dig-avasthitāni | a-mamāny a-parigrahāṇi deyāni + ity uktaṃ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Trisamayarāja</s> too it is said that 'jewel-mountains born on land, jewel-mountains born in water, and jewels born from land and water, established in the ten directions — being without possessiveness and without attachment — should be given.'

body.text: anayā ca diśā sarva-bhaiṣajyāni sarva-rasāyanāni sarva-salilāni an-avadyāni ap-maṇḍalāni | sarva-kāñcana-maṇḍalāni | vivṛtteṣu vā loka-dhātuṣu ye parama-rasa-sparśa-saṃpannā bhū-parpaṭakāḥ | a-mṛta-latā | a-kṛṣṭa-uptā vā śālayaḥ | sarva-uttara-kuru-dvīpeṣu | pariśuddheṣu ca loka-dhātuṣu ye ramaṇīyatarāḥ paribhogāḥ ||
body.translated_text: And by this same method, all medicines, all elixirs (<s>rasāyana</s>), all blameless waters, water-circles, all golden circles; and in worlds that have evolved, the finest crusts of earth endowed with supreme flavors and textures; the creepers of ambrosia; rice growing without being planted; all in the <s>Uttarakuru</s> continents; and whatever are the most delightful enjoyments in purified world-realms —

body.text: yathā ca + ārya-ratna-meghe eva + āha | sa yāni + imāni sūtra-anteṣu + udāra-udārāṇi tathā-gata-pūjā-upasthānāni śṛṇoti | tāny āśayatas tīvreṇa + adhyāśayena buddha-bodhisatvebhyaḥ pariṇāmayati + iti | tathā | sa vividhāni pūjā-upasthānāni anuvicintayati + iti ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Ārya-Ratnamegha</s> itself: 'He hears of those supremely magnificent offerings and attendances upon the <s>Tathāgata</s> [described] in the <s>sūtra</s>-conclusions, and with earnest intention and fervent higher aspiration, he dedicates them to the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s>.' Likewise: 'He mentally visualizes various offerings and attendances.'

body.text: deśanā pūrva-uktā + iva | ārya-akṣayamati-sūtre tv ātma-para-pāpa-deśanā puṇya-saṃbhāre paṭhyate | anumodanā bhadra-caryā-gāthayā | candra-pradīpa-anumodanā-parivartena vā | adhyeṣaṇā bhadra-caryayā + eva | pariṇāmanā tu sakala-samāptā + ārya-bhadra-caryayā + eva | vajra-dhvaja-pariṇāmanāṃ vā paśyet ||
body.translated_text: Confession is as stated previously. But in the <s>Ārya-Akṣayamati Sūtra</s>, the confession of one's own and others' sins is read as [part of] the accumulation of merit. Rejoicing is [done] through the <s>Bhadracaryā</s> verses; or through the chapter on rejoicing in the <s>Candrapradīpa</s>. Entreaty is through the <s>Bhadracaryā</s> itself. Dedication, however, is completely accomplished through the noble <s>Bhadracaryā</s> (Prayer of Good Conduct) itself; or one may refer to the <s>Vajradhvajapariṇāmanā</s> (Vajra-banner Dedication).

body.text: atha-vā daśa-bhūmaka-uktāni mahā-praṇidhānāni | yathā + āha | yad uta + a-śeṣa-niḥ-śeṣa-an-avaśeṣa-sarva-buddha-pūjā-upasthāpanāya | sarva-ākāra-vara-upetam udāra-adhimukti-viśuddhaṃ dharma-dhātu-vipulam ākāśa-dhātu-paryavasānam a-para-anta-koṭī-niṣṭhaṃ sarva-kalpa-saṃkhyā-buddha-utpāda-saṃkhyā-pratiprasrabdhaṃ | mahā-pūjā-upasthānāya | prathamaṃ mahā-praṇidhānam abhinirharati ||
body.translated_text: Alternatively, [one may use] the great aspirations stated in the <s>Daśabhūmaka</s>. As it says: 'Namely, for the purpose of establishing offerings and attendance upon all <s>Buddhas</s> — entirely, completely, without remainder — endowed with all the best modes, purified through noble aspiration, as vast as the <s>Dharma</s>-realm, extending to the limits of space, reaching the ultimate limit of the furthest end, relaxing through the number of all <s>kalpas</s> and the number of <s>Buddha</s>-arisings — for the purpose of the great offering and attendance, he brings forth the first great aspiration.'

body.text: yad uta sarva-tathā-gata-bhāṣita-dharma-netrī-saṃdhāraṇāya sarva-buddha-bodhi-satva-parigrahāya | sarva-samyak-saṃbuddha-śāsana-parirakṣaṇāya | dharma-dhātu-vipulam ākāśa-dhātu-paryavasānam a-para-anta-koṭī-niṣṭhaṃ | sarva-saṃkalpa-saṃkhyā-buddha-utpāda-saṃkhyā-pratiprasrabdhaṃ | sad-dharma-parigrahāya | dvitīyaṃ mahā-praṇidhānam abhinirharati ||
body.translated_text: 'Namely, for the purpose of retaining the <s>Dharma</s>-vision spoken by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; for the support of all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s>; for the protection of the teaching of all perfectly awakened ones — as vast as the <s>Dharma</s>-realm, extending to the limits of space, reaching the ultimate limit of the furthest end, relaxing through the number of all <s>kalpas</s> and the number of <s>Buddha</s>-arisings — for the purpose of embracing the true <s>Dharma</s>, he brings forth the second great aspiration.'

body.text: yad uta sarva-buddha-utpāda-nir-avaśeṣa-sarva-loka-dhātu-prasareṣu | tuṣita-bhavana-vāsam ādiṃ kṛtvā cyavana-ācaṅkramaṇa-garbha-sthiti-janma-kumāra-krīḍā-antaḥ-pura-vāsa-abhiniṣkramaṇa-duṣ-kara-caryā-bodhi-maṇḍa-upasaṃkramaṇa-māra-dharṣaṇa-abhisaṃbodhy-adhyeṣaṇa-mahā-dharma-cakra-pravartana-mahā-parinirvāṇa-upasaṃkramaṇāya | pūjā-dharma-saṃgraha-prayoga-pūrvaṃ-gamaṃ kṛtvā sarva-traikāla-vivartanāya | dharma-dhātu-vipulam ākāśa-dhātu-paryavasānam a-para-anta-koṭī-niṣṭhaṃ sarva-kalpa-saṃkhyā-buddha-utpāda-saṃkhyā-pratiprasrabdhaṃ yāvan mahā-parinirvāṇa-upasaṃkramaṇāya | tṛtīyaṃ mahā-praṇidhānam abhinirharati ||
body.translated_text: 'Namely, for the purpose of [attending upon] the arising of all <s>Buddhas</s> throughout all world-realms without remainder — beginning with the dwelling in the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, the descent, the walking [in the mother's womb], the abiding in the womb, the birth, the youth's sports, the dwelling in the inner palace, the going forth, the difficult practice, the approach to the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>), the conquest of <s>Māra</s>, the perfect awakening, the entreaty [to teach], the turning of the great wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, and the approach to the great <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — making the effort of worship and <s>Dharma</s>-gathering the forerunner, for the revolution of all in the three times — as vast as the <s>Dharma</s>-realm, extending to the limits of space, reaching the ultimate limit of the furthest end, relaxing through the number of all <s>kalpas</s> and the number of <s>Buddha</s>-arisings, up to the approach to the great <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — he brings forth the third great aspiration.'

body.text: yad uta sarva-bodhi-satva-caryā-vipula-mahad-gata-a-pramāṇa-a-saṃbhinna-sarva-pāramitā-su-saṃgrahītaḥ | sarva-bhūmi-pariśodhanaṃ sa-aṅga-upāṅga-nirhāraṃ yāvat sa-lakṣaṇa-vi-lakṣaṇa-saṃvarta-vivarta-sarva-bodhi-satva-caryā-bhūta-yathā-vad bhūmi-patha-upadeśa-pāramitā-parikarma-avavāda-anuśāsany--anupradāna-upastambha-citta-utpāda-abhinirhārāya | dharma-dha-tu-vipulam ākāśa-dhātu-paryavasānam a-para-anta-koṭī-niṣṭhaṃ sarva-kalpa-saṃkhyā-caryā-saṃkhyā-pratiprasrabdhaṃ citta-utpāda-abhinirhārāya | caturthaṃ mahā-praṇidhānam abhinirharati ||
body.translated_text: 'Namely, [for the purpose of] the vast, great, immeasurable, unconfused, well-gathered practice of all <s>bodhisattvas</s> in all the perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>); the purification of all stages with their parts and sub-parts; up to the teaching of the path of stages of the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct as it truly is, with its characteristics and distinctions, its involution and evolution — the instruction, guidance, bestowal, support, and production of the mind-generation through the perfection of the training of the path — as vast as the <s>Dharma</s>-realm, extending to the limits of space, reaching the ultimate limit of the furthest end, relaxing through the number of all <s>kalpas</s> and the number of practices — for the purpose of producing the mind-generation, he brings forth the fourth great aspiration.'

body.text: yad uta nir-avaśeṣa-sarva-satva-dhātu-rūpy-a-rūpi-saṃjñā-saṃjñi na + eva saṃjñi na + a-saṃjñy aṇḍa-ja-jarāyu-ja-saṃsveda-ja-aupapāduka-traidhātuka-paryāpanna-ṣaḍ-gati-samavasṛta-sarva-upapatti-paryāpanna-nāma-rūpa-saṃgṛhīta-a-śeṣa-sarva-satva-dhātu-paripācanāya | sarva-buddha-dharma-avatāraṇāya | sarva-gati-saṃkhyā-vyavacchedanāya | sarva-jña-jñāna-pratiṣṭhāpanāya | dharma-dhātu-vipulam ākāśa-dhātu-paryavasānam a-para-anta-koṭī-niṣṭhaṃ sarva-kalpa-saṃkhyā-satva-dhātu-saṃkhyā-pratiprasrabdhaṃ |sarva-satva-dhātu-paripācanāya | pañcamaṃ mahā-praṇidhānam abhinirharati ||
body.translated_text: 'Namely, for the purpose of ripening the entire realm of beings without remainder — those with form and without form, with perception and without perception, neither with perception nor without perception; egg-born, womb-born, moisture-born, and spontaneously born; included within the three realms, entering the six destinies, included in all modes of birth, comprised in name-and-form — the entire realm of beings without remainder; for entering into all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>; for cutting off all destinies; for establishing [them] in omniscient knowledge — as vast as the <s>Dharma</s>-realm, extending to the limits of space, reaching the ultimate limit of the furthest end, relaxing through the number of all <s>kalpas</s> and the number of the realm of beings — for the purpose of ripening the entire realm of beings, he brings forth the fifth great aspiration.'

body.text: yad uta nir-avaśeṣa-sarva-loka-dhātu-vipula-saṃkṣipta-mahad-gata-a-pramāṇa-sūkṣma-audārika-vyatyasta-avamūrddha-sama-tala-praveśa-samavasaraṇa-anugata-indra-jāla-vibhāga-daśa-dig-a-śeṣa-vaimātrya-praveśa-vibhāga-jñāna-anugama-pratyakṣatāyai | dharma-dhātu-vipulam ākāśa-dhātu-paryavasānam a-para-anta-koṭī-niṣṭhaṃ sarva-kalpa-saṃkhyā-loka-dhātu-saṃkhyā-pratiprasrabdhaṃ loka-dhātu-vaimātrya-avatāraṇāya | ṣaṣṭhaṃ mahā-praṇidhānam abhinirharati ||
body.translated_text: 'Namely, for the purpose of the direct perception and knowledge that follows the diversity of all world-realms without remainder — vast and contracted, great and immeasurable, subtle and gross, inverted and upside-down, level and flat — their entry, convergence, following, <s>Indra</s>'s-net distribution, the entry into the diversity of the ten directions without remainder — as vast as the <s>Dharma</s>-realm, extending to the limits of space, reaching the ultimate limit of the furthest end, relaxing through the number of all <s>kalpas</s> and the number of world-realms — for the purpose of entering the diversity of world-realms, he brings forth the sixth great aspiration.'

body.text: yad uta sarva-kṣetra-eka-kṣetra eka-kṣetra sarva-kṣetrai-samavaśaraṇa-pariśodhanaṃ

children.text: | a-pramāṇa-buddha-kṣetra prabhā-vyūha-alaṃ-kāra-pratimaṇḍitaṃ | sarva-kleśa-apanayana-pariśuddhi-patha-upetaṃ | a-pramāṇa-jñāna-ākāra-satva-paripūrṇam udāra-buddha-viṣaya-samavasaraṇaṃ | yathā-āśaya-sarva-satva-saṃdarśana-saṃtoṣaṇāya | dharma-dhātu-vipulam ākāśa-dhātu-paryavasānam a-para-anta-koṭī-niṣṭhaṃ |sarva-kalpa-saṃkhyā-buddha-kṣetra-saṃkhyā-pratiprasrabdhaṃ |sarva-buddha-kṣetra-pariśodhanāya |saptamaṃ mahā-praṇidhānam abhinirharati ||
children.translated_text: '— adorned with the luminous array of immeasurable <s>Buddha</s>-fields; endowed with the path of purification that removes all afflictions; filled with beings of immeasurable knowledge-modes in the noble convergence of the <s>Buddha</s>-domain; for the purpose of displaying and satisfying all beings according to their aspirations — as vast as the <s>Dharma</s>-realm, extending to the limits of space, reaching the ultimate limit of the furthest end, relaxing through the number of all <s>kalpas</s> and the number of <s>Buddha</s>-fields — for the purpose of purifying all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, he brings forth the seventh great aspiration.'

body.translated_text: 'Namely, for the purpose of purifying all fields as one field and one field as all fields, their convergence and purification —'

body.text: yad uta sarva-bodhi-satva-eka-āśaya-prayogatāyai | niḥ-sapatna-kuśala-mūla-upacayāya | eka-ārambaṇa-sarva-bodhi-satva-samatāyai | a-virahita-satata-samita-buddha-bodhi-satva-samavadhānāya | yathā-iṣṭa-buddha-utpāda-saṃdarśanāya | sva-citta-utpāda-tathā-gata-prabhāva-jñāna-anugamāya | a-cyuta-anugāminy--abhijñā-pratilambhāya | sarva-loka-dhātv-anuvicaraṇāya sarva-parṣan-maṇḍala-pratibhāsa-prāptaye | sarva-upapatti-sva-śarīra-anugamāya | a-cintya-mahā-yāna-upetatāyai | bodhi-satva-caryā-caraṇa-a-vyavacchedāya | dharma-dhātu-vipulam ākāśa-dhātu-paryavasānam a-para-anta-koṭī-niṣṭhaṃ | sarva-kalpa-saṃkhyā-caryā-saṃkhyā-pratiprasrabdhaṃ | mahā-yāna-avatāraṇāya | aṣṭamaṃ mahā-praṇidhānam abhinirharati ||
body.translated_text: 'Namely, for the purpose of the unity of aspiration and effort of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>; for the accumulation of wholesome roots without rivalry; for the equality of all <s>bodhisattvas</s> in a single object; for the constant and uninterrupted communion with <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s>; for the display of the arising of <s>Buddhas</s> as desired; for the following of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s power and knowledge through one's own mind-generation; for the attainment of unfailing higher knowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>); for wandering through all world-realms; for attaining the reflection-appearance in all assemblies; for following one's own body in all modes of birth; for being endowed with the inconceivable <s>Mahāyāna</s>; for the unbroken practice of the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct — as vast as the <s>Dharma</s>-realm, extending to the limits of space, reaching the ultimate limit of the furthest end, relaxing through the number of all <s>kalpas</s> and the number of practices — for the purpose of entering the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, he brings forth the eighth great aspiration.'

body.text: yad uta + a-vivartya-cakra-samārūḍha-bodhi-satva-caryā-caraṇāya | a-mogha-kāya-vāṅ-manas-kareṇa | saha-darśana-niyata-sarva-buddha-dharma-pratilambhāya | saha-ghoṣa-udāhāra-jñāna-anugamāya | saha-prasāda-kleśa-vivartanāya | mahā-bhaiṣajya-rāja-upama-āśraya-pratilambhāya | cintā-maṇi-vat kāya-pratilambhāya | sarva-bodhi-satva-caryā-caraṇāya | dharma-dhātu-vipulam ākāśa-dhātu-paryavasānam a-para-anta-koṭī-niṣṭhaṃ | sarva-kalpa-saṃkhyā-caryā-saṃkhyā-pratiprasrabdhaṃ |amogha-ghoṣatāyai | navamaṃ mahā-praṇidhānam abhinirharati ||
body.translated_text: 'Namely, for the purpose of practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct mounted on the irreversible wheel; with unfailing body, speech, and mind-action; for the attainment of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> definite upon being seen; for following knowledge through the utterance of a single sound; for the turning away of afflictions upon a single moment of faith; for attaining a support like the great king of medicines; for attaining a body like a wish-fulfilling gem; for the practice of all <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct — as vast as the <s>Dharma</s>-realm, extending to the limits of space, reaching the ultimate limit of the furthest end, relaxing through the number of all <s>kalpas</s> and the number of practices — for the purpose of unfailing proclamation, he brings forth the ninth great aspiration.'

body.text: yad uta sarva-loka-dhātuṣv an-uttara-samyak-saṃbodhy-abhisaṃbodhanāya | eka-vāla-patha-a-vyativṛtta-sarva-bāla-pṛthag-jana-janma-upapatty-abhiniṣkramaṇa-vikurvaṇa-bodhi-maṇḍa-dharma-cakra-pravartana-mahā-parinirvāṇa-upadarśanāya | mahā-buddha-viṣaya-prabhāva-jñāna-anugamāya | sarva-satva-dhātu-yathā-āśaya-buddha-utpāda-kṣaṇa-kṣaṇa-avabodha-praśama-prāpaṇa-saṃdarśanāya | eka-abhisaṃbodhi-sarva-dharma-dhātu-nirmāṇa-spharaṇāya | eka-ghoṣa-udāhāra-sarva-satva-citta-āśaya-saṃtoṣaṇāya | mahā-parinirvāṇa-upadarśana-caryā-bala-a-vyupacchedāya | mahā-jñāna-bhūmi-sarva-dharma-vyutthāpana-saṃdarśanāya | dharma-jñāna-ṛddhi-māyā-abhijñā-sarva-loka-dhātu-spharaṇāya | dharma-dhātu-vipulam ākāśa-dhātu-paryavasānam a-para-anta-koṭī-niṣṭhaṃ | sarva-kalpa-saṃkhyā-abhisaṃbodhi-saṃkhyā-pratiprasrabdhaṃ | mahā-yāna-abhinirhārāya | daśamaṃ mahā-praṇidhānam abhinirharati + iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Namely, for the purpose of fully awakening to unsurpassed perfect awakening in all world-realms; for displaying, without going beyond a single hair-tip, the birth, arising, going forth, miraculous transformation, approach to the seat of awakening, turning of the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, and approach to the great <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of all confused ordinary persons; for following the power and knowledge of the great <s>Buddha</s>-domain; for displaying to the entire realm of beings, moment by moment, awakening and pacification according to their aspirations and the moments of <s>Buddha</s>-arising; for pervading the entire <s>Dharma</s>-realm with emanations from a single awakening; for satisfying the minds and aspirations of all beings through a single utterance; for the unbroken power of conduct even while displaying the great <s>parinirvāṇa</s>; for displaying the establishment of all <s>dharmas</s> from the ground of great knowledge; for pervading all world-realms through the knowledge of <s>Dharma</s>, miraculous power, and magical higher knowledge — as vast as the <s>Dharma</s>-realm, extending to the limits of space, reaching the ultimate limit of the furthest end, relaxing through the number of all <s>kalpas</s> and the number of awakenings — for the purpose of bringing forth the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, he brings forth the tenth great aspiration.'

body.text: etac ca bhāvayan sarvatra pariṇāmayāmi + iti yojyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: And while contemplating this, one should connect [the thought:] 'I dedicate everywhere.'

body.text: ārya-avalokiteśvara-vimokṣe ca yad uktaṃ tad apy evaṃ yojyaṃ | etat kuśala-mūlaṃ sarva-satva-prapāta-bhaya-vigamāya pariṇāmayāmi | sarva-satvān sāntānika-bhaya-praśamanāya | sarva-satva-saṃmoha-bhaya-vinivartanāya pariṇāmayāmi | sarva-satva-bandhana-bhaya-samucchedāya | sarva-satva-jīvita-uparodha-upakrama-bhaya-vyāvartanāya | sarva-satva-upakaraṇa-vaikalya-bhaya-apanayanāya | sarva-satva-ājīvikā-bhaya-vyupaśamanāya | sarva-satva-a-śloka-bhaya-samatikramaṇāya pariṇāmayāmi | sarva-satva-sāṃsārika-bhaya-upaśamanāya | sarva-satva-parṣac-chāradya-bhaya-vigamāya | sarva-satva-maraṇa-bhaya-vyatikramāya | sarva-satva-dur-gati-bhaya-vinivartanāya | sarva-satva-tamo-andha-kāra-vi-ṣama-gaty-a-pratyudāvartana-avabhāsa-karaṇāya pariṇāmayāmi | sarva-satvānāṃ vi-sabhāga-samavadhāna-bhaya-abhyanta-vigamāya | sarva-satva-priya-vi-prayoga-bhaya-nirodhāya | sarva-satva-a-priya-saṃvāsa-bhaya-apanayanāya | sarva-satva-kāya-paripīḍā-bhaya-visaṃyogāya | sarva-satva-citta-paripīḍana-bhaya-nirmokṣaṇāya | sarva-satva-duṣkha-daurmanasya-upāyāsa-samatikramaṇāya pariṇāmayāmi + iti ||
body.translated_text: And what is stated in the <s>Ārya-Avalokiteśvara-vimokṣa</s> should also be applied thus: 'I dedicate this wholesome root for the removal of all beings' fear of falling into the abyss; for the pacification of all beings' fear of [the continuity of] their continuum; for the turning back of all beings' fear of delusion; for the complete cutting off of all beings' fear of bondage; for the averting of all beings' fear of attacks upon their life; for the removal of all beings' fear of lacking requisites; for the pacification of all beings' fear of [losing their] livelihood; for the overcoming of all beings' fear of ill repute. I dedicate it for the pacification of all beings' fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>; for the removal of all beings' fear of timidity in assemblies; for the overcoming of all beings' fear of death; for the turning back of all beings' fear of lower realms; for illuminating all beings' dark, blind, and treacherous course so that they do not turn back. I dedicate it for the internal removal of all beings' fear of being placed among those of dissimilar disposition; for the cessation of all beings' fear of separation from the dear; for the removal of all beings' fear of association with the unpleasant; for the disjunction of all beings' fear of bodily affliction; for the liberation from all beings' fear of mental affliction; for the overcoming of all beings' suffering, despondency, and distress.'

body.text: saṃkṣepataḥ punar iyam an-uttarā pariṇāmanā yā + iyam ārya-bhadra-caryā-gāthāyāṃ | mañjuśirī yatha jānati śūraḥ so ca samantata bhadra tatha + eva | teṣu ahaṃ anuśikṣayamāṇo nāmayamī kuśalaṃ imu sarvaṃ ||
body.translated_text: In summary, this is the unsurpassed dedication, which is [expressed] in the verse of the noble <s>Bhadracaryā</s> (Prayer of Good Conduct): 'Just as <s>Mañjuśrī</s> knows — he the hero — and <s>Samantabhadra</s> likewise, training after them, I dedicate all this wholesomeness.'

body.text: sarva-triy-adhva gatebhi jinebhir yā pariṇāmana varṇita agrā | tāya ahaṃ kuśalaṃ imu sarvaṃ nāmayamī vara-bhadra-carīye | iti ||
body.translated_text: By that foremost dedication praised by all the <s>Jinas</s> gone in the three times, I dedicate all this wholesome [merit] to the excellent <s>Bhadracarī</s> (noble conduct).

body.text: iti śikṣā-samuccaye bhadra-caryā-vidhiḥ ṣoḍaśamaḥ paricchedaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the sixteenth chapter of the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>: the Method of the <s>Bhadracarī</s> (Noble Conduct).

children.translated_text: XVII. Benefits of Prostration and So Forth

body.text: vandanā-anuśaṃsāḥ saptadaśaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Benefits of prostration and so forth — the seventeenth chapter.

body.text: ukto vandanā-ādi-vidhiḥ | tena puṇya-vṛddhir bhavati + iti kuto gamyate ||
body.translated_text: The method of prostration and so forth has been stated. From what source is it known that through this the increase of merit occurs?

body.text: ārya-avalokana-sūtrāt | evaṃ hi tatra + uktaṃ | varjayaty a-kṣaṇāny aṣṭau yae ime deśitā mayā | kṣaṇaṃ ca + ārāgayaty ekaṃ buddha-utpādaṃ su-śobhanaṃ ||
body.translated_text: From the <s>Ārya-Avalokana-sūtra</s>. For thus it is said therein: 'He avoids the eight inopportune states that have been taught by me, and he obtains that one opportune state — the most glorious arising of a <s>Buddha</s>.'

body.text: varṇavān rūpa-saṃpanno lakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃ-kṛtaḥ sthāmnā balena ca + upeto na + asau kausīdyam ṛcchati
body.translated_text: 'Endowed with complexion, possessed of physical beauty, adorned with [auspicious] marks, endowed with vigor and strength — he does not fall into laziness.'

body.text: āḍhyo mahā-dhanaś ca + asau a-dhṛṣyaḥ puṇyavān api | ārāgya loka-pradyotaṃ sat-karoti punaḥ punaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'He is wealthy and of great riches, invincible and meritorious. Having obtained the Light of the World, he worships [him] again and again.'

body.text: śreṣṭhī-kuleṣu sphīteṣu sa āḍhyeṣu + upapadyate | bhaved dāna-patiḥ śūro mukta-tyāgo hy a-matsarī ||
body.translated_text: 'He is reborn in prosperous, wealthy merchant families. He becomes a heroic lord of generosity, free in giving, without avarice.'

body.text: rājā bhaved dhārmiko * asau catur-dvīpa-īśvaraḥ prabhuḥ | praśāsayen mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ samudra-giri-kuṇḍalām ||
body.translated_text: 'He becomes a righteous king, lord and sovereign of the four continents. He governs the entire earth, garlanded by oceans and mountains.'

body.text: maha-rddhikaś cakra-vartī sapta-ratna-samanvitaḥ | rājye pratiṣṭhito buddhān sat-karoti punaḥ punaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Of great supernatural power, a universal monarch endowed with the seven treasures, established in sovereignty, he worships the <s>Buddhas</s> again and again.'

body.text: ścyuta/ ca + asmād gataḥ svargaṃ prasanno jina-śāsane | śakro bhavati deva-indraḥ īśvaro maru-mūrddhani ||
body.translated_text: 'Fallen from here, he goes to heaven, devoted to the <s>Jina</s>'s teaching. He becomes <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>, sovereign at the summit of the <s>Marus</s>.'

body.text: na śakyaṃ bhāṣatā varṇaṃ kṣapayituṃ kalpa-koṭibhiḥ | ya stūpaṃ loka-nāthasya naraḥ kuryāt pradakṣiṇam ||
body.translated_text: 'It is not possible even in <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> to exhaust in speech the merit of a person who would circumambulate the <s>stūpa</s> of the Protector of the World.'

body.text: na jātu so * andhaḥ khañjo vā kalpānām api koṭibhiḥ | utpādya bodhi-cittaṃ yaḥ śāstu stūpaṃ hi vandate ||
body.translated_text: 'Never for even <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> is he blind or lame — he who, having generated <s>bodhicitta</s>, prostrates at the Teacher's <s>stūpa</s>.'

body.text: dṛḍha-vīryo dṛḍha-sthāmo vīraś ca dṛḍha-vikramaḥ | kauśalyaṃ gacchati kṣipraṃ kṛtvā stūpa-pradakṣiṇam ||
body.translated_text: 'Of firm vigor, firm strength, heroic and of firm prowess — he swiftly attains skillfulness, having circumambulated the <s>stūpa</s>.'

body.text: yo buddha-koṭi-niyuta-śata-sahasrān kalpān koṭī ca tuliya sat-karayā | yaś ca + iha kalpe caramaka ghora-kāle vandeya stūpaṃ bahutara tasya puṇyam ||
body.translated_text: 'He who for <s>kalpas</s> equal to <s>koṭi-niyuta</s> hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>koṭis</s> worships with equal devotion, and he who in this <s>kalpa</s>, in the final terrible age, would prostrate at a <s>stūpa</s> — greater is the merit of the latter.'

body.text: agro hi buddho * a-tuliya dakṣiṇīyo * agrāṃ caritvā cariya-viśeṣa prāptaḥ | tasya + iha pūjāṃ karia nara-riṣabhasya vipāka śreṣṭho bhavati a-tulya-rūpaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'For the <s>Buddha</s> is the supreme, the incomparable worthy recipient, who has attained excellence of conduct by practicing the supreme course. Having made worship of that Bull among Men here — the ripening becomes the finest, of incomparable form.'

body.text: itaś cyutvā manuṣyebhyas trāyastriṃśeṣu gacchati | vimānaṃ labhate tatra vicitraṃ ratanām ayam ||
body.translated_text: 'Having fallen from here among humans, he goes to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> [heaven]. There he obtains a palace, splendid, made of jewels.'

body.text: kūṭa-āgāraṃ svayaṃ datvā apsaro-gaṇa-sevitaḥ | mālāṃ stūpe saṃpradāya trāyastriṃśeṣu jāyate ||
body.translated_text: 'Having given a pinnacled mansion, attended by hosts of <s>apsarases</s> — by offering a garland at a <s>stūpa</s>, he is born in the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> [heaven].'

body.text: aṣṭa-aṅga-jala-saṃpūrṇāṃ suvarṇa-sikata-āstritām | vaiḍūrya-sphaṭikaiś ca + eva divyāṃ puṣkariṇīṃ labhet ||
body.translated_text: 'Filled with water possessing the eight qualities, strewn with golden sand, adorned with <s>vaiḍūrya</s> and crystal — he obtains a divine lotus pool.'

body.text: bhuktvā ca tāṃ ratiṃ divyāṃ āyuḥ saṃpūrya paṇḍitaḥ | cyutvā ca deva-lokāt sa manuṣyo bhavati bhogavān ||
body.translated_text: 'Having enjoyed that divine pleasure, having completed his lifespan, the wise one, falling from the world of the <s>devas</s>, becomes a wealthy human.'

body.text: jāti-koṭi-sahasraṇi śatāni niyutāni ca | sat-kṛtaḥ syāc ca sarvatra caitye mālāṃ pradāya ca ||
body.translated_text: 'For thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of births, and hundreds and <s>niyutas</s>, he is honored everywhere — by having offered a garland at a <s>caitya</s>.'

body.text: cakra-vartī ca rājā + asau śakraś ca bhavati + īśvaraḥ | brahmā ca brahma-lokasmin caitye mālāṃ pradāya ca ||
body.translated_text: 'He becomes a universal monarch, and <s>Śakra</s>, the sovereign lord, and <s>Brahmā</s> in the <s>Brahma</s>-world — by having offered a garland at a <s>caitya</s>.'

body.text: paṭṭa-pradāna datvā tu loka-nāthasya tāyinaḥ | sarve * asya + arthāḥ samṛdhyanti ye divyā ye ca mānuṣāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Having given an offering of silk to the Protector of the World, the Savior — all his purposes prosper, both divine and human.'

body.text: tyajed * dhīnān a-kuśalān na sa tatra + upapadyate | mālā-vihāraṃ kṛtvā ca loka-nāthasya dhātuṣu | a-bhedya-parivāreṇa rājā bhūyān maha-rddhikaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'He abandons the lower, unwholesome [realms]; he is not reborn there. And having made a garland-shrine for the relics of the Protector of the World — he becomes a king of great supernatural power, with an unbreakable retinue.'

body.text: priyaḥ sadayitaś ca + asau sat-kṛtaś ca praśaṃsitaḥ | davānām atha nāgānāṃ ye lokesmiṃś ca paṇḍitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'He is dear, beloved, honored, and praised — by <s>devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, and those who are wise in this world.'

body.text: yatra + asau jāyate vīraḥ puṇya-tejaḥ-su-dīpitaḥ | te kulāḥ sat-kṛtā bhonti rāṣṭrāṇi nagarāṇi ca ||
body.translated_text: 'Wherever that hero is born, blazing with the splendor of merit — those families become honored, as do the kingdoms and cities.'

body.text: yaḥ sarṣapāt sūkṣmataraṃ gṛhītvā dhūpeya dhūpaṃ bhagavati caityakeṣu | tasya + anuśaṃsān śṛṇuta prabhāṣato me prasanna-cittā jahiya khilāṃ malāṃś ca ||
body.translated_text: 'He who, taking [incense] finer than a mustard seed, would offer incense at the <s>caityas</s> of the Blessed One — listen with devoted minds to the benefits as I proclaim them; abandon obstinacy and defilements!'

body.text: sa puṇyavāṃś carati diśaḥ samantād ārogya-prāpto dṛḍha-matir a-pramattaḥ | vineti śokaṃ vicarati cārikāyāṃ priyo manāpo bhavati mahā-janasya ||
body.translated_text: 'That meritorious one travels in all directions, having attained health, firm in mind, heedful. He dispels sorrow, wanders on his journey — dear and agreeable to the great multitude.'

body.text: rājyaṃ ca labdhvā jina varu sat-karotī mahā-anubhāvo vidu cakra-vartī | suvarṇa-varṇo vicitra-lakṣaṇaiḥ sa mano-jña-gandhān labhi sarva-loke ||
body.translated_text: 'Having obtained sovereignty, he worships the supreme <s>Jina</s> — of great power, learned, a universal monarch. Of golden complexion, with varied marks — he obtains delightful fragrance in all the world.'

body.text: jāta-mātro labhate śreṣṭha-vastrān divya-viśiṣṭa-su-rucira-kauśikāṃś ca | bhotī sukha-su-kāyaḥ saṃveṣṭya-stūpaṃ nāthasya cīvaraiḥ | yaś cīvareṇa caityeṣu kuryāt pūjām a-tulāṃ nāyakānāṃ | tasya + iha bhotī a-sadṛśu ātma-bhāvo dvātriṃśatībhiḥ kavacita lakṣaṇebhiḥ | pāṇī-taleṣu su-ruciru mukta-hārāḥ prādur-bhavantī vividha an-anta-kalpāḥ | siṃha-latāḥ su-rucira-varṇa-sūtrā veṭhitva stūpaṃ bhagavata cīvarebhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Immediately upon birth, he obtains the finest garments — divine, excellent, beautiful silks. He becomes one of a happy, beautiful body — by having wrapped the <s>stūpa</s> of the Protector with robes. He who with a robe would make incomparable worship at the <s>caityas</s> of the Guides — for him there arises an incomparable body, armored with the thirty-two marks. Upon his palms, beautiful strings of pearls appear — various, endless, for [many] <s>kalpas</s>. Lion-tendrils, of beautiful color and thread — by wrapping the <s>stūpa</s> of the Blessed One with robes.'

body.text: datvā patākāṃ bhagavata cetikeṣū chandaṃ janitvā tatha siya buddha-loke | sa pūjanīyo bhavati mahā-janasya carantu śreṣṭho jina-cārikāye ||
body.translated_text: 'Having given a banner at the <s>caityas</s> of the Blessed One, having generated the aspiration, may he be in the <s>Buddha</s>-field. He becomes worthy of worship by the great multitude, practicing the supreme conduct of the <s>Jina</s>'s journey.'

body.text: suvarṇa-varṇo bhavati si ātma-bhāvo lābhī sa bhotī su-rucira-cīvarāṇāṃ | karpāsikānāṃ su-sahita kambalānāṃ du-kūlakānāṃ tatha vara-kauśakānāṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'His body becomes of golden complexion; he obtains beautiful robes — of cotton, well-made woolen [blankets], fine muslin, and excellent silk.'

body.text: dhvajaṃ daditvā hata-raji satva-sāre dhanaṃ prabhūtaṃ pratilabhi na cireṇa | prabhūta-koṣo bhavati an-anta-prajño paricāru tasya bhavaty a-dīna-cittaḥ | na citta-śūlaṃ janayati so parasya prasāda-cittaḥ sada a-pramattaḥ | na tasya agniḥ kramati viṣanna-śastraṃ udvīkṣaṇīyo bhavati mahā-janasya ||
body.translated_text: 'Having given a flag, with defilements destroyed, of firm essence — he obtains abundant wealth before long. He becomes one of abundant treasury and boundless wisdom; his retinue becomes undaunted in spirit. He does not generate mental pain in others — his mind is ever devoted, heedful. Fire, poison, and weapons do not approach him; he becomes worthy of admiration by the great multitude.'

body.text: adho upādāya ca vibhava-agru yāvat jāmbūnadaṃ tena bhavati buddha-kṣetraṃ | śakyaṃ kṣayetuṃ āyu-śriya eva-rūpā na buddha-stūpe dharayata eka dīpam ||
body.translated_text: 'From below upward to the foremost splendor, up to <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold — by that, there comes to be a <s>Buddha</s>-field. One may exhaust such lifespans and glory, but not [the merit of one who] maintains a single lamp at a <s>Buddha</s>-<s>stūpa</s>.'

body.text: na tasya kāyo bhavati a-varṇita-aṅgo dṛḍha-asu bhotī parigha-bhujo * a-chambhī | āloka-prāpto

children.text: vicarati sarva-loke daditva dīpaṃ bhagavata cetikeṣu ||
children.translated_text: he wanders through all the world — by having offered a lamp at the <s>caityas</s> of the Blessed One.'

body.translated_text: 'His body becomes one with unblemished limbs; he becomes firm in life-force, with arms [strong as] iron bars, fearless. Having attained illumination,

body.text: yadi buddha-kṣetrā niyuta-śatā sahasrā bhaveyu pūrṇā śikha-gata-sarṣapebhiḥ | śakyaṃ gaṇetuṃ tulayitu bhāṣituṃ vā na tathā-gateṣū dharayitu eka-dīpam ||
body.translated_text: 'If <s>niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddha</s>-fields were filled with mustard seeds piled to the tips — one might count, measure, or describe [those seeds], but not [the merit of one who] maintains a single lamp for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

body.text: alaṅ-karitvā su-rucira-darśanīyaṃ yo deti chatraṃ bhagavata cetikeṣu | tasya + iha bhoty a-sadṛśa ātma-bhāvo dvātriṃśatībhiḥ kavacita lakṣaṇebhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'He who gives a beautiful, splendid parasol at the <s>caityas</s> of the Blessed One — for him there arises an incomparable body, armored with the thirty-two marks.'

body.text: yebhir jinasya pratapata ātma-bhāvo rūpaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ yatha-r-iva

children.text: kāñcanasya | jāmbūnado vā su-rucira-darśanīyā abhikīrṇa ... kusumita lakṣaṇebhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: of gold — of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> [gold], beautiful and splendid to behold, covered and blossoming with [auspicious] marks.'

body.translated_text: 'Those by which the body of the <s>Jina</s> blazes — a form distinguished, as if

body.text: abhijña-prāpto bhavati mahā-yaśa-ākhyaḥ carati śreṣṭha-āvara-cārikāyāṃ | na bhoga-hānir bhavati kadā-cid asya devāna bhoti guru-kṛta pūjitaś ca ||
body.translated_text: 'Having attained the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), he becomes one renowned as greatly famous. He practices the supreme excellent conduct. Never does his enjoyment diminish; he becomes venerated and worshipped by the <s>devas</s>.'

body.text: na kāma-bhogau ramati kadā-ci dhīro viśuddha-śīlaḥ sa-kuśala-brahma-caryaḥ |samādayitvā van-upavane uṣitvā + abhiyukti-dhyāno bhavati viśeṣa-prāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Never does the resolute one delight in sensual pleasures — of purified moral conduct, practicing the wholesome <s>brahmacarya</s> (holy life). Having undertaken [the practice], dwelling in a forest hermitage — he becomes one devoted to meditation, having attained distinction.'

body.text: na jñāna-hānir bhavati kadā-cid asya na bodhi-cittaṃ vijahati so kathañ-cit | maitrī-vihārī bhavati a-dīna-citto datvā + iha chattraṃ bhagavata-cetikeṣu ||
body.translated_text: 'Never does his knowledge diminish; never does he in any way abandon <s>bodhicitta</s>. He becomes one who abides in <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), undaunted in spirit — by having given a parasol at the <s>caityas</s> of the Blessed One.'

body.text: vādyena pūjāṃ nara-vṛṣabhasya kṛtvā na śoka śalya-vaśa jātu bhoti | mano-jña-ghoṣo bhavati manuṣya-loke svara-aṅgu tasya + a-vi-kala viśuddha bhoti ||
body.translated_text: 'Having made worship with music to the Bull among Men, he never falls under the power of sorrow's dart. He becomes one of delightful voice in the human world; his vocal members become complete and pure.'

body.text: viśuddha-cakṣur bhavati sa saṃprajanyo viśuddha-śrotro bhavati udagra-cittaḥ | ghraṇa-indriyaṃ parama uttapta bhoti vāditva vādyaṃ bhagavata cetikeṣu ||
body.translated_text: 'He becomes one of pure eyesight, possessed of clear comprehension; he becomes one of pure hearing, with an exalted mind. His faculty of smell becomes supremely refined — by having played music at the <s>caityas</s> of the Blessed One.'

body.text: jihvā + asya bhoti su-rucira darśanīyā su-sūkṣma mṛdvī rucira mano-jña ghoṣā | raktā pravālā yatha-r-iva

children.translated_text: of the <s>devas</s> — it produces immeasurable <s>koṭis</s> of excellent vocal tones.'

body.translated_text: 'His tongue becomes beautiful and lovely to behold — most subtle, soft, beautiful, and of delightful voice; red like coral, as if

body.text: na jātu bhotī ura-gu a-jihvako vā na khañja-kubjo na + api ca nāmita-aṅgaḥ | viśiṣṭa bhotī su-rucira ātma-bhāvo vāditva vādyaṃ bhagavata cetikeṣu ||
body.translated_text: 'Never does he become a serpent or one without a tongue, nor lame, hunchbacked, nor one with crooked limbs. He becomes one of distinguished, beautiful body — by having played music at the <s>caityas</s> of the Blessed One.'

body.text: na jātu kaś-cij janaye prasādaṃ devo ca nāgo manu-ja mahā-ura-go vā | āśvāsa-prāpto vicarati sarva-loke vāditva vādyaṃ bhagavata cetikeṣu ||
body.translated_text: 'Never does anyone fail to generate devotion — whether <s>deva</s>, <s>Nāga</s>, human, or great serpent. Having attained comfort, he wanders through all the world — by having played music at the <s>caityas</s> of the Blessed One.'

body.text: kalpāna koṭī-niyuta-śatā sahasraṃ viśiṣṭa-kāyo bhavati a-nindita-aṅgaḥ | prāsādiko * asau kavacita lakṣaṇebhiḥ saṃśodhya stūpaṃ bhagavata nirvṛtasya ||
body.translated_text: 'For hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, he becomes one of distinguished body with unblemished limbs — gracious, armored with [auspicious] marks — by having cleaned the <s>stūpa</s> of the Blessed One who has attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>.'

body.text: vimāna-śreṣṭhaṃ labhati mano-jña-gandhaṃ divyaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ su-rucira-candanasya | na jātu tṛṣṇāṃ janayati so kadā-cit saṃśodhya stūpaṃ bhagavata nirvṛtasya ||
body.translated_text: 'He obtains a supreme palace of delightful fragrance, divine, distinguished, of beautiful sandalwood. Never does he generate craving at any time — by having cleaned the <s>stūpa</s> of the Blessed One who has attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>.'

body.text: pralopa-kāle jina-vara-śāsanasmin na jātu bhotī upagata jambu-dvīpe | svarge sa bhoti pratiṣṭhita tasmi kāle gandha-anulepaṃ dadiya jinasya stūpe ||
body.translated_text: 'In the time of decline of the supreme <s>Jina</s>'s teaching, he is never born in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> [during that time]. He abides in heaven at that time — by having offered fragrant ointment at the <s>Jina</s>'s <s>stūpa</s>.'

body.text: dur-gandhi-kāmān a-śuci-jugupsanīyān varjeti nityaṃ pratiṣṭhita śīla-skandhe | carī sa nityam imu vara brahma-caryaṃ gandha-anulepaṃ kariya jinasya stūpe ||
body.translated_text: 'He always avoids foul-smelling, impure, and loathsome [things], established in the aggregate of moral conduct. He constantly practices this excellent holy life — by having applied fragrant ointment at the <s>Jina</s>'s <s>stūpa</s>.'

body.text: itaś cyuto * asau maru-pati svarga-loke arthaṃ sahasrā tulayati na + u cireṇa | karoti ca + arthaṃ su-vipula-devatānāṃ gandha-anulepaṃ kariya jinasya stūpe ||
body.translated_text: 'Fallen from here, [he becomes] lord of the <s>Marus</s> in the heavenly world; before long he measures out thousands of riches. He performs the purposes of the abundant <s>devas</s> — by having applied fragrant ointment at the <s>Jina</s>'s <s>stūpa</s>.'

body.text: viśiṣṭa-vākyo bhavati mano-jña-ghoṣaḥ priyo manāpo bahu-jana-sat-kṛtaś ca | sukhaṃ ca tasya bhavati sadā prasannaṃ gandha-anulepaṃ kariya jinasya stūpe ||
body.translated_text: 'He becomes one of distinguished speech, of delightful voice — dear, agreeable, and honored by the multitude. His happiness is always serene — by having applied fragrant ointment at the <s>Jina</s>'s <s>stūpa</s>.'

body.text: apāya-bhūmiṃ ... vijahāty a-śeṣāṃ āsannako bhavati tathā-gatānāṃ | prasāda-labdhaḥ sada sukhi premaṇīyo gandha-anulepaṃ kariya jinasya stūpe ||
body.translated_text: 'He leaves behind the realm of lower destinies entirely; he becomes one near to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Having obtained devotion, always happy and endearing — by having applied fragrant ointment at the <s>Jina</s>'s <s>stūpa</s>.'

body.text: so * a-kṣaṇaṃ vai vijahāti sarvaṃ aṣṭa kṣaṇāś ca + asya viśiṣṭa bhonti | buddhāna pūjām a-tuliya so karoti choritva jālaṃ bhagavata cetikeṣu ||
body.translated_text: 'He avoids every inopportune state, and his eight [favorable] opportunities become distinguished. He makes incomparable worship of the <s>Buddhas</s> — by having spread a net [canopy] at the <s>caityas</s> of the Blessed One.'

body.text: śūraś ca bhoti dṛḍha-matir a-pramatto na kāma-bhoge * abhiratiṃ janeti | naiṣkramya-prāptau ca a-dīna-cittaḥ choritva jālaṃ bhagavata cetikeṣu ||
body.translated_text: 'He becomes heroic, firm-minded, and heedful; he does not generate delight in sensual pleasures. Undaunted in spirit in the attainment of renunciation — by having spread a net [canopy] at the <s>caityas</s> of the Blessed One.'

body.text: na bodhi-cittaṃ pramuṣyati tasya jātu a-khaṇḍa-śīlo * asti su-saṃvṛtaś ca | dharmaṃ vi-rāgaṃ labhate viśuddhaṃ upanīya jālaṃ bhagavata cetikeṣu ||
body.translated_text: 'Never is his <s>bodhicitta</s> stolen away; he is of unbroken morality and well-restrained. He obtains the pure <s>Dharma</s> of dispassion — by having offered a net [canopy] at the <s>caityas</s> of the Blessed One.'

body.text: dur-vācatāṃ vijahati sarva-kālaṃ prajñā-a-bhāvaṃ ca jahāty a-śeṣam |viśāla-prajño viharati cārikāyāṃ upanīya jālaṃ bhagavata cetikeṣu ||
body.translated_text: 'He abandons harsh speech for all time, and he leaves behind the absence of wisdom entirely. Of vast wisdom, he abides on his journey — by having offered a net [canopy] at the <s>caityas</s> of the Blessed One.'

body.text: lābhī ca bhotī śuci-bhojanānāṃ vastrān viśiṣṭān labhate suvarṇān | sparśa-abhyupetān ruci-darśanīyān upanīya jālaṃ jina-cetikebhyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'He obtains pure foods and distinguished garments, of golden [color], endowed with touch, beautiful to behold — by having offered a net [canopy] at the <s>Jina</s>'s <s>caityas</s>.'

body.text: abhyutkṣipitvā jina-cetikebhyaḥ nir-mālya-śuṣkaṃ pramudita-vega-jātaḥ | vrajeta kāmān duḥkha-da-vaira-ghorān ārāgayed daśa-bala-sa-artha-vāhān ||
body.translated_text: Having tossed out the withered and discarded offerings from the <s>Jina</s>-shrines, born of a surge of joy, he would overcome the terrible enmity of the suffering-giving <s>kāmas</s> (sensual pleasures) and would please the Caravan-leaders of the Ten Powers.

body.text: prāsādiko bhoti viśuddha-kāyaḥ udvīkṣaṇīyo bahu-jana-pūjanīyaḥ | na tasya rājā + api praduṣṭa-cittaḥ yo jīrṇa-puṣpān apaneya caitye ||
body.translated_text: He becomes gracious, of purified body, worthy of being looked upon, to be honored by multitudes of people. Not even a king becomes hostile-minded toward one who removes withered flowers from a shrine.

body.text: ku-mārga sarvaṃ pithita apāya-bhūmiḥ sa śīla-skandhe sthita bodhi-satvaḥ | avatārayitvā jina-cetikebhyaḥ puṣpaṃ ca prāg anya-naraiḥ pradattaṃ ||
body.translated_text: All evil paths are blocked, the lower realms [closed off] — that <s>bodhisattva</s>, established in the aggregate of moral conduct, having brought down from the <s>Jina</s>-shrines the flowers previously offered by other people.

body.text: śokāṃś ca doṣān vijahāty a-matto rogān a-śeṣān vijahāty an-ekān | āśvāsa-prāptaś ca an-anta-kalpān yo jīrṇa-puṣpān apaneti caitye ||
body.translated_text: He abandons sorrows and faults, free from intoxication; he abandons all manner of diseases without remainder. And he attains relief for endless <s>kalpas</s> — one who removes withered flowers from a shrine.

body.text: buddhaś ca bhoty a-sadṛśa-dakṣiṇīyo * a-tulya-prāpto nara-maru-pūjanīyaḥ | alaṃ-kṛto bhavati viśuddha-kāyaḥ yo jīrṇa-puṣpān apaneti caitye ||
body.translated_text: He becomes a <s>Buddha</s>, an incomparable field of offerings, attaining the unequalled, to be worshipped by humans and gods. He becomes adorned, of purified body — one who removes withered flowers from a shrine.

body.text: dadyāc ca yaḥ su-rucira-divya puṣpaṃ māndāravān apy atha pāṭalaṃ vā | nir-mālyakaṃ yo * apanayeta caitye vipāka śreṣṭho * asya bhaved a-tulyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Were someone to give beautiful, divine flowers — <s>māndārava</s> blossoms or <s>pāṭala</s> flowers — and another were to remove the withered offerings from a shrine, the fruit of the latter would be superior and incomparable.

body.text: yaḥ prāñjaliḥ praṇamati nātha-stūpaṃ chandaṃ janitvā ca sa-buddha-loke | so bhoti loke guru-kṛtu sat-kṛtaś ca prāsādiko bhavati su-darśanīyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: One who, with palms joined, bows to the <s>stūpa</s> of the Protector, having generated aspiration for the <s>Buddha</s>-realm — he becomes in the world honored and revered by the teacher, gracious and fair to behold.

body.text: tasya + iha rājyaṃ nipatati sarva-loko deva-asurā nāga-manuṣyakāś ca | sarvāḥ sahasrāḥ kusumita loka-dhātuḥ praśāsti rājño vaśa īśvarāṃś ca ||
body.translated_text: Sovereignty over this world falls to him — gods, <s>asuras</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, and humans. All the thousands of blossoming world-realms — he rules over kings and lords.

body.text: ye tasya rājye sthita bhonti satvāḥ sthāpeya sarvān a-kaluṣa-buddha-jñāne | apāya-bhūmyas tyaktā bhavanti karoti ca + eṣāṃ parama-su-śreṣṭham artham ||
body.translated_text: Whatever beings dwell in his kingdom, he would establish them all in the stainless <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. The lower realms are abandoned [for them], and he accomplishes for them the supreme, most excellent purpose.

body.text: paricāro * asya bhavati mano-jña-ghoṣaḥ puṇyair upetaḥ smṛti-mati-pūjanīyaḥ | āśvāsa-prāpto vicarati jīva-loke sadā + abhiprāyaṃ janayati śreṣṭha-prītiṃ ||
body.translated_text: His retinue is of pleasing voice, endowed with merit, to be honored for mindfulness and wisdom. Having attained relief, he moves about in the world of the living, always generating aspiration and the highest joy.

body.text: paricāra bhoty asya svara-aṅga śuddhaḥ jñāyeta satvair madhura-praśānta-vākyo | na tasya kaś-cij janayati ca + īśvaratvaṃ vilokanīyo bhavati mahā-janasya | dāna-pramodaṃ priyatā-artha-caryāṃ samāna-arthatāṃ janayati mahā-janasya | ākruṣṭaḥ san na + ājanayeta roṣaṃ yaḥ prāñjaliḥ praṇamati buddha-stūpaṃ ||
body.translated_text: His retinue is of pure vocal qualities; he is known by beings as one of sweet and tranquil speech. No one generates hostility toward him — he becomes one to be looked upon by the multitudes. He generates delight in giving, conduct that serves the good of others, and common purpose among the multitudes. When insulted, he does not generate anger — one who with joined palms bows to the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>stūpa</s>.

body.text: deva-indra bhoty upagata-svarga-loke manuṣyako bhavati narasya rājā | na pārihāṇir bhavati kadā-cid asya yo * añjalībhir namati + iha stūpaṃ ||
body.translated_text: He becomes <s>Indra</s> among the gods, ascending to the heavenly world; among humans he becomes a king of men. There is never any decline for one who with joined palms bows here to the <s>stūpa</s>.

body.text: na + asāv apāye prapateta jātu hīnāṃś ca varjeta sa kāma loke | āḍhyo dhanī bhoti prabhūta-koṣo yo * añjalībhir namati buddha-stūpam ||
body.translated_text: He never falls into the lower realms, and he avoids the inferior among the sense-desire realms. He becomes wealthy, rich, with abundant treasure — one who with joined palms bows to the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>stūpa</s>.

body.text: sūtra-anta-caryā na kadā-cid asya na + a-sthāna-kopaṃ kurute nṛ-loke | satvāś ca tṛptā muditā + asya bhonti yaḥ saṃpramuñcī guṇavati eka-vācaṃ ||
body.translated_text: The <s>sūtra</s>-conduct never [fails] for him; he does not generate misplaced anger in the human world. And beings are satisfied and delighted with him — one who utters a single word in praise of one who is endowed with qualities.

body.text: yaḥ puṣpa-muṣṭiṃ gṛhītvā + udagra-cittaḥ prasādato * avakirati loka-nāthe | sa puṇyavān bhavati manuṣya-loke rākṣe ca sthitvā jina sat-karoti ||
body.translated_text: One who, having grasped a handful of flowers with exalted mind, scatters them out of faith upon the Lord of the World — he becomes meritorious in the human world, and standing in the realm of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, he honors the <s>Jina</s>.

body.text: śokā na doṣāḥ khila-mala na + asya bhonti a-tulyatā-āptaś ca su-saṃsthita-aṅgaḥ | ālokanīyaś ca mahā-janasya vrajeta kāmāna bhaya-kara-vaira-ghorān | iti ||
body.translated_text: He has no sorrows, no faults, no rigidity or stain; having attained the unequalled, with well-composed limbs, worthy of being looked upon by the multitudes, he would overcome the terrible enmity of fear-producing <s>kāmas</s>. Thus —

body.text: ārya-mahā-karuṇā-puṇḍarīka-sūtre * apy uktaṃ |tiṣṭhatu tāvad ānanda yo māṃ saṃmukhaṃ sat-kuryāt | tiṣṭhatu me śarīrasya pūjā sarṣapa-phala-ma-treṣu dhātuṣu | tiṣṭhatu mām uddiśya kṛteṣu stūpeṣu sat-kāraḥ | ye ke-cid ānanda buddham ālambya + antaśa eka-puṣpam apy ākāśe kṣepsyanti | tasya puṇya-skandhasya yo vipākaḥ saced yāvān an-ādiḥ saṃsāro yasya pūrvā koṭir na prajñāyate | tāvataḥ kalpān saṃsaratāṃ teṣāṃ śakratvaṃ brahmatvaṃ cakra-vartitvaṃ | na śakyas tat-paryanto * adhigantum | tiṣṭhatu buddha-ālambatā + antaśa ākāśe * apy eka-puṣpa-nikṣepaḥ | saced antaśaḥ svapna-antara-gatā api satvā buddham ālambya + ākāśe eka-puṣpam api kṣepsyanti tad apy ahaṃ kuśala-mūlaṃ nirvāṇa-paryavasānaṃ vadāmi + iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Mahākaruṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra</s> also it is said: 'Set aside, O <s>Ānanda</s>, one who would honor me face to face. Set aside worship of my body. Set aside honor to <s>stūpas</s> made [to enshrine] relics even as small as a mustard seed. Whoever, O <s>Ānanda</s>, relying on the <s>Buddha</s>, will cast even a single flower into the sky — the fruit of that aggregate of merit, if the beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s> whose prior limit is not discerned [were to be measured against it]: for as many <s>kalpas</s> as they would transmigrate, sovereignty as <s>Śakra</s>, sovereignty as <s>Brahmā</s>, sovereignty as a <s>cakravartin</s> — the end of that [merit] cannot be reached. Set aside relying on the <s>Buddha</s> and casting even a single flower into the sky — if beings who have entered even into a dream, relying on the <s>Buddha</s>, will cast even a single flower into the sky, even that I declare to be a wholesome root culminating in <s>nirvāṇa</s>.'

body.text: uktaṃ ca + ārya-bṛhatsāgara-nāga-rāja-paripṛcchāyāṃ | aṣṭābhir bhuja-ga-adhipate dharmaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhi-satvāḥ satata-samitaṃ buddha-samavadhānaṃ pratilabhante | katamair aṣṭābhiḥ | buddha-bimba-darśana-satva-samādāpanatayā | tathā-gatasya + upasthāna-karaṇatayā | tathā-gatasya + abhīkṣṇaṃ varṇa-bhāṣaṇatayā | tathā-gata-pratimā-karaṇatayā | tathā-gata-darśana-sarva-satva-samādāpanatayā | yatra ca buddha-kṣetre tathā-gata-śravaṃ śṛṇvanti tatra praṇidhānam utpādayanti | na ca + avalīna-saṃtatayo bhavanti | udāra-saṃtatikāś ca buddha-jñānam abhilaṣantae iti ||
body.translated_text: And it is said in the <s>Ārya-Bṛhatsāgaranāgarājaparipṛcchā</s>: 'Endowed with eight <s>dharmas</s>, O Lord of Serpents, <s>bodhisattvas</s> constantly and continually obtain the presence of the <s>Buddha</s>. Which eight? Through inspiring beings to behold <s>Buddha</s>-images; through rendering service to the <s>Tathāgata</s>; through frequently speaking the praises of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; through making images of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; through inspiring all beings to behold the <s>Tathāgata</s>; and in whatever <s>Buddha</s>-field they hear the fame of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, they generate aspiration [to be born] there; and they are not of shrunken resolve; and they are of lofty resolve, aspiring to <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge.'

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ puṇya-vṛddhy-arthino buddha-samavadhānena prayojana-bhūtaṃ | yasya guṇa-paryantam a-sarva-jño na + adhigacchet ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, what is the purpose accomplished by the presence of the <s>Buddha</s> for one who desires the increase of merit — whose limit of qualities a non-omniscient one could not reach?

body.text: yathā + ārya-gaṇḍa-vyūhe saṃvarṇitaṃ | su-dur-labho buddha-śabdaḥ kalpa-koṭi-śatair api | kiṃ punar darśanaṃ sarva-kāṅkṣā-cchedanam uttamam ||
body.translated_text: As celebrated in the <s>Ārya-Gaṇḍavyūha</s>: 'Rare is the word "<s>Buddha</s>" even in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> — how much rarer then is seeing [the <s>Buddha</s>], the supreme cutting-off of all doubts!'

body.text: su-dṛṣṭo loka-pradyotaḥ sarva-dharma-gatiṃ gataḥ | puṇya-tīrthaṃ trailokasya sarva-satva-viśodhanam ||
body.translated_text: 'Well-seen is the Light of the World, who has gone to the course of all <s>dharmas</s> — the sacred ford of merit for the three worlds, the purification of all beings.'

body.text: mahat puṇyam ayaṃ kṣetraṃ muditaṃ jñāna-maṇḍalaṃ | bhāsayaty abhitaṃ lokaṃ puṇya-skandha-vivarddhanam ||
body.translated_text: 'Great is the merit — this field, a delightful sphere of knowledge; it illuminates the world all around, increasing the aggregate of merit.'

body.text: chedano duṣkha-jālasya jñāna-skandha-viśodhanaḥ | na dur-gati-bhayaṃ teṣāṃ yair iha + ārāgito jinaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'The cutter of the net of suffering, the purifier of the aggregate of knowledge — there is no fear of the lower realms for those by whom the <s>Jina</s> has been pleased here.'

body.text: vipulaṃ jāyate cittaṃ paśyatāṃ dvi-pada-uttamaṃ | prajñā-balam a-saṃkhyeyaṃ jāyate ca prabhāsvaraṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'A vast mind arises in those who behold the Supreme among Bipeds; the power of wisdom, incalculable, arises, and it becomes luminous.'

body.text: punar atra + eva + āha | arthāya sarva-satvānām utpadyante tathā-gatāḥ | mahā-kāruṇikā vīrā dharma-cakra-pravartakāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Again, in this very [text] it says: 'For the benefit of all beings, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise — the Greatly Compassionate Heroes, the Turners of the Wheel of <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: pratikartuṃ kathaṃ śakyaṃ buddhānāṃ sarve-dehibhiḥ | satva-artheṣv abhiyuktānāṃ kalpa-koṭi-śatair api ||
body.translated_text: 'How could all embodied beings possibly repay the <s>Buddhas</s>, who are devoted to the welfare of beings, even in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>?'

body.text: kalpa-koṭiṃ varaṃ paktuṃ try-apāye bhṛśa-dāruṇe | na tv eva + a-darśanaṃ śāstuḥ sarva-sarga-nivartinaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Better to be cooked for <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> in the three lower realms, most terrible, than to not see the Teacher who turns away all [re]births.'

body.text: yāvantaḥ sarva-lokasminn apāya-gatayaḥ pṛthak | varaṃ tatra ciraṃ vāso buddhānām a-śrutir na ca ||
body.translated_text: 'However many the various courses of the lower realms in all the world — better to dwell there long than not to hear of the <s>Buddhas</s>.'

body.text: kiṃ kāraṇam apāyeṣu nivāsaś ciram iṣyate | yat-kāraṇaṃ jina-indrasya darśanaṃ jñāna-vardhanam ||
body.translated_text: 'For what reason is a long stay in the lower realms preferred? Because seeing the Lord of <s>Jinas</s> increases knowledge.'

body.text: chidyante sarva-duṣkhāṇi dṛṣṭvā loka-īśvaraṃ jinaṃ | saṃbhavaty avatāraś ca jñāne saṃbuddha-go-care ||
body.translated_text: 'All sufferings are cut by seeing the <s>Jina</s>, the Lord of the World; and there arises entry into the knowledge that is the domain of the Fully Awakened One.'

body.text: kṣapayaty āvṛtīḥ sarvā dṛṣṭvā buddhaṃ nara-uttamam | vardhayaty a-mitaṃ puṇyaṃ yena bodhir avāpyatae | iti ||
body.translated_text: 'One destroys all obscurations by seeing the <s>Buddha</s>, the Supreme among Men; one increases immeasurable merit, by which awakening is attained.' Thus —

body.text: tad evam asti puṇya-vṛddhau buddha-samavadhānena prayojanaṃ |api ca pratimā-mātra-darśanam api tāvad a-parimita-phalaṃ tathā-gatānāṃ | kiṃ punaḥ sva-rūpeṇa ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, there is indeed this purpose accomplished by the presence of the <s>Buddha</s> for the increase of merit. Moreover, even the mere seeing of an image of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> has immeasurable fruit — how much more so [seeing them] in their own form!

body.text: uktaṃ hy ārya-śraddhā-bala-ādhāna-avatāra-mudrā-sūtre | yaḥ kaś-cin mañjuśrīḥ kula-putraḥ kula-duhitā vā sarva-loka-dhātu-raja-upamānāṃ praty-eka-buddhānāṃ dine dine śata-rasam āhāraṃ dadyāt divyāni ca vastrāṇi | evaṃ dadad gaṅgā-nadī-vālukā-upamān kalpān dadyāt | yaś ca + anyo mañjuśrīḥ kula-putraḥ kula-duhitā vā citra-karma-likhitaṃ vā pustaka-karma-kṛtaṃ vā buddhaṃ paśyed | ayaṃ tato * a-saṃkhyeyataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati | kaḥ punar vādo yo * añjali-pragrahaṃ vā kuryāt puṣpaṃ vā dadyāt dhūpaṃ vā gandhaṃ vā dīpaṃ vā dadyād | ayam eva tato * a-saṃkhyeyataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati + iti ||
body.translated_text: For it is said in the <s>Ārya-Śraddhābalādhānāvatāramudrā Sūtra</s>: 'If, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, some son or daughter of good family were to give daily food of a hundred flavors and divine garments to <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> as numerous as the particles of dust in all world-realms, and were to give thus for <s>kalpas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River — and if another son or daughter of good family, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, were to see a <s>Buddha</s> painted in a picture or fashioned from a manuscript — this latter generates immeasurably more merit than the former. How much more so one who would make a gesture of joined palms, or offer a flower, or incense, or perfume, or a lamp — this very one generates immeasurably more merit than the former.'

body.text: ārya-bodhi-satva-piṭake * api puṇya-vṛddhy-upāya uktaḥ | yas tathā-gata-caityaṃ śodhayati sa catasro * agrāḥ praṇidhāna-viśuddhīr anuprāpnoti | katamāś catasraḥ | agrāṃ rūpa-praṇidhāna-viśuddhiṃ | agrāṃ dṛḍha-samādāna-praṇidhāna-viśuddhiṃ | agrāṃ tathā-gata-darśana-praṇidhāna-viśuddhiṃ |agrāṃ lakṣaṇa-saṃpat-praṇidhāna-viśuddhim iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Bodhisattvapiṭaka</s> also a means for the increase of merit is stated: 'One who cleans a <s>Tathāgata</s>-shrine attains four supreme purifications of aspiration. Which four? The supreme purification of the aspiration for form; the supreme purification of the aspiration for firm undertaking; the supreme purification of the aspiration for seeing the <s>Tathāgata</s>; the supreme purification of the aspiration for the perfection of the [major] marks.'

body.text: punar atra + eva + ākhyātaṃ | tathā-gata-caityeṣu puṣpa-avaropaṇaṃ gandha-anulepanaṃ kṛtvā + aṣṭāv a-vi-kalatā anuprāpnoti | katamā aṣṭau | na rūpa-vi-kalo bhavati | na bhoga-vi-kalaḥ | na parivāra-vi-kalaḥ | na śīla-vi-kalaḥ | na samādhi-vi-kalaḥ | na śruta-vi-kalo na prajñā-vi-kalo na praṇidhāna-vi-kala iti ||
body.translated_text: Again, in this very [text] it is declared: 'By placing flowers and applying ointments at <s>Tathāgata</s>-shrines, one attains eight non-deficiencies. Which eight? One is not deficient in form; not deficient in enjoyments; not deficient in retinue; not deficient in moral conduct; not deficient in <s>samādhi</s> (concentration); not deficient in learning; not deficient in wisdom; not deficient in aspiration.'
