body.text: uktaṃ ca + ārya-ratna-rāśi-sūtre | ye tri-bhava-paryāpannāḥ satvās te sarve praty-ekaṃ tathā-gata-stūpān kārayeyur evaṃ-rūpān uccaistvena | tad yathā sumeruḥ parvata-rājaḥ | tāṃś ca gaṅgā-nadī-vālikā-samān kalpān praty-ekaṃ sarva-sat-kāraiḥ sat-kuryuḥ | yaś ca bodhi-satvo * a-virahita-sarva-jñatā-cittena + eka-puṣpam apy āropayet | ayaṃ tasmāt pūrvakāt puṇya-skandhād bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet ||
body.translated_text: And it is said in the <s>Ārya-Ratnarāśi Sūtra</s>: 'If all beings in the three realms of existence were each to build <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>stūpas</s> of such a form and height as <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, and were each to honor them with every kind of worship for <s>kalpas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River — and if a <s>bodhisattva</s>, with a mind inseparable from omniscience, were to place even a single flower [upon a shrine] — this latter would generate far more merit than that former aggregate of merit.'

body.text: atra + eva + uktaṃ | ye khalu punas tri-sāhasra-mahā-sāhasre loka-dhātau satvās te sarve mahā-yāna-saṃprasthitā bhaveyuḥ | sarve ca cakra-varti-rājya-samanvāgatā bhaveyur eka-ekaś ca rājā cakra-vartī mahā-samudra-pramāṇa-dīpa-sthālīṃ kṛtvā | sumeru-mātrāṃ vartīm ādīpya praty-ekam evaṃ-rūpāṃ dīpa-pūjāṃ tathā-gata-caityeṣu pravartayet | yaś ca + abhiniṣkrānta-gṛha-āvāso bodhi-satvas taila-prakṣiptāṃ vartīṃ kṛtvā + ādīpya tathā-gata-caitye dhārayet | asyās taila-prakṣiptāyā varter etat pūrvakaṃ pradīpa-dānaṃ śatatamīm api kalāṃ na + upaiti | yāvad upaniṣadam api na kṣamatae iti | peyālaṃ ||
body.translated_text: In this very [sūtra] it is said: 'If all beings in the trichiliocosm were set out in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, and all were endowed with <s>cakravartin</s>-sovereignty, and each <s>cakravartin</s> king were to make a lamp-vessel the size of the great ocean with a wick the size of <s>Sumeru</s>, and were to light it and offer such a lamp-offering at <s>Tathāgata</s>-shrines — and if a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has gone forth from the household life were to make a wick dipped in oil and light it and maintain it at a <s>Tathāgata</s>-shrine — the former gift of lamps would not approach even the hundredth part of this wick dipped in oil, nay, it would not bear even a fraction.' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: ye ca khalu punas te rājānaś cakra-vartino buddha-pramukhaṃ bhikṣu-saṃghaṃ sarva-sukha-upadhānaiḥ sat-kuryuḥ yaś ca + abhiniṣkrānta-gṛha-āvāso bodhi-satvaḥ piṇḍa-pātraṃ caritvā pātra-paryāpannaṃ pareṣāṃ saṃvibhajya paribhuñjīta | idaṃ tato bahutaraṃ ca mahā-arghataraṃ ca | yac ca te rājānaś cakra-vartinaḥ sumeru-mātraṃ cīvara-rāśiṃ buddha-pramukhāya bhikṣu-saṃghāya dadyuḥ | yac ca + abhiniṣkrānta-gṛha-āvāso bodhi-satvas tri-cīvaraṃ bahir-dhā mahā-yāna-saṃprasthitāya buddha-pramukhāya bhikṣu-saṃghāya vā tathā-gata-caitye vā dadyād | idaṃ bhikṣoś cīvara-dānam etat pūrvaka-cīvara-rāśim abhibhavati | yac ca te rājānaḥ praty-ekaṃ sarvaṃ jambū-dvīpaṃ puṣpa-saṃstṛtaṃ kṛtvā tathā-gata-caitye niryātayet | yac ca + abhiniṣkrānta-gṛha-āvāso bodhi-satvaḥ antaśa eka-puṣpam api tathā-gata-caitye āropayet | asya dānasya + etat pūrvakaṃ dānaṃ śatatamīm api kalāṃ na + upaiti | yāvad upaniṣadam api na + upaiti + iti ||
body.translated_text: And indeed, even if those <s>Cakravartin</s> kings were to honor the <s>Bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s> with all provisions of comfort — yet if a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has gone forth from the household life, having gone on his alms-round, were to share with others the [food] contained in his bowl and partake of it — this is far more abundant and of far greater value. And even if those <s>Cakravartin</s> kings were to give a heap of robes the size of <s>Mount Sumeru</s> to the <s>Bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s> — yet if a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has gone forth from the household life were to give his three robes externally to the <s>Bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s>, who have set out in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, or to a <s>Tathāgata</s>-shrine — this gift of robes by a monk surpasses that former heap of robes. And even if those kings, each having strewn the entire <s>Jambudvīpa</s> with flowers, were to offer them to a <s>Tathāgata</s>-shrine — yet if a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has gone forth from the household life were to place even a single flower upon a <s>Tathāgata</s>-shrine — that former gift does not equal even a hundredth part of this gift, nor even a fraction thereof.

body.text: ārya-anupūrva-samudgata-parivarte * api deśitaṃ | catura imān bhadra-anuśaṃsān paśyan bodhi-satvas tathā-gata-pūjāyām utsuko bhavati | katamāṃś caturaḥ | agraś ca me dakṣiṇīyaḥ pūjito bhaviṣyati māṃ ca dṛṣṭvā + anye * api tathā śikṣiṣyanti | tathā-gataṃ ca pūjayitvā bodhi-cittaṃ dṛḍhaṃ bhaviṣyati | dvātriṃśatāṃ ca mahā-puruṣa-lakṣaṇānāṃ saṃmukha-darśanena kuśala-mūlam upacitaṃ bhaviṣyati | imāś catvāraḥ iti ||
body.translated_text: It is also taught in the noble <s>Anupūrvasamudgataparivarta</s>: 'Seeing these four excellent benefits, the <s>bodhisattva</s> becomes zealous in worshipping the <s>Tathāgata</s>. What are the four? "The foremost field of merit will have been honored by me, and others, seeing me, will also train likewise. Having worshipped the <s>Tathāgata</s>, my <s>bodhicitta</s> will become firm. And by the direct vision of the thirty-two marks of a great person (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>), my wholesome roots will be augmented." These are the four.'

body.text: idaṃ ca nir-uttaraṃ tathā-gata-pūjā-upasthānaṃ |yathā + udāhṛtam ārya-sāgaramati-paripṛcchā-sūtre | trīṇi + imāni sāgaramate tathā-gatasya nir-uttarāṇi pūjā-upasthānāni | katamāni trīṇi | yac ca bodhi-cittam utpādayati | yac ca sad-dharmaṃ parigṛhṇāti | yac ca satveṣu mahā-karuṇā-cittam utpādayati + iti ||
body.translated_text: And this is the unsurpassed worship and attendance upon the <s>Tathāgata</s>. As it is illustrated in the noble <s>Sāgaramatiparipṛcchāsūtra</s>: 'There are three forms of unsurpassed worship and attendance upon the <s>Tathāgata</s>, O <s>Sāgaramati</s>. What are the three? Generating <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening); upholding the true <s>Dharma</s>; and generating the mind of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) toward beings.'

body.text: nirdiṣṭam apy ārya-ratna-meghe | daśabhiḥ kula-putra dharmaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhi-satvā an-anuliptā garbha-malena jāyante | katamair daśabhiḥ | yad uta | tathā-gata-pratimā-karaṇatayā | jīrṇa-caitya-saṃskaraṇatayā | tathā-gata-caityeṣu gandha-vilepana-anupradānena | tathā-gata-pratimāsu gandha-udaka-snāna-anupradānena | tathā-gata-caityeṣu saṃmārjana-upalepana-anupradānena | mātā-pitṝṇāṃ kāya-paricaryā-ācaraṇena ācārya-upādhyāyānāṃ kāya-paricaryā-ācaraṇena | sa-brahma-cāriṇāṃ kāya-paricaryā-ācaraṇena | tac ca nir-āmiṣeṇa cittena na sa-āmiṣeṇa | tac ca kuśalam evaṃ pariṇāmayanti | anena kuśala-mūlena sarva-satvā nir-upaliptā garbha-malena jāyantām iti | tac ca tīvreṇa + āśayena cintayanti | ebhiḥ kula-putra daśabhir dharmair iti ||
body.translated_text: It is also taught in the noble <s>Ratnamegha</s>: '<s>Bodhisattvas</s> endowed with ten <s>dharmas</s>, O son of good family, are born unstained by the impurity of the womb. What are the ten? Namely: by making images of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; by restoring dilapidated shrines; by offering fragrant ointments at <s>Tathāgata</s>-shrines; by offering baths of fragrant water to images of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; by offering sweeping and plastering at <s>Tathāgata</s>-shrines; by performing bodily service to one's mother and father; by performing bodily service to one's teachers and preceptors; by performing bodily service to fellow practitioners of the holy life; and [doing] this with an unselfish mind, not with a selfish one. And they dedicate that merit thus: "By this wholesome root, may all beings be born unstained by the impurity of the womb." And they contemplate this with intense intention (<s>āśaya</s>). These are the ten <s>dharmas</s>, O son of good family.'

body.text: anumodana-anuśaṃsās tv ārya-prajñā-pāramitāyām uktāḥ | yaḥ prathama-yāna-saṃprasthitānāṃ bodhi-satvānāṃ mahā-satvānāṃ tāṃś citta-utpādān anumodate |caratām api bodhi-satva-caryāṃ tāṃś citta-utpādān anumodate | a-vinivartanīyām api a-vinivartanīya-dharmatām anumodate bodhi-satvānāṃ mahā-satvānāṃ | kiyantaṃ sa bhagavan kula-putro vā kula-duhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇya-skandhaṃ prasavati ||
body.translated_text: The benefits of rejoicing (<s>anumodanā</s>) are stated in the noble <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>: 'One who rejoices in the mental aspirations of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who have set out in the first vehicle, and who rejoices in the mental aspirations of those practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct, and who rejoices in the irreversible nature of irreversible <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> — how great a mass of merit, O Blessed One, does that son or daughter of good family produce?'

body.text: evam ukte bhagavān śakraṃ devānām indram etad avocat | pe | syāt khalu punaḥ kauśika tri-sāhasra-mahā-sāhasrasya loka-dhātoḥ pala-agreṇa tulyamānasasya pramāṇam udgrahītuṃ | na tv eva kauśika bodhi-satvasya mahā-satvasya teṣām anumodanā-saha-gatānāṃ citta-utpādānāṃ puṇya-pramāṇaṃ grahītuṃ ||
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One spoke to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: [abbreviated] 'It would be possible, O <s>Kauśika</s>, to determine the weight of the <s>Trisāhasramahāsāhasra</s> world-system weighed grain by grain — but it is not possible, O <s>Kauśika</s>, to determine the measure of the merit of those mental aspirations accompanied by rejoicing of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.'

body.text: evam ukte śakro devānām indro bhagavantam etad avocat | māra-adhiṣṭhitās te bhagavan satvā veditavyā | ye bodhi-satvānāṃ mahā-satvānāṃ prathama-citta-utpādam upādāya yāvad an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhānām evam a-prameyam anumodanā-saha-gataṃ puṇyam iti na śṛṇvanti na jānanti | tām anumodanāṃ na samanvāharanti | māra-pakṣikās te bhagavan satvā bhaviṣyanti ||
body.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, spoke to the Blessed One: 'Those beings, O Blessed One, should be known as influenced by <s>Māra</s> — those who do not hear, do not know of, and do not bring to mind this immeasurable merit accompanied by rejoicing, from the first generation of <s>bodhicitta</s> by <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> up to [their attainment of] supreme, perfect awakening. Those beings, O Blessed One, will be of <s>Māra</s>'s faction.'

body.text: bhagavān āha | pe | yaiḥ kauśika kula-putraiḥ kula-duhitṛbhiś ca + ime citta-utpādā anumoditā bodhi-satva-yānikair vā praty-eka-buddha-yānikair vā śrāvaka-yānikair vā | te kṣipraṃ tathā-gatān arhataḥ samyak-saṃbuddhān ārāgayiṣyanti ||
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: [abbreviated] 'Those sons or daughters of good family, O <s>Kauśika</s>, who have rejoiced in these mental aspirations — whether they follow the <s>bodhisattva</s>-vehicle, the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle, or the <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle — they will quickly please the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened ones.'

body.text: bhagavān āha ||
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said:

body.text: evaṃ tair anumodanā-saha-gataiś citta-utpāda-kuśala-mūlair yatra yatra + upapatsyante tatra tatra sat-kṛtāś ca bhaviṣyanti guru-kṛtāś ca mānitāś ca pūjitāś ca arcitāś ca apacāyitāś ca bhaviṣyanti | na ca te * a-mana-āpāni rūpāṇi drakṣyanti | na ca te * a-mana-āpān śabdān śroṣyanti | evaṃ na gandhān na rasān na spraṣṭavyān sprakṣyanti na ca teṣām apāyeṣu + upapattiḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyā svarga-upapattis teṣāṃ pratikāṅkṣitavyā | tat kasya hetoḥ | tathā hi taiḥ satvaiḥ sarva-satva-sukha-āvahanāni a-saṃkhyeyānāṃ satvānāṃ kuśala-mūlāny anumoditāni yāvad an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhya + a-prameya-a-saṃkhyeyān satvān parinirvāpayiṣyanti + iti ||
body.translated_text: 'By those wholesome roots of mental aspiration accompanied by rejoicing, wherever they are reborn, there they will be honored, esteemed, respected, worshipped, revered, and venerated. They will not see unpleasant forms, nor will they hear unpleasant sounds. Likewise, they will not encounter [unpleasant] smells, tastes, or tangible objects. Rebirth in the lower realms is not to be expected for them; rebirth in the heavens is to be expected for them. For what reason? Because those beings have rejoiced in the wholesome roots of innumerable beings, [roots] that bring happiness to all beings — and they will, having attained supreme, perfect awakening, lead immeasurable and innumerable beings to final <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.'

body.text: punar atra + eva + āha | ye subhūte gaṅgā-nadī-vālikā-upameṣu tri-sāhasra-mahā-sāhasreṣu loka-dhātuṣu sarva-satvās te sarve * an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhiṃ pratitiṣṭheyur an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhiṃ pratiṣṭhāya gaṅgā-nadī-vālikā-samān kalpān upalambha-saṃjñinaś catvāri dhyānāni samāpadyeran | yaś ca bodhi-satvo mahā-satvo * anayā prajñā-pāramitayā upāya-kauśalyena ca parigṛhītā + atīta-an-āgata-praty-utpannānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ śīla-samādhi-prajñā-vimukti-vimukti-jñāna-darśana-skandhaṃ | śrāvakānāṃ praty-eka-buddhānām api śīla-samādhi-prajñā-vimukti-vimukti-jñāna-darśana-skandhaṃ sarvam ekato * abhisaṃkṣipya piṇḍayitvā tulayitvā nir-avaśeṣam anumodeta + agrayā + anumodanayā jyeṣṭhayā śreṣṭhayā varayā pravarayā praṇītayā uttarayā nir-uttarayā uttara-uttarayā a-samayā + a-sama-samayā + a-prati-samayā + anumodanayā + anumodya + anumodanā-saha-gataṃ

children.text: puṇya-kriyā-vastv an-uttarāyai samyak-saṃbodhaye pariṇāmayati | asya subhūte * anumodanā-saha-gatasya puṇya-kriyā-vastuno * asau pūrvaka aupalambhikānāṃ bodhi-satvānāṃ catur-dhyāna-mayaḥ puṇya-abhisaṃskāraḥ śatatamīm api kalāṃ na + upaiti yāvad upaniṣadam api na kṣamatae iti ||
children.translated_text: were to dedicate to supreme, perfect awakening — this mass of meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing, O <s>Subhūti</s>, compared with the former merit-formation consisting of the four <s>dhyānas</s> of those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who grasp [at objects], does not equal even a hundredth part, nor even a fraction thereof.'

body.translated_text: And again in the same [text] it says: 'If, O <s>Subhūti</s>, all beings in <s>Trisāhasramahāsāhasra</s> world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> were all to abide in supreme, perfect awakening, and having attained supreme, perfect awakening, were to enter the four <s>dhyānas</s> for <s>kalpas</s> equal to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, with the perception of grasping — and if a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, embraced by this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and skillful means, were to take the aggregate of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation of the past, future, and present <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones, and also of the <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, and having gathered, collected, and weighed all of it together, were to rejoice without remainder, with the foremost, the highest, the best, the most excellent, the most supreme, the most eminent, the unsurpassed, the supremely unsurpassed, the unequaled, the equally unequaled, the incomparably unequaled rejoicing — and having rejoiced, the mass of merit accompanied by that rejoicing

body.text: ayam eva nayaḥ pariṇāmanāyām uktaḥ | atha-vā + agra-pariṇāmanayā pariṇāmitatvāt sarva-puṇyānām asya buddhatvāya sat-kṛta-praṇidhi-buddhatvam eva syāt | ataḥ kā parā puṇya-vṛddhiḥ | tad * dhy a-śeṣa-satva-mokṣa-kṛta-puṇya-jñāna-upetaṃ nir-vikalpaṃ ca ||
body.translated_text: This same method is stated with regard to dedication (<s>pariṇāmanā</s>). Or rather, because all merits are dedicated through the foremost dedication toward <s>Buddhahood</s>, for one whose aspiration is honored, there would be <s>Buddhahood</s> itself. Therefore, what greater increase of merit could there be? For that [dedication] is endowed with merit and knowledge created for the liberation of all beings without remainder, and is free from conceptual construction.

body.text: adhyeṣaṇāyās tv anuśaṃsā ārya-ugra-paripṛcchāyām uktā dharma-grāhyatām upādāya + a-prameya-a-saṃkhyeyeṣu buddha-kṣetreṣv āyuḥ parirakṣaṇāya + iti ||
body.translated_text: The benefits of entreaty (<s>adhyeṣaṇā</s>) are stated in the noble <s>Ugraparipṛcchā</s>, with regard to receiving the <s>Dharma</s> — for the preservation of [the <s>Buddhas</s>'] lifespan in immeasurable and innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-fields.

body.text: ārya-śikṣā-samuccaye vandanā-ādy-anuśaṃsā saptadaśa-paricchedaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The seventeenth chapter of the noble <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>, [entitled] 'The Benefits of Salutation and So Forth' (<s>vandanādyanuśaṃsa</s>), is concluded.

body.text: ratna-traya-anusmṛtir nāma + aṣṭādaśaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The eighteenth chapter, entitled 'Recollection of the Three Jewels' (<s>Ratnatrayānusmṛti</s>).

body.text: uktā bhadra-caryā-vidhinā puṇya-vṛddhiḥ | asyāś ca + ayam a-paro hetuḥ | yo * ayaṃ śraddhā-ādīnāṃ sadā + abhyāsaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The increase of merit through the method of virtuous conduct (<s>Bhadracaryā</s>) has been stated. And the further cause of this is the constant practice of faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) and the other [faculties].

body.text: yathā + uktam ārya-tathā-gata-guhya-sūtre | catvāra ime mahā-rāja dharmā mahā-yāna-saṃprasthitānāṃ viśeṣa-gāmitāyai saṃvartante * a-parihāṇāya ca | katame catvāraḥ | śraddhā mahā-rāja viśeṣa-gāmitāyai saṃvartate * a-parihāṇāya | tatra katamā śraddhā | yayā śraddhayā āryān upasaṃkrāmati | a-karaṇīyaṃ ca na karoti ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the noble <s>Tathāgataguhyasūtra</s>: 'There are four <s>dharmas</s>, O great king, that conduce to the progress and non-decline of those who have set out in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. What are the four? Faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), O great king, conduces to progress and non-decline. What is that faith? It is the faith by which one approaches the noble ones and does not do what should not be done.'

body.text: gauravaṃ mahā-rāja viśeṣa-gāmitāyai saṃvartate | yena gauraveṇa su-bhāṣitaṃ śṛṇoti śuśrūṣate * a-virahita-śrotraś ca dharmaṃ śṛṇoti ||
body.translated_text: 'Reverence (<s>gaurava</s>), O great king, conduces to progress — the reverence by which one listens to well-spoken [teachings], attends to them, and hears the <s>Dharma</s> without being parted from [the opportunity to] listen.'

body.text: nir-mānatā mahā-rāja viśeṣa-gāmitāyai saṃvartate | yayā nir-mānatayā āryāṇām abhinamati praṇamati namasyati ||
body.translated_text: 'Freedom from pride (<s>nirmānatā</s>), O great king, conduces to progress — the freedom from pride by which one bows down before, prostrates to, and pays homage to the noble ones.'

body.text: vīryaṃ mahā-rāja viśeṣa-gāmitāyai saṃvartate * a-parihāṇāya | yena vīryeṇa kāya-laghutāṃ citta-laghutāṃ ca pratilabhate sarva-kāryāṇi ca + uttārayati ||
body.translated_text: 'Vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), O great king, conduces to progress and non-decline — the vigor by which one attains lightness of body and lightness of mind, and accomplishes all tasks.'

body.text: ime mahā-rāja catvāra iti ||
body.translated_text: 'These are the four, O great king.'

body.text: eṣāṃ śraddhā-ādīnāṃ sadā + abhyāsaḥ kāryaḥ | atha-vā + anyeṣāṃ śraddhā-ādīnāṃ ||
body.translated_text: The constant practice of these — faith and the others — should be undertaken. Or alternatively, [the practice] of the other [set of qualities beginning with] faith.

body.text: yathā + āha ārya-akṣayamati-sūtre pañca + imāni + indriyāṇi | katamāni pañca | śraddhā-indriyaṃ vīrya-indriyaṃ smṛti-indriyaṃ samādhi-indriyaṃ prajñā-indriyam iti ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the noble <s>Akṣayamatisūtra</s>: 'There are five faculties (<s>indriya</s>). What are the five? The faculty of faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), the faculty of vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), the faculty of mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), the faculty of concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and the faculty of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>).'

body.text: tatra katamā śraddhā | yathā śraddhāyāś caturo dharmān abhiśraddadhāti | katamāṃś caturaḥ | saṃsāra-avacarīṃ laukikīṃ samyag-dṛṣṭiṃ śraddadhāti | sa karma-vipāka-prati-śaraṇo bhavati | yad yat karma kariṣyāmi tasya tasya karmaṇaḥ phala-vipākaṃ pratyanubhaviṣyāmi + iti | sa jīvita-hetor api pāpaṃ karma na karoti | bodhi-satva-cārikām abhiśraddadhāti | tac-caryā-pratipannaś ca + anyatra yāne spṛhāṃ na + utpādayati | parama-artha-nīta-arthaṃ gambhīra-pratītya-samutpāda-nairātmya-niḥ-satva-nir-jīva-niḥ-pudgala-vyavahāra-śūnyatā-nimitta-a-praṇihita-lakṣaṇān sarva-dharmān śrutvā śraddadhāti | sarva-dṛṣṭi-kṛtāni ca na + anuśete sarva-buddha-dharmān bala-vaiśāradya-prabhṛtīṃś ca śraddadhāti | śraddhāya ca vigata-kathaṃ-kathas tān buddha-dharmān samudānayati | idam ucyate śraddhā-indriyam ||
body.translated_text: Therein, what is faith? It is that by which one has faith in four <s>dharmas</s> through faith. What are the four? One has faith in right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) that pertains to <s>saṃsāra</s> and is worldly — one becomes one who takes refuge in the ripening of <s>karma</s>, [thinking:] 'Whatever <s>karma</s> I perform, I shall experience the fruit and ripening of that <s>karma</s>.' One does not perform evil <s>karma</s> even for the sake of one's life. One has faith in the <s>bodhisattva</s>-conduct — and being engaged in that conduct, one does not generate longing for another vehicle. Having heard all <s>dharmas</s> that are led to the ultimate meaning, [characterized as] profound dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), selflessness, absence of beings, absence of a life-principle, absence of a person, emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), signlessness, and wishlessness — one has faith [in them]. And one does not cling to [positions] made by any views. And one has faith in all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, beginning with the powers (<s>bala</s>) and confidences (<s>vaiśāradya</s>). And being free from doubt through faith, one brings forth those <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. This is called the faculty of faith (<s>śraddhā-indriya</s>).

body.text: tatra katamad vīrya-indriyaṃ | yān dharmān śraddhā-indriyeṇa śraddadhāti tān dharmān vīrya-indriyeṇa samudānayati + idam ucyate vīrya-indriyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'Therein, what is the faculty of vigor (<s>vīryendriya</s>)? Whatever <s>dharmas</s> one has faith in through the faculty of faith — those <s>dharmas</s> one energetically pursues through the faculty of vigor. This is called the faculty of vigor.'

body.text: tatra katamat smṛti-indriyaṃ | yān dharmān vīrya-indriyeṇa samudānayati tān dharmān smṛti-indriyeṇa na vipraṇāśayati | idam ucyate smṛti-indriyam ||
body.translated_text: 'Therein, what is the faculty of mindfulness (<s>smṛtīndriya</s>)? Whatever <s>dharmas</s> one energetically pursues through the faculty of vigor — those <s>dharmas</s> one does not let slip through the faculty of mindfulness. This is called the faculty of mindfulness.'

body.text: tatra katamat samādhi-indriyaṃ | yān dharmān smṛti-indriyeṇa na vipraṇāśayati tān samādhi-indriyeṇa + eka-agrī-karoti + idam ucyate samādhi-indriyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'Therein, what is the faculty of concentration (<s>samādhīndriya</s>)? Whatever <s>dharmas</s> one does not let slip through the faculty of mindfulness — those one makes one-pointed through the faculty of concentration. This is called the faculty of concentration.'

body.text: tatra katamat prajñā-indriyam |yān dharmān samādhi-indriyeṇa + eka-agrī-karoti tān prajñā-indriyeṇa pratyavekṣate pratividhyati | yad eteṣu dharmeṣu praty-ātma-jñānam a-para-pratyaya-jñānam idam ucyate prajñā-indriyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'Therein, what is the faculty of wisdom (<s>prajñendriya</s>)? Whatever <s>dharmas</s> one makes one-pointed through the faculty of concentration — those one examines and penetrates through the faculty of wisdom. That which is personal knowledge, not dependent on others, regarding these <s>dharmas</s> — this is called the faculty of wisdom.'

body.text: evam imāni pañca-indriyāṇi sahitāny anuprabaddhāni sarva-buddha-dharmān paripūrayanti | vyākaraṇa-bhūmiṃ ca + āpyayanti iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Thus these five faculties, united and connected, fulfill all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> and bring one to the stage of prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>).'

body.text: śraddhā-ādīnāṃ balānāṃ sadā + abhyāsaḥ kāryaḥ | yathā + uktam ārya-ratna-cūḍa-sūtre | tatra katamat kula-putra bodhi-satvasya bala-caryā-pariśuddhiḥ | yad ebhir eva + indriyair upastabdho * an-avamardyo bhavati sarva-māraiḥ | a-saṃhāryo bhavati śrāvaka-praty-eka-buddha-yānābhyāṃ | a-vinivartyo bhavati mahā-yānāt | dur-dharṣo bhavati sarva-kleśaiḥ | dṛḍho bhavati pūrva-pratijñāsu | tṛpto bhavati cittena | balavān bhavati kāyena | gupto bhavati + indriyaiḥ | duḥ-parājayo bhavati tīrthi-karaiḥ | ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: The constant practice of the powers beginning with faith should be undertaken. As stated in the <s>Ārya-Ratnacūḍa Sūtra</s>: 'Therein, what is the purification of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s conduct of the powers, O son of good family? That, supported by these very faculties, he becomes uncrushed by all <s>Māras</s>; cannot be drawn away by the <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle and <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle; is irreversible from the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; is unconquerable by all afflictions; is firm in previous pledges; is content in mind; is strong in body; is guarded in faculties; is difficult to defeat by <s>tīrthika</s> teachers,' and so forth.

body.text: evaṃ tāvac * chraddhā-ādīnāṃ sadā + abhyāsaḥ puṇya-vṛddhaye ||
body.translated_text: Thus, the constant practice of [the powers] beginning with faith is for the increase of merit.

body.text: kā maitrī ||
body.translated_text: What is <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness)?

body.text: yathā + āha candra-pradīpa-sūtre | yāvanti pūjā bahu-vidha a-prameyā yā kṣetra-koṭīn a-yuta-bimbareṣu | tāṃ pūja-kṛtvā puruṣa-vareṣu nityaṃ saṃkhyā-kalāpo na bhavati maitra-citta | iti ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Candrapradīpa Sūtra</s>: 'Whatever offerings, manifold and immeasurable, are [made] in <s>koṭis</s> of fields, in <s>ayutas</s> and <s>vimbaras</s> — having made such offerings to the best among men constantly — they do not amount to a fraction of a mind of loving-kindness.'

body.text: kā buddha-ādy-anusmṛtiḥ ||
body.translated_text: What is the recollection of the <s>Buddha</s> and others (<s>buddhānusmṛti</s>)?

body.text: tatra rāṣṭrapāla-sūtre saṃvarṇitā | vandāmi te kanaka-varṇa-nibhā vara-lakṣaṇā vi-mala-candra-mukhā | vandāmi te a-sama-jñāna-parā sadṛśo na te * asti tri-bhave vi-rajā ||
body.translated_text: It is praised in the <s>Rāṣṭrapāla Sūtra</s>: 'I bow to you, [O <s>Buddha</s>,] resembling gold in complexion, bearing the supreme marks, with a face like the stainless moon. I bow to you, supreme in incomparable knowledge — there is none equal to you in the three realms, O stainless one.'

body.text: mṛdu cāru snigdha śubha keśa nakhā giri-rāja-tulya tava ca + uṣṇir iha | na + uṣnīṣam īkṣitu tava + asti samo vibhrājate bhruvi tava + ūrṇa mune ||
body.translated_text: 'Soft, beautiful, smooth, and auspicious are your hair and nails; and your <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown-protuberance) here is like the king of mountains. There is no one equal to [the task of] seeing your <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>; the <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft of hair) shines between your brows, O Sage.'

body.text: kunda-indu-śaṅkha-hima-śubhra-nibhā nīla-utpala-abha-śubha-netra-varā | kṛpayā + īkṣase jagad idaṃ hi yayā vandāmi te vi-mala-netra jina ||
body.translated_text: 'White like the <s>kunda</s> (jasmine), the moon, the conch, and snow; with beautiful, supreme eyes like the blue <s>utpala</s> lotus — with the compassion by which you look upon this world, I bow to you, O <s>Jina</s> (Victor) of stainless eyes.'

body.text: jihvā prabhūta tanu tāmra-nibhā vadanaṃ ca chādayasi yena svakaṃ | dharmaṃ vadan vinayase ca jagat vandāmi te madhura-snigdha-girā ||
body.translated_text: 'Your tongue is broad, thin, and copper-colored, with which you cover your own face. Teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, you discipline the world — I bow to you, of sweet and gentle speech.'

body.text: daśanāḥ śubhāḥ su-dṛḍha vajra-nibhāḥ triṃśad-daśa + apy a-viralāḥ sahitāḥ | kurvan smitaṃ vinayase ca jagat vandāmi te madhura-satya-kathā ||
body.translated_text: 'Your teeth are beautiful, very firm, resembling <s>vajra</s> (diamond), forty [in number], close together and even. Smiling, you discipline the world — I bow to you, of sweet and truthful words.'

body.text: rūpeṇa ca + a-prati-samo * asi jinaḥ prabhayā ca bhāsayasi kṣetra-śatān | brahma-indra-pāla-jagato bhagavan jihmī-bhavanti tava te prabhayā ||
body.translated_text: 'In form you are matchless, O <s>Jina</s>; with your radiance you illuminate hundreds of fields. <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the protectors of the world, O <s>Bhagavān</s> — they become dim before your radiance.'

body.text: eṇeya jaṅgha bhagavann a-samā gaja-rāja-barhi-mṛga-rāja-gato | īkṣan vrajasy api yugaṃ bhagavan saṃkampayan dharaṇi-śaila-taṭān ||
body.translated_text: 'Your calves are like the antelope's, O <s>Bhagavān</s> — incomparable; your gait is that of the king of elephants, the peacock, the king of lions. Even when you walk a single step, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, you cause the earth and mountain slopes to tremble.'

body.text: kāyaś ca lakṣaṇa-cito bhagavan sūkṣma chavī kanaka-varṇa-nibhā | na + īkṣañ jagad vrajati tṛptim idaṃ rūpaṃ tava + a-pratima-rūpa-dhara ||
body.translated_text: 'Your body is adorned with the [thirty-two] marks, O <s>Bhagavān</s>; subtle is your skin, resembling gold in complexion. This world does not reach satiation in beholding [you] — O bearer of incomparable form!'

body.text: tvaṃ pūrva-kalpa-śata-cīrṇa-tapāḥ tvaṃ sarva-tyāga-dama-dāna-rataḥ | tvaṃ sarva-satva-kṛpa-maitra-manāḥ vandāmi te parama-kāruṇikam ||
body.translated_text: 'You have practiced austerities for hundreds of former <s>kalpas</s>; you delight in complete renunciation, self-control, and giving; your mind is of compassion and loving-kindness toward all beings — I bow to you, O supremely compassionate one.'

body.text: tvaṃ dāna-śīla-nirataḥ satataṃ tvaṃ kṣānti-vīrya-nirataḥ su-dṛḍhaḥ | tvaṃ dhyāna-prajña-prabha-teja-dharo vandāmi te a-sama-jñāna-dhara ||
body.translated_text: 'You are always devoted to giving and moral conduct; you are firmly devoted to patience and vigor; you bear the radiance and brilliance of meditation and wisdom — I bow to you, O bearer of incomparable knowledge.'

body.text: tvaṃ vādi-sūra ku-gaṇa-pramathī tvaṃ siṃha-van nadasi parṣadi ca | tvaṃ vaidya-rāja tri-mala-anta-karo vandāmi te parama-prīti-kara ||
body.translated_text: 'You are a hero in debate, a crusher of evil hosts; you roar like a lion in the assembly; you are the king of physicians, destroyer of the three defilements — I bow to you, O supreme bringer of joy.'

body.text: vāk-kāya-mānasa-viśuddha mune tri-bhaveṣv a-lipta-jala-padmam iva | tvaṃ brahma-ghoṣa-kalaviṅka-ruto vandāmi te traibhava-pāra-gatam ||
body.translated_text: 'O Sage of pure speech, body, and mind, unattached to the three realms like a lotus in water; your voice is like <s>Brahmā</s>'s, like the <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird — I bow to you who have gone beyond the three realms.'

body.text: māyā-upamaṃ jagad imaṃ bhavatā naṭa-raṅga-svapna-sadṛśaṃ viditaṃ | na + ātmā na satva na ca jīva-gatī dharmā marīci-daka-candra-samāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'By you this world has been known as like an illusion — resembling an actor's stage, a dream. There is no self, no being, no life-course — <s>dharmas</s> are like a mirage, like water, like the [reflection of the] moon.'

body.text: śūnyāś ca śānta an-utpāda-nayaṃ a-vijānad eva jagad udbhramati | teṣām upāya-naya-yukti-śataiḥ avatārayasy ati-kṛpālutayā ||
body.translated_text: 'Empty and peaceful, the way of non-arising — yet the world, not understanding, wanders in confusion. By hundreds of skillful means and reasoning, you cause them to enter [the truth], through your supreme compassion.'

body.text: rāga-ādibhiś ca bahu-rāga-śataiḥ saṃbhrāmitaṃ satata vīkṣya jagat | vaidya-upamo vicarase * a-pratimo parimocayan su-gata satva-śatān ||
body.translated_text: 'Seeing the world constantly bewildered by attachment and hundreds of forms of passion — like a physician you wander, incomparable, liberating hundreds of beings, O <s>Sugata</s>.'

body.text: jātī-jarā-maraṇa-śoka-hataṃ priya-vi-prayoga-parideva-śataiḥ | satata-āturaṃ jagad avekṣya mune parimocayan vicarase kṛpayā ||
body.translated_text: 'Seeing the world stricken by birth, aging, death, and grief, with hundreds of lamentations from separation from the dear — constantly afflicted — beholding [this], O Sage, you wander liberating [them] through compassion.'

body.text: ratha-cakra-vad bhramati sarva-jagat tiryakṣu preta-niraye su-gatau | mūḍhā a-deśika a-nātha-gatāḥ tasya pradarśayasi mārga-varaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'Like a chariot-wheel, the entire world revolves — among animals, <s>pretas</s>, hells, and happy realms. Deluded, without a guide, without a protector — to them you show the supreme path.'

body.text: ye te babhūvu purimāś ca jināḥ dharma-īśvarā jagati ca + artha-karāḥ | ayam eva taiḥ prakathita-ārya-patho yad deśayasy api vibho * a-pratimaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Those <s>Jinas</s> who were in the past, lords of <s>Dharma</s>, workers of benefit in the world — this is the very noble path proclaimed by them, which you too teach, O sovereign, O incomparable one.'

body.text: snigdhaṃ hy a-karkaśa mano-jña varaṃ brahma-adhikaṃ parama-prīti-karaṃ | gandharva-kinnara-vara-apsarasām abhibhūya tāṃ giram udāharase ||
body.translated_text: 'Tender, not harsh, pleasant, supreme, surpassing <s>Brahmā</s>, supremely delightful — surpassing [the voices of] <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and the best <s>apsaras</s> — you utter that speech.'

body.text: satya-ārjava-a-kṣayam upāya-nayaiḥ pariśodhitāṃ giram an-anta-guṇāṃ | śrutvā hi yāṃ niyuta-satva-śatāḥ yāna-trayeṇa janayanti śamam ||
body.translated_text: 'Purified through truth, uprightness, and inexhaustible skillful means — that speech of infinite virtues — hearing which, <s>niyutas</s> of hundreds of beings generate peace through the three vehicles.'

body.text: tava pūjayā sukham an-eka-vidham divyaṃ labhanti manu-jeṣu tathā | āḍhyo mahā-dhana mahā-vibhavo bhavate jagad-dhita-karo nṛ-patiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Through worship of you, they obtain manifold, divine happiness, and likewise among humans. They become wealthy, of great riches, of great splendor, and become kings who benefit the world.'

body.text: bala-cakra-varty api ca dvīpa-patiḥ jagad āvṛṇoti daśabhiḥ kuśalaiḥ | ratnāni sapta labhate su-śubhā tvayi saṃprasāda-janako * a-pratimaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'They become powerful <s>cakravartins</s>, lords of the continents, covering the world with the ten wholesomeness; they obtain the seven jewels, most auspicious — through generating faith in you, O incomparable one.'

body.text: brahmā + api śakra api loka-patiḥ bhavate ca saṃtuṣiṭa deva-patiḥ | para-nirmito * api ca sa yāma-patiḥ tvat-pūjayā bhavati ca + api jinaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'They become <s>Brahmā</s>, or <s>Śakra</s>, or world-protectors, or lords of the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, or lords of the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> or <s>Yāma</s> [heavens] — through worship of you they even become <s>Jinas</s>.'

body.text: evaṃ hy a-mogha tava pūjā kṛtā saṃdarśanaṃ śravaṇam apy a-samaṃ | bhavate jagad vividha-duḥkha-haraṃ spṛśate padaṃ ca paramaṃ vi-rajaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'Thus your worship, performed without being fruitless — even seeing [you] and hearing [you] is incomparable — removes the manifold sufferings of the world, and [the worshipper] touches the supreme, stainless state.'

body.text: mārga-jña mārga-kuśalā bhagavan ku-pathān nivārayasi lokam imaṃ | kṣeme śive vi-raji ārya-pathe pratiṣṭhāpayasi jagad bhagavan ||
body.translated_text: 'O knower of the path, skilled in the path, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, you turn this world back from evil paths. On the safe, auspicious, stainless, noble path you establish the world, O <s>Bhagavān</s>.'

body.text: puṇya-arthikasya tava puṇya-nidhe satata-a-kṣayā bhavati puṇya-kriyā | bahu-kalpa-koṭiṣu na yāti kṣayaṃ yāvad * dhi na spṛśati bodhi varāṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'For one who seeks merit, O treasury of merit, the meritorious activity is constant and inexhaustible. For <s>koṭis</s> of many <s>kalpas</s> it does not reach exhaustion — as long as one does not touch the supreme <s>bodhi</s>.'

body.text: pariśuddha-kṣetra labhate ruciraṃ parinirmita-abha sada prīti-karaṃ | śuddhāś ca kāya-vacasā manasā satvā bhavanty api ca kṣetra-vare ||
body.translated_text: 'One obtains a purified, beautiful field, resembling the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> [heaven], always delightful; and beings too become pure in body, speech, and mind, in that supreme field.'

body.text: ity evam ādi-guṇa na + eka-vidhān labhate jina-arcana-kṛtān manu-jaḥ | svarga-apavarga manu-jeṣu sukhaṃ labhate ca puṇya-nidhi sarva-jage ||
body.translated_text: 'Thus a human being obtains these and many other kinds of virtues through worshipping the <s>Jina</s>. Happiness in heaven, liberation, and happiness among humans — the treasury of merit obtains [all this] in the entire world.'

body.text: kīrti-yaśaś ca prasṛtaṃ vipulaṃ tava sarva-dikṣu bahu-kṣetra-śatān | saṃkīrtayanti su-gatāḥ satataṃ tava varṇa-māla pariṣatsu jināḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Vast and extensive fame and renown [spread] in your name throughout hundreds of fields in all directions. The <s>Sugatas</s> constantly proclaim your garland of praises in the assemblies of the <s>Jinas</s>.'

body.text: vigata-jvarā jagati mokṣa-karāḥ priya-darśanā a-sama-kāruṇikāḥ | śānta-indriyā śama-ratā bhagavan vandāmi te nara-vara-pravara ||
body.translated_text: 'Free from fever, liberators in the world, beautiful to behold, of incomparable compassion, with pacified senses, delighting in peace, O <s>Bhagavān</s> — I bow to you, O supreme among the best of men.'

body.text: labdhā abhijña jina pañca mayā gagane sthitena te niśamya giram | bhavitā + asmi vīra su-gata-pratimo vibhajiṣya dharmam a-malaṃ jagataḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Having attained the five higher knowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), O <s>Jina</s>, standing in the sky, having heard your speech — I shall become one equal to the <s>Sugata</s>, O Hero, and shall teach the stainless <s>Dharma</s> to the world.'

body.text: stutvā + adya sarva-guṇa-pāra-gataṃ nara-deva-nāga-mahitaṃ su-gataṃ | puṇyaṃ yad arjitam idaṃ vipulaṃ jagad āpnuyād api ca buddha-padam |iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Having praised the <s>Sugata</s> who has gone beyond all virtues, honored by gods, men, and <s>nāgas</s> — whatever vast merit has been earned by this, may the world attain even the state of <s>Buddhahood</s>!'

body.text: atha-vā yathā + ārya-dharma-saṃgīti-sūtre kathitaṃ | punar a-paraṃ buddhā bhagavanto mahā-puṇya-jñāna-saṃbhārā mahā-maitrī-mahā-karuṇā-go-carā mahā-satva-rāśeḥ trāṇa-bhūtā mahā-bhaiṣajya-śalya-hartāraḥ sarva-satva-sama-citta-a-nitya-samādhi-go-carāḥ saṃsāra-nirvāṇa-vimuktā yāvat satvānāṃ mātā-pitṛ-kalpāḥ samāna-maitra-cittāḥ | pe ||
body.translated_text: Or else, as stated in the <s>Ārya-Dharmasaṃgīti Sūtra</s>: 'Furthermore, the <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s> are endowed with the great accumulations of merit and knowledge; their domain is great loving-kindness and great compassion; they are the refuge of the great mass of beings; they are the great physicians who extract the thorns [of suffering]; their domain is the <s>samādhi</s> of equanimity, impermanence, and equal mind toward all beings; they are liberated from <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>; they are like the mothers and fathers of beings, with equal minds of loving-kindness.' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: sarva-loka-an-abhibhūtāḥ sarva-lokasya + āloka-bhūtā mahā-yoga-yogino mahā-ātmāno mahā-jana-parivārā viśiṣṭa-jana-parivārā a-nivārita-darśana-śravaṇa-paryupāsanāḥ sva-sukha-nir-apekṣāḥ para-duṣkha-praśamana-priyā dharma-priyā dharma-dharā dharma-āhārā dharma-bhiṣajo dharma-īśvarā dharma-svāmino dharma-dāna-patayo nitya-tyāga-abhiratā nitya-a-pramattā nitya-viveka-abhiratāḥ sarvatra tīrtha-setu-bhūtā mahā-rāja-mārga-prakhyā yāvad * a-secanaka-darśanā buddhā bhagavanta | evaṃ tān anusmarati | evaṃ ca tān anusmṛtya tad-guṇa-pariniṣpatty-arthaṃ smṛtim upasthāpayati + iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Unconquered by the entire world, they are the light of the entire world; great practitioners of yoga, great-souled, attended by great assemblies, attended by distinguished assemblies; their seeing, hearing, and attendance is unrestricted; without concern for their own happiness, delighting in the pacification of others' suffering; loving the <s>Dharma</s>, upholding the <s>Dharma</s>, nourished by the <s>Dharma</s>, physicians of the <s>Dharma</s>, lords of the <s>Dharma</s>, masters of the <s>Dharma</s>, patrons of the gift of <s>Dharma</s>; always delighting in relinquishment, always vigilant, always delighting in seclusion; everywhere being the ford and bridge [for crossing]; renowned like a great royal highway; and their appearance is never wearying — such are the <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s>. Thus one recollects them. And having thus recollected them, one establishes mindfulness for the purpose of completing those qualities.'

body.text: tad ucyate buddha-anusmṛtir iti ||
body.translated_text: This is called the recollection of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>buddhānusmṛti</s>).

body.text: atra + eva dharma-anusmṛtim āha | iha bodhi-satvasya + evaṃ bhavati | yae ete buddhā bhagavanto * an-anta-a-paryanta-guṇā ete dharma-jā dharma-padā dharma-nirmitā dharma-adhipateyā dharma-prabhā dharma-go-carā dharma-prati-śaraṇā dharma-niṣpannāḥ | peyālaṃ ||
body.translated_text: In this same [sūtra] it states the recollection of the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmānusmṛti</s>): 'Here the <s>bodhisattva</s> thinks thus: "These <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s> of infinite and boundless virtues — they are born of the <s>Dharma</s>, their station is the <s>Dharma</s>, they are fashioned by the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Dharma</s> is their sovereign, their radiance is the <s>Dharma</s>, their domain is the <s>Dharma</s>, their refuge is the <s>Dharma</s>, they are accomplished through the <s>Dharma</s>."' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: yāny api laukikāni loka-uttarāṇi ca sukhāni santi | tāny api dharma-jāni dharma-niṣpannāni | tasmān mayā bodhy-arthikena dharma-gurukeṇa bhavitavyaṃ | dharma-gauraveṇa dharma-prati-śaraṇena dharma-parāyaṇena dharma-sāreṇa dharma-anva ... dharma-pratipannena | iti + iyam ucyate bodhi-satvasya dharma-anusmṛtiḥ ||
body.translated_text: '"Whatever mundane and supramundane happinesses there are — they too are born of the <s>Dharma</s>, accomplished through the <s>Dharma</s>. Therefore I, who seek awakening, should hold the <s>Dharma</s> as my teacher; should have reverence for the <s>Dharma</s>; the <s>Dharma</s> as my refuge; the <s>Dharma</s> as my final resort; the <s>Dharma</s> as my essence; ... should practice the <s>Dharma</s>." This is called the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s recollection of the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: punar a-paraṃ bodhi-satvasya + evaṃ bhavati | samo hi dharmaḥ samaḥ satveṣu pravartate | dharmo hīna-madhya-viśiṣṭa-an-apekṣyaḥ pravartate | tathā mayā dharma-sadṛśa-cittena bhavitavyaṃ | na dharmo sukha-prekṣikayā pravartate | a-pakṣa-patito hi dharmaḥ | tathā mayā dharma-sadṛśa-cittena bhavitavyaṃ |na dharmaḥ kālam apekṣya pravartate |ākāliko hi dharmaḥ | aihipaśyikaḥ | praty-ātma-vedanīyaḥ |tathā mayā dharma-sadṛśa-cittena bhavitavyaṃ |na dharma udāre pravartate hīneṣu na pravartate | an-unnāma-avanāmo hi dharmaḥ |tathā mayā dharma-sadṛśa-cittena bhavitavyaṃ |na dharmaḥ śuddheṣu pravartate kṣateṣu na pravartate | utkarṣa-apakarṣa-apagato hi dharmas tathā mayā dharma-sadṛśa-cittena bhavitavyaṃ |na dharma āryeṣu pravartate pṛthag-janeṣu na pravartate | kṣetra-dṛṣṭi-vigato hi dharmaḥ | tathā mayā dharma-sadṛśa-cittena bhavitavyaṃ | na dharmo divā pravartate rātrau na pravartate | rātryāṃ vā pravartate divā na pravartate | sadā + adhiṣṭhito hi dharmaḥ | tathā mayā dharma-sadṛśa-cittena bhavitavyam | na dharmo vinaya-velām atikrāmati | na dharmasya kva-cid vilambaḥ | tathā mayā dharma-sadṛśa-cittena bhavitavyam | na dharmasya + ūnatvaṃ na pūrṇatvam a-prameya-a-saṃkhyeyo hi dharma ākāśa-van na kṣīyate na vardhate | tathā mayā dharma-sadṛśa-cittena bhavitavyaṃ | na dharmaḥ satvai rakṣyate | dharmaḥ satvān rakṣati | tathā mayā dharma-sadṛśa-cittena bhavitavyaṃ |na dharmaḥ śaraṇaṃ paryeṣate |dharmaḥ sarva-lokasya śaraṇaṃ |tathā mayā dharma-sadṛśa-cittena bhavitavyaṃ |na dharmasya kva-cit pratighāto | a-prati-hata-lakṣaṇo hi dharmaḥ |tathā mayā dharma-sadṛśa-cittena bhavitavyaṃ |na dharmo * anuśayaṃ vahati | nir-anuśayo hi dharmaḥ |tathā mayā dharma-sadṛśa-cittena bhavitavyam | na dharmaḥ saṃsāra-bhaya-bhīto na nirvāṇa-anunītaḥ | sadā nir-vikalpo hi dharmaḥ |tathā mayā dharma-sadṛśa-cittena bhavitavyam |evaṃ bodhi-satvo dharma-vad dharme smṛtim upasthāpayati | tad ucyate dharma-anusmṛtir iti ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>bodhisattva</s> reflects thus: 'The <s>Dharma</s> is equal; it operates equally among beings. The <s>Dharma</s> operates without regard for the inferior, middling, or superior. Thus I should have a mind like the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Dharma</s> does not operate with partiality for the pleasant. For the <s>Dharma</s> is free from taking sides. Thus I should have a mind like the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Dharma</s> does not operate with regard to time. For the <s>Dharma</s> is timeless, to-be-seen-for-oneself, to-be-personally-experienced. Thus I should have a mind like the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Dharma</s> does not operate in the exalted and not in the lowly. For the <s>Dharma</s> is without elevation or depression. Thus I should have a mind like the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Dharma</s> does not operate in the pure and not in the impaired. For the <s>Dharma</s> is free from superiority and inferiority. Thus I should have a mind like the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Dharma</s> does not operate in the Noble Ones and not in ordinary people. For the <s>Dharma</s> is free from the view of a [particular] field. Thus I should have a mind like the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Dharma</s> does not operate by day and not by night, nor by night and not by day. For the <s>Dharma</s> is always established. Thus I should have a mind like the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Dharma</s> does not transgress the limit of the <s>Vinaya</s>. The <s>Dharma</s> has no delay anywhere. Thus I should have a mind like the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Dharma</s> has no deficiency nor fullness, for the <s>Dharma</s> is immeasurable and incalculable — like space, it neither diminishes nor increases. Thus I should have a mind like the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Dharma</s> is not protected by beings; the <s>Dharma</s> protects beings. Thus I should have a mind like the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Dharma</s> does not seek refuge; the <s>Dharma</s> is the refuge of the entire world. Thus I should have a mind like the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Dharma</s> has no obstruction anywhere. For the <s>Dharma</s> is characterized as unobstructed. Thus I should have a mind like the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Dharma</s> does not carry latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>). For the <s>Dharma</s> is free from latent tendencies. Thus I should have a mind like the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Dharma</s> is not frightened by the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>, nor is it enticed by <s>nirvāṇa</s>. For the <s>Dharma</s> is always free from conceptual construction.' Thus I should have a mind like the <s>Dharma</s>. In this way, the <s>bodhisattva</s> establishes mindfulness of the <s>Dharma</s> in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>. This is called the recollection of the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmānusmṛti</s>).

body.text: atra + eva + āha | saṃgho hi dharma-vādī dharma-caraṇo dharma-cintako dharma-kṣetraṃ dharma-dharo dharma-prati-śaraṇo dharma-pūjako dharma-kṛtya-kārī dharma-go-caro dharma-cāritra-saṃpannaḥ | sva-bhāva-ṛjukaḥ sva-bhāva-śuddhaḥ sa-anukrośo dharma-anukāruṇikaḥ sadā viveka-go-caraḥ | sadā dharma-parāyaṇaḥ sadā śukla-kārī + ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: In this very [sūtra] it says: 'The <s>Saṅgha</s> is one that speaks the <s>Dharma</s>, practices the <s>Dharma</s>, contemplates the <s>Dharma</s>, is a field of the <s>Dharma</s>, bears the <s>Dharma</s>, takes the <s>Dharma</s> as refuge, worships the <s>Dharma</s>, performs the work of the <s>Dharma</s>, has the <s>Dharma</s> as its domain, is endowed with the conduct of the <s>Dharma</s>. It is upright by nature, pure by nature, compassionate, kindly in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, always dwelling in solitude, always devoted to the <s>Dharma</s>, always doing what is wholesome,' and so forth.

body.text: tatra bodhi-satvasya saṃgham anusmarataḥ evaṃ bhavati | yae ete saṃghasya bhūtā guṇā ete mayā + ātmanaḥ sarva-satvānāṃ ca niṣpādayitavyā iti ||
body.translated_text: Therein, when the <s>bodhisattva</s> recollects the <s>Saṅgha</s>, he reflects thus: 'These are the true qualities of the <s>Saṅgha</s> — these I should bring to fulfillment in myself and in all beings.'

body.text: yathā + ārya-vimalakīrti-nirdeśe bodhi-satva-guṇā uktās tathā saṃgha-anusmṛtir bhāvyā | sarva-satvāna ye rūpā ruta-ghoṣāś ca īritāḥ | eka-kṣaṇena darśenti bodhi-satvā viśāradāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Just as the qualities of the <s>bodhisattva</s> are described in the <s>Ārya-Vimalakīrtinirdeśa</s>, so should the recollection of the <s>Saṅgha</s> (<s>saṅghānusmṛti</s>) be cultivated: 'Whatever forms, sounds, and voices are uttered by all beings — the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the Confident Ones, display them in a single moment.'

body.text: te jīrṇa-vyādhitā bhonti bodhi-satvā mṛtam ātmāna darśayī |satvānāṃ paripākāya māyā-dharma vikrīḍitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> appear as aged, sick, and show themselves as dead — for the ripening of beings, they sport in the illusory nature of things (<s>māyā-dharma</s>).'

body.text: kalpa-uddāhaṃ ca darśenti uddahitvā vasuṃ-dharām | nitya-saṃjñina satvānām a-nityam iti darśayī ||
body.translated_text: 'They display the conflagration of the <s>kalpa</s> and, having burned up the earth, they show the impermanent to beings who have the perception of permanence.'

body.text: satvaiḥ śata-sahasrebhir eka-rāṣṭre nimantritāḥ | sarveṣāṃ gṛha bhuñjanti sarvān nāmanti bodhaye ||
body.translated_text: 'Invited by hundreds of thousands of beings in a single kingdom, they eat in the houses of all and incline all toward awakening.'

body.text: ye ke-cin mantra-vidyā vā śilpa-sthānā bahu-vidhāḥ | sarvatra pārami-prāptāḥ sarva-satva-sukha-āvahāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>mantras</s>, sciences, or manifold arts there are — in all they have attained perfection, bringing happiness to all beings.'

body.text: yāvanto loka pāṣaṇḍāḥ sarvatra pravrajanti te | nānā-dṛṣṭi-gataṃ prāptāṃs te satvān paripācati ||
body.translated_text: 'In all the heretical sects of the world, they go forth [as wanderers]. They ripen those beings who have fallen into various views.'

body.text: candrā vā bhonti sūryā vā śakra-brahma-praja-īśvarāḥ | bhavanti āpas tejaś ca pṛthivī mārutas tathā ||
body.translated_text: 'They become the moon or the sun, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, or <s>Prajāpati</s>; they become water, fire, earth, and wind likewise.'

body.text: roga antara-kalpeṣu bhaiṣajyaṃ bhonti uttamāḥ | yena te satva mucyante sukhī bhonti an-āmayāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'During the intermediate <s>kalpas</s> of disease, they become supreme medicines; by which those beings are freed and become happy and free from illness.'

body.text: dur-bhikṣā-antara-kalpeṣu bhavantī pāna-bhojanam |kṣudhā-pipāsām apanīya dharmaṃ deśenti prāṇinām ||
body.translated_text: 'During the intermediate <s>kalpas</s> of famine, they become food and drink; having removed hunger and thirst, they teach the <s>Dharma</s> to living beings.'

body.text: śastra antara-kalpeṣu maitrī-dhyāyī bhavanti te | a-vyāpāde niyojenti satva-koṭi-śatān bahūn ||
body.translated_text: 'During the intermediate <s>kalpas</s> of weapons, they become meditators on <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness); they yoke many hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of beings in non-hostility.'

body.text: mahā-saṃgrāma-madhye ca sama-pakṣā bhavanti te | sandhi-sāmagri rocenti bodhi-satvā mahā-balāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'And in the midst of great battles, they take the side of both parties; the <s>bodhisattvas</s> of great power promote peace and reconciliation.'

body.text: ye ca + api nirayāḥ ke-cid buddha-kṣetreṣv a-cintiṣu | saṃcintya tatra gacchanti satvānāṃ hita-kāraṇāt ||
body.translated_text: 'And whatever hells there are in inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-fields — deliberately they go there, for the sake of benefiting beings.'

body.text: yāvantyā gatayaḥ kāś-cit tiryag-yonau prakāśitāḥ | sarvatra dharmaṃ deśenti tena ucyanti nāyakāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'In all the various destinies manifest in the animal realm — everywhere they teach the <s>Dharma</s>; therefore they are called Guides.'

body.text: kāma-bhogāṃś ca darśenti dhyānaṃ ca dhyāyināṃ tathā | vidhvasta māraṃ kurvanti avatāraṃ na denti te ||
body.translated_text: 'They display sensual enjoyments and also meditation for meditators; they vanquish <s>Māra</s> and do not give him an opening.'

body.text: agni-madhye yathā padmam a-bhūtaṃ taṃ vinirdiśet | evaṃ kāmāṃś ca dhyānaṃ ca a-bhūtaṃ te vidarśayī ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as a lotus in the midst of fire would be declared impossible — even so they show that both sensual pleasures and meditation are unreal.'

body.text: saṃcintya gaṇikāṃ bhonti puṃsām ākarṣaṇāya te | rāga-aṅku saṃlobhya buddha-jñāne sthāpayanti te ||
body.translated_text: 'Deliberately they become courtesans, for the purpose of attracting men; having lured them with the hook of passion, they establish them in <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge.'

body.text: grāmikāś ca sadā bhonti sa-artha-vāhāḥ puro-hitāḥ | agra-amātya + atha ca + amātyaḥ
body.translated_text: 'They always become village chiefs, caravan-leaders, priests, chief ministers and also ministers'

body.text: daridrāṇāṃ ca satvānāṃ nidhānā bhonti a-kṣayāḥ | teṣāṃ dānāni datvā ca bodhi-cittaṃ janenti te ||
body.translated_text: 'For poor beings they become inexhaustible treasuries; having given them gifts, they generate in them the aspiration for awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>).'

body.text: māna-stabdheṣu satveṣu mahā-nagnā bhavanti te | sarva-mānasam udghātaṃ bodhiṃ prārthenti uttamām ||
body.translated_text: 'Among beings who are stiff with pride, they become great naked ascetics; having uprooted all pride, they aspire to supreme awakening.'

body.text: bhaya-arditānāṃ satvānāṃ saṃtiṣṭhante * agrataḥ sadā | a-bhayaṃ teṣu datvā ca paripācenti bodhaye ||
body.translated_text: 'For beings afflicted by fear, they always stand at the forefront; having given them fearlessness, they ripen them for awakening.'

body.text: pañca-abhijñāś ca te bhūtvā ṛṣayo brahma-cāriṇaḥ | śīle satvān niyojenti kṣānti-sauratya-saṃyame ||
body.translated_text: 'And having become seers (<s>ṛṣis</s>) endowed with the five higher knowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), practitioners of the holy life (<s>brahmacārin</s>), they yoke beings in moral conduct, patience, gentleness, and restraint.'

body.text: upasthāna-gurūn satvān paśyanti + iha viśāradāḥ | ceṭā bhavanti dāsā vā śiṣyatvam upayānti ca ||
body.translated_text: 'They see beings here who hold teachers in reverence, the Confident Ones; they become servants or slaves, or they assume the role of disciples.'

body.text: yena yena + eva ca + aṅgena satvo dharma-rato bhavet | darśenti hi kriyāḥ sarvā mahā-upāya-su-śikṣitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'By whatever means a being might become one who delights in the <s>Dharma</s>, they display all [corresponding] actions — well-trained in the great skillful means.'

body.text: yeṣām an-antā śikṣā hi an-antaś ca + api go-caraḥ | an-anta-jñāna-saṃpannā an-anta-prāṇi-mocakāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Those whose training is endless, whose domain is also endless, who are endowed with endless knowledge, who liberate endless beings'

body.text: na teṣāṃ kalpa-koṭībhiḥ kalpa-koṭi-śatair api | buddhair api vadadbhis tu guṇa-antaḥ su-vaco bhaved | iti ||
body.translated_text: '— not in <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, not even in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, even with the <s>Buddhas</s> speaking, could the limit of their qualities be easily expressed.' Thus —

body.text: yathā + ārya-ratna-ulkā-dhāraṇyāṃ bodhi-satva-guṇā uktās tathā bhāvayitavyāḥ | raśmi pramuñciya mālya-viyūhā mālya-vataṃsaka mālya vitānāḥ | mālya-vicinna-vikīrṇa-samantāḥ te jina-pūja karonti mahā-ātmā ||
body.translated_text: Just as the qualities of the <s>bodhisattva</s> are described in the <s>Ārya-Ratnolkā-dhāraṇī</s>, so should they be cultivated: 'Emitting rays arrayed with garlands, with garland-diadems and garland-canopies, with garlands scattered variously all around — those great beings make worship of the <s>Jinas</s>.'

body.text: raśmi pramuñciya cūrṇa-viyūhā cūrṇa-vataṃsaka cūrṇa-vitānāḥ | cūrṇa-vicitra-vikīrṇa samantān te jina-pūja karonti maha--ātmā ||
body.translated_text: 'Emitting rays arrayed with powders, with powder-diadems and powder-canopies, with powders scattered variously all around — those great beings make worship of the <s>Jinas</s>.'

body.text: raśmi pramuñciya padma-viyūhā padma-vataṃsaka padma-vitānā | padma-vicitra-vikīrṇa-samantān te jina-pūja karonti mahā-ātmā ||
body.translated_text: 'Emitting rays arrayed with lotuses, with lotus-diadems and lotus-canopies, with lotuses scattered variously all around — those great beings make worship of the <s>Jinas</s>.'

body.text: raśmi pramuñciya hāra-viyūhā hāra-vataṃsaka hāra-vitānā | hāra-vicitra-vikīrṇa-samantān te jina-pūja karonti mahā-ātmā ||
body.translated_text: 'Emitting rays arrayed with necklaces, with necklace-diadems and necklace-canopies, with necklaces scattered variously all around — those great beings make worship of the <s>Jinas</s>.'

body.text: raśmi pramuñciya dhvaja-agra-viyūhā te dhvaja pāṇḍura-lohita-pītāḥ | nīlam an-eka patāka vicitrā ||
body.translated_text: 'Emitting rays arrayed with the finest banners — banners white, red, and yellow, blue, with various multi-colored pennants'

body.text: dhvaja samalaṃ-karite jina-kṣetrāḥ te maṇi-jāla-vicitra-viyūhā | paṭṭa patāka pralambita dāmā kiṅkiṇi-jāla jina-svara-ghoṣān ||
body.translated_text: '— the <s>Jina</s>-fields adorned with banners, arrayed with variegated jewel-nets, with silk pennants and hanging garlands, with jingling nets [sounding with] the voice of the <s>Jina</s>.'

body.text: chatra dharenti tathā-gata-mūrdhne te yatha eka-jinasya karonti | pāṇi-talāt tu a-cintiya-pūjāṃ evam a-śeṣata-sarva-jinānāṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'They hold parasols over the heads of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>; just as they do for one <s>Jina</s>, from the palms of their hands they make inconceivable worship — even so for all the <s>Jinas</s> without exception.'

body.text: eṣa samādhi vikurva ṛṣīṇāṃ te jaga-saṃgraha-jñāna-vikurvā | agra-samādhy-abhinirharamāṇāḥ sarva-kriyā upacāra sukhebhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'This is the <s>samādhi</s>-display of the seers; they are displays of the knowledge that gathers the world. Bringing forth the supreme <s>samādhi</s>, through all activities, services, and comforts'

body.text: satva vinenti upāya-sahasraiḥ ke-ci tathā-gata-pūja-mukhena | dāna a-cinti a-tyāga-mukhena sarva-dhutaṃ-guṇa-śīla-mukhena ||
body.translated_text: 'they discipline beings by thousands of skillful means: some through the means of <s>Tathāgata</s>-worship; [some] through the means of inconceivable, unrelinquished giving; [some] through the means of the moral conduct of all ascetic (<s>dhūta</s>) qualities;'

body.text: a-kṣaya-kṣānti a-kṣobhya-mukhena ke-ci vrataṃ tapa-vīrya-mukhena | dhyāna praśānti vihāra-mukhena sv-artha-viniścaya-prajña-mukhena ||
body.translated_text: 'some through the means of inexhaustible, unshakable patience; some through the means of vows, austerities, and vigor; some through the means of meditation, tranquility, and the [meditative] abodes; some through the means of the wisdom of determining one's own welfare;'

body.text: sarva upāya sahasra-mukhena brahma-vihāra abhijña-mukhena | saṃgraha-vastu hita-eṣi-mukhena puṇya-samuccaya jñāna-mukhena ||
body.translated_text: 'some through the means of thousands of skillful means; through the means of the <s>brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes) and the higher knowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>); through the means of the bases of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>) and benevolent intent; through the means of the accumulation of merit and knowledge;'

body.text: satya-pratītya vimokṣa-mukhena ke-ci bala-indriya-mārga-mukhena | śrāvaka-yāna-vimukti-mukhena pratyaya-yāna-viśuddhi-mukhena ||
body.translated_text: 'some through the means of truth, dependent origination, and liberation; some through the means of the powers, faculties, and the path; some through the means of liberation in the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle; some through the means of purification in the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle;'

body.text: uttama-yāna-vikurva-mukhena ke-cid a-nityata-duṣkha-mukhena | ke-ci nir-ātma-ni-jīva-mukhena a-śubhata saṃjñi-virāga-mukhena ||
body.translated_text: 'some through the means of the displays of the supreme vehicle; some through the means of impermanence and suffering; some through the means of non-self and non-living-being; some through the means of the perception of the impure and dispassion;'

body.text: śānta-nirodha-samādhi-mukhena yātuka carya-mukhā jagatī ye |yātuka dharma-mukhāḥ pratiyantaḥ te tu samanta-vimokṣa-mukhena ||
body.translated_text: 'some through the means of the peaceful <s>nirodha-samādhi</s> (cessation-concentration). Whatever conduct-doors the beings of the world may follow, whatever <s>Dharma</s>-doors they may approach — through the door of universal liberation'

body.text: satva vinenti yathā-āśaya loke ye tu samanta-vimokṣa-mukhena | satva vinenti yathā-āśaya loke teṣa nimitta na śakya grahītuṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'they discipline beings according to their dispositions in the world. Those who [discipline] through the door of universal liberation discipline beings according to their dispositions in the world. Their signs cannot be grasped.'

body.text: kena-cid eṣa samādhi-vikurvāḥ tena ti-vyūhata

children.translated_text: 'the supreme <s>samādhi</s>. Conforming to the ripening of the entire world, with all delights, joy, and elation of the face,'

body.translated_text: 'Through some [particular display], this <s>samādhi</s>-transformation — by that, the three-fold array'

body.text: cintiya darśayi sarva vinenti yatra dur-bhikṣa su-dur-labha sarvaṃ | ye pariṣkāra sukha-āvaha loke tatra ca sarva-bhiprāya-kriyābhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'displaying [things] purposefully, they discipline all. Where there is famine and everything is hard to obtain — whatever requisites bring happiness in the world — there, through activities fulfilling all intentions,'

body.text: dātu dadanti karonti jaga-arthaṃ te vara-bhojana-pāna-rasa-agraiḥ |vastra-nibandhana-ratna-vicitraiḥ rājya-dhana-ātma-priyaiḥ parityāgaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'to those who wish to give, they give and act for the world's welfare, with the finest foods, drinks, and flavors, with various garments, bindings, and jewels, with the relinquishment of kingdoms, wealth, self, and loved ones.'

body.text: dāna-dhimukti jagad vinayanti te vara-lakṣaṇa-citrita-gātrā | uttama ābharaṇā vara-dhīrāḥ mālya-vibhūṣita-gandha-nuliptā ||
body.translated_text: 'Through the resolve for generosity they discipline the world. Those [bodhisattvas], with bodies adorned with supreme marks, wearing the finest ornaments, supremely steadfast, adorned with garlands and anointed with fragrances,'

body.text: rūpa vidarśiya satva vinenti darśana prīti-praharṣa-ratānāṃ | te vara-rūpa-su-rūpa-su-medhāḥ uttama-rūpa nidarśayamānāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'displaying [beautiful] form, they discipline beings — for those who delight in and are attached to the sight [of beauty]. Those of supreme form, beautiful form, and fine intellect, displaying the finest form,'

body.text: rūpa-dhimukti jagad vinayanti te madhuraiḥ kalaviṅka-rutebhī | kokila-haṃsa-kuṇāla-raveṇa dundubhi-kinnara-brahma-rutena deśayi sarva-dhimuktiṣu dharmam ||
body.translated_text: 'through the resolve for form they discipline the world. With sweet songs like the <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird, with the calls of cuckoos, geese, and <s>kuṇāla</s> birds, with the sound of drums, <s>kiṃnaras</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s>'s voice — they teach the <s>Dharma</s> in accordance with all resolves.'

body.text: ye catur eva aśīti sahasrā yebhi jinā jagato * artha karonti | tebhita dharma-prabheda-mukhebhiḥ satva vinenti yathā-āśaya loke ||
body.translated_text: 'Whatever eighty-four thousand [dharma-doors] by which the <s>Jinas</s> serve the world's purpose — through those <s>Dharma</s>-classification doors they discipline beings according to their dispositions in the world.'

body.text: te sukha-duṣkha-sahāya karonti artha-an-artha-sahāyaka bhontī | sarva-kriyāsu sahāya bhavitvā satva vinenti sahāya-mukhena ||
body.translated_text: 'They become companions in happiness and suffering; they become companions in what is beneficial and what is not. Having become companions in all activities, they discipline beings through the door of companionship.'

body.text: duṣkha-upadrava-sat-kṛta-doṣān te tu sahanti sahāya-nidānās | tebhi sahāya sahantiya pīḍāṃ sarva-jagasya hitāya sukhāya ||
body.translated_text: 'They endure the faults of suffering and calamity, honored [by those who come] — on account of [being] companions. Enduring affliction together with those companions, [they act] for the welfare and happiness of all the world.'

body.text: yatra na niṣkramaṇaṃ na ca dharmo jñāyati raṇya-gato na ca mokṣaḥ | tatra tu rājya-samṛddhi-sahāya niṣkrama-śānta-manā a-niketāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Where there is no going forth, where the <s>Dharma</s> is not known, where the forest-dwelling path to liberation [is unknown] — there, endowed with the companionship of royal prosperity, they become ones of peaceful mind who have gone forth, homeless.'

body.text: te gṛha-bandhana-tṛṣṇa-niketāt sarva-jagat-parimocana-hetoḥ | sarvata kāma-ratī a-niketā niṣkrama-moks.a prabhāvayamānāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'For the sake of liberating all the world from the abode of the bondage and craving of household life — homeless from all attachment to sensual pleasures — they manifest the going-forth and liberation.'

body.text: te daśa carya prabhāvayamānā ācari dharma mahā-puruṣāṇāṃ | sarvam a-śeṣata carya ṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvayamāna karonti jaga-arthaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'Manifesting these ten courses of conduct, the conduct of the <s>Dharma</s> of great beings — cultivating the entire conduct of the <s>Ṛṣis</s> (seers) without remainder — they accomplish the purpose of the world.'

body.text: yatr amita-āyuṣa satva bhavantī saukhya-samarpita-manda-kileśāḥ | tatra jarā-ardita vyādhina-pṛṣṭā darśayi mṛtyu-vaśaṃ a-vaśa-ātmā ||
body.translated_text: 'Where beings are of immeasurable lifespan, immersed in pleasure, of feeble afflictions — there they display [themselves as] tormented by old age, afflicted by disease, showing the power of death, with self not in control.'

body.text: rāga-pradīpitu doṣa-pradīptaṃ moha-mahā-agni-pradīpitu lokam | prajvalitaṃ jara-vyādhita-mṛtyu loka nidarśayi satva vinenti ||
body.translated_text: 'The world inflamed with passion, blazing with hatred, ablaze with the great fire of delusion — blazing with old age, disease, and death — they display [this] to the world, and thereby discipline beings.'

body.text: daśa-balaiś catur-vaiśāradyair aṣṭadaśair api dharma-viśeṣaiḥ | buddha-mahā-ātma tu sūcayamānāḥ buddha-guṇebhi karonti jaga-artham ||
body.translated_text: 'Manifesting the <s>Buddha</s>'s great nature through the ten powers, the four [types of] fearlessness, and the eighteen special <s>dharmas</s> — they accomplish the purpose of the world through the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>.'

body.text: te ca adeśa ṛddhy-anuśāstī rūpa-dhiṣṭhāna-balena samantāt | darśayamāna tathā-gata ṛddhī ṛddhi-vikurvita satva vinenti ||
body.translated_text: 'And in that [realm], [they employ] the instruction of miraculous power, by the force of the superimposition of forms everywhere — displaying the miracles of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, they discipline beings through miraculous transformations.'

body.text: te vividhehi upāya-nayehi loka-vicāri karonti jaga-arthaṃ | loki a-lipta jale yatha padmaṃ prīti-prasāda-karā vicaranti ||
body.translated_text: 'Through various skillful means and methods, they wander in the world and accomplish the purpose of the world. Unstained by the world, like a lotus in water, they move about, producing joy and faith.'

body.text: kāvya-karāḥ kavi-rāja bhavantī te naṭa-nartaka jhallaka-mallāḥ | utkuṭa-śobhika-hāraka-nṛtyā māya-karāḥ pṛthu rūpa-nidarśī ||
body.translated_text: 'They become poets, master poets; they become actors, dancers, jesters, wrestlers — acrobats, jugglers, tumblers, dancers — and great magicians, displaying manifold forms.'

body.text: grāmika nāyaka sārathi bhontī sa-arthika śreṣṭhika gṛha-pati bhonti | rāja amātya puro-hita-dūtā vaidya-viśārada-śāstra-vidhi-jñāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'They become village-chiefs, leaders, charioteers; they become caravan-leaders, guild-masters, householders; kings, ministers, court-priests, ambassadors — physicians, skilled healers, knowers of the rules of the sciences.'

body.text: te aṭavīṣu mahā-druma bhontī auṣadha a-kṣaya-ratna-nidhānāḥ | cinta-maṇi druma kāma-dadāś ca deśika utpatha-mārga-gatānāṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'In the forests, they become great trees, inexhaustible medicines, and storehouses of treasures — wish-fulfilling gems and wish-granting trees — and guides for those who have lost the right path.'

body.text: arcciya santu tu loka viditvā karma-vidhīṣu a-jānaka satvāḥ | te kṛṣi-karma-prayoga-vaṇijyā śilpi-vicitra prabhāvayi loke ||
body.translated_text: 'Having understood that beings in the world are worthy of honor and yet ignorant of the rules of <s>karma</s> — they manifest in the world agriculture, craftsmanship, and commerce, and various arts.'

body.text: ye a-viheṭha a-hiṃsa-prayogaḥ sarva-sukha-āvaha-vijña-praśastāḥ | vidya-bala-auṣadhi śāstra-vicitrāḥ sarva prabhāvita tebhi ṛṣībhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Those who are non-harming, of non-violent practice, praised by the wise as bringing all happiness — various kinds of knowledge, powers, medicines, and sciences — all are manifested by those seers.'

body.text: ye ṛṣiṇāṃ caraṇāḥ parama-agrā yatra + adhimukta sa-devaku lokaḥ | ye vrata-duṣ-kara ye tapa-śreṣṭhāḥ sarvi prabhāvita tebhi vidūbhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Whatever supreme and foremost practices of the seers in which the world with its gods has faith — whatever difficult vows, whatever excellent austerities — all are manifested by those wise ones.'

body.text: te carakāḥ parivrājaka tīrthyāḥ tāpasa-gotama-mona-carāṇām | nagna acela-guru-śramaṇānāṃ tīrthika ācaryā hi bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: 'They become wanderers, mendicants, and sectarians — teachers of ascetics, <s>Gautamas</s>, silent sages, <s>Jainas</s>, unclothed renunciants, and great <s>śramaṇas</s>.'

body.text: te tu ajīvika dharma-carāṇāṃ uttarikāṇa an-uttarikāṇāṃ | dīrgha-jaṭāna kumāra-vratānāṃ teṣv api ācaryā hi bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: 'And they become teachers of <s>Ājīvikas</s>, practitioners of <s>dharma</s>, of those with and without upper garments, of the long-haired, and of those who practice the vow of celibacy.'

body.text: sūrya-nuvartaka-pañca-tapānāṃ kukkura-go-vratikā mṛga-caryā | cārika tīrthya daśa tritayānāṃ teṣv api ācaryā hi bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: 'Of sun-worshippers, of those who practice the five-fire austerity, of dog-vow and cow-vow practitioners and deer-conduct ascetics, of wandering sectarians practicing the three-decade [vow] — in all these too they become teachers.'

body.text: devata-jñāna-praveśa-ratānāṃ tīrth-upadarśana-deśa-carāṇāṃ | mūla-phala-ambu-carā api bhūtvā dharma a-cintiya te parama-agrāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Of those who delight in entering the knowledge of deities, of those who wander to sacred fords and [pilgrimage] sites — they also become subsisting on roots, fruits, and water, [teaching] the inconceivable <s>Dharma</s>, supreme and foremost.'

body.text: utkuṭa-sthāyina eka-carāṇāṃ kaṇṭaka-bhasma-tṛṇa-śśayanānāṃ | ye muṣale-śaya

children.text: yukti-vihārī teṣv api ācaryā hi bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: and dwell in disciplined practice — in all these too they become teachers.'

body.translated_text: 'Of those who stand in the squatting posture, of solitary wanderers, of those who sleep on thorns, ashes, and grass — of those who sleep on pestles

body.text: yāvata bāhirakāḥ pṛthu-tīrthyā āśaya teṣv adhimukti samīkṣya | tīkṣṇa-dur-āsada-ugra-tapebhī tīrthika duṣkha-prahāṇa vinenti ||
body.translated_text: 'However many the various external sectarians — having examined the dispositions and the faiths in them, through sharp, unapproachable, and fierce austerities they discipline the sectarians to abandon suffering.'

body.text: dṛṣṭi-samākula loke viditvā sarva-ku-dṛṣṭi-samāśrita tīrthyāḥ | sūkṣma-padebhir upāyana yebhī satya-prakāśana teṣu karonti ||
body.translated_text: 'Having understood that the world is confused by [wrong] views, that the sectarians are attached to all wrong views — through subtle approaches by which they reveal the truth to them.'

body.text: keṣu-ci drāmiḍa-mantra-padebhī deśayi satya su-gupta-padebhiḥ | keṣu uja .. vyakta-padebhiḥ keṣu-cid eva rahasya-padebhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'To some, through <s>Drāmiḍa</s>-<s>mantra</s> words, they teach the truth through well-guarded words. To some through direct and clear words; to some through secret words.'

body.text: keṣu-ci akṣara-bheda-padebhiḥ artha-viniścaya-vajra-padebhiḥ | vādi-pramardana-jñāna-padebhiḥ śāstra-a-dharmaka-mokṣa-padebhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'To some through words that distinguish syllables; through words that are adamantine in determining meaning; through words of knowledge that crush [opposing] disputants; through words of liberation in treatises and doctrines.'

body.text: keṣu-ci mānuṣa-mantra-padebhiḥ sarva-praveśa-nirukti-padeṣu | keṣu-ci deva-nirukti-padebhiḥ nāga-niruktita yakṣa-padebhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'To some through human <s>mantra</s>-words; through all approaches in etymological explanations; to some through the etymology-words of <s>devas</s>; through <s>Nāga</s>-language and <s>Yakṣa</s>-words.'

body.text: rākṣasa-atha-gandharva-padebhiḥ bhūta-kumbhāṇḍa-mahā-ura-gakebhiḥ | kiṃnara-apsara-garuḍa-padebhiḥ satya-prakāśana-mokṣ-upanenti ||
body.translated_text: 'Through the words of <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Bhūtas</s>, <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, and great <s>Uragas</s>; through words of <s>Kiṃnaras</s>, <s>Apsarases</s>, and <s>Garuḍas</s> — they lead [beings] to the revelation of truth and liberation.'

body.text: te yatha-satya nirukti-vidhi-jñā evam a-śeṣata ye jina-dharmā | dharmam a-cintiya vākya-patha-jñā deśayi eṣa samādhi-vikurvā ||
body.translated_text: 'Those who know the method of etymology as it truly is — thus, without exception, all the <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>Jinas</s> — knowing the inconceivable <s>Dharma</s> and the path of speech, they teach this through the transformation of <s>samādhi</s>.'

body.text: te jaga-saukhyata agra-samādhī sarva-jage abhinirharamānā | raśmim a-cintiyam utsṛjamānā raśmi pramuñciya satva vinenti ||
body.translated_text: 'Bringing forth for the world's happiness the supreme <s>samādhi</s>, manifesting it throughout all the world — emitting inconceivable rays, they release rays and thereby discipline beings.'

body.text: raśmi pramuñciya darśayamānā yāvata satva vijānita raśmi | teṣu su-darśana bhoti a-mogham hetu an-uttari jñāna-varasya ||
body.translated_text: 'Releasing rays and displaying [them], however many beings perceive those rays — for them the seeing is not in vain: it becomes the cause of unsurpassed, supreme knowledge.'

body.text: darśayi buddha vidarśayi dharmaṃ saṃgha nidarśayi mārga narāṇām | darśayi cetika te jina-bimbā tena su-darśana-raśmi nivṛttā ||
body.translated_text: 'They display the <s>Buddha</s>, they reveal the <s>Dharma</s>, they show the <s>Saṃgha</s>, they demonstrate the path to humankind. They display <s>caityas</s> and images of the <s>Jinas</s> — thereby that ray of auspicious vision is accomplished.'

body.text: raśmi pramuñci prabhaṃ-kara nāmā yā prabha jihma karoti marūṇāṃ | sarva-rajaṃ ca tamaṃ ca hanitvā so prabha bhāsati loka-hitānāṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'They release a ray called <s>prabhāṃkara</s> (light-maker), that radiance which humbles [the glory] of the <s>Marus</s> (<s>devas</s>). Having destroyed all dust and darkness, that radiance shines for the benefit of the world.'

body.text: tāya prabhāsaya codita satvās te jina-pūja-pradīpa dharentī | te jina-pūja-pradīpa dharitvā loka-pradīpa-karā jina bhonti ||
body.translated_text: 'Beings, illumined and inspired by that radiance, maintain the lamp of <s>Jina</s>-worship. Having maintained the lamp of <s>Jina</s>-worship, they become world-illuminating <s>Jinas</s>.'

body.text: taila-pradīpa ghṛtasya pradīpā dāru tṛṇā naḍa-veṇu pradīpān | gandha-rasāyana-ratna-pradīpān datva jineṣu prabhaṃ-kara labdhāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'By giving oil-lamps, ghee-lamps, lamps of wood, grass, reed, and bamboo, lamps of fragrance, elixir, and jewels to the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>prabhāṃkara</s> [ray] is obtained.'

body.text: raśmi pramuñciya pratāraṇi nāmā tāya prabhāsaya codita satvāḥ | ... nāva-pratāraṇi-nadya-patheṣu | dūṣita saṃskṛta varṇita śāntī tena pratāraṇi raśmi nivṛttā ||
body.translated_text: 'They release a ray called <s>pratāraṇī</s> (one that causes crossing). Beings, illumined and inspired by that radiance — [provide] boats and ferries on river-crossings. Having shown the impurity of the conditioned and praised peace — thereby the <s>pratāraṇī</s> ray is accomplished.'

body.text: raśmi pipāsa-vinodani nāmā tāya prabhāsaya codita satvāḥ | kāma-guṇeṣu tṛṣāṃ prajahitvā dharma-vimukti-rasa-arthika bhonti ||
body.translated_text: 'A ray called <s>pipāsa-vinodanī</s> (thirst-removing) — beings illumined and inspired by that radiance, having abandoned thirst for the objects of sensual pleasure, become seekers of the flavor of liberation through the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: kāma-guṇeṣu tṛṣāṃ prajahitvā dharma-vimukti-rasa-arthika bhūtvā | buddha bhavanty a-mṛtaṃ-jala-varṣī tṛṣṇa-pipāsa-vinodana loke ||
body.translated_text: 'Having abandoned thirst for the objects of sensual pleasure, having become seekers of the flavor of liberation through the <s>Dharma</s>, they become <s>Buddhas</s> who rain the water of the deathless, removing thirst and craving in the world.'

body.text: puṣkariṇī nadi-kūpa-taḍāgā utsaya kārita bodhi-nidānāḥ | kāma vivarṇita varṇita-dhyānā tṛṣṇa-vinodani tena nivṛttā ||
body.translated_text: 'Pools, rivers, wells, and reservoirs, springs made for the cause of awakening — having deprecated sensual pleasures and praised <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) — thereby the <s>tṛṣṇā-vinodanī</s> [ray] is accomplished.'

body.text: prīti-karī yada raśmi pramuñcī tāya prabhāsaya codita satvāḥ | prīti-phuṭā vara-bodhi-nidānaṃ cinta janenti bhaviṣya svayaṃ-bhū ||
