body.translated_text: 'When a ray called <s>prīti-karī</s> (joy-maker) is released — beings illumined and inspired by that radiance, suffused with joy, the cause of supreme awakening, generate the thought: "We shall become <s>Svayaṃbhūs</s> (self-arisen [Buddhas])."'

body.text: lakṣaṇa-maṇḍita padma-niṣaṇṇā yat kṛta-vigraha kāruṇikānāṃ | bhāṣita buddha-guṇāḥ sada kālaṃ prīti-karī prabha tena nivṛttā ||
body.translated_text: 'Having fashioned images of the compassionate ones, adorned with marks and seated on lotuses — having proclaimed the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities at all times — thereby the <s>prīti-karī</s> radiance is accomplished.'

body.text: raśmi pramuñci ratiṃ-kara nāmā tāya prabhāsaya bodhita satvā | buddha-ratī-rata dharma-ratī-rata saṃgha-ratī-rata te sada bhonti ||
body.translated_text: 'They release a ray called <s>ratiṃkara</s> (delight-maker). Beings illumined and awakened by that radiance become always delighted in the <s>Buddha</s>, delighted in the <s>Dharma</s>, delighted in the <s>Saṃgha</s>.'

body.text: tritaya-ratī-rata te sada bhūtvā buddha-samāgama-dharma-gaṇa-ārye | labdha-nupattika-kṣānti labhanti codita smārita ye bahu satvā ||
body.translated_text: 'Having always become delighted in the Three [Jewels], [delighted in] the encounter with the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the Noble <s>Saṃgha</s> — the many beings who are inspired and reminded obtain the <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>).'

body.text: buddha-anusmṛti-dharma-gaṇa-ārye bodhi ya citta-guṇān vivaritvā | tena ratiṃ-kara raśmi nivṛttā ||
body.translated_text: 'Having expanded the <s>Buddha</s>-recollection, the <s>Dharma</s>, the Noble <s>Saṃgha</s>, and the qualities of <s>bodhicitta</s> — thereby the <s>ratiṃkara</s> ray is accomplished.'

body.text: puṇya-samuccaya-raśmi pramuñcī tāya prabhāsaya codita satvā | dānu dadanti vicitram an-ekaṃ prārthayamānu an-uttaru bodhiṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'They release the <s>puṇya-samuccaya</s> (merit-accumulation) ray. Beings illumined and inspired by that radiance give manifold and various gifts, aspiring for unsurpassed awakening.'

body.text: āśaya pūritu yācanakānāṃ yajña nir-argaḍa tair yajamānaiḥ | sarva-bhiprāyata dānu daditvā puṇya-samuccaya raśmi nivṛttā ||
body.translated_text: 'Having fulfilled the wishes of supplicants, making offerings without restraint by those performers of worship — having given gifts fulfilling all intentions — the <s>puṇya-samuccaya</s> ray is thereby accomplished.'

body.text: jñānavatī yada raśmi pramuñcī tāya prabhāsaya codita satvāḥ | eka tu dharma mukhātu an-ekā dharma-mukhān avabuddhi kṣaṇena ||
body.translated_text: 'When a ray called <s>jñānavatī</s> (knowledge-bearing) is released — beings illumined and inspired by that radiance comprehend from a single <s>Dharma</s>-door many <s>Dharma</s>-doors in an instant.'

body.text: dharma-prabheda ... grāhita satvān artha-viniścaya jñāna vibhaktī | dharma-pada-artha-vibhāṣaṇa kṛtvā jñānavatī prabha tena nivṛttā ||
body.translated_text: 'Having made beings grasp the distinctions of the <s>Dharma</s>, the division of the knowledge of determination of meaning — having expounded the words and meanings of the <s>Dharma</s> — thereby the <s>jñānavatī</s> radiance is accomplished.'

body.text: prajña-pradīpaya osari raśmi tāya prabhāsaya codita satvāḥ | śūnya ni-satva a-jāta-vipannān otari dharma a-bhāva-sva-bhāvān | māya-marīci-samā daka-candra-svapna-samān pratibimba-samān vā | dharma a-svāmika śūnya nir-īhān bhāṣati prajña-pradīpa nivṛttā ||
body.translated_text: 'A ray enters for the lamp of wisdom (<s>prajñā-pradīpa</s>). Beings illumined and inspired by that radiance — [perceiving] <s>dharmas</s> that are empty, without a being, unborn and unperishing — enter <s>dharmas</s> whose own-nature is non-existence. Like illusion, like a mirage, like the moon in water, like a dream, like a reflection — they proclaim <s>dharmas</s> as ownerless, empty, without striving — and the <s>prajñā-pradīpa</s> [ray] is accomplished.'

body.text: dharma-vikurvaṇi raśmi pramuñcī tāya prabhāsaya codita satvā | dhāraṇi a-kṣaya-koṣu labhitvā sarva-tathā-gata-koṣu labhenti ||
body.translated_text: 'They release the <s>dharma-vikurvaṇī</s> (Dharma-transformation) ray. Beings illumined and inspired by that radiance, having obtained the inexhaustible treasury of <s>dhāraṇī</s>, obtain the treasuries of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

body.text: dharma-dharāṇu parigrahu kṛtvā dhārmika-rakṣa karitva ṛṣīṇāṃ | dharma anugraha kṛtva jagasya dharma-vikurvaṇi raśmi nivṛttā ||
body.translated_text: 'Having undertaken the custody of the <s>Dharma</s>-bearers, having performed the protection of the righteous seers, having rendered the grace of the <s>Dharma</s> to the world — the <s>dharma-vikurvaṇī</s> ray is thereby accomplished.'

body.text: tyāgavatī yada raśmi vimuñcī tāya ya matsara codita satvā | jñātvā a-nitya a-śāśvata-bhogān tyāga-ratī-rata te sada bhonti ||
body.translated_text: 'When a ray called <s>tyāgavatī</s> (full of generosity) is released — beings afflicted by avarice, illumined by that radiance, having known enjoyments to be impermanent and non-eternal, become always delighted in generosity.'

body.text: matsara-dur-dama satva a-dāntā jñātva dhanaṃ supina-abhra-sva-bhāvaṃ | bṛṃhita tyāga prasannam anena tyāgavatī-prabha tena nivṛttā ||
body.translated_text: 'Beings hard-to-tame and undisciplined through avarice, having known wealth to be of the nature of a dream and a cloud — generosity is nourished and made serene by this — thereby the <s>tyāgavatī</s> radiance is accomplished.'

body.text: niṣ-paridāha ya osari raśmiḥ tāya duḥ-śīlaya codita satvā | śīla-viśuddhi pratiṣṭhita bhūtvā cinta janenti bhaveya svayaṃ-bhūḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'A ray enters called <s>niṣparidāha</s> (non-burning). Beings of bad moral conduct, illumined by that radiance, become established in the purity of moral conduct and generate the thought: "May I become a <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> (self-arisen <s>Buddha</s>)."'

body.text: karma-pathe kuśale pariśuddhe śīla samādayi yad bahu-satvān | bodhayi citta samādayanena raśmi nivṛtta sa niṣ-paridāhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'When many beings are made to undertake morality in the wholesome courses of <s>karma</s>, purified — having awakened their minds through this undertaking — that <s>niṣparidāha</s> ray is accomplished.'

body.text: kṣānti-viyūha ya osari raśmi tāya ya a-kṣama codita satvāḥ | krodha-khilaṃ adhimāna jahitvā kṣānti-ratī-rata te sada bhonti ||
body.translated_text: 'A ray enters called <s>kṣānti-viyūha</s> (patience-array). Beings who are impatient, illumined by that radiance, having abandoned the hardness of anger and the conceit of pride, become always delighted in patience.'

body.text: duḥ-kṛta kṣānti apāya-matīnāṃ citta a-kṣobhita bodhi-nidānaṃ | varṇita kṣānti-guṇāḥ sada-kālaṃ tena nivṛtta sa kṣānti-viyūhā ||
body.translated_text: 'The patience of wrongdoing toward those of low disposition — the mind unshaken, the cause of awakening — having praised the qualities of patience at all times — thereby that <s>kṣānti-viyūha</s> [ray] is accomplished.'

body.text: raśmi uttaptavatī yada muñcī tāya kuśīdaya codita satvāḥ | yukta prayukta triṣū rataneṣu pūja karonti a-khinna-prayogāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'When a ray called <s>uttaptavatī</s> (refined one) is released — beings who are lazy, illumined by that radiance, become devoted and yoked to the Three Jewels and make worship with unflagging effort.'

body.text: yukta prayukta triṣū rataneṣu pūja karitva a-khinna-prayogāḥ | te catu māra-pathā atikrāntāḥ kṣipra spṛśanti an-uttara bodhiṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'Devoted and yoked to the Three Jewels, having made worship with unflagging effort — they transcend the paths of the four <s>Māras</s> and swiftly touch unsurpassed awakening.'

body.text: vīrya samādayi yad bahu-satvān pūja karitva triṣū rataneṣu | dharma dharitva kṣayaṃ-gata kāle tena utaptavatī prabha labdhā ||
body.translated_text: 'When many beings are made to undertake vigor, having performed worship of the Three Jewels — having maintained the <s>Dharma</s> in the time of decline — thereby the <s>uttaptavatī</s> radiance is obtained.'

body.text: śānti-karī yada raśmi pramuñcī tāya vibhrāntaya codita satvāḥ | teṣu na rāgu na dveṣa na mohāḥ bodhita bhonti samāhita cittāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'When a ray called <s>śānti-karī</s> (peace-maker) is released — beings who are confused, illumined by that radiance — in them there is no passion, no hatred, no delusion; awakened, they become ones of composed mind.'

body.text: pāpa ku-mitra kiliṣṭa carīye saṃgaṇikā-vinivartana kṛtvā |varṇita dhyāna praśānta araṇye śānti-karī prabha tena nivṛttā ||
body.translated_text: 'Having turned away from evil companions, defiled conduct, and association with crowds — having praised meditation, peaceful, in the forest — thereby the <s>śānti-karī</s> radiance is accomplished.'

body.text: prajña-viyūha ya osari raśmī tāya duḥ-prajña saṃcodita satvāḥ | satya-pratītya vimokṣanaye asmin nidriya jñāna-gatiṃ gata bhonti ||
body.translated_text: 'A ray enters called <s>prajñā-viyūha</s> (wisdom-array). Beings of poor wisdom, aroused by that radiance — in this method of truth, dependent origination, and liberation — become ones who have gone to the course of knowledge, with faculties [fully developed].'

body.text: indriya-jñāna-gatiṃ gata bhūtvā ... | sūrya-pradīpa-samādhi labhitvā prajña-prabhāsa-karā jina bhonti ||
body.translated_text: 'Having become ones who have gone to the course of faculty-knowledge — having obtained the <s>sūrya-pradīpa-samādhi</s> (sun-lamp concentration) — they become <s>Jinas</s> who make the light of wisdom shine.'

body.text: rājya-dhana-ātma-priyaiḥ parityāgaiḥ dharma ya mārgita bodhi-nidānaṃ | taṃ ca sat-kṛtya prakāśiya dharmaṃ raśmi nivṛtta sa prajña-viyūhāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Through renunciation of kingdom, wealth, self, and loved ones, <s>Dharma</s> was sought as the cause of <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening); having honored and illuminated that <s>Dharma</s>, the ray called <s>Prajñā-vyūha</s> (array of wisdom) returned.

body.text: buddhavatī yada raśmi pramuñcī tāya prabhāya saṃcodita satvāḥ | buddha sahasra an-eka a-cintyān paśyiṣu padma-vaneṣu niṣaṇṇān ||
body.translated_text: When the ray called <s>Buddhavatī</s> (possessing Buddhas) is released, beings impelled by its radiance behold thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, innumerable and inconceivable, seated in lotus groves.

body.text: buddha-mahā-ātmata buddha-vimokṣā bhāsita buddha-vikurva an-antā | buddha-bala-avi-prabhāvana kṛtvā buddhavatī prabha tena nivṛttā ||
body.translated_text: The greatness of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>-liberations, the infinite <s>Buddha</s>-transformations were proclaimed; having displayed the power of the <s>Buddha</s>-strengths, the radiance called <s>Buddhavatī</s> thereby returned.

body.text: te * a-bhayaṃ-dada raśmi pramuñcī tāya + a-bhaya-ardita satva sa-spṛṣṭāḥ | bhūta-graha-avadha-tāḍana-bandhe mucyiṣu sarv-upasarga-bhayebhyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The ray called <s>Abhayaṃdadā</s> (giving fearlessness) is released; beings touched by its radiance, afflicted by fear, are freed from all dangers — seizure by spirits, slaughter, beating, and bondage.

body.text: ye a-bhayena nimantrita satvāḥ prāṇi-badhāt tu nivārita bhonti | trāyita yac-charaṇa-āgata bhītās tena bhayaṃ-dada raśmi nivṛttā ||
body.translated_text: Those beings who were invited with fearlessness, who were restrained from killing living creatures, who were protected when frightened beings came for refuge — by that, the ray called <s>Bhayaṃdadā</s> (giving fearlessness) returned.

body.text: sarva-sukha-āvaha osari raśmī tāya gilānaya ātura spṛṣṭāḥ | sarvata vyādhi-dukhāt pratimuktā dhyāna-samādhi-sukhāni labhanti ||
body.translated_text: The ray called <s>Sarva-sukhāvahā</s> (bringing all happiness) shines forth; touched by it, the sick and afflicted are completely freed from the suffering of all diseases and obtain the bliss of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration).

body.text: roga-vinodani mūla phal-oṣadha ratna rasāyana gandh-anulepān | phāṇita kṣīra madhū ghṛta telān bhojana pāna daditvaya labdhā ||
body.translated_text: Having given and obtained medicines of roots, fruits, and herbs that dispel disease, jewels, elixirs, fragrant ointments, sugar, milk, honey, ghee, oil, food, and drink,

body.text: buddha-nidarśani raśmi pramuñcī tāya sa-codita āyu kṣayānte | buddha anusmari paśyiṣu buddham te cyuta gacchi sa-buddha-kkṣetraṃ ||
body.translated_text: the ray called <s>Buddha-nidarśanī</s> (showing the Buddha) is released; impelled by it, those at the end of their lifespan, recollecting the <s>Buddha</s>, behold the <s>Buddha</s>, and upon death they go to a <s>Buddha-kṣetra</s> (Buddha-field).

body.text: kāla karonti ca smārita buddhā darśita-prīta-karā jina-bimbān | buddha-gatāḥ śaraṇaṃ maraṇa-ante bhāsiya buddha-nidarśani labdhā ||
body.translated_text: They die remembering the <s>Buddhas</s>, shown the joy-producing images of the <s>Jinas</s> (victors); having gone to the <s>Buddha</s> as refuge at the time of death, the radiance called <s>Buddha-nidarśanī</s> was obtained.

body.text: dharma-prabhāvani raśmi pramuñcī tāya prabhāya saṃcodita satvā | dharma paṭhanti śṛṇvanti likhantī dharma-ratī rata te sada bhonti ||
body.translated_text: The ray called <s>Dharma-prabhāvanī</s> (glorifying the Dharma) is released; beings impelled by its radiance recite, hear, and write the <s>Dharma</s>, and they are always devoted to delight in the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: |dharma-dur-bhikṣaya dyotitu dharmo dharma-gaveṣiṇa pūrita āśā | chanda janitva prayujyatha dharme bhāṣata dharma-prabhāvani labdhā ||
body.translated_text: In times of <s>Dharma</s>-famine, the <s>Dharma</s> is illuminated; the aspirations of <s>Dharma</s>-seekers are fulfilled; having generated zeal and being engaged in the <s>Dharma</s>, the radiance called <s>Dharma-prabhāvanī</s> is proclaimed.

body.text: ghoṣavatī yada raśmi pramuñcī buddha-sutā paricodanatāyāṃ | yātuka śabda-pracāru tri-loke sarva tathā-gata-ghoṣa śṛṇvanti ||
body.translated_text: When the ray called <s>Ghoṣavatī</s> (possessing sound) is released, for the exhortation of the sons of the <s>Buddha</s>, a proclamation of sound goes forth in the three worlds, and all hear the voice of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

body.text: ucca svareṇa stavanti maha-rṣīn tūrya-mahattara-ghaṇṭa-pradānaiḥ | sarva-jage jina-ghoṣa-ruta-arthaṃ niścari ghoṣavatī prabha-labdhā ||
body.translated_text: With loud voices they praise the great sages, with offerings of supreme musical instruments and bells; throughout all the world, for the purpose of the <s>Jina</s>'s (victor's) voiced message, the radiance called <s>Ghoṣavatī</s> shines forth, having been obtained.

body.text: te * a-mṛtaṃ-dada raśmi pramuñcī tāya prabhāsaya codita satvāḥ | sarva pramāda ciraṃ prajahitvā sarva-guṇaiḥ pratipadyati yogaṃ ||
body.translated_text: The ray called <s>Amṛtaṃdadā</s> (giving the deathless) is released; beings impelled by its radiance, having long abandoned all heedlessness, attain <s>yoga</s> (spiritual union) through all virtues.

body.text: duṣkha an-eka upadrava-pūrṇaṃ bhāṣita saṃskṛta nityam a-kṣemaṃ | śānti-nirodha-sukhaṃ sada kṣemaṃ bhāṣayatā a-mṛtaṃ-dada labdhā ||
body.translated_text: Having declared the conditioned to be filled with manifold suffering and calamity, always unsafe, and having proclaimed the bliss of <s>śānti</s> (peace) and <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) as always safe — by that, the ray <s>Amṛtaṃdadā</s> was obtained.

body.text: raśmi viśeṣavatī yada muñcī tāya prabhāsaya codita satvāḥ | śīla-viśeṣa samādhi-viśeṣaṃ prajña-viśeṣa śṛṇonti jinānāṃ ||
body.translated_text: When the ray called <s>Viśeṣavatī</s> (possessing distinction) is released, beings impelled by its radiance hear of the distinction of <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), the distinction of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and the distinction of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) of the <s>Jinas</s> (victors).

body.text: śīlata agra samādhita agro prajñata agra mahā-muni-rājā | ya stuta varṇita bodhi-nidānaṃ tena viśeṣavatī prabha labdhā ||
body.translated_text: Supreme in <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), supreme in <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), supreme in <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) — the great king of sages, who was praised and extolled as the cause of <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening) — by that, the radiance <s>Viśeṣavatī</s> was obtained.

body.text: ratna-viyūha ya osari raśmi tāya prabhāsaya codita satvāḥ | akṣara ratna-nidhāna labhitvā pūjayi ratna-varebhi maha-rṣīn ||
body.translated_text: The ray called <s>Ratna-vyūha</s> (array of jewels) shines forth; beings impelled by its radiance, having obtained inexhaustible jewel-treasures, worship the great sages with the finest jewels.

body.text: ratna-visarga jine jina-stūpe saṃgrahi kṛtsna-janaṃ ratanebhiḥ | ratna-pradāna karitva jinānāṃ raśmi nivṛtta ya ratna-viyūhāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Having made jewel-offerings to the <s>Jinas</s> (victors) and <s>Jina</s>-<s>stūpas</s>, having gathered all people through jewels, and having made jewel-gifts to the <s>Jinas</s>, the ray called <s>Ratna-vyūha</s> returned.

body.text: gandha-prabhāsa ya osari raśmī tāya prabhāsaya codita satvāḥ | ghrātvā a-mānuṣa gandha mano-jñān buddha-guṇe niyutāni bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: The ray called <s>Gandha-prabhāsā</s> (fragrance-radiance) shines forth; beings impelled by its radiance, having smelled superhuman and delightful fragrances, become devoted to the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: gandh-anulepanu-mānuṣa-divyair

children.text: yat kṛta pūja nara-adhipatīnāṃ | gandha-mayān jina-vigraha-stūpān kṛtva nivṛtta su-gandha-prabhāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: having made worship of the lords among men, and having fashioned <s>Jina</s>-images and <s>stūpas</s> made of fragrance — the radiance <s>Sugandha-prabhāsa</s> (beautiful fragrance-radiance) returned.

body.translated_text: With superhuman and divine fragrant ointments,

body.text: muñcati raśmi vicitra-viyūhān indra-patāka-dhvaja-agra vicitrān | tūrya-ninādita-gandha-pradhūpita śobhi-sura-uttama-puṣpa-vikīrṇaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Rays of variegated arrays are released — splendid with banners of <s>Indra</s>, pennants, and flagstaffs, resounding with music, perfumed with incense, adorned and strewn with the finest celestial flowers.

body.text: tūrya-pratyudgami pūja-jinānāṃ puṣpa-vilepana-dhūpana-cūrṇaiḥ | chattra-dhvaja-agra-patāka-vitānais tena vicitra-viyūha nivṛttāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Having worshipped the <s>Jinas</s> (victors) with musical welcomes, flowers, ointments, incense, and powders, with parasols, banners, flagstaffs, pennants, and canopies — by that, the rays called <s>Vicitra-vyūha</s> (variegated array) returned.

body.text: raśmi prasāda-karī yada muñcī pāṇi-tala-upama saṃsthihi bhūmiḥ | śodhayato ṛṣi āśrama-stūpān tena prasāda-karī prabha labdhā ||
body.translated_text: When the ray called <s>Prasāda-karī</s> (producing serenity) is released, the ground becomes smooth as the palm of a hand; by purifying the hermitages and <s>stūpas</s> of the sages, the radiance <s>Prasāda-karī</s> was obtained.

body.text: muñcati meghavatī yada raśmiṃ saṃsthihi gandha pravarṣati meghaṃ | stūpa vara-aṅgaṇa-gandha-jalena + āsiñciya meghavatī prabha labdhā ||
body.translated_text: When the ray called <s>Meghavatī</s> (possessing clouds) is released, a cloud forms and rains down fragrance; by sprinkling the <s>stūpas</s> and excellent courtyards with fragrant water, the radiance <s>Meghavatī</s> was obtained.

body.text: bhūṣaṇa-vyūha pramuñcatu raśmīn nagna acela su-bhūṣaṇa bhontī | vastra-nibandhana-hāra-vicitraṃ datva vibhūṣaṇa raśmi nivṛttā ||
body.translated_text: Releasing the rays called <s>Bhūṣaṇa-vyūha</s> (array of ornaments), the naked and unclothed become beautifully adorned; having given garments, bindings, variegated necklaces, and ornaments, the ray returned.

body.text: raśmi rasa-agravatī yada muñcī bhukṣita bhojya rasa-agra labhantī | bhojana pāna vicitra rasa-agrān datva rasa-agravatī prabha labdhā ||
body.translated_text: When the ray called <s>Rasa-agravatī</s> (possessing the finest flavors) is released, the hungry obtain the finest food and flavors; having given food, drink, and variegated finest flavors, the radiance <s>Rasa-agravatī</s> was obtained.

body.text: artha-nidarśani muñcati raśmīn ratna-nidhāna labhanti daridrāḥ | a-kṣaya-ratna-nidhiṃ tribhi ratnair dānata artha-nidarśani labdhā ||
body.translated_text: The ray called <s>Artha-nidarśanī</s> (showing wealth) releases its rays; the poor obtain jewel-treasures; through giving inexhaustible jewel-treasures by means of the three jewels, the radiance <s>Artha-nidarśanī</s> was obtained.

body.text: cakṣu-viśodhani muñcati raśmīn andha tadā dṛśi rūpa vicitram | dīpa-pradāna jine jina-stūpe cakṣu-viśodhani raśmi nivṛttā ||
body.translated_text: The ray called <s>Cakṣu-viśodhanī</s> (purifying the eye) releases its rays; the blind then see variegated forms; through the offering of lamps to the <s>Jinas</s> and <s>Jina</s>-<s>stūpas</s>, the ray <s>Cakṣu-viśodhanī</s> returned.

body.text: śrotra-viśodhani muñcati raśmīn śrotra-vihīna śruṇī pṛthu-śabdān | vādya-pradāna-jine jina-stūpe śrotra-viśodhani raśmi nivṛttā ||
body.translated_text: The ray called <s>Śrotra-viśodhanī</s> (purifying the ear) releases its rays; the deaf hear abundant sounds; through the offering of music to the <s>Jinas</s> and <s>Jina</s>-<s>stūpas</s>, the ray <s>Śrotra-viśodhanī</s> returned.

body.text: ghrāṇa-viśodhani muñcati raśmīn ghrāyi a-ghrāyita-pūrva su-gandhān | gandha-pradāna jine jina-stūpe ghrāṇa-viśodhani raśmi nivṛttā ||
body.translated_text: The ray called <s>Ghrāṇa-viśodhanī</s> (purifying the nose) releases its rays; they smell fragrances never smelled before; through the offering of incense to the <s>Jinas</s> and <s>Jina</s>-<s>stūpas</s>, the ray <s>Ghrāṇa-viśodhanī</s> returned.

body.text: jihva-viśodhani muñcati raśmīn snigdha-mano-jña-rutai stuti buddhān | vāca dur-ukta vivarjita rukṣā ślakṣṇa udīrita raśmi nivṛttā ||
body.translated_text: The ray called <s>Jihvā-viśodhanī</s> (purifying the tongue) releases its rays; they praise the <s>Buddhas</s> with smooth and delightful speech; harsh and rough speech is abandoned, and with gentle utterance, the ray returned.

body.text: kāya-viśodhani muñcati raśmīn indriya-hīna su-indriya bhonti | kāya-praṇāma jine jina-stūpe kurvata kāya-viśodhani labdhvā ||
body.translated_text: The ray called <s>Kāya-viśodhanī</s> (purifying the body) releases its rays; those with deficient faculties become endowed with perfect faculties; by making bodily prostration to the <s>Jinas</s> and <s>Jina</s>-<s>stūpas</s>, the radiance <s>Kāya-viśodhanī</s> was obtained.

body.text: citta-viśodhani muñcati raśmīn unmatu sarva sa-cita bhavanti | citta samādhi-vaśa-anuga kṛtvā citta-viśodhani raśmi nivṛttā ||
body.translated_text: The ray called <s>Citta-viśodhanī</s> (purifying the mind) releases its rays; the deranged all become of sound mind; having brought the mind under the power of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), the ray <s>Citta-viśodhanī</s> returned.

body.text: rūpa-viśodhani muñcati raśmīn paśyiya cintiya rūpa-nara-indrān | rūpaka-śodhani citra-samantāt stūpa alaṃ-karatā pratilabdhā ||
body.translated_text: The ray called <s>Rūpa-viśodhanī</s> (purifying form) releases its rays; they see and contemplate the forms of the lords of men; by adorning <s>stūpas</s> with varied paintings all around, the radiance of form-purification was obtained.

body.text: śabda-viśodhani muñcati raśmīn śabda a-śabdata śūnya vijānī | pratyaya jāta prati-śruta-tulyaṃ śabda-prakāśana raśmi nivṛttā ||
body.translated_text: The ray called <s>Śabda-viśodhanī</s> (purifying sound) releases its rays; one understands sound, soundlessness, and emptiness; knowing that it arises from conditions, like an echo — the ray of sound-illumination returned.

body.text: gandha-viśodhani muñcati raśmīn sarva du-gandha su-gandha bhavantī | gandha-vara-agra janair jina-stūpān snāpana-bodhi-druma prabha eṣā ||
body.translated_text: The ray called <s>Gandha-viśodhanī</s> (purifying smell) releases its rays; all foul smells become fragrant; this is the radiance of bathing the <s>Jina</s>-<s>stūpas</s> and <s>Bodhi</s>-trees with the finest fragrant waters.

body.text: te rasa-śodhani muñcati raśmīn sa-dviṣa nir-viṣa bhonti rasa-agrāḥ | buddha sa-śrāvaka-mātṛ-pitṝṇāṃ sarva-rasa-agra-pradāna prabha + eṣāṃ ||
body.translated_text: The ray called <s>Rasa-śodhanī</s> (purifying taste) releases its rays; poisonous flavors become non-poisonous and supreme; this is the radiance of offering the finest flavors to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Śrāvakas</s> (disciples), mothers, and fathers.

body.text: sparśa-viśodhani muñcati raśmīn kakkhaṭa sparśa mṛdū sukha bhontī | śakti-tri-śūla + asi

children.translated_text: showers of spears, tridents, and swords become garlands, soft lotuses, and <s>utpalas</s> (blue lotuses).

body.translated_text: The ray called <s>Sparśa-viśodhanī</s> (purifying touch) releases its rays; rough touches become soft and pleasant;

body.text: duṣya an-eka mṛdū sukha-sparśā saṃstari mārgi vrajanti jinānāṃ | puṣpa-vilepana-cīvara-sūkṣmā mālya-vitāna pradāna prabhā + iyam ||
body.translated_text: With manifold soft fabrics of pleasant touch, they spread coverings on the paths of the <s>Jinas</s> (victors); this is the radiance of offering flowers, ointments, fine robes, garlands, and canopies.

body.text: dharma-viśodhani muñcati raśmīn sarvata romata cintiya dharmān | niścarataḥ śruṇi loka-hitānāṃ toṣayi sarva-dhimukti-jinānām ||
body.translated_text: The ray called <s>Dharma-viśodhanī</s> (purifying the Dharma) releases its rays; from every pore, contemplating the <s>Dharma</s>, teachings beneficial to the world emerge and are heard, bringing delight to all <s>Jinas</s> of resolute faith.

body.text: pratyaya jāta a-jāta sva-bhāvā dharma-śarīra a-jāta-śarīrāḥ | dharmata nitya-sthitā gagana-sthā sūcata dharma-viśodhani labdhā ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Dharmas</s> are conditionally arisen, unborn in intrinsic nature; the <s>Dharma</s>-body has an unborn body; the <s>Dharmatā</s> (true nature of things) is eternally abiding, abiding in space — this is indicated by the radiance <s>Dharma-viśodhanī</s> obtained.

body.text: raśmi sukhā-pramukhā iti kṛtvā ekatu roma-mukhāt tu ṛṣīṇāṃ | niścari gaṅga-raja-upama raśmī sarva-pṛthag-vidha-karma-prayogāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Rays beginning with <s>Sukhā</s> (blissful) and so forth — from each single pore of the sages, rays innumerable as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> (Ganges) shine forth, each with its own distinct action and purpose.

body.text: te yatha ekata roma-mukhāto osari gaṅga-raja-upama raśmī | evam a-śeṣata sarvatu romā deśa samādhi-vikurva ṛṣīṇāṃ ||
body.translated_text: Just as from a single pore, rays innumerable as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> shine forth, so too from every single pore without exception — such is the realm of the sages' <s>samādhi</s>-transformation.

body.text: yena guṇena ya raśmi nivṛttā tasmi guṇeṣu sahāyaka pūrve | teṣu tam eva pramuñcati raśmiṃ jñāna-vikurvaṇa eṣa ṛṣīṇāṃ ||
body.translated_text: By whatever virtue a ray was generated, in those very virtues were there prior companions; for those, that very ray is released — this is the <s>jñāna</s>-transformation (knowledge-transformation) of the sages.

body.text: teṣa ya puṇya sahāyaka pūrve yair anumodita yācita yebhiḥ | yebhi ca dṛṣṭa śubha-upacitaṃ vā te ima raśmi prajānati teṣāṃ ||
body.translated_text: Those who were prior companions in merit, those who rejoiced in it and those who requested it, those who beheld it or accumulated good — they perceive these rays intended for them.

body.text: ye ca śubha-upacitāḥ kṛta-puṇyāḥ pūjita yebhi punaḥ punaḥ buddhāḥ | arthika chandika buddha-guṇebhiḥ codana teṣa karotiya raśmiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Those who have accumulated good and made merit, those who have worshipped the <s>Buddhas</s> again and again, those who desire and aspire to the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> — for them, the ray produces exhortation.

body.text: sūrya yathā jāty-andha na paśyī na + u ca sa na + asti udeti sa loke | cakṣu-sameta udāgamu jñātvā sarva prayujya svaka svaka dharme ||
body.translated_text: Just as the sun is not seen by one born blind, yet it is not that it does not exist — it rises in the world; knowing that one with eyes has come forth, all engage in their respective duties.

body.text: evata raśmi mahā-puruṣāṇāṃ asti ca te itare ca na paśyī | mithya-hatā adhimukti-vihīnāḥ dur-labha te ca udāra-matīnāṃ ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, the rays of the great beings exist, yet others do not see them; those struck by wrong views, devoid of <s>adhimukti</s> (resolute faith) — these rays are hard to obtain for those of base understanding.

body.text: ābharaṇāni nipāna vimānāḥ ratna rasāyana gandh-anulepāḥ | te pi tu asti mahā-ātma-janasya te ca su-dur-labha kṛcchra-gatānāṃ ||
body.translated_text: Ornaments, drinking pools, palaces, jewels, elixirs, fragrant ointments — these indeed exist for the great-souled ones, yet they are extremely hard to obtain for those in miserable states.

body.text: evata raśmi mahā-puruṣāṇāṃ asti ca te itare ca na paśyī | mithya-hatā adhimukti-vihīnāḥ dur-labha te ca udāra-matīnāṃ ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, the rays of the great beings exist, yet others do not see them; those struck by wrong views, devoid of <s>adhimukti</s> (resolute faith) — these rays are hard to obtain for those of base understanding.

body.text: yasy imu

children.translated_text: having heard this classification of rays, will have faith and resolute conviction,

children.text: prasādaḥ | tena na kāṅkṣa na saṃśaya kāryo na + aṅga na bheṣyi mahā-guṇa-ketuḥ ||
children.translated_text: and serene confidence — for them, no doubt or hesitation should be entertained; surely they will become bearers of great virtues.

body.translated_text: For whoever,

body.text: te parivāra-viyūha-vikurvā agra-samādhy-abhinirharamāṇāḥ | sarva-daśa-ddiśi a-pratimānāḥ darśayi buddha-sutāḥ parivāraṃ ||
body.translated_text: They, producing retinue-arrays and transformations, bringing forth the foremost <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations), incomparable in all ten directions — the sons of the <s>Buddha</s> display their retinue.

body.text: te tri-sahasra-pramāṇu-vicitraṃ padmam adhiṣṭhihi raśmi-viyūhāḥ | kāya-paryaṅka parisphuṭa-padmaṃ darśayi eṣa samādhi-vikurvā ||
body.translated_text: They magically project a lotus of the extent of the three-thousandfold world, variegated with arrays of rays; with body seated cross-legged on the fully blossoming lotus — this is the display of <s>samādhi</s>-transformation.

body.text: te daśa-kṣetra-raja-upama anye padmam adhiṣṭhihi saṃparivāraṃ | sarva parīvṛta buddha-sutebhī ye ca samādhy-a-samādhi-vihārī ||
body.translated_text: Others magically project a lotus the extent of ten lands of dust-motes, together with their retinue; all surrounded by sons of the <s>Buddha</s>, both those abiding in <s>samādhi</s> and those not in <s>samādhi</s>.

body.text: ye paripācita tena ṛṣīṇāṃ satva niṣpa-dita buddha-guṇeṣu | te parivāri ataṃ maha-padmaṃ sarva udikṣiṣu prāñjali-bhūtāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Those beings who were ripened by those sages, perfected in the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> — they surround that great lotus, all gazing upward with palms joined in reverence.

body.text: te ca samāhita bāla-śarīre vyutthihi yauvana-vega-sthitebhyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: They enter <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) in the form of a child and emerge in bodies established in the vigor of youth.

body.text: yauvana-vega-sthiteṣu samāhita vyutthihi jīrṇaka vṛddha śarīrāḥ | jīrṇaka-vṛddha-śarīri samāhita vyutthihi śraddha upāsika-kāyāt ||
body.translated_text: Having entered <s>samādhi</s> in those established in the vigor of youth, they emerge as aged and elderly bodies; having entered <s>samādhi</s> in aged and elderly bodies, they emerge from the body of a faithful female lay-devotee.

body.text: śraddha upāsika-kāya-samāhita vyutthihi bhikṣuṇi-kāya-śarīrā | bhikṣuṇi-kāya śarīri samāhita vyutthihi bhikṣu-bahu-śruta-kāyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Having entered <s>samādhi</s> in the body of a faithful female lay-devotee, they emerge in the body of a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun); having entered <s>samādhi</s> in the body of a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, they emerge as bodies of learned <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks).

body.text: bhikṣu-bahu-śruta-kāya samāhita vyutthihi śaikṣa a-śaikṣa-śarīrāḥ | śaikṣa a-śaikṣa-śarīri samāhita vyutthihi pratyaya-buddha-śarīrā ||
body.translated_text: Having entered <s>samādhi</s> in the bodies of learned <s>bhikṣus</s>, they emerge as bodies of <s>śaikṣas</s> (trainees) and <s>aśaikṣas</s> (those beyond training); having entered <s>samādhi</s> in the bodies of <s>śaikṣas</s> and <s>aśaikṣas</s>, they emerge in the body of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one).

body.text: pratyaya buddha śarīri samāhita vyutthihi buddha-vara-agra-śarīrā | buddha-vara-agra-śarīri samāhita vyutthihi devata-kāya śarīrā ||
body.translated_text: Having entered <s>samādhi</s> in the body of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, they emerge in the supreme and excellent body of a <s>Buddha</s>; having entered <s>samādhi</s> in the supreme body of a <s>Buddha</s>, they emerge in the body of a <s>devatā</s> (deity).

body.text: devata-kāya-śarīri samāhita vyutthihi nāga-maha-rddhika-kāyāḥ | nāga-maha-rddhika-kāya-samāhita vyutthihi yakṣa-maha-rddhika-kāyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Having entered <s>samādhi</s> in the body of a <s>devatā</s>, they emerge as bodies of <s>Nāgas</s> (serpent-beings) of great supernatural power; having entered <s>samādhi</s> in the bodies of <s>Nāgas</s> of great supernatural power, they emerge as bodies of <s>Yakṣas</s> (nature spirits) of great supernatural power.

body.text: yakṣa-maha-rddhika-kāya-samāhita vyutthihi sarvata-bhūta-śarīrāḥ | sarvata-bhūta-śarīri samāhita vyutthihi ekatu-roma-mukhātaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Concentrated in bodies of great-powered <s>Yakṣas</s>, they emerge from all sentient bodies. Concentrated in all sentient bodies, they emerge from a single pore-opening.'

body.text: ekatu roma-mukhasmi samāhita vyutthihi sarvata roma-mukheṣu | sarviṣu roma-mukheṣu samāhita vyutthihi ekatu vāla-pathātaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Concentrated in a single pore-opening, they emerge from all pore-openings. Concentrated in all pore-openings, they emerge from a single hair-tip.'

body.text: ekatu vāla-pathasmi samāhita vyutthihi sarvata vāla-pathebhyaḥ | sarviṣu vāla-patheṣu samāhita vyutthihi te parama-aṇu-rajātaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Concentrated in a single hair-tip, they emerge from all hair-tips. Concentrated in all hair-tips, they emerge from the finest atomic particles.'

body.text: eka-rajasmi samāhita bhūtvā vyutthihi sarva-rajebhya a-śeṣam | sarva-rajeṣu samāhita bhūtvā vyutthihi sāgara-vajra-talātaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Having become concentrated in a single particle, they emerge without remainder from all particles. Having become concentrated in all particles, they emerge from the diamond-floor of the ocean.'

body.text: sāgara-vajra-talasmi samāhita vyutthihi te maṇi-vṛkṣa-phalebhyaḥ | vṛkṣa-phaleṣu samāhita bhūtvā vyutthihi raśmi-mukhebhi jinānāṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'Concentrated in the diamond-floor of the ocean, they emerge from the fruits of the jewel-trees. Having become concentrated in the tree-fruits, they emerge from the ray-openings of the <s>Jinas</s>.'

body.text: raśmi-mukheṣu jināna samāhita vyutthihi sāgara-toya-nadībhyaḥ | sāgara-toya-nadīṣu samāhita vyutthihi teja-pathātu mahā-ātmā ||
body.translated_text: 'Concentrated in the ray-openings of the <s>Jinas</s>, they emerge from the ocean-waters and rivers. Concentrated in the ocean-waters and rivers, these great beings emerge from the path of fire.'

body.text: teja-pathasmi samāhita bhūtvā vyutthihi vāyu-patha-anusmṛti + imān | vāyu-pathe tu samāhita bhūtvā vyutthihi bhūmi-talānu mahā-ātmā ||
body.translated_text: 'Having become concentrated in the path of fire, they emerge from the wind-path — [this is] their mindfulness. Having become concentrated in the wind-path, these great beings emerge from the surface of the earth.'

body.text: bhūmi-tale tu samāhita bhūtvā vyutthihi sarvatu deva-vimānāt | sarvi tu deva-balāna samāhita vyutthihi te gagana-anusmṛti + imān ||
body.translated_text: 'Having become concentrated in the surface of the earth, they emerge from all the heavenly palaces. Concentrated in all the powers of the gods, they emerge from these — [this is] their mindfulness of space.'

body.text: eti samādhi vimokṣa a-cintyās teṣa a-cintya-guṇa-upacitānāṃ | kalpa a-cintya prabhāṣiyamāṇāḥ sarva-jinebhi na śakya kṣayītum ||
body.translated_text: 'Such are the <s>samādhis</s> and liberations, inconceivable, of those who are endowed with inconceivable qualities. Even with <s>kalpas</s> inconceivable spent in proclaiming them, by all the <s>Jinas</s> they cannot be exhausted.'

body.text: sarva-jinebhi ca bhāṣita ete karma-vipāku jagasya a-cintyo | nāga-vikurvita buddha-vikurvā dhyāyina dhyāna a-cintya vikurvā ||
body.translated_text: 'And by all the <s>Jinas</s> it is declared that the ripening of <s>karma</s> for the world is inconceivable. The <s>nāga</s>-transformations, the <s>Buddha</s>-transformations — the meditators' inconceivable transformations of <s>dhyāna</s>.'

body.text: te ca vaśe sthita aṣṭa vimokṣāḥ śrāvaka eka bhavī-bahu bhontī | bhūtva bahuḥ puna eka bhavitvā dhyāyati prajvalate gaganasmin ||
body.translated_text: 'And those eight liberations (<s>vimokṣas</s>) stand under their control. The <s>śrāvakas</s>, being one, become many; having become many, they become one again; and they meditate and blaze forth in the sky.'

body.text: te hi mahā-karuṇāya vihīnā bodhi an-arthiku loka upekṣī | darśayi kāya-vikurva a-cintyā kasya na darśayi loka hita-eṣī ||
body.translated_text: 'But they are devoid of great compassion, not aspiring to awakening, indifferent to the world. They display inconceivable bodily transformations — but who does not display [them] if they are a seeker of the world's welfare?'

body.text: candra sa sūrya nabhe vicarantau darśayi sarva-diśi pratibhāsaṃ | utsa-saro-hrada-kūpa-taḍāge bhājana-ratna-samudra-nadīṣu ||
body.translated_text: 'The moon and sun, moving in the sky, display their reflection in all directions — in springs, lakes, pools, wells, and ponds, in vessels, jewels, oceans, and rivers.'

body.text: evam a-cintiya darśiyi rūpaṃ sarva-daśa-ddiśi te nara-vīrāḥ | sarva-samādhi-vimokṣa-vidhi-jñā yatra tathā-gata sākṣi svayaṃ-bhūḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Even so, those heroes among men display inconceivable forms in all ten directions — those who know all the methods of <s>samādhi</s> and liberation, where the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the Self-born One, is witness.'

body.text: sāgara-deva rutāvati-nāmā yāvat satva samudry utpannā | teṣu svara-aṅga-ruteṣu vidhi-jñā toṣayi sarva-rutān sva-rutena ||
body.translated_text: 'The ocean-goddess named <s>Rutāvatī</s> — whatever beings arise in the ocean, knowing the method of their vocal sounds and calls, she satisfies all calls with her own voice.'

body.text: sā hi sa-rāga sa-doṣa rutāvati sarva-rute pratighoṣa vidhi-jñā | dhāraṇi-dharma-balaṃ vaśi-prāptā kaḥ sa na toṣi sa-devaka-lokam ||
body.translated_text: 'She, though partaking of passion and of fault, knows the method of echoing all calls. Having obtained mastery through the power of the <s>Dharma</s> of <s>dhāraṇī</s> — who would not satisfy the world with its gods?'

body.text: māya-karo yatha vidya-vidhi-jño darśayi rūpa vicitra an-antān | rātri-diva-eka-muhūrtuku māsān varṣa-śataṃ puna sphīta-pradīptān ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as a magician, expert in the method of his art, displays forms variously and endlessly — night and day, a single moment and months, and a hundred years, radiant and brilliant.'

body.text: māya-karo hi sa-rāgu sa-doṣo toṣayi māya-vikurvita lokaṃ | dhyāna abhijña vimokṣa-su-śikṣita kasya na toṣayi carya-vidhi-jñaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'A magician, though partaking of passion and fault, satisfies the world with his magical transformations. One well-trained in <s>dhyāna</s>, higher knowledges, and liberation — who would he not satisfy, the one skilled in the method of conduct?'

body.text: rāhu yatha-iṣa ya nirmaṇi kāyaṃ kurvati vajra pade tala-bandhaṃ | darśana sāgaru nābhi-pramāṇaṃ bhoti sumeru-tale sama śīrṣaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as <s>Rāhu</s>, who at will creates a body, makes a diamond base under his feet — his appearance reaches the height of the ocean up to the navel, his head level with the base of <s>Sumeru</s>.'

body.text: so * api sa-rāgu sa-doṣa sa-moho rāhu nidarśayi īdṛśa ṛddhī | māra-pramardana loka-pradīpa kasya na darśayi ṛddhi an-antā ||
body.translated_text: 'He too, partaking of passion, fault, and delusion — <s>Rāhu</s> displays such powers. The <s>Māra</s>-crusher, the Light of the World — would he not display endless powers?'

body.text: paśya a-cintiya śakra-vikurvā deva-sura-indra-raṇasmi pravṛtte | yātuka bimbar-an-eka-surāṇāṃ tātuka nirmaṇi śakru sva-kāyān ||
body.translated_text: 'Behold the inconceivable transformation of <s>Śakra</s>: when battle erupts between the lords of gods and <s>asuras</s> — however many the images of the manifold hosts of gods, <s>Śakra</s> creates just that many forms of his own body.'

body.text: sarva-sura-indra-surāś ca vijānī śakrama ... purato gata sva-āyum |eṣa gṛhyeta vajra-dharāṇāṃ saṃbhramu gacchisu sarva-sura-indrāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'All the hosts of the lord of gods know: "<s>Śakra</s> ... has gone before us, offering his own life." Grasped by the wielders of the vajra — all the hosts of gods rush into battle.'

body.text: netra sahasra bhayaṅ-kara darśī jvāla-pramuñcana vajra gṛhītaṃ | varmita kāya dur-āsada teja śakram udīkṣya palātv asura-indrāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'With a thousand eyes, of terrifying appearance, releasing flames, grasping the vajra, armored in body, of unapproachable radiance — seeing <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of <s>asuras</s> flees.'

body.text: so hita itvara-puṇya-balenā śakra vikurvati deva-jaya-arthī | sarva-jagasya a-śeṣata trāṇāṃ a-kṣaya-puṇya kuto na vikurvī ||
body.translated_text: 'That one, merely by the power of modest merit, <s>Śakra</s>, transforms [himself] desiring victory over the gods. For the protection of the entire world without remainder — how would one of inexhaustible merit not transform?'

body.text: ... vāyuta saṃbhuta megha-pravarṣī vāyuta megha punaḥ prasamentī | vāyuta sasya virohati loke vāyu sukha-āvaha sarva-jagasya ||
body.translated_text: 'From the wind, clouds are produced and it rains; from the wind, clouds again disperse. From the wind, crops grow in the world — the wind brings happiness to the entire world.'

body.text: so hi a-śikṣita pāramitāsu buddha-guṇeṣu a-śikṣita vāyuḥ | darśayi loka-vipāka a-cintyā kasya na darśayi te vara-labdhā ||
body.translated_text: 'That wind, untrained in the perfections, untrained in the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities — displays inconceivable ripening for the world. Who, having obtained such supreme attainment, would not display [such powers]?'

body.text: iti śikṣā-samuccaye ratna-traya-anusmṛti-nāma + aṣṭādaśaḥ paricchedaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>, the eighteenth chapter called Recollection of the Three Jewels (<s>ratnatrayānusmṛti</s>) is completed.

body.text: navadaśaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The nineteenth chapter.

body.text: anyo * api puṇya-vṛddhaye hetuḥ kāryaḥ | yo * ayaṃ sarva-avasthāsu satva-arthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: There is yet another cause to be undertaken for the increase of merit: namely, the welfare of beings in all situations.

body.text: yathā kathitaṃ ca + ārya-ratna-meghe | sa tathā-gata-caitye vā tathā-gata-vigrahe vā puṣpaṃ vā dhūpaṃ vā gandhaṃ vā dadat sarva-satvānāṃ dauḥśīlya-daurgandhya-mala-apanayanāya tathā-gata-śīla-pratilambhāya ca pariṇāmayati | sa san-mārjana-upalepanaṃ kurvan sarva-satvānām a-prāsādika-īryā-patha-vigamāya | prāsādika-īryā-patha-saṃpade ca pariṇāmayati | sa puṣpa-cchatram āropayan sarva-satvānāṃ sarva-kleśa-paridāha-vigamāya pariṇāmayati | sa vihāraṃ praviśann evaṃ cittam utpādayati | sarva-satvān nirvāṇa-puraṃ praveśayeyaṃ | sa niṣkramann evaṃ cittam utpādayati | sarva-satvān saṃsāra-cārakān niṣkrāmayeyaṃ | sa labhana-dvāram udghāṭayann evaṃ cittam utpādayati | sarva-satvānāṃ loka-uttareṇa jñānena nirvāṇa-su-gati-dvāram udghāṭayeyaṃ | sa pithad evaṃ cittam utpādayati | sarva-satvānāṃ sarva-apāya-dvārāṇi pidadhyāṃ | sa niṣīdann evaṃ cittam utpādayati | sarva-satvān bodhi-maṇḍe niṣādayeyaṃ | sa dakṣiṇena pārśvena śayyāṃ kalpayann evaṃ cittam utpādayati | sarva-satvān eva parinirvāpayeyaṃ | sa tato vyuttiṣṭhann evaṃ cittam utpādayati | sarva-satvān vyutthāpayeyaṃ sarva-kleśa-paryutthānebhyaḥ | sa śarīra-gatyā gacchann evaṃ cittam utpādayati | sarva-satvā mahā-puruṣa-gatyā gacchantu | sa tatra + upaviṣṭae evaṃ cittam utpādayati | sarva-satvā niḥ-śalya-kriyā yad uta rāga-dveṣa-mohebhyaḥ | sa śaucaṃ kurvann evaṃ cittam utpādayati | sarva-satvānāṃ kleśa-malāt prakṣālayeyaṃ |sa hastau prakṣālayann evaṃ cittam utpādayati | sarva-satvānāṃ sarva-kleśa-vāsanām apanayeyaṃ |sa pādau prakṣālayann evaṃ cittam utpādayati sarva-satvānām an-eka-prakārāṇi kleśa-rajāṃsy apanayeyaṃ |mukhaṃ prakṣālayann evaṃ cittam utpādayati | sarva-satvānāṃ sarva-dharma-mukhāni pariśodhayeyaṃ | sa danta-kāṣṭhaṃ bhakṣayann evaṃ cittam utpādayati | sarva-satvānāṃ nānā-vidhān kleśa-malān apanayeyaṃ | sarvāṃ kāya-avasthāṃ sarva-satva-hita-sukhāya pariṇāmayati | tathā-gata-caityaṃ vandamāna evaṃ cittam utpādayati | sarva-satvā vandanīyā bhavantu sa-devakasya lokasya + iti ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Ārya-Ratnamegha</s>: 'When he offers a flower, incense, or fragrance at a <s>Tathāgata</s>-shrine or before a <s>Tathāgata</s>-image, he dedicates it to the removal of the stain of the foul odor of bad morality from all beings and to the attainment of the moral conduct of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. When he sweeps and plasters [the shrine], he dedicates it to the removal of the disagreeable deportment of all beings and to the attainment of graceful deportment. When he raises a flower-parasol, he dedicates it to the removal of the burning heat of all afflictions from all beings. When he enters a <s>vihāra</s> (monastery), he generates the thought: "May I cause all beings to enter the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>." When he exits, he generates the thought: "May I cause all beings who wander in <s>saṃsāra</s> to come out." When he opens a door-bolt, he generates the thought: "May I open the door of the happy destiny of <s>nirvāṇa</s> for all beings through supramundane knowledge." When he closes [it], he generates the thought: "May I close the doors of all lower realms for all beings." When he sits down, he generates the thought: "May I seat all beings at the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>)." When he lies down on his right side, he generates the thought: "May I cause all beings to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>." When he rises therefrom, he generates the thought: "May I cause all beings to rise from all the surges of the afflictions." When he walks with bodily movement, he generates the thought: "May all beings walk with the gait of a great being." When he sits down there, he generates the thought: "May all beings have the thorns extracted — namely, those of passion, hatred, and delusion." When he cleans himself, he generates the thought: "May I wash all beings from the stain of the afflictions." When he washes his hands, he generates the thought: "May I remove the latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of all afflictions from all beings." When he washes his feet, he generates the thought: "May I remove the manifold kinds of affliction-dust from all beings." When he washes his face, he generates the thought: "May I purify all <s>Dharma</s>-doors for all beings." When he chews a tooth-stick, he generates the thought: "May I remove the various kinds of affliction-stain from all beings." He dedicates every bodily posture to the welfare and happiness of all beings. When bowing to a <s>Tathāgata</s>-shrine, he generates the thought: "May all beings become worthy of veneration by the world with its gods."'

body.text: atha-vā yathā + ārya-prajñā-pāramitāyāṃ | punar a-paraṃ śāriputra vyāḍa-kāntāra-madhya-gatena bodhi-satvena mahā-satvena na + uttrasitavyaṃ na saṃtrasitavyam na saṃtrāsam āpattavyam | tat kasmād * dhetoḥ | tathā hi tena sarvaṃ parityaktaṃ sarva-satvānām arthāya | tena + evaṃ cittam utpādayitavyam |sacen māṃ vyāḍā bhakṣayeyus tebhya eva tad dānaṃ dattaṃ bhavatu | mama ca dāna-pāramitā-paripūrir bhaviṣyati | abhyāsannā ca bhaviṣyati | tathā ca kariṣyāmi yathā me * an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhim abhisambuddhasya satas tatra buddha-kṣetre tiryag-yoni-gatāḥ satvāḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ na bhaviṣyanti na prajñāsyante ||
body.translated_text: Alternatively, as in the <s>Ārya-Prajñāpāramitā</s>: 'Furthermore, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who has entered the midst of a wilderness of wild beasts should not be terrified, should not be alarmed, should not fall into fear. For what reason? Because he has relinquished everything for the sake of all beings. He should generate the thought: "If wild beasts should devour me, may that gift be given to them. And my perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) will be fulfilled and will be brought near. And I shall act in such a way that, when I have fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, in that <s>Buddha</s>-field beings born in the animal realm will absolutely in no way exist or be known."'

body.text: cora-kāntāra-madhya-gatena śāriputra bodhi-satvena mahā-satvena na + uttrasitavyaṃ na saṃtrasitavyaṃ na saṃtrāsam āpattavyaṃ |tat kasmād * dhetoḥ | sarvasva-parityāga-kuśalā hi te bodhi-satvā mahā-satvā utsṛṣṭa-kāyena + api ca bodhi-satvena bhavitavyaṃ parityakta-pariṣkāra-upakaraṇena ca | tena + evaṃ cittam utpādayitavyaṃ |te cen me satvāḥ pariṣkāra-upakaraṇāni haranti tebhya eva + etad dānaṃ dattaṃ bhavatu | sacen māṃ ke-cij jīvitād vyaparopayeyuḥ tatra mayā na dveṣo na krodha utpādayitavyaḥ | teṣām api mayā na kāyena na vacasā na manasā + aparāddhavyaṃ | evaṃ ca me tasmin samaye dāna-pāramitā ca śīla-pāramitā ca kṣānti-pāramitā ca paripūriṃ gamiṣyati | an-uttarā ca me samyak-saṃbodhir abhyāsannā bhaviṣyati | tathā ca kariṣyāmi tathā pratipatsye yathā me * an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhasya satas tatra buddha-kṣetre | ete ca + anye ca doṣāḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvaṃ na bhaviṣyanti na prajñāsyante ||
body.translated_text: 'A <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who has entered the midst of a wilderness of robbers, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, should not be terrified, should not be alarmed, should not fall into fear. For what reason? Because those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> are skilled in the relinquishment of all possessions, and the <s>bodhisattva</s> should be one who has abandoned the body and one who has relinquished equipment and requisites. He should generate the thought: "If those beings take my equipment and requisites, may that gift be given to them. If some should deprive me of life, I should not generate hatred or anger toward them. Nor should I offend them by body, speech, or mind. And at that time my perfection of giving, my perfection of moral conduct, and my perfection of patience will be fulfilled. And my unsurpassed perfect awakening will be brought near. And I shall act and practice in such a way that, when I have fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, in that <s>Buddha</s>-field these and other faults will absolutely in no way exist or be known."'

body.text: pānīya-kāntāra-madhya-gatena śāriputra bodhi-satvena mahā-satvena na + uttrasitavyaṃ na saṃtrasitavyaṃ na saṃtrāsam āpattavyaṃ |tat kasmād * dhetoḥ | a-saṃtrasta-dharmāṇo hi bodhi-satvā mahā-satvā bhavanti | evaṃ ca + anena cittam utpādayitavyaṃ | sarva-satvānāṃ mayā sarva-tṛṣṇa-cchedāya śikṣitavyaṃ | na bodhi-satvena mahā-satvena saṃtrāsam āpattavyaṃ |saced ahaṃ tṛṣṇayā kālaṃ kariṣyāmi | api tu khalu punaḥ satvānām antike mahā-karuṇā-cittam utpādayiṣyāmi | aho vata + alpa-puṇyā amī satvā yad eteṣāṃ loke evaṃ-rūpāṇi pānīya-kāntārāṇi prajñāyante | tathā punar ahaṃ kariṣyāmi tathā pratipatsye yathā me * an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhasya satas tatra buddha-kṣetre sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvaṃ pānīya-kāntārāṇi na prajñāsyante | tathā ca sarva-satvān puṇyaiḥ saṃyojayiṣyāmi yathā + aṣṭa-aṅga-upeta-pānīya-lābhino bhaviṣyanti | tathā dṛḍhaṃ vīryam ārapsye sarva-satvānāṃ kṛtaśo yathā vīrya-pāramitā tasmin samaye paripūriṃ gamiṣyanti ||
body.translated_text: 'A <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who has entered the midst of a waterless wilderness, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, should not be terrified, should not be alarmed, should not fall into fear. For what reason? Because <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> are of unfearful disposition. And he should generate the thought: "I should train myself for the cutting off of all thirsts of all beings. The <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should not fall into fear. If I should die of thirst, I shall rather generate a mind of great compassion toward beings: 'Alas, of little merit are these beings, that such waterless wildernesses are found in the world for them.' And I shall further act and practice in such a way that, when I have fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, in that <s>Buddha</s>-field waterless wildernesses will absolutely in no way be found. And I shall yoke all beings with merit such that they will obtain water endowed with eight qualities. And I shall arouse firm vigor on behalf of all beings, so that the perfection of vigor will be fulfilled at that time."'

body.text: punar a-paraṃ śāriputra bubhukṣā-kāntāra-madhya-gatena bodhi-satvena mahā-satvena na + uttrasitavyaṃ na saṃtrasitavyaṃ na saṃtrāsam āpattavyaṃ | evaṃ ca + anena saṃnāhaḥ saṃnaddhavyaḥ | tathā dṛḍhaṃ vīryam ārapsye tathā ca svaṃ buddha-kṣetraṃ pariśodhayiṣyāmi yathā me * an-uttarāṃ samyak-saṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhasya satas tatra buddha-kṣetre sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvaṃ evaṃ-rūpāṇi bubhukṣā-kāntārāṇi na bhaviṣyanti na prajñāsyante | sukhitā eva te satvā bhaviṣyanti sukha-samaṅginaḥ | sarva-sukha-samarpitās tathā ca kariṣyāmi yathā teṣāṃ satvānāṃ yo ya eva + abhiprāyo bhaviṣyati yad yad eva + ākāṅkṣiṣyanti manasā tat tad eva prādur-bhaviṣyati | tad yathā + api nāma devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ manasā sarvaṃ prādur-bhavati manasā sarvam utpadyate | tathā dṛḍhaṃ vīryam ārapsye yathā teṣāṃ satvānāṃ dhārmikā abhiprāyāḥ paripūriṃ gamiṣyanti | a-vaikalyaṃ ca jīvita-pariṣkāraiḥ sarva-satvānāṃ bhaviṣyati sarveṣāṃ sarvataḥ sarvadā + iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> who has entered the wilderness of hunger should not be frightened, not be terrified, not fall into terror. And he should don the armor thus: "I shall exert such firm vigor, and I shall so purify my own <s>Buddha</s>-field, that when I have fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, in that <s>Buddha</s>-field of mine there will be no wildernesses of hunger whatsoever, in any way — they will not be known at all. Those beings will be happy, endowed with happiness, furnished with all happiness. And I shall act in such a way that whatever desire those beings will have, whatever they will wish for in their minds — that very thing will appear. Just as for the gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three) heaven, everything appears by the mind, everything is produced by the mind — so shall I exert firm vigor so that the righteous desires of those beings will be fulfilled. And there will be no deficiency in the requisites of life for all beings, everywhere, at all times."'

body.text: evam ayaṃ ... sarva-avasthāsu satva-arthaḥ ... puṇya-vṛrdhi-hetuḥ | vistaratas tv ārya-go-cara-pariśuddhi-sūtre draṣṭavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus this... the benefit of beings in all circumstances... is the cause of the increase of merit. But it should be seen in detail in the <s>Ārya-Gocarapariśuddhi Sūtra</s>.

body.text: kiṃ ca | ... dharma-dānaṃ nir-āmiṣaṃ | puṇya-vṛddhi-nimittaṃ bhavati ||
body.translated_text: Moreover: ...the gift of <s>Dharma</s>, selfless [and without material aim], becomes the cause of the increase of merit.

body.text: yathā + uktam ārya-adhyāśaya-saṃcodana-sūtre | viṃśatir ime maitreya + anuśaṃsā nir-āmiṣa-dāne | yo lābha-sat-kāram a-pratikāṅkṣan dharma-dānaṃ dadāmi | katame viṃśatiḥ | yad uta | smṛtimāṃś ca bhavati matimāṃś ca bhavati buddhimāṃś ca bhavati gatimāṃś ca bhavati dhṛtimāṃś ca bhavati prajñāvāṃś ca bhavati | loka-uttarāṃ ca prajñām anuvidhyati | alpa-rāgo bhavati | alpa-dveṣo * alpa-mohaḥ | māraś ca + asya + avatāraṃ na labhate | buddhair bhagavadbhiḥ samanvāhriyate | a-manuṣyāś ca + enaṃ rakṣanti | devāś ca + asya + ojaḥ kāye praks.ipanti | a-mitrāś ca + asya + avatāraṃ na labhante | mitrāṇi ca + asya + a-bhedyāni bhavanti | ādeya-vacanaś ca bhavati | vaiśāradyāṃś ca pratilabhate | saumanasya-bahulaś ca bhavati vidvat-praśastaś ca | anusmaraṇīyaṃ ca + asya tad dharma-dānaṃ bhavati | ime maitreya viṃśatir anuśaṃsā iti ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Ārya-Adhyāśayasaṃcodana Sūtra</s>: 'These are twenty benefits, O <s>Maitreya</s>, of selfless giving. [For] one who, not expecting gain and honor, gives the gift of <s>Dharma</s>. Which twenty? Namely: he becomes endowed with mindfulness, endowed with intelligence, endowed with wisdom, endowed with understanding, endowed with resolution, endowed with discernment; he penetrates supramundane wisdom; he has little attachment; he has little hatred, little delusion; <s>Māra</s> does not find an opening against him; the <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s> remember him; non-human beings protect him; the gods cast vitality into his body; enemies do not find an opening against him; his friends become unbreakable; he becomes one whose words are accepted; he attains confidence; he abounds in happiness; he is praised by the wise; and that <s>Dharma</s>-gift of his becomes memorable. These, O <s>Maitreya</s>, are the twenty benefits.'

body.text: ārya-prajñā-pāramitāyāṃ tv āha | sacet tvam ānanda śrāvaka-yānikānāṃ pudgalānāṃ śrāvaka-bhūmau dharmaṃ deśeyaḥ | tasyāṃ ca dharma-deśanāyāṃ ye tri-sāhasra-mahā-sāhasre loka-dhātau satvās te sarve * arhatvaṃ sākṣāt kuryus tad adya + api tvayā me śrāvakeṇa śrāvaka-kṛtyaṃ na kṛtaṃ syāt | sacet punaḥ tvam ānanda bodhi-satvasya mahā-satvasya + ekam api prajñā-pāramitā-pratisaṃyuktaṃ padaṃ deśayeḥ prakāśayer evam ahaṃ tvayā śrāvakeṇa + ārādhitaḥ syāṃ | tayā ca pūrvikayā dharma-deśanayā ye tri-sāhasra-mahā-sāhasre loka-dhātau satvās te sarve * arhatvaṃ prāpnuyus teṣāṃ ca + arhatāṃ yad dāna-mayaṃ puṇya-kriyā-vastu śīla-mayaṃ puṇya-kriyā-vastu bhāvanā-mayaṃ puṇya-kriyā-vastu | tat kiṃ manyase ānanda + api tu sa bahu puṇya-skandhaḥ | āha | bahu bhagavan bahu su-gata | bhagavān āha | ataḥ sa ānanda śrāvaka-yānika-pudgalo bahutaraṃ puṇya-skandhaṃ prasavati yo bodhi-satvānāṃ mahā-satvānāṃ prajñā-pāramitā-pratisaṃyuktaṃ dharmaṃ deśayati | ato * apy ānanda bahutaraṃ puṇya-skandhaṃ prasavati yo bodhi-satvo mahā-satvo * a-parasya bodhi-satvasya prajñā-pāramitā-pratisaṃyuktaṃ dharmaṃ deśayati | antaśa eka-divasam api | tiṣṭhatv ānanda eka-divasaḥ | antaśaḥ prāg-bhaktam api | tiṣṭhatv ānanda prāg-bhaktaṃ | antaśa eka-nālikām api | yāvad antaśa eka-kṣaṇa-saṃnipātam api | peyālaṃ ||
body.translated_text: But in the <s>Ārya-Prajñāpāramitā</s> it says: 'Suppose, O <s>Ānanda</s>, you were to teach the <s>Dharma</s> to persons of the <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle on the <s>śrāvaka</s>-stage; and suppose that by that <s>Dharma</s>-teaching, all the beings in the three-thousand great-thousand world-system were to directly realize <s>arhatship</s> — even then, O <s>Ānanda</s>, you as my <s>śrāvaka</s> would not have accomplished the <s>śrāvaka</s>'s task. But suppose, O <s>Ānanda</s>, you were to teach even a single word connected with the Perfection of Wisdom (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>) to a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, and illuminate it — then I would be pleased with you as my <s>śrāvaka</s>. And by that previous <s>Dharma</s>-teaching, all the beings in the three-thousand great-thousand world-system would attain <s>arhatship</s>; and the merit-producing basis of those <s>arhats</s> — [consisting of] the merit-producing basis of giving, the merit-producing basis of moral conduct, and the merit-producing basis of meditation — what do you think, <s>Ānanda</s>? Is that a large mass of merit?' He said: 'Large, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! Large, O <s>Sugata</s>!' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Even greater, O <s>Ānanda</s>, is the mass of merit produced by that <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle person who teaches the <s>Dharma</s> connected with the Perfection of Wisdom to <s>bodhisattvas</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s>. And even greater still, O <s>Ānanda</s>, is the mass of merit produced by a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> who teaches the <s>Dharma</s> connected with the Perfection of Wisdom to another <s>bodhisattva</s> — even for a single day. Set aside a single day, <s>Ānanda</s>. Even for a single morning meal. Set aside a morning meal, <s>Ānanda</s>. Even for a single water-clock's time. Even for a single instant.' [Abbreviation.]

body.text: idam ānanda tasya bodhi-satvasya mahā-satvasya dharma-dānaṃ sarva-śrāvaka-yānikānām api sarva-praty-eka-buddha-yānikānāṃ ca pudgalānāṃ kuśala-mūlam abhibhavati | evaṃ kuśala-mūla-samanvāgato bodhi-satvo mahā-satvaḥ | evaṃ kuśala-mūlaṃ samanvāharann a-sthānam ānanda + an-avakāśo yat sa bodhi-satvo mahā-satvo vivarteta + an-uttarāyāḥ samyak-saṃbodheḥ | na + etat sthānaṃ vidyatae iti ||
body.translated_text: 'This, O <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>Dharma</s>-gift of that <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, which surpasses the wholesome roots even of all <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle persons and all <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle persons. A <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> endowed with such wholesome roots, accumulating such wholesome roots — it is impossible, O <s>Ānanda</s>, there is no occasion for that <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> to turn back from unsurpassed perfect awakening. Such a thing is not possible.'

body.text: kathaṃ dharma-dānaṃ dātavyaṃ | yathā + ārya-sad-dharma-puṇḍarīke * abhihitaṃ | kālena ca + u cintayamānu paṇḍitaḥ praviśya layanaṃ tatha ghaṭṭayitvā | vipaśya dharmaṃ imi sarva yoniśo utthāya deśeta a-līna-cittaḥ ||
body.translated_text: How should the gift of <s>Dharma</s> be given? As stated in the <s>Ārya-Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s>: 'The wise one, constantly reflecting at the [proper] time, having entered a cave and having examined [the teaching], having seen all these <s>dharmas</s> thoroughly, should arise and teach with an unreserved mind.'

body.text: sukha-sthito bhoti sadā vicakṣaṇo sukhaṃ niṣaṇṇas tatha dharma bhāsate | udāra-prajñapta karitva āsanaṃ caukṣe mano-jñe pṛthivī-pradeśe ||
body.translated_text: 'The discerning one is always seated comfortably and happily, and teaches the <s>Dharma</s> while comfortably seated; having prepared a noble seat in a clean and pleasant place on the earth.'

body.text: caukṣaṃ ca so cīvara prāvaritvā su-rakta-raṅgaṃ ca prasanna-raṅgaiḥ | āsevakaṃ kṛṣṇa tathā daditvā mahā-pramāṇaṃ ca nivāsayitvā ||
body.translated_text: 'And having put on a clean robe, well-dyed with pleasing colors, and having put on a black under-garment, and having put on a large outer robe —'

body.text: sa-pāda-pīṭhasmi niṣadya āsane vicitra-duṣyehi su-saṃstṛtasmin | su-dhauta-pādaś ca upāruhitvā snigdhena śīrṣeṇa mukhena ca + api ||
body.translated_text: 'Seated on a seat with a footstool, covered with various fine cloths, having mounted with well-washed feet, with an affable head and face —'

body.text: dharma-āsane tatra niṣīdiyānaḥ eka-agra satveṣu samaṃ vipaśyan | upasaṃharec citra-kathā bahūś ca bhikṣūnaś ca + u bhikṣunikās tathā + eva ||
body.translated_text: 'Seated there on the <s>Dharma</s>-seat, with one-pointed [mind], looking equally upon all beings, he should draw together various and many discourses, and [address] monks and nuns as well.'

body.text: kilāsitāś ca + api vivarjayīta na ca + api utpādayi kheda-saṃjñāṃ | a-ratiṃ ca sarvāṃ vijahīta paṇḍitaḥ maitrī-balaṃ parṣadi bhāvayec ca ||
body.translated_text: 'He should avoid those who are hostile, and he should not generate the perception of weariness. The wise one should abandon all dissatisfaction, and should cultivate the power of loving-kindness in the assembly.'

body.text: bhāṣec ca rātriṃ-divam agra-dharmān dṛṣṭa-anta-koṭī-niyutaiḥ sa paṇḍitaḥ | saṃharṣayet tāṃ ca tathā + eva toṣayet na ca + api kiñ-cit tatra jātu prārthayet ||
body.translated_text: 'That wise one should speak the supreme <s>dharmas</s> day and night, with <s>niyutas</s> of <s>koṭis</s> of similes. He should both delight and satisfy them, and should never seek anything whatsoever from them.'

body.text: khādyaṃ ca bhojyaṃ ca tathā + anna-pānaṃ vastrāṇi śayyā-āsana-cīvarāṇi | gilāna-bhaiṣajya na cintayet saḥ na vijñapet parṣadi kiñ-cid anyat ||
body.translated_text: 'He should not think about food and drink, or eatables, or robes, bedding, seats, or garments, or medicine for the sick. He should not request anything else from the assembly.'

body.text: anyatra cinteya sadā vicakṣaṇaḥ bhaveya buddho * aham ime ca satvā | etac ca me sarva-sukha-upadhānaṃ yaṃ dharma śrāvemi hitāya loke ||
body.translated_text: 'Rather, the discerning one should always think: "May I become a <s>Buddha</s>, and [may] these beings [become Buddhas too]! And this is my provision of all happiness — that I proclaim the <s>Dharma</s> for the benefit of the world."'

body.text: atra + eva + āha ||
body.translated_text: In this same [sūtra] it says:

body.text: na kasya-cid antaśo dharma-premṇā + apy adhikataram anugrahaṃ karoti ||
body.translated_text: 'He should not show greater favor to anyone, not even out of love of the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: ārya-candra-pradīpa-sūtre * apy āha | adhyeṣayeyur yadi tvāṃ te dharma-dānasya kāraṇāt | prathamaṃ vāca bhāṣeyā na + ahaṃ vaitulya-śikṣitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Candrapradīpa Sūtra</s> it also says: 'If they should beseech you for the sake of the gift of <s>Dharma</s>, first you should say these words: "I have not been trained in the extensive [teachings] (<s>vaipulya</s>)."'

body.text: evaṃ tvaṃ vāca bhāṣeyā yuṣme vā vijña-paṇḍitāḥ | kathaṃ mahā-ātmanāṃ śakyaṃ purato bhāṣituṃ mayā ||
body.translated_text: 'Thus you should say these words: "You are wise scholars — how is it possible for me to speak in the presence of great-souled ones?"'

body.text: sahasā + eṣāṃ na jalpeta tulayitvā tu bhājanaṃ | yadi bhājanaṃ vijānīyāḥ an-adhīṣṭo * api deśayeḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'One should not speak to them hastily, but having weighed whether [the listener is] a suitable vessel. If you know [them to be] a suitable vessel, you should teach even when not entreated.'

body.text: yadi duḥ-śīlān paśyesi pariṣāyāṃ bahūn sthitān | saṃlekhaṃ mā prabhāṣe tvaṃ varṇaṃ dānasya kīrtayeḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'If you see many of corrupt morality standing in the assembly, you should not speak on austerity; you should praise the virtues of generosity.'

body.text: bhaveyur yadi ca + alpa-icchāḥ śuddhāḥ śīle pratiṣṭhitāḥ | maitraṃ cittaṃ janitvā tvaṃ kuryāḥ saṃlekhikīṃ kathām ||
body.translated_text: 'But if they should be of few wants, pure, established in moral conduct — then having generated a mind of loving-kindness, you should give a discourse on austerity.'

body.text: parīttā yadi pāpa-icchāḥ śīlavanto * atra vistarāḥ | labdha-pakṣas tadā bhūtvā varṇaṃ śīlasya kīrtayeḥ | iti ||
body.translated_text: 'If the wicked-intentioned are few and the morally virtuous are the majority — then, having gained their support, you should praise the virtues of moral conduct.'

body.text: uktaṃ ca + ārya-sāgara-mati-sūtre | tad yathā | same | samavati | śamita-śatru | aṅkure | maṅkure | māra-jite | karāḍe | keyūre | oghavati | ohokayati | viśaṭha-nir-male | mala-apanaye | okhare | kharograse | grasane | he-mukhī | parāṅ-mukhī | ā-mukhī | śamitāni sarva-graha-bandhanāni | nigṛhītāḥ sarva-para-pravādinaḥ | vimuktā māra-pāśāḥ | sthāpitā buddha-mudrāḥ samudghātitāḥ sarva-mārāḥ | a-calita-pada-pariśuddhyā vigacchanti sarva-māra-karmāṇi ||
body.translated_text: And as stated in the <s>Ārya-Sāgaramati Sūtra</s>: 'Namely: <s>same</s>, <s>samavati</s>, <s>śamitaśatru</s>, <s>aṅkure</s>, <s>maṅkure</s>, <s>mārajite</s>, <s>karāḍe</s>, <s>keyūre</s>, <s>oghavati</s>, <s>ohokayati</s>, <s>viśaṭhanirmale</s>, <s>malāpanaye</s>, <s>okhare</s>, <s>kharograse</s>, <s>grasane</s>, <s>hemukhī</s>, <s>parāṅmukhī</s>, <s>āmukhī</s>! All the bonds of seizure are pacified! All rival disputants are subdued! The snares of <s>Māra</s> are freed! The seals of the <s>Buddha</s> are established! All <s>Māras</s> are demolished! Through the purity of the unmoved state, all the works of <s>Māra</s> depart!'

body.text: imāni sāgaramate mantra-padāni dharma-bhāṇakena su-pravṛttāni kṛtvā dharma-āsanakena su-pravṛttāni kṛtvā dharma-āsana-niṣaṇṇena sarvāṃ parṣadaṃ bodhy-ākāra-abhinirhṛtayā maitryā spharitvā | ātmani vaidya-saṃjñām utpādya dharme bhaiṣajya-saṃjñāṃ dharma-śravaṇikeṣv ātura-saṃjñāṃ tathā-gate sat-puruṣa-saṃjñāṃ dharma-netryāṃ cira-sthitika-saṃjñām utpādya + imāni mantra-padāny ā-mukhī-kṛtya dharma-saṃkathā karaṇīyā | tasya samantād yo jana-śate na māro na māra-kāyikā vā devatā upasaṃkramayiṣyanti vi-cakṣuḥ-karaṇe | ye * apy enam upasaṃkramiṣyanti te * apy asya na śakṣyanty antarāyaṃ kartum iti ||
body.translated_text: 'O <s>Sāgaramati</s>, a <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, having properly recited these <s>mantra</s>-words and having properly arranged the <s>Dharma</s>-seat, seated on the <s>Dharma</s>-seat, should pervade the entire assembly with loving-kindness produced through the mode of awakening. Having generated the perception of himself as a physician, the perception of the <s>Dharma</s> as medicine, the perception of the <s>Dharma</s>-listeners as patients, the perception of the <s>Tathāgata</s> as a true person, and the perception that the <s>Dharma</s>-vision will endure long — having recited these <s>mantra</s>-words from the beginning, the <s>Dharma</s>-discourse should be given. For a hundred <s>yojanas</s> around him, neither <s>Māra</s> nor the <s>Māra</s>-host deities will approach to make [the teaching] blind. And even those who do approach him will not be able to create obstacles for him.'

body.text: atra + eva + āha | dharma-bhāṇakena caukṣeṇa śuci-samudācāreṇa su-snātena śuci-nivāsitena bhavitavyam iti ||
body.translated_text: In this same [sūtra] it says: 'A <s>Dharma</s>-preacher should be clean, of pure conduct, well-bathed, and cleanly dressed.'

body.text: evaṃ dharma-dānaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Thus [is described] the gift of <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: bodhi-cittaṃ ca puṇyasya vṛddhi-hetuḥ samāsataḥ ||
body.translated_text: And <s>bodhicitta</s> is, in summary, the cause of the increase of merit.

body.text: yathā + uktam ārya-ratna-karaṇḍaka-sūtre | tad yathā + api nāma mañjuśrīr nānā-gandha-vṛkṣāś ca catur-dhātu-saṃgṛhītā vivardhante | evam eva mañjuśrīr nānā-saṃbhāra-upacitaṃ bodhi-satvasya kuśala-mūlaṃ | bodhi-citta-saṃgṛhītaṃ sarva-jñatā-pariṇāmitaṃ vivardhatae | iti ||
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Ārya-Ratnakaraṇḍaka Sūtra</s>: 'O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, just as various fragrant trees, gathered by the four elements, grow — just so, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the wholesome root of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, accumulated through various provisions, gathered by <s>bodhicitta</s> and dedicated to omniscience, grows.'

body.text: eṣā + ādikā ādi-karmikāṇāṃ sahasā bodhi-satva-śikṣā smaraṇa-artham upadarśitā | vistaratas tu buddha-viṣaya eva ||
body.translated_text: This elementary <s>bodhisattva</s> training has been shown briefly for beginners, for the purpose of remembering. But in detail, it is the very domain of the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: atra ca + asyā yathā-uktāyāḥ śikṣāyāḥ | siddhiḥ samyak-prahāṇānām a-pramāda-a-viyojanāt | smṛtyā + atha saṃprajanyena yoniśaś cintanena ca ||
body.translated_text: And herein, the accomplishment of this training as stated [comes about] through the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), through non-separation from diligence, through mindfulness and awareness, and through proper reflection.

body.text: tatra + an-utpannānāṃ pāpakānām a-kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām an-utpādāya + eva chandaṃ janayati vyāyacchati vīryam ārabhate cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti samyak-praṇidadhāti + ity anena rakṣā ||
body.translated_text: Therein: 'He generates the desire, strives, initiates vigor, applies the mind, and rightly resolves for the very non-arising of unarisen sinful, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>' — by this, protection [is accomplished].

body.text: utpannānāṃ ca prahāṇāya chandaṃ janayati + ity anena śuddhiḥ | an-utpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām utpādāya chandaṃ janayati | yāvad utpannānāṃ ca sthitaye bhūyo-bhāvāya chandaṃ janayati + ity ādi | anena vṛddhiḥ | etāni ca nityam a-pramāda-adhiṣṭhitāni kāryāṇi sarva-kuśala-mūlānāṃ tan-mūlatvāt ||
body.translated_text: 'He generates the desire for the abandonment of [already] arisen [unwholesome dharmas]' — by this, purification [is accomplished]. 'He generates the desire for the arising of unarisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>.' Up to: 'He generates the desire for the stability and further increase of arisen [wholesome dharmas],' and so forth — by this, increase [is accomplished]. And these should always be performed, established in diligence, since they are the root of all wholesome roots.

body.text: yathā + uktam ārya-candra-pradīpa-sūtre | yāvanta dharmāḥ kuśalāḥ prakīrtitāḥ śīla-śrutaṃ tyāgu tathā + eva kṣāntiḥ | sarveṣu mūlaṃ hy ayam a-pramādo nidhāna-lambhaḥ su-gatena deśita | iti ||
body.translated_text: As it is said in the <s>Ārya-Candrapradīpa-sūtra</s>: 'However many wholesome <s>dharmas</s> have been proclaimed — moral conduct, learning, generosity, and likewise patience — heedfulness (<s>apramāda</s>) is the root of all of them, taught by the <s>Sugata</s> as the finding of a treasury.'

body.text: ko * ayam a-pramādo nāma | iṣṭa-vighāta-an-iṣṭa-āgama-śaṅkā-pūrvakaṃ prati-kāra-tātparyaṃ | tad yathā tīvra-kopa-prasādasya rājño bhaiṣajya-taila-paripūrṇa-bhājanaṃ gṛhītvā picchila-saṃkrameṇa bhṛtyasya gacchataḥ ||
body.translated_text: What is this heedfulness? It is the concern for a counter-measure, preceded by the apprehension of the obstruction of what is desired and the arrival of what is undesired. It is like a servant who carries a vessel full of medicinal oil and walks across a slippery bridge, in the service of a king of fierce anger and favor.

body.text: uktaṃ hy ārya-tathā-gata-guhya-sūtre |tatra katamo * a-pramādo |yad indriya-saṃvaraḥ | sa cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā na nimitta-grāhī bhavati | na + anuvyañjana-grāhī | evaṃ yāvan manasā dharmān vijñāya na nimitta-grāhī bhavati | na + anuvyañjana-grāhī | sarva-dharmeṣv āsvādaṃ ca + ādīnavaṃ ca niḥ-śaraṇaṃ ca yathā-bhūtaṃ prajānāti | ayam ucyate * a-pramādaḥ ||
body.translated_text: For it is said in the <s>Ārya-Tathāgataguhya-sūtra</s>: 'Therein, what is heedfulness? It is the restraint of the sense-faculties. Having seen forms with the eye, he does not seize upon the general mark. He does not seize upon the secondary marks. Likewise, up to: having cognized <s>dharmas</s> with the mind, he does not seize upon the general mark. He does not seize upon the secondary marks. With respect to all <s>dharmas</s>, he knows as it truly is the gratification, the danger, and the escape. This is called heedfulness.'

body.text: punar a-param a-pramādo yat sva-cittasya damanaṃ para-cittasya + ārakṣā kleśa-rater a-parikarmaṇā dharma-rater anuvartanaṃ yāvad * ayam ucyate * a-pramādaḥ | yasya guhyaka-adhipate śraddhā ca + a-pramādaś ca tasya + anulomikena vīryeṇa kāryaṃ | yena tān a-pramāda-kāraṇān śraddhā-kāraṇāṃś ca dharmān samudānayati | yasya guhyaka-adhipate śraddhā ca + a-pramādaś ca vīryaṃ ca tena smṛti-saṃprajanye yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | yena smṛti-saṃprajanyena sarvān bodhi-pakṣān dharmān na vipraṇāśayati | yasya guhyaka-adhipate śraddhā ca + a-pramādaś ca vīryaṃ ca smṛti-saṃprajanyaṃ ca tena yoniśaḥ prayoge yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | yoniśaḥ prayukto hi guhyaka-adhipate bodhi-satvo yad asti tad asti + iti prajānāti | yan na + asti tan na + asti + iti prajānāti | yāvad asti saṃvṛtyā cakṣur ity ādi ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, heedfulness is: the taming of one's own mind, the guarding of others' minds, the non-cultivation of delight in afflictions, and the following of delight in the <s>Dharma</s> — up to: this is called heedfulness. For one who has faith and heedfulness, O Lord of <s>Guhyakas</s>, effort in accordance [with them] must be made — by which he brings together those <s>dharmas</s> that are the causes of heedfulness and the causes of faith. For one who has faith, heedfulness, and vigor, O Lord of <s>Guhyakas</s>, the practice of mindfulness and clear comprehension must be undertaken — by which mindfulness and clear comprehension he does not lose any of the <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening. For one who has faith, heedfulness, vigor, and mindfulness and clear comprehension, O Lord of <s>Guhyakas</s>, the practice of methodical application must be undertaken. For, O Lord of <s>Guhyakas</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> who is methodically applied knows: "What exists, exists"; he knows: "What does not exist, does not exist." Up to: there conventionally exists [what is called] the eye, and so on.'

body.text: tathā + atra + eva + āha | sadā + a-pramādo hy a-mṛtasya mūlaṃ satva-artha-yuktasya ca bodhi-cittaṃ | yad yoniśaś ca + eva viveka-cittam a-parigrahaḥ sarva-sukhasya mūlam iti ||
body.translated_text: And right here it says: 'For heedfulness is always the root of the deathless, and <s>bodhicitta</s> [the root] of one devoted to the purpose of beings. And that methodical [application] together with the mind of detachment — non-grasping is the root of all happiness.'

body.text: āha ca | para-ātma-samatā-abhyāsād bodhi-cittaṃ dṛḍhī-bhavet | āpekṣikaṃ para-ātmatvaṃ pāra-avāraṃ yathā-mṛṣā ||
body.translated_text: And it says: 'Through the practice of the equality of other and self, <s>bodhicitta</s> becomes firm. The otherness of other and self is relative — like the near and far banks [of a river], it is false.'

body.text: tat-kūlaṃ na svataḥ pāraṃ kim apekṣya + astv a-pāratā | ātmatvaṃ na svataḥ siddhaṃ kim apekṣya paro bhavet ||
body.translated_text: 'That bank is not "far" from its own [standpoint] — in dependence on what would there be "non-far-ness"? Selfhood is not established from its own [side] — in dependence on what could "other" exist?'

body.text: tad-duṣkhena na me bādhā + ity ato yadi na rakṣasi | na + āgāmi-kāya-duṣkhāt te bādhā tat kena rakṣasi ||
body.translated_text: '"His suffering does not harm me" — if on that account you do not protect [him], [then] the suffering of [your own] future body does not harm you [now either] — so why do you protect against that?'

body.text: aham eva tadā + api + iti mithyā + iyaṃ parikalpanā | anya eva mṛto yasmād anyas tatra prajāyate ||
body.translated_text: '"But I myself will exist even then" — this is a false construction. For it is one who dies and another who is born there.'

body.text: anyaś cej jāyate tatra kiṃ puṇyena prayojanaṃ | yūnaḥ kiṃ vṛddha-kāyasya sukhāya dhana-saṃcayaiḥ ||
