body.translated_text: 'If it is another who is born there, what is the use of merit? What use to a youth are the accumulations of wealth for the happiness of an old body?'

body.text: mṛte garbha-gate tāvad anyo bālaḥ prajāyate | mṛte bālye kumāratvaṃ tan-nāśāya + āgato yuvā ||
body.translated_text: 'When [the first] has died and [the next] has entered the womb, another child is born. When childhood has died, youth arrives — for the destruction of that [childhood].'

body.text: tan-nāśāc ca + āgato vṛddhaḥ | ekaḥ kāyaḥ kathaṃ mataḥ | evaṃ prati-kṣaṇaṃ ca + anyaḥ kāyaḥ keśa-nakha-ādi-vat ||
body.translated_text: 'And from the destruction of that [youth], old age arrives. How is it considered a single body? Thus, at every moment, the body is different — like hair and nails and so forth.'

body.text: atha bālyā-parityāgād bālo yāti kumāratāṃ | kāya-sva-bhāvo vaktavyo yo * avasthā-rahitaḥ sthitaḥ | kāyaś cet pratimā-ākāraḥ pesī-bhasmasu na + asti saḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'But if, through the abandonment of infancy, the child goes to youth, then a bodily own-nature that remains without [change of] state must be specified. If the body is like a statue — it does not exist in [a mere] lump of flesh or in ashes.'

body.text: sūkṣma-bhāvena cet tatra sthaulyaṃ tyaktvā vyavasthitaḥ | a-nirdeśyaḥ svataḥ prāptaḥ | kāya ity ucyate na saḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'If [one says] it exists there in subtle form, having abandoned grossness and remaining — [then] it has become [something] indescribable, self-arrived; it is not called a "body."'

body.text: tatra cintā + eva me na + asti dṛśya-kāyas tu nāśavān | avasthābhiś ca saṃbandhaḥ saṃvṛtyā ca + eva dṛśyate ||
body.translated_text: 'There, my concern simply does not exist — the visible body is perishable. The connection with [various] states is also seen only conventionally.'

body.text: āgamāc ca tad astitvaṃ yukty-āgama-nivāritam | na guṇa-vyatirekeṇa pradhānaṃ vidyate yataḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'And its existence [posited] from scripture is refuted by both reasoning and scripture — since the <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter) does not exist apart from the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities).'

body.text: na ca trīṇi pradhānāni tathā sattā guṇā api | praty-ekaṃ try-ātmakās te * api śeṣaṃ na + eka-vidhaṃ jagat ||
body.translated_text: 'Nor are three [things] the <s>pradhāna</s>; likewise, the <s>guṇas</s> do not exist [as three independent things]. Those three themselves are each triple-natured — the rest [of the argument shows that] the world is not of a single kind.'

body.text: a-cetanaṃ ca vastra-ādi tat-sukha-ādy-ātmakaṃ katham | sukha-āder na paṭṭa-utpattiḥ paṭṭa-ādes tu sukha-ādayaḥ | paṭṭa-ādīnām a-hetutvād a-bhāvas tat-sukhaṃ kutaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'And cloth and the like are non-sentient — how could they be of the nature of pleasure and so forth? Pleasure and so forth do not produce silk; rather, from silk and so forth [come] pleasures and so forth. Since silk and the like are non-causes [of pleasure in themselves], their [supposed inherent] pleasure — whence would it come?'

body.text: tasmād āgama-yuktibhyāṃ a-nityaṃ sarva-saṃskṛtaṃ |tad * dhetu-phala-saṃbandhaḥ praty-akṣatvān na sādhyate ||
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, by both scripture and reasoning, all conditioned things are impermanent. The connection of cause and effect is not established as directly perceived.'

body.text: sva-saṃtāne ca dṛṣṭo * asau nityeṣu ca kathaṃ yathā | param aṇus

children.translated_text: too is not one — due to the impossibility of spatial divisions.'

body.translated_text: 'And it is seen in one's own continuum — but how in permanent [things]? The ultimate atom

body.text: dīpa-tailaṃ kṣayaṃ yāti kṣīyamānaṃ na lakṣyate | evaṃ bhāvā na lakṣyante kṣīyamānāḥ prati-kṣaṇaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'The oil of a lamp goes to exhaustion; [yet] its diminishing is not perceived. Just so, beings are not perceived as they diminish moment by moment.'

body.text: saṃtānaḥ samudāyaś ca paṅkti-senā-ādi-van mṛṣā | tatra + abhyāsād ahaṃ-kāraḥ parasmin kiṃ na jāyate ||
body.translated_text: 'A continuum, an aggregate — like a row, an army, and so forth — is false. Therein, from habit, the sense of "I" [arises] — why should it not arise in regard to another?'

body.text: tasmād evaṃ jagat jñeyaṃ yathā + āyatana-saṃcayaḥ | a-prāptam eva tad duṣkhaṃ prati-kāryaṃ para-ātmanoḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, the world should be known thus: as a collection of sense-bases. That suffering has not [yet] arrived — [but] it should be countered, [whether] of other or of self.'

body.text: a-yuktam api ced etat sva-ātmany asti + itaratra na | yad a-yuktaṃ nivartyaṃ tat svam anyad vā yathā-balaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'Even if this is illogical — [the objection being that] it exists in one's own self but not in another — what is illogical should be removed, whether one's own or another's, according to [one's] ability.'

body.text: kṛpayā bahu duṣkhaṃ cet kasmād utpādyate balāt | jagad-duṣkhaṃ nirūpya + idaṃ kṛpā-duṣkhaṃ kathaṃ bahu ||
body.translated_text: 'If through compassion much suffering [is generated], why is it forcibly produced? Having reflected upon the suffering of the world, how could the suffering of compassion be much [in comparison]?'

body.text: evaṃ bhāvita-saṃtānāḥ para-duṣkha-sama-priyāḥ | avīcīm avagāhante haṃsāḥ padma-vanaṃ yathā ||
body.translated_text: 'Those whose continua are thus cultivated, who hold the suffering of others as dear [as their own] — they plunge into <s>Avīci</s> [hell] as swans [plunge] into a lotus lake.'

body.text: satveṣu mucyamāneṣu ye te prāmodya-sāgarāḥ | tair eva nanu paryāptaṃ mokṣeṇa + apy a-rasena kim ||
body.translated_text: 'When beings are liberated, those oceans of joy [that arise] — are they not sufficient? What need of liberation that is flavorless?'

body.text: evaṃ para-arthaṃ kṛtvā + api na mado na ca vismayaḥ | na vipāka-phala-ākāṅkṣā para-artha-eka-anta-tṛṣṇayā
body.translated_text: 'Thus, even having acted for the benefit of others, there is no pride and no wonder; no expectation of the fruit of ripening — through the sole craving for the benefit of others.'

body.text: daśa-dik-satva-saṃpattir ātmīyā + asya na saṃśayaḥ | na + asty erṣyā-avakāśo * api para-saukhye sva-saṃjñayā ||
body.translated_text: 'The prosperity of beings in all ten directions is his own — of this there is no doubt. There is no occasion even for jealousy at others' happiness, through the perception [of it as] one's own.'

body.text: pareṣām ātmano vā + api sāmānyā pāpa-deśanā | puṇya-anumodanā ca + evaṃ buddha-adhyeṣaṇa-yācanaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'The confession of sins, whether of others or of oneself, is the same; the rejoicing in merit likewise; and the entreaty and supplication of the <s>Buddhas</s> [is the same].'

body.text: pariṇāmanam apy evaṃ nir-viśeṣaṃ pravartate | puṇyaṃ pravartate tasmād an-antaṃ satva-dhātu-vat ||
body.translated_text: 'The dedication too operates without distinction. Therefore, merit operates endlessly — like the realm of beings.'

body.text: ayaṃ sa mārga-pravaraḥ kṣema-an-anta-sukha-utsavaḥ | bodhi-satva-mahā-sa-artha kalila-prīti-vardhanaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'This is the supreme path — a festival of peace, endless happiness; the great, meaningful [path] of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, increasing the joy of the dense [forest of merit].'

body.text: pālyamānaś ca satataṃ vajra-pāṇy-ātiyāntrikaiḥ | māra-gulmika-saṃtrāsa-jananair buddha-kiṃ-karaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'And [this path is] constantly guarded by <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> and his most intimate [attendants], who strike terror in the bands of <s>Māra</s> — the servants of the <s>Buddha</s>.'

body.text: saṃbuddha-rāja-tanayā bodhi-citta-ratha-sthitāḥ | vahante tena mārgeṇa stūyamānāḥ sura-ādibhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'The sons of the Fully-Awakened King, established upon the chariot of <s>bodhicitta</s>, are carried along that path, praised by <s>devas</s> and others.'

body.text: tasmād ātmatvam āropya satveṣv abhyāsa-yogataḥ | para-ātma-duṣkha-śānty-artham ātma-ādīn sarvathā + utsṛjet ||
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, having superimposed selfhood upon beings through the practice of habituation, one should abandon the self and all else entirely, for the purpose of pacifying the suffering of other and self.'

body.text: tṛṣṇā parigraho yasya tasya duṣkhaṃ na śāmyati | pariṇāma-vināśitvāt sa duṣkha-janako yataḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'For one who has craving and grasping, suffering does not cease — since that [craving], because of its nature of transformation and destruction, produces suffering.'

body.text: loke duṣkha-agni-tapte ca kā ratiḥ su-sukhe bhavet | samantād dahyamānasya nakha-a-dāhe * api kiṃ sukham ||
body.translated_text: 'In a world scorched by the fire of suffering, what delight could there be in pleasure? For one burning on all sides, what happiness even in the non-burning of a fingernail?'

body.text: ātma-tṛṣṇā ca sarveṣāṃ duṣkhāṇāṃ mūlam uttamaṃ | tasmān nihanmi tām eva satvebhyaḥ sva-artham utsṛjan ||
body.translated_text: 'And craving for the self is the supreme root of all sufferings. Therefore I shall destroy that very [craving], abandoning self-interest for the sake of beings.'

body.text: tad agra-dūtī jñātā-icchā jetavyā sarva-yatnataḥ | ātma-tatva-smṛtiṃ kṛtvā pratītya-utpāda-cintayā ||
body.translated_text: 'Its advance scout — the desire for what is known — should be conquered with all effort, by establishing mindfulness of the true nature of self through the contemplation of dependent origination.'

body.text: yad bhayān na + utsṛjāmy etat tad eva + ādadato bhayaṃ | prati-kṣaṇaṃ hi yāty eva kāyaś cittaṃ ca me yataḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'If out of fear I do not abandon this [body], that very grasping [of it] is the [real] fear — since this body and mind of mine are departing at every moment.'

body.text: yadi nityā + apy a-nityena nir-malā mala-vāhinā | bodhiḥ kāyena labhyeta nanu labdhā mayā + eva sā ||
body.translated_text: 'If awakening could be obtained with this body — [a body that is] permanent even though impermanent, pure even though carrying defilements — would I not have already obtained it?'

body.text: evam ātmānam utsṛjya sarva-satva-artham ācaret | bhaiṣajya-pratimā-kalpo loka-dharmeṣv a-cintakaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Thus, having abandoned the self, one should act for the benefit of all beings — like a healing remedy or an image, not thinking about worldly <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text: sarva-satva-artha-mantritve sva-prajñāṃ viniyojayet | yuktyā saṃrakṣya tu dravyaṃ satveṣu vā + upayojayet ||
body.translated_text: 'One should employ one's own wisdom in the ministry of the welfare of all beings. And one should protect property with discernment, or employ it for the sake of beings.'

body.text: sva-kāye para-kāye vā yad duṣkhaṃ na + iha duṣkha-kṛt | satvānāṃ bhoga-vighnatvāt kleśāḥ śodhyāḥ prayatnataḥ | loka-upajīvyāt sat-tīrthād

children.translated_text: [afflictions should be removed] like snake-corpses [from a pond].'

body.translated_text: 'Whatever suffering exists in one's own body or in another's body — it does not cause suffering here [to the awakened one]. Because afflictions are the obstruction to beings' enjoyment, they should be purified with effort. From the sacred ford that is the livelihood of the world,

body.text: puṇya-kṣetram idaṃ śuddhaṃ saṃpat-sasya-mahā-phalaṃ | sukha-dur-bhikṣa-saṃtaptaṃ jagat saṃtarpayiṣyati ||
body.translated_text: 'This purified field of merit, bearing the great fruit of the harvest of prosperity, will satisfy the world, scorched by the famine of happiness.'

body.text: lābha-sat-kāra-kāya-ādi tyaktaṃ nanu-jane

children.text: mayā | kopaḥ kasya + artham adya + api mṛṣā vā tan mayā + uditam ||
children.translated_text: Why then anger even now? Or was that said falsely by me?'

body.translated_text: 'Gain, honor, body, and so forth have been abandoned by me among the people.

body.text: sva-artha-ghneṣu yadi dveṣaḥ kṛpā kutra bhaviṣyati | nir-dayasya + api kaḥ kopaḥ para-artho yadi naśyati ||
body.translated_text: 'If there is hatred toward those who destroy one's own interest, where will compassion be? For one who is merciless, what is anger [about] if the interest of others is destroyed?'

body.text: ākrośa-ādi-kṣamāḥ satyam ikṣukas tūrika-ādayaḥ | svāmy--asanena dur-nyastā na + upabhogyā bhavanti te ||
body.translated_text: 'Truly, sugarcane, cotton, and the like are patient with being cut and so forth. [But] badly placed by the master in his seat, they do not become objects of enjoyment.'

body.text: cintayati pratīkāraṃ na ca svāmi-hita-icchayā | na + api saṃcodayaty enaṃ bhoga-arthaṃ na + upayāti ca ||
body.translated_text: 'He does not think about retaliation; he has no desire for the master's benefit; he does not urge him on; he does not approach him for the purpose of enjoyment.'

body.text: anusmṛtyā + upasmṛtya + etān a-kṛṣṭa-uptā jina-ātma-jāḥ | nānā-viṣaya-dhātūnāṃ sārva-indriya-mahā-gadān ||
body.translated_text: 'By recollecting and remembering these [truths] — the sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, [like plants] growing unsown — [they cure] the great diseases of all the sense-faculties in the various elemental realms.'

body.text: vijñapya smārayitvā + etān kruddhān apy upakāriṇaḥ | sva-bhāvā-tyakta-mādhuryāḥ sukhayanty eva duṣkhitān ||
body.translated_text: 'Having informed and reminded these [beings], [the bodhisattvas are] benefactors even of those who are angry. Of a sweetness not abandoned by their own nature, they bring happiness to the suffering.'

body.text: dhātavaḥ pañca bhū-vāri-tejo * anila-kha-saṃjñitāḥ | yāvat satvāḥ sthitās tāvat sarveṣām artha-kāriṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'The five elements — called earth, water, fire, wind, and space — as long as beings exist, for that long they serve the purpose of all.'

body.text: sarva-duś-caritena + eṣāṃ satva-arthād vinivartanaṃ | evam etān karomy eṣa dhātūn ṣaḍ api nir-vyathān ||
body.translated_text: 'By all evil conduct, these [elements] are turned away from the purpose of beings. Thus, I shall make these six elements also free from distress.'

body.text: yāvad ākāśa-niṣṭasya niṣṭhā lokasya saṃbhavet | tāvat sthāsyāmi loka-arthaṃ kurvan jñāna-puraḥ-saraḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'For as long as space endures, for as long as the world's end may come — for that long I shall remain, acting for the purpose of the world, with knowledge as my guide.'

body.text: ātma-ācāryo * anuśiyaṣyād * dhi sadā + ātmānaṃ su-śiṣya-vat | a-pṛṣṭvā ca + ātmanā + ātmānaṃ balena + a-rakṣita-kriyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'One should be one's own teacher, always training oneself as a good pupil trains. And without asking oneself [permission], one who is unguarded in actions by force [of habit] —'

body.text: ka eva mama duṣkhena duṣkhī syān me bhayād bhayī | tad-doṣa-anuśaya-jño vā yathā + ātma-gurur ātmanaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Who indeed would be pained by my pain, afraid by my fear? Or who would know the latent tendencies of my faults — as one's own teacher is to oneself?'

body.text: a-virāgy a-palāyī ca karuṇā-viṣayo * api vā | nitya-saṃnihitaś ca + api śiṣya ātma-samaḥ kutaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Not dispassionate, not fleeing, also an object of compassion, and always present — where is there a pupil equal to oneself?'

body.text: kleśa-unmatto * atha moha-andhaḥ prapāta-bahule pathi | skhalan pade pade śocyaḥ para ātmā ca sarvadā ||
body.translated_text: 'Maddened by afflictions, blinded by delusion, on a path full of precipices — stumbling at every step, pitiable — another's self [too is] always [thus].'

body.text: skhalita-anveṣaṇaṃ tasmāt samāna-vyasanāj janāt | na yuktaṃ yujyate tv atra guṇān dṛṣṭvā + adbhutaṃ mahat ||
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, seeking out the faults of one who shares the same calamity is not proper. But what is proper here is, seeing [others'] qualities, the great wonder [of appreciation].'

body.text: na + ekena śakyam ādātuṃ mayā doṣa-mahā-udadhiḥ | kṛtyam anyair mama + eva + atra ko * anya-doṣeṣu mā + īkṣaṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'The great ocean of faults cannot be taken up by me alone. My task here is with others — so what use gazing at the faults of others?'

body.text: para-codana-dakṣāṇām an-adhīṣṭa-upakāriṇāṃ | vākyaṃ mūrdhnā pratīcchāmi sarva-śiṣyo bhavāmy ahaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'I shall accept upon my head the words of those who are skilled at correcting others, who render service unasked — I shall be a pupil of all.'

body.text: saṃgrāmo hi mama + ekasya bahubhiḥ kleśa-śatrubhiḥ | tatra + ekena raṇa-āsaktam anye nighnanti māṃ sukham ||
body.translated_text: 'For the battle is mine alone against many enemies — the afflictions. Therein, while I am engaged in combat with one, the others strike me comfortably.'

body.text: tatra yaḥ pṛṣṭhato bhītiṃ śrāvayed anyato * api vā | pradviṣṭo vā prasanno vā same prāṇa-pradaḥ su-hṛt ||
body.translated_text: 'Therein, one who would announce fear from behind, or from another direction — whether hostile or friendly — such a one who saves my life is [my true] friend.'

body.text: ali-saṃhāta-nīlena cīra-bhāraṇa-bhāriṇā | vicitra-surabhi-sphīta-puṣpa-śekhara-hāriṇā ||
body.translated_text: By him whose body is dark as a swarm of bees, who bears the burden of bark-garments, who captivates with a crest-garland of variegated, fragrant, and abundant flowers —

body.text: yugapat sarva-dig-buddha-kṣetra-sāgara-cāriṇā | balinā prati-kāryeṇa sarva-māra-apahāriṇā ||
body.translated_text: By him who simultaneously traverses the ocean of <s>Buddha</s>-fields in all directions, who is mighty, who acts on behalf [of beings], who vanquishes all <s>Māras</s> —

body.text: naraka-preta-saṃtāpa-praśama-unmukta-vāriṇā | saṃsāra-gahana-anta-stha-bhavya-satva-artha-sāriṇā ||
body.translated_text: By him who releases the cooling waters that allay the torment of hells and <s>pretas</s>, who furthers the welfare of beings worthy [of liberation] dwelling in the depths of the thicket of <s>saṃsāra</s> —

body.text: jagan-netra-ucchava-utpādi-bala-alaṅ-kāra-dhāriṇā | viduṣā bāla-vapuṣā loka-vismaya-kāriṇā ||
body.translated_text: By him who bears the ornament of the powers that produce the festival of the world's eye, who though wise bears the form of a youth, causing wonder in the world —

body.text: mañjuśrī saṃjñakaṃ yat tat piṇḍī-bhūtaṃ jagad-dhitaṃ | sarveṇa + eva + ātma-bhāvena namas tasmai punaḥ punaḥ ||
body.translated_text: To that one known by the name <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, who is the embodiment of the world's welfare, with my entire being I pay homage again and again.

body.text: an-eka-duṣkha-saṃtapta-prahlādana-mahā-hradaṃ | trailokya-tṛṣṇā-pātāla-prapūraṇa-mahā-ambu-dam ||
body.translated_text: To the great lake that refreshes those scorched by manifold sufferings, to the great rain-cloud that fills the abyss of craving of the three worlds,

body.text: jagad-iṣṭa-phala-sphīta-daśa-dik-kalpa-pāda-paṃ |prārthita-prāpti-saṃhṛṣṭa-jagan-netra-utpala-arcitaṃ ||
body.translated_text: To the <s>kalpa</s>-tree in the ten directions, abundant with the fruits desired by the world, honored by the lotus-eyes of beings gladdened by the attainment of their wishes,

body.text: vismaya-udgata-romāñcair bodhi-satva-śataiḥ stutam | mañjuśriyaṃ namasyāmi praṇāmair uttara-uttaraiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Praised by hundreds of <s>bodhisattvas</s> with hair standing on end in wonder — I pay homage to <s>Mañjuśrī</s> with salutations ever more supreme.

body.text: niḥ-śeṣa-duṣkha-vaidyāya sukha-sattra-pradāyine | sarva-ākāra-upajīvyāya mañjughoṣāya te namaḥ ||
body.translated_text: To the physician of all suffering without remainder, to the bestower of the feast of happiness, to him who is the sustainer of all in every way — homage to you, <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>!

body.text: iti jina-tanayānāṃ sarvathā + aty-adbhutānāṃ caritam upanibdhya + upārjitaṃ yac * chubhaṃ me | bhavatu sukham an-antaṃ dehināṃ tena yāvat su-gata-padam an-anta-vyoma-sīmā-ādhipatyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Thus, having composed [this account] of the conduct of the sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, who are in every way most wondrous — by whatever merit has been earned by me, may there be endless happiness for all embodied beings, until [they attain] the state of the <s>Sugata</s>, the sovereignty over the boundless expanse of infinite space.

body.text: puṇya-vṛddhiḥ samāptā ||
body.translated_text: The [chapter on] the Increase of Merit is concluded.

body.text: samāptaś ca + ayaṃ bodhi-satva-vinayo * an-eka-sūtra-anta-uddhṛtaḥ śikṣā-samuccaya iti ||
body.translated_text: And thus is completed this <s>Bodhisattva</s>-discipline extracted from numerous <s>sūtras</s>, [called] the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> (Compendium of Training).
